q: 最适合做购物车主存储的是？
options: PostgreSQL（关系型）
Redis（内存 KV）
Neo4j（图数据库）
Elasticsearch（搜索引擎）

q: 补全 ACID：
text: ACID = {{Atomicity}} 原子性、{{Consistency}} 一致性、{{Isolation}} 隔离性、{{Durability}} 持久性。
why: ACID 是关系型事务的四个保证，是「为什么强一致数据放关系型」的根本原因。
why_en: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability—the four guarantees behind relational transactions.

q: 相比单主关系型数据库，Cassandra 在写密集负载下的主要优势是？
options: 更强的 ACID 事务
无主架构下的水平写扩展
更丰富的 SQL join
更低的存储成本
why: Cassandra 无主、每个节点都能接受写，写吞吐随节点数近似线性扩展；这是它牺牲 join 和强一致换来的。
why_en: Cassandra is masterless so every node accepts writes, giving near-linear horizontal write scaling—traded off against joins and strong consistency.
options_en: Stronger ACID transactions
Horizontal write scaling with a leaderless architecture
Richer SQL joins
Lower storage cost

q: 补全缓存的代价与缓解：
text: 在数据库前加了缓存，就必须处理 {{stale}} 旧数据，常用 {{TTL}} 过期或写时 {{invalidation}} 失效来控制。

scenario: 要在数十亿行历史数据上做分析报表：大范围聚合、按列扫描，不是逐行事务。
q: 最合适的存储是？
options: OLTP 的 PostgreSQL 主库
列式/数仓 (ClickHouse / BigQuery)
Redis
Neo4j
why: 这题的关键词是「数十亿行历史数据 + 大范围聚合 + 按列扫描」。这属于 OLAP/报表分析负载：一次查询会扫很多行，但通常只用少数几列，比如 time、region、price。列式 OLAP/数仓只读取相关列，并用 MPP 把扫描和聚合拆到多节点并行执行；行存 OLTP 主库更适合逐行事务，不适合拿来扫全历史做报表。
why_en: The key signals are billions of historical rows, wide aggregations, and column scans. This is an OLAP analytics workload: a query scans many rows but often touches only a few columns. Columnar OLAP warehouses read only the needed columns and use MPP to parallelize scans and aggregation across nodes, while a row-store OLTP primary is built for short row-level transactions.
whenOtherWins: 如果是「按时间看单个指标/单个 entity 的曲线」，时序库更贴；如果是跨全量历史数据做多维报表、group by、top K、dashboard 聚合，ClickHouse/BigQuery 这类列式 OLAP/MPP 数仓更贴。数据量中等时，PostgreSQL 加物化视图、分区或列存扩展也可能够用。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线分析处理：面向历史数据报表、聚合、group by、top K、趋势分析的大扫描查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLAP means analytical queries over historical data, such as reports, aggregations, group by, top K, and trend analysis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线事务处理：面向用户下单、付款、发评论这类短事务，强调单行/少量行读写和强一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OLTP means short business transactions such as orders, payments, and comments, usually touching one or a few rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列存数据，而不是按整行存。查 sum(price) by region 时只读 price、region 等相关列，不把整行所有字段都读出来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Columnar storage keeps values by column, so a query like sum(price) by region reads only price and region instead of full rows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大规模并行处理：把一个分析 SQL 拆成多个分区/阶段，让很多节点一起扫描、过滤、聚合，最后合并结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MPP splits an analytical query into partitions and stages so many nodes can scan, filter, aggregate, and merge results in parallel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门放历史分析数据的系统，常从业务库、日志、事件流同步数据，用来做 BI 报表和离线/交互式分析。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data warehouse stores historical analytical data, often copied from OLTP databases, logs, or event streams for BI and analytics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源列式 OLAP 数据库，适合低延迟聚合分析、实时 dashboard、日志/事件分析。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ClickHouse is an open-source columnar OLAP database for low-latency aggregations, dashboards, and log/event analytics.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google Cloud 托管数仓，适合超大规模 SQL 分析，用户少管服务器，按扫描/计算资源付费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BigQuery is Google Cloud's managed data warehouse for large-scale SQL analytics without managing servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以时间为主轴存指标点，擅长高频写入、时间范围查询、降采样和保留策略；窄查询很强，跨全部 series 的复杂多维分析不一定最合适。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-series database stores timestamped metric points and is strong at high-ingest time-range queries, downsampling, and retention; it is not always best for broad cross-series analytics.

scenario: 支付接口去重：同一 request_id 只处理一次，记录保留 24 小时后自动过期，且「判断是否存在 + 写入」必须原子完成。
q: 哪条 Redis 命令最适合做这个幂等标记？
options: SET req:{id} 1 EX 86400
SET req:{id} 1 NX EX 86400
SETEX req:{id} 86400 1
INCR req:{id}
why: NX = 仅当 key 不存在时才写入，用返回值就知道「是不是第一次」；EX 86400 顺带设 24h 过期。判断 + 写入一步原子完成，正是幂等标记要的。
why_en: Use SET with NX and EX so the write happens only when the key is absent and expires in 24 hours, giving an atomic idempotency guard.
codeSample:
# 原子：仅当不存在时写入 + 24h 过期
SET req:abc123 1 NX EX 86400
#  返回 OK  -> 首次请求，继续处理
#  返回 nil -> 重复请求，直接跳过
options_en: SET req:{id} 1 EX 86400
SET req:{id} 1 NX EX 86400
SETEX req:{id} 86400 1
INCR req:{id}

scenario: 面试官让你解释你如何驱动 AI agent 完成工程任务，而不是只问你用过哪些工具。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to explain how you drive an AI agent through engineering work, not just list which tools you've used.
q: 面试官问「你怎么用 AI/agent 工作」，最能拿分的回答核心是什么？
q_en: The interviewer asks how you work with AI/agents — what's the strongest core answer?
options: 把用过的 AI 工具按项目顺序逐一报一遍，讲清版本和特性
强调自己几乎全程手写代码，尽量少让 AI 插手关键逻辑
把 agent 当成要工程化驾驭的系统：讲清怎么喂上下文、定成功标准、防失败
强调 AI 很快会取代程序员，讨论这份工作还有没有必要存在
options_en: List every AI tool you've used, project by project, with versions and features.
Emphasize that you hand-write almost all the code and rarely let AI touch core logic.
Treat the agent as a system to engineer: how you feed context, define success, and guard against failure.
Emphasize that AI will soon replace programmers and question whether the job still matters.
why: 这题考工程化理解，不是工具清单：高分答案讲清怎么喂上下文、怎么定义成功(evals)、怎么防失败(failure modes)。
why_en: The strongest answer treats the agent as an engineered system: how you feed context, define success with evals, and prevent failure modes.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题明确是工具经验盘点，可以简短列工具，但仍要回到你如何控制质量和风险。
tradeoff: 工具清单的广度 vs 工程化驾驭的深度

面试官能看到你怎么控制上下文、成功标准和失败模式
偏离了「你怎么用 agent 工作」这个具体问题
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer hears a list of names and sees no judgment.
It can make you look unable to use AI effectively.
The interviewer sees how you control context, success criteria, and failure modes.
It drifts away from the actual question of how you work with an agent.

只有话题本身在讨论行业趋势时才适合展开这点

scenario: 你要在白板上画出一个自主 agent 从接到任务到完成的完整运行链路。
scenario_en: You're sketching on a whiteboard how an autonomous agent runs end-to-end, from receiving a task to finishing it.
q: 一个自主 agent 的基本工作循环是什么？
q_en: What is the basic working loop of an autonomous agent?
options: 读取上下文、规划下一步、调用工具行动、观察结果，再对照成功标准判断是否收尾
把最终代码方案一次性生成，不做任何验证或修正就交付
只生成代码草稿，从来不真正执行，也不做任何验证
不断随机尝试各种可能操作，直到偶然凑巧碰对答案
options_en: Read context, plan the next step, act via a tool, observe the result, then check it against success criteria before looping again.
Generate the final code solution in one shot and ship it with no verification or correction.
Only draft code but never actually execute it or verify anything.
Keep randomly trying possible actions until one happens to work by luck.
why: agent = 在循环里运行的 LLM。工程发力点都在这个循环的每一步：上下文、工具、验证、终止条件。
why_en: An agent is an LLM in a loop: read context, plan, act via tools, observe, then verify against success criteria before looping again.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  P[读取上下文] --> PL[规划下一步]
  PL --> A[调用工具 行动]
  A --> O[观察结果]
  O --> V{达到成功标准?}
  V -->|否| PL
  V -->|是| D[完成]

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，agent 循环里做规划和决策的核心引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LLM is the large language model that drives planning and decisions inside the agent loop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能自主感知环境、规划步骤、调用工具完成任务的程序系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is a program that autonomously perceives its environment, plans steps, and calls tools to complete a task.

optionMeanings: 把 agent 定义为「读取-规划-行动-观察-验证」的循环

optionMeanings_en: Defines an agent as a read-plan-act-observe-verify loop.
Equates the agent with a one-shot generator that has no verification step.
Equates the agent with a draft generator that never executes.
Equates the agent with directionless random trial and error.

画出的链路会少掉观察和纠错，无法解释怎么处理错误
链路缺了行动和观察，说明不了 agent 怎么真正干活
链路没有规划和终止条件，解释不了成功标准怎么起作用
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The chain fully explains what engineering lever belongs at each step.
The chain drawn is missing observation and correction, so it can't explain error handling.
The chain is missing action and observation, so it can't explain how the agent actually works.
The chain has no planning or stop condition, so it can't explain how success criteria matter.

只有极简单、不需要迭代的任务才可能一次成型

几乎不适用于任何工程场景，缺少收敛机制
optionDirectness_en: Fits best when describing the general autonomous-agent loop.
Fits only extremely simple tasks that never need iteration.
Fits only pure-generation assistance that never needs execution feedback.
Fits almost no engineering scenario since it has no convergence mechanism.

scenario: 你要决定把一个任务做成固定 workflow，还是让模型自主规划、调用工具并迭代。
scenario_en: You must decide whether to build a task as a fixed workflow or let the model plan, call tools, and iterate on its own.
q: 该先用固定 workflow，还是该上能自主决策的 agent？
q_en: Should you use a fixed workflow, or an agent that decides autonomously?
options: 只要能用 agent 就用，它永远比固定 workflow 更好用
agent 不需要任何工具，也能独立完成整个工程任务
两者本质上没有区别，选哪个都不影响结果
复杂、高价值、模型能胜任、出错可恢复时才上 agent，否则用固定 workflow
options_en: Use an agent whenever you can — it's always better than a fixed workflow.
An agent can finish the whole engineering task without any tools at all.
The two are basically the same, so it doesn't matter which one you pick.
Only go agentic when the task is complex, high-value, the model can handle it, and errors are recoverable — otherwise use a fixed workflow.
why: 先用最简单的方案；workflow 是预定义路径，agent 让模型自决步骤。判断看四问：复杂度、价值、可行性、错误代价，任一为否就别上 agent。
why_en: Go agentic only when the task is complex, valuable, the model can handle it, and errors are recoverable — otherwise keep the predefined workflow.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务路径稳定、错误代价高，或规则就能覆盖，固定 workflow 更可控、更便宜。
tradeoff: agent 自主决策的灵活性 vs 固定 workflow 的可控与低成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 预定义的固定代码执行路径，步骤和顺序在写代码时就确定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A workflow is a predefined code path where the steps and order are fixed at authoring time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 能自主感知环境、规划步骤、调用工具完成任务的程序系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An agent is a program that autonomously perceives its environment, plans steps, and calls tools to complete a task.

optionMeanings: 认为 agent 在任何场景都比 workflow 更优
认为 agent 完全不需要工具就能独立工作
认为两种方案没有区别、可以随便选
把上 agent 的决策浓缩成四个判断条件
optionMeanings_en: Assumes an agent beats a workflow in every scenario.
Assumes an agent can work independently with no tools at all.
Assumes the two approaches are equivalent and interchangeable.
Condenses the decision to go agentic into four concrete conditions.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会在简单任务上过度设计，白白增加不确定性和成本
忽视了 agent 本来就要靠工具行动这一核心机制
会让本该稳定可控的任务承担不必要的行为风险
能按复杂度、价值、可行性、错误代价四问做出取舍
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It over-engineers simple tasks, adding unneeded uncertainty and cost.
It ignores that acting through tools is the agent's core mechanism.
It exposes a task that should be stable and controllable to needless behavioral risk.
Lets you decide using four questions: complexity, value, feasibility, and error cost.
optionDirectness: 只有全部四个判断条件都成立时才对，不能无脑套用
只有纯推理、完全不需要外部行动的任务才成立
只有两个方案代价和可控性完全等价时才成立，现实很少见
四问都满足时最贴合「什么时候该上 agent」这个判断
optionDirectness_en: Only valid when all four conditions actually hold — never a blanket rule.
Fits only pure-reasoning tasks that never need any external action.
Only valid when cost and controllability are truly identical, which is rare in practice.
Fits best when all four questions point the same way — that's exactly when to go agentic.

scenario: 生产环境里，写码、测试、审查、安全四个专职 agent 排成流水线，由一个协调者按顺序派活。
scenario_en: In production, four specialized agents — coding, testing, review, and security — run in a pipeline, dispatched in order by one orchestrator.
q: 这种「协调者派活给专职子 agent」的结构属于哪种模式？
q_en: What pattern is this 'orchestrator delegates to specialized sub-agents' structure?
options: prompt chaining（提示链）
orchestrator-workers（编排器-子 agent）
autocomplete 自动补全
single-shot 单次 prompt 直出结果
options_en: Prompt chaining (a serial chain of prompts).
Orchestrator-workers (an orchestrator delegating to sub-agents).
Autocomplete.
A single-shot prompt that outputs a result directly.
why: 生产里常见「数字装配线」：编排器把活派给专职子 agent，靠 MCP 等协议打通工具，这是六大 agentic 模式之一。
why_en: A production pipeline like this has an orchestrator delegating to specialized sub-agents wired together via MCP — one of six agentic patterns.
tradeoff: 编排器统一派活的协作深度 vs 单个 agent 独立完成的简单性

rows: 串行步骤，前一步喂后一步
一个生成、一个评判迭代
模型自主决定轨迹和工具

termDefinitions.meaning: 让 agent 以统一协议连接外部工具和数据源的标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MCP is a standard protocol that lets an agent connect to external tools and data sources uniformly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个编排器把任务拆给多个专职子 agent 分别处理的架构模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orchestrator-workers is a pattern where one orchestrator splits a task across specialized sub-agents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把任务拆成串行步骤，前一步的输出作为后一步的输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prompt chaining breaks a task into serial steps, feeding each step's output into the next.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据已有上下文补全下一段文本或代码，不具备多步自主规划。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autocomplete predicts the next chunk of text or code from context, without multi-step autonomous planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次性把问题丢给模型，只产出一次直接结果，没有循环或分工。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single-shot prompt asks the model once and gets one direct result, with no loop or division of labor.

optionMeanings: 把流水线结构误认成串行提示链
编排器统一派活，子 agent 各管一段
把多 agent 协作误认成简单文本补全
把整个流水线误认成一次性直出
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes the pipeline structure for a serial prompt chain.
One orchestrator dispatches work while sub-agents each own a slice.
Mistakes multi-agent collaboration for simple text completion.
Mistakes the whole pipeline for a single direct output.

准确对应写码测试审查安全四个专职角色分工
完全忽略了协调派活和多角色分工
忽略了四个阶段各自独立运行、有中间产出

It matches exactly the four specialized roles: coding, testing, review, security.
It completely ignores the coordination and division of roles.
It ignores that the four stages run independently with intermediate outputs.

只有任务能被压缩成一次调用时才成立，这里明显不是

Fits best when there's one coordinator plus several specialized sub-agents.
Fits only single-model text completion, with no multi-agent setup at all.

scenario: code agent 执行任务时，日志显示它调用了一个从未出现在工具列表里的函数名。
scenario_en: While running a task, a code agent's log shows it calling a function name that never appeared in its tool list.
q: 这属于下面哪一种失败模式？
q_en: Which failure mode does this describe?
options: 范围蔓延，在陌生环境里跑偏
提前终止，任务没做完就收尾
幻觉 / 编造动作
工具误用，传错了参数
options_en: Scope creep, drifting off track in an unfamiliar environment.
Premature termination, wrapping up before the task is done.
Hallucination / fabricated actions.
Tool misuse, passing the wrong parameters.
why: 编造一个不存在的工具/函数名并尝试调用，是「幻觉/编造动作」的典型样例——模型生成的是看似合理却不真实的输出。
why_en: Inventing a tool name that was never given and calling it anyway is a textbook hallucinated action — plausible-looking but unreal output.

rows: 调用不存在的工具或数据
没做完就收尾，或停不下来
明确可量化的完成标准
在陌生环境里越界操作
精确规格+阶段性校验门
参数传错或误调用工具
工具层护栏，参数校验/幂等
长任务里忘记早期约束
多阶段校验+人在环审批

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型生成看似合理但实际不存在或不真实的内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hallucination is when a model generates plausible-sounding output that is not actually real or true.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 在执行中悄悄扩大了任务边界，触碰了不该动的部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is when an agent quietly expands beyond the task's intended boundary.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 调用工具时传错参数或用错工具，导致操作出错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tool misuse is when an agent calls a tool with the wrong parameters or the wrong tool entirely.

任务还没完成 agent 就提前收尾了
模型编造出实际不存在的工具/数据
调用了正确的工具，但参数传错了

The agent wraps up before the task is actually complete.

The log shows a wrong function call, not an early wrap-up.
It matches exactly the never-registered function name in the log.

看到模型调用了列表外的工具/函数时最贴切
只有工具本身存在、只是参数用错时才适用

Fits only when the task is abandoned halfway without reaching its goal.
Fits best when the model calls a tool or function outside its given list.
Fits only when the tool itself exists and just the parameters are wrong.

scenario: 你的 code agent 有时停不下来一直烧钱，有时又没做完就收尾。
scenario_en: Your code agent sometimes runs forever burning cost, and other times stops before the task is actually done.
q: 该给 agent 补上什么，才能同时防死循环和防收尾过早？
q_en: What should you add to the agent to prevent both infinite loops and early stopping?
options: 定义明确可量化的完成标准，给循环清晰终止条件
换一个参数量更大、更贵的基础模型
干脆不给 agent 配任何外部工具
不断往 prompt 里堆更多形容词和提示词
options_en: Define explicit, measurable completion criteria that give the loop a clear stop condition.
Switch to a bigger, more expensive base model.
Simply give the agent no external tools at all.
Keep piling more adjectives and instructions into the prompt.
why: 明确的完成标准把无限循环变成告警而不是天价账单；像给探员写任务书一样定义可量化的成功条件。
why_en: Explicit completion criteria turn a runaway loop into an alert instead of a runaway bill, by giving the agent a quantifiable definition of done.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本来就简单、几步就能完事，加终止条件的工程成本可能不值得。
tradeoff: 可量化终止条件的确定性 vs 模型/工具/提示词调整的间接性

termDefinitions.meaning: 喂给模型的指令文本，用来设定任务和期望输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A prompt is the instruction text given to a model to set the task and expected output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断任务是否算完成的可量化条件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Completion criteria are the quantifiable conditions that determine whether a task counts as done.

把问题误归因到模型能力不足
把问题误归因到工具太多
把问题误归因到提示词不够多
optionMeanings_en: Adds a quantifiable completion condition that stops the loop.
Misattributes the problem to insufficient model capability.
Misattributes the problem to having too many tools.
Misattributes the problem to not having enough prompt text.

没工具 agent 更难完成任务，无法解决终止问题
堆词不会给循环一个可量化的停止信号
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It guards against both a runaway loop and stopping too early.

Piling on words gives the loop no quantifiable stop signal.

只有真正因为模型能力不足才答错时才适用
只有工具本身在制造无限循环时才沾边
只有提示词本身缺失必要信息时才有点用
optionDirectness_en: Fits best when the loop has no clear stop condition.
Fits only when the model's capability is genuinely the bottleneck.

scenario: agent 的输出经常格式不对或编造字段，下游系统直接崩。
scenario_en: The agent's output is often malformed or has invented fields, and it crashes the downstream system.
q: 性价比最高的一道防线是什么？
q_en: What's the highest-ROI defense to add here?
options: 安排人工逐条检查所有输出
一旦报错就整体重启 agent 重来
忽略这个问题，反正大多数输出是对的
用 schema 校验输出格式，在进入下游前挡掉不合规内容
options_en: Have a human manually review every single output.
Restart the whole agent from scratch every time it errors.
Ignore the problem since most outputs are correct anyway.
Validate output against a schema and block noncompliant results before they hit downstream systems.
why: schema 校验是最高 ROI 的韧性手段之一：结构化输出符合机器可校验的格式，低成本挡掉大量幻觉/畸形输出。
why_en: Schema validation is one of the highest-ROI resilience patterns — machine-checkable structured output cheaply catches malformed or hallucinated results.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出格式本来就自由（如长文创作），schema 校验意义不大，更适合靠人工或 LLM judge 把关。
tradeoff: 机器可校验的低成本防线 vs 人工逐条检查的高成本保障

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述数据应有字段和类型的规范，用来机器校验输出是否合规。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A schema defines the expected fields and types of data, letting a machine check whether output is valid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型按预定义格式(如 JSON schema)产出结果，而不是自由文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Structured output means the model produces results in a predefined format, such as JSON matching a schema, instead of free text.

optionMeanings: 靠人力逐条兜底校验
出错就整体重启，没有针对性校验
放任不管，赌大多数输出没问题
用机器可校验的格式规则挡在下游前面
optionMeanings_en: Relies on a human to check every item as a backstop.
Restarts everything on any error, with no targeted validation.
Does nothing and bets that most outputs are fine.
Uses a machine-checkable format rule as a gate before downstream systems.
optionScenarioImpacts: 能挡住错误，但人力成本随输出量线性增长
浪费已完成的工作，也不保证下次不再出错
少数错误一旦流入下游系统仍会崩溃
低成本挡住大量幻觉和畸形输出，规模化可行
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It catches errors, but labor cost grows linearly with output volume.
It wastes completed work and doesn't guarantee the next run avoids the error.
Even a few bad outputs reaching downstream systems still cause a crash.
It cheaply blocks most hallucinated or malformed output and scales well.
optionDirectness: 只有输出量很小、可以负担人工时才现实
只有重启成本极低、且错误随机不复现时才勉强适用
只有下游对错误完全容忍时才可能适用，通常不成立
输出量大、需要自动化把关时最贴切
optionDirectness_en: Realistic only when output volume is small enough for a human to keep up.
Barely works only when restarts are nearly free and errors are random, not systematic.
Only viable if downstream is fully tolerant of errors, which is rarely true.
Fits best when output volume is high and gating needs to be automated.

scenario: agent 感知不到你的代码库现状、运行环境和你的真实意图。
scenario_en: The agent can't perceive the current state of your codebase, its runtime environment, or your real intent.
q: 为了让它对齐，你要承担的核心工程任务是什么？
q_en: What's the core engineering task this creates, so the agent stays aligned?
options: 什么都不用管，相信模型自己能补全所有背景信息
做上下文工程：策划系统提示、精简工具、按需检索，给出精确规格和意图
把整个代码库一次性全部塞进上下文窗口喂给它
换成价格更贵、参数量更大的基础模型
options_en: Do nothing and trust the model to fill in all the missing background itself.
Do context engineering: curate the system prompt, trim tools, retrieve just-in-time, and give a precise spec and intent.
Dump the entire codebase into the context window all at once.
Switch to a more expensive base model with more parameters.
why: 上下文是有限资源，越长模型越容易走神(context rot)。要主动 curate：合适高度的提示、按需检索、必要时压缩。
why_en: Context is a finite resource — the longer it gets, the more the model drifts (context rot) — so you curate it deliberately instead of dumping everything in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文越长，模型准确率和专注度反而下降的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context rot is the phenomenon where a longer context window makes the model less accurate and less focused, not more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为 agent 主动策划提示、工具、检索和记忆，而不是被动塞入所有信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context engineering is deliberately curating an agent's prompt, tools, retrieval, and memory instead of passively dumping in everything.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在需要时才取相关信息，而不是提前把所有数据都放进上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Just-in-time retrieval fetches only the information needed at the moment, instead of loading everything into context upfront.

optionMeanings: 假设模型能凭空补全缺失的项目背景
主动为 agent 策划提示、工具、检索和压缩
把全部代码库不加筛选地塞进上下文
把问题误归因为模型参数不够大
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the model can conjure up missing project background on its own.
Proactively curates the agent's prompt, tools, retrieval, and compaction.
Stuffs the entire codebase into context without any curation.
Misattributes the problem to the model not being large enough.
optionScenarioImpacts: 模型会猜测代码库状态，输出经常文不对题
让 agent 拿到刚好够用、准确的背景信息
触发 context rot，模型反而更容易走神出错
换模型不会补上它本来就拿不到的项目背景
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The model guesses at the codebase state and output often misses the mark.
The agent gets background information that is accurate and just enough.
It triggers context rot, making the model more likely to drift and err.
Swapping models doesn't supply the project background it never had access to.
optionDirectness: 只有任务极简单、不依赖具体环境时才勉强成立
感知不到环境和意图这个约束下最贴切
只有代码库极小、完全装得下时才可能不出问题
只有原模型确实能力不足时才是正确方向
optionDirectness_en: Barely holds only for extremely simple tasks that don't depend on the environment.
Fits best given the constraint that the agent can't perceive environment or intent on its own.
Only safe when the codebase is tiny enough to fit entirely.
Only the right move when the original model's capability is genuinely the bottleneck.

scenario: 你在给一个处理退款的 agent 写评估脚本，要决定主要给什么打分。
scenario_en: You're writing an eval script for a refund-processing agent and deciding what to grade primarily.
q: 评估 agent 时，应该主要给什么打分？
q_en: When evaluating an agent, what should you primarily grade?
options: 严格规定并检查它走的每一步操作路径
它一共调用了多少次工具、耗费多少 token
它最终达成的结果状态，路径(trajectory)只用来调试
它的回复措辞是否得体、风格是否讨喜
options_en: Strictly define and check every step of the path it takes.
How many tool calls it made and how many tokens it burned.
The final outcome it achieves — use the trajectory only to debug why.
Whether its wording is polite and its tone is likeable.
why: outcome(如「退款真落库了吗」)是客观达成证据；trajectory 只用来调试为什么。原则是主要给结果打分，别过度规定路径。
why_en: Grade the outcome, the final state such as whether the refund landed, and use the trajectory only to debug why it happened.
whenOtherWins: 如果需要审计安全合规或调试反复失败的用例，trajectory 检查同样必不可少。
tradeoff: 结果导向的评分客观性 vs 路径规定的可解释性/可调试性

rows: 判断任务是否真的完成
调试为什么失败或低效

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务执行后达成的最终状态，是否客观完成目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Outcome is the final state after execution — whether the goal was objectively achieved.

termDefinitions.meaning: agent 为完成任务走过的具体步骤、工具调用和推理过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Trajectory is the specific sequence of steps, tool calls, and reasoning an agent takes to complete a task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理文本的最小计量单位，调用成本通常按 token 计费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the basic unit of text a model processes, and usage cost is typically billed per token.

optionMeanings: 把路径本身当成评分标准
把资源消耗量当成评分标准
把最终达成状态当成评分标准，路径只做调试
把语言风格当成评分标准
optionMeanings_en: Treats the path itself as the scoring criterion.
Treats resource consumption as the scoring criterion.
Treats the final achieved state as the score, using the path only for debugging.
Treats language style as the scoring criterion.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会惩罚 agent 找到的、你没预料到的有效解法
调用次数和 token 量说明不了任务是否真的完成
既不束缚 agent 找新解法，又能在失败时回查原因
退款有没有真正落库，跟措辞讨不讨喜无关
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It penalizes valid solutions the agent finds that you didn't anticipate.
Call count and token usage don't tell you whether the task was actually completed.
It doesn't constrain the agent's creativity yet still lets you trace failures.
Whether the refund actually landed has nothing to do with how likeable the wording is.
optionDirectness: 只有路径本身有强合规要求(如审计)时才该这样评
只有优化成本本身是目标时才该主要看这个
评估「任务是否真的完成」这个目标时最贴切
只有面向用户的语气确实是评估目标时才适用
optionDirectness_en: Should be graded this way only when the path itself has strict compliance requirements.
Worth grading mainly on this only when cost optimization itself is the goal.
Fits best when the goal is judging whether the task was truly completed.
Applies only when user-facing tone is itself the thing being evaluated.

scenario: 你要给一个多步骤 agent 建评估集，需要选合适的打分方式组合。
scenario_en: You're building an eval set for a multi-step agent and need to pick the right mix of graders.
q: code / LLM-judge / human 三种评分器该怎么组合使用？
q_en: How should you combine code-based, LLM-judge, and human graders?
options: code 查客观结果，LLM judge 打主观维度，定期人工校准
只用人工评分最稳妥、别的都不需要
只用 LLM 打分，不需要代码检查或人工介入
评分标准不重要，随便打个分数就行
options_en: Code checks objective outcomes, LLM-judge grades subjective dimensions, humans calibrate periodically.
Only use human review — nothing else is needed.
Only use an LLM to score — no code checks or human review needed.
The grading rubric doesn't matter much — any rough score works.
why: 有效评估通常组合：确定性 code 检查客观结果 + LLM rubric 打主观维度 + 定期人工校准，评估集从真实失败里攒。
why_en: Effective evals combine deterministic code checks for objective outcomes, an LLM rubric for subjective dimensions, and periodic human calibration.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务极简单、结果二元可判，单用 code 检查就够，不必上 LLM judge。
tradeoff: 自动化评分的速度与规模 vs 人工评分的准确与信任度

termDefinitions.meaning: 用另一个大模型按 rubric 给 agent 输出打分的评估方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM-as-judge uses another large language model to score an agent's output against a rubric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述评分维度和标准的打分细则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rubric is the set of criteria and standards used to score an output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一批用来系统检验 agent 表现的任务样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An eval set is a batch of task samples used to systematically check an agent's performance.

optionMeanings: 三种评分器按各自强项组合使用
只信任人工评分
只信任 LLM judge 单一评分器
认为评分标准不重要
optionMeanings_en: Combines all three graders, each used for its own strength.
Trusts only human grading and nothing else.
Trusts only a single LLM-judge grader.
Assumes the grading rubric doesn't really matter.
optionScenarioImpacts: 客观结果、主观维度、人工校准三层都覆盖到
人工成本高、难规模化，覆盖不了大量任务
LLM judge 本身非确定性，缺了客观核对和人工校准
评分不一致，无法真实反映 agent 是否变好
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It covers objective outcomes, subjective dimensions, and human calibration all at once.
Human review is expensive and doesn't scale to cover a large task volume.
LLM-judge is itself non-deterministic and lacks objective checks and human calibration.
Inconsistent scoring can't reliably show whether the agent is actually improving.
optionDirectness: 多步骤、既有客观又有主观维度时最贴切
只有任务量极小、结果高风险时单靠人工才现实
只有任务纯主观、允许一定噪声时才可能够用
几乎不成立，任何评估都需要明确标准
optionDirectness_en: Fits best for multi-step tasks that have both objective and subjective dimensions.
Realistic only when task volume is tiny and the stakes are very high.
May be enough only for purely subjective tasks that tolerate some noise.
Almost never valid — any evaluation needs a clear standard.

scenario: 你在给一个『帮用户填退款表单』的 agent 定评估指标，要求每次交互都必须成功，不能偶尔失败。
scenario_en: You're defining an eval metric for an agent that fills out refund forms, and every single interaction must succeed — occasional failure is not acceptable.
q: 面向用户、要求「每次都稳」的场景，该看哪个指标？
q_en: For a user-facing case that must succeed every single time, which metric should you use?
options: pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功
只看单次调用的成功率
只看平均响应延迟
pass^k：k 次必须全部成功
options_en: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Just look at the single-call success rate.
Just look at average response latency.
pass^k: all k tries must succeed.
why: pass@k=1-(1-p)^k(至少1次成功)，pass^k=p^k(全部成功)。次次要稳就看 pass^k：p=99%时10步全稳概率仅约90%，逼你把单次成功率顶到99.9%+。
why_en: pass@k means at least one success in k tries; pass^k means all k succeed. User-facing reliability needs pass^k, since 99% per step compounds to ~90% over 10 steps.

termDefinitions.meaning: k 次尝试里至少成功一次的概率/指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pass@k measures the probability that at least one of k attempts succeeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: k 次尝试全部成功的概率/指标，等于单次成功率的 k 次方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: pass^k measures the probability that all k attempts succeed, equal to the single-run success rate raised to the k-th power.

optionMeanings: 选项主张：pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功。
选项主张：只看单次调用的成功率。
选项主张：只看平均响应延迟。
选项主张：pass^k：k 次必须全部成功。
optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
适合本题给出的约束。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让系统依赖「pass@k：k 次里至少 1 次成功」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只看单次调用的成功率」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只看平均响应延迟」这个前提。
会让方案围绕「pass^k：k 次必须全部成功」展开。
optionMeanings_en: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Just look at the single-call success rate.
Just look at average response latency.
pass^k: all k tries must succeed.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when the goal is to pass @k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
Only fits when this statement is true: just look at the single-call success rate.
Only fits when this statement is true: just look at average response latency.
Use when pass@k means at least one success in k tries.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It commits the design to this assumption: pass@k: at least 1 success out of k tries.
It commits the design to this assumption: Just look at the single-call success rate.
It commits the design to this assumption: Just look at average response latency.
It commits the design to this path: pass^k: all k tries must succeed.

scenario: AI 编码面试刚开始，你被放进一个已有多文件项目，类、模型和业务逻辑都已经存在。
scenario_en: At the start of an AI coding interview, you are dropped into an existing multi-file project with classes, models, and business logic already in place.
q: 面对陌生代码库，最先应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do first when facing an unfamiliar codebase?
options: 马上让 AI 根据题目生成完整实现
先重构目录结构，让代码更符合你的习惯
先快速建立代码库地图，再决定怎么提示 AI
只读 README，不打开源码
why: 已有项目里最容易踩的坑是改到现有模式之外；先扫入口、模型和状态流建地图，提示才会贴合代码库。代价是多花几分钟阅读，但能省下返工。
why_en: Orient yourself first so your prompts fit the entry points, models, and state flow that already exist, instead of drifting from established patterns.
whenOtherWins: 如果是完全空白的开放式题目，可以更快进入建模和实现，但仍要先读清需求边界。
tradeoff: 先建心智地图 vs 直接提示 AI 生成
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Task[New repo] --> Read[Read structure]
  Read --> Map[Mental map]
  Map --> Plan[Plan change]
  Plan --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
options_en: Ask the AI to generate a full implementation right away.
Refactor the directory structure to match your own habits first.
Quickly build a mental map of the codebase, then decide how to prompt the AI.
Only read the README and never open the source files.
optionMeanings: 跳过阅读，把需求直接丢给 AI 生成代码
还没搞懂用途就先按个人习惯重排目录
先扫入口、模型、接口和状态，建立心智地图
只看文档摘要，完全不打开源码文件
optionScenarioImpacts: 提示词会踩中未知的既有模式，生成代码容易和代码库冲突
破坏现有约定，还可能引入无关的改动风险
提示会贴合真实入口和状态，减少后续返工
README 通常滞后于代码，看不到真实类和调用关系
optionDirectness: 空白原型且没有既有接口时，快速生成可当探索稿
目录确实混乱且需求允许重构时，重排应放在理解之后
已有代码有模式和状态流时，先建地图再写提示
README 可当入口线索，但不能覆盖真实调用路径
optionMeanings_en: Skip reading and hand the requirement straight to the AI.
Reorganize folders to your own taste before you understand them.
Scan entry points, models, interfaces, and state to build a mental map.
Only skim the README summary and never open the source files.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Prompts will hit unknown existing patterns and clash with the codebase.
It breaks existing conventions and adds unrelated change risk.
Prompts stay grounded in real entry points and state, cutting rework.
READMEs usually lag the code, so real classes and calls stay hidden.
optionDirectness_en: Fast generation can work as an exploration draft only in a blank prototype.
If the tree is truly messy, refactor only after you understand it.
When existing patterns and state flow matter, map first and prompt second.
A README is a useful entry clue, but it cannot replace tracing real calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 项目根目录下介绍用途和用法的说明文件，内容常滞后于实际代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A README is the top-level file that explains a project's purpose, and it often lags behind the actual code.

q: 跳过代码库阅读、直接提示 AI，最容易给面试官什么信号？
q_en: If you skip codebase reading and prompt the AI right away, what signal are you most likely sending the interviewer?
options: 你会在不了解系统时就开始改代码
你很会节省时间
你已经掌握了所有业务约束
你不需要验证 AI 输出

why_en: Skipping orientation signals you might change unfamiliar production code before understanding it, which lowers how interviewers rate you.
options_en: You might start changing a system before you understand it.
You're good at saving time.
You already grasp all the business constraints.
You don't need to verify AI output.
optionMeanings: 把跳过阅读映射成未来会不了解系统就动手改代码

面试官不会把跳步骤读成效率，反而读成风险信号

跳过阅读和跳过验证是两件不同的事，此项文不对题
optionDirectness: 未读代码就动手改时，这个团队协作风险最明显

只有长期维护者才可能已知全部约束，新面试场景不适用
验证 AI 输出是后续环节，不能解释跳过取向的信号
optionMeanings_en: Map skipping reading to changing a system before understanding it.
Frame skipping reading as an efficiency win.
Assume all business constraints are already absorbed in minutes.
Assume AI output no longer needs verification either.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This is exactly the team-risk behavior interviewers watch for.
Interviewers read this as risk, not efficiency.
No one absorbs every constraint in minutes; the assumption fails.
Skipping reading and skipping verification are separate issues.
optionDirectness_en: This team-risk signal is strongest when you change code before reading it.
Skipping steps reads as efficiency only after the boundaries are clear.
Only a long-time maintainer could already know every constraint.
AI verification is a later step; it does not explain skipping orientation.

q: 把快速建立代码库心智地图的顺序排好：
q_en: Put the quick codebase orientation steps in order:
steps: 追踪数据如何流过关键类和方法
找到执行入口或请求入口
确认公共接口、状态归属和测试
先看目录结构，判断项目的大致组织方式
why: 先看整体组织，再找入口并顺着数据流深入，最后确认接口、状态和测试，能用最少时间抓住代码库骨架。
why_en: A strong orientation moves from structure to entry point to data flow, then checks interfaces, state ownership, and tests.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Tree[Project tree] --> Entry[Entry points]
  Entry --> Core[Core logic]

q: 阅读陌生项目时，为什么入口点通常是第一批要找的代码？
q_en: When reading an unfamiliar project, why are entry points usually among the first code to find?
options: 入口点里一定包含全部业务逻辑
入口点通常是全库最短、读起来最快的文件
入口点能够替代阅读测试用例
入口点标出执行起点和请求/命令进入系统的方式
why: 入口点能让你沿真实调用路径追踪对象创建和方法调用，而不是孤立读文件；代价是复杂系统里入口可能不止一个。
why_en: The entry point shows where execution begins so you can trace real calls instead of reading files in isolation.
options_en: The entry point always contains all the business logic.
The entry point is usually the shortest file in the repo, so it's the fastest read.
The entry point can replace reading the test suite.
The entry point marks where execution starts and how requests or commands enter the system.
optionMeanings: 假设入口文件本身装下了全部业务逻辑
把入口点的价值错误归因为文件短小

文件长短和是否值得优先读没有必然关系
跳过测试会让你错过一份现成的行为说明书
顺着入口能看到对象怎么被创建、方法怎么被调用
optionDirectness: 入口文件适合当起点，不适合当全量业务说明
短文件可先读，但长度不是判断入口价值的主因
测试适合确认行为，不能替代入口处的调用路径
需要顺调用链建图时，入口点是最合适的起点
optionMeanings_en: Assume the entry file itself contains all business logic.
Misattribute the entry point's value to being a short file.
Assume the entry point can substitute for checking expected behavior.
Define the entry point as where execution starts and requests enter the system.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Real systems spread logic across many classes, so this assumption misses code.
File length has no real link to whether it's worth reading first.
Skipping tests means missing a ready-made behavior spec.
Following it shows what gets instantiated and which methods get called.
optionDirectness_en: An entry file is a starting point, not a complete business spec.
A short file may be easy to read, but length is not the reason.
Tests confirm behavior, but they do not replace the entry call path.
When you need a call-chain map, the entry point is the best start.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序或服务开始执行的位置，比如 main 函数或 HTTP 请求处理器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The entry point is where a program or service begins executing, such as a main function or an HTTP request handler.

q: 哪些位置通常是陌生代码库里的高价值“代码指针”？（多选）
q_en: Which places are usually high-value code pointers in an unfamiliar codebase? (Select all that apply.)
options: 请求处理器、main 函数或 CLI 入口
承载核心业务逻辑的复杂函数
核心数据模型和类层级
随机挑一个样式文件从头读到尾
why: 入口、核心函数和数据模型能解释系统怎么启动、做什么、数据长什么样；随机文件通常解锁不了全局理解。
why_en: Entry points, core functions, and data models reveal how the system starts, what it does, and how data is shaped, far more than a random file.
options_en: Request handlers, the main function, or the CLI entry point.
The complex function that carries the core business logic.
Core data models and the class hierarchy.

q: 补全状态管理阅读目标：

q: 为什么已有测试是很好的代码库说明文档？
q_en: Why are existing tests good documentation for a codebase?

Tests explain behavior; implementation details still require source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次提交代码后自动运行构建和测试的流程。

Trust the source code and correct your understanding of the method.
Just delete the misread method.
optionMeanings: 把速度当成信任 AI 摘要的理由
把发现的差异当成可以先搁置的小事
把源码当作行为的最终判断依据
把误读的方法当成问题本身删掉
optionScenarioImpacts: 继续基于错误摘要实现，后续逻辑会跟着错
差异会被埋进后续代码里，排查成本更高
先纠正理解，再动手实现，方向才不会跑偏
方法本身没问题，问题出在对它的理解，删除解决不了
optionDirectness: AI 摘要适合产生假设，不能高于源码事实
差异只在无关路径上可暂放；当前方法行为必须纠正
当源码和摘要冲突时，应以源码修正心智模型
删除只适合确认代码无用且有测试保护时
optionMeanings_en: Treat speed as a reason to trust the AI summary.
Treat the discrepancy as something safe to set aside for now.
Treat the source code as the final judge of behavior.
Treat the misread method as the problem and delete it.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Continuing on the wrong summary lets the error propagate into your logic.
The discrepancy gets buried in later code, raising the cost to debug.
Correcting your understanding first keeps the implementation on track.
The method itself is fine; the problem is your understanding, so deleting it fixes nothing.
optionDirectness_en: AI summaries are good for hypotheses, not for overruling source code.
Set aside discrepancies only on irrelevant paths; this method must be fixed.
When source and summary conflict, update your mental model from the source.
Delete code only when it is unused and tests protect the change.

scenario: 代码库使用你不熟悉的 decorators、generics 或框架惯用法，你卡住了两分钟。
scenario_en: The codebase uses unfamiliar decorators, generics, or framework idioms, and you have been stuck for two minutes.
q: 合理的 AI 用法是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable way to use AI here?
options: 假装看懂，继续提示实现
要求 AI 删除所有陌生语法
跳过看不懂的相关文件
让 AI 解释这段语法，再回源码核对
why: 面试官更愿意看到你用 AI 快速补齐语法认知，而不是在不懂的地方硬猜；代价是要花几十秒确认解释是否准确。
why_en: Interviewers would rather see you use AI to quickly close a syntax gap than guess or stall in silence.
whenOtherWins: 如果陌生语法不在当前变更路径上，可以先标记略过，避免被旁支细节拖走。
tradeoff: 用 AI 补齐语法认知 vs 装懂硬猜或跳过
options_en: Pretend to understand and keep prompting for the implementation.
Ask the AI to delete all unfamiliar syntax.
Skip the files you don't understand.
Ask the AI to explain the syntax, then verify it against the source.
optionMeanings: 假装理解陌生语法，继续往下推进
把陌生语法当成要清除的障碍
遇到陌生语法就绕开相关文件
先让 AI 解释语法，再回源码验证解释是否准确
optionScenarioImpacts: 基于错误理解继续提示，后续实现更容易出错
删掉陌生语法可能破坏框架要求的写法
跳过的文件可能正好是本题的关键路径
几十秒内补齐认知，之后的提示词也更准确
optionDirectness: 只有完全无关的语法细节才可暂时略过，不能装懂关键路径
删除语法只在迁移框架时讨论，本题只是理解问题
陌生文件不在变更路径上时，才可以先标记略过
陌生语法卡住当前路径时，先问 AI 再核对最合适
optionMeanings_en: Pretend to understand unfamiliar syntax and keep moving.
Treat unfamiliar syntax as an obstacle to remove.
Avoid the files whenever the syntax looks unfamiliar.
Have the AI explain the syntax first, then verify against the source.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Continuing to prompt on a wrong understanding makes later implementation more error-prone.
Deleting unfamiliar syntax may break a pattern the framework requires.
The skipped file might be exactly the key path for this task.
Closing the gap in seconds makes later prompts more accurate too.
optionDirectness_en: Only irrelevant syntax can be postponed; do not fake a key-path gap.
Removing syntax is a migration discussion; this is an understanding gap.
Mark a file to skip only when it is outside the change path.
When syntax blocks the current path, ask AI, then verify.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给类或方法附加额外行为的一种语法标记，常见于 Python、TypeScript 等语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A decorator is syntax that attaches extra behavior to a class or method, common in languages like Python and TypeScript.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让类型作为参数传入的语言特性，用来写可复用的类型安全代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Generics let a type be passed in as a parameter, enabling reusable, type-safe code.

scenario: 面试刚开始你感到时钟压力，很想马上开始生成代码。
scenario_en: At the start of the interview, you feel time pressure and want to start generating code immediately.
q: 最好的沟通方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to communicate?
options: 说明在确认理解代码库，并边读边叙述发现
沉默地读五分钟，不说明在看什么
先让 AI 生成，出错再回头查
直接说不需要看代码
why: 短暂取向是合理的，但要边读边叙述让面试官听到你在形成有效模型；代价是要多说几句，但换来的是面试官的信任。
why_en: Orienting briefly is expected, but narrating what you find keeps the interviewer confident you're building a real model.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求立刻修一个极小 bug，可以先定位那条路径，同时保持最小必要取向。
tradeoff: 边读边叙述 vs 沉默阅读或跳过取向
options_en: Say you're confirming your understanding first, and narrate findings as you read.
Read silently for five minutes without narrating anything.
Let the AI generate code first and debug whatever errors show up.
Tell the interviewer you don't need to look at the code.
optionMeanings: 一边确认理解、一边把发现说给面试官听
选择沉默地进行取向，不对外输出任何信息
把取向阶段跳过，直接进入生成再纠错
直接否定取向这一步骤的必要性
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官能听到你在建立正确的模型，安心得多
面试官只看到停滞，猜不到你在做什么
报错才发现问题，比先取向浪费更多时间
这句话本身就会被面试官当成风险信号
optionDirectness: 边读边叙述适合有时间压力但仍需取向的面试开场
沉默只适合几秒钟查找，不适合持续取向
先生成适合已掌握代码路径后的小改动，不适合开场
不看代码只适合纯白板题，已有项目里会丢上下文
optionMeanings_en: Confirm your understanding out loud while narrating findings.
Choose to orient silently, saying nothing out loud.
Skip orientation and jump straight to generate-then-debug.
Flatly deny that orientation is necessary at all.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer hears you building the right model and feels reassured.
The interviewer just sees a stall and can't tell what you're doing.
Discovering the problem via errors costs more time than orienting first would have.
That statement itself reads as a risk signal to the interviewer.
optionDirectness_en: Narrate while reading when time is tight but orientation is still needed.
Silence works for a few seconds of lookup, not sustained orientation.
Generate first only for small edits after the code path is known.
Skipping code fits pure whiteboard tasks, not existing-project interviews.

q: 补全有效取向叙述：
q_en: Complete an effective orientation narration:
text: 取向时要说出你正在学到的具体结构，例如“Board 使用 {{二维网格}} 的 Cell，每个 Cell 跟踪自己的{{状态}}和{{邻居}}。”
why: 具体观察让取向阶段显得有产出，也让面试官相信你会基于真实结构做决策。
why_en: Concrete narration makes orientation productive and shows your decisions are grounded in the code.

q: 如果你假设 AI 已经理解整个代码库，可能出现哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: If you assume the AI already understands the whole codebase, what problems may happen? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 调用不存在或不该用的接口
AI 复用和项目模式冲突的抽象
AI 忽略关键副作用
AI 自动获得面试官的隐含偏好
why: AI 常缺少完整上下文，你需要把真实类名、接口和约束放进提示，并检查输出有没有偏离；最后一项不成立，偏好不会被自动感知。
why_en: Because the AI may lack full codebase context, you must supply real interfaces and constraints and check its output for drift.
options_en: The AI calls interfaces that don't exist or shouldn't be used.
The AI reuses abstractions that conflict with the project's patterns.
The AI overlooks important side effects.
The AI automatically picks up the interviewer's unstated preferences.
optionMeanings: 假设 AI 完全清楚项目里有哪些真实接口
假设 AI 生成的抽象自然会贴合项目风格
假设 AI 能看到所有隐藏的副作用
假设 AI 能感知面试官没说出口的偏好
optionScenarioImpacts: AI 会编出看似合理但项目里根本不存在的方法
生成的代码会和现有模式冲突，增加返工
副作用被忽略后，bug 往往在别处才暴露
面试官的偏好不会通过代码库自动传给 AI
optionDirectness: AI 不知道真实接口时，最容易编出不存在的调用
项目已有模式强时，通用抽象最容易冲突
副作用藏在状态更新或 I/O 里时，AI 最容易漏
偏好需要面试官说出来，不能从代码库自动推断
optionMeanings_en: Assume the AI fully knows every real interface in the project.
Assume AI-generated abstractions naturally match the project's style.
Assume the AI can see every hidden side effect.
Assume the AI can sense the interviewer's unstated preferences.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The AI invents methods that sound plausible but don't exist in the project.
Generated code clashes with existing patterns, adding rework.
Ignored side effects mean bugs surface somewhere else later.
Interviewer preferences don't propagate to the AI through the codebase.
optionDirectness_en: When AI lacks real interfaces, it most often invents calls.
Generic abstractions clash most when the project has strong patterns.
AI misses side effects most when they hide in state updates or I/O.
Preferences must be stated by the interviewer, not inferred from code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序对外暴露、供调用的接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the interface a program exposes for other code to call.

q: AI 编码面试里的沟通为什么比传统面试更难？
q_en: Why is communication in an AI coding interview harder than in a traditional interview?
options: 因为必须背诵固定提示词
因为面试官看不到你的屏幕
因为你同时要对 AI 和对面试官两条线沟通
因为 AI 输出的内容不允许被讨论
why: 决定性因素是你要同时维持两条沟通线——AI 和面试官；只顾 AI 会让面试官读不到你的判断过程。
why_en: AI coding interviews are harder to communicate through because you must run two conversations at once, with the AI and with the interviewer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Candidate[Candidate] --> Interviewer[Interviewer]
  Candidate --> AI[AI tool]
  AI --> Candidate
  Candidate --> Code[Codebase]
  Code --> Interviewer
options_en: Because you have to recite a fixed set of prompts.
Because the interviewer can't see your screen.
Because you have to communicate on two channels at once, to the AI and to the interviewer.
Because AI output is off-limits for discussion.
optionMeanings: 把沟通难度归因为背模板提示词。
假设面试官看不到你的操作过程。
把沟通难度归因为要同时维护两条对话线。
假设 AI 输出是不能讨论的黑箱。
optionScenarioImpacts: 背模板不能应对具体代码上下文，帮不上真实沟通。
事实相反：面试官能看到提示和输出，只是看不到你的思路。
点出了两条线同时维护才是难度来源。
误解了规则：解释 AI 输出正是沟通该做的事。
optionDirectness: 背诵不是沟通技巧，遇到没背过的场景就会露馅。
前提有误：不是看不到屏幕，是看不到你的思路。
这条线索决定了你要主动说出思路，而不是只操作 AI。
前提有误：讨论 AI 输出正是加分项，不是禁区。
optionMeanings_en: This blames the difficulty on reciting template prompts.
This assumes the interviewer can't see what you're doing.
This blames the difficulty on maintaining two conversation threads at once.
This assumes AI output is a black box you can't discuss.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Reciting a template doesn't handle real code context, so it doesn't help.
The opposite is true: the interviewer sees the prompts and output, just not your thinking.
It names the real source of difficulty: keeping two channels alive at once.
It misreads the rules: explaining AI output is exactly what good communication looks like.
optionDirectness_en: Reciting isn't a communication skill, it breaks down outside the memorized case.
Wrong premise: it's not the screen that's hidden, it's your thought process.
This is the actual reason you must voice your thinking, not just operate the AI.
Wrong premise: discussing AI output is a plus signal, not off-limits.

scenario: 你准备让 AI 给 Order 类实现输入校验。
scenario_en: You are about to ask the AI to add input validation to the Order class.
q: 提示 AI 前，最应该先对面试官说什么？
q_en: Before prompting the AI, what should you say to the interviewer first?
options: “我要给 Order 加校验，先查空字段和数量范围。”
“我先让 AI 随便试着写写看，看它怎么处理。”
“等它写完了，我再跟你解释我的思路。”
“不说什么，先直接开始打字提示它。”
why: 决定性约束是面试官只能看到提示和输出、看不到你的思路；先说意图能把后续内容放进上下文。
why_en: State your intent before prompting so the interviewer can follow your plan instead of just watching you type.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是改一个显而易见的一行 typo，可以边改边说一句，不需要完整铺陈。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Intent[State intent] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Explain[Explain next step]
options_en: I'm going to add validation to Order, checking null fields and quantity range first.
I'll just let the AI take a random first pass and see what it does.
I'll wait until it's done, then explain my thinking to you.
I won't say anything, I'll just start typing the prompt.
tradeoff: 提示前先说明意图 vs 直接开始打字
optionMeanings: 先公开具体校验范围的意图声明。
把决策权交给 AI 随机尝试。
把说明推迟到 AI 写完之后。
完全跳过意图声明。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官能提前知道校验范围，跟上后续每一步。
面试官只能等结果出来才知道你在做什么。
面试官全程只能看操作，事后才补上下文。
面试官从头到尾看不到你的判断依据。
optionDirectness: 三秒声明换来面试官全程可跟随的上下文。
只适合改一行显而易见的 typo，不适合完整功能。
输出量大时可以事后补充细节，但不能替代提示前的意图声明。
只在改动极小、几乎不需要解释时才勉强够用。
optionMeanings_en: Stating the specific validation scope up front.
Handing the decision to a random first AI attempt.
Delaying the explanation until after the AI finishes.
Skipping the intent statement entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer knows the validation scope ahead of time and can follow each step.
The interviewer only learns what you're doing once the result appears.
The interviewer can only watch actions and gets context after the fact.
The interviewer never sees your reasoning at any point.
optionDirectness_en: A three-second statement buys context the interviewer can follow the whole way.
Fine for an obvious one-line typo fix, not for a full feature.
Useful when output is large, but it can't replace stating intent before prompting.
Barely acceptable only when the change is tiny and needs no explanation.

q: 把推荐的 AI 编码沟通节奏排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the recommended AI coding communication rhythm in the correct order:
steps: 审阅 AI 输出并说出是否符合预期
继续下一步或重新提示
说明你接下来要做什么
向 AI 发出具体提示
why: 有效节奏是先声明意图，再提示 AI，然后公开审阅结果，最后决定继续或修正。
why_en: The useful rhythm is state intent, prompt the AI, review aloud, then continue or correct course.
tradeoff: 先声明意图再行动 vs 先动手后解释
diagram:
flowchart LR
  SayPlan[Say plan] --> AskAI[Ask AI]
  AskAI --> Narrate[Narrate wait]
  Narrate --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Next[State next move]

q: AI 生成代码后，哪些口头反馈是好信号？（多选）
q_en: After the AI generates code, which spoken reactions are good signals? (Select all that apply.)
options: “AI 写了，所以肯定对。”
“这符合我的目标，它检查了 null 字段和数量。”
“它用了异常，但项目里用 error object，我会重新提示。”
“这段很多，我先读一遍确认。”
why: 这些反馈展示你在验证、纠偏和主动审查；盲目接受 AI 输出是负面信号。
why_en: Good narration shows that you verify, correct, and review AI output rather than accepting it blindly.
options_en: The AI wrote it, so it must be correct.
This matches my goal, it checks for null fields and validates quantity.
It used exceptions, but this codebase uses error objects, so I'll reprompt.
This is a lot of code, let me read through it first to confirm.
optionMeanings: 把结果好坏归因于 AI 本身而非你的核验。
确认输出是否命中你已声明的校验目标。
发现风格不符并主动要求重新生成。
承认大段输出需要先读完再判断。
optionScenarioImpacts: 跳过核验，面试官会认为你在盲目接受。
证明你在核对具体校验点，不是走过场。
展示你能发现代码库风格冲突并纠偏。
展示你不会因为代码量大就跳过审阅。
optionDirectness: 唯一站不住脚的判断：输出正确与否不取决于是谁写的。
点名具体校验点的确认，是可评估的核验信号。
发现风格冲突并重提示，是纠偏能力的直接证据。
承认需要时间审阅，是诚实且专业的信号。
optionMeanings_en: Attributing correctness to the AI itself rather than your own verification.
Confirming the output hits the validation goal you stated.
Spotting a style mismatch and asking for a reprompt.
Admitting a large output needs a read-through before judgment.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Skipping verification makes the interviewer think you accept output blindly.
It proves you're checking specific validation points, not just going through motions.
It shows you can catch a codebase style conflict and correct it.
It shows you won't skip review just because the output is long.
optionDirectness_en: The one claim that doesn't hold up: correctness doesn't depend on who wrote it.
Naming a specific check point is evaluable verification.
Catching a style conflict and reprompting is direct evidence of self-correction.
Admitting you need time to review is an honest, professional signal.

q: AI 编码面试里，面试官更应该被当成什么角色？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what role should you treat the interviewer as?
options: 只看最终结果、不参与过程的考官
不能被打扰的旁观者
可以被 AI 取代的角色
和你一起结对写代码的伙伴
why: AI 编码面试更像结对编程，面试官需要持续听到你的意图、判断和修正才能评估你。
why_en: Treat the interviewer like a pair partner who needs to keep hearing your intent, judgment, and corrections.
options_en: An examiner who only looks at the final result and ignores the process.
A bystander you should not interrupt.
A role the AI can substitute for.
A pair-programming partner working alongside you.
tradeoff: 把面试官当结对伙伴持续沟通 vs 当考官只交最终结果
optionMeanings: 把评估窗口收窄成只看结果的模型。
把面试官当成不该打断的旁观者。
误以为讲清楚给 AI 听就够了。
把面试官当成需要持续同步的搭档。
optionScenarioImpacts: 你会倾向沉默写代码，到最后才展示成果。
你会不敢开口说思路，错过评估窗口。
面试官听到的是你和 AI 的对话，不是你的判断。
你会持续讲意图、判断和修正，让评估全程可见。
optionDirectness: 只适合纯笔试式评审，不适合边讲边写的面试形式。
只在你完全不需要任何反馈的极端场景下才成立。
把判断权交给 AI，面试官学不到你的思路。
结对式沟通让面试官全程跟上你的意图和修正。
optionMeanings_en: This narrows the evaluation window to a results-only model.
This treats the interviewer as a bystander you shouldn't interrupt.
This mistakenly assumes talking to the AI is communication enough.
This treats the interviewer as a partner who needs constant syncing.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You'd tend to code silently and only reveal the result at the end.
You'd hesitate to voice your thinking and lose the evaluation window.
The interviewer hears your conversation with the AI, not your judgment.
You keep narrating intent, judgment, and corrections so evaluation stays visible.
optionDirectness_en: Fits a pure written exam, not a talk-while-you-build interview.
Only holds in the extreme case where no feedback is ever needed.
Handing judgment to the AI means the interviewer learns nothing about you.
Pair-style communication keeps the interviewer following your intent and fixes throughout.

q: 补全 AI 编码面试的推荐沟通节奏：
q_en: Complete the recommended communication rhythm for an AI coding interview:
text: 有效沟通节奏是：先说明{{意图}}，再提示 AI，接着公开{{审阅输出}}，最后说明{{下一步}}。
why: 这个节奏让面试官持续看到你在做决策，而不是把判断外包给 AI。
why_en: This rhythm keeps the interviewer aware that you are making the decisions, not outsourcing judgment to the AI.

scenario: AI 在结构化平台里响应很慢，屏幕上出现加载动画，你在等待生成结果。
scenario_en: The AI is slow to respond in a structured platform, and you are waiting on a loading spinner.
q: AI 还在生成时，这段等待时间最好怎么用？
q_en: While the AI is still generating, how should you best use the waiting time?
options: 沉默盯着加载动画
打开无关网页放松一下
向面试官讲你的方案、预期输出或边界条件
不断重复提交同一个提示

scenario: 你需要安静想十几秒，确认当前算法能否覆盖边界情况。
scenario_en: You need to think quietly for ten or so seconds to confirm whether the current algorithm covers edge cases.
q: 这时最合适的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this moment?
options: 直接沉默，让面试官自己猜
立刻让 AI 生成新方案
说“我想一下这个边界情况”，然后短暂停顿
跳过边界情况，先往下写
why: 一句框定语能把沉默变成可理解的思考时间，避免面试官误以为你卡住或走神。
why_en: A short framing sentence turns silence into an understandable thinking pause instead of ambiguous dead air.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有可运行测试，可以边说边跑测试，用结果帮助思考。
options_en: Go silent and let the interviewer guess what's happening.
Immediately have the AI generate a new approach.
Say 'let me think about this edge case' and pause briefly.
Skip the edge case and keep moving.
tradeoff: 一句框定语再沉默 vs 直接沉默不说明
optionMeanings: 把思考时间处理成无声的空白。
用生成新方案代替独立思考的时间。
用一句框定语把沉默变成可理解的停顿。
跳过边界情况本身，回避而非思考。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官分不清你是在想、卡住还是走神。
还没想清楚就重新生成，容易越改越乱。
面试官清楚知道这是正常思考停顿。
边界情况被跳过，后续可能因未覆盖而出错。
optionDirectness: 只在你已经框定过一次、马上要继续时才勉强不需要重复。
只有在你已经确定当前方案整体不可行时才该重来。
几秒钟的框定语几乎零成本换来清晰的沉默。
只在边界情况明显不影响正确性时才能跳过。
optionMeanings_en: Treating thinking time as silent dead air.
Substituting a new generation for actual independent thought.
Using a framing sentence to make silence understandable.
Skipping the edge case itself, avoiding rather than thinking.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer can't tell if you're thinking, stuck, or distracted.
Regenerating before you've thought it through risks making things messier.
The interviewer clearly knows this is a normal thinking pause.
The edge case gets skipped and may surface as a bug later.
optionDirectness_en: Barely skippable only right after you've already framed a pause once.
Only worth it once you've confirmed the whole approach is unworkable.
A few seconds of framing buys clear silence at almost no cost.
Only skippable when the edge case clearly doesn't affect correctness.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现搜索函数，需要让面试官清楚你选的是 BFS，而不是把决策交给 AI。
scenario_en: You want the AI to implement a search function, and the interviewer needs to know you chose BFS rather than handing the decision to the AI.
q: 哪组“口头说明 + 提示”最能体现你在主导决策？
q_en: Which pair of spoken framing and prompt best shows that you are driving the decision?
options: 说明：我看看 AI 会怎么处理。提示：“solve this”
说明：用 BFS 找最短路径。提示：在 Grid 上实现 BFS 并返回坐标路径。
说明：不说明。提示：“make it work”
说明：AI 应该知道怎么做。提示：“写一个复杂的解法”
why: 先公开你的策略，再把同一策略写进提示，能让 AI 输出贴合方案，同时向面试官展示你在做决策。
why_en: State your strategy out loud and put the same strategy in the prompt so the AI executes your decision, not its own.
whenOtherWins: 如果算法选择还没确定，可以先说明你在比较 BFS、DFS 或 Dijkstra，再决定后提示。
options_en: Framing: let's see what the AI does. Prompt: 'solve this.'
Framing: I'll use BFS for the shortest path. Prompt: implement BFS on Grid and return the coordinate path.
Framing: none. Prompt: 'make it work.'
Framing: the AI should already know. Prompt: 'write a complex solution.'
tradeoff: 先说策略再写进提示 vs 不说明直接丢给 AI 决定
optionMeanings: 用被动语气把决策权交给 AI 自行判断。
先声明算法选择，再把同一约束写进提示。
完全不给上下文，只留一句模糊指令。
假设 AI 会自己猜到你要的复杂方案。
optionScenarioImpacts: AI 可能选出你无法在面试里讲清楚的方案。
AI 输出直接落在 BFS 实现上，面试官也看到你的判断。
AI 可能选任意算法，偏离你原本的意图。
AI 缺少约束，产出方向和你预期脱节的风险很高。
optionDirectness: 只有在你确实还没想清楚算法、想先看 AI 建议时才该用，且要说明这是在探索。
策略在口头和提示里保持一致，是这类场景的标准做法。
空指令几乎总会导致返工，任何场景都不推荐。
“复杂解法”不是可执行约束，AI 无法据此写出你要的代码。
optionMeanings_en: Using a passive framing that hands the decision to the AI.
Stating the algorithm choice first, then encoding the same constraint in the prompt.
Giving no context at all, just one vague instruction.
Assuming the AI will guess the complex solution you want.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The AI may pick an approach you can't defend clearly in the interview.
The AI's output lands directly on a BFS implementation, and the interviewer sees your judgment.
The AI might pick any algorithm, drifting from your actual intent.
With no constraint, the AI's output direction is likely to miss what you expected.
optionDirectness_en: Only appropriate when you're genuinely still exploring and say so explicitly.
Keeping strategy consistent between speech and prompt is the standard move here.
An empty instruction almost always causes rework, never recommended.
'A complex solution' isn't an executable constraint the AI can build from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层从起点向外扩展，用于无权图找最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, explores a graph layer by layer from the start node and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索，沿一条路径尽量往前探索，走到底再回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, explores as far as possible along one path before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权图最短路径的经典算法，每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's Algorithm finds shortest paths in a weighted graph by always expanding the lowest-known-cost node next.

q: 事后解释你刚让 AI 做了什么，为什么弱于提示前先说明？
q_en: Why is explaining what you just asked the AI to do weaker than stating it before prompting?
options: 事后解释会让 AI 生成变慢
事后解释在大多数面试规则里是被禁止的
两者对面试官来说完全一样
事前说明让面试官实时看到计划，而不是事后倒推
why: 面试评估的是过程控制；事前说明能让你的意图在行动发生的同时就被看到。
why_en: Interviews evaluate process control, and explaining before you act makes your intent visible in real time.
options_en: Explaining after the fact makes the AI generate more slowly.
Explaining after the fact is against the rules in most interviews.
The two approaches are exactly the same to the interviewer.
Explaining beforehand lets the interviewer see your plan in real time, instead of reconstructing it afterward.
optionMeanings: 把叙述时机和 AI 生成速度错误挂钩。
把叙述时机误判为规则问题。
认为叙述时机不影响面试官的理解。
把叙述时机和可见性直接挂钩。
optionScenarioImpacts: 叙述发生在 AI 生成之外，不影响生成速度。
大多数面试并不禁止事后解释，只是效果更弱。
事后解释让面试官只能靠回忆倒推你的判断过程。
面试官能在行动发生的同时看到你的意图，评估更直接。
optionDirectness: 叙述和生成速度是两条独立的机制，不存在因果。
多数场景下允许事后解释，只是信号强度更弱，不是被禁止。
事前和事后的可见性差异正是这题的关键，不能等同。
实时可见性是面试评估过程控制能力的核心依据。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly linking narration timing to AI generation speed.
Mistaking narration timing for a rule violation.
Assuming narration timing doesn't affect the interviewer's understanding.
Directly linking narration timing to visibility.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Narration happens outside AI generation, so it doesn't affect speed.
Most interviews don't forbid after-the-fact explanation, it's just a weaker signal.
After-the-fact explanation forces the interviewer to reconstruct your judgment from memory.
The interviewer sees your intent as the action happens, making evaluation more direct.
optionDirectness_en: Narration and generation speed are unrelated mechanisms with no causal link.
Most settings allow after-the-fact explanation, it's just a weaker signal, not forbidden.
The before-versus-after visibility gap is exactly the point of this question, not equal.
Real-time visibility is the core basis for evaluating process control in an interview.

scenario: AI 一次性输出了一大段代码，你还没有读完确认。
scenario_en: The AI produced a large block of code all at once, and you have not finished reviewing it.
q: 这时最好的口头反馈是什么？
q_en: What is the best spoken response here?
options: “应该可以，继续下一步。”
“我不需要看，直接用。”
“这段挺长，我先读一遍确认它符合计划。”
“面试官你帮我读一下吧。”
why: 承认需要审阅是好信号，说明你不会因为代码看起来完整就直接接受。
why_en: Saying you need to review a large output shows you won't accept complete-looking code blindly.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出只是一行你能立刻确认的改动，可以快速说明确认点后继续。
options_en: 'Looks fine, let's move on.'
'I don't need to look, I'll just use it.'
'This is a lot, let me read through it to confirm it matches the plan.'
'Can you read through this for me instead?'
tradeoff: 承认需要审阅 vs 假设输出直接可信
optionMeanings: 跳过审阅，假设长输出自动正确。
彻底放弃审阅这一步。
承认输出量大，需要先读完再判断。
把审阅责任转移给面试官。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官会认为你在盲目接受 AI 输出。
隐藏的 bug 会在后续测试或追问时暴露。
把审阅动作摆到明面上，面试官看得到你的核验习惯。
审阅本该是候选人的职责，转移会显得缺乏主导。
optionDirectness: 只有输出极短、你已确认过风格时才勉强够快。
任何场景都不该完全跳过审阅。
输出量越大，先声明再审阅的价值越高。
面试官的角色是评估者，而非代你审阅代码。
optionMeanings_en: Skipping review and assuming a long output is automatically correct.
Abandoning the review step entirely.
Admitting the output is large and needs a read-through first.
Shifting review responsibility onto the interviewer.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer thinks you're accepting AI output blindly.
Hidden bugs surface later during testing or follow-up questions.
It puts your verification habit on display for the interviewer to see.
Review is the candidate's job — shifting it looks like a lack of ownership.
optionDirectness_en: Barely fast enough only when the output is tiny and style is already confirmed.
Skipping review entirely is never appropriate.
The bigger the output, the more value there is in stating you'll review it first.
The interviewer's role is to evaluate, not to review code on your behalf.

q: 补全沟通节奏的练习方法：
q_en: Complete the practice method for building communication rhythm:
text: 用 AI 解题时录下自己，回看哪里{{沉默太久}}、哪里{{过度叙述}}，几次练习后会形成自然节奏。
why: 沟通节奏很难只靠阅读形成，录像回放能立刻暴露盲点。
why_en: Recording practice sessions exposes long silences and over-narration so you can tune your rhythm.

q: 编码过程中，哪句话属于过度叙述而非有用沟通？
q_en: During coding, which sentence is over-narration rather than useful communication?
options: “我现在要输入 function 这个单词。”
“我接下来实现 search 函数。”
“这段输出用了错误的错误处理风格，我会重提示。”
“我需要想一下这个边界情况。”
why: 有用沟通聚焦决策和状态，机械播报键盘动作只会消耗时间和注意力。
why_en: Useful narration covers decisions and state, while keystroke-level commentary just wastes time and attention.
options_en: 'I'm about to type the word function now.'
'I'm going to implement the search function next.'
'This output uses the wrong error-handling style, I'll reprompt it.'
'I need to think about this edge case for a second.'
tradeoff: 播报决策和状态 vs 播报键盘动作
optionMeanings: 把叙述粒度细到单个单词的输入动作。
叙述即将开始的实现步骤，属于决策级信息。
叙述发现的风格问题和纠偏动作。
叙述即将进行的思考过程。
optionScenarioImpacts: 纯键盘播报不携带任何判断信息，只会拖慢节奏。
让面试官提前知道你在做什么，属于有效同步。
展示你能发现代码库风格冲突并主动纠正。
让沉默变成可理解的思考停顿。
optionDirectness: 唯一不该采用的叙述粒度，任何场景都不该照做。
步骤级叙述几乎总是值得说的决策信息。
风格冲突是典型的应该主动指出的偏差。
思考停顿前的框定语几乎零成本。
optionMeanings_en: Narrating down to the act of typing a single word.
Narrating an upcoming implementation step, which is decision-level information.
Narrating a discovered style issue and the correction action.
Narrating an upcoming thinking process.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Pure keystroke commentary carries no judgment and just slows the pace.
It lets the interviewer know ahead of time what you're doing, which is useful syncing.
It shows you can catch a codebase style conflict and correct it proactively.
It turns silence into an understandable thinking pause.
optionDirectness_en: The one narration granularity to never use, in any scenario.
Step-level narration is almost always worth saying.
A style conflict is a textbook case worth flagging proactively.
A framing sentence before a thinking pause costs almost nothing.

q: 出问题时，哪些沟通动作能把局面拉回可评估状态？（多选）
q_en: When something goes wrong, which communication moves bring the situation back into an evaluable state? (Select all that apply.)
options: 说明当前错误或阻塞点
给出你对根因的判断
解释为什么要改变方向
静默删除大量代码，不作说明
why: 问题本身不可怕，可怕的是面试官看不到你如何诊断和调整。
why_en: When things go wrong, visible diagnosis and explicit adjustment matter more than hiding the struggle.
options_en: Name the current error or blocker.
State your judgment about the root cause.
Explain why you're changing direction.
Silently delete a large chunk of code without explanation.
optionMeanings: 把当前卡点说清楚。
给出你对问题根因的判断。
解释转向背后的理由。
用静默删除代替任何说明。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官知道你在诊断哪个具体问题。
面试官能评估你的诊断能力，而不只是结果。
面试官看到的是主动调整，而非随意重来。
面试官看到的是混乱的删改，无法判断你的判断依据。
optionDirectness: 问题定位是让面试官重新跟上进度的第一步。
根因判断把“出了问题”升级成“我知道为什么”。
转向原因把重写和乱改区分开来。
静默删除是这类场景里唯一该避免的动作。
optionMeanings_en: Stating the current blocker clearly.
Giving your judgment about the root cause.
Explaining the reasoning behind a pivot.
Using silent deletion instead of any explanation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer knows exactly which problem you're diagnosing.
The interviewer can evaluate your diagnostic ability, not just the outcome.
The interviewer sees a deliberate adjustment, not a random restart.
The interviewer sees confused edits with no visible reasoning behind them.
optionDirectness_en: Naming the problem is the first step to getting the interviewer back up to speed.
A root-cause judgment upgrades 'something's wrong' to 'I know why.'
The pivot reason separates a deliberate rewrite from random flailing.
Silent deletion is the one action to avoid in this scenario.

scenario: 面试官已经看过很多候选人做同一道题，熟悉常见的死路在哪里。
scenario_en: The interviewer has seen many candidates solve this same problem and knows the common dead ends.
q: 你走进死路时，最应该向面试官展示什么？
q_en: When you hit a dead end, what should you most show the interviewer?
options: 永远不承认自己走错方向
继续微调错误方向直到时间用完
把责任推给 AI 的建议
尽快识别死路、说明原因并干净转向
why: 面试官不指望你避开所有死路，但会评估你发现和恢复的速度。
why_en: Interviewers don't expect you to avoid every dead end, but they do evaluate how fast you notice and recover.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是实现细节的小错，先局部修正即可；只有方向性错误才需要明确转向。
options_en: Never admit you went the wrong way.
Keep tweaking the wrong direction until time runs out.
Blame the AI's suggestion for the wrong turn.
Recognize the dead end quickly, explain why, and pivot cleanly.
tradeoff: 快速识别并转向 vs 硬撑原方向到超时
optionMeanings: 用否认掩盖已经发生的方向错误。
把时间都花在修补根本方向错误上。
把方向判断的责任转嫁给 AI。
把识别、解释、转向三步都做完整。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官很快能看穿，可信度反而下降。
时间耗尽却没有可用方案，是最差结果之一。
决策始终是你做的，责任转嫁站不住脚。
面试官评估的正是发现和恢复问题的速度。
optionDirectness: 否认几乎从不奏效，面试官见过太多类似情况。
只有在剩余时间极少、别无选择时才勉强合理。
选择权在你手里，AI 建议不能替你承担判断责任。
面试官不指望零失误，但会评估恢复速度。
optionMeanings_en: Using denial to cover up a direction error that already happened.
Spending all remaining time patching a fundamentally wrong direction.
Shifting the direction decision's responsibility onto the AI.
Completing all three steps: recognize, explain, and pivot.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer sees through it quickly and credibility drops.
Time runs out with no working solution, one of the worst outcomes.
The decision was always yours, so blame-shifting doesn't hold up.
This is exactly what the interviewer evaluates: how fast you notice and recover.
optionDirectness_en: Denial almost never works, interviewers have seen this pattern many times.
Barely reasonable only when time is nearly out and there's no alternative.
The choice was yours; an AI suggestion can't carry your judgment responsibility.
Interviewers don't expect zero errors, but they do evaluate recovery speed.

q: 把“AI 输出不符合项目风格”后的沟通链排好：
q_en: Put the communication chain in order after the AI output does not match the project style:
steps: 重新提示 AI 使用项目现有错误处理风格
说明你观察到它用了异常而项目用 error object
继续前先读生成的改动是否符合预期
指出这会和代码库模式冲突
why: 先说观察，再说影响，然后重定向 AI，最后审阅结果，能完整展示控制力。
why_en: The correction loop is observe, explain impact, reprompt with constraints, then review the revised output.
tradeoff: 观察+影响+重定向+复核的完整闭环 vs 直接静默重写
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BadStyle[Output off style] --> Say[Name mismatch]
  Say --> Reprompt[Reprompt with local pattern]
  Reprompt --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Test[Run tests]
  Test --> Explain[Explain outcome]

q: AI coding 面试进入执行阶段后，面试官最常评估的不是你打字多快，而是什么？
q_en: Once an AI coding interview reaches execution, what are interviewers really evaluating?
options: 你是否持续提示、审阅并掌控 AI 的输出
你是否让 AI 独自决定架构方案
你是否尽量避免运行和验证代码
你是否写出全场最长的一段提示
options_en: Whether you keep prompting, reviewing, and steering the AI's output.
Whether you let the AI decide the architecture entirely on its own.
Whether you avoid running and verifying the code.
Whether you write the single longest prompt in the room.
why: 执行阶段考核的是你能否按计划驱动 AI、审阅它的产出并持续掌控方向，而不是把决策权交给模型。
why_en: During execution, interviewers watch whether you keep driving, reviewing, and steering the AI instead of handing it the decisions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Run[Run code]
  Run --> Adjust[Adjust]
  Adjust --> Prompt
optionMeanings: 持续提示、审阅、掌控的驾驶循环。
把架构决策整体让给 AI 的做法。
跳过运行验证、直接往下写的做法。
用提示长度而非内容质量取胜的做法。
optionScenarioImpacts: 方向始终由你把关，AI 只负责实现细节。
面试官看不到你的判断，只看到 AI 的判断。
错误会在多步之后才暴露，难以定位。
提示变长不等于约束更清楚，反而更难读。
optionDirectness: 命中评分点：驱动+审阅+掌控就是执行阶段的核心。
方向错：决策权旁落，面试官学不到你的判断。
步骤缺：跳过验证不是省时间，是风险来源。
粒度错：长度不是评分维度，内容精确度才是。
optionMeanings_en: The loop of prompting, reviewing, and steering.
Handing the whole architecture decision to the AI.
Skipping run-time verification and pushing ahead anyway.
Winning on prompt length instead of prompt quality.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Direction stays under your control while the AI handles implementation.
The interviewer sees the AI’s judgment, not yours.
Errors surface many steps later and are harder to trace.
A longer prompt does not mean clearer constraints — it gets harder to read.

q: 写 AI 提示时，粒度的“甜点区”具体是什么？

options: 只给原始题目，让 AI 自己决定所有方案

options_en: Hand over the raw problem and let the AI pick the whole approach.

Dictate variable names and formatting line by line.
Skip the AI entirely.
why: 太泛会让 AI 接管决策，太细又变成隔着 AI 手写代码；合适粒度是你定策略、AI 写实现。
why_en: The sweet spot is stating the what and how clearly while letting the AI handle syntax and idiomatic implementation.
tradeoff: 约束够用 vs 微管理成本 —— 提示太泛让 AI 接管决策，提示太细就变成隔着 AI 手写代码。
optionMeanings: 把方案决策权完全交给 AI 的提示风格。
只锁定方案和约束、放开语法细节的提示风格。

完全跳过 AI 辅助的极端选项。

打字提示的时间接近手打代码，等于隔着 AI 抄写。
放弃了 AI 能带来的速度优势，回到纯手写节奏。
optionDirectness: 粒度错：太粗，决策权跑到 AI 手里。
命中甜点区：约束到方案层，放开到语法层。

optionMeanings_en: A prompt style that hands the whole decision to the AI.
A prompt style that fixes the approach but leaves syntax open.
A prompt style that dictates every line of implementation.
The extreme option of skipping AI assistance altogether.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The AI may pick an approach you cannot defend clearly in the interview.
The AI’s output fits your plan while saving line-by-line typing time.
Typing the prompt takes about as long as typing the code yourself.
You give up the speed advantage the AI could have offered.
optionDirectness_en: Wrong granularity: too broad, control shifts to the AI.
Hits the sweet spot: approach fixed, syntax left open.
Wrong granularity: too narrow, you become a typing proxy.
Wrong scope: this drops the tool instead of tuning granularity.

scenario: 你要实现前缀搜索，并已经决定使用 trie（前缀树），每个节点要保存字符和是否为单词结尾。
scenario_en: You need prefix search and have already chosen a trie, where each node stores a character and an end-of-word flag.
q: 哪条提示最符合推荐的提示粒度？
q_en: Which prompt best matches the recommended level of granularity?
options: 不给任何设计信息，只说一句“写点代码把前缀搜索功能实现掉，随便怎么做”
trie 支持 insert 和 prefix search，节点存 character、children、isEndOfWord
先声明一个变量 a，再写好 for 循环，然后要求 AI 逐行照我口述的语句往下写
需求只是新增一个前缀搜索方法，却要求 AI 顺带把整个项目重写成更好的分层架构
options_en: Give zero design detail and just say 'write some code, any way you like, for prefix search.'
A trie supporting insert and prefix search, each node storing character, children, and isEndOfWord.

Even though you only need one new method, ask the AI to rewrite the whole project into a better layered architecture.
why: 这条提示锁定了数据结构和节点字段，但把语法实现留给 AI，正好落在推荐的提示粒度上。
why_en: This prompt fixes the data structure and node fields while leaving syntax to the AI, landing right in the recommended granularity.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是改一行判断条件，自己直接写通常比提示 AI 更快。
tradeoff: 锁定方案与字段 vs 逐行口述实现 —— 提示到数据结构层就够，细到变量名就是隔着 AI 手写。
codeSample:
Implement a trie that supports insert(word) and searchByPrefix(prefix).
Each TrieNode stores: character, children map, isEndOfWord boolean.
Fit it into the existing Dictionary class; keep it concise.

跳过测试直接继续

Always hand-write it and avoid AI entirely.

whenOtherWins: 如果难点是算法选择或边界推理，应先自己想清楚再让 AI 实现。

optionMeanings: AI 出实现、你出方案并核对正确性的分工做法。

如果 AI 选错结构，后续边界情况可能出错。
把潜在 bug 一路带进下一步开发。
optionDirectness: 命中评分点：AI 管体量，你管判断。
效率错：拒绝工具反而拖慢已验证的体力活。

步骤缺：跳过验证，正确性无从确认。
optionMeanings_en: The AI implements while you choose the approach and check correctness.
Refusing AI unconditionally, even for verifiable grunt work.
Handing the structure choice — which should be yours — to the AI.
Moving on without testing what was just generated.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The implementation lands in ten seconds, freeing five minutes for harder work.
Five minutes are spent on an implementation you already knew was correct.

Any hidden bug carries straight into the next step of development.

q: 补全 AI 使用原则：
q_en: Complete the principle for using AI during execution:

tradeoff: AI 出体量 vs 你出判断 —— 生成速度换不来方案责任，选择和取舍必须你来担。

q: 为什么不要连续堆叠多次 AI 生成后才第一次运行代码？
q_en: Why should you not stack several AI generations before running the code for the first time?
options: AI 会拒绝继续生成
多个局部正确的改动可能互相冲突，最后形成级联错误
运行代码会降低面试评分
测试只能在最后运行
options_en: The AI will refuse to keep generating.
Several locally-correct changes can conflict and surface as one cascading failure.
Running code lowers your interview score.
Tests can only be run at the very end.
why: 每次有意义生成后运行能把错误隔离在最近一步，避免最后同时面对多处冲突。
why_en: Running after each meaningful generation isolates failures to the latest change instead of creating a cascade.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Gen1[Generate step 1] --> Gen2[Generate step 2]
  Gen2 --> Gen3[Generate step 3]
  Gen3 --> Fail[Mixed failure]
  Run[Run each step] -.-> Isolate[Small failure]
optionMeanings: 把工具行为想象成会主动拒绝的极端说法。
把多步生成的冲突后果说成级联错误的说法。
把运行代码和评分倒挂的错误说法。
把测试时机限制死在最后一步的说法。
optionScenarioImpacts: 不成立，AI 不会因为堆叠生成就拒绝工作。
越堆越多，最后一次运行时要同时定位多处冲突。
实际相反，面试官更认可频繁验证的习惯。
如果只在最后测，前面的错误早已互相掩盖。
optionDirectness: 事实错：不是 AI 拒绝，是错误会累积。
命中评分点：局部正确不等于整体正确，冲突在最后爆发。
方向反：运行验证是加分项，不是扣分项。
时机错：测试应贴着每步生成走，不是攒到最后。
optionMeanings_en: The extreme claim that the tool would actively refuse to continue.
Naming the conflict outcome of stacked generations as a cascade.
The inverted claim that running code lowers your score.
Fixing test timing to the very last step only.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Not true — the AI doesn’t refuse just because generations stack up.
The pile grows, and the final run must untangle several conflicts at once.
The opposite is true — interviewers favor frequent verification.
If testing only happens at the end, earlier errors are already masked.
optionDirectness_en: Wrong fact: it is not refusal, it is accumulated error.
Hits the mark: locally correct is not globally correct, and the conflict surfaces at the end.
Reversed direction: running code is a plus, not a minus.
Wrong timing: tests should track each generation, not pile up until the end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个局部改动叠加后互相冲突，在最后一次运行时集中爆发的一串错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascading errors happen when several stacked changes conflict and surface together the first time you finally run the code.

q: 把增量执行循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the incremental execution loop in the correct order:
steps: 修复本轮引入的问题
让 AI 完成一个明确小步骤
运行测试或编译检查
确认通过后进入下一步
why: 核心原则是每个有意义变更后马上验证，有问题先修，不在破损代码上继续叠新功能。
why_en: The loop is: generate one clear step, run checks, fix any breakage, then move on.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Prompt[Prompt one change] --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Run[Run tests]
  Run --> Decide{Pass?}
  Decide -->|yes| Next[Next step]
  Decide -->|no| Fix[Fix latest step]
  Fix --> Run

q: AI 的“训练数据偏置”（更容易给出训练语料里最常见的解法）在面试中常表现为什么？
q_en: How does training-data bias usually show up in an AI coding interview?
options: 给出教科书式解法，但不一定适合当前约束或代码库
永远拒绝回答算法题
只能生成注释不能生成代码
自动识别所有公司偏好

It always refuses to answer algorithm questions.
It can only generate comments, never code.
It automatically detects every company's preferences.
why: AI 可能给出技术上正确、策略上不合适的常见解法，你要判断它是否匹配题目约束和现有工具。

optionMeanings: 把训练语料里最常见解法直接搬过来的表现。
把偏置误解成完全拒答的极端说法。

把偏置误解成一种万能感知能力的说法。

不成立，训练偏置不等于拒绝作答。

optionDirectness: 命中评分点：常见解法不等于贴合当前约束的解法。

定义错：偏置和输出形式无关。
定义错：偏置不带来公司级别的感知能力。
optionMeanings_en: Reaching for the most common solution in the training corpus.
The extreme claim that bias means outright refusal.
The misconception that bias limits generation to comments only.
The misconception that bias grants company-specific awareness.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The solution is technically correct but may skip a simpler codebase-fit option.
Not true — training bias does not mean refusing to answer.
Not true — bias is unrelated to the ability to generate code.
Not true — the AI has no automatic awareness of company preferences.
optionDirectness_en: Hits the mark: common does not mean constraint-fitting.
Wrong definition: bias is a content tendency, not a refusal behavior.
Wrong definition: bias is unrelated to output form.
Wrong definition: bias grants no company-level awareness.

termDefinitions.meaning: AI 更容易给出训练语料里最常见的解法，而不一定是最贴合当前约束的解法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-data bias means the AI defaults to the most common solution in its training data, which may not fit your specific constraints.

q: AI 输出过度冗长的主要代价是什么？

你需要理解、验证并解释更多不必要的抽象和注释

q: 哪些是 AI 常见的设计捷径或过度设计？（多选）
q_en: Which are common AI design shortcuts or over-designs? (Select all that apply.)
options: 为两个几乎无关的类创建 BaseProcessor
不必要地引入深继承层级
把简单 if-else 包成 strategy pattern
遵守现有最小接口
options_en: Create a BaseProcessor superclass for two barely related classes.
Introduce unnecessarily deep inheritance hierarchies.
Wrap a simple if-else in a strategy pattern.
Stick to the existing minimal interface.
why: 这些抽象可能不直接破坏功能，但会显得你接受了没有必要的设计复杂度。
why_en: Unneeded base classes, deep inheritance, and strategy wrappers can signal that you accepted lazy over-engineering.

在简单继承关系上叠出多层不必要的父类。

不额外新增抽象，保持接口和现状一致。

定位一个方法实际生效在哪一层变得更难。
读者要多理解一层模式结构才能看懂分支逻辑。

命中：模式复杂度超过了分支本身的复杂度。

Stacking unnecessary extra layers onto a simple inheritance chain.
Wrapping a three-line branch in a design pattern.
Adding no extra abstraction and keeping the interface as-is.

The interface stays minimal, so readers learn nothing new.
