optionMeanings: 指出提示过细会把 AI 变成转录者，你的错误会原样落地。
误以为提示越详细，AI 就越能自行发现并纠正逻辑错误。
误以为把索引写死会让代码天然更好验证。
误以为提示够具体后，状态语义就不再需要人来把关。
optionScenarioImpacts: 一个写错的 base case 公式或 return cell 会被原样实现，且不会有报错提示。
AI 并不会主动质疑你给出的公式是否正确，它默认你是对的。
验证仍然要靠手推例子和测试，和提示是否具体无关。
状态语义决定 base case 和 return cell 该是什么，仍然必须由人确认。
optionDirectness: 最直接；这正是“过于具体”提示的核心风险。
不直接；AI 不会主动验证你给的公式，只会执行它。
不直接；验证难度取决于测试和手推例子，不取决于提示细节。
不直接；状态语义的重要性不会因为提示写得细就消失。
optionMeanings_en: Names how an overly detailed prompt turns the AI into a transcriber that ships your mistakes unchanged.
Wrongly assumes more detail lets the AI self-correct logic errors.
Wrongly assumes hardcoded indices automatically make the code easier to verify.
Wrongly assumes a specific-enough prompt removes the need for human state review.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A wrong base-case formula or return cell gets implemented exactly as written, with no warning.
The AI does not question the formula you supplied; it assumes you are correct.
Verification still depends on hand-traced examples and tests, regardless of prompt detail.
State semantics still determine the base case and return cell, and still need a human to confirm them.
optionDirectness_en: Most direct; this is exactly the risk of being overly specific.
Not direct; the AI does not actively verify your formula, only executes it.
Not direct; verification difficulty depends on tests and hand traces, not on prompt detail.
Not direct; the importance of state semantics does not disappear because the prompt got detailed.

scenario: 你准备提示 AI 写 DP 代码，但还没实现任何东西。
scenario_en: You are about to prompt the AI to write DP code, but you have not implemented anything yet.
q: 在提示 AI 之前，最值得先做的事是什么？
q_en: What is the most valuable thing to do before prompting the AI?
options: 只跑一次最大规模输入看性能
等代码生成后再猜 base case
不写测试，直接读完整张表
先写几个小测试和边界测试，锁定期望答案
options_en: Run only the largest-scale input once to check performance.
Wait until the code is generated, then guess the base cases.
Skip tests and read the entire table directly.
Write a few small and edge-case tests first to pin down the expected answers.
why: 测试会逼你思考 base case，也给 AI 输出一个可验证目标。DP 的空字符串、相等字符串、单字符等边界特别容易错。
why_en: Writing tests before prompting pins down DP base cases and gives the AI output something concrete to prove.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目还没理解清楚，可以先手推一个小例子；但很快应把它转成测试。
tradeoff: 先写测试再提示（多几分钟但有验证目标）vs 直接提示（省时间但没有可核对的基准）
optionMeanings: 只关心大输入下代码是否跑得动，跳过正确性验证。
把 base case 的确定顺序颠倒，让代码先于设计存在。
打算靠肉眼通读整张表来找 bug。
在写代码前先把期望输出钉死成几个可核对的用例。
optionScenarioImpacts: 大输入难手算验证，也漏掉了空串、单字符这些易错边界。
没先手推 base case，之后难判断 AI 给的边界值对不对。
DP 表格常有几十上百格，逐格通读在面试压力下不现实。
空串、相等串、单字符提前想清楚，AI 的代码有了验证目标。
optionDirectness: 不直接；性能不是这一步要解决的问题，正确性才是。
不直接；这是本末倒置，base case 应该先于代码确定。
不直接；通读整张表效率低，且容易漏掉具体 bug。
最直接；测试同时锁定规范并强迫你想清楚边界。
optionMeanings_en: Cares only about whether the code runs fast on large input, skipping correctness checks.
Reverses the order, letting code exist before the base cases are pinned down.
Plans to eyeball the entire table to spot bugs.
Pins down expected outputs as a few checkable cases before any code exists.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A large input is hard to hand-verify and misses easy-to-break edges like empty or single-character strings.
Without tracing base cases first, it is hard to judge whether the AI's edge values are right later.
A DP table often has dozens of cells; reading them all under interview pressure is unrealistic.
Empty, equal, and single-character cases get thought through ahead, giving the AI's code a target.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; performance is not the problem this step solves — correctness is.
Not direct; this puts the cart before the horse — base cases should precede code.
Not direct; reading the whole table is slow and easy to miss a specific bug in.
Most direct; tests pin down the spec and force you to think through the edges.

scenario: 拼写纠错要从字典中找和输入词最接近的词，距离按插入、删除、替换字符数计算。
scenario_en: A spell checker must find the closest dictionary word to the input word, where distance is counted by insertions, deletions, and replacements.
q: 解决“最接近的词”这个核心子问题，应该用哪种算法？
q_en: Which algorithm should solve the core closest-word subproblem?
options: LRU Cache
Edit distance 的二维 DP
拓扑排序
只按字符串长度排序
options_en: An LRU cache
The 2D edit-distance DP
Topological sort
Sorting purely by string length
why: 两个字符串、三种编辑操作、求最小操作数，是 edit distance 的标准形状。外层可以遍历候选词，核心距离用 DP 算。
why_en: Spell-check closeness by single-character edits is the classic edit-distance DP.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是固定模式查找，KMP、trie 或正则可能更合适；edit distance 用于允许模糊编辑的相似度。
tradeoff: 允许模糊编辑求最小代价（edit distance DP）vs 只做精确/固定模式匹配（trie、KMP）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Empty[empty prefix] --> Row[base row]
  Empty --> Col[base col]
  Row --> Cell[dp i j]
  Col --> Cell
  Cell --> Answer[dp m n]
optionMeanings: 缓存淘汰策略，和字符串相似度计算无关。
两个字符串前缀的二维表，衡量把一个变成另一个的最少编辑次数。
给有依赖关系的节点排出线性顺序的图算法。
只比较单词长度，不看具体字符差异。
optionScenarioImpacts: 解决的是内存管理问题，不能衡量两个词有多接近。
能精确算出输入词和每个候选词之间的最少编辑次数，直接支撑“最接近”的判断。
拼写纠错里候选词之间没有依赖关系，用不上拓扑排序。
长度接近的词不一定编辑距离小，例如替换和插入代价不同。
optionDirectness: 不直接；LRU 是缓存策略，不衡量字符串相似度。
最直接；正是插入/删除/替换求最小操作数的标准场景。
不直接；本题没有节点依赖关系需要排序。
不直接；长度排序会漏掉字符本身的差异。
optionMeanings_en: A cache-eviction policy unrelated to string similarity.
A 2D table over two string prefixes that measures the minimum edits to turn one into the other.
A graph algorithm that orders dependent nodes linearly.
Comparing only word length, not the actual character differences.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This solves a memory-management problem and cannot measure how close two words are.
It computes the exact minimum edit count between the input and each candidate, directly supporting the closeness ranking.
Spell-check candidates have no dependency relationship, so topological sort has nothing to order.
Similar-length words are not necessarily close in edits, since insert and replace have different effects.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; an LRU cache does not measure string similarity.
Most direct; this is exactly the standard insert/delete/replace minimum-edit setup.
Not direct; there is no node dependency here to order.
Not direct; length-based sorting misses the actual character differences.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements needed to turn one string into another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种线性时间的精确子串匹配算法，不处理模糊编辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KMP is a linear-time exact substring matching algorithm that does not handle fuzzy edits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树：按公共前缀组织字符串的树形结构，适合精确前缀查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a tree that organizes strings by shared prefixes, suited to exact prefix lookups.

q: 填空：Edit distance 的状态定义。
q_en: Fill in the state definition for edit distance.
text: `dp[i][j]` 表示把第一个字符串的{{前 i 个字符}}变成第二个字符串的{{前 j 个字符}}所需的最少编辑次数。
why: 这个状态定义直接解释了为什么需要二维表：两个前缀长度各占一个维度。后续 base case 和递推都从它推出。
why_en: Edit-distance state is the minimum edits between prefixes of lengths i and j.

q: Edit distance 的边界行列应该如何理解？
q_en: How should you understand the border row and column in edit distance?
options: `dp[0][j] = j`，空串变成长度 j 的前缀需要 j 次插入
`dp[i][0] = i`，长度 i 的前缀变成空串需要 i 次删除
`dp[0][j]` 全部为 0，因为空串不需要操作
`dp[i][0]` 全部为 1，因为只删一次
options_en: dp[0][j] = j: turning an empty string into a length-j prefix takes j insertions.
dp[i][0] = i: turning a length-i prefix into an empty string takes i deletions.
dp[0][j] is always 0 because an empty string needs no operations.
dp[i][0] is always 1 because it only takes one delete.
why: 边界值可以直接从状态语义看出来，不需要递推。它们也是最常见的 off-by-one bug 来源。
why_en: The edit-distance borders count insertions from empty and deletions to empty.
optionMeanings: 正确的边界：空串到长度 j 前缀的编辑数等于插入次数 j。
正确的边界：长度 i 前缀到空串的编辑数等于删除次数 i。
误把“空串不需要操作”套用到了另一个前缀非空的方向。
误把删除次数当成固定值 1，忽略了前缀长度 i。
optionScenarioImpacts: 这是顶部一整行的正确初始化，不需要经过递推计算。
这是最左一整列的正确初始化，不需要经过递推计算。
只有 `dp[0][0] = 0` 成立；`dp[0][j]`（j>0）应该等于 j，不是 0。
只有 i=1 时才恰好是 1；i=3 时应该是 3 次删除，不是 1。
optionDirectness: 正确；直接从状态定义推出，不用递推验证。
同样正确；只是把方向从空前缀行换成了空前缀列。
不正确；混淆了 `dp[0][0]` 和 `dp[0][j]`（j>0）两种情况。
不正确；把变量 i 错误地固定成了常数 1。
optionMeanings_en: Correct border: the edits from empty to a length-j prefix equal the insert count j.
Correct border: the edits from a length-i prefix to empty equal the delete count i.
Wrongly applies the empty-to-empty case to the direction where the prefix is non-empty.
Wrongly treats the delete count as a fixed 1, ignoring the prefix length i.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This correctly initializes the entire top row without needing the recurrence.
This correctly initializes the entire left column without needing the recurrence.
Only dp[0][0] = 0 holds; dp[0][j] for j>0 should equal j, not 0.
This only happens to be 1 when i=1; for i=3 it should be 3 deletions, not 1.
optionDirectness_en: Correct; it follows directly from the state definition, no recurrence needed.
Also correct; it is the same idea applied to the empty-prefix column instead of the row.
Incorrect; it confuses dp[0][0] with dp[0][j] for j greater than 0.
Incorrect; it wrongly fixes the variable i to the constant 1.

q: Edit distance 内部格子的递推核心是什么？
q_en: What is the core recurrence for an inner edit-distance cell?
options: 不管字符是否相等，永远取上方格子
相等复制左上角；不等则替换/删除/插入取最小加一
不管字符是否相等，永远取左方格子加 2
字符相等时也必须额外加 1 的代价
options_en: Always take the cell above, regardless of whether the characters match.
On a match, copy the diagonal; otherwise take one plus the minimum of replace, delete, or insert.
Always take the cell to the left plus 2, regardless of match.
Even a matching character must add an extra cost of 1.
why: 左上、上方、左方分别对应替换、删除、插入。字符已经相等时不需要额外编辑，直接继承左上角。
why_en: Edit distance copies the diagonal on a match and otherwise takes one plus the cheapest replace, delete, or insert predecessor.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Up[delete] --> Min[min plus 1]
  Left[insert] --> Min
  Diag[replace] --> Min
  Same[same char] --> Copy[copy diag]
optionMeanings: 只考虑删除操作，忽略替换和插入两条路径。
正确的递推：按字符是否相等分两支，取三种操作中最便宜的一种。
既忽略了替换/插入路径，也凭空多加了固定代价 2。
把“字符相等不需要编辑”误当成“字符相等也要付一次代价”。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会漏掉替换和插入更便宜的情况，算出的编辑距离偏大或直接错误。
三条路径（替换、删除、插入）都被考虑，取最小值保证结果最优。
凭空加 2 没有任何操作语义支撑，纯属编造的规则。
如果对每个匹配字符都多算一次编辑，最终距离会比真实值大。
optionDirectness: 不直接；只覆盖了删除这一种操作。
最直接；覆盖了匹配与不匹配两种情况和全部三种操作。
不直接；这个规则没有对应任何真实的编辑操作。
不直接；违反了“匹配字符不产生编辑”的基本定义。
optionMeanings_en: Considers only the delete path, ignoring replace and insert.
The correct recurrence: branch on whether characters match and take the cheapest of the three operations.
Ignores replace and insert while also adding an unexplained constant of 2.
Wrongly treats a matching character as still costing one edit.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This misses cases where replace or insert is cheaper, producing an inflated or wrong edit distance.
All three paths — replace, delete, insert — are considered, and taking the minimum guarantees optimality.
Adding 2 has no operational meaning behind it; it is simply invented.
Charging an edit for every matching character makes the final distance larger than the true value.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; it only covers the delete operation.
Most direct; it covers both the match and mismatch cases across all three operations.
Not direct; this rule corresponds to no real edit operation.
Not direct; it violates the basic definition that a matching character costs nothing.

scenario: AI 已经按“字符相等复制左上角、不等取三者最小值加一”的递推写出了下面这段 edit distance 内层代码，你在检查匹配分支。
scenario_en: The AI has written the edit-distance inner loop using copy diagonal on a match and one plus the minimum of three choices on a mismatch; you are checking the match branch.
q: 这段 edit distance 的分支中，`dp[i - 1][j - 1]` 在字符相等时代表什么？
q_en: In this edit-distance branch, what does dp[i - 1][j - 1] mean when the characters match?
options: 当前字符必须替换的成本
哈希冲突次数
去掉当前两个相同字符后，两个前缀的最优编辑数
整张表的最大值
options_en: The cost of replacing the current character.
The number of hash collisions.
The optimal edit count for the two prefixes with the current matching characters removed.
The maximum value across the entire table.
why: 当前字符相等时不用编辑它们，问题退化为对齐前面的两个前缀。这个分支是检查递推正确性的重点。
why_en: On a character match, the cost is exactly the diagonal subproblem for the previous prefixes.
optionMeanings: 误以为匹配分支仍然在计算一次替换操作的成本。
把 DP 表格错认成哈希表，套用不相关的概念。
正确解释：对角线格子就是去掉这对相同字符后，剩余前缀的最优编辑数。
误以为这个格子存的是全表统计量，而不是某一对前缀的答案。
optionScenarioImpacts: 字符相等时代码没有加 1，说明这里根本没有付出替换成本。
DP 数组是按索引寻址的表格，不存在哈希冲突这个概念。
这正是为什么匹配分支直接复制对角线格子而不额外加一的原因。
整张表并不是在维护一个全局最大值，每个格子只对应它自己的一对前缀。
optionDirectness: 不直接；代码里没有 +1，说明没有产生替换成本。
不直接；哈希表和这段 DP 递推无关。
最直接；直接对应代码里 `dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]` 这一行的语义。
不直接；每个格子对应特定前缀对，不是全表最大值。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes the match branch still charges a replace cost.
Mistakes the DP table for a hash table and applies an unrelated concept.
Correct: the diagonal cell is the optimal edit count for the remaining prefixes once the matching pair is removed.
Wrongly assumes this cell stores a whole-table statistic instead of one prefix pair's answer.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The code adds no 1 on a match, showing no replace cost is charged here.
A DP array is indexed by position; there is no hash collision concept involved.
This is exactly why the match branch copies the diagonal cell without adding anything.
The table is not tracking a running maximum; each cell belongs to its own prefix pair.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; there is no +1 in the code, so no replace cost is charged.
Not direct; hash tables are unrelated to this DP recurrence.
Most direct; it matches exactly what dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] means.
Not direct; each cell belongs to a specific prefix pair, not a table-wide maximum.

q: 把 edit distance 的推导顺序排好。
q_en: Put the edit-distance derivation steps in order.
steps: 说出 base cases：空串到前缀是插入，前缀到空串是删除。
定义状态：两个字符串前缀之间的最少编辑数。
用一个小例子如 KATE 到 SAT 手算答案 2。
描述递推：相等取左上，不等取插入/删除/替换的最小值加 1。
提示 AI 写 bottom-up 代码，再用测试和表格验证。
why: 先用具体例子确认语义，再抽象成状态、边界和递推。这样 AI 输出有明确的验证依据。
why_en: A strong edit-distance derivation moves from a tiny example to state, base cases, recurrence, and AI-assisted implementation.
tradeoff: 先手推例子再抽象（多两分钟但有验证基准）vs 直接抽象定义（省时间但没有可核对的具体答案）

termDefinitions.meaning: 自底向上：从最小子问题开始按依赖顺序填表，不使用递归调用栈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bottom-up fills the table from the smallest subproblem in dependency order, without a recursive call stack.

scenario: AI 生成了 DP 代码，你不想逐行盯所有索引，但需要快速验证递推和边界。
scenario_en: The AI generated DP code, and you need to quickly verify the recurrence and borders without staring at every index.
q: 文章推荐的高杠杆调试提示是什么？
q_en: What high-leverage debugging prompt does the article recommend?
options: 只盯着函数最后一行的变量名反复对照
让 AI 打印小输入的完整 dp 表，然后对照手推的几个格子
不看任何中间输出，直接删掉所有测试用例
不做任何验证，直接把 DP 全部换成贪心重写
options_en: Only stare repeatedly at the variable names on the function's last line.
Ask the AI to print the full dp table for a small input, then check it against a few hand-traced cells.
Skip every intermediate output and delete all the test cases outright.
Skip verification entirely and rewrite the whole thing as greedy instead.
why: 打印表格能把隐藏在循环里的错误变成可观察状态。先对照左上 2x2，就能定位 base case 或递推问题。
why_en: Printing a small DP table makes base-case and recurrence bugs visible without reading every loop expression.
whenOtherWins: 如果代码很短且你已经很熟悉，也可以直接读循环；但表格验证在面试压力下更稳。
tradeoff: 打印表格核对（多一步但错误可定位）vs 直接读循环代码（省步骤但压力下容易漏看）
optionMeanings: 只看返回值所在的那一行，忽略中间过程。
把循环内部的隐藏状态变成可以对照的具体数字。
彻底放弃用具体输入检验代码是否正确。
误以为验证手段是换算法，而不是核实当前算法的实现。
optionScenarioImpacts: 只看最后一行看不出 base case 或中间格子是否算错。
对照左上 2x2，base case 错就在首行/首列露出来，递推错就在第一个内部格子露出来。
没有测试就没有可重复验证的依据，bug 只能靠肉眼通读代码猜。
换算法不解决当前 DP 实现是否正确的问题，而且贪心不一定适用。
optionDirectness: 不直接；只看变量名看不出中间计算是否正确。
最直接；这是文章点名的高杠杆调试手段。
不直接；删测试只会让验证更难，不会帮你定位问题。
不直接；这是换了问题而不是验证当前代码。
optionMeanings_en: Only looks at the line holding the return value, ignoring intermediate steps.
Turns the loop's hidden state into concrete numbers you can check.
Gives up entirely on verifying the code against a concrete input.
Wrongly assumes verification means switching algorithms rather than checking the current implementation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Looking only at the last line reveals nothing about whether base cases or intermediate cells are wrong.
Checking the top-left 2x2 shows a base-case bug in the first row/column and a recurrence bug in the first inner cell.
Without tests there is no repeatable evidence, and bugs can only be guessed by reading code.
Switching algorithms does not verify whether the current DP implementation is correct, and greedy may not even apply.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; variable names alone reveal nothing about intermediate correctness.

q: 验证 edit distance 时，哪些测试很有价值？
q_en: Which tests are valuable for verifying edit distance?
options: 两个相同字符串应返回 0
空串到 `abc` 应返回 3

只测试一个很长随机字符串且不知道答案

'kate' to 'sat' should return 2.
Testing only one long random string with an unknown expected answer.

why_en: Good DP tests include equal inputs, empty-prefix cases, and a small hand-computed nontrivial case.
optionMeanings: 覆盖“字符完全相同，编辑距离应为 0”的基础情况。
覆盖空串这一整行/整列边界的插入次数。
覆盖一个非平凡的手算例子，同时检验递推的替换/删除/插入分支。
用一个连答案都不知道的大输入去测正确性。
optionScenarioImpacts: 如果这个都算错，说明匹配分支或 base case 有明显 bug。
如果这个算错，说明边界初始化（`dp[0][j] = j`）有问题。
如果这个算错，能直接定位到递推的三选一最小值逻辑。
算出一个数字后你没有基准可以判断对不对，无法定位任何具体 bug。
optionDirectness: 直接；是最基础也最容易先验证的用例。
直接；专门验证边界初始化是否正确。
直接；专门验证内部递推是否正确。
不直接；没有已知答案，测试失败或通过都无法归因。
optionMeanings_en: Covers the basic case: identical characters should give edit distance 0.
Covers the entire empty-prefix row/column boundary and its insert count.
Covers a nontrivial hand-computed example that also checks the replace/delete/insert branches.
Tests correctness with a large input whose expected answer is unknown.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Getting this wrong points straight at a bug in the match branch or a base case.
Getting this wrong points straight at broken border initialization such as dp[0][j] = j.
Getting this wrong points straight at the recurrence's three-way minimum logic.
Without a known answer, you have no baseline to attribute a pass or fail to any specific bug.
optionDirectness_en: Direct; it is the simplest and easiest case to verify first.
Direct; it specifically checks that border initialization is correct.
Direct; it specifically checks that the inner recurrence is correct.
Not direct; with no known answer, a pass or failure cannot be attributed to anything.

scenario: 一个 DP 测试失败了，你正准备把报错信息发给 AI。
scenario_en: A DP test failed, and you are about to send the error output to the AI.
q: 为什么不该只把报错扔给 AI 说“修一下”？
q_en: Why should you not just throw an error at the AI and say fix it?
options: 所有隐藏测试都会自动覆盖这个具体边界
DP 代码天生正确，永远不需要调试
先形成具体假设，再带着假设去提示 AI
AI 完全无法读取或理解测试失败信息
options_en: Every hidden test will automatically cover this specific edge.
DP code is inherently correct and never needs debugging.
Form a hypothesis first, such as an off-by-one base case, then prompt the AI with it.
The AI is entirely unable to read or understand test-failure output.
why: 带假设的提示证明你仍在控制调试方向，也能防止 AI 盲目重写整个方案。面试官会看到你的定位能力。
why_en: When a DP test fails, prompt with a concrete hypothesis so the AI fixes the suspected structure rather than thrashing.
optionMeanings: 把测试覆盖率和调试策略混为一谈。
误以为调试这个动作本身对 DP 不适用。
正确做法：先自己定位可能出错的结构，再带着具体假设提示 AI。
误以为 AI 完全看不懂测试失败的输出。
optionScenarioImpacts: 测试覆盖率是提前写测试时决定的，和这次“怎么提示 AI 修 bug”无关。
DP 代码和其他代码一样会有 bug，需要照常调试，只是要带着假设去做。
带假设提示能让 AI 直接检查你怀疑的那部分，而不是重写整个方案碰运气。
AI 完全可以读懂报错和期望/实际值的差异，只是它不知道该往哪个方向改。
optionDirectness: 不直接；这里的问题是调试策略，不是测试覆盖率。
不直接；DP 一样需要调试，只是调试方式有讲究。
最直接；这正是文章点名的“先假设再提示”策略。
不直接；AI 能读报错，缺的是方向而不是能力。
optionMeanings_en: Conflates test coverage with debugging strategy.
Wrongly assumes debugging itself does not apply to DP.
The correct move: locate the likely broken structure yourself, then prompt the AI with that specific hypothesis.
Wrongly assumes the AI cannot understand test-failure output at all.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Test coverage was decided when the tests were written earlier and is unrelated to how you prompt a fix now.
DP code has bugs like any other code and still needs debugging, just guided by a hypothesis.
A hypothesis-driven prompt lets the AI check exactly the part you suspect instead of rewriting the whole solution on a guess.
The AI can perfectly well read the error and the expected-vs-actual values; what it lacks is direction, not ability.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; the issue here is debugging strategy, not test coverage.
Not direct; DP still needs debugging, just done thoughtfully.
Most direct; this is exactly the hypothesis-first prompting strategy the article names.
Not direct; the AI can read the error — what is missing is direction, not capability.

q_en: Where do DP bugs most often live structurally?

It commits the design to this path: The returned cell or state.

q: AI 给出一个“几乎正确”的 DP 递推（能跑、通过部分测试却是错的），为什么特别危险？
q_en: Why is an almost-correct DP recurrence especially dangerous?
options: 这种代码一定会编译失败
这种问题只会影响代码风格
类型检查总能自动发现这种错误
AI 可能套用了相邻问题的错误递推模板
options_en: Code like this is guaranteed to fail to compile.
A problem like this only affects code style.
Type checking will always catch this kind of error automatically.
The AI may have borrowed the wrong recurrence template from a neighboring problem.
why: 相邻 DP 题的表格形状很像，但递推语义不同。代码能跑、简单测试也可能过，隐藏测试才会暴露。
why_en: Almost-right recurrences are dangerous because neighboring DP problems can share table shapes but need different transitions.
optionMeanings: 误以为逻辑错误一定表现为语法错误。
误以为递推写错只是美观问题，不影响正确性。
误以为类型系统能检查出算法语义上的错误。
指出错误的真实来源：借用了相邻问题的递推模板。
optionScenarioImpacts: “几乎正确”的代码通常语法完全合法，能正常编译运行。
递推选错会直接导致输出的数值错误，不是风格问题。
类型检查只管变量类型对不对，不管数值语义对不对。
edit distance 和 LCS（最长公共子序列）表格形状几乎一样，但一个是最小代价、一个是最大长度，混淆后代码依然能跑。
optionDirectness: 不直接；语法层面完全没问题，这不是编译错误。
不直接；这是正确性问题，不是风格问题。
不直接；类型检查不覆盖算法语义。
最直接；这正是文章点名的“几乎正确的递推”成因。
optionMeanings_en: Wrongly assumes a logic error must show up as a syntax error.
Wrongly assumes a wrong recurrence is only a style issue, not a correctness issue.
Wrongly assumes the type system can catch algorithmic semantic errors.
Names the real cause: borrowing the recurrence template from a neighboring problem.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Almost-right code is usually syntactically valid and compiles and runs fine.
Picking the wrong recurrence directly produces wrong output values, not a style problem.
Type checking only validates variable types, not numeric semantics.

optionDirectness_en: Not direct; there is no syntax problem here, so it is not a compile error.
Not direct; this is a correctness issue, not a style issue.
Not direct; type checking does not cover algorithmic semantics.
Most direct; this is exactly what the article calls an almost-right recurrence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最长公共子序列：两个序列中都出现且顺序一致的最长子序列长度，用最大化递推求解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LCS is the length of the longest subsequence appearing in the same order in both sequences, solved with a maximizing recurrence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个所需要的最少插入、删除、替换次数，用最小化递推求解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements to turn one string into another, solved with a minimizing recurrence.

q: AI 在 DP 里多加了一个你解释不了的维度（例如 `dp[i][j][k]`），应该怎么处理？
q_en: What should you do if the AI adds a DP dimension you cannot explain, such as dp[i][j][k]?

让 AI 证明这个维度的语义和必要性；解释不了就要求简化状态
直接删掉所有已经验证过的 base case
无条件全盘接受，维度越多说明考虑越周全
options_en: Forcibly turn the entire 2D state table into a string.
Ask the AI to justify the dimension's meaning and necessity; simplify the state if it cannot.
Delete all the base cases that were already verified.

把“维度多”误当成“更保险”，不做任何审查。

能确认这个维度是真实需要（比如额外约束）还是模型的保守堆叠。
base case 是递推的根基，删掉后整个表都失去起点。

optionDirectness: 不直接；换数据结构不解决维度语义不清的问题。
最直接；这是文章给出的具体处理办法。
不直接；这是无关且有破坏性的动作。
不直接；维度多不等于正确，也不等于更保险。
optionMeanings_en: Proposes a change unrelated to the dimension problem.
The correct move: make the AI explain what the new dimension tracks, and simplify if it cannot.
Proposes a destructive action that breaks the recurrence's foundation.
Wrongly treats more dimensions as inherently safer, with no review at all.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Swapping the table for a string does not answer what the dimension is actually tracking.
This confirms whether the dimension is genuinely needed, such as for an extra constraint, or just defensive padding.
Base cases anchor the recurrence; deleting them removes the table's starting point entirely.
More dimensions mean a larger state space and harder debugging, not inherently more safety.

Most direct; this is the concrete remedy the article recommends.
Not direct; this is an unrelated and destructive action.

scenario: 你的状态是“前 i 个元素”，循环需要写到 `i = n`。
scenario_en: Your state means the first i elements, and the loop needs to write through i = n.
q: 这个 DP 数组的大小通常应该是什么？
q_en: What size should this DP array usually be?
options: 固定 1
与输入无关
options_en: A fixed size of 1
n minus 1
n plus 1
Independent of the input

why_en: Prefix-based states usually need n plus one cells to include the empty prefix and the full prefix.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态定义是“从索引 i 开始”而不是“前 i 个”，大小可能是 n；关键是让数组大小和状态语义一致。

少分配了一格，会让最后一次写入越界。
正确大小：覆盖从空前缀 0 到完整前缀 n 的全部状态。
误以为数组大小和状态定义无关。
optionScenarioImpacts: 常量大小 1 放不下 `i` 从 0 到 n 的所有状态。
循环写到 `dp[n]` 时数组只有 n 格（索引 0..n-1），会越界。
`dp[0]` 到 `dp[n]` 共 n+1 格，正好对上“前 i 个”这个状态。
数组大小必须和状态定义的取值范围一致，不能凭空决定。
optionDirectness: 不直接；常量大小无法覆盖变化的输入规模。
不直接；这是典型的少一格 off-by-one。
最直接；直接从“前 i 个元素”这个状态语义推出来。
不直接；数组大小恰恰应该由状态定义决定。
optionMeanings_en: Ignores the input size entirely and hardcodes a constant array size.
Allocates one cell too few, so the final write goes out of bounds.
The correct size: covers every state from the empty prefix 0 to the full prefix n.
Wrongly assumes array size is unrelated to the state definition.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A constant size of 1 cannot hold all states for i from 0 to n.
Writing dp[n] goes out of bounds since the array only has n cells, indices 0 through n-1.
dp[0] through dp[n] is n+1 cells, matching the first-i-elements state exactly.
Array size must match the range the state definition allows, not be picked arbitrarily.
optionDirectness_en: Not direct; a constant size cannot cover a variable input size.
Not direct; this is a classic off-by-one under-allocation.
Most direct; it follows directly from the first-i-elements state semantics.
Not direct; array size should be exactly determined by the state definition.

这是业界公认的所有 DP 面试标准写法

The standard approach initializes dp[0] or the first row/column correctly in the table itself, not with a special-cased entry guard.

scenario: 题目要求列出所有和为 k 的子集，而不是只问有多少种或最优值。
scenario_en: The problem asks you to list all subsets that sum to k, not just count them or find one optimal value.

LRU Cache
只返回一个 DP 数字
回溯枚举所有合法子集

An LRU cache

直接忽略其中一个资源约束
按更紧张的归一化资源需求排序，另一维只作可行性检查
声称一维 FFD 在这里仍然精确最优
options_en: Sort tasks only by their name string.
Simply ignore one of the two resource constraints.
Sort by the tighter normalized resource demand and use the other dimension only as a feasibility check.
Claim that one-dimensional FFD is still exactly optimal here.
why: 多维装箱更难，实用做法是用一个启发式排序近似处理，并明确说明放弃了精确最优保证。成熟回答会讲清 tradeoff。
why_en: For multi-resource packing, a practical interview heuristic sorts by the tightest normalized resource and checks all capacities.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目要求严格最优且规模很小，可以回溯搜索；如果只需可行分配，启发式更务实。
tradeoff: 归一化排序启发式（务实、放弃精确最优）vs 精确回溯/搜索（能保证最优、规模必须很小）

错误策略只是运行得慢一点而已
近似有保证但可能非最优；错误则不满足题意，必须换算法

An approximate strategy can never return any valid solution.
A wrong strategy is merely a bit slower.

why_en: Approximate greedy can be acceptable with stated guarantees, while incorrect greedy fails the required objective.

scenario: 图最短路问题存在负权边，AI 生成了 Dijkstra。
scenario_en: The shortest-path graph has negative-weight edges, and the AI generated Dijkstra.
q: AI 用 Dijkstra 处理带负权边的最短路，你应该如何纠正？
q_en: If the AI uses Dijkstra on shortest paths with negative edges, how should you correct it?
options: 只把优先队列换成普通队列，其他逻辑不变
指出非负权重前提被打破，改用 Bellman-Ford
删掉所有带负权的边来回避这个问题
断言负权边完全不会影响最短路结果
options_en: Just replace the priority queue with a plain queue and leave the rest.
Point out that the non-negative-weight assumption is broken; switch to Bellman-Ford.
Delete every negative-weight edge to sidestep the problem.
Assert that negative edges have no effect on the shortest path at all.
why: Dijkstra 是贪心式扩展最近节点，依赖非负权重。负权会让已确定距离后来变小。
why_en: Negative edges invalidate Dijkstra's greedy finalization assumption, so Bellman-Ford is the safer alternative.
whenOtherWins: 如果确认所有权重非负，Dijkstra 仍然是合适选择。
tradeoff: Dijkstra（贪心扩展、要求非负权重、更快）vs Bellman-Ford（允许负权、松弛 V-1 轮、更慢）

scenario: 任务有依赖关系，某任务必须在另一个任务之后才能开始。
scenario_en: Tasks have dependencies, so some tasks can only start after other tasks finish.
q: 为什么“每次选最短任务”不足以处理带依赖的调度？
q_en: Why is choosing the shortest task each time not enough for scheduling with dependencies?
options: 任务依赖关系总是可以被贪心直接忽略
所有任务其实都必须同时开始
会违反依赖关系，需要先用拓扑排序建立合法顺序，再谈优化
最短任务优先策略在任何场景下都最优

All tasks must actually start at the same time.

Shortest-task-first is optimal in every scenario.
why: 依赖关系是硬约束，不能靠局部时长排序绕过。先保证合法顺序，再谈成本或时间优化。
why_en: Dependencies are hard constraints, so topological ordering must come before greedy duration choices.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有依赖、只有独立任务的排序或资源分配，贪心调度可能成立。
tradeoff: 先拓扑排序保证合法顺序（硬约束优先）vs 直接按时长贪心（可能违反依赖）

q: 面对 NP-hard 装箱变体，提示 AI 时应该明确说清什么？
q_en: For an NP-hard packing variant, what should you make explicit when prompting the AI?
options: 用贪心启发式，并说明已知的近似保证或明确不保证最优
直接声称这个方案一定返回最优解
不用向 AI 说明任何取舍

options_en: Ask for a greedy heuristic and state the known approximation bound or that optimality isn't guaranteed.

把命中格子的上下左右邻居加入 target 队列
只继续向右射击直到越界
停止并等待 `all_sunk()` 变 true

Push the hit cell's four neighbors onto the target queue
Keep firing rightward only, until running off the board

tradeoff: 四邻域局部追击（省枪但要维护队列状态） vs 回到盲扫（简单但浪费已知信息）
why: 船是连续且轴对齐的，所以命中后下一格船身很可能在四邻域里。先探索四邻居能尽快确定方向并击沉。
why_en: After a hit, the four adjacent cells are the highest-value probes because ships are contiguous and axis-aligned.
whenOtherWins: 如果船可以任意弯曲或不连续，四邻域追击就不再有这个结构性优势。

why: 任意连续 3 个整数的模 3 余数会覆盖 0、1、2。横船和竖船的 row+col 都形成连续值，所以三格船必有一格落在 hunt 集合里。
why_en: Every length-three horizontal or vertical ship spans three consecutive row-plus-column sums, including one divisible by three.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modulo three is the remainder left after dividing an integer by three.

纵向相邻时 row 每次加 1，row+col 连续变化
三个连续整数的模 3 余数一定各出现一次
所有船都必须从 `(0, 0)` 开始
options_en: For a horizontal ship, col increases by 1 each step, so row+col changes by 1 each time
For a vertical ship, row increases by 1 each step, so row+col changes by 1 each time
Any three consecutive integers hit every residue mod three exactly once
Every ship must start at `(0, 0)`
why: 证明只依赖轴对齐和长度至少 3。它不依赖船出现在哪一行、哪一列。
why_en: The guarantee follows from axis alignment and three consecutive sums, not from any particular ship location.

q: mod-3 hunt 集合大小最直接影响什么？
q_en: What does the size of the mod-3 hunt set most directly affect?
text: 把候选格从 100 降到 34，直接降低的是{{hunt 阶段的射击预算}}。
why: 稀疏 hunt 把基线的 100 个潜在探针降到 34 个（100/3 向上取整），这个数字直接决定了 hunt 阶段大约要花多少枪；target 阶段再补上击沉已发现船的开销。
why_en: The sparse hunt set shrinks the blind search space from 100 candidates to 34, which sets the rough shot budget the hunt phase alone will spend.

q: 为什么优化解把 hunt 列表打乱，而不是固定行优先遍历？
q_en: Why does the optimized solver shuffle the hunt list instead of scanning row-first?
options: 打乱会破坏 mod-3 覆盖证明
打乱能让 seeded 多局平均不被固定顺序主导
打乱能让 `check_shot` 跑得更快
打乱之后就能省掉 `tried` 集合
options_en: Shuffling would break the modulo-three coverage guarantee
Shuffling keeps the average over seeded layouts from being dominated by one fixed order
Shuffling makes `check_shot` run faster
Shuffling lets the solver drop the `tried` set entirely
tradeoff: 随机顺序换更公平的基准平均 vs 固定顺序换可复现的单次轨迹
why: 覆盖集合不变，改变的是先后顺序。随机顺序让基准更像平均搜索，而不是押注某个行优先开局特别幸运。
why_en: Shuffling preserves coverage but avoids overfitting the benchmark to one deterministic traversal order.

q: 把 hunt+target 的决策链排成正确顺序。

why: 先靠稀疏 hunt 保证发现，再靠 target 消化反馈，最后用去重守住预算。这个组合把开环扫描变成闭环探测。
why_en: The optimized flow combines sparse guaranteed discovery, feedback-driven targeting, and deduplication.

scenario_en: The optimization test has 100 cards, removes exactly 3 cards per turn, and has no random refill; since 100 = 33×3 + 1, the game can have at most 33 full turns and must leave one card unplayed.

q: 朴素 first-found 策略为什么会比最优少走回合？

options: 它会选出三张点数加起来不等于目标和的牌

它每回合会移除四张牌而不是规定的三张
它可能消耗掉其它三元组依赖的关键牌，导致剩余牌被孤立
why: 移动合法不代表后续空间好。first-found 完全不评估清除后还剩多少选择。
why_en: A legal triple can be strategically bad if it strands cards needed by many future triples.
options_en: It would pick three cards whose values do not actually sum to the target.
It errors out whenever a value repeats among the cards.
It removes four cards per turn instead of the required three.
It can consume cards that other triples depend on, stranding the rest of the board.

q: 朴素 `find_triple` 每次调用的时间复杂度是多少？
q_en: What is the time complexity of one naive `find_triple` call?
options: O(n)
why: 它三层嵌套枚举位置组合，属于三重穷举；完整 play loop 最多调用约 T 次，所以整体是 O(n^3 · T)，T 是打出的回合数。
why_en: Enumerating triples of positions is a triple-nested loop, so one call is cubic, and the full game is O(n^3 times T) for T turns played.
scenario: find_triple 对当前网格里所有位置做三重穷举，直到找到一个和等于目标的组合；你要评估这一次调用的时间复杂度。

q: 第二版三元组枚举最贴近哪种算法模式？
q_en: Which algorithm pattern best matches the second-version triple enumeration?
options: 对所有牌做 DFS 回溯，穷举到游戏结束
固定一个位置，用哈希表在剩余牌里找补数配对
随机抽三张牌，直到凑巧命中目标和
每个点数只保留第一张牌，丢弃其余重复牌
why: 3-sum 思路把内层查找转成哈希补数查询，从 O(n^3) 降到 O(n^2)。这只是加速枚举，不自动改善选择质量。
why_en: The 3-sum pattern fixes one card and uses a hash table to find complementary pairs.
whenOtherWins: 如果后续还要给每个候选做昂贵的位置级评分，枚举加速本身仍然不够。
options_en: Run DFS backtracking over all cards, exhausting the game tree to the end.
Fix one position and use a hash map to find the complementary pair among the rest.
Randomly draw three cards until they happen to hit the target sum.
Keep only the first card of each value and discard the rest.
tradeoff: 哈希补数加速枚举 vs 完整博弈树搜索的指数级开销

termDefinitions.meaningEn: 3-sum fixes one value and uses a hash map to find the other two in near-linear time, cutting a cubic triple-enumeration down to quadratic.

q_en: Fill in: in the optimization test, the number of distinct values V is {{25}}, and value-triple enumeration checks about {{325}} combination classes.
text: 优化测试中不同点数个数 V = {{25}}，值三元组枚举约检查 {{325}} 类组合。
why: 不同值只有 V=25 种；两两不同值组合最多 C(25,2)=300 种，加上 25 种三值相同的情况，一共约 325 类要检查，这远小于位置级候选的规模，是后续评分变快的直接原因。
why_en: With only V=25 distinct values, there are at most C(25,2)=300 distinct-value pairs plus 25 same-value cases, about 325 patterns total — far fewer than positional candidates, which is exactly why scoring gets cheap.
scenario: 把三元组枚举从 100 个位置压缩到按点数分桶后，你要估算这个更小状态空间里要检查多少组候选点数组合。

scenario: 你要给几百个值三元组候选做一层 lookahead，热点循环里不想为每个候选复制数组。
scenario_en: You are scoring hundreds of value-triple candidates with one-step lookahead and do not want to copy arrays inside the hot loop.
q: lookahead 热循环里应该用什么实现技巧？
q_en: What implementation trick should the lookahead hot loop use?
options: 每次都深拷贝整个网格对象
把所有候选先写入磁盘，排序后再处理
原地把三个值的计数减一，评分后再加回来
直接禁用所有包含重复点数的候选
codeSample:
hist[v1] -= 1; hist[v2] -= 1; hist[v3] -= 1
score = self._count_value_triples(hist)
hist[v1] += 1; hist[v2] += 1; hist[v3] += 1
why: 减一再恢复避免了热循环中的大量分配。只要恢复严格成对执行，外层状态保持正确。
why_en: In-place decrement-and-restore keeps lookahead allocation-free in the hot loop.
whenOtherWins: 如果代码可读性比速度更重要且候选很少，复制直方图会更不容易写错。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Hist[hist before] --> Minus[minus candidate]
  Minus --> Score[score rest]
  Score --> Restore[add counts back]
  Restore --> Next[next candidate]

Decrement the three value counts in place, score, then add them back.

q_en: Fill in: {{log10(2500) ≈ 3.4}} shows that the full tree can approach the {{10^112}} scale.
text: 文章用 {{log10(2500) ≈ 3.4}} 说明完整树规模会接近 {{10^112}} 级别。
why: log10(2500)≈3.4，如果 33 层都保持这个分支因子，叶子数量级接近 10^112；这个估算忽略了分支会随着牌变少而衰减，但数量级已足够说明完整博弈树不可行，一层 lookahead 是更现实的折中。
why_en: log10(2500) is about 3.4, so treating all 33 layers as having that branching factor puts the leaf count near 10^112 — even ignoring branching decay, that is obviously infeasible, which is why one-step lookahead is the practical compromise.
scenario: 第一层分支约 2500 种选择，你要估算完整博弈树规模的数量级，判断穷举回溯是否可行。

options: 每次落子都复制一份新棋盘对象
原地修改棋盘，递归结束后撤销落子
只记录列号，棋盘保持不变
把棋盘写入文件，用完再读回
why: 原地试探加撤销是回溯的标准形状，避免大量棋盘拷贝。关键是不管分支如何结束都要配对撤销。
why_en: Drop-and-undo backtracking avoids allocating a new board for every searched node.
whenOtherWins: 如果棋盘很小且实现撤销容易出错，复制状态可以换取更简单的正确性。

Write the board to a file and read it back afterward.

q: 填空：朴素 minimax 的复杂度约为 {{O(b^d)}}，其中 b 是分支因子，d 是搜索深度。
q_en: Fill in: naive minimax is about {{O(b^d)}}, where b is branching factor and d is search depth.
text: 朴素 minimax 的复杂度约为 {{O(b^d)}}，其中 b 是分支因子，d 是搜索深度。
why: 每层尝试所有合法列，树的叶子指数增长。列填满会降低实际分支，但上界仍按 b^d 理解。
why_en: Naive minimax grows exponentially with search depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复杂度上界：叶子数量随分支因子 b 的深度 d 次方增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(b to the d) means the leaf count grows as the branching factor raised to the power of the depth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个节点平均可展开的子节点数，Connect Four 里最多是 7（列数）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The branching factor is the average number of children per search node, at most 7 in Connect Four.

q: 填空：alpha 是 maximizer 当前保证的最好分数，beta 是 {{minimizer}} 当前保证的最好分数。
q_en: Fill in: alpha is the maximizer's best guaranteed score, and beta is the {{minimizer}}'s best guaranteed score.
text: alpha 是 maximizer 当前保证的最好分数，beta 是 {{minimizer}} 当前保证的最好分数。
why: alpha-beta 通过上下界判断剩余孩子是否还可能影响根节点选择。不能影响答案的子树会被跳过。
why_en: Alpha and beta track bounds that tell the search when remaining children cannot affect the result.

termDefinitions.meaning: maximizer 在当前路径上已经保证能拿到的最好分数（下界）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Alpha is the best score the maximizer is already guaranteed on the current search path.

termDefinitions.meaning: minimizer 在当前路径上已经保证能拿到的最好分数（上界）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Beta is the best score the minimizer is already guaranteed on the current search path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 minimax 上加两个边界值，一旦证明某分支不会影响根节点的选择就直接跳过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Alpha-beta pruning adds two bound values to minimax and skips any branch proven unable to change the root's choice.

q: alpha-beta 剪枝为什么是 sound 的？
q_en: Why is alpha-beta pruning sound?
options: 它只跳过对手已经不会允许、或当前方已经不会选择的分支
它随机跳过一半叶子，所以平均正确
它改变了 minimax 的评分规则
它只在棋盘满时才运行
why: 剪枝条件只在某分支已不可能改善上层选择时触发。因此结果与完整 minimax 一致，只是少算。
why_en: Alpha-beta pruning skips only subtrees that cannot change the minimax choice.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Alpha[alpha best max] --> Test{alpha >= beta}
  Beta[beta best min] --> Test
  Test -->|yes| Prune[Prune rest]
  Test -->|no| Search[Search child]

It randomly skips half the leaves, so it is correct on average.
It changes minimax's scoring rule.
It only runs once the board is full.

why_en: A large win score leaves room for depth-based tie-breaking without overwhelming win/loss semantics.

winner 检查规定只能在根节点运行一次

why_en: Terminal cases define the recursion boundary, while the table is mainly for nonterminal repeated states.
whenOtherWins: 有些引擎也缓存终局分数以提高命中率，但仍必须保证 winner 优先语义正确。

A TT-style cache table cannot store tuples at all.
A winner check is only allowed to run once, at the root node.
The valid columns must be shuffled before a table lookup.
tradeoff: 终局优先直接返回 vs 先查缓存表

scenario: 你要说明 Connect Four 四版解法的工程演进。
scenario_en: You need to explain the engineering evolution of the four Connect Four solver versions.
q: 把四个层级排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four solution layers in the correct order.
steps: 用 transposition table 缓存重复局面，减少迭代加深的重复搜索
用 alpha-beta 和中心优先排序剪掉不会改变 minimax 答案的子树
用朴素 minimax 建立对抗搜索的正确性模型
用迭代加深把固定深度问题改成固定预算问题
why: 第一步是正确搜索，后面三步分别处理剪枝、预算适配和重复状态。最终组合才满足 Phase 3。
why_en: The solution ladder is minimax for correctness, alpha-beta for pruning, iterative deepening for budget, and TT for reuse.
tradeoff: 先求对（minimax） vs 再求快（剪枝+预算+缓存三层优化）

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 minimax 上加两个边界值，一旦证明某分支不会影响根节点的选择就直接跳过。

q: 把 minimizer 节点触发 alpha-beta 剪枝的逻辑排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the minimizer-node alpha-beta cutoff logic in the correct order.
steps: minimizer 已经找到一个足够低的 child 分数，使 beta 降低
上层 maximizer 已经有 alpha，代表它可选择的更好下界
当 alpha >= beta 时，剩余 child 不可能让上层选择这个分支
停止搜索该 minimizer 的剩余孩子并返回当前界内值
why: 剪枝依赖上下界相遇：上层已有更好选择，本分支继续细算不会改变根答案。它不是猜测，而是边界证明。
why_en: Alpha-beta cuts when the bounds prove that remaining children cannot affect the ancestor's choice.

termDefinitions.meaning: maximizer 在当前路径上已经保证能拿到的最好分数（下界）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Alpha is the best score the maximizer is already guaranteed on the current search path.

termDefinitions.meaning: minimizer 在当前路径上已经保证能拿到的最好分数（上界）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Beta is the best score the minimizer is already guaranteed on the current search path.

q: 这组 benchmark 数据（huge: 5000 users, 25000 edges, scan-all 361.8ms, two-hop 7.6ms）说明了什么？
q_en: What design conclusion do these benchmark numbers show: huge has 5000 users, 25000 edges, scan-all takes 361.8ms, and two-hop takes 7.6ms?

The two-hop walk narrows the candidate space from the whole network to a local neighborhood, giving roughly a 48x measured speedup.
Both algorithms have identical asymptotic complexity, differing only by a constant factor.

why_en: The benchmark quantifies a real structural win: the 48x gap comes from narrowing the candidate space, not from a constant-factor tweak.

q: First-Fit 的规则是什么？
q_en: What is the First-Fit rule?
options: 对每个 item 都尝试所有已开 bin 的组合，挑出全局最优的分配方案
按输入顺序处理每个 item，放进第一个能同时满足两个容量的已开 bin；都放不下才新开一个 bin
把 item 和 bin 都随机打乱，反复重排直到凑出一个合法分配
不管当前 bin 是否还有空间，每个 item 都直接新开一个独立 bin
options_en: Try every combination across all opened bins for each item and pick the globally optimal assignment.
Process items in input order and place each one in the first already-open bin that satisfies both capacity limits; open a new bin only if none fit.
Shuffle items and bins randomly and keep reshuffling until a legal assignment appears.
Open a brand-new bin for every item regardless of whether an existing bin still has room.
why: First-Fit 是纯贪心：第一个合法位置就提交，不回头。它实现简单且保证约束有效。
why_en: First-Fit greedily places each item into the first existing bin that can hold it.
tradeoff: 先合法即提交的贪心速度 vs 穷举比较求全局最优
whenOtherWins: 如果输入顺序对抗性强，先排序的 First-Fit Decreasing 通常更稳。

q: 为什么 `break` 很关键？
q_en: Why is `break` critical here?
options: 没有 break 的话，后面每个 bin 的 `can_fit` 检查都会被强制跳过，永远判定为放不下
break 触发后会自动新开一个 bin，把当前 item 重新放进这个新开的 bin 里
break 会让后面所有 bin 的两个容量检查都被跳过，从而让放置流程整体变快
item 已经放置成功；继续扫描后面的 bin 可能造成重复放置，或者把 assignment 记录覆盖成错误的 bin id
options_en: Without break, the can_fit check on every later bin would be forced to skip and always report infeasible.
Triggering break automatically opens a new bin and re-places the current item into that new bin.
break skips both capacity checks on every remaining bin, making the whole placement loop faster.
The item is already placed; scanning later bins could double-place it or overwrite the assignment with the wrong bin id.
why: First-Fit 的定义就是第一个能放就停。继续循环既浪费，也可能覆盖记录。
why_en: First-Fit commits to the first feasible bin, so the bin loop must stop after placement.
tradeoff: 第一个可行 bin 立即停止 vs 继续扫描以寻找更优 bin
whenOtherWins: Best-Fit 需要扫描所有可行 bin 后再选剩余空间最小者，那时不能在第一个可行 bin 处 break。

q: First-Fit 装 n 个物品、已开 b 个 bin 时总体复杂度如何描述？
q_en: How should you describe First-Fit's total complexity for n items and b opened bins?
options: O(log n)，因为每次放置都在做二分查找
O(n · b)，最坏情况 b = n 时退化为 O(n²)
O(2ⁿ)，因为要枚举所有子集
O(1)，因为每个 item 只放一次就结束
options_en: O(log n), because each placement does a binary search.
O(n times b), which degrades to O(n squared) in the worst case when b equals n.
O(2 to the n), because it enumerates every subset.
O(1), because each item is placed exactly once.
why: 每个 item 最多扫一遍已有 bin，n×b 是 O(n·b)；最坏每个物品都新开 bin 时 b=n，退化成 O(n²)。这说明千级 catalog 下 First-Fit 仍够快，不必换算法。
why_en: First-Fit scans existing bins for each item, so n items times b bins gives O(n·b), which only degrades to O(n squared) when every item opens its own bin.

options: ascending 排序之后，can_fit 的两个容量检查会被跳过，让装箱结果直接变成非法

tradeoff: 先难后易（descending） vs 先易后难（ascending）

q: Best-Fit Decreasing 和 First-Fit Decreasing 的区别是什么？

options: BFD 完全不需要先排序这一步，只有 FFD 才需要先排序再放置
两者都先按 footprint 降序排序；BFD 把 item 放进剩余空间最少的可行 bin，FFD 放进扫到的第一个可行 bin

options_en: BFD skips the sorting step entirely; only FFD needs to sort before placing.
Both sort by descending footprint first; BFD places the item into the feasible bin with the least remaining room, while FFD places it into the first feasible bin scanned.
BFD ignores both the weight and size capacity limits, while only FFD checks them.
The two are completely equivalent in placement rule, sort order, and implementation complexity.

options: 直接告诉面试官，这个装箱方案已经没有任何办法可以再继续改进了，只能维持现状
建议删掉 weight 或 size 两个容量约束中的一个，用简化问题换取更少的 bin 数
建议把一部分 item 随机丢弃掉，用减少物品总数来减少最终的 bin 数

why_en: Naming BFD and exact search options shows the tradeoff between heuristic quality and optimality.

options_en: Compute a global safe lower bound across these dishes.
Check whether this recipe's content repeats.
Sort by finish time, start time, then dish index as a deterministic tie-break.
Force the selection of the single slowest available chef.

key = (end, start, index)
if best_key is None or key < best_key:

    best_move = (index, dish, step_index, station, chef, start, end)

steps: 计算安全 lower bound，若不可能 beat 当前 best 就剪枝

q: dish-order greedy 和 dispatch 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between dish-order greedy and dispatch?
options: dispatch 会对已经提交的选择做完整回溯撤销
greedy 锁定 dish 顺序；dispatch 每轮选局部最早完成的 ready step
greedy 执行完就能证明自己达到全局最优解
dispatch 调度时完全不维护 station_free 状态
options_en: Dispatch fully backtracks and undoes choices it already committed.
Greedy locks in dish order up front; dispatch picks the locally earliest-finishing ready step each round.
Greedy can prove it reaches the global optimum once it finishes.
Dispatch never tracks station_free state at all.
why: dispatch 延迟了承诺并允许 interleaving，但仍没有搜索；两者都可能被局部选择卡住。
why_en: Dispatch interleaves dishes by choosing among ready steps, but it remains a greedy one-pass scheduler.
tradeoff: 一次性锁定 dish 顺序 vs 每轮重新挑 ready step（都不做搜索/回溯）

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

q_en: What condition must a valid Maximize Unique Characters solution satisfy?
options: 选出的所有单词按字典序连续

q: 最自然的第一版搜索框架是什么？

q: 在朴素 include/skip 回溯中，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: In plain include/skip backtracking, which statements are correct?
options: skip 分支永远合法
include 分支必须先确认当前单词字符与 used 不相交
include 后必须在返回前撤销 current 和 used 的修改
到叶子节点时不需要更新 best
why: 跳过单词不会破坏合法性；选择单词必须无冲突，并且所有就地修改都要对称撤销，叶子或改进点都要维护 best。
why_en: Skip is always legal, include requires disjoint characters, and every mutation must be undone after the recursive call.
optionExplanations: 对：跳过不修改任何状态，不可能违反约束。
对：字符集合有交集时 include 非法，必须先判断。
对：current/used 是共享可变状态，退出前必须复原对称。
错：叶子或任何改进点都要检查并更新 best，否则丢最优解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: skipping mutates nothing, so it can never break legality.
Correct: overlapping characters make the include illegal, so check first.
Correct: current and used are shared mutable state and must be restored.
Wrong: every leaf or improvement must update best or the optimum is lost.
options_en: The skip branch is always legal.
The include branch must first confirm the word's characters are disjoint from used.
After including, current and used must be restored before returning.
There is no need to update best at a leaf node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个集合没有任何共同元素。

q: 哪段 Python 判断最直接表达「word 与已用字符没有冲突」？
q_en: Which Python check best says that word has no conflict with used?
options: if set(word) <= used:
if used.isdisjoint(set(word)):

why: 合法 include 的条件是两个字符集合交集为空，`isdisjoint` 正好表达这个判断。
why_en: The include branch is legal exactly when the word's character set is disjoint from the used-character set.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态已经是整数 bitmask，就应该用按位与判断，而不是再构造 set。
codeSample:
word_chars = set(word)
if used.isdisjoint(word_chars):
    current.append(word)

    current.pop()

对：两个集合没有交集，用 isdisjoint 一次调用直接表达。
错：长度比较和字符冲突无关，无法判断是否合法。
错：`word not in used` 是判断整词是否为成员，语义完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the subset direction is backwards and misses the disjoint check.
Correct: isdisjoint directly expresses zero character overlap.
Wrong: comparing lengths says nothing about character conflicts.
Wrong: `word not in used` checks whole-word membership, not character overlap.
options_en: Check whether word's character set is a subset of used.
Check whether used and word's character set are disjoint.
Check whether the word is longer than the used set.
Check whether word as a whole is a key in used.

q: 回溯 include 分支中忘记 `current.pop()` 或忘记从 `used` 移除刚加入字符，最直接的后果是什么？
q_en: What happens if the include branch forgets current.pop() or removing new chars from used?
options: 只会影响运行时间，不影响答案
兄弟分支会看到不属于自己的选择，导致错误剪枝或错误答案
递归深度会自动变浅
Python 会自动回滚局部变量

why_en: If mutations are not undone, sibling branches inherit stale state and the search can reject legal combinations or return a wrong result.
diagram:
flowchart TD

  Include --> Return[return without undo]
  Return --> Sibling[sibling sees abcd]

错：`used`/`current` 是可变对象，Python 不会自动帮你撤销。

Correct: leftover characters in used make sibling branches see false conflicts.
Wrong: recursion depth is driven by index i, unrelated to cleanup.
Wrong: used and current are mutable objects; Python never auto-restores them.

Sibling branches inherit stale state, causing wrong pruning or a wrong answer.
Recursion depth automatically becomes shallower.
Python automatically rolls back local variables.

对当前单词先尝试 skip 分支
若字符不冲突，加入当前单词并递归 include 分支
返回 include 分支后撤销加入的单词和字符
递归状态从第 i 个单词和当前 used 集合开始
why: 朴素搜索围绕同一状态展开两个分支，任何 include 的状态修改都要在回到父帧前恢复。

q: 朴素 include/skip 回溯的最坏时间复杂度最接近哪一个？
q_en: What is the closest worst-case time complexity for plain include/skip backtracking?
options: O(n log n)
O(m · 2^n)，m 是单词长度量级
why: n 个单词各有选或不选两种分支，最坏有 2^n 个组合；每帧还要做与单词长度相关的集合检查或更新。
why_en: The worst case has two branches per word, producing 2^n combinations with per-frame work proportional to word length.
optionExplanations: 错：这是排序级复杂度，回溯树的分支数不是 n log n。
对：n 个二元决策给出 2^n 组合，每帧还有 O(m) 的集合操作。
错：26 是字母表大小的常数，和单词数 n 的搜索树无关。
错：n^3 是多项式，掩盖了每个单词二元分支带来的指数增长。

Correct: n binary decisions give 2^n combinations, each frame doing O(m) set work.
Wrong: 26 is the constant alphabet size, unrelated to the search tree over n words.
Wrong: n cubed is polynomial and hides the exponential branching per word.
scenario: 词表里有 n 个单词，每个单词长度约 m；你要预估朴素 include/skip 回溯在最坏输入下的运行时间量级，判断这套方案能不能扛住较大的 n。
scenario_en: The word list has n words of length about m; you need the worst-case runtime scale for plain include/skip backtracking to judge whether it can handle a larger n.
options_en: O(n log n).
O(m times 2 to the n), where m is the word-length scale.
O(26 squared).
O(n cubed).

q: 为什么包含大量二三字母短词的数据集会让朴素回溯变慢？
q_en: Why do many two- or three-letter words make plain backtracking slow?
options: 短词冲突少，合法分支能扎得很深
短字符串同样能转换成 set
短词字符少，通常覆盖不了全部字母
短词长度不会让递归失败返回
why: 冲突本身是朴素回溯唯一的自然剪枝；短词互相冲突少，就会保留大量深层分支。
why_en: Short words collide with few others, so conflict-based pruning leaves many deep legal branches alive.
optionExplanations: 对：冲突是唯一的自然剪枝，短词冲突少，深层分支大量存活。
错：任何长度的字符串都能用 set() 转换，和这无关。
错：短词字符少，远达不到覆盖完整字母表。
错：递归返回由函数结构决定，跟单词长短无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: conflict is the only natural pruning, and short words rarely conflict.
Wrong: any string converts to a set() regardless of length.
Wrong: short words have few characters and rarely cover the full alphabet.
Wrong: recursion always returns based on control flow, unrelated to word length.
options_en: Short words rarely conflict, so legal branches can go deep.
Short strings convert into a set just as well as long ones.
Short words have few characters and rarely cover the full alphabet.
Word length has no effect on whether recursion returns.

q: 应该引入哪类优化？
q_en: What kind of optimization should be added?
options: branch-and-bound，用乐观上界剪掉无望子树
把递归改成 while 循环但不改变剪枝
把所有单词拼接成一个字符串
只保留第一个合法组合

why_en: Branch-and-bound prunes a subtree when an optimistic upper bound proves it cannot beat the current best.
whenOtherWins: 如果能推导出多项式最优算法，优先换算法；这里没有这种结构，剪枝是现实杠杆。

flowchart TD

错：拼接字符串会丢失哪个字符属于哪个单词的边界信息。
错：第一个合法解不一定是覆盖最多字符的最优解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: estimate an optimistic ceiling per frame and cut when it can't win.
Wrong: swapping recursion for a loop doesn't reduce visited branches.
Wrong: concatenating words loses which characters belong to which word.
Wrong: the first legal solution is not guaranteed to be the optimal one.
options_en: Branch-and-bound: prune hopeless subtrees using an optimistic upper bound.
Convert the recursion to a while loop without changing the pruning.
Concatenate all words into a single string.
Keep only the first legal combination found.

q: 补全 suffix-union 上界：
q_en: Fill in the suffix-union upper bound.
text: 在索引 i 的递归帧，剩余单词最多还能贡献 {{suffix_union[i] - used}} 中的字符，所以总覆盖上界是 {{len(used)}} + {{len(suffix_union[i] - used)}}。
why: 这个上界假设剩余所有新字符都能一起拿到，因此一定偏乐观，拿它剪枝是安全的。
why_en: The suffix-union bound is safe because it overestimates how many fresh characters the remaining words could add.

flowchart LR
  Used[used chars] --> Now[current count]
  Suffix[suffix union i] --> Rem[new possible chars]
  Rem --> Bound[optimistic total]
  Now --> Bound

termDefinitions.meaningEn: suffix_union is a right-to-left precomputed array whose i-th entry is the union of character sets from index i to the end.

q: 为什么 `len(used) + len(suffix_union[i] - used) <= best_count` 时可以直接 return？
q_en: Why can we return when len(used) + len(suffix_union[i] - used) <= best_count?
options: 因为这说明当前分支一定非法
因为即使拿到剩余所有新字符，也不能严格超过 best
因为 suffix_union 只包含已选择单词
因为等号时一定能找到同样好的不同答案
why: 搜索只需要改进 best；当乐观上界都不大于 best 时，任何后代都不可能成为新最优。
why_en: If even the optimistic ceiling cannot strictly beat the best count, no descendant can improve the answer.
optionExplanations: 错：合法性和上界大小是两回事，剪枝不代表分支非法。
对：上界是最乐观估计，连它都赢不了 best 就没必要往下搜。
错：suffix_union 恰好相反，装的是尚未处理的剩余单词。
错：打平不保证存在别的等好解，只是不值得继续搜。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: legality and bound size are unrelated; pruning doesn't mean illegal.
Correct: even the most optimistic estimate can't beat best, so stop searching.

q: 哪段更新逻辑最符合文章里的 BFS 模板？
q_en: Which update block best matches the BFS template?

parent[neighbor] = None; visited.clear()  # 每一步都清空已有的搜索进度

q: 哪段 clone 写法能避免候选列表共享 bug？
q_en: Which clone implementation avoids the shared-candidate-list bug?
options: np = puzzle; nrp = row_poss; ncp = col_poss
np = puzzle.clone(); nrp = [list(x) for x in row_poss]; ncp = [list(x) for x in col_poss]
np = puzzle.clone(); nrp = row_poss; ncp = col_poss
np = puzzle.clone(); nrp = list(row_poss); ncp = list(col_poss)
options_en: Reuse the same puzzle and candidate lists with no copying at all.
Clone the puzzle, and deep-copy every row and column candidate list.
Clone the puzzle grid but keep sharing the same row and column candidate lists.
Clone the puzzle and copy the outer candidate lists, but the inner lists stay shared.
why: grid 和每条线的候选列表都要复制；只复制 grid 仍会让传播共享并修改父分支的候选列表。
why_en: A search branch needs independent copies of both the puzzle grid and every row and column candidate list.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据结构是持久化不可变结构，可以共享旧版本并返回新版本；普通 list 不能这样共享。
tradeoff: 深拷贝 grid+候选列表（安全但多花内存和时间）vs 共享引用（省内存但会互相污染）
codeSample:
np = puzzle.clone()
nrp = [list(x) for x in row_poss]   # 深拷贝每行候选
ncp = [list(x) for x in col_poss]   # 深拷贝每列候选
np.set_cell(r, c, state)
result = _search(np, nrp, ncp)

options: 因为给行排序一定能把 NP-hard 问题变成 O(n)
因为 row-by-row 在所有 15×15 题目上都已经足够快

Because row-by-row is already fast enough on every 15 by 15 puzzle.
Because column clues are actually redundant and can be deleted.

why: row_bt 的问题不是单纯顺序不好，而是没有把列约束用来推导格子；传播把两轴信息都前置使用。
why_en: The key is that columns are not just validators; they should actively shrink possibilities and force cells.
whenOtherWins: 如果列约束非常弱或题目只要求小规模，row-by-row 加简单剪枝也可能足够。

q: 这条链对并行调度设计意味着什么？

why: 链上任务必须严格串行，1+8+8+8+1=26 秒是任何调度都无法突破的下界，所以关键链必须优先拿到 worker。

  B1 --> B2[build 2]
  B2 --> B3[build 3]
  B3 --> Final[finalize]
  Final --> Bound[critical path lower bound 26]
scenario: critical-path graph 里 setup→build-1→build-2→build-3→finalize 的 duration 分别是 1/8/8/8/1 秒，这五个任务必须严格顺序执行。
scenario_en: In the critical-path graph, setup, build-1, build-2, build-3, and finalize take 1, 8, 8, 8, and 1 seconds and must run in strict order.
options_en: Adding enough workers can compress this chain to finish faster.
Splitting the chain across workers in parallel can beat this lower bound.
No matter how many workers you have, the makespan can never beat this chain's total duration, so the scheduler must keep it running back to back.
This chain is no more important than the independent tasks, so run order doesn't matter.

q: fixed-order scheduler 在 critical-path graph 上为什么得到 38 秒？

    et, tn, wi = heapq.heappop(events)
    completed.add(tn)
    completion_times[tn] = et
    heapq.heappush(workers, (et, wi))
# all workers finishing at end_time are freed first

  Drain --> Assign
  Event -->|no| Finish[return schedule]

scenario: 招聘人在电话中途说：「说实话，我们现在还没到能从 Meta/TikTok 这种级别招人的阶段。」这是一个软拒绝信号。
scenario_en: Mid-call the recruiter says, "Honestly, we're not hiring at the Meta/TikTok level yet." It's a soft-rejection signal.
q: 听到这句软拒绝，下一步最该怎么做？
q_en: What's the right next move when you hear this soft rejection?
options: 当作没听见，假装那句软拒绝不存在，顺着他的话继续答下一个技术问题，指望级别的顾虑自己会过去
顺着他点头：「嗯，可能我确实更适合更成熟一点的团队」，然后主动把话题岔到别的项目上去
直接接住并重定级别：「我不是来要 senior 头衔的——你描述的 PSP 集成、税务、checkout 正是我想端到端 own 的活，我冲的是问题不是级别。」
反驳他：「我在 Meta/TikTok 带过更大的 scope，这个级别对我其实偏低了」，坚持自己配得上更高职位
tradeoff: 正面接住 vs 假装没听见：假装能躲开当场那点尴尬，代价是对方带着「不匹配」的结论挂断电话。
why: 软拒绝必须当场正面接住，并把级别重新框成「我要的就是这摊活」——我冲的是问题不是头衔。装作没听见，通话结束时对方只会认定我不匹配。
why_en: Address a soft rejection head-on and reframe the level right away — I'm here for the problem, not the title — because ignoring it ends the call with them sure I misfit.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实只想要更高级别的岗位、不愿降级做这摊活时，才该顺着「级别不够」结束——那说明这个岗位本就不适合你。
options_en: Pretend the soft rejection didn't happen, keep answering his next technical question, and hope the level concern just passes.
Nod along — "Yeah, maybe I'm a better fit for a more established team" — and then steer the topic to a different project.

Address it head-on and reframe the level: "I'm not here for a senior title — the PSP, tax, and checkout work you described is exactly what I want to own end-to-end. I'm here for the problem, not the level."
Push back: "I've owned bigger scope at Meta/TikTok, this level is actually low for me," insisting you deserve a higher role.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方看你没接信号，通话结束时默认你不匹配。
等于替对方把自己淘汰，白丢一个机会。
对方从「你太 senior」松动为「他要的就是这活」，软拒绝被你当场接回。
坐实 over-positioned 的顾虑，把软拒绝推成硬拒绝。

They shift from "too senior" to "this is the work he wants" — you catch the soft no in the moment.
You confirm the over-positioned worry and push the soft no into a hard no.

scenario: 招聘人用整整 2 分钟介绍了岗位：数字支付产品、PSP 集成、税务处理、checkout、tap-to-pay。现在轮到你做 self-intro。
scenario_en: The recruiter just spent two full minutes describing the role: digital payments, PSP integrations, tax handling, checkout, tap-to-pay. Now it's your turn to self-intro.
q: 你的 self-intro 该怎么开头？
q_en: How should your self-intro open?
options: 挑他刚说的一个信号反射回去：「你说的 PSP 集成和 checkout，正好对上我在 Meta 做的从商家输入到后端的多步骤数据流，我想在支付方向深入。」
从最早的实习开始，按时间顺序把简历从头到尾讲一遍，指望对方自己听出哪一段跟这个支付岗位相关
直接开讲你最自豪的 Promotion Day 项目，细节拉满，却完全不提它跟 PSP、checkout 有没有关系
先反问一句「能再把这个岗位的职责和技术栈说一遍吗」，用澄清把开场的主动权交回给对方
tradeoff: 先反射信号 vs 直接背简历：背简历省掉当场读岗位的功夫，代价是开场没有连接，对方得自己猜你合不合适。
why: 先反射对方刚描述的一个具体信号，再桥接到能对上的项目——先说连接点，再说简历。开局若是流水账，对方感觉不到你和这个岗位的关系。
why_en: Reflect back one concrete signal they just described, then bridge to a matching project — lead with the connection, not a chronological resume dump.
whenOtherWins: 只有当对方完全没描述岗位、直接说「介绍下你自己」时，才用一段结构化的背景概述来开头。
options_en: Reflect one signal back: "The PSP and checkout work you described maps to the multi-step data flow I built at Meta from business input to backend — I want to go deeper on payments."
Start from your earliest internship and walk the resume chronologically to now, hoping they figure out which part relates to this payments role.
Launch into your proudest project (Promotion Day) in full detail, never tying it to PSP or checkout at all.
First ask, "Could you repeat the role's responsibilities and stack?" — using clarification to hand the opening back to them.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻感到你听懂了岗位，也看到你背景对得上。

项目再强，跟支付无关就显得你没在听。

scenario_en: They just spent two minutes describing the role/product, then say "tell me about yourself." You want a self-intro that connects to the role.
q: 把「连接岗位的 self-intro」四步排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four steps of a role-connected self-intro in the correct order.
steps: 桥接到一个能对上这个信号的、你自己做过的项目
完整听完对方对岗位/产品的描述，先不急着开口
点出你最想在这个方向深入的地方，把话头留给对方
从他的描述里挑一个具体信号，用一句话反射回去
why: 顺序是先听、再反射一个具体信号、再桥接到我的项目、最后留一个想深入的钩子——连接永远排在简历前面。
why_en: The order is listen fully, reflect one concrete signal back, bridge to my matching project, then leave a hook — the connection always comes before the resume.

q: 面试前，每个要提到的项目该准备好哪三件技术底细？
q_en: For each project you'll mention, which three technical details must you have ready?
text: 每个会在面试里提到的项目，提前准备三件事：(1) 数据在{{后端}}怎么存，(2) {{前端}}怎么把更新发过去，(3) {{schema}} 大概长什么样。
text_en: For each project you'll mention, prep three things: (1) how data is stored on the {{backend}}, (2) how the {{frontend}} sends updates, (3) what the {{schema}} looks like.
why: 我在 self-intro 里提了 Meta onboarding，却答不出步骤状态怎么存——那是我自己的项目。每个要提的项目都先备好这三件，追问就不会卡。
why_en: I described my own Meta onboarding project but couldn't say how step state was stored — prep backend storage, frontend update path, and schema for every project I'll mention.

why_en: Blanking on how my own project stored state is embarrassing; the real fix is before the call — rehearse storage, update path, and schema for every project I'll mention.
whenOtherWins: 只有当追问的是一个你确实没参与、边界之外的模块时，「这块不是我负责、我需要看下代码」才是诚实且合适的答法。

scenario_en: This is the fifth interview asking "why are you leaving TikTok." Across companies you've given different directions — sometimes "end-to-end ownership, closer to the customer," but on a VC call "go deeper into infra platform and reliability."
q: 该怎么处理这个反复出问题的答案？
q_en: How should you handle this repeatedly-fumbled answer?
options: 每家公司临场即兴，挑当下听起来最顺的方向说
定一个真实且一致的方向（端到端 ownership、更接近客户痛点），每次都这么说，练到自动
看岗位是平台还是产品——平台就说 infra、产品就说 ownership
干脆说得模糊些（「想成长、想学新东西」），避免自相矛盾
tradeoff: 固定一个方向 vs 见人下菜：临场换方向听着灵活，代价是招聘人一交叉比对，方向漂移就露馅。
why: 招聘人网络会互相对信息，方向反复会露馅。选一个真实的方向——端到端 ownership、更接近客户痛点——每次一致，练到脱口而出。
why_en: Recruiter networks compare notes, so pick one true direction — end-to-end ownership, closer to customer pain — and say it consistently until it's automatic.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实在专门投基础设施岗位时，才该整体切到 infra 方向——但也要全程只用那一个方向，不能来回混。

Fix one true, consistent direction (end-to-end ownership, closer to customer pain) and drill it until automatic.
Switch by role — say infra for platform jobs, ownership for product jobs.
Keep it vague ("want to grow, learn new things") to avoid contradicting yourself.

q: 「why startup」的答案里，比「end-to-end ownership」更具体的那句升级短语是什么？
q_en: In the "why startup" answer, what's the upgrade phrase that's more concrete than "end-to-end ownership"?
text: 「why startup」比「end-to-end ownership」更具体的升级说法是：{{tighter connection between engineering work and customer pain}}——强调工作离真实问题更近，而不只是 own 得更多。
text_en: The upgrade over "end-to-end ownership" for the why-startup answer is: {{tighter connection between engineering work and customer pain}} — the work sits closer to a real problem, not just owning more.
why: 「end-to-end ownership」太泛，升级成「工作和客户痛点之间更紧密的连接」——在大公司一个小改动要 5 个团队、3 个月对齐，我想直接看到这种连接。
why_en: "End-to-end ownership" is vague, so upgrade it to a tighter connection between engineering work and customer pain — in a big org a small change means five teams and three months of alignment.

scenario: 面试快结束，面试官问「你有什么想问我的吗？」这是你连续第六次面试走到这一步。
scenario_en: The interview is wrapping up and the interviewer asks, "Any questions for me?" This is the sixth interview in a row you've reached this point.
q: 前五次你都没问出实质问题——这次该怎么做？
q_en: You asked nothing substantive the last five times — what should you do now?
options: 笑着说「你介绍得很全面，我要问的其实都覆盖到了，暂时没有问题」，就此把反问环节收掉
只问流程性的问题：面试还有几轮、大概什么时候出结果、下一步是谁来面
随口抛一个谁都能问的泛问题，比如「公司文化怎么样？团队氛围好不好？」
问两个会前写在纸上的实质问题（如：团队现在最大的、还没定的技术决策是什么？工程师怎么直接接触客户反馈？）
why: 连续六次没问实质问题已成模式。每次会前把两个实质问题写在纸上，不管通话怎样都问出来——这是显示我认真评估岗位的地方。
why_en: Six interviews with no real questions is a pattern; write two substantive questions on paper before every call and ask them no matter how the call went.
whenOtherWins: 如果你原本想问的两个问题在前面聊天里都已被自然回答，就现场追一个更深的后续问题，而不是硬套清单。
options_en: Smile and say, "You covered everything really well — the things I'd ask are already answered, so no questions for now," and close the round out.
Only ask process questions: how many rounds are left, roughly when you'll hear back, who's interviewing next.
Toss out a generic question anyone could ask, like "What's the company culture like? Is the team a good vibe?"
Ask two substantive questions written on paper beforehand (e.g., the biggest open technical decision the team faces; how engineers get direct customer feedback).

scenario: 你问了团队结构，面试官给了很实在的回答（30 人、7 名工程师、扁平层级、每个工程师都直接和客户交流）。现在轮到你接话。
scenario_en: You asked about team structure and got a real answer (30 people, 7 engineers, flat hierarchy, every engineer talks to customers directly). Now it's your turn again.
q: 得到这个好答案后，接下来最该做什么？
q_en: After getting that good answer, what's the best next move?
options: 顺着深挖一个实质后续问题：「你说工程师直接和客户交流——通常怎么发生的？是陪着参加销售电话，还是通过产品反馈异步进行？」
顺势点点头，然后转去问流程性的问题：面试还剩几轮、结果大概什么时候出、下一步谁来面
只回一句「明白了，听起来挺有意思」，就把反问环节收掉，没有接着往下追
跳到一个跟刚才回答完全无关的新话题，比如薪资、假期或者能不能远程办公
tradeoff: 深挖一层 vs 退回流程：直接收口省事，代价是等于告诉对方「我没别的想问了」，好奇心没展示出来。
why: 一个好问题后面跟着流程问题，读起来就是「我问完了」。真正的好答案值得顺着再深挖一层，展示我在认真消化对方说的话。
why_en: One good question followed by a process question reads as "I ran out"; a strong answer deserves a deeper substantive follow-up that shows I'm actually engaging.
whenOtherWins: 如果时间确实快到、面试官已经在收尾，那用一个简短的流程/下一步问题收口是合适的。
options_en: Dig one layer deeper with a substantive follow-up: "You said engineers talk to customers directly — how does that usually happen? Sitting in on sales calls, or async through product feedback?"
Nod along, then switch to process questions: how many rounds are left, when you'll hear back, who's interviewing next.
Just say "Got it, that's interesting" and wrap up the questions without going any deeper.
Jump to a topic unrelated to their answer, like salary, vacation, or whether remote work is allowed.

scenario: 面试快结束，面试官抛来一个开放问题：「你希望团队记住你什么？」这家 Alex AI 做 AI 招聘系统；你在 Meta 做过 AI onboarding，在 TikTok 做过面向广告主的规模化产品界面。
scenario_en: At the close, the interviewer asks an open question: "What would you want the team to remember you for?" Alex AI builds an AI recruiter; you built AI onboarding at Meta and an advertiser-facing scaled product interface at TikTok.
q: 这个开放收尾问题，怎么答最好？
q_en: How do you best answer this open closing question?
options: 给一句泛泛的热情：「我真的很期待能加入、和你们一起努力工作、快速成长，成为团队的一份子。」
打「快速学习」牌：「我是个学得很快的人，不管什么技术栈、什么领域，给我一点时间都能很快上手。」
一个具体连接：「我已经做过你们需要的两面——Meta 的 AI onboarding，和 TikTok 规模化的用户端产品界面，我不是来学这些的。」
谦虚地说自己还有很多东西要学、经验也许还不够，但保证会非常拼、加班加点也要补上来
tradeoff: 具体连接 vs 泛泛热情：热情谁都会说，代价是转身就被忘，你已具备的匹配一点没留下。
why: 这个开放问题是礼物，别退回泛泛的热情。用一个具体连接——我已经做过你们需要的两面（AI 层 + 用户端产品），不是来学的——才会被记住。
why_en: This open question is a gift; don't default to generic enthusiasm — leave a specific connection (I've already built both sides you need) that they'll actually remember.
whenOtherWins: 如果你和这个岗位的连接确实不强，那与其硬编一个假连接，不如诚实说你最想快速补上的一块——但那也说明这家匹配度本就不高。
options_en: Offer generic enthusiasm: "I'm really excited to join, work hard with you all, grow fast, and be part of the team."
Play the fast-learner card: "I pick things up quickly — whatever the stack or domain, give me a little time and I'll be up to speed."
A specific connection: "I've already built both sides you need — Meta's AI onboarding and TikTok's scaled user-facing product. I'm not here to learn those."
Humbly say you still have a lot to learn and maybe not enough experience, but you'll work extra hard and put in the hours to catch up.
optionScenarioImpacts: 泛泛热情，任何候选人都能说，转身就忘。
「学得快」回避了这个展示具体价值的机会。
具体连接留下记忆点，直接对上他们的需求。
强调不足反而弱化了你已具备的匹配。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Generic enthusiasm any candidate could say, forgotten instantly.
"Fast learner" dodges the chance to show specific value.
A concrete connection sticks and maps straight to their need.
Emphasizing gaps undercuts the fit you already have.

scenario: 面试官在 42 分钟处暂停对话，说「你每道题前都停顿很久」，并问你是不是在用 AI；她说技术轮会上检测。
scenario_en: At minute 42 the interviewer paused the call to say "you pause a lot before every answer" and asked if you were using AI, adding that detection will be added in technical rounds.
q: 每题前长时间停顿、被怀疑用 AI——标准修复是什么？
q_en: Long pauses before every answer that trigger an AI suspicion — what's the standard fix?
text: 停顿感 / AI 嫌疑的修复：面试前做 {{10}} 分钟出声预热，凭记忆、计时回答 {{3-4}} 个问题；如果用笔记，只写{{关键词}}（如「trade-offs: speed vs safety」），不要写整句。
text_en: Fix for the pausing / AI-perception flag: a {{10}}-minute out-loud warmup before the call, answering {{3-4}} questions from memory and timed; keep notes as {{single keywords}}, not full sentences.
why: 有没有真用 AI 不重要，长停顿的模式让人觉得我在读 AI。会前 10 分钟出声预热，把答案先流起来；笔记只留关键词，不然会照着念。
why_en: Whether or not AI was used, the long-pause pattern looks like reading from a bot, so warm up out loud for ten minutes and keep notes as keywords, not sentences.

q: Meta 外面的人听不懂「HAC」「PRAC」——面试里该分别说成什么？
q_en: Outsiders don't understand "HAC" or "PRAC" — what should you say instead in an interview?
text: 面试里别说 Meta 内部黑话：把「HAC」说成 {{PHP 后端}}（Hack 是 PHP 派生的服务端语言），把「PRAC」说成 {{React 前端}}。公司名可以说，内部项目代号不行。
text_en: Don't say Meta-internal jargon in interviews: say {{PHP backend}} instead of "HAC" (Hack is a PHP-derived server language), and {{React frontend}} instead of "PRAC". The company name is fine; internal codenames are not.
why: 「HAC」「PRAC」是 Meta 内部对 Hack 和 React 的缩写，外面的人听到是乱码。说「PHP 后端」「React 前端」，对方一听就懂。
why_en: "HAC" and "PRAC" are Meta-internal shorthand for Hack and React that sound like gibberish outside; say "PHP backend" and "React frontend" instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 内部用的一种 PHP 派生的服务端语言；对外说「PHP 后端」更好懂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hack is Meta's PHP-derived server-side language; say "PHP backend" so outsiders understand.

scenario: 面试官问「你为什么想来我们公司？」这家 Alex AI 做的是 AI 招聘系统。你在 Meta 做过 AI onboarding，在 TikTok 做过面向广告主的复杂工作流界面。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks "Why do you want to work here?" Alex AI builds an AI recruiter. You built AI onboarding at Meta and an advertiser-facing complex-workflow interface at TikTok.
q: 「为什么选这家公司」怎么答才到位？
q_en: How do you answer "why this company" well?
options: 给一串对任何创业公司都成立的通用理由：「我就是喜欢创业公司——product focus、团队小、节奏快、能端到端 own 一个东西。」
点一个具体产品事实连到你真做过的东西：「AI 招聘系统要 AI 层 + 面向用户的产品——正好是我在 Meta 做的 AI onboarding 和 TikTok 的广告主界面这两条腿。」
夸他们的融资和团队规模：「你们刚融完一轮、团队还在扩，势头很好，我觉得前景不错、很想上车。」
「我一直想进 AI 这个方向，你们做的正好是 AI，我觉得挺契合的，很想加入你们团队一起做。」
tradeoff: 具体产品事实 vs 通用创业理由：通用理由对每家都成立，代价是零区分度，证明不了你为这家做过功课。
why: 「product focus、team 小、end-to-end」对任何创业公司都成立，等于没说。要点一个具体产品事实，连到我真做过的东西——这才证明我为这家做了功课。
why_en: "Product focus, small team, end-to-end" is true of any startup and says nothing; name one specific product fact and connect it to something I actually built.
whenOtherWins: 如果这家公司你确实只被通用的创业属性吸引、找不到具体连接点，那可能说明匹配度不够——但至少该在会前研究出一个具体事实。
options_en: Give reasons true of any startup: "I just love startups — product focus, small team, fast pace, owning something end-to-end."

Name a specific product fact and connect it to what you built: "An AI recruiter needs an AI layer plus a user-facing product — exactly the two legs of my Meta AI onboarding and my TikTok advertiser interface."
Praise their funding and team size: "You just raised a round and the team's still growing — there's real momentum, the outlook looks great and I want in."
"I've always wanted to move into AI, and you happen to do AI, so it feels like a good fit and I'd love to join the team and build with you."
optionScenarioImpacts: 通用创业理由，对方听过一百遍，零区分度。
具体产品事实 + 真实经历，证明你研究过也匹配。
夸融资规模跟你能做什么无关，留不下印象。
「你们做 AI」太泛，没连到你具体做过什么。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: A generic startup reason they've heard a hundred times, zero differentiation.
A specific product fact plus real experience proves research and fit.
Praising funding says nothing about what you can do.
"You do AI" is too vague and connects to nothing you built.

scenario: 这是一个 VC 的 sourcing 电话——招聘人手上有 3-5 家 portfolio 公司要给你匹配，不是在筛你进某一个具体岗位。你的 self-intro 快讲完了。
scenario_en: This is a VC sourcing call — the recruiter has 3-5 portfolio companies to match you to, not one specific job to screen you for. Your self-intro is wrapping up.
q: self-intro 该用哪种框架收尾？
q_en: How should the self-intro close in this framing?
options: 给一个可匹配的画像：「我在找 early-stage AI 公司，想做最早的工程师之一、端到端 own 一个产品面，哪家 portfolio 对得上都想聊。」
像在投单个岗位那样收尾：「我在找一个能让我做 X 的后端工程师岗位」，把自己框死在一个具体职位上，让 VC 没法跨公司匹配
反过来问他们：「你们现在具体在招哪个岗位？职责、技术栈、团队是什么样的？」，把方向的皮球又踢回给对方
只顺着简历把过往经历从头到尾又讲一遍，完全不提自己想要什么阶段、什么问题域、什么方向的公司
why: VC 是在把我匹配到 3-5 家公司，不是筛一个岗位。要给可匹配的材料——公司规模、问题域、团队结构，以「我想做早期工程师、最擅长 X」收尾，而不是「我在找一个做 X 的岗位」。
why_en: A VC is matching me to several portfolio companies, so give a matchable profile — company stage, problem domain, team structure — framed as "I want to be an early hire best at X," not "I'm looking for a role that does X."
whenOtherWins: 如果这通电话其实是某家公司自己的招聘人在招一个确定的岗位，那就该针对那个具体岗位来定位，而不是给宽泛画像。
options_en: Give a matchable profile: "I'm looking for early-stage AI companies where I can be one of the first engineers and own a product surface end-to-end — whichever portfolio company fits, I'd love to talk."
Close like you're applying to one job: "I'm looking for a backend engineer role where I do X," boxing yourself into one position so the VC can't match you across companies.
Turn it around and ask them: "Which specific role are you hiring for? What are the responsibilities, stack, and team like?" — punting the direction back to them.
Just recount your past experience end to end from the resume again, without saying what stage, problem domain, or direction of company you want.
optionScenarioImpacts: 给出可匹配画像，VC 能立刻往 portfolio 里对号入座。
单岗位口径，VC 没法把你匹配到多家公司。
把匹配的主动权丢回去，VC 要的是你的画像。
只讲过去、不讲想要，VC 无从匹配。

scenario: 面试官给「设计一个欺诈检测系统」这类模糊题，你要在 ~45 分钟内把它变成一个有条理的设计。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives an ambiguous prompt like 'design a fraud detection system' and you have ~45 min to turn it into a coherent design.
q: ML 系统设计的 6 步框架依次是哪 6 步？
q_en: What are the six steps of the ML system design framework, in order?
why: 顺序是「先定问题再谈解法」：澄清范围→数据策略→模型设计→评估→部署上线→监控迭代，监控发现漂移再回流到数据策略形成闭环。它是思考+沟通工具，不是死板脚本。
why_en: The order goes problem first then solution: clarify scope, data strategy, model design, evaluation, serving, monitoring, with monitoring feeding back into data strategy as a loop.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["1 澄清&范围"] --> B["2 数据策略"]
  B --> C["3 模型设计"]
  C --> D["4 评估"]
  D --> E["5 部署上线"]
  E --> F["6 监控迭代"]
  F -. 漂移回流 .-> B
options: 1 澄清与范围 → 2 数据策略 → 3 模型设计 → 4 评估 → 5 部署上线 → 6 监控迭代；监控回流到数据策略
1 模型设计 → 2 数据策略 → 3 澄清范围 → 4 评估 → 5 部署上线 → 6 监控迭代；先定模型再倒推数据
1 澄清范围 → 2 模型设计 → 3 数据策略 → 4 部署上线 → 5 评估 → 6 监控；评估放到上线之后再补
1 数据策略 → 2 澄清范围 → 3 模型设计 → 4 评估 → 5 监控 → 6 部署上线；先囤数据再定问题
options_en: 1 clarify & scope → 2 data strategy → 3 model design → 4 evaluation → 5 serving → 6 monitoring; monitoring loops back to data.
1 model design → 2 data strategy → 3 clarify scope → 4 evaluation → 5 serving → 6 monitoring; pick the model then back-fit data.
1 clarify scope → 2 model design → 3 data strategy → 4 serving → 5 evaluation → 6 monitoring; evaluate only after launch.
1 data strategy → 2 clarify scope → 3 model design → 4 evaluation → 5 monitoring → 6 serving; hoard data before defining the problem.
optionExplanations: 对；每一步都建立在上一步之上，先钉住问题再往下走，监控闭环回流到数据是持续改进的关键。
把模型放最前面就是没定清问题和数据就选架构，等于先造引擎再想车往哪开。
评估必须在上线前完成——线下指标不过关就上线，等于拿用户流量做第一次验证。
先囤数据再定问题会白收：没有明确目标，数据口径往往对不上，大批返工。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — each step builds on the prior one; pin the problem first, and the monitoring loop back to data drives continuous improvement.
Putting model design first means choosing an architecture before problem and data are set — building the engine before deciding where the car goes.
Evaluation must finish before launch; shipping without offline checks means validating on real user traffic first.
Hoarding data before defining the problem wastes effort: with no clear target the labels are off-spec and get redone in bulk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊 ML 题变成设计的 6 步顺序脚手架：澄清→数据→模型→评估→部署→监控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A six-step scaffold that turns an ambiguous ML prompt into a design: clarify, data, model, evaluation, serving, monitoring.

scenario: 面试官只说「推荐视频」，没给目标。你有 3-5 分钟做第 1 步问题澄清。
scenario_en: The interviewer just says 'recommend videos' with no stated goal; you have 3-5 min for step 1, problem clarification.
q: 第 1 步该先做什么，才算把模糊题目收敛成可设计的问题？
q_en: In step 1, what do you do first to converge an ambiguous prompt into a designable problem?
why: 先追问目标用户、业务目标、规模、延迟，把「推荐视频」收敛成一个精确目标（最大化观看时长？多样性？降低流失？）。面试官正是在听你「先收敛再解题」。
why_en: First ask about target user, business objective, scale, and latency to converge 'recommend videos' into a precise goal, because interviewers listen for whether you narrow before solving.
whenOtherWins: 若题目已经把目标、规模、延迟都给死（如「已定：优化 CTR，1M QPS，<50ms」），澄清可以很短，直接进入数据策略。
options: 先默认一个目标（比如最大化点击），直接开始画模型架构，节省澄清时间
追问目标用户、业务目标、规模、延迟，把「推荐视频」收敛成一个精确的优化目标
先把候选的所有模型（GBT、双塔、Transformer）都列出来，让面试官挑一个
先估算需要多少台服务器和多大存储，用容量数字锁定系统边界
options_en: Assume a default goal (say maximize clicks) and start drawing the model architecture right away to save clarification time.
Ask about target user, business objective, scale, and latency to converge 'recommend videos' into a precise optimization goal.
List every candidate model (GBT, two-tower, transformer) up front and let the interviewer pick one.
Estimate how many servers and how much storage you need, and lock the system boundary with capacity numbers.
optionExplanations: 默认一个目标就跳过了整个第 1 步，选错方向后面全白做；面试官会记你「没收敛就动手」。
对；用户/目标/规模/延迟是四个把问题钉死的维度，收敛后才知道优化什么、约束是什么。
还没定优化目标就罗列模型名，正是本课警告的「报菜名」，不是设计。
容量估算属于部署/serving，问题都没澄清就算服务器数，是把顺序搞反了。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming a goal skips all of step 1; a wrong target wastes everything downstream, and interviewers note that you acted before narrowing.
Correct — user, objective, scale, and latency are the four axes that pin the problem so you know what to optimize and what constrains it.
Reciting model names before an objective is set is exactly the 'naming' anti-pattern, not design.
Capacity sizing belongs to serving; computing server counts before the problem is clarified reverses the order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统真正要优化的业务结果（观看时长、留存、GMV），而非代理指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The business objective is the real outcome the system optimizes (watch time, retention, GMV), not a proxy metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示中被点击的比例，推荐/广告常用的线上指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions that get clicked, a common online metric for recs and ads.

scenario: 45 分钟的面试里，第 1 步问题澄清有个建议的时间上限。
scenario_en: In a 45-min interview, step 1 problem clarification has a recommended time cap.
q: 填空：第 1 步问题澄清的时间预算，以及面试官在听什么。
q_en: Fill in: the time budget for step 1 and what the interviewer is listening for.
text: 第 1 步问题澄清花 {{3-5}} 分钟；这是给定的节奏目标不是公式推导。面试官在听你是否在动手前先 {{收敛/narrow}} 问题，这是结构化思维和容忍模糊的信号。
text_en: Spend {{3-5}} minutes on step 1 clarification; this is a given pacing target, not a formula. The interviewer listens for whether you {{narrow}} before solving, a signal of structured thinking and ambiguity tolerance.
why: 3-5 分钟是节奏目标（给定值），不是算出来的；它约束的是「不能无限澄清、要尽快收敛」。超时不收敛本身就是负信号。
why_en: The 3-5 minutes is a given pacing target, not a computed number, and it constrains you to converge quickly rather than clarify endlessly.

scenario: 第 2 步数据策略要给训练数据打标签，你在「显式反馈」和「隐式反馈」之间选。
scenario_en: In step 2 data strategy you must label training data, choosing between explicit and implicit feedback.
q: 显式标签 vs 隐式标签，核心区别在哪个维度？
q_en: Explicit vs implicit labels — on which dimension do they differ?
why: 显式（评分、点赞）干净但稀疏——用户很少主动打分；隐式（点击、观看时长）海量但有噪声——点了不代表满意。取舍轴是「标签质量 vs 标签数量」。
