Their approaches are identical; the only difference is seniors use a more expensive offline eval set.
optionExplanations: 反了：验证代理恰是 senior 的动作，junior 常跳过 A/B 直接信离线指标。
描述对调了：反推指标是 senior 的做法，套模板是 junior 的做法。
对；senior 多了「从目标反推 + A/B 验证代理」，junior 停在按任务类型套指标。
差别不在评估集贵贱，而在是否从业务目标反推并验证代理这条推理链。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: validating the proxy is the senior move; juniors often skip A/B and trust offline metrics.
The descriptions are swapped: deriving is the senior move, templating is the junior move.
Correct — seniors add 'derive from objective + A/B-validate the proxy,' while juniors stop at templated metrics.
The difference isn't a pricier eval set but whether you derive from the objective and validate the proxy chain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检验改进某 ML 指标是否真的移动业务指标，通常靠线上 A/B。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Proxy validation checks whether improving an ML metric actually moves the business metric, usually via online A/B.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 视频推荐，业务目标是参与度 = 观看时长；工程师最初用 CTR/AUC 当排序分。
scenario_en: Video recommendation where the business goal is engagement = watch time; the engineer first uses CTR/AUC as the ranking score.
q: 为什么 CTR 是坏代理，更好的排序分是什么？
q_en: Why is CTR a poor proxy here, and what is a better ranking score?
why: 优化 CTR 会奖励标题党：点击涨但看得更少，与观看时长背离；更好的代理是用「预测观看时长」当排序分，直接对齐业务目标。
why_en: Optimizing CTR rewards clickbait — clicks rise but watch time falls, diverging from the goal — so a better proxy is ranking by predicted watch time, aligned directly with engagement.
tradeoff: CTR（测点击，易被标题党钻空） vs 预测观看时长（直接对齐参与度）
options: CTR 坏在计算太慢，换成同样测点击但更快的指标即可，无需改目标
CTR 会奖励标题党（点击涨、观看降），改用「预测观看时长」当排序分直接对齐参与度
CTR 没问题，观看时长才是坏代理，应该继续优化 CTR
两个指标都不行，应该直接优化 30 天留存当排序分
options_en: CTR is bad because it's slow to compute; swap in a faster click metric with no goal change needed.
CTR rewards clickbait (clicks up, watch time down); rank by predicted watch time to align directly with engagement.
CTR is fine; watch time is the bad proxy, so keep optimizing CTR.
Both metrics fail; optimize 30-day retention directly as the ranking score instead.
whenOtherWins: 若业务目标本就是点击/导流（如按曝光点击计费的广告），CTR 才是对的代理。
optionExplanations: CTR 的问题不是慢，是激励错了方向；换个更快的点击指标照样奖励标题党。
对；CTR 与观看时长背离，用预测观看时长当排序分把优化对准真正的业务目标。
说反了：CTR 才是与参与度脱钩的那个，观看时长恰恰是更贴近目标的代理。
30 天留存太滞后、信号太稀，做不了逐条打分的排序分；预测观看时长才可行。
optionExplanations_en: CTR's problem isn't speed but wrong incentives; a faster click metric still rewards clickbait.
Correct — CTR diverges from watch time, so ranking by predicted watch time points optimization at the real goal.
Backwards: CTR is the one decoupled from engagement; watch time is the closer proxy to the goal.
30-day retention is too lagging and sparse to be a per-item ranking score; predicted watch time is what's feasible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例；优化它易奖励标题党。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of impressions clicked; optimizing it tends to reward clickbait.

termDefinitions.term: predicted watch time / 预测观看时长
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测用户会看多久，用作排序分可直接对齐观看时长目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Predicted watch time is the model's estimate of how long a user will watch, used as a ranking score to align with the watch-time goal.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 欺诈检测，业务目标是保护收入；既怕漏欺诈（直接损失）又怕误拦正常交易（伤体验）。
scenario_en: Fraud detection where the goal is protecting revenue; you fear both missing fraud (direct loss) and blocking legit transactions (hurts experience).
q: 怎么用一个 ML 指标同时兜住这对权衡？
q_en: How can a single ML metric capture both sides of this trade-off?
why: 用「固定 precision 下的 recall」，如 recall @ 95% precision：先把误拦率钉在阈值内，再最大化抓到的欺诈，把漏欺诈 vs 拦正常这对权衡编进指标本身。
why_en: Use recall at a fixed precision floor, e.g. recall @ 95% precision: pin the false-block rate within a threshold, then maximize fraud caught, encoding the miss-vs-block trade-off inside the metric itself.
tradeoff: recall @ 固定 precision（把权衡编进指标） vs 单看 recall 或单看 precision（只顾一边）
options: 只优化 recall，把误拦当作可以接受的代价，反正抓得多就行
只优化 precision，把漏欺诈当作可以接受的代价，反正拦得准就行
用 recall @ 95% precision：先把误拦率钉在阈值内，再最大化抓到的欺诈
优化整体准确率 accuracy，一个数把两类错误都盖住最省事
options_en: Optimize recall only, treating false blocks as acceptable cost since catching more is all that matters.
Optimize precision only, treating missed fraud as acceptable cost since being precise is all that matters.
Use recall @ 95% precision: pin the false-block rate within a threshold, then maximize fraud caught.
Optimize overall accuracy — one number that conveniently covers both error types at once.
whenOtherWins: 若误拦几乎无代价（如纯离线复核、拦下也只是排队人工审），可放开 precision 约束单追 recall。
optionExplanations: 单追 recall 会把误拦率放飞，伤正常交易体验，只兜住了权衡的一边。
单追 precision 会放过大量欺诈，直接损失收入，也只兜住一边。
对；固定 precision 当约束、最大化 recall，把两类错误的取舍钉进一个指标里。
欺诈样本极不平衡，accuracy 会被海量正常样本主导，全预测正常都能高分，没用。
optionExplanations_en: Recall alone lets the false-block rate run wild, hurting legit transactions — only one side of the trade-off.
Precision alone lets lots of fraud through, directly losing revenue — again only one side.
Correct — fix precision as a constraint and maximize recall, pinning both error costs into one metric.
Fraud is highly imbalanced, so accuracy is dominated by the legit majority; predicting 'all legit' scores high yet is useless.

termDefinitions.term: recall at fixed precision / 固定精确率下的召回
termDefinitions.meaning: 先把 precision 钉在某个下限（如 95%），在此约束下最大化 recall。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall at fixed precision pins precision to a floor (e.g. 95%) and maximizes recall under that constraint.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 电商搜索：离线 NDCG@10 +6%，但上线 A/B 后收入没有任何变化。
scenario_en: E-commerce search: offline NDCG@10 is +6%, but after an online A/B test revenue shows no change at all.
q: 最可能的根因是什么？
q_en: What is the most likely root cause?
why: 代理断了：训练用的相关性标签没有捕捉「购买意图」，模型把「看着相关」的排前面却不带来收入；offline 赢 ≠ business 赢，必须靠 A/B 验证。
why_en: The proxy broke: the relevance labels used for training don't capture purchase intent, so the model ranks 'looks relevant' up without driving revenue — an offline win that isn't a business win, which is why A/B validation is essential.
options: A/B 流量太小，属于统计噪声，加大流量收入就会涨
训练用的相关性标签没捕捉购买意图，NDCG 涨了但不带来收入（代理失效）
模型延迟变高拖慢了页面，纯工程问题，与指标选择无关
NDCG@10 计算有 bug，实际排序并没有真的变好
options_en: A/B traffic is too small (statistical noise); revenue will rise with more traffic.
The relevance labels used for training don't capture purchase intent, so NDCG rose but revenue didn't (broken proxy).
Higher model latency slowed the page — a pure engineering issue unrelated to metric choice.
NDCG@10 has a computation bug; the ranking didn't actually improve.
optionExplanations: 噪声是随机的，不会稳定表现为「NDCG 明确涨、收入零变化」；这是系统性的代理错配。
对；相关性 ≠ 购买意图，标签口径没对准收入，NDCG 涨也推不动业务，正是代理失效。
题目说的是收入没变而非页面变慢；把它归因到延迟脱离了给定信号。
若 NDCG 是 bug 造成的虚涨，那是计算错误；但更典型、更该先想到的是相关性标签选错了口径。
optionExplanations_en: Noise is random and won't consistently show 'clear NDCG gain, zero revenue change'; this is a systematic proxy mismatch.
Correct — relevance is not purchase intent; the labels aren't aligned to revenue, so NDCG can rise without moving business — proxy failure.
The prompt says revenue was flat, not that the page slowed; blaming latency departs from the given signal.
A buggy NDCG would be a computation error, but the more typical and first hypothesis is that the relevance labels are mis-specified.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标注「结果与查询多相关」，若不代表购买意图，就与收入脱钩。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relevance label marks how relevant a result is to a query; if it doesn't reflect purchase intent, it decouples from revenue.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 信息流排序持续优化 CTR/AUC 一段时间后。
scenario_en: A feed-ranking system has been optimizing CTR/AUC for a while.
q: 「参与度陷阱（engagement trap）」会怎么反噬业务？
q_en: How does the 'engagement trap' backfire on the business?
why: 优化 CTR 会把耸动/分裂性内容推上来：短期点击/参与涨，但几周后留存跌——点击 ≠ 长期满意，这是典型的代理与业务背离。
why_en: Optimizing CTR surfaces sensational/divisive content: short-term clicks and engagement rise, but retention falls weeks later — clicks aren't long-term satisfaction, a classic proxy-versus-business divergence.
options: 优化器推出耸动/分裂内容，短期点击涨，但几周后留存跌，点击 ≠ 长期满意
优化 CTR 会让点击和留存同步上涨，没有任何副作用
CTR 涨会直接拉高服务器成本，属于纯基础设施问题
CTR 优化会降低短期点击但提升长期留存，是一种延迟收益
options_en: The optimizer surfaces sensational/divisive content; short-term clicks rise but retention falls weeks later — clicks aren't long-term satisfaction.
Optimizing CTR makes clicks and retention rise together with no side effects.
Higher CTR directly raises server cost — a pure infrastructure issue.
CTR optimization lowers short-term clicks but raises long-term retention, a delayed benefit.
optionExplanations: 对；CTR 只测点击这一维，优化器用耸动内容刷点击，几周后留存被反噬。
若真同步上涨就没有陷阱可言；现实是短期点击涨掩盖了留存下滑。
服务器成本不是这里的机制；参与度陷阱讲的是内容激励导致留存受损。
方向反了：是短期点击涨、长期留存跌，不是短期降长期升。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — CTR measures only clicks, so the optimizer farms clicks with sensational content, and retention is hit weeks later.
If both truly rose together there'd be no trap; reality is short-term clicks mask a retention decline.
Server cost isn't the mechanism here; the engagement trap is about content incentives harming retention.
Direction reversed: it's short-term clicks up, long-term retention down — not the opposite.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只优化点击/参与代理，激励出耸动内容，短期涨、长期留存跌。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The engagement trap is optimizing a click/engagement proxy that incentivizes sensational content — up short-term, but retention falls long-term.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 音乐服务按「完播率 NDCG」优化推荐一段时间。
scenario_en: A music service optimizes recommendations on completion-based NDCG for a while.
q: 会出现什么退化，最终后果是什么？
q_en: What degradation appears, and what is the final consequence?
why: 会收敛到窄的安全/热门曲目：离线 NDCG 涨但推荐重复单调，NPS 下降、churn 上升——指标忽略了多样性（variety），这叫多样性坍缩。
why_en: It converges on a narrow set of safe/popular tracks: offline NDCG rises but recommendations get repetitive, NPS drops and churn rises — the metric ignored variety, called diversity collapse.
options: 推荐更加多样化，NDCG 和多样性同时提升，用户更满意
系统崩溃无法出结果，属于可用性故障而非指标问题
收敛到窄的安全/热门曲目，NDCG 涨但重复单调，NPS 降、churn 升（忽略了多样性）
完播率下降但探索性提升，长期 NPS 反而更好
options_en: Recommendations become more diverse, NDCG and diversity rise together, and users are happier.
The system crashes and returns nothing — an availability failure, not a metric issue.
It converges on narrow safe/popular tracks; NDCG rises but gets repetitive, NPS drops and churn rises (variety ignored).
Completion drops but exploration rises, so long-term NPS actually improves.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反：单优化完播 NDCG 会牺牲多样性，不是同时提升。
这不是可用性崩溃，系统照常出结果，只是结果越来越单调。
对；只追完播 NDCG 让模型选最安全的热门曲，重复导致 NPS 降、churn 升。
方向反了：完播 NDCG 是涨的，代价是多样性没了、NPS 跌。
optionExplanations_en: The opposite: optimizing completion NDCG alone sacrifices diversity, not raises it.
This isn't an availability crash; the system still returns results, just increasingly monotonous ones.
Correct — chasing completion NDCG makes the model pick the safest popular tracks, and repetition drops NPS and raises churn.
Direction reversed: completion NDCG rises, at the cost of lost diversity and falling NPS.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只优化完播/相关性代理，推荐收敛到窄的热门集，重复单调伤满意度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Diversity collapse is when optimizing a completion/relevance proxy converges recommendations onto a narrow popular set, hurting satisfaction through repetition.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 既想继续优化主指标（如观看时长），又不想踩出参与度陷阱、多样性坍缩这类坑。
scenario_en: You want to keep optimizing a primary metric (e.g. watch time) without falling into the engagement trap or diversity collapse.
q: 标准做法是什么？
q_en: What is the standard approach?
why: 定义 secondary/guardrail（护栏）指标：给伤害设上限（如留存不许跌超阈值），在不越界的前提下优化主指标；并常问「这个指标激励了什么行为？」
why_en: Define secondary/guardrail metrics that cap harm (e.g. retention must not drop past a threshold) so you optimize the primary within a safe region, and keep asking 'what behavior does this metric incentivize?'
tradeoff: 加护栏指标（主指标可优化但设伤害上限） vs 单目标优化（更猛但易反噬）
options: 彻底放弃主指标，只盯留存这一个指标，稳妥优先
把主指标阈值调低一点，跑更长时间的 A/B 就能自动避开坑
多训练几个模型取平均，用集成来消除标题党倾向
定义护栏（guardrail）指标给伤害设上限，在不越界前提下优化主指标
options_en: Abandon the primary metric entirely and track only retention, prioritizing safety.
Lower the primary threshold a bit and run a longer A/B to automatically avoid the trap.
Train several models and average them, using an ensemble to remove clickbait tendencies.
Define guardrail metrics that cap harm and optimize the primary metric within the safe region.
whenOtherWins: 若某个次级维度是绝对红线（如安全/合规），可直接把它当硬约束甚至主指标，而非仅护栏。
optionExplanations: 只盯留存等于换一个单目标，仍会催生它自己的钻空子行为，没解决根本。
调阈值/延长 A/B 不改变「主指标忽略其他维度」这件事，坑照踩。
集成只是降方差，标题党倾向来自目标定义而非模型方差，压不掉。
对；护栏给伤害设上限，让主指标在可行域内优化，正是应对参与度陷阱的标准姿势。
optionExplanations_en: Tracking only retention just swaps in another single objective that breeds its own gaming — root cause unsolved.
Tuning thresholds or a longer A/B doesn't change that the primary ignores other dimensions; the trap remains.
An ensemble only cuts variance; clickbait tendency comes from the objective definition, not model variance.
Correct — guardrails cap harm so the primary optimizes within a feasible region, the standard fix for the engagement trap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带预设阈值的次级指标，越界则拦住上线，防止主指标优化造成伤害。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a secondary metric with a preset threshold that blocks launch if crossed, preventing harm from primary-metric optimization.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 为什么说 A/B 测试是 ML 代理指标的「终审」？
q_en: Why is A/B testing the ultimate validator for ML proxy metrics?
why: 离线指标只是代理，可能和业务脱钩；只有线上 A/B 能测出改进 ML 指标是否真的移动业务指标，offline 赢必须被 online 确认才算数。
why_en: Offline metrics are only proxies that can decouple from business; only an online A/B measures whether improving the ML metric truly moves the business metric, so an offline win only counts once confirmed online.
options: 因为 A/B 的样本量总是比离线大，所以数值更精确
因为离线指标是代理、可能和业务脱钩，只有线上 A/B 能证实改进真的推动业务
因为 A/B 能替代离线评估，有了 A/B 就不用再算 NDCG/AUC
因为 A/B 只测工程延迟，和业务指标涨跌无关
options_en: Because A/B always has a larger sample than offline, giving more precise numbers.
Because offline metrics are proxies that can decouple from business, and only an online A/B proves the improvement truly moves business.
Because A/B replaces offline evaluation, so with A/B you no longer compute NDCG/AUC.
Because A/B only measures engineering latency, unrelated to business-metric moves.
optionExplanations: 不是样本量的问题；即使离线样本再大，代理和业务脱钩它也测不出来。
对；A/B 在真实用户上测「ML 指标改进 → 业务指标是否动」，这是代理关系唯一的实证。
A/B 不替代离线：离线快、便宜用于筛选，A/B 贵、用于最终确认，二者互补。
A/B 恰恰测业务指标（留存/收入）的变化，不只是延迟。
optionExplanations_en: It's not about sample size; even a huge offline sample can't catch a proxy decoupled from business.
Correct — A/B tests on real users whether an ML-metric gain moves the business metric, the only empirical check of the proxy link.
A/B doesn't replace offline: offline is cheap for screening, A/B is costly for final confirmation — they complement each other.
A/B precisely measures business-metric moves (retention/revenue), not just latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 确认代理指标真实有效的最终手段，这里指线上 A/B 测试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ultimate validator is the final means of confirming a proxy metric truly works, here the online A/B test.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 补全 precision / recall 的公式与各自的适用场景：
q_en: Fill in the precision/recall formulas and when each applies:
text: Precision = TP / (TP + {{FP}})，当{{误报}}代价高时盯它；Recall = TP / (TP + {{FN}})，当{{漏报}}危险时盯它。
text_en: Precision = TP / (TP + {{FP}}), optimize it when {{false positives}} are costly; Recall = TP / (TP + {{FN}}), optimize it when {{misses}} are dangerous.
why: 两个公式只差分母：precision 分母含 FP（惩罚误报），recall 分母含 FN（惩罚漏报）；先想清哪类错误更贵，再决定盯哪个。
why_en: The two formulas differ only in denominator: precision's has FP (penalizes false alarms), recall's has FN (penalizes misses), so decide which error is costlier first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真正例：真正为正、也被判为正的样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A True Positive (TP) is a case that is truly positive and correctly predicted positive.

termDefinitions.meaning: FP 误报=把负当正；FN 漏报=把正当负。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP (False Positive) predicts positive on a negative; FN (False Negative) misses a true positive.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 收入类业务指标（revenue）通常怎么细化，常用在哪类系统、什么时间尺度？
q_en: How is the revenue business metric typically broken down, and in which systems and horizons?
why: 收入拆成 rev/user、AOV（平均订单额）、每次曝光广告收入等；周/月尺度衡量，常见于广告排序、电商搜索，目标形如「+2% rev/session」。
why_en: Revenue breaks into rev/user, AOV (average order value), ad revenue per impression, etc., measured weekly/monthly in ads ranking and e-commerce search, with targets like '+2% rev/session'.
options: 拆成 rev/user、AOV、广告收入/曝光等货币量，周/月尺度，用于广告排序、电商搜索
拆成 D1/D7/D30 回访率，季度尺度，用于订阅产品的健康监控
拆成点击、时长、会话数等互动量，日尺度，用于信息流参与度
拆成 precision、recall、AUC 等模型级量，离线尺度，用于分类评估
options_en: Breaks into rev/user, AOV, ad revenue per impression, etc., weekly/monthly, for ads ranking and e-commerce search.
Breaks into D1/D7/D30 return rates, quarterly, for subscription health monitoring.
Breaks into clicks, duration, session counts, daily, for feed engagement.
Breaks into precision, recall, AUC, offline, for classification evaluation.
optionExplanations: 对；revenue 是货币结果，拆成 rev/user、AOV 等，广告/电商最看重，周/月看趋势。
D1/D7/D30 是留存的拆法，不是收入；混淆了两个业务指标。
点击/时长/会话是参与度（engagement）的拆法，不是收入。
precision/recall/AUC 是 ML 代理指标，不是业务收入指标。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — revenue is a monetary outcome split into rev/user, AOV, etc., central to ads/e-commerce, trended weekly/monthly.
D1/D7/D30 is how retention breaks down, not revenue; this confuses two business metrics.
Clicks/duration/sessions are how engagement breaks down, not revenue.
Precision/recall/AUC are ML proxy metrics, not the business revenue metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均订单额：每笔订单的平均金额，是收入的常见拆解项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AOV (Average Order Value) is the average amount per order, a common decomposition of revenue.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 参与度（engagement）衡量什么，常用在哪类系统、什么时间尺度？
q_en: What does engagement measure, and in which systems and horizons?
why: 参与度测互动强度：点击、时长、每日会话数；信息流排序、视频推荐用它，日/周尺度，目标形如「+5% 会话时长」。
why_en: Engagement measures interaction intensity — clicks, duration, sessions per day — used in feed ranking and video recs at a daily/weekly cadence, with targets like '+5% session duration'.
options: 测每笔订单金额和广告收入，季度尺度，用于电商定价
测调查满意度和推荐意愿，季度尺度，用于品牌健康
测互动强度：点击、时长、每日会话数，日/周尺度，用于信息流、视频推荐
测模型排序质量 NDCG/AUC，离线尺度，用于搜索评估
options_en: Measures order amounts and ad revenue, quarterly, for e-commerce pricing.
Measures survey satisfaction and recommend-likelihood, quarterly, for brand health.
Measures interaction intensity — clicks, duration, sessions per day — daily/weekly, for feeds and video recs.
Measures model ranking quality NDCG/AUC, offline, for search evaluation.
optionExplanations: 订单金额/广告收入是 revenue 的拆法，不是参与度。
满意度/推荐意愿是 NPS，季度滞后指标，不是参与度。
对；参与度测互动强度（点击/时长/会话），信息流和视频推荐最看重，日/周看。
NDCG/AUC 是 ML 代理指标，不是业务参与度指标。
optionExplanations_en: Order amounts/ad revenue are how revenue breaks down, not engagement.
Satisfaction/recommend-likelihood is NPS, a quarterly lagging metric, not engagement.
Correct — engagement measures interaction intensity (clicks/duration/sessions), central to feeds and video recs, viewed daily/weekly.
NDCG/AUC are ML proxy metrics, not the business engagement metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互动强度类业务指标：点击、时长、每日会话数，日/周尺度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engagement is an interaction-intensity business metric — clicks, duration, sessions per day — on a daily/weekly horizon.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 准备把某个 ML 指标定为优化目标、正式写进 loss 之前。
scenario_en: Before locking an ML metric as the optimization target and writing it into the loss.
q: 最该先问自己哪个问题，以提前发现反噬？
q_en: What question should you ask yourself first to catch backfire early?
why: 先问「这个指标激励了什么行为？」——优化器会钻指标与业务意图的缝隙；想清激励方向，才能提前预判标题党、多样性坍缩这类反噬。
why_en: Ask 'what behavior does this metric incentivize?' first — the optimizer exploits the gap between metric and intent, so reasoning about incentives lets you foresee clickbait or diversity collapse.
tradeoff: 先问指标激励什么行为（预判反噬） vs 直接上线看数字（事后才发现坑）
options: 先问「这个指标能不能算得更快」，性能优先
先问「这个指标激励了什么行为」，预判优化器会怎么钻空子
先问「竞品用的是哪个指标」，跟着抄最省事
先问「离线数据集够不够大」，样本量优先
options_en: Ask 'can this metric be computed faster?' — performance first.
Ask 'what behavior does this metric incentivize?' — foresee how the optimizer will game it.
Ask 'which metric do competitors use?' — copying is easiest.
Ask 'is the offline dataset large enough?' — sample size first.
whenOtherWins: 当指标与业务意图已知高度一致、且历史上没出现过钻空子时，激励分析的边际价值下降，可更快推进。
optionExplanations: 算得快不解决方向对不对；一个激励错误的指标算得再快也把系统带偏。
对；优化器只会最大化你给的数，先想清它激励什么行为，才能提前堵住标题党/坍缩。
抄竞品指标不代表适配你的业务目标，别人的代理未必是你的好代理。
样本量再大也救不了「优化了错的东西」，方向问题优先于数据量。
optionExplanations_en: Speed doesn't fix direction; a mis-incentivized metric misleads the system no matter how fast it computes.
Correct — the optimizer maximizes whatever number you give it, so reasoning about incentives first heads off clickbait/collapse.
Copying a competitor's metric doesn't mean it fits your objective; their proxy may not be yours.
A bigger sample can't rescue 'optimizing the wrong thing'; direction outranks data volume.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定指标前预判优化器会被激励出什么行为，用来提前发现反噬。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Incentive analysis anticipates what behavior a metric will drive the optimizer toward, to catch backfire before launch.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 业务指标和 ML 指标在「归属」上有什么区别，为什么这个区别在设计沟通里重要？
q_en: How do business and ML metrics differ in ownership, and why does that matter for design communication?
why: 业务指标归产品/管理层（他们定目标），ML 指标归 ML 团队（可离线算、可优化）；分清归属才能讲清「我优化 ML 指标去推动你们的业务指标」这条责任链。
why_en: Business metrics belong to product/leadership (who set goals) and ML metrics to the ML team (computable and optimizable); separating ownership lets you articulate 'I optimize the ML metric to move your business metric.'
tradeoff: 业务指标（产品拥有，定方向） vs ML 指标（ML 团队拥有，可优化的代理）
options: 两者都归 ML 团队拥有，产品团队只负责看报表
业务指标归产品/管理层、ML 指标归 ML 团队，说清「优化代理去推动业务」的责任链
两者都归产品拥有，ML 团队只是执行方，不对任何指标负责
归属可以随意，谁先提出指标就归谁，不影响设计沟通
options_en: Both are owned by the ML team; product just reads dashboards.
Business metrics belong to product/leadership and ML metrics to the ML team, framing the 'optimize proxy to move business' accountability chain.
Both belong to product; the ML team only executes and owns no metric.
Ownership is arbitrary — whoever proposes a metric owns it — and doesn't affect design communication.
optionExplanations: 业务指标不归 ML 团队；把它算到 ML 头上会让你背不该背的目标。
对；产品拥有业务指标、ML 团队拥有代理指标，责任链清楚才好沟通设计取舍。
ML 团队并非什么都不负责，它对自己选择和优化的 ML 代理指标负责。
归属不是随意的，它直接决定谁定目标、谁负责推动，影响沟通与问责。
optionExplanations_en: Business metrics don't belong to the ML team; putting them on ML makes you own goals you shouldn't.
Correct — product owns business metrics and the ML team owns proxy metrics; a clear chain aids communicating design trade-offs.
The ML team isn't accountability-free; it owns the ML proxy it chooses and optimizes.
Ownership isn't arbitrary; it determines who sets goals and who drives them, affecting communication and accountability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 谁定义并对某指标负责：业务指标归产品，ML 代理归 ML 团队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric ownership is who defines and is accountable for a metric: business metrics to product, ML proxies to the ML team.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 把「参与度陷阱」从优化到反噬再到修复的因果链排序：
q_en: Order the engagement trap's causal chain from optimization to backfire to fix:
steps: 几周后：点击 ≠ 长期满意，留存开始下降
优化器把耸动/分裂性内容推上来
把 CTR/AUC 单独当优化目标
短期：点击和参与度上升，看着像在赢
加护栏指标：给留存设下限，允许在不越界内优化 CTR
why: CTR 只测点击这一维，优化器会用耸动内容刷点击；短期参与涨掩盖几周后的留存下滑，护栏指标给留存兜底才切断这条链。
why_en: CTR measures only clicks, so the optimizer farms clicks with sensational content; short-term gains mask a later retention drop, and only a retention guardrail cuts the chain.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  A["单优化 CTR/AUC"] --> B["推耸动内容"]
  B --> C["短期点击/参与↑"]
  C --> D["几周后留存↓"]
  D --> E["加护栏：留存设下限"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 只优化点击代理，激励耸动内容，短期涨长期留存跌。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The engagement trap optimizes a click proxy that incentivizes sensational content — up short-term, retention down long-term.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 搜索结果排序，用户主要看前几条，位置越靠前越重要。
scenario_en: Search-result ranking where users mostly see the top few and earlier positions matter more.
q: 评估排序质量该用 NDCG 还是 AUC？
q_en: Should you evaluate ranking quality with NDCG or AUC?
why: NDCG 按位置折损，奖励「把最相关的放最前」，匹配「用户只看前几条」；AUC 只看整体正负排序、不区分位置，发现不了「相关项被排到第 8 位」的损失。
why_en: NDCG's position discount rewards putting the most relevant at the very top, matching 'users see only the top few,' while AUC ignores position and misses the loss of a relevant item ranked 8th.
tradeoff: NDCG（位置敏感，测榜首质量） vs AUC（位置无关，测整体可分性）
options: 用 NDCG：位置折损，奖励把最相关的放最前，匹配用户只看前几条
用 AUC：只要正样本整体排在负样本前即可，具体名次不重要
用 RMSE：把相关性打分的数值误差压到最小最要紧
用 precision：单看第一条对不对就够了，其余位置不用管
options_en: Use NDCG: its position discount rewards putting the most relevant at the top, matching users seeing only the top few.
Use AUC: as long as positives outrank negatives overall, exact position doesn't matter.
Use RMSE: minimizing numeric error of relevance scores matters most.
Use precision: checking only whether the first result is right is enough; ignore the rest.
whenOtherWins: 若只关心「正样本整体是否排在负样本前」而不在意具体名次（如二分类阈值调优），AUC 更合适。
optionExplanations: 对；用户只看前几条，NDCG 的位置折损正好惩罚把相关项排到后面。
AUC 位置无关，抓不住「相关项排到第 8 位」的损失，与「只看前几条」不匹配。
这是排序不是回归，RMSE 的数值误差衡量错了目标。
只看第一条太粗，用户会翻前几条，precision@1 丢掉了榜单其余位置的质量。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — users see only the top few, and NDCG's position discount precisely penalizes ranking relevant items lower.
AUC is position-blind and misses the loss of a relevant item at rank 8 — a mismatch with 'top few only.'
This is ranking not regression; RMSE's numeric error measures the wrong target.
Only the first result is too coarse; users scan the top few, and precision@1 drops the rest of the list's quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按位置折损的有序列表质量指标，榜首权重最大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) scores ranked-list quality with a position discount, weighting the top most.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨所有阈值的排序质量，位置无关，只看整体正负可分性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is ranking quality across thresholds, position-blind, capturing only overall separability.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

q: 补全「业务目标 → ML 指标」的三步对齐框架：
q_en: Fill in the three-step business-to-ML alignment framework:
text: 对齐三步：先识别{{业务目标}}，再选与它最可靠相关的{{代理}} ML 指标，最后用 {{A/B}} 测试验证改进它真的推动业务指标。
text_en: Three steps: identify the {{business objective}}, pick the best-{{proxy}} ML metric most reliably correlated with it, then validate with {{A/B}} testing that improving it really moves the business metric.
why: 顺序不能反：目标先定方向，代理是对目标的近似，A/B 是把「代理→业务」这条链落到真实用户上的唯一实证。
why_en: The order can't flip: the objective sets direction, the proxy approximates it, and A/B is the only empirical check that the proxy-to-business link holds on real users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 收入/参与/留存/安全之一，决定该往哪个方向优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The business objective (revenue/engagement/retention/safety) sets which direction to optimize.

category: Defining Success Business Metrics Vs ML Metrics

scenario: 推荐系统上线后 CTR +3%，一周后 Day-7 留存 −0.8%，主指标涨、留存跌。
scenario_en: After a recsys launch CTR is +3%, then a week later Day-7 retention is −0.8% — primary up, retention down.
q: 这种「主指标涨、另一业务指标显著跌」的现象叫什么，根因是什么？
q_en: What is this 'primary metric up, another business metric significantly down' phenomenon, and its root cause?
why: 叫 metric cannibalization（指标蚕食）：优化主指标造成另一重要业务/体验指标统计显著退化。这不是 bug，是在多维价值空间里做单目标优化的可预期结果——loss 没装下留存。
why_en: It's metric cannibalization: optimizing the primary metric causes a statistically significant drop in another business metric — a predictable result of single-objective optimization when the loss didn't capture retention.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["主指标 CTR
单目标"] -->|"优化器只顶这一维"| M["模型"] M -->|"CTR +3%"| W["看着在赢"] M -.->|"没进 loss 的维度"| R["Day-7 留存 −0.8%"]
options: 过拟合：离线指标虚高、线上会打折，加正则化或早停即可，与目标函数无关
指标蚕食：优化主指标导致另一业务指标统计显著退化，是单目标优化的可预期后果
统计噪声：A/B 样本量不足的随机波动，加大流量或延长实验后留存会回正
数据漂移：线上特征分布偏移导致效果打折，重新训练模型即可修复退化
options_en: Overfitting: offline metrics inflated and discounted online; add regularization or early stopping — unrelated to the objective.
Metric cannibalization: optimizing the primary metric causes a statistically significant drop in another business metric, a predictable side effect.
Statistical noise: random fluctuation from a small A/B sample; retention recovers with more traffic or a longer run.
Data drift: an online feature-distribution shift discounts the gain; retrain the model to fix the degradation.
optionExplanations: 过拟合让离线虚高，但这里 CTR 是线上真涨；真问题是主指标漏了留存这一维，不是拟合。
对；主指标只顶一维，优化器把没进 loss 的留存压下去，是可预期的单目标副作用。
噪声方向随机，不会稳定表现为「点击涨、留存稳定跌」；这是系统性错配不是样本量。
漂移会让线上整体打折，但这里 CTR 明确涨却伤留存，是目标定义问题不是分布问题。
optionExplanations_en: Overfitting inflates offline metrics, but here CTR truly rose online; the real issue is the primary misses retention.
Correct — a single-objective optimizer pushes down the retention dimension left out of the loss, a predictable side effect.
Noise is random and won't consistently show 'clicks up, retention steadily down'; this is systematic mismatch, not sample size.
Drift discounts online results broadly, but CTR clearly rose while hurting retention — an objective-definition problem, not distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化主指标导致另一重要业务/体验指标出现统计显著退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric cannibalization is when optimizing the primary metric causes a statistically significant degradation in another important business/UX metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例，常被当作排序主指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of impressions that get clicked, often used as a primary ranking metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 注册后第 7 天仍回访的用户比例，衡量短中期留存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Day-7 retention is the share of users who return on the 7th day after signup, a short-to-mid-term retention measure.

scenario: MAANG 规模产品，一次改动让某次级指标只跌 0.1%。
scenario_en: A MAANG-scale product where one change drops a secondary metric by just 0.1%.
q: 为什么 L5+ 要在被问之前主动提出蚕食风险，0.1% 也值得在意？
q_en: Why should an L5+ proactively raise cannibalization risk before being asked, and why does 0.1% matter?
why: 在数亿用户规模下，0.1% 的次级指标下降就是数千万人。成熟度信号是不等面试官提示、自己先说出可能被蚕食的维度和护栏，而不是只报主指标涨了多少。
why_en: At hundreds of millions of users, a 0.1% secondary-metric drop is tens of millions of people, so the maturity signal is naming the at-risk dimension and its guardrail before being prompted.
options: 0.1% 属可忽略误差，等 PM 复盘时再补护栏，模型工程师无需主动关注
0.1% 必落在噪声内，统计上不可能显著，可以直接忽略这类小幅波动
只要主指标涨幅够大，次级指标无论跌多少都能被整体收益覆盖掉
数亿用户下 0.1% 也等于数千万人受影响，L5+ 应主动预判并提出蚕食风险
options_en: 0.1% is negligible; wait for the PM's retro to add a guardrail — the ML engineer needn't flag it.
0.1% must be within noise and can't be statistically significant, so ignore such small swings.
As long as the primary gain is big enough, any secondary drop is covered by the overall win.
At hundreds of millions of users 0.1% is tens of millions affected, so an L5+ proactively raises cannibalization risk.
optionExplanations: 0.1% 在数亿规模下不是误差；等 PM 提才补，说明你没主动预判风险。
越界与否看统计显著性，不看绝对值小；0.1% 在大样本下完全可能显著。
「主指标够大就能覆盖」正是蚕食思维的坑，次级维度崩了照样伤业务。
对；0.1%×数亿=数千万人，L5+ 的成熟度信号就是被问前先说风险。
optionExplanations_en: At hundreds of millions of users 0.1% isn't rounding error; waiting for the PM shows you didn't proactively flag risk.
A breach is judged by significance, not small absolute size; 0.1% can be significant at large sample sizes.
'A big primary gain covers it' is exactly the cannibalization trap; a broken secondary still hurts the business.
Correct — 0.1% times hundreds of millions is tens of millions of users; the L5+ signal is flagging risk before being asked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指最大的几家科技公司，代表数亿级用户规模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAANG refers to the largest tech companies (Meta, Apple, Amazon, Netflix, Google), a stand-in for hundreds-of-millions user scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 资深工程师职级，面试期望主动发现并管理系统风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L5+ denotes senior engineer levels, where interviewers expect proactive risk-finding and management.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带预设阈值的次级指标，越界即拦上线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a secondary metric with a preset threshold that blocks launch if breached.

scenario: 信息流排序用 CTR/AUC 当主指标，持续优化一段时间（Meta News Feed 式）。
scenario_en: Feed ranking uses CTR/AUC as its primary metric and optimizes it for a while (Meta News Feed style).
q: 最可能被蚕食的次级指标是什么，激励机制是什么？
q_en: Which secondary metric is most likely cannibalized, and by what incentive?
why: CTR 只奖励点击，优化器会推标题党内容：点击涨但用户几周后不回来，Day-7 留存被蚕食。这是「点击 vs 留存」这类经典蚕食。
why_en: CTR only rewards clicks, so the optimizer surfaces clickbait — clicks rise but users don't return weeks later, cannibalizing Day-7 retention.
tradeoff: CTR（奖励点击，易催标题党） vs Day-7 留存（用户长期是否回来）
options: Day-7 留存被蚕食：CTR 奖励点击，优化器推标题党，点击涨但用户几周后不回来
点击成本被蚕食：CTR 上升直接推高服务器与广告竞价成本，属基础设施问题
AUC 被蚕食：优化 CTR 会让排序 AUC 同步下降，二者天然此消彼长
购买转化率被蚕食：CTR 涨会让加购转化同步下降，与内容质量无关
options_en: Day-7 retention is cannibalized: CTR rewards clicks, the optimizer pushes clickbait, clicks rise but users don't return weeks later.
Click cost is cannibalized: higher CTR directly raises server and ad-bidding cost — an infrastructure issue.
AUC is cannibalized: optimizing CTR lowers ranking AUC in lockstep, a natural trade-off.
Purchase conversion is cannibalized: rising CTR lowers add-to-cart conversion, unrelated to content quality.
whenOtherWins: 若产品目标本就是点击/导流（如按点击计费的广告位），CTR 涨就是真收益，不构成蚕食。
optionExplanations: 对；CTR 只奖励点击，优化器推标题党，点击涨但用户几周后不回来，留存被蚕食。
服务器/竞价成本不是这里的机制；蚕食讲的是内容激励伤留存。
AUC 和 CTR 都测排序，不会天然此消彼长；被蚕食的是留存这类业务指标。
转化率是电商「CTR vs 转化」那类的受害者，不是信息流场景的答案。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — CTR only rewards clicks, so the optimizer farms clickbait; clicks rise but users don't return, cannibalizing retention.
Server/bidding cost isn't the mechanism; cannibalization is about content incentives hurting retention.
AUC and CTR both measure ranking and don't naturally trade off; the victim here is a business metric like retention.
Conversion is the victim in the e-commerce 'CTR vs conversion' pattern, not the feed scenario.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例，优化它易奖励标题党。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of impressions clicked; optimizing it tends to reward clickbait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨所有阈值的排序质量指标，位置无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is a position-blind ranking-quality metric across all thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用夸张误导标题骗点击的内容，点击高但留不住人。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Clickbait uses sensational, misleading titles to farm clicks — high clicks but poor retention.

scenario: 视频推荐用「总观看时长」当主指标（YouTube 式），持续优化一段时间。
scenario_en: Video recommendation uses total watch time as its primary metric (YouTube style), optimized over time.
q: 会蚕食哪个次级指标，机制是什么？
q_en: Which secondary metric gets cannibalized, and by what mechanism?
why: 优化器把用户带进极端内容兔子洞：观看时长涨，但用户满意度调查下滑。这是「时长 vs 幸福感」这类经典蚕食——时长只测一维，没测「看完是否更好」。
why_en: The optimizer leads users into extreme-content rabbit holes: watch time rises but satisfaction surveys fall — the 'watch time vs wellbeing' pattern.
tradeoff: 总观看时长（易把人带进极端内容） vs 用户满意度调查（长期体验好坏）
options: 会蚕食点击率：延长观看时长必然压低单次点击率，两个指标天然互斥此消彼长
会蚕食广告收入：观看时长上涨会挤占广告插入位，直接减少每次曝光的收入
会蚕食满意度调查：优化器把用户带进极端内容兔子洞，时长涨但满意度下滑
会蚕食加载延迟：更长的视频体积更大导致加载变慢，属于工程性能问题
options_en: It cannibalizes CTR: longer watch time necessarily lowers per-view click rate, a natural mutual trade-off.
It cannibalizes ad revenue: rising watch time crowds out ad slots, directly cutting revenue per impression.
It cannibalizes satisfaction surveys: the optimizer leads users into extreme-content rabbit holes, watch time up but satisfaction down.
It cannibalizes load latency: longer videos are larger and load slower — an engineering performance issue.
whenOtherWins: 若产品明确以纯观看时长变现、且满意度长期稳定（如无广告长视频订阅），时长本身就是目标，不算蚕食。
optionExplanations: 延长时长不必然压低点击，二者不是天然互斥；这不是被蚕食的那个维度。
广告位挤占不是这里的机制；YouTube 式蚕食伤的是满意度不是收入。
对；优化器把人带进极端内容兔子洞，时长涨但满意度调查下滑，是典型蚕食。
加载延迟是工程性能问题，与「优化时长伤满意度」的激励机制无关。
optionExplanations_en: Longer watch time doesn't necessarily lower clicks; they aren't naturally exclusive, so this isn't the cannibalized dimension.
Ad-slot crowding isn't the mechanism; the YouTube-style cannibalization hurts satisfaction, not revenue.
Correct — the optimizer leads users into extreme-content rabbit holes; watch time rises but satisfaction surveys drop.
Load latency is an engineering issue, unrelated to the 'optimize watch time, hurt satisfaction' incentive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户观看视频的总时长，视频推荐常用的主指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Watch time is the total time users spend watching, a common primary metric for video recommendation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 问卷测用户对产品/推荐的满意程度，一种次级护栏信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A satisfaction survey polls how satisfied users are with the product/recommendations, a secondary guardrail signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐把用户越推越极端、越沉迷的路径，时长涨但体验变差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rabbit hole is a recommendation path pulling users into ever more extreme content — watch time up, wellbeing down.

scenario: 电商搜索排序用 CTR 当主指标（Amazon/电商式），持续优化一段时间。
scenario_en: E-commerce search ranking uses CTR as its primary metric (Amazon/e-commerce style), optimized over time.
q: 会蚕食哪个指标，机制是什么？
q_en: Which metric gets cannibalized, and by what mechanism?
why: 优化 CTR 会把标题/图片误导性强的商品排前面：点击涨但用户到了商品页并不下单，购买转化率被蚕食。这是「CTR vs 转化」这类经典蚕食。
why_en: Optimizing CTR ranks misleading listings higher: clicks rise but users don't buy, cannibalizing purchase conversion — the 'CTR vs conversion' pattern.
tradeoff: CTR（奖励点击，易推误导性商品） vs 购买转化率（用户是否真的下单）
options: 曝光量被蚕食：CTR 涨会减少搜索结果页展示的商品总数，展示更少
购买转化率被蚕食：把误导性强的商品排前面，点击涨但用户到商品页不下单
召回率被蚕食：优化 CTR 会漏掉相关商品，属检索覆盖质量问题
库存周转被蚕食：CTR 涨会让热门商品缺货，属供应链问题
options_en: Impressions are cannibalized: rising CTR cuts the total number of products shown on the results page.
Purchase conversion is cannibalized: misleading listings ranked higher get clicks but don't convert on the product page.
Recall is cannibalized: optimizing CTR misses relevant products — a retrieval-coverage issue.
Inventory turnover is cannibalized: rising CTR makes popular items go out of stock — a supply-chain issue.
whenOtherWins: 若排序目标就是把用户导到商品页（如按点击计费的赞助位），CTR 是对的目标，不必盯转化。
optionExplanations: 曝光量不是被蚕食的对象；CTR 优化不会系统性减少总曝光。
对；优化 CTR 把误导性强的商品排前面，点击涨但下单转化跌，是典型蚕食。
召回是检索覆盖问题，不是 CTR 优化蚕食的那个业务指标。
库存周转属供应链，与「CTR 优化伤转化」的排序激励无关。
optionExplanations_en: Impressions aren't the cannibalized target; optimizing CTR doesn't systematically cut total impressions.
Correct — optimizing CTR ranks misleading listings higher; clicks rise but purchase conversion falls.
Recall is a retrieval-coverage issue, not the business metric cannibalized by CTR optimization.
Inventory turnover is supply chain, unrelated to the ranking incentive of CTR hurting conversion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：曝光中被点击的比例，电商搜索常用主指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of impressions clicked, a common primary metric in e-commerce search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点进商品后真正下单的比例，衡量排序是否带来真实成交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Conversion rate is the share of clicks that end in a purchase, measuring whether ranking drives real sales.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标题或图片夸大、与实物不符、专为骗点击的商品条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A misleading listing has an exaggerated title/image mismatched to the item, engineered to farm clicks.

q: 三类经典蚕食（点击 vs 留存、时长 vs 满意度、CTR vs 转化）共同的根因是什么？
q_en: What is the shared root cause of the three classic cannibalization patterns?
why: 根因是主指标只测多维价值里的一维，优化器会最大化你给的那个数、专钻它和真实业务意图的缝隙——就像学生只背考试答案来提分，分数涨了但没真学会。
why_en: The root cause is that the primary captures only one dimension of value, and the optimizer exploits the gap to true intent — like a student memorizing answers to raise a score.
options: 都是模型容量不足，换更大更深的模型就能同时兼顾两个相互冲突的指标
都是 A/B 实验分流设计有误，用正确的随机分组后蚕食现象会自动消失
都是特征工程不到位，补上更多高质量特征后两个指标就会一起上涨
主指标只捕捉用户价值的一个维度，优化器专钻它与整体业务意图的缝隙
options_en: All are model-capacity limits; a bigger, deeper model can satisfy both conflicting metrics at once.
All are flawed A/B splitting; with correct randomization the cannibalization disappears on its own.
All are weak feature engineering; adding more quality features makes both metrics rise together.
The primary captures only one dimension of user value, and the optimizer exploits the gap to overall business intent.
optionExplanations: 换更大模型不解决方向问题；主指标漏掉的维度再大的模型也补不回来。
A/B 分流正确也照样蚕食，问题在目标定义不在实验设计。
补特征不改变「只优化一维」这件事，蚕食照旧发生。
对；主指标只测一维价值，优化器专钻它与业务意图的缝隙，像背答案刷分。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger model doesn't fix direction; no model recovers a dimension the primary omits.
Correct A/B splitting still cannibalizes; the problem is objective definition, not experiment design.
More features doesn't change that you optimize one dimension; cannibalization persists.
Correct — the primary measures one value dimension, and the optimizer exploits the gap to intent, like memorizing answers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按给定 loss 最大化目标的训练过程，会钻指标与真实意图的缝隙。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The optimizer is the training process maximizing the given loss; it exploits gaps between the metric and true intent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主指标只代理了部分业务价值，与真实意图之间的差距被优化器利用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The proxy gap is the distance between a partial-value primary metric and true intent, which the optimizer exploits.

q: 护栏指标（guardrail metric）的定义是什么，在实验流水线里扮演什么角色？
q_en: What defines a guardrail metric, and what role does it play in the experimentation pipeline?
why: 护栏是带预设阈值的次级指标：只要显著越界就拦住上线，不管主指标涨多少。它是实验流水线里的断路器（circuit breaker），把主指标漏掉的价值维度变成硬闸门。
why_en: A guardrail is a secondary metric with a preset threshold that blocks launch on significant breach regardless of primary gains — a circuit breaker in the experiment pipeline.
options: 带预设阈值的次级指标：越阈值就不许上线，无论主指标涨多少，像流水线的断路器
主优化指标的别名：就是被写进 loss、由优化器直接最大化的那个目标量
只用于事后监控的指标：不参与上线闸门，仅供诊断和长期趋势参考
一种离线评估数据集：用于训练阶段筛掉过拟合的候选模型版本
options_en: A threshold-bearing secondary metric: a breach blocks launch regardless of primary gains, like the pipeline's circuit breaker.
An alias for the primary metric: the target written into the loss and directly maximized by the optimizer.
A monitor-only metric: it doesn't gate launch, serving only diagnostics and long-term trends.
An offline evaluation dataset used during training to screen out overfit candidate models.
optionExplanations: 对；护栏是带阈值的次级指标，越界即拦上线、不管主指标涨多少，是断路器。
写进 loss 被优化的是主指标，不是护栏；护栏是约束不是优化目标。
只监控不闸门的是 observational；护栏必须能拦上线才叫护栏。
护栏不是离线数据集，它是上线判定里的次级指标闸门。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a guardrail is a threshold secondary metric that blocks launch on breach regardless of primary gains, a circuit breaker.
What's written into the loss and optimized is the primary, not the guardrail; a guardrail is a constraint.
Monitor-only-no-gate describes observational; a guardrail must be able to block launch.
A guardrail isn't a dataset; it's a secondary-metric gate in the launch decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带预设阈值的次级指标，显著越界就拦住上线，不管主指标涨多少。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a secondary metric with a preset threshold that blocks launch on significant breach, regardless of primary gains.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一超过安全阈值就自动切断的机制，这里指护栏拦住上线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker trips once a safety threshold is exceeded; here the guardrail blocks launch.

q: 生产级指标体系分哪三层，各层在上线判定里的作用是什么？
q_en: What are the three tiers of a production metric hierarchy, and each tier's role in the launch decision?
why: 三层是成熟度信号：primary 是唯一被优化的目标；guardrail 是带阈值的硬闸门，显著越界就拦上线；observational 只监控诊断、不参与放行。面试里能叫全三层，说明你知道上线不是只看主指标。
why_en: Three tiers signal maturity: primary is the sole optimization target, guardrail is a threshold hard gate that blocks launch on breach, and observational is monitored but doesn't gate release.
tradeoff: primary（被优化的单目标） vs guardrail（带阈值的硬闸门） vs observational（仅监控不闸门）
options: primary 定阈值闸门、guardrail 被优化、observational 也被优化，三者都参与上线判定
三层本质都是监控指标，只是刷新频率不同，都不参与上线的放行闸门
primary 单目标被优化；guardrail 带阈值当硬闸门、越界拦上线；observational 仅监控不闸门
primary 与 guardrail 都写进 loss 一起被优化，observational 只是它们的离线镜像
options_en: Primary sets the threshold gate, guardrail is optimized, observational is optimized — all three gate launch.
All three are essentially monitoring metrics differing only in refresh rate, and none gates launch.
Primary is the single optimization target; guardrail is a threshold hard gate blocking launch on breach; observational only monitors.
Primary and guardrail both go into the loss and are co-optimized, and observational is their offline mirror.
optionExplanations: 反了：primary 是被优化的、不是定阈值闸门；三者角色搞混了。
三层不是同类监控：guardrail 会闸门上线，observational 才只监控。
对；primary 单目标优化、guardrail 越界拦上线、observational 只监控，角色分明。
只有 primary 进 loss 被优化；guardrail 是约束、observational 只观测，不一起优化。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: the primary is optimized, not the threshold gate; the roles are mixed up.
The tiers aren't the same kind of monitoring: guardrails gate launch, only observational is monitor-only.
Correct — primary is the single optimization target, guardrail gates launch on breach, observational only monitors.
Only the primary goes into the loss; the guardrail is a constraint and observational only observes, not co-optimized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一被优化的目标，如观看时长、CTR、每次会话收入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary metric is the single optimization target, e.g. watch time, CTR, or revenue per session.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带阈值的硬约束，显著越界就拦上线，如留存、举报率、退货率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a threshold hard constraint that blocks launch on breach, e.g. retention, report rate, return rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只监控诊断、不参与上线闸门，如内容多样性、创作者上传率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An observational metric is monitored for diagnostics only and doesn't gate launch, e.g. content diversity or creator upload rate.

scenario: 面试官抛出「1B 用户 embedding 要多少存储？」这种没有边界的容量题。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks an open-ended capacity question like 'how much storage for 1B user embeddings?'
q: back-of-envelope 估算里面试官真正在评分的是什么？
q_en: In a back-of-the-envelope estimate, what is the interviewer actually grading?
why: 面试官评的是推理链不是算术精度：先显式声明假设（在线比例、精度、利用率），再一步步推到量级。算错一个量级内不致命，说不出假设才致命。
why_en: Interviewers grade the reasoning chain, not arithmetic precision, so state assumptions first and reason to an order of magnitude.
options: 算出精确到个位 GB 的最终数字，任何一步算错都直接扣分
先显式列出假设、用量级近似，展示可复查的推理链
背出 A100、GPT-3 的官方参数表，记得越全越显专业
不解释怎么推的，直接甩出一个范围，回答越快越好
options_en: Nail the final number to the exact GB; any slip in a step loses points.
State assumptions explicitly and reason to an order of magnitude via a checkable chain.
Recite the official spec sheets of A100 and GPT-3 — the more the better.
Just blurt a range without explaining how you got it; speed is all that matters.
optionExplanations: 面试不看小数点：错一个量级内不致命，死磕个位精度反而错过了考点——推理链。
对；先声明在线比例/精度/利用率这些假设再逐步推量级，「先说假设再算」就是 senior 信号。
基准数是最后 sanity-check 用的，不是主线；背参数表答不出「怎么推导」。
给范围没错，但不解释假设就没有推理链可评，面试官看不到你的思路。
optionExplanations_en: Interviews don't care about decimals; being off within an order of magnitude is fine, but obsessing over the last digit misses the point — the chain.
Correct — declare assumptions like online ratio, precision, utilization, then step to a magnitude; 'assume before compute' is the senior signal.
Benchmark numbers are for the final sanity-check, not the main line; reciting specs doesn't show derivation.
A range is fine, but without stated assumptions there's no chain to grade and the interviewer can't see your thinking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模糊的容量问题拆成子问题、声明假设、快速推出量级答案的技能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Back-of-the-envelope estimation decomposes a vague capacity question into subproblems, states assumptions, and quickly derives an order-of-magnitude answer.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: ML 系统容量估算通常拆成哪四个支柱？
q_en: What are the four pillars an ML-system capacity estimate decomposes into?
why: 四支柱 = 模型大小 / 存储 / 吞吐 / 训练时间，每块一个公式，把模糊的容量题变成四个可算的子问题。认出题在问哪根支柱，是套对公式的前提。
why_en: The four pillars are model size, storage, throughput, and training time — each with its own formula that turns a vague question into a computable subproblem.
diagram:
flowchart TD Q["模糊容量问题"] --> P1["模型大小
params × bytes"] Q --> P2["存储
实体 × 维度 × 副本"] Q --> P3["吞吐
QPS ÷ 单卡吞吐"] Q --> P4["训练时间
计算量 ÷ 有效算力"]
options: CPU、内存、磁盘、网络这四种硬件资源
数据、模型、评估、部署这四个流程阶段
模型大小、存储、吞吐、训练时间
准确率、召回率、延迟、成本这四个指标
options_en: The four hardware resources: CPU, memory, disk, network.
The four pipeline stages: data, model, evaluation, deployment.
Model size, storage, throughput, training time.
The four metrics: accuracy, recall, latency, cost.
optionExplanations: 这是通用硬件清单，不是 ML 估算的四支柱；支柱是按「要算什么量」分的。
这是 ML 项目的生命周期阶段，不是容量估算的四个可算子问题。
对；模型大小/存储/吞吐/训练时间各有公式，是估算题的标准拆法。
这些是模型质量/成本指标，不是容量估算要推的四个量级。
optionExplanations_en: That's a generic hardware list, not the four estimation pillars, which split by 'what quantity to compute'.
Those are ML lifecycle stages, not the four computable subproblems of a capacity estimate.
Correct — model size/storage/throughput/training time each have a formula, the standard decomposition.
Those are model-quality/cost metrics, not the four magnitudes a capacity estimate derives.
category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 补全模型大小（推理）的核心公式：
q_en: Fill in the core model-size (inference) formula:
text: 模型内存（推理）= 参数量 × {{每参数字节数}}；推理估算到这一步就结束。
text_en: Model memory (inference) = parameters × {{bytes_per_parameter}}; for inference the estimate stops here.
why: 公式：参数量 × 每参数字节数；每参数字节数由精度决定（FP32=4、FP16=2、INT8=1）。它是后续算单卡够不够、要不要多卡的基数。
why_en: Model memory equals parameters times bytes-per-parameter, where bytes-per-parameter is set by precision and feeds every downstream GPU-fit decision.
category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 补全每参数字节数随精度的取值：
q_en: Fill in bytes-per-parameter by precision:
text: 每参数字节数看精度：FP32 = {{4}} bytes，FP16/BF16 = {{2}} bytes，INT8 = {{1}} byte。
text_en: Bytes per parameter by precision: FP32 = {{4}} bytes, FP16/BF16 = {{2}} bytes, INT8 = {{1}} byte.
why: FP16 半精度把显存砍半，INT8 量化砍到 1/4；选精度直接决定模型能不能塞进单卡。这些字节数是模型大小公式的乘子。
why_en: FP16 halves memory and INT8 quantization cuts it to a quarter, so precision directly decides whether the model fits a single card.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全精度浮点，每参数 4 字节，传统训练用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP32 (32-bit floating point) uses 4 bytes per parameter, the traditional full-precision format for training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 半精度浮点，每参数 2 字节，推理与混合精度训练的标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP16/BF16 are half-precision formats at 2 bytes per parameter, standard for inference and mixed-precision training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 8 位整数量化，每参数 1 字节，优化服务用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INT8 (8-bit integer) quantization uses 1 byte per parameter, used for optimized serving.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

scenario: 线上推理服务显存吃紧，想在单卡塞下更大模型，且能容忍轻微精度损失。
scenario_en: An online inference service is memory-constrained, wants a bigger model on one card, and can tolerate slight accuracy loss.
q: 该选哪种数值精度来服务？
q_en: Which numeric precision should you serve with?
why: 选 INT8 量化 = 1 byte/param，显存砍到 FP32 的 1/4、FP16 的 1/2，正好换取「单卡塞更大模型」。代价是量化会掉一点精度。
why_en: Pick INT8 at 1 byte per parameter to cut memory to a quarter of FP32 so a bigger model fits one card, trading a little accuracy.
tradeoff: INT8（显存最省、有精度损失） vs FP16（省一半、精度损失更小）
options: FP32 = 4 byte/param，精度最高但最占显存，塞不下更大模型
FP16/BF16 = 2 byte/param，把显存砍半，精度损失很小
各层凭直觉混用不同精度，边跑边手调，最灵活
INT8 量化 = 1 byte/param，显存砍到 FP32 的四分之一
options_en: FP32 = 4 bytes/param: highest accuracy but most memory, can't fit a bigger model.
FP16/BF16 = 2 bytes/param: halves memory with tiny accuracy loss.
Hand-mix different precisions per layer by intuition, tuning as you go — most flexible.
INT8 quantization = 1 byte/param: cuts memory to a quarter of FP32.
whenOtherWins: 若模型对精度敏感（高精度回归、金融风控），量化掉点太多，就退回 FP16 只砍一半显存换更小的损失。
optionExplanations: FP32 精度最高但最占显存，与「省显存塞更大模型」的目标相反。
FP16 是很好的折中，但题目已说能容忍精度损失且显存最紧，INT8 更省。
凭直觉逐层混精度不可控、难复现，不是标准服务化做法。
对；显存最紧又容忍掉点时选 INT8，1 字节/参数把空间腾出来塞更大模型。
optionExplanations_en: FP32 has top accuracy but the most memory, opposite to 'save memory, fit bigger model'.
FP16 is a fine middle ground, but with tolerance for loss and tightest memory, INT8 saves more.
Ad-hoc per-layer precision is uncontrolled and hard to reproduce, not a standard serving move.
Correct — when memory is tightest and you tolerate loss, INT8 at 1 byte/param frees room for a bigger model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 8 位整数量化，每参数 1 字节，最省显存但有精度损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INT8 (8-bit integer) quantization uses 1 byte per parameter, saving the most memory at some accuracy cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把高精度浮点权重压成低位表示（如 INT8）以省显存、提速。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization compresses high-precision float weights into a lower-bit representation (e.g. INT8) to save memory and speed up serving.

q: 7B 参数模型用 FP16 做推理，大约需要多少显存？
q_en: About how much memory does a 7B-parameter model need for FP16 inference?
why: 公式：7e9 × 2 bytes = 14 GB（FP16 = 2 字节/参数）。它是判断单卡 80 GB HBM 够不够、要不要多卡的基数——别和训练的 84 GB 混。
why_en: 7e9 times 2 bytes equals 14 GB, the base number for deciding whether a single 80 GB HBM card suffices.
options: ~7 GB
~28 GB
~14 GB
~84 GB
options_en: ~7 GB
~28 GB
~14 GB
~84 GB

termDefinitions.meaning: 半精度浮点，每参数 2 字节，推理标准精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP16 (16-bit floating point) uses 2 bytes per parameter, the standard precision for inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: GPU 上的高带宽显存，单张 A100 约 80 GB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HBM (High-Bandwidth Memory) is the GPU's on-package memory; a single A100 has about 80 GB.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 补全 Adam + FP32 训练的每参数显存拆解：
q_en: Fill in the per-parameter training memory breakdown for Adam + FP32:
text: Adam + FP32 训练 ≈ 参数 × {{16}} bytes = {{4}}（权重）+ 4（梯度）+ {{8}}（两个动量项）。
text_en: Adam + FP32 training ≈ params × {{16}} bytes = {{4}} (weights) + 4 (gradients) + {{8}} (two momentum terms).
why: 训练除权重外还要存梯度和 Adam 的两个动量项，所以 ≈16 bytes/param，是推理（FP16=2）的约 4–6×；这解释了为什么同一模型训练显存远大于推理。
why_en: Training also stores gradients and Adam's two momentum terms, so about 16 bytes per parameter, roughly 4–6x inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用优化器，除权重外还维护一阶、二阶两个动量项，训练显存翻倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adam (Adaptive Moment Estimation) is a common optimizer that keeps first- and second-moment terms beyond the weights, inflating training memory.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

scenario: 7B 模型 FP16 推理只要 14 GB，但用 Adam 混合精度训练要 84 GB+（优化器状态+梯度+激活）。
scenario_en: A 7B model needs 14 GB for FP16 inference but 84 GB+ to train with Adam mixed precision (optimizer states + gradients + activations).
q: 这个 84 GB 的数字带来什么设计后果？
q_en: What design consequence does the 84 GB figure force?
why: 84 GB > 单张 A100 的 80 GB HBM，塞不进一张卡 → 要么把模型/优化器状态跨卡分片（ZeRO、张量并行），要么把优化器状态 offload 到 CPU。这就是「推理能单卡、训练要多卡」的根因。
why_en: 84 GB exceeds a single A100's 80 GB HBM, so you must shard across GPUs (ZeRO/tensor parallel) or offload optimizer state to CPU.
diagram:
flowchart LR I["推理 14 GB"] --> T["训练 84 GB+
+梯度+优化器"] T --> H{"> 80 GB A100 HBM?"} H -->|是| S["分片 / ZeRO / offload"]
options: 超过单张 A100 的 80 GB HBM，必须跨多卡分片，或用 ZeRO/offload
无所谓，训练和推理显存一样，14 GB 就够用了
把 batch size 调大就能把训练显存压下来，不用多卡
换成 CPU 训练就没有显存上限，直接单机跑完
options_en: It exceeds a single A100's 80 GB HBM, so shard across GPUs or use ZeRO/offload.
No issue — training and inference memory are the same, 14 GB is enough.
Just raise the batch size to shrink training memory; no multi-GPU needed.
Train on CPU to remove the memory ceiling and finish on one machine.
optionExplanations: 对；84 GB 塞不进 80 GB HBM，只能分片或 offload，这正是训练要多卡的根因。
反了：训练带梯度+优化器状态，是推理的 4–6×，绝不等同 14 GB。
batch 越大激活越多、显存更吃紧，调 batch 救不了权重+优化器的固定占用。
CPU 训练慢到不可用，且题目问的是 GPU 显存约束，绕开约束不是设计。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 84 GB won't fit 80 GB HBM, so sharding or offload is required, the reason training needs multiple GPUs.
Backwards: training adds gradients + optimizer state, 4–6x inference, never equal to 14 GB.
Bigger batches add activations and use more memory; batching can't cut the fixed weight+optimizer footprint.
CPU training is unusably slow, and the question is about GPU memory — dodging the constraint isn't a design.

termDefinitions.meaning: GPU 高带宽显存，单张 A100 约 80 GB，模型能否塞进单卡看它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HBM (High-Bandwidth Memory) is GPU memory; a single A100 has ~80 GB, which decides whether a model fits one card.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把优化器状态/梯度/参数切分到多卡，消除冗余以省显存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer) shards optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across GPUs to remove redundancy and save memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把优化器状态等从 GPU 挪到 CPU/内存以腾出显存，代价是变慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offload moves optimizer state from GPU to CPU/host memory to free HBM, at the cost of speed.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 把「从模型规模推到训练要不要多卡」的推理链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the reasoning chain from model size to the multi-GPU decision for training:
steps: 权重显存 = 7e9 × 2 = 14 GB（推理下限）
定参数量与精度：7B 参数、FP16 = 2 bytes/param
对比单卡 80 GB HBM：训练 84 GB 装不下
加梯度 + Adam 两个动量项 → 训练 ≈ 84 GB
决定跨多卡分片 / ZeRO / offload
why: 先由参数×精度得推理下限，再叠加梯度和优化器状态得训练显存，和 80 GB HBM 一比就知道要不要分片。跳过优化器状态是最常见的低估。
why_en: Derive the inference floor from params times precision, add gradients and optimizer state for the training footprint, then compare to 80 GB HBM to decide sharding.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["7B × FP16"] --> B["权重 14 GB"]
  B --> C["+梯度+Adam ≈ 84 GB"]
  C --> D["> 80 GB HBM"]
  D --> E["多卡分片"]
category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 补全 embedding 存储估算公式：
q_en: Fill in the embedding-storage estimation formula:
text: embedding 存储 = 实体数 × {{维度}} × {{每浮点字节数}} × {{副本数}}。
text_en: Embedding storage = num_entities × {{embedding_dim}} × {{bytes_per_float}} × {{replication}}.
why: 四个乘子缺一不可，最常被漏的是副本数（replication）；生产常 3x 副本。它是后续算要几块盘、跨几个副本的基数。
why_en: All four multipliers matter, and the most-forgotten is replication; the result feeds how many disks and replicas you provision.
category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 10 亿用户 embedding，每个 256 维 FP32，裸存储约多少？
q_en: 1B user embeddings at 256 dim FP32 — about how much raw storage?
why: 公式：1e9 × 256 × 4 bytes = 1.024e12 ≈ 1 TB（FP32 = 4 字节/浮点）。这个裸数是起点——再乘 3x 副本≈3 TB，还要叠加多版本和特征快照。
why_en: 1e9 × 256 × 4 bytes ≈ 1 TB, the raw base that then multiplies by ~3x replication to ~3 TB before versions and snapshots.
options: ~1 TB
~4 TB
~26 GB
options_en: ~1 TB
~4 TB
~26 GB

termDefinitions.meaning: 全精度浮点，每个浮点 4 字节，embedding 常按它算裸存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP32 (32-bit floating point) is 4 bytes per float, often used to size raw embedding storage.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

scenario: 有人估 embedding 存储时只算了 1B × 256 × FP32 ≈ 1 TB 就上报了。
scenario_en: Someone estimates embedding storage as just 1B × 256 × FP32 ≈ 1 TB and reports that.
q: 这个估算漏了什么，生产实际要留多少？
q_en: What did this estimate miss, and what should production actually budget?
why: 漏了副本和版本：生产为容灾/读扩展常 3x 副本，再叠加多个模型版本（回滚/AB）。所以 1 TB 的裸数落地常是 3 TB+，漏 replication 是最常见的低估来源。
why_en: It ignored replication and versioning: production typically runs 3x replicas plus multiple model versions, so 1 TB raw becomes 3 TB+.
options: 应该再除以 3，因为列式压缩通常能省掉三分之二空间
漏了 GPU 显存，存储应该按 GPU 张数再乘一遍
没漏，1 TB 就是最终答案，直接照此采购磁盘即可
漏了副本和版本：生产常 3x 副本 + 多版本，实际按 3 TB 起留余量
options_en: Divide by 3 — columnar compression usually saves two-thirds of the space.
It missed GPU memory — storage should be multiplied again by the GPU count.
Nothing missed — 1 TB is the final answer; purchase disks accordingly.
It missed replication and versioning: prod runs 3x replicas + multiple versions, so budget from 3 TB up.
optionExplanations: 压缩能省空间但不该默认，且方向反了——生产是往上乘副本，不是往下除。
GPU 显存和落盘存储是两码事，把它乘进存储是概念混淆。
只报裸数会系统性低估，漏掉副本和版本是估存储最常见的坑。
对；乘副本（容灾/读扩展，常 3x）再叠版本（回滚/AB），裸数 1 TB 落地 3 TB+。
optionExplanations_en: Compression can save space but shouldn't be assumed, and the direction is wrong — prod multiplies up for replicas, not down.
GPU memory and on-disk storage are different things; multiplying storage by GPUs conflates them.
Reporting only the raw number systematically underestimates; missing replicas/versions is the classic storage trap.
Correct — multiply by replicas (DR/read-scaling, ~3x) then add versions (rollback/AB), turning 1 TB into 3 TB+.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为容灾和读扩展把数据复制多份，生产常 3x，直接乘进存储量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication copies data (commonly 3x) for durability and read-scaling, multiplying total storage.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 估 ML 系统总存储时，为什么模型参数量往往是最小的一块？
q_en: When sizing an ML system's total storage, why is the model often the smallest piece?
why: 模型是 GB 级，但特征存储按天快照 × 90 天留存会累积，训练日志常到 PB 级——远超模型。估总量别只盯模型，数据侧才是大头。
why_en: The model is gigabytes, but feature stores compound daily snapshots over 90-day retention and training logs reach petabytes, dwarfing it.
tradeoff: 模型存储（GB 级、静态） vs 训练数据/特征存储（PB 级、随快照×留存累积）
options: 模型参数总是最大的一块，其余数据都可以忽略不计
特征只存当前值、从不留历史，所以整体存储很小
训练数据训练完就删，不占长期存储，所以模型最大
特征存储按天快照 × 90 天留存累积，训练日志常达 PB 级，远超模型的 GB 级
options_en: The model is always the biggest piece and other data is negligible.
Features store only current values and never keep history, so total storage is tiny.
Training data is deleted after training and takes no long-term storage, so the model is largest.
Feature stores compound daily snapshots over 90-day retention and logs hit petabytes, dwarfing the GB-scale model.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反：GB 级的模型常是最小项，数据侧才是主导。
特征存储通常保留历史快照做训练/回填，不是只存当前值。
训练数据/日志常长期保留用于复训与审计，不会训练完即删。
对；每日快照 × 90 天留存 + PB 级日志把总量顶上去，模型只是零头。
optionExplanations_en: The opposite: the GB-scale model is usually the smallest term; the data side dominates.
Feature stores usually keep historical snapshots for training/backfill, not just current values.
Training data/logs are often retained long-term for retraining and audit, not deleted after training.
Correct — daily snapshots × 90-day retention plus petabyte logs dominate; the model is a rounding error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放模型特征的系统，常按天快照并保留数十天，累积量很大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store holds model features, often snapshotted daily and retained for weeks, accumulating large volume.

termDefinitions.meaning: 1 PB ≈ 1000 TB ≈ 1e15 字节，大规模训练日志的常见量级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PB (Petabyte) is about 1000 TB (1e15 bytes), a common scale for large training logs.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 补全吞吐（要几张 GPU）的估算公式：
q_en: Fill in the throughput (how many GPUs) estimation formula:
text: 所需 GPU 数 = 峰值 QPS ÷ 单卡吞吐，其中单卡吞吐 = {{batch_size}} ÷ {{每 batch 延迟}}。
text_en: Required GPUs = peak QPS ÷ per-GPU throughput, where per-GPU throughput = {{batch_size}} ÷ {{latency_per_batch}}.
why: 需求侧 = 峰值 QPS，供给侧 = 单卡吞吐（每 batch 处理多少 ÷ 处理一 batch 要多久）。QPS = Queries Per Second，这个数决定要买/租多少张卡。
why_en: Demand is peak QPS and supply is per-GPU throughput (batch size over per-batch latency); the result sizes the GPU fleet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，吞吐估算的需求侧基数，通常用峰值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) is the demand-side base for throughput estimation, usually taken at peak.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 增大推理 batch size 对吞吐和每请求延迟分别有什么影响？
q_en: How does a larger inference batch size affect throughput versus per-request latency?
why: 大 batch 把 GPU 核心喂满 → 吞吐/利用率上去，但请求要等凑够一批 → p99 延迟上去。离线管线偏大 batch，在线低延迟服务偏小 batch。
why_en: A larger batch saturates GPU cores so throughput and utilization rise, but requests wait to fill a batch so p99 latency rises.
tradeoff: 大 batch（吞吐高、利用率高） vs 小 batch/单条（延迟低、实时友好）
diagram:
flowchart LR S["大 batch"] --> U["GPU 核心喂满
吞吐↑ 利用率↑"] S --> L["要等凑够一批
每请求延迟↑"]
options: 吞吐↑、延迟↓，纯赚没有代价，永远该开最大 batch
吞吐↓、延迟↑，两头都变差，所以永远不该 batch
只影响显存占用，对吞吐和延迟都没有影响
吞吐↑（GPU 核心喂满、利用率高），但每请求延迟↑（要等凑够一批）
options_en: Throughput↑ and latency↓ — pure win, always max out the batch.
Throughput↓ and latency↑ — both worse, so never batch.
It only affects memory use, with no effect on throughput or latency.
Throughput↑ (cores saturated, high utilization) but per-request latency↑ (waiting to fill a batch).
optionExplanations: 没有纯赚：吞吐涨的代价就是延迟涨，实时服务扛不住。
方向错一半：batch 提吞吐是真的，只是同时抬高了延迟。
batch 直接改变吞吐和延迟，说它只影响显存是错的。
对；大 batch 换吞吐/利用率但牺牲每请求延迟，是最核心的取舍轴。
optionExplanations_en: No pure win: the price of higher throughput is higher latency, which real-time serving can't take.
Half wrong: batching does raise throughput, it just raises latency at the same time.
Batching directly changes throughput and latency; saying it only touches memory is wrong.
Correct — a big batch trades throughput/utilization for per-request latency, the core axis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 请求快于该值的尾延迟，衡量最坏体验，实时服务的关键约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the tail below which 99% of requests complete, the key constraint for real-time serving.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

scenario: 网约车 ETA 预测要求 p99 < 100ms 的在线响应；另一头是夜间离线特征回填管线。
scenario_en: Ride-share ETA prediction needs an online p99 < 100 ms; the other job is a nightly offline feature-backfill pipeline.
q: 这两种场景该用一样的 batching 策略吗？
q_en: Should both use the same batching strategy?
why: 不该：p99<100ms 是给定的 SLO 目标（不是算出来的），它直接封死大 batch——等不起；离线回填没有延迟约束，才能用大 batch 把 GPU 喂满冲吞吐。
why_en: No — the p99 < 100 ms SLO forbids large batches for online ETA, while offline backfill has no latency budget and can batch big for throughput.
tradeoff: 在线低延迟（小 batch，受 p99 SLO 约束） vs 离线高吞吐（大 batch，无延迟约束）
options: 该：两者都用最大 batch，吞吐永远优先，延迟不重要
不该：ETA 受 p99<100ms 约束只能小 batch，离线回填不在乎延迟可用大 batch
该：两者都用 batch=1，延迟永远优先，吞吐不重要
无所谓：batch size 只影响显存，跟延迟和吞吐都无关
options_en: Yes: max batch for both, throughput always first, latency doesn't matter.
No: ETA is bound by p99 < 100 ms so small batch, while offline backfill ignores latency and can batch big.
Yes: batch=1 for both, latency always first, throughput doesn't matter.
Doesn't matter: batch size only affects memory, unrelated to latency or throughput.
whenOtherWins: 若在线服务延迟预算宽松（如秒级的批量推荐），也可以攒一点 micro-batch 换吞吐，不必死守单条。
optionExplanations: 在线全上最大 batch 会击穿 p99<100ms 的 SLO，用户等不起。
对；延迟约束决定 batch：在线被 SLO 封死只能小 batch，离线放开可大 batch。
离线也用 batch=1 会白白浪费吞吐、拖长回填时间，没必要。
batch 直接影响延迟和吞吐，说它只碰显存是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Max batch online blows the p99 < 100 ms SLO; users can't wait.
Correct — the latency constraint sets the batch: online is SLO-capped to small, offline is free to batch big.
Using batch=1 offline wastes throughput and stretches the backfill for no reason.
Batch size directly affects latency and throughput; claiming it only touches memory is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 请求快于该值的尾延迟，实时服务的关键约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the tail below which 99% of requests complete, a key real-time constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标，如 p99<100ms，是给定约束不是算出来的结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service-Level Objective) like p99 < 100 ms is a given target, not a computed result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计到达时间，网约车里需实时低延迟预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) is the predicted arrival time, needing low-latency real-time inference in ride-share.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 同样跑在 GPU 上，稠密矩阵乘和稀疏 embedding 查表的吞吐为什么差很多？
q_en: On the same GPU, why do dense matmuls and sparse embedding lookups have very different throughput?
why: matmul 每读一份数据算很多次 → 卡在算力（compute-bound），能靠 batching 提吞吐；embedding 查表随机取一行几乎不算 → 卡在显存带宽（bandwidth-bound），batching 帮助小，要按带宽而非算力配卡。
why_en: Matmuls reuse data across many ops so they're compute-bound and batch well, while embedding lookups fetch a row and barely compute, so they're bandwidth-bound.
tradeoff: 稠密 matmul（计算受限、吞吐高、batching 有效） vs 稀疏 embedding 查表（带宽受限、吞吐低、batching 帮助小）
diagram:
flowchart TB
  D["稠密 matmul"] -->|计算受限| DH["吞吐高"]
  E["稀疏 embedding 查表"] -->|带宽受限| EH["吞吐低"]
options: 稠密 matmul 计算受限、能喂满核心吞吐高；稀疏查表内存带宽受限、吞吐低得多
两者吞吐一样，都只看单卡峰值 FLOPS，op 类型不影响
稀疏查表更快，因为它做的乘法运算更少、更省算力
稠密 matmul 更慢，因为它涉及的参数更多、读得更多
options_en: Dense matmul is compute-bound and saturates cores for high throughput; sparse lookup is memory-bandwidth-bound and far lower.
Both have identical throughput — only peak FLOPS matters and op type is irrelevant.
Sparse lookup is faster because it does fewer multiplications and uses less compute.
Dense matmul is slower because it involves more parameters and more reads.
optionExplanations: 对；matmul 卡算力能 batching 提吞吐，查表卡带宽 batching 帮助小，配卡逻辑不同。
op 类型恰恰决定卡在算力还是带宽，吞吐差别很大，不是只看 FLOPS。
查表算得少不代表快——它卡在随机取数的带宽上，反而吞吐低。
matmul 虽算得多但计算能被喂满，吞吐反而高，方向说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — matmul is compute-bound and batches to high throughput, lookups are bandwidth-bound and batch poorly, so provisioning differs.
Op type is exactly what decides compute- vs bandwidth-bound; throughput differs a lot, not just FLOPS.
Fewer multiplies doesn't mean faster — lookups are bottlenecked on random-access bandwidth, so throughput is low.
Matmul computes more but keeps cores fed, giving higher throughput — the direction is reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 瓶颈在算力叫计算受限，瓶颈在显存带宽叫带宽受限，决定 batching 是否有效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compute-bound means the bottleneck is arithmetic; bandwidth-bound means it's memory bandwidth, which decides whether batching helps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 矩阵乘法，稠密网络的主运算，数据复用高、计算受限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A matmul (matrix multiply) is the main dense-network op, with high data reuse and compute-bound behavior.

q: 为什么「优化延迟」和「优化吞吐」不能混为一谈？
q_en: Why can't 'optimize latency' and 'optimize throughput' be treated as the same goal?
why: 延迟=单请求多快返回，吞吐=单位时间处理多少；batching 提吞吐却常抬高延迟，两个目标手段相反。先问清哪个约束主导，再选手段。
why_en: Latency is how fast one request returns and throughput is how many per second; batching lifts throughput but raises latency, so the goals pull opposite ways.
tradeoff: 延迟优化（小 batch、就近部署） vs 吞吐优化（大 batch、高利用率）
options: 两者本质一回事，只要吞吐高延迟就一定低，一起优化即可
延迟只由网络决定、吞吐只由 CPU 决定，二者互不相关
延迟=单请求多快，吞吐=单位时间处理多少；batching 提吞吐却抬高延迟，目标相反
只要一味提高吞吐，就总能顺带把延迟也降下来
options_en: They're essentially the same — high throughput always means low latency, so optimize together.
Latency depends only on the network and throughput only on the CPU; they're unrelated.
Latency is per-request speed, throughput is volume per second; batching raises throughput but hurts latency, opposite goals.
Just keep pushing throughput and latency will always come down along with it.
optionExplanations: 反了：提吞吐常靠 batching，恰恰会抬高延迟，两者不是同涨。
延迟和吞吐都受 batch、部署、op 类型影响，不是各管一个硬件。
对；它们是相反方向的目标，先分清哪个约束主导，别用错手段。
一味提吞吐通常牺牲延迟，实时服务会被拖垮，不是顺带双赢。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: raising throughput often uses batching, which raises latency — they don't move together.
Both latency and throughput depend on batch, placement, and op type, not one hardware each.
Correct — they are opposing goals; identify which constraint dominates before choosing a tactic.
Pushing throughput usually sacrifices latency and crushes real-time serving — no free win.
category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 补全训练时间的估算公式：
q_en: Fill in the training-time estimation formula:
text: 训练时间 = (数据量 × epoch 数 × {{每样本 FLOPs}}) ÷ (GPU 数 × 单卡峰值 FLOPS × {{利用率因子}})。
text_en: Training time = (dataset × epochs × {{FLOPs_per_sample}}) ÷ (num_GPUs × peak_FLOPS × {{utilization_factor}}).
why: 分子=总计算量，分母=实际算力；最容易漏的是利用率因子（真实 30–50%，不是 100%）。FLOPs=工作量、FLOPS=每秒算力，别混。
why_en: The numerator is total work and the denominator is real compute; the most-forgotten term is the utilization factor, which is 30–50%, not 100%.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浮点运算次数，衡量一次训练的总工作量（小写 s）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FLOPs (Floating-Point Operations) count total arithmetic work, the numerator of training time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒浮点运算数，衡量硬件算力（大写 S）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FLOPS (Floating-Point Operations Per Second) measures hardware compute rate, the denominator.

q: 估训练时间时，单卡有效算力该按标称峰值 FLOPS 的多少来算？
q_en: When estimating training time, what fraction of nominal peak FLOPS should you assume as effective?
why: 经验法则（rule of thumb）：真实 GPU 利用率约 30–50%，被 all-reduce 通信、数据加载停顿、流水线气泡吃掉。有效 FLOPS = 峰值 × 0.3~0.5，是训练时间分母的关键折扣；忽略它会把训练时间低估 2–3 倍。
why_en: As a rule of thumb, real GPU utilization is 30–50% after all-reduce comms, data-loading stalls, and pipeline bubbles, so effective FLOPS = peak × 0.3–0.5.
options: 100%，直接用标称峰值
恰好 80%
options_en: 100% — use nominal peak directly.
Exactly 80%.
30–50% (rule of thumb).

termDefinitions.meaning: 多卡训练同步梯度的集合通信，是利用率被吃掉的主因之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: All-reduce is the collective communication that syncs gradients across GPUs, a main reason utilization drops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有效算力占标称峰值的比例，真实约 30–50%，训练时间分母要乘它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The utilization factor is effective compute over nominal peak, about 30–50% in practice, multiplying the training-time denominator.

category: Back Of The Envelope Estimation For ML Systems

q: 6e18 FLOPs 的训练任务，单张 A100（312 TFLOPS FP16 @ 40% 利用率）大约要多久？
q_en: A 6e18-FLOP training job on one A100 (312 TFLOPS FP16 @ 40% util) — about how long?
why: 有效算力 = 312 TFLOPS × 40% ≈ 125e12 FLOPS；6e18 ÷ 125e12 ≈ 48,000 s ≈ 13.3 h。TFLOPS=每秒万亿次浮点运算。这个数用来判断要不要多卡、排期多长。
why_en: Effective compute = 312 TFLOPS × 40% ≈ 125e12 FLOPS, and 6e18 ÷ 125e12 ≈ 48,000 s ≈ 13.3 h.
options: ~13 小时
~5 分钟
options_en: ~13 hours
~1.3 hours
~130 hours
~5 minutes

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒万亿（1e12）次浮点运算，单卡算力单位，A100 FP16 约 312。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TFLOPS (Tera Floating-Point Operations Per Second) is 1e12 ops/sec; an A100 does about 312 in FP16.

scenario: 上面算出训练在单张 A100 上约 13 小时，理论上一张卡放得下也跑得完。
scenario_en: The estimate says training fits in ~13 hours on a single A100, which technically holds the job.
q: 实践中为什么还要配 2–4 张卡？
q_en: Why still provision 2–4 GPUs in practice?
why: 单卡够但脆：13 小时里一旦故障就全重来，多卡能并行缩短墙钟时间、加容错。代价是多卡引入 all-reduce 通信开销、利用率还会再降一点，要在成本和鲁棒间权衡。
why_en: One card suffices but is fragile — a 13-hour run lost to a crash restarts fully, so 2–4 GPUs cut wall-clock time and add fault tolerance.
options: 因为单卡显存一定不够，必须堆更多卡才装得下这个任务
为通信留余量、加容错、缩短墙钟时间——单卡跑 13h 中途挂了要全重来
为了把 GPU 利用率从 40% 一路提到 100%，省电又省钱
没必要，一张卡最省钱，就用一张跑满 13 小时最优
options_en: Because one card's memory can't hold the job, so you must stack more cards.
To leave headroom for comms, add fault tolerance, and cut wall-clock — a 13-hour single-card run lost to a crash restarts fully.
To push GPU utilization from 40% all the way to 100%, saving power and money.
No need — one card is cheapest, so running it flat-out for 13 hours is optimal.
optionExplanations: 题目说单卡放得下，显存不是这里的瓶颈，堆卡的理由是容错和墙钟时间。
对；多卡换鲁棒与更短墙钟，代价是通信开销和利用率再降，是成本-鲁棒权衡。
多卡反而因 all-reduce 通信让利用率更低，不会到 100%，方向说反了。
单卡最便宜但最脆，13h 无冗余一挂全丢，生产不接受这种风险。
optionExplanations_en: The prompt says one card fits, so memory isn't the bottleneck; the reason is fault tolerance and wall-clock.
Correct — more GPUs buy robustness and shorter wall-clock at the cost of comms and lower utilization, a cost-robustness trade-off.
More GPUs actually lower utilization via all-reduce comms, never reaching 100% — direction reversed.
One card is cheapest but most fragile; 13h with no redundancy loses everything on a crash, unacceptable in prod.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务实际经历的真实时间，多卡并行可缩短它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wall-clock time is the real elapsed duration of a job, which parallel GPUs can shorten.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多卡同步梯度的集合通信，引入开销并压低利用率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: All-reduce is the gradient-sync collective across GPUs, adding overhead and lowering utilization.

q: 把训练时间估算的 worked example 排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the training-time worked example correctly:
steps: 总计算量 = 1e9 样本 × 2 GFLOPs × 3 epoch = 6e18 FLOPs
加通信 + 容错余量 → 实际配 2–4 张卡
取单卡峰值 312 TFLOPS × 利用率 40% ≈ 125e12 有效 FLOPS
why: 先由数据×epoch×每样本 FLOPs 得总工作量，再把峰值算力乘利用率因子得有效算力，相除得单卡时间，最后为通信和容错配 2–4 卡。
why_en: Compute total work from data×epochs×FLOPs-per-sample, scale peak by the utilization factor for effective compute, divide for single-card time, then provision 2–4 GPUs.

q: 以下哪些是 back-of-envelope 估算的经典低估陷阱？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are classic underestimation traps in back-of-the-envelope estimation? (multiple)
why: 三大低估都来自「把折扣项当没有」：GPU 利用率、优化器状态、副本/版本。用 1e9、2 的幂取整反而是好习惯，别当成错误。
why_en: The three traps all ignore a discount factor — GPU utilization, optimizer state, and replication — while aggressive rounding is good practice, not a trap.
options: 假设 GPU 利用率 100%（真实 30–50%，训练时间会低估 2–3×）
忘记优化器状态显存（训练是推理的 4–6×）
忽略副本/版本（生产存储常 3x 起，还要叠加多个模型版本）
用 1e9、2 的幂做粗略取整（这其实是推荐做法，不是陷阱）
options_en: Assuming 100% GPU utilization (real 30–50%, underestimating training time 2–3×).
Forgetting optimizer-state memory (training is 4–6× inference).
Ignoring replication/versioning (prod storage runs 3x+ and stacks multiple model versions).
Rounding with 1e9 and powers of 2 (this is recommended practice, not a trap).
optionExplanations: 对；100% 利用率是空想，漏乘 0.3~0.5 的因子会把训练时间低估几倍。
对；只算权重、漏梯度和优化器状态，会把训练显存低估 4–6 倍。
对；只报裸存储、漏副本和版本，是估存储最常见的系统性低估。
取整是加速心算、聚焦量级的好习惯，不是低估来源，所以不选。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 100% utilization is fantasy; omitting the 0.3–0.5 factor underestimates training time several-fold.
Correct — counting only weights and dropping gradients/optimizer state underestimates training memory 4–6×.
Correct — reporting raw storage without replicas/versions is the classic systematic storage underestimate.
Rounding speeds mental math and focuses on magnitude — not an underestimate, so not selected.

q: 估算题里最高信号的一句话动作是什么？
q_en: What is the highest-signal one-line move in an estimation question?
why: 算完主动说「让我对照一个已知基准核对一下」，把结果和 A100(80GB)/GPT-3(175B) 比一比。它展示你知道结果该落在什么量级、能自己抓离谱错误——这是资深信号。
why_en: Say 'let me sanity-check this against a known benchmark' and compare your result to A100 (80 GB) or GPT-3 (175B) — it shows you know the right order of magnitude.
options: 把小数点后再多算两位，让最终数字显得更精确可信
算完主动说「让我对照一个已知基准核对一下」，跟 A100/GPT-3 比一比
直接拒绝给任何数字，反复说「这要看具体情况」
只报最终数字、不解释任何假设，让回答显得又快又利落
options_en: Compute two more decimal places to make the final number look more precise.
Proactively say 'let me sanity-check this against a known benchmark' and compare to A100/GPT-3.
Refuse to give any number and keep repeating 'it depends'.
Report only the final number with no assumptions, to seem fast and slick.
optionExplanations: 多算小数位是伪精确，面试看的是量级对不对，不是位数多。
对；sanity-check 展示你有量级直觉、能自查离谱错误，是最高信号动作。
一味「看情况」不给量级，等于没展示估算能力。
不解释假设就没有推理链，快而空反而扣分。
optionExplanations_en: Extra decimals are false precision; interviews care about the right magnitude, not digit count.
Correct — a sanity-check shows magnitude intuition and self-correction, the highest-signal move.
Endless 'it depends' with no magnitude shows no estimation ability.
No stated assumptions means no chain; fast but empty loses points.
