optionExplanations: 随机分区会切断大量边,跨机通信暴涨,负载均衡也换不回被通信吃掉的吞吐。
对;最小化割边让消息传递多在本地,再靠批量+重叠+异步预取藏住剩余通信,吞吐才稳。
全图复制到每台机内存放不下(数十亿边),正是内存瓶颈要解决的问题,复制无解。
丢弃节点会破坏图结构、丢失多跳信号,是损害模型质量的错误简化。
optionExplanations_en: Random partitioning cuts many edges, exploding cross-machine comms; balance can't win back throughput lost to comms.
Correct — minimizing cut edges keeps message passing local, and batching, overlap, and async prefetch hide the rest, stabilizing throughput.
Replicating the whole graph won't fit in each machine's memory (billions of edges) — the very memory bottleneck at hand.
Dropping nodes breaks graph structure and loses multi-hop signal, a harmful over-simplification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大图切分到多台机器,尽量减少跨分区的边以降低跨机通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graph partitioning splits a large graph across machines, minimizing cross-partition edges to reduce cross-machine communication.

category: Graph Neural Networks In System Design

scenario: 推荐/排序系统用 GNN,图变化不快(如社交连接),但线上打分有严格延迟预算。
scenario_en: A rec/ranking system uses a GNN on a slowly changing graph (social links) but has a strict online-scoring latency budget.
q: 延迟约束下,最有效的 serving 策略是什么?
q_en: Under the latency constraint, what's the most effective serving strategy?
why: 离线批量算好所有节点 embedding,存进特征库,线上把 GNN 退化成一次特征查表——最有效的降延迟手段,把 GNN 变成特征生成管线。图变化慢时定期刷新即可;代价是 embedding 有一定 staleness。
why_en: Precompute all node embeddings offline into a feature store and serve them as lookup features, turning the GNN into a feature-generation pipeline with periodic refresh.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  G["离线跑 GNN"] --> E["节点 embedding"]
  E --> F["特征库"]
  F --> S["线上查表打分"]
options: 每次请求实时跑完整多跳 GNN,保证 embedding 绝对最新
离线批量算好 embedding 存特征库,线上退化为查表,定期刷新;代价是有一定 staleness
把 GNN 层数加到 8 层以提高准确率,延迟以后再优化
只在客户端跑 GNN,服务器不参与
options_en: Run the full multi-hop GNN live per request to keep embeddings perfectly fresh.
Precompute embeddings offline into a feature store, degrade serving to a lookup, refresh periodically; the cost is some staleness.
Deepen the GNN to 8 layers for accuracy and optimize latency later.
Run the GNN only on the client, with the server not involved.
whenOtherWins: 当图变化极快(如实时欺诈图),预算好的 embedding 会过时,这时才需要实时推理(配合缓存热点邻域+限深 2 层)。
optionExplanations: 实时跑多跳 GNN 正是延迟瓶颈本身,严格预算下扛不住。
对;图变化慢时离线预算 embedding 把推理挪出实时路径,是最有效的降延迟手段。
加深层数会 over-smoothing 且更慢,和降延迟目标相悖。
端上跑多跳 GNN 受设备算力和本地图数据限制,不现实。
optionExplanations_en: Running the multi-hop GNN live is the latency bottleneck itself, untenable under a strict budget.
Correct — on a slow graph, precomputing embeddings moves inference off the hot path, the most effective latency fix.
Deepening layers causes over-smoothing and more latency, contradicting the goal.
Running a multi-hop GNN on the client is limited by device compute and local graph data — impractical.

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线把结果算好存起来,线上直接查,把重计算挪出实时路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precomputation computes results offline and stores them for online lookup, moving heavy work off the hot path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计算结果与当前真实状态之间的时间差,刷新周期越长越陈旧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staleness is the lag between precomputed results and current reality, worse with longer refresh intervals.

category: Graph Neural Networks In System Design

scenario: 实时欺诈检测,图变化极快(新账户/新交易秒级产生),离线预算好的 embedding 很快过时。
scenario_en: Real-time fraud detection on a fast-changing graph (new accounts/transactions every second), where precomputed embeddings go stale fast.
q: 这种必须实时的场景怎么控住延迟?
q_en: How do you control latency when real-time is unavoidable?
why: 缓存热点节点的邻域,并把深度严格限制在 2 层——两招都在砍每次实时推理要拉取和计算的邻居量,把多跳 fetch 压到能满足 <50ms。这是接受实时不可避免后的现实折中,而非首选。
why_en: Cache hot-node neighborhoods and strictly cap depth at 2 layers, both shrinking the neighbors fetched and computed per real-time inference.
options: 坚持离线预算 embedding,反正过时一点也能用
缓存热点节点邻域 + 严格限深 2 层,压住每次实时推理的拉取和计算量
把图存到更慢但更大的冷存储里,腾出内存给模型
取消延迟要求,让欺诈判定慢慢跑几秒也没关系
options_en: Stick with precomputed embeddings; a bit stale is still usable.
Cache hot-node neighborhoods and strictly cap depth at 2 layers, shrinking the fetch and compute per real-time inference.
Move the graph to slower, larger cold storage to free memory for the model.
Drop the latency requirement and let fraud decisions take a few seconds.
whenOtherWins: 当图变化慢、可容忍分钟级 staleness 时,离线预算 embedding 才是更省的默认解,不必实时。
optionExplanations: 欺诈图秒级变化,过时 embedding 会漏掉刚出现的欺诈模式,这里不能容忍 staleness。
对;缓存热邻域+限深把实时多跳砍到可控,是必须实时时压延迟的现实折中。
换冷存储只会让拉邻居更慢,与 <50ms 目标背道而驰。
欺诈判定必须实时拦截,几秒延迟意味着钱已经被转走,不能取消要求。
optionExplanations_en: A fraud graph changes by the second, so stale embeddings miss just-emerged patterns — staleness is intolerable here.
Correct — caching hot neighborhoods and capping depth shrinks real-time multi-hop to a controllable size, the realistic latency compromise.
Cold storage only makes neighbor fetches slower, working against the <50ms goal.
Fraud must be blocked in real time; a few seconds means the money is already gone, so you can't drop the requirement.

termDefinitions.term: hot-node neighborhood cache / 热点邻域缓存
termDefinitions.meaning: 把高频访问节点的邻居预先缓存,减少实时推理时的跨机拉取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot-node neighborhood cache pre-stores frequently accessed nodes' neighbors to cut cross-machine fetches at inference.

category: Graph Neural Networks In System Design

scenario: 面试里被问"要不要用 GNN",按一个可复用的 4 步框架回答最稳。
scenario_en: Asked 'should you use a GNN' in an interview, a reusable 4-step framework is the safest answer.
q: 把 GNN 决策的 4 步顺序排好:
q_en: Order the 4-step GNN decision sequence:
steps: 选并论证架构:GraphSAGE(inductive/可扩/常新节点) or GAT(邻居重要性差异大且延迟允许)
确认图信号超过表格基线,并举具体例子(二跳交易模式暴露 mule 账户)
标注缓解手段:采样 fan-out、限深 2 层、图分区、embedding 维度
显式说明 serving 模式:推荐/排序离线预算,只有快变图才实时
why: 先确认图信号值得(否则别上),再选并论证架构,接着定 serving 模式(离线预算 vs 实时),最后标注采样/限深/分区等缓解。按这个顺序答,把"是否用、用什么、怎么服务、怎么扛成本"一次讲透。
why_en: First confirm the graph signal beats tabular, then choose and justify the architecture, state the serving pattern, and finally annotate the mitigations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上如何提供 GNN 结果:离线预算 embedding 查表,还是实时多跳推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving pattern is how GNN results are delivered online: precomputed embedding lookup or real-time multi-hop inference.

category: Graph Neural Networks In System Design

scenario: LinkedIn 用 GraphSAGE,把 fan-out 调成 hop1 采 10 个、hop2 采 5 个邻居。
scenario_en: LinkedIn uses GraphSAGE with fan-out tuned to 10 neighbors at hop1 and 5 at hop2.
q: 这个 fan-out 配置在设计上起什么作用?
q_en: What does this fan-out configuration accomplish by design?
why: fan-out 直接决定计算图大小:10×5=50 个 hop2 邻居,加 10 个 hop1,单目标约几十个节点,把 serving 成本钉成有界常数、防邻域爆炸。近跳采多、远跳采少,因为近邻信息量更大、远邻边际收益递减。
why_en: Fan-out fixes the computation-graph size (10 then 5 gives tens of nodes per target), bounding serving cost and preventing neighborhood explosion.
options: 它决定模型有多少层,10 和 5 就是层数
它把每目标的计算图钉成有界大小(约几十节点),防邻域爆炸、锁定 serving 成本
它设定学习率,10 和 5 是两个阶段的 lr
它是准确率指标,越大代表模型越准
options_en: It sets how many layers the model has; 10 and 5 are the layer counts.
It fixes each target's computation graph to a bounded size (tens of nodes), preventing neighborhood explosion and locking serving cost.
It sets the learning rate; 10 and 5 are the two-stage LRs.
It's an accuracy metric where higher means a more accurate model.
optionExplanations: 层数是 hop 数(这里 2 层),fan-out 是每跳采几个邻居,两者不是一回事。
对;fan-out 把计算图大小固定,是让 serving 成本可预测、不爆炸的关键旋钮。
10/5 是采样邻居数不是学习率,和优化器超参无关。
fan-out 是成本/覆盖旋钮不是准确率,采太多反而更慢还可能引噪。
optionExplanations_en: Layers are hop count (2 here); fan-out is neighbors sampled per hop — different things.
Correct — fan-out fixes the computation-graph size, the key knob making serving cost predictable and non-exploding.
10/5 are sampled neighbor counts, not learning rates, unrelated to optimizer hyperparameters.
Fan-out is a cost/coverage knob, not accuracy; sampling too many is slower and can add noise.
category: Graph Neural Networks In System Design

scenario: 面试官评价:GNN 答案里有一句话往往是信号最高的。
scenario_en: The interviewer notes one sentence is usually the highest-signal line in a GNN answer.
q: GNN 答案里信号最高的一句通常是什么?
q_en: What's usually the highest-signal sentence in a GNN answer?
why: "我们离线预算节点 embedding,从特征库里以查表方式服务"——它一句话证明你懂 GNN 的真正瓶颈是实时多跳延迟,并给出把 GNN 变成特征生成管线的标准解法,直接体现工程成熟度。
why_en: 'We precompute node embeddings offline and serve them as lookups from a feature store' shows you grasp the real latency bottleneck and its standard fix.
options: "我们把层数堆到 10 层来捕捉更远的关系"
"我们离线预算节点 embedding,从特征库以查表方式服务"
"我们用了最新的 GNN 论文架构,准确率业界第一"
"我们每个请求都实时跑完整多跳推理保证最新"
options_en: 'We stack 10 layers to capture longer-range relations.'
'We precompute node embeddings offline and serve them as lookups from a feature store.'
'We used the newest GNN paper architecture, top-1 accuracy in the industry.'
'We run full multi-hop inference live per request to stay fresh.'
optionExplanations: 堆 10 层会 over-smoothing,暴露你不懂 GNN 的深度限制,是负信号。
对;这句点中 GNN 的服务瓶颈和标准解法,一句话显出工程成熟度。
只报论文名不谈工程约束,是知识展示不是设计能力。
实时全跑多跳正是延迟瓶颈本身,说明你没意识到 serving 成本。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking 10 layers over-smooths and reveals you miss the depth limit — a negative signal.
Correct — it nails the serving bottleneck and standard fix, showing engineering maturity in one line.
Naming a paper without engineering constraints is knowledge display, not design skill.
Running full multi-hop live is the latency bottleneck itself, showing unawareness of serving cost.
category: Graph Neural Networks In System Design

scenario: 题目要求同时优化 CTR、转化率和参与度"三个目标一起",单目标模型只对一个负责。
scenario_en: The prompt asks to optimize CTR, conversion, and engagement simultaneously, but a single-objective model serves only one.
q: 多目标要求下该用什么架构范式?
q_en: What architecture paradigm fits a multi-objective requirement?
why: 用多任务学习(MTL):一个共享表示骨干 + 多个任务专属 head,每个 head 预测一个目标。共享骨干摊薄算力、任务间互相正则提升数据效率;核心取舍是冲突目标会互相拖累(negative transfer)。
why_en: Use multi-task learning: a shared representation backbone plus per-task heads, which amortizes compute and shares signal, with the risk that conflicting objectives degrade each other.
diagram:
flowchart TD I["用户-物品输入"] --> T["共享骨干
shared representation"] T --> H1["head: P(click)"] T --> H2["head: P(conversion)"] T --> H3["head: watch time"]
options: 训三个完全独立的单目标模型,线上各跑一遍再人工拼分
多任务学习:共享表示骨干 + 多个任务专属 head,一次前向出多目标
只训 CTR 一个模型,转化和参与度靠事后规则硬凑
把三个目标简单相加成一个标签,训一个普通回归模型
options_en: Train three fully independent single-objective models, run each online, and combine scores by hand.
Multi-task learning: a shared representation backbone plus per-task heads, one forward pass for multiple objectives.
Train only a CTR model and patch conversion and engagement with post-hoc rules.
Sum the three objectives into one label and train an ordinary regression model.
whenOtherWins: 当各目标数据分布/特征差异极大、几乎无共享信号,且服务预算允许时,独立单目标模型反而避免了负迁移。
optionExplanations: 三个独立模型丢掉了任务间可共享的信号,还要跑三份前向,serving 成本高且样本效率差。
对;共享骨干+多 head 一次前向出多目标,既摊薄算力又让任务互相正则,是多目标标准范式。
只训 CTR 会漏掉转化/参与目标,事后规则硬凑无法端到端优化。
把异构目标相加会互相污染标签,单回归学不到各目标的独立信号。
optionExplanations_en: Three independent models drop shareable cross-task signal and run three forward passes, costly and sample-inefficient.
Correct — a shared backbone with multiple heads yields multiple objectives in one pass, amortizing compute and cross-regularizing tasks.
Training only CTR misses conversion/engagement, and post-hoc rules can't optimize end to end.
Summing heterogeneous objectives contaminates the label; single regression can't learn each objective's distinct signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个共享表示骨干带多个任务 head,同时学多个相关目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTL (Multi-Task Learning) uses a shared representation backbone with multiple task heads to learn several related objectives at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率,曝光中被点击的比例,是排序系统常见优化目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions that get clicked, a common ranking objective.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 面试官问最基础的 MTL 架构 shared-bottom 长什么样。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what the most basic MTL architecture, shared-bottom, looks like.
q: shared-bottom 架构的数据流是什么?
q_en: What is the data flow of a shared-bottom architecture?
why: 共享主干(深层 MLP 或 transformer 编码器)对每个物品跑一次,输出共享 embedding,再分叉进多个任务专属 tower head,各自预测一个目标(P(click)、P(conversion)、watch time)。主干一次前向、head 轻量,延迟随 head 增长而非整模型复制。
why_en: A shared trunk runs once per item to produce a shared embedding, which branches into task-specific tower heads that each predict one objective.
options: 每个任务各自一条完整独立网络,没有任何共享层
共享主干跑一次出共享 embedding,再分叉进多个任务专属 head 各预测一个目标
多个专家网络+每任务门控,门控加权组合专家输出
一个 head 输出所有目标的拼接向量,不分任务
options_en: Each task has its own complete independent network with no shared layers.
A shared trunk runs once to produce a shared embedding, branching into per-task heads that each predict one objective.
Multiple expert networks with per-task gating that weight-combines expert outputs.
One head outputs a concatenated vector of all objectives with no task split.
optionExplanations: 完全独立无共享层就不是 MTL,而是几个单独模型,丢了共享信号和一次前向的效率。
对;共享主干+分叉 head 正是 shared-bottom,主干一次前向,延迟随轻量 head 增长。
多专家+每任务门控是 MMoE,不是 shared-bottom,后者只有单一共享主干。
单 head 拼接所有目标无法给每个目标独立的 tower 建模,不是 shared-bottom 形态。
optionExplanations_en: Fully independent with no shared layers isn't MTL but separate models, losing shared signal and one-pass efficiency.
Correct — a shared trunk with branching heads is shared-bottom; the trunk runs once and latency grows with light heads.
Multiple experts with per-task gating is MMoE, not shared-bottom, which has a single shared trunk.
One concatenating head can't model each objective with its own tower — not the shared-bottom form.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最基础的 MTL 架构:单一共享主干 + 多个任务专属 head。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shared-bottom is the basic MTL architecture: a single shared trunk plus multiple task-specific heads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接在共享 embedding 上、专门预测某一个目标的轻量子网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A task head (tower) is a light sub-network on top of the shared embedding that predicts one specific objective.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 面试官让你说清 shared-bottom 相比训多个独立模型的好处。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks the benefits of shared-bottom over training separate models.
q: shared-bottom 带来哪些好处?(多选)
q_en: What benefits does shared-bottom bring? (multiple)
why: 三个好处:单次前向效率(主干每物品只跑一次,延迟随轻量 head 增长,不是复制整模型);跨任务正则(点击监督帮助正则化转化所需特征,稀疏标签样本效率更好);实现简单(加目标=加一个 head+loss 项,不动主干)。
why_en: Shared-bottom gives single-pass efficiency, cross-task regularization improving sample efficiency on sparse labels, and simple implementation.
options: 单次前向:主干每物品跑一次,延迟随轻量 head 增长而非复制整模型
跨任务正则:点击监督正则化转化所需特征,稀疏标签样本效率更好
实现简单:加目标=加一个 head+loss 项,不动主干
彻底消除冲突目标的负迁移,任务再冲突也不会互相拖累
options_en: Single forward pass: the trunk runs once per item, latency grows with light heads not full replicas.
Cross-task regularization: click supervision regularizes features conversion needs, better sample efficiency on sparse labels.
Implementation simplicity: adding an objective means adding a head plus a loss term, no trunk change.
Fully eliminates negative transfer, so conflicting tasks never drag each other down.
optionExplanations: 对;主干共享让一次前向服务多目标,延迟只随轻量 head 增加,serving 成本低。
对;一个任务的监督信号能正则化另一个任务的特征,尤其对购买这种稀疏标签更省样本。
对;新目标只需 append 一个 head 和 loss 项,工程改动最小。
错;shared-bottom 恰恰在冲突任务上会被迫折中产生负迁移,这是它的核心局限。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a shared trunk serves multiple objectives in one pass, with latency rising only with light heads, keeping serving cheap.
Correct — one task's supervision regularizes another's features, saving samples especially for sparse labels like purchases.
Correct — a new objective just appends a head and loss term, minimal engineering change.
Wrong — shared-bottom specifically suffers negative transfer on conflicting tasks, its core limitation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个任务的监督约束共享特征,间接帮助另一个任务泛化,提升样本效率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-task regularization is when one task's supervision constrains shared features, helping another task generalize and improving sample efficiency.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: shared-bottom 同时学 CTR 和参与度,结果为拉高点击学出了标题党特征,反而伤害了参与度。
scenario_en: A shared-bottom model learns CTR and engagement together but develops clickbait features that boost clicks while hurting engagement.
q: shared-bottom 在异构/冲突任务上的核心失败模式叫什么,机制是什么?
q_en: What's shared-bottom's core failure on heterogeneous/conflicting tasks, and the mechanism?
why: 叫 negative transfer(负迁移):CTR 想要"标题党"式抓眼球特征,参与度想要真实价值特征,两者在同一共享主干的权重上互相拉扯,主干被迫折中,结果哪个任务都学不好。这正是要上 MMoE 的信号。
why_en: It's negative transfer: conflicting objectives pull the same shared trunk weights in opposite directions, forcing a compromise that hurts both.
options: 过拟合:主干记住训练集,加正则即可解决,与任务冲突无关
负迁移:冲突目标在共享主干权重上互相拉扯,主干被迫折中,两个任务都学不好
梯度爆炸:学习率太高,调小 lr 就能消除
数据泄漏:测试集混进训练,和架构无关
options_en: Overfitting: the trunk memorizes the training set; add regularization, unrelated to task conflict.
Negative transfer: conflicting objectives pull the shared trunk's weights against each other, forcing a compromise that hurts both.
Gradient explosion: learning rate too high; lowering LR removes it.
Data leakage: the test set bleeds into training, unrelated to architecture.
optionExplanations: 过拟合是记训练集,和"两个目标互相拖累"是不同问题,正则化治不了任务冲突。
对;负迁移的机制是共享权重被冲突梯度拉扯折中,是 shared-bottom 面对异构任务的核心局限。
梯度爆炸是数值不稳定,和目标冲突无关,调 lr 不解决负迁移。
数据泄漏是评测问题,与共享主干上的任务冲突机制无关。
optionExplanations_en: Overfitting is memorizing the training set, a different problem from two objectives dragging each other; regularization won't fix task conflict.
Correct — negative transfer's mechanism is conflicting gradients forcing a compromise on shared weights, shared-bottom's core limitation on heterogeneous tasks.
Gradient explosion is numerical instability unrelated to objective conflict; tuning LR doesn't fix negative transfer.
Data leakage is an evaluation problem, unrelated to the task-conflict mechanism on the shared trunk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 冲突任务在共享参数上互相拉扯,使主干折中、每个任务都变差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Negative transfer is when conflicting tasks pull shared parameters against each other, forcing a compromise that worsens every task.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 要联合预测的几个目标高度相关(如 P(click) 和 P(like)),数据分布和特征需求接近。
scenario_en: The objectives to predict jointly are closely related (like P(click) and P(like)) with similar feature needs.
q: 紧密相关的任务用 shared-bottom 还是 MMoE?
q_en: For closely related tasks, shared-bottom or MMoE?
why: 选 shared-bottom:任务紧密相关时共享表示是净收益(强跨任务正则),负迁移风险低,而且它 serving 更便宜、实现更简单。MMoE 的门控和专家平衡是为异构冲突任务准备的,这里用它只是徒增复杂度和超参。
why_en: Pick shared-bottom for closely related tasks: shared representation is a net gain with low conflict, and it's cheaper and simpler than MMoE.
options: MMoE,任何多任务都该上门控,越复杂越好
shared-bottom,任务紧密相关时共享表示净收益、负迁移低、更省更简单
训 N 个独立模型,彻底避免任何共享
shared-bottom 但去掉共享主干,只留 head
options_en: MMoE — any multi-task setup should use gating, more complex is better.
Shared-bottom — with closely related tasks the shared representation is a net gain, low conflict, cheaper and simpler.
Train N independent models to avoid any sharing at all.
Shared-bottom but drop the shared trunk, keeping only the heads.
whenOtherWins: 当任务异构/弱相关甚至冲突(如 YouTube 观看时长 vs 满意度调查)时,才需要 MMoE 的每任务门控来缓解负迁移。
optionExplanations: MMoE 复杂度和超参更高,相关任务上用它是过度设计,收益换不回复杂度。
对;相关任务共享有益、冲突小,shared-bottom 更省更简单是正解。
独立模型丢了相关任务本可共享的正则信号,样本效率和成本都更差。
去掉共享主干就没有共享表示了,失去了 MTL 的意义。
optionExplanations_en: MMoE's higher complexity and hyperparameters make it over-engineering on related tasks, not worth the cost.
Correct — for related tasks sharing helps with little conflict, so cheaper, simpler shared-bottom is right.
Independent models drop the shareable regularization signal of related tasks, worsening sample efficiency and cost.
Dropping the shared trunk removes the shared representation, defeating the point of MTL.
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: YouTube 要同时优化参与度(观看时长)和满意度(问卷质量分),两者只弱相关,shared-bottom 会互相拖累。
scenario_en: YouTube optimizes engagement (watch time) and satisfaction (survey quality), only weakly correlated, so shared-bottom drags them down.
q: 异构弱相关任务该换哪种架构?
q_en: For heterogeneous weakly correlated tasks, which architecture?
why: 选 MMoE:多个专家子网络各自处理输入,每个任务有自己的门控网络(对专家做 softmax 加权),让不同目标各自倚重合适的专家,不强迫共享同一表示,从而缓解负迁移。代价是更复杂、超参更多、要防专家负载不均。
why_en: Pick MMoE: per-task gating over shared experts lets each objective lean on its own experts instead of forcing one representation, mitigating negative transfer.
options: 继续 shared-bottom,再加大主干容量硬扛冲突
MMoE:多专家+每任务门控,各目标倚重合适专家,不强迫共享表示,缓解负迁移
把两个目标合并成一个加权标签,退回单任务
只保留观看时长一个目标,放弃满意度
options_en: Stay shared-bottom and just enlarge the trunk to brute-force the conflict.
MMoE: multiple experts plus per-task gating, each objective leans on suitable experts without a forced shared representation, mitigating negative transfer.
Merge the two objectives into one weighted label, back to single-task.
Keep only watch time and drop satisfaction.
whenOtherWins: 若任务其实紧密相关、共享有益,shared-bottom 更省更简单,不必上 MMoE 的门控复杂度。
optionExplanations: 加大主干不改变"被迫共享一个表示"的根因,冲突任务照样互相拖累。
对;每任务门控让各目标选自己的专家组合,绕开强制共享,正是异构任务的解法。
合并标签把冲突信号糊在一起,退回单任务丢失多目标能力。
放弃满意度等于不满足多目标要求,是回避问题不是解决。
optionExplanations_en: Enlarging the trunk doesn't change the forced-shared-representation root cause; conflicting tasks still drag each other.
Correct — per-task gating lets each objective pick its own expert mix, bypassing forced sharing, the fix for heterogeneous tasks.
Merging labels blends conflicting signal and reverts to single-task, losing multi-objective capability.
Dropping satisfaction fails the multi-objective requirement, dodging rather than solving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个专家子网络+每任务一个门控,门控 softmax 加权组合专家输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MMoE (Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts) has multiple expert sub-networks and a per-task gate that softmax-weights their outputs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为某个任务学习各专家权重的小网络,输出 softmax 权重组合专家。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gating network learns per-expert weights for a task, outputting a softmax combination over experts.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 面试官要你用一张对比说清 shared-bottom 和 MMoE 的取舍。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to contrast shared-bottom and MMoE in one comparison.
q: shared-bottom 与 MMoE 的核心区别在哪几维?
q_en: On what dimensions do shared-bottom and MMoE differ?
why: shared-bottom 单主干+任务头、serving 便宜、实现简单,但冲突任务负迁移高;MMoE 多专家+每任务门控、负迁移被门控缓解、适合异构任务,代价是更复杂(门控调参、专家负载均衡)、serving 更贵(稀疏激活缓解)。取舍轴=任务相关度 vs 复杂度/成本。
why_en: Shared-bottom is cheap and simple but conflict-prone; MMoE adds per-task gating to handle heterogeneity at higher complexity and cost.
options: shared-bottom 多专家+门控,MMoE 单主干,和实际相反
架构(单主干 vs 多专家门控)、适合任务(相关 vs 异构)、负迁移、复杂度/成本
两者唯一区别是参数量,其他完全一样
MMoE 更简单更便宜,shared-bottom 更复杂,应优先 MMoE
options_en: Shared-bottom is multi-expert with gating and MMoE is single-trunk — reversed from reality.
Architecture (single trunk vs multi-expert gating), best-fit tasks (related vs heterogeneous), negative transfer, complexity/cost.
The only difference is parameter count; everything else is identical.
MMoE is simpler and cheaper and shared-bottom more complex, so prefer MMoE.
optionExplanations: 架构说反了:单主干是 shared-bottom,多专家门控才是 MMoE。
对;这四维正好覆盖架构、适用、负迁移、成本,是选型该比较的轴。
两者在架构范式、适用任务、负迁移处理上本质不同,不止参数量。
恰恰相反:MMoE 更复杂更贵,shared-bottom 才简单便宜。
optionExplanations_en: Architecture is reversed: single-trunk is shared-bottom, multi-expert gating is MMoE.
Correct — these four dimensions cover architecture, fit, negative transfer, and cost, the selection axes.
They differ fundamentally in paradigm, fit, and conflict handling, not just parameter count.
The opposite: MMoE is more complex and costly; shared-bottom is the simple, cheap one.
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: MMoE 专家数变多,担心参数量上去后 serving 算力扛不住。
scenario_en: As MMoE's expert count grows, you worry serving compute can't handle the extra parameters.
q: MMoE 靠什么控住算力,又要防什么退化?
q_en: How does MMoE keep compute in check, and what degeneration must it prevent?
why: 靠稀疏激活:每个输入只点亮一部分专家(门控权重集中在少数专家上),所以参数量虽大、实际算力可控。要防 expert collapse——门控退化成只用极少数专家,其余长期闲置、白占参数还削弱专业分工。
why_en: Sparse activation fires only a subset of experts per input so compute stays manageable, but gating must avoid expert collapse where only a few experts are ever used.
options: 靠给每个输入激活全部专家来保证准确率,不需要防任何退化
靠稀疏激活(每输入只点亮部分专家)控算力;要防 expert collapse(门控只用极少数专家)
靠把专家数减到 1 来省算力,本质退回 shared-bottom
靠冻结门控不训练来省算力,专家随机分配即可
options_en: Activate all experts per input to guarantee accuracy, needing no degeneration prevention.
Sparse activation (only a subset of experts fire per input) keeps compute in check; must prevent expert collapse (gating using only a few experts).
Cut experts to 1 to save compute, essentially reverting to shared-bottom.
Freeze gating without training to save compute, assigning experts at random.
optionExplanations: 全激活所有专家等于放弃稀疏性,算力随专家数线性上涨,与控成本背道而驰。
对;稀疏激活让大参数量下算力可控,而 expert collapse 会让门控只依赖少数专家、削弱分工。
减到 1 个专家就失去了 MMoE 的专业分工能力,不是控算力的正解。
冻结随机门控无法学到任务该用哪些专家,专业分工失效。
optionExplanations_en: Activating all experts drops sparsity, so compute scales linearly with expert count, against the cost goal.
Correct — sparse activation keeps compute manageable at large param counts, while expert collapse makes gating rely on only a few experts, hurting specialization.
Cutting to one expert loses MMoE's specialization, not a way to control compute.
Frozen random gating can't learn which experts a task needs, so specialization fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个输入只激活一部分专家,使大参数量的模型实际算力可控。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sparse activation fires only a subset of experts per input, keeping compute manageable despite a large parameter count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 门控退化成只用极少数专家,其余长期不被激活、丧失分工。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expert collapse is when gating degenerates to using only a few experts, leaving the rest idle and losing specialization.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 训练时观察到:提升 CTR 的每一步都在稳定地把转化率往下带。
scenario_en: During training, every step that improves CTR steadily drags conversion down.
q: 这种"一个任务变好另一个变差"在梯度层面是什么机制?
q_en: At the gradient level, what mechanism makes one task improve while another worsens?
why: task interference(任务干扰):反向传播时两个任务在共享权重上产生方向相反的梯度,优化器把它们平均,结果在冲突方向上震荡或收敛到次优折中。例如广告里 CTR 要抓眼球视觉特征,转化要价格敏感/品牌偏好信号,压在同一权重矩阵上。
why_en: Task interference: two tasks produce opposing gradients on shared weights, and the optimizer averages them into oscillation or a suboptimal compromise.
options: 是随机噪声,多训几轮自然消失,与梯度方向无关
两任务在共享权重上产生方向相反的梯度,优化器平均→震荡/次优折中
是学习率过低导致收敛慢,调大 lr 即可
是 batch 太小的采样偏差,加大 batch 就好
options_en: It's random noise that fades with more epochs, unrelated to gradient direction.
Two tasks produce opposing gradients on shared weights, and the optimizer averages them into oscillation or a suboptimal compromise.
It's slow convergence from too-low learning rate; raise LR to fix.
It's sampling bias from a small batch; enlarge the batch to fix.
optionExplanations: 这不是随机噪声,而是稳定的反向拉扯,多训只会持续折中不会消失。
对;冲突梯度在共享权重上相消/平均,是负迁移在梯度层面的具体机制。
lr 高低改变的是步长,改变不了两任务梯度方向相反这个根因。
batch 大小影响方差,消不掉方向性冲突的系统性干扰。
optionExplanations_en: It's not random noise but a steady opposing pull; more training keeps compromising, not fading.
Correct — conflicting gradients canceling/averaging on shared weights is negative transfer's mechanism at the gradient level.
LR changes step size, not the root cause of two tasks' opposing gradient directions.
Batch size affects variance, not the systematic directional interference.

termDefinitions.term: task interference / conflicting gradients / 任务干扰
termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务在共享权重上产生反向梯度,优化器平均后震荡或次优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task interference is when tasks produce opposing gradients on shared weights, which the optimizer averages into oscillation or suboptimality.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 想监控多任务训练中任务之间是合作还是冲突。
scenario_en: You want to monitor whether tasks cooperate or conflict during multi-task training.
q: 用什么指标判断任务梯度是否冲突?
q_en: What metric tells you whether task gradients conflict?
why: 监控任务梯度之间的余弦相似度:负余弦=两个梯度方向相反(冲突),正余弦=方向一致(合作)。它给出一个可观测的信号,提示何时该上 PCGrad/GradNorm 这类缓解手段。
why_en: Track the cosine similarity between task gradients: negative means conflicting, positive means cooperating.
options: 看两任务的 loss 绝对值大小,谁大谁就在冲突
看任务梯度的余弦相似度:负=冲突、正=合作
看参数总数,参数越多越冲突
看训练时长,训得越久冲突越少
options_en: Compare the two tasks' absolute loss values; whichever is larger is conflicting.
Look at the cosine similarity between task gradients: negative means conflict, positive means cooperation.
Look at total parameter count; more params means more conflict.
Look at training time; longer training means less conflict.
optionExplanations: loss 绝对值受量纲和难度影响,大小不代表方向冲突,判断不了干扰。
对;梯度余弦的符号直接反映方向是否相反,是判断任务冲突的标准信号。
参数量与梯度方向是否冲突无关,不是冲突指标。
训练时长不衡量方向冲突,冲突可以贯穿整个训练。
optionExplanations_en: Absolute loss depends on scale and difficulty; its magnitude doesn't indicate directional conflict.
Correct — the sign of gradient cosine directly reflects opposing directions, the standard conflict signal.
Parameter count is unrelated to whether gradients conflict, not a conflict metric.
Training time doesn't measure directional conflict, which can persist throughout training.

termDefinitions.term: gradient cosine similarity / 梯度余弦相似度
termDefinitions.meaning: 两个任务梯度向量夹角的余弦,负值表示方向相反即冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gradient cosine similarity is the cosine of the angle between two task gradient vectors; negative means opposing, i.e. conflict.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 面试官问 GradNorm 和 PCGrad 分别从哪个角度缓解任务干扰。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how GradNorm and PCGrad each mitigate task interference.
q: GradNorm 和 PCGrad 的缓解思路差在哪?
q_en: How do GradNorm and PCGrad differ in mitigation approach?
why: GradNorm 调"幅度":按各任务训练速度动态重加权 loss,别让训练快的任务主导梯度。PCGrad 调"方向":把一个梯度里与另一个梯度冲突的分量投影掉,保留不冲突的部分。一个平衡量级,一个消解方向冲突。
why_en: GradNorm rebalances magnitude by reweighting task losses by training rate, while PCGrad fixes direction by projecting away the conflicting gradient component.

rows: 按训练速度重加权 loss

options: 两者都调学习率,只是名字不同
GradNorm 按训练速度重加权 loss(调幅度);PCGrad 投影掉冲突梯度分量(调方向)
GradNorm 调方向、PCGrad 调幅度,和实际相反
两者都是把冲突任务直接删掉一个
options_en: Both tune the learning rate, just different names.
GradNorm reweights losses by training rate (magnitude); PCGrad projects away the conflicting gradient component (direction).
GradNorm fixes direction and PCGrad fixes magnitude — reversed from reality.
Both simply delete one of the conflicting tasks.
optionExplanations: 两者都不是调 lr:GradNorm 重加权 loss,PCGrad 改梯度方向,机制不同。
对;一个平衡各任务梯度量级、一个消解方向冲突,分工清楚。
角色说反了:GradNorm 管幅度、PCGrad 管方向。
两者都保留所有任务,不是删任务,而是调梯度让它们共存。
optionExplanations_en: Neither tunes LR: GradNorm reweights losses and PCGrad alters gradient direction, different mechanisms.
Correct — one balances gradient magnitudes across tasks, the other resolves directional conflict, a clean split.
Roles reversed: GradNorm handles magnitude and PCGrad handles direction.
Both keep all tasks, not delete one; they adjust gradients so tasks coexist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个任务的训练速度动态重加权其 loss,防快任务主导梯度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GradNorm dynamically reweights each task's loss by its training rate so a fast task doesn't dominate the gradient.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个任务梯度里与另一个冲突的分量投影掉,保留非冲突信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PCGrad (Projecting Conflicting Gradients) projects away the component of one task's gradient that conflicts with another, keeping the non-conflicting signal.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 面试时间有限,任务间有轻微干扰,想给一个既显成熟又不用推导复杂算法的缓解方案。
scenario_en: Limited interview time, mild task interference, and you want a mitigation that shows maturity without deriving a complex algorithm.
q: 面试里主动提哪种缓解最稳妥?
q_en: Which mitigation is safest to propose in an interview?
why: 先提手动 loss 加权:L = w1·L_CTR + w2·L_conv + w3·L_engage,权重按业务优先级经验调。它简单、可解释、上手快;主动点名任务干扰再提出哪怕是手动加权,就已显出成熟度,不必现场推导 PCGrad。
why_en: Propose manual loss weighting first: a weighted sum of task losses tuned by business priority, simple and interpretable enough to show maturity without deriving PCGrad.
options: 现场从头推导 PCGrad 的投影公式,证明数学功底
先提手动 loss 加权(按业务优先级调权重),简单可解释,配合点名任务干扰
说任务干扰无解,只能删掉冲突任务
把所有任务权重都设成相等且永不调整,最公平
options_en: Derive PCGrad's projection formula from scratch on the spot to prove math skill.
Propose manual loss weighting first (weights tuned by business priority), simple and interpretable, alongside naming task interference.
Say task interference is unsolvable and you must delete the conflicting task.
Set all task weights equal and never adjust them, which is fairest.
whenOtherWins: 当手动加权调不动、干扰严重且需自动平衡时,才升级到 GradNorm(平衡量级)或 PCGrad(消方向冲突)。
optionExplanations: 现场推导 PCGrad 既费时又非重点,面试要的是判断力不是背公式。
对;主动点名干扰+提出手动加权就已显成熟,简单可解释、落地快,是稳妥答法。
干扰有多种缓解手段,说无解暴露知识盲区。
等权且不调忽略了业务优先级差异,冲突时反而放大问题。
optionExplanations_en: Deriving PCGrad on the spot is time-consuming and beside the point; the interview wants judgment, not formula recall.
Correct — naming interference and proposing manual weighting already shows maturity, simple, interpretable, and quick to ship.
Interference has several mitigations; calling it unsolvable reveals a knowledge gap.
Equal, never-adjusted weights ignore differing business priorities and amplify the problem under conflict.

termDefinitions.term: manual loss weighting / 手动损失加权
termDefinitions.meaning: 把各任务 loss 按固定权重相加,权重依业务优先级经验设定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Manual loss weighting sums task losses with fixed weights set empirically by business priority.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 回忆手动多任务 loss 的组合形式。
scenario_en: Recall the form of a manual multi-task loss.
q: 补全手动多任务损失加权公式:
q_en: Fill in the manual multi-task loss-weighting formula:
text: L = {{w₁}}·L_CTR + {{w₂}}·L_conv + {{w₃}}·L_engage,权重按{{业务优先级}}经验调。
text_en: L = {{w₁}}·L_CTR + {{w₂}}·L_conv + {{w₃}}·L_engage, with weights tuned by {{business priority}}.
why: 总损失是各任务损失的加权和,权重编码了业务对每个目标的相对重视度。它简单直接,是缓解任务干扰的最朴素手段;权重通常靠线上实验而非纯离线指标定。
why_en: Total loss is a weighted sum of task losses, with weights encoding each objective's business priority.
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: Meta feed 排序从共享用户-物品表示里联合预测多个行为概率。
scenario_en: Meta feed ranking jointly predicts multiple behavior probabilities from a shared user-item representation.
q: Meta feed 的多任务排序里,为什么要单独预测并惩罚 P(hide)?
q_en: In Meta feed's multi-task ranking, why predict and penalize P(hide)?
why: 它联合预测 P(click)/P(like)/P(comment)/P(share)/P(hide)/观看时长,最终分是这些的加权组合。单列 P(hide) 并在打分时对它加负权,能主动压低会引起负体验(用户隐藏)的内容,而不是只追点击。
why_en: Meta jointly predicts P(click)/P(like)/.../P(hide) and combines them, penalizing P(hide) to suppress content that causes negative experiences rather than only chasing clicks.
options: P(hide) 是唯一目标,其他行为都不重要
把 P(hide) 加负权,能主动压低引起负体验的内容,而非只追点击
P(hide) 只是日志字段,不参与打分
预测 P(hide) 是为了提高点击,和负体验无关
options_en: P(hide) is the only objective; other behaviors don't matter.
Weighting P(hide) negatively actively suppresses content causing negative experiences, not just chasing clicks.
P(hide) is just a log field, not used in scoring.
Predicting P(hide) is to raise clicks, unrelated to negative experience.
optionExplanations: P(hide) 是众多目标之一,不是唯一,点赞/评论/分享也都参与组合。
对;负权 P(hide) 让排序主动规避用户反感内容,是多目标平衡体验的关键。
P(hide) 明确进入加权组合分,不是纯日志字段。
预测 P(hide) 正是为了降负体验,方向说反了。
optionExplanations_en: P(hide) is one of many objectives, not the only one; likes/comments/shares also contribute.
Correct — a negative weight on P(hide) makes ranking actively avoid disliked content, key to balancing experience across objectives.
P(hide) explicitly enters the weighted combination score, not a mere log field.
Predicting P(hide) is exactly to reduce negative experience — the direction is reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户隐藏/不想看该内容的概率,负体验信号,打分时给负权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P(hide) is the probability a user hides the content, a negative-experience signal given negative weight in scoring.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 多头 MTL 把 P(click)、P(conversion)、watch time 组合成一个排序分,要定各头的组合权重(scalarization)。
scenario_en: A multi-head MTL combines P(click), P(conversion), watch time into one ranking score, needing scalarization weights.
q: scalarization 的组合权重该怎么定?
q_en: How should you tune the scalarization weights?
why: 靠线上 A/B 实验调,而不是离线指标:权重的微小改变会移动 UX 与营收的平衡,离线指标预测不了这种线上权衡。scalarization 本质是产品/政策决策,得在真实流量上看它对整体体验和收入的影响。
why_en: Tune scalarization weights via online A/B tests, not offline metrics, because small weight shifts move the UX-revenue balance that offline metrics can't capture.
options: 只用离线 AUC 调权重,离线最优就直接上线
靠线上 A/B 实验调,因为权重微调会移动 UX 与营收平衡,离线指标预测不了
权重设成相等且固定,永远不调
让模型自己端到端学权重,不需要任何人工或实验
options_en: Tune weights by offline AUC only and ship whatever is offline-optimal.
Tune via online A/B tests, because small weight shifts move the UX-revenue balance that offline metrics can't predict.
Set weights equal and fixed, never adjusting.
Let the model learn the weights end to end with no human or experiment.
whenOtherWins: 在早期离线迭代、还没上线流量时,离线指标可用于粗筛权重范围,但最终权重仍要线上 A/B 定。
optionExplanations: 离线 AUC 抓不住 UX 与营收的真实权衡,离线最优上线常常掉整体收益。
对;scalarization 是产品/政策决策,权重的商业影响只有线上 A/B 才看得准。
等权固定忽略各目标的商业价值差异,也无法随业务变化调整。
端到端学不出"营收 vs 体验"这种业务价值权衡,那是产品决策不是纯优化。
optionExplanations_en: Offline AUC misses the real UX-revenue trade-off, so offline-optimal often loses overall value in production.
Correct — scalarization is a product/policy decision whose business impact only online A/B measures accurately.
Equal fixed weights ignore differing business value and can't adapt as the business changes.
End-to-end learning can't derive the revenue-vs-experience trade-off, which is a product decision, not pure optimization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个目标的预测按权重合成一个可排序的单一分数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scalarization combines multiple objective predictions by weights into a single rankable score.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 团队在纠结把 MTL 系统设计精力主要投在哪一步。
scenario_en: The team debates where to invest most of the MTL system-design effort.
q: 多目标排序里最有影响力的设计决策是哪一步?
q_en: What is the most impactful design decision in multi-objective ranking?
why: 把各头输出组合成单一排序分的 scalarization 是最有影响力的决策:它直接决定 UX 与营收的平衡,权重微调就能改变用户体验和收入,所以要靠线上 A/B 谨慎调而非拍脑袋。
why_en: Scalarization — combining head outputs into one ranking score — is the most impactful decision because it directly sets the UX-revenue balance.
options: 选 optimizer(Adam vs SGD)是最关键决策
scalarization(把各头组合成单一排序分)最有影响力,直接决定 UX 与营收平衡
共享主干用几层是最关键决策
batch size 的选择是最有影响力的决策
options_en: Choosing the optimizer (Adam vs SGD) is the key decision.
Scalarization (combining heads into one ranking score) is most impactful, directly setting the UX-revenue balance.
How many layers the shared trunk has is the key decision.
Batch size choice is the most impactful decision.
optionExplanations: optimizer 是训练细节,影响收敛不影响"最终怎么排序"这个业务杠杆。
对;scalarization 直接决定线上排序结果和商业权衡,是影响面最大的决策。
主干层数是模型容量细节,不如组合权重直接左右业务结果。
batch size 影响训练稳定性,不是决定 UX/营收平衡的杠杆。
optionExplanations_en: The optimizer is a training detail affecting convergence, not the business lever of final ranking.
Correct — scalarization directly determines online ranking and the business trade-off, the highest-impact decision.
Trunk depth is a capacity detail, less directly steering business outcomes than the combination weights.
Batch size affects training stability, not the UX/revenue balance lever.
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: MTL 里不同 head 任务性质不同:有的是二分类,有的要输出有序列表,有的下游依赖预测概率的准度。
scenario_en: Different MTL heads differ: some are binary classification, some output ordered lists, some feed downstream that relies on probability accuracy.
q: 各 head 的 loss 该怎么按任务性质选?
q_en: How should you pick each head's loss by task nature?
why: 分类 head 用交叉熵;要产出有序列表的用排序损失(如 pairwise/listwise);当下游依赖预测概率的绝对准度(如竞价 bid=P(click)×value)时要做校准。loss 要匹配每个 head 的目标性质,不是全用一种。
why_en: Use cross-entropy for classification heads, ranking losses for ordered lists, and calibration when downstream relies on predicted probabilities.
options: 所有 head 一律用 MSE,统一最省事
分类用交叉熵、有序列表用排序损失、下游依赖概率时做校准,按任务性质选
所有 head 一律用排序损失,反正都是排序系统
loss 随便选,反正共享主干才决定效果
options_en: Use MSE for all heads, uniform and simplest.
Cross-entropy for classification, ranking loss for ordered lists, calibration when downstream relies on probabilities — by task nature.
Use ranking loss for all heads since it's all a ranking system.
Pick any loss; only the shared trunk decides quality.
whenOtherWins: 若某个 head 的下游只需相对排序、不需概率绝对值,就用排序损失而非追求校准,省掉校准环节。
optionExplanations: MSE 对分类和排序都不合适,概率预测和有序度都会变差。
对;loss 匹配任务性质——分类交叉熵、列表排序损失、依赖概率就校准,才各得其所。
分类和概率校准任务用排序损失会丢掉概率语义,不是全场景通用。
loss 直接决定每个 head 学到什么,不是无关紧要的细节。
optionExplanations_en: MSE suits neither classification nor ranking, degrading both probability prediction and ordering.
Correct — matching loss to task nature (cross-entropy, ranking, calibration) serves each head properly.
Ranking loss on classification/calibration heads loses probability semantics; it isn't universal.
The loss directly determines what each head learns; it's not an irrelevant detail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让预测概率与真实频率一致(说 0.3 就真有约 30% 发生),下游竞价/阈值依赖它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration makes predicted probabilities match real frequencies (0.3 means about 30% happen), relied on by downstream bidding/thresholds.

category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 从零设计一个多目标排序的 MTL 系统,要有条理地走一遍关键决策。
scenario_en: Designing a multi-objective ranking MTL system from scratch, walk the key decisions in order.
q: 把 MTL 设计流程排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the MTL design flow correctly:
steps: 监控梯度余弦相似度,发现任务干扰
按任务相关度选架构:相关用 shared-bottom,异构用 MMoE
上缓解手段:GradNorm/PCGrad 或手动 loss 加权
用线上 A/B 调 scalarization 权重组合最终排序分
why: 先按任务相关度选架构,再监控梯度余弦发现干扰,接着上缓解(手动加权/GradNorm/PCGrad),最后用线上 A/B 调 scalarization 定最终排序分。顺序保证"先定结构、再诊断、再治疗、最后定业务权衡"。
why_en: Choose architecture by task relatedness, monitor gradient cosine for interference, apply mitigation, then A/B-tune scalarization for the final score.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["选架构"] --> B["监控梯度余弦"]
  B --> C["上缓解手段"]
  C --> D["A/B 调 scalarization"]
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: YouTube 的参与度(观看时长)和满意度(问卷质量分)只弱相关。
scenario_en: YouTube's engagement (watch time) and satisfaction (survey quality) are only weakly correlated.
q: 为什么弱相关的目标让 YouTube 从 shared-bottom 转向 MMoE?
q_en: Why do weakly correlated objectives push YouTube from shared-bottom to MMoE?
why: 两个目标只弱相关,shared-bottom 强迫它们共享同一表示,会互相拖累(负迁移),不足以兼顾。MMoE 的每任务门控让参与度和满意度各自倚重不同专家家族,专业分工避免了被迫折中。
why_en: Weakly correlated objectives make a forced shared representation drag them down, so MMoE's per-task gating lets each lean on its own experts.
options: 因为 MMoE 参数更少所以更快,与相关性无关
两目标弱相关,shared-bottom 强迫共享表示会互相拖累;MMoE 门控让各自倚重不同专家
因为观看时长和满意度其实完全相同,合并即可
因为 shared-bottom 不支持两个 head,MMoE 才支持
options_en: Because MMoE has fewer params and is faster, unrelated to correlation.
The two are weakly correlated, so shared-bottom's forced shared representation drags them down; MMoE's gating lets each lean on different experts.
Because watch time and satisfaction are actually identical, so just merge them.
Because shared-bottom can't support two heads and only MMoE can.
optionExplanations: MMoE 参数通常更多不是更少,转向它的理由是异构性不是参数量。
对;弱相关=共享表示净收益低、冲突高,每任务门控的专业分工正好对症。
两目标弱相关不是相同,合并会丢掉满意度这个独立信号。
shared-bottom 完全支持多 head,转向 MMoE 是为处理异构,不是能力限制。
optionExplanations_en: MMoE usually has more params, not fewer; the reason to switch is heterogeneity, not param count.
Correct — weak correlation means low sharing benefit and high conflict, and per-task gating's specialization is the fix.
Weakly correlated isn't identical; merging drops satisfaction as an independent signal.
Shared-bottom fully supports multiple heads; switching to MMoE handles heterogeneity, not a capability limit.
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 面试小测:训练中提升 CTR 一致地拉低了转化率,问根因。
scenario_en: Quiz: during training, improving CTR consistently degrades conversion; what's the root cause?
q: 这个现象的根因是什么?
q_en: What is the root cause of this phenomenon?
why: 根因是共享参数上的冲突梯度(负迁移):CTR 和转化在同一共享权重上要的特征方向相反,优化器一平均就把转化往下带。识别它才能对症上 PCGrad/门控/手动加权。
why_en: The cause is conflicting gradients on shared parameters (negative transfer): CTR and conversion demand opposite feature directions on shared weights.
options: 转化率数据太少,加数据即可,与共享参数无关
共享参数上的冲突梯度(负迁移):CTR 与转化要的特征方向相反,优化器平均拖低转化
学习率设置错误,与任务冲突无关
模型容量不够,加大主干就消除
options_en: Too little conversion data; add data, unrelated to shared parameters.
Conflicting gradients on shared parameters (negative transfer): CTR and conversion demand opposite feature directions, the optimizer's average drags conversion down.
Wrong learning rate, unrelated to task conflict.
Insufficient model capacity; enlarging the trunk removes it.
optionExplanations: 加数据缓解不了方向性冲突,负迁移是梯度方向相反造成的,不是数据量。
对;这正是负迁移/冲突梯度的定义,识别它才能选对缓解手段。
lr 改步长不改方向冲突,治不了两任务梯度相反。
加容量不改变共享权重上的方向冲突,负迁移照旧。
optionExplanations_en: More data can't relieve directional conflict; negative transfer comes from opposing gradient directions, not data volume.
Correct — this is the definition of negative transfer/conflicting gradients, and identifying it guides the mitigation.
LR changes step size, not directional conflict, so it won't fix opposing task gradients.
Adding capacity doesn't change the directional conflict on shared weights; negative transfer persists.
category: Multi Task And Multi Objective Learning

scenario: 一个 CTR 模型离线 AUC 很高,但输出的 P(click) 系统性偏高,广告竞价按 bid=P(click)×价值出价后开始悄悄超支。
scenario_en: A CTR model has high offline AUC but systematically overestimates P(click), and ad bidding at bid=P(click)×value quietly overspends.
q: 为什么损失函数选择要当成生产设计决策,而非纯理论?
q_en: Why treat loss-function choice as a production design decision, not pure theory?
why: 因为损失直接决定输出的性质:一个只最大化 AUC 但概率不校准的模型,会在二价拍卖里扭曲出价、悄悄流失营收。分类/排序/校准三类损失各服务不同下游需求,选错就算离线指标好看线上照样亏钱。
why_en: Loss shapes the output's usable property: an AUC-maximizing but miscalibrated model distorts second-price auction bids and silently loses revenue, so classification/ranking/calibration losses serve different downstream needs.
diagram:
flowchart TD L["损失函数选择"] --> C["分类损失
CE/Focal"] L --> R["排序损失
BPR/Lambda*"] L --> K["校准
Platt/Isotonic"]
options: 损失函数只影响训练收敛速度,不影响业务结果,随便选
损失决定输出性质:只追 AUC 但概率不校准会扭曲拍卖出价、流失营收,选错线上会亏钱
只要模型够大,任何损失都收敛到同样结果,选择无关紧要
损失函数是学术概念,生产系统统一用 MSE 即可
options_en: Loss only affects training convergence speed, not business outcomes, so pick any.
Loss decides the output's property: chasing AUC without calibration distorts auction bids and loses revenue, so wrong choices cost money in production.
With a big enough model, any loss converges to the same result, so choice is irrelevant.
Loss is academic; production uses MSE uniformly.
whenOtherWins: 若下游只需相对排序、完全不用概率绝对值(如纯召回排序),那对概率校准的要求可以放松,选排序损失即可。
optionExplanations: 损失直接决定输出是否可当概率用,"只影响收敛"低估了它的业务影响。
对;AUC 高不等于概率可用,校准差会在竞价/阈值这些下游悄悄亏钱,这就是它是设计决策的原因。
不同损失优化不同目标(排序 vs 概率),再大模型也收敛到不同性质的输出。
MSE 对分类和排序都不合适,统一用它会牺牲概率语义和排序质量。
optionExplanations_en: Loss decides whether the output is usable as a probability; 'only affects convergence' underrates its business impact.
Correct — high AUC doesn't mean usable probabilities, and poor calibration silently loses money downstream, which is why it's a design decision.
Different losses optimize different goals (ranking vs probability), so even big models converge to differently-shaped outputs.
MSE suits neither classification nor ranking; using it uniformly sacrifices probability semantics and ranking quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量模型排序能力(正样本排在负样本前的概率),但不反映概率是否校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures ranking ability (probability a positive outranks a negative) but not whether probabilities are calibrated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 赢家按第二高出价付费的拍卖机制,广告竞价常用,出价依赖校准的 P(click)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A second-price auction charges the winner the second-highest bid, common in ad auctions, where bids rely on calibrated P(click).

scenario: CTR 预估 head 要一个默认分类损失,类别大致均衡,下游还想直接用输出概率。
scenario_en: A CTR head needs a default classification loss with roughly balanced classes, and downstream wants to use the output probability directly.
q: 二元交叉熵默认好在哪,什么条件下输出接近校准?
q_en: Why is binary cross-entropy the default, and when is its output near-calibrated?
why: 二元交叉熵 L=−[y·log(p)+(1−y)·log(1−p)],向真实标签方向给平滑梯度,是 CTR head 和二/多分类的工业标准。当类别大致均衡时,它的输出近似校准的后验概率,可直接用于下游竞价/阈值。
why_en: Binary cross-entropy gives smooth gradients toward the true label and, when classes are roughly balanced, yields approximately calibrated posterior probabilities.
options: 它专为极端不均衡设计,类别越偏越校准
它给平滑梯度、是工业标准;类别大致均衡时输出近似校准的后验概率
它只优化排序,不产出可用概率
它输出的分数没有概率意义,必须再套一层校准才能用
options_en: It's designed for extreme imbalance; the more skewed the classes, the better calibrated.
It gives smooth gradients and is the industry standard; with roughly balanced classes it yields approximately calibrated posterior probabilities.
It only optimizes ranking and produces no usable probability.
Its scores have no probability meaning and always need a calibration layer to be usable.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反:极端不均衡下简单 CE 会被易负样本主导,那时才需要 focal loss。
对;平滑梯度+均衡时近似校准,是它当 CTR 默认损失的原因。
CE 是分类概率损失不是排序损失,它就产出概率。
均衡数据上 CE 输出本就近似校准,不是必须再套校准层。
optionExplanations_en: The opposite: under extreme imbalance plain CE is dominated by easy negatives, which is when focal loss is needed.
Correct — smooth gradients plus near-calibration when balanced is why it's the default CTR loss.
CE is a classification probability loss, not a ranking loss; it does produce probabilities.
On balanced data CE output is already near-calibrated, so a calibration layer isn't always required.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类默认损失 L=−[y·log(p)+(1−y)·log(1−p)],向真实标签给平滑梯度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Binary cross-entropy is the default classification loss, giving smooth gradients toward the true label.

termDefinitions.term: calibrated posterior / 校准后验概率
termDefinitions.meaning: 输出概率与真实发生频率一致(说 0.3 就约 30% 发生)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibrated posterior means predicted probabilities match real frequencies (0.3 means about 30% happen).

scenario: 欺诈检测正样本占比 <1/10,000,用普通交叉熵训练时海量易分负样本主导了梯度,模型学不到稀有正类。
scenario_en: Fraud positives are <1 in 10,000, and with plain cross-entropy the flood of easy negatives dominates the gradient so the model can't learn the rare positives.
q: 极端类别不均衡下该换什么损失?
q_en: Under extreme class imbalance, which loss should you switch to?
why: 用 focal loss:它加一个调制因子 (1−p_t)^γ,把已高置信分对的样本(p_t→1)的梯度压下去,让模型把注意力放到难分的稀有正类上。普通 CE 在 <1/10,000 这种不均衡下会被易负样本淹没。
why_en: Use focal loss: its modulating factor down-weights easy, high-confidence examples so the model focuses on hard rare positives, which plain CE drowns out under extreme imbalance.
options: 继续用普通 CE,再把学习率调大就能学到正类
focal loss:加调制因子 (1−p_t)^γ 压低易分样本梯度,聚焦难分的稀有正类
改用 MSE 回归标签,回归对不均衡更鲁棒
把所有负样本直接删到和正样本一样多,信息损失不重要
options_en: Stay with plain CE and just raise the learning rate to learn the positives.
Focal loss: add a modulating factor (1-p_t)^gamma that down-weights easy examples and focuses on hard rare positives.
Switch to MSE on the labels; regression is more robust to imbalance.
Delete negatives down to the positive count; the information loss doesn't matter.
whenOtherWins: 当类别大致均衡、无需压易样本时,普通交叉熵反而更简单、开箱校准更好,不必上 focal loss。
optionExplanations: 调大 lr 不改变易负样本主导梯度的结构,稀有正类照样被淹没。
对;调制因子静默易分样本梯度,把学习信号集中到难分稀有正类,正是极端不均衡的解。
MSE 不是分类概率损失,对不均衡分类既不校准也不聚焦难例。
粗暴删负样本丢大量信息且不是损失层面的解,focal 才是在损失里重加权。
optionExplanations_en: Raising LR doesn't change easy negatives dominating the gradient; rare positives stay drowned out.
Correct — the modulating factor silences easy-example gradients and concentrates learning on hard rare positives, the fix for extreme imbalance.
MSE isn't a classification probability loss; it neither calibrates nor focuses on hard cases under imbalance.
Bluntly deleting negatives loses information and isn't a loss-level fix, whereas focal reweights within the loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在交叉熵上乘调制因子 (1−p_t)^γ,压低易分样本、聚焦难分样本,治极端不均衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Focal loss multiplies cross-entropy by (1-p_t)^gamma to down-weight easy examples and focus on hard ones, for extreme imbalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型已高置信判为负的样本,在不均衡下数量巨大会主导梯度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Easy negatives are samples confidently classified as negative; under imbalance their sheer number dominates the gradient.

scenario: 面试官问 focal loss 里 (1−p_t)^γ 这个调制因子具体在干什么。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what focal loss's modulating factor (1-p_t)^gamma actually does.
q: focal loss 的调制因子如何改变各样本的梯度?
q_en: How does focal loss's modulating factor change per-example gradients?
why: L_focal=−α_t·(1−p_t)^γ·log(p_t)。对已分对的高置信样本 p_t→1,(1−p_t)^γ→0,梯度被静默;对难分样本 p_t 小,因子接近 1,梯度基本保留。于是学习信号自动从易样本转移到难样本。
why_en: For confident correct examples (p_t to 1) the factor (1-p_t)^gamma goes to 0 and silences the gradient, while hard examples keep near-full gradient, shifting learning to hard cases.
options: 它放大所有样本的梯度,让训练更快
对高置信分对样本(p_t→1)静默梯度,对难分样本保留梯度,学习信号转向难例
它只作用于负样本,对正样本没有任何影响
它把梯度全部置零,相当于停止训练
options_en: It amplifies every example's gradient to train faster.
It silences gradients for confident correct examples (p_t to 1) and keeps them for hard examples, shifting learning to hard cases.
It only affects negatives and has no effect on positives.
It zeros all gradients, effectively stopping training.
optionExplanations: 它不是放大所有梯度,而是选择性压低易样本梯度,方向相反。
对;(1−p_t)^γ 随置信度增大趋零,把梯度预算从易样本挪给难样本。
它对任何已高置信分对的样本(含正类)都压梯度,不只负样本。
只有 p_t→1 的样本梯度趋零,难样本梯度保留,训练照常进行。
optionExplanations_en: It doesn't amplify all gradients; it selectively down-weights easy examples — the opposite.
Correct — (1-p_t)^gamma goes to zero as confidence rises, reallocating gradient budget from easy to hard examples.
It down-weights any confidently correct example including positives, not just negatives.
Only p_t-to-1 examples have gradients near zero; hard examples keep theirs, so training continues.

termDefinitions.meaning: focal loss 里的 (1−p_t)^γ,随预测置信度升高而减小,压低易样本贡献。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The modulating factor (1-p_t)^gamma in focal loss shrinks as prediction confidence rises, down-weighting easy examples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型对真实类别赋予的概率,p_t→1 表示已高置信分对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p_t is the probability the model assigns to the true class; p_t near 1 means a confident correct prediction.

scenario: RetinaNet 默认 γ=2;一个 p_t=0.9 的样本损失被压到约原来的 1/100;γ 一般在验证集上调在 1–5。
scenario_en: RetinaNet defaults to gamma=2; an example at p_t=0.9 has its loss cut ~100x; gamma is tuned in 1-5 on validation.
q: focal loss 的 γ 该怎么理解和调?
q_en: How should you understand and tune focal loss's gamma?
why: γ 控压制强度:γ=0 退化成普通 CE;γ=2(RetinaNet 默认)时 p_t=0.9 的样本损失约降 100 倍。在验证集上 1–5 之间调,权衡稀有正类召回 vs 多数类精度;太大会连易样本都欠拟合。这是经验超参不是公式常量。
why_en: Gamma sets suppression strength: gamma=0 is plain CE, gamma=2 cuts a p_t=0.9 example's loss ~100x, tuned in 1-5 to trade rare-positive recall against majority precision.
options: γ 是学习率,越大训练越快
γ 控压制强度:γ=0 即 CE,γ=2 时 p_t=0.9 损失约降 100 倍,验证集 1–5 调,太大欠拟合易样本
γ 是类别数量,固定等于正负两类
γ 越大一定越准,应尽量设到最大
options_en: Gamma is the learning rate; larger trains faster.
Gamma sets suppression strength: gamma=0 is CE, gamma=2 cuts a p_t=0.9 loss ~100x, tuned 1-5 on validation, too high underfits easy examples.
Gamma is the number of classes, fixed at two for positive/negative.
Larger gamma is always more accurate, so set it as high as possible.
optionExplanations: γ 不是学习率,它只调易样本的压制强度,与步长无关。
对;γ 是压制旋钮,γ=0 退回 CE、γ=2 是常用默认,过大反而欠拟合易样本,得验证集上调。
γ 与类别数无关,它是控制调制因子陡峭度的连续超参。
γ 太大会把易样本梯度也压没导致欠拟合,不是越大越好。
optionExplanations_en: Gamma isn't the learning rate; it only sets easy-example suppression, unrelated to step size.
Correct — gamma is the suppression knob: gamma=0 reverts to CE, gamma=2 is a common default, and too high underfits easy examples, so tune on validation.
Gamma is unrelated to class count; it's a continuous hyperparameter controlling the modulating factor's steepness.
Too-high gamma suppresses easy-example gradients into underfitting, so bigger isn't always better.

termDefinitions.meaning: focal loss 里控制易样本压制强度的超参,γ=0 即普通 CE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gamma is focal loss's focusing hyperparameter controlling easy-example suppression; gamma=0 is plain cross-entropy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提出 focal loss 的稠密目标检测模型,默认 γ=2。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RetinaNet is the dense object-detection model that introduced focal loss, defaulting to gamma=2.

scenario: 有人以为上了 focal loss 就不必再管数据采样了。
scenario_en: Someone assumes adopting focal loss removes any need for data sampling.
q: focal loss 能替代过采样/类别加权采样吗?
q_en: Does focal loss replace oversampling / class-weighted sampling?
why: 不能替代:focal 在损失层面重加权,过采样在数据层面平衡分布,两者互补。实践中把 focal loss 与分层小批(每个 batch 保证一定比例正样本)结合,效果最好;只靠 focal 而 batch 里几乎没有正样本,梯度依旧稀薄。
why_en: Focal loss reweights at the loss level while oversampling balances at the data level, so combine focal with stratified mini-batches rather than replacing sampling.
options: 能,focal loss 完全取代采样,数据侧不用再动
不能,focal 在损失层重加权、采样在数据层平衡,应与分层小批结合
能,只要 γ 够大就不需要任何采样
两者冲突,用了 focal 就绝不能再做任何采样
options_en: Yes, focal loss fully replaces sampling; the data side needs no change.
No — focal reweights at the loss level and sampling balances at the data level, so combine focal with stratified mini-batches.
Yes, as long as gamma is large enough no sampling is needed.
They conflict; using focal means never doing any sampling.
optionExplanations: focal 不平衡 batch 里的样本构成,若一个 batch 几乎全是负样本,梯度仍稀薄。
对;损失重加权与数据采样互补,分层小批+ focal 才能同时保证正样本出现和难例聚焦。
γ 再大也解决不了 batch 里正样本极少的问题,采样管的是分布不是权重。
两者不冲突而是互补,实践中常一起用。
optionExplanations_en: Focal doesn't balance batch composition; if a batch is almost all negatives, gradients stay thin.
Correct — loss reweighting and data sampling are complementary, so stratified mini-batches plus focal ensure both positive presence and hard-case focus.
No gamma fixes batches with almost no positives; sampling controls distribution, not weights.
They don't conflict but complement, and are commonly used together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 构造每个训练 batch 时保证各类别有一定比例,防某类在 batch 中缺席。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stratified mini-batch is built to guarantee each class a share, preventing a class from being absent in the batch.

scenario: 小测:在 γ>0 的 focal loss 下,一个已经分得很好的样本(p_t→1)的梯度会怎样?
scenario_en: Quiz: under focal loss with gamma>0, what happens to the gradient of a well-classified example (p_t to 1)?
q: γ>0 时,已分好样本的梯度贡献如何变化?
q_en: With gamma>0, how does a well-classified example's gradient change?
why: 显著减小:(1−p_t)^γ 在 p_t→1 时趋近 0,把这些已学会样本的梯度几乎抹掉,好让优化器把力气花在还没学好的难样本上。这正是 focal loss 治不均衡的核心机制。
why_en: It is significantly reduced, because (1-p_t)^gamma approaches zero as p_t to 1, nearly erasing well-classified examples' gradients so the optimizer focuses on hard ones.
options: 显著增大,模型更用力去学已经会的样本
显著减小,(1−p_t)^γ→0 抹掉已学好样本的梯度,力气转向难样本
完全不变,与普通 CE 一样
先增大后减小,取决于 batch 大小
options_en: Significantly increased; the model works harder on already-learned examples.
Significantly reduced; (1-p_t)^gamma to 0 erases well-classified examples' gradients, shifting effort to hard ones.
Unchanged, same as plain CE.
First increases then decreases depending on batch size.
optionExplanations: 已学会的样本正是要压制的对象,不该增大它们的梯度。
对;调制因子在高置信处趋零,静默易样本、聚焦难样本,是 focal 的设计目的。
γ>0 时它明显不同于 CE,易样本梯度被压,不是不变。
变化只取决于 p_t 和 γ,和 batch 大小无关。
optionExplanations_en: Already-learned examples are exactly what to suppress; their gradients shouldn't grow.
Correct — the modulating factor nears zero at high confidence, silencing easy and focusing on hard examples, focal's design goal.
With gamma>0 it clearly differs from CE; easy-example gradients are suppressed, not unchanged.
The change depends only on p_t and gamma, not batch size.

scenario: 排序损失按"一次看多少数据"分成三类,面试官要你区分。
scenario_en: Ranking losses split by 'how much data at once' into three units; the interviewer asks you to distinguish them.
q: pointwise / pairwise / listwise 的区别是什么?
q_en: What distinguishes pointwise / pairwise / listwise?
why: pointwise 给每个物品一个绝对分,忽略它在列表中的相对位置;pairwise 只要求相关项排在不相关项之前(成对比较);listwise 直接优化整张列表的指标(如 NDCG)。粒度从单点→成对→整列,越靠后越贴近最终排序指标但计算越贵。
why_en: Pointwise scores each item absolutely, pairwise enforces relevant-over-irrelevant order, and listwise optimizes a whole-list metric like NDCG.
options: 三者完全一样,只是叫法不同
pointwise 单项绝对分;pairwise 成对相对序;listwise 优化整列表指标(如 NDCG)
pointwise 优化整列表、listwise 单项打分,和实际相反
三者都只看单个物品,不考虑列表
options_en: All three are the same, just different names.
Pointwise scores single items absolutely; pairwise enforces pairwise relative order; listwise optimizes a whole-list metric like NDCG.
Pointwise optimizes the whole list and listwise scores single items — reversed from reality.
All three look only at a single item, ignoring the list.
optionExplanations: 三者优化粒度不同(点/对/列),直接影响是否对齐最终排序指标,不是叫法差异。
对;从单点到成对到整列,粒度递增、越贴近 NDCG 但越贵,是排序损失的分类主轴。
角色说反了:pointwise 是单项打分,listwise 才优化整列表。
只有 pointwise 只看单项;pairwise 看成对、listwise 看整列表。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in granularity (point/pair/list), which affects alignment to the final ranking metric — not just naming.
Correct — from point to pair to list, granularity rises, closer to NDCG but costlier, the main axis of ranking losses.
Roles reversed: pointwise scores single items and listwise optimizes the whole list.
Only pointwise looks at a single item; pairwise looks at pairs and listwise at the whole list.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序质量指标,越靠前的相关项贡献越大,越靠后折扣越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a ranking-quality metric where relevant items higher up contribute more.

scenario: 推荐里只有隐式反馈(用户点了什么),没有显式评分,想训一个学相对偏好的模型。
scenario_en: A recommender has only implicit feedback (what users clicked), no explicit ratings, and wants to learn relative preference.
q: BPR 的优化目标和适用信号是什么?
q_en: What is BPR's objective and the feedback it suits?
why: BPR 是 pairwise:最大化"正样本 i 的分高于随机采样负样本 j"的概率,L_BPR=−log σ(x̂_ui−x̂_uj)。它只需正确的相对排序、不需绝对分,天然适配点击这类隐式反馈,靠负采样能扩到数十亿对,是候选生成的默认损失。
why_en: BPR is pairwise: it maximizes the probability a positive scores above a sampled negative, needing only correct ordering, so it suits implicit feedback and scales via negative sampling.
options: BPR 要求每个物品有精确的绝对评分,只能用显式反馈
BPR pairwise 最大化正样本分>采样负样本,只需相对序,适配隐式反馈,负采样可扩
BPR 直接优化 NDCG,是 listwise 损失
BPR 输出校准的点击概率,专为竞价设计
options_en: BPR requires an exact absolute rating per item, usable only with explicit feedback.
BPR is pairwise, maximizing positive-over-sampled-negative, needing only relative order, suited to implicit feedback, scalable via negative sampling.
BPR directly optimizes NDCG and is a listwise loss.
BPR outputs calibrated click probabilities, designed for bidding.
optionExplanations: BPR 恰恰不需要绝对评分,它只比较正负相对高低,专为无评分的隐式反馈设计。
对;pairwise 相对序+负采样让它便宜可扩,是候选生成阶段的默认损失。
BPR 是 pairwise 不是 listwise,它不直接优化 NDCG(那是 LambdaRank)。
BPR 优化排序不保证概率校准,竞价需要校准的概率损失而非 BPR。
optionExplanations_en: BPR specifically needs no absolute ratings; it compares positive vs negative order, built for rating-free implicit feedback.
Correct — pairwise relative order plus negative sampling make it cheap and scalable, the default candidate-generation loss.
BPR is pairwise not listwise; it doesn't directly optimize NDCG (that's LambdaRank).
BPR optimizes ranking without guaranteeing calibration; bidding needs a calibrated probability loss, not BPR.

termDefinitions.meaning: pairwise 排序损失,最大化正样本得分高于采样负样本,适配隐式反馈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BPR (Bayesian Personalized Ranking) is a pairwise ranking loss maximizing a positive scoring above a sampled negative, for implicit feedback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户行为(点击/购买)隐含的偏好信号,没有显式打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Implicit feedback is preference inferred from behavior (clicks/purchases) with no explicit ratings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从海量未交互项里随机抽负样本与正样本配对,避免全量计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Negative sampling randomly draws negatives from the vast un-interacted items to pair with positives, avoiding full computation.

scenario: 召回(candidate generation)阶段要从数十亿物品里快速筛出几百个候选,只需近似排序、追求速度和规模。
scenario_en: The candidate-generation stage must quickly narrow billions of items to a few hundred, needing only approximate ordering at speed and scale.
q: 召回阶段的排序损失该选什么?
q_en: Which ranking loss fits candidate generation?
why: 选 BPR:候选生成只需近似正确的相对序、要快要能扩,BPR 的 pairwise+负采样正好又快又能到数十亿对。精细的、按位置加权的 listwise(LambdaRank)留给最终重排,那里指标对齐更值这份算力。
why_en: Pick BPR: candidate generation needs fast, scalable approximate ordering, which pairwise-plus-negative-sampling delivers, leaving metric-aligned listwise for final re-ranking.
options: LambdaRank,直接优化 NDCG 最精确,召回也该用最好的
BPR,pairwise+负采样又快又可扩,近似排序满足召回的速度/规模需求
普通 MSE 回归,召回只要回归分数
focal loss,召回阶段最怕类别不均衡
options_en: LambdaRank — it optimizes NDCG most precisely, and recall deserves the best too.
BPR — pairwise plus negative sampling is fast and scalable, and approximate ordering meets recall's speed/scale needs.
Plain MSE regression — recall just needs regressed scores.
Focal loss — recall most fears class imbalance.
whenOtherWins: 到最终重排阶段,候选只剩几百个、指标对齐比速度更重要时,才换成 LambdaRank/LambdaMART。
optionExplanations: LambdaRank 逐位置加权算得贵,数十亿候选上跑不动,精度换不回召回要的吞吐。
对;BPR 便宜可扩、近似排序够用,是召回阶段的默认选择。
MSE 回归不直接优化排序,召回要的是相对序不是绝对回归值。
focal 是分类不均衡损失,不解决召回的大规模排序问题。
optionExplanations_en: LambdaRank's per-position weighting is costly and can't run over billions of candidates; precision doesn't buy back recall's needed throughput.
Correct — BPR is cheap, scalable, and approximate ordering suffices, the default at the recall stage.
MSE regression doesn't directly optimize ranking; recall needs relative order, not absolute regressed values.
Focal is a classification-imbalance loss, not a fix for recall's large-scale ranking.

scenario: 用 BPR 训练排序,发现它对"交换发生在列表哪个位置"一视同仁。
scenario_en: Training ranking with BPR, you notice it treats a swap the same regardless of where in the list it happens.
q: BPR 相比 listwise 的关键局限是什么?
q_en: What is BPR's key limitation versus listwise?
why: BPR 不加权"交换发生在列表哪里":把第 1、2 名交换和第 98、99 名交换视为同等,但对用户/指标而言头部错序代价远大。listwise(LambdaRank)正是用 NDCG 变化给不同位置的交换赋不同权重来补上这点。
why_en: BPR doesn't weight where a swap occurs, treating top-of-list and bottom swaps equally, whereas listwise weights by NDCG change.
options: BPR 无法处理隐式反馈,只能用显式评分
BPR 不加权交换位置:头部错序和尾部错序同等对待,忽略了位置的重要性差异
BPR 计算太贵,无法扩到大规模
BPR 会输出过度校准的概率,破坏排序
options_en: BPR can't handle implicit feedback and needs explicit ratings.
BPR doesn't weight swap position: it treats top and bottom mis-orderings equally, ignoring positional importance.
BPR is too expensive to scale.
BPR outputs over-calibrated probabilities that break ranking.
optionExplanations: BPR 正是为隐式反馈设计的,这说反了。
对;不区分交换位置是 BPR 的核心局限,头部排序质量因此得不到重点优化。
BPR 靠负采样恰恰便宜可扩,不是贵。
BPR 不优化概率校准,谈不上过度校准,和它的位置局限无关。
optionExplanations_en: BPR is designed for implicit feedback — this is reversed.
Correct — not distinguishing swap position is BPR's core limitation, so top-of-list quality isn't prioritized.
BPR is cheap and scalable via negative sampling, not expensive.
BPR doesn't optimize calibration, so over-calibration doesn't apply and is unrelated to its positional limitation.

scenario: 最终重排要让头部顺序尽量对,交换排名靠前的两个物品应该比交换靠后的更受重视。
scenario_en: Final re-ranking must get the head order right, so swapping two top items should matter more than swapping bottom ones.
q: LambdaRank 如何让排序对齐 NDCG?
q_en: How does LambdaRank align ranking with NDCG?
why: LambdaRank 给每对样本的 pairwise 梯度乘上"交换这两个位置带来的 NDCG 变化":交换 1↔2 对 NDCG 影响大、权重大,交换 98↔99 影响小、权重小。这样直接把优化力度对齐到最终排序指标,而无需对不可导的 NDCG 求导。
why_en: LambdaRank weights each pairwise gradient by the NDCG change from swapping those two positions, so top swaps get larger gradients aligned to the metric.
options: 它对所有位置的交换赋予相同权重,和 BPR 一样
它给每对梯度乘上交换这两位带来的 NDCG 变化,头部交换权重更大,对齐指标
它直接对 NDCG 求导来反向传播
它放弃排序,改成逐项概率回归
options_en: It gives all swap positions equal weight, just like BPR.
It multiplies each pairwise gradient by the NDCG change from swapping those two positions, so top swaps get larger weight aligned to the metric.
It directly differentiates NDCG for backprop.
It abandons ranking for per-item probability regression.
optionExplanations: 等权正是 BPR 的做法,LambdaRank 的价值恰恰是按位置差异化加权。
对;用 NDCG 变化加权每对梯度,让优化重点落在头部,是它对齐指标的核心。
NDCG 不可导,LambdaRank 正是绕开求导、直接用指标变化当梯度权重。
它仍是排序损失,只是给 pairwise 梯度加了指标权重,不是回归。
optionExplanations_en: Equal weighting is BPR's approach; LambdaRank's value is exactly position-differentiated weighting.
Correct — weighting each pairwise gradient by NDCG change concentrates optimization on the head, its metric-alignment core.
NDCG is non-differentiable; LambdaRank specifically sidesteps differentiation by using metric change as the gradient weight.
It remains a ranking loss, just adding a metric weight to pairwise gradients, not regression.

termDefinitions.meaning: listwise 排序,用交换两位带来的 NDCG 变化加权每对 pairwise 梯度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LambdaRank is a listwise method weighting each pairwise gradient by the NDCG change from swapping two positions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 这些经指标加权的梯度,无需对不可导的 NDCG 求导即可得到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The lambdas are these metric-weighted gradients, obtained without differentiating the non-differentiable NDCG.

scenario: 特征丰富的搜索排序场景,想要 listwise 的指标对齐,又想用树模型的表达力。
scenario_en: A feature-rich search-ranking setting wants listwise metric alignment with the expressiveness of tree models.
q: LambdaMART 是怎么构成的,擅长什么?
q_en: How is LambdaMART built, and what is it good at?
why: LambdaMART = 把 LambdaRank 的 λ 梯度放进 GBDT:每一轮 boosting 用一棵树去拟合这些指标加权的 lambda 梯度。它是 Bing 搜索排序的主力,在特征丰富的场景里与神经排序器不相上下。
why_en: LambdaMART puts LambdaRank's lambda gradients inside GBDT, fitting a tree to those metric-weighted gradients each boosting round, the backbone of Bing search ranking.
options: 把 LambdaRank 的 λ 梯度塞进神经网络的注意力层
把 LambdaRank 的 λ 梯度放进 GBDT,每轮树拟合这些指标加权梯度;Bing 搜索排序主力
一种纯 pointwise 回归损失,与 NDCG 无关
只是 BPR 的另一个名字,机制完全相同
options_en: Put LambdaRank's lambda gradients into a neural attention layer.
Put LambdaRank's lambda gradients into GBDT, fitting a tree to those metric-weighted gradients each round; the backbone of Bing search ranking.
A pure pointwise regression loss unrelated to NDCG.
Just another name for BPR with identical mechanics.
optionExplanations: LambdaMART 用的是梯度提升树 GBDT 不是神经注意力,载体说错了。
对;λ 梯度 + GBDT 的组合,让树模型也能对齐 NDCG,在特征丰富场景很强。
它是 listwise 指标对齐的,不是与 NDCG 无关的 pointwise 回归。
它是 GBDT 载体的 listwise 方法,和 pairwise 的 BPR 机制不同。
optionExplanations_en: LambdaMART uses gradient-boosted trees (GBDT), not neural attention — wrong carrier.
Correct — lambda gradients plus GBDT let trees align to NDCG, strong in feature-rich settings.
It's listwise metric-aligned, not an NDCG-agnostic pointwise regression.
It's a GBDT-based listwise method, mechanically different from pairwise BPR.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 LambdaRank 的 λ 梯度用在 GBDT 上的 listwise 排序方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LambdaMART is a listwise ranking method applying LambdaRank's lambda gradients within GBDT.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐轮加树、每棵拟合前一轮残差/梯度的树集成模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT (Gradient-Boosted Decision Trees) is a tree ensemble adding trees round by round, each fitting the previous round's residual/gradient.

scenario: 最终重排阶段只剩几百个候选,要把头部顺序做到最精,直接对齐 NDCG 换取业务价值。
scenario_en: Final re-ranking has a few hundred candidates and must perfect the head order, aligning to NDCG for business value.
q: 最终重排该用哪类损失?
q_en: Which loss family for final re-ranking?
why: 用 LambdaMART/LambdaRank 这类 listwise:候选少、可承受更高算力,而它们按位置用 NDCG 加权梯度,把头部排序做精,指标对齐直接转成业务价值。BPR 只给近似序、不加权位置,精度不够。
why_en: Use listwise LambdaMART/LambdaRank: few candidates afford the compute, and NDCG-weighted gradients perfect the head order for business value.
options: BPR,pairwise 又快又能扩,重排也该优先速度
LambdaMART/LambdaRank(listwise),按位置 NDCG 加权把头部排序做精,指标对齐
focal loss,重排最怕不均衡
普通交叉熵逐项打分,忽略列表结构
options_en: BPR — pairwise is fast and scalable, and re-ranking should prioritize speed too.
LambdaMART/LambdaRank (listwise) — NDCG-weighted by position to perfect the head order, aligned to the metric.
Focal loss — re-ranking most fears imbalance.
Plain cross-entropy per-item scoring, ignoring list structure.
whenOtherWins: 在召回阶段、候选达数十亿、速度和规模压倒精度时,反而该用 BPR 而非 listwise。
optionExplanations: 重排阶段候选已很少,速度不再是瓶颈,BPR 的近似序换不来头部精度。
对;listwise 按位置加权对齐 NDCG,把头部做精,正是重排追求的价值。
focal 是分类不均衡损失,与重排的列表排序目标不符。
逐项 CE 忽略列表结构,得不到 listwise 的位置加权优势。
optionExplanations_en: At re-ranking candidates are already few and speed isn't the bottleneck, so BPR's approximate order doesn't buy head precision.
Correct — listwise weights by position to align with NDCG and perfect the head, exactly re-ranking's goal.
Focal is a classification-imbalance loss, mismatched to re-ranking's list-ordering objective.
Per-item CE ignores list structure and misses listwise's positional weighting advantage.

scenario: 面试官要你横向比较 CE、BPR、LambdaRank、LambdaMART 的方法和最佳用途。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare CE, BPR, LambdaRank, and LambdaMART by approach and best use.
q: 这四个损失的方法与最佳用途分别是什么?
q_en: What are each loss's approach and best use?
why: CE 是 pointwise 单项概率,做 CTR;BPR pairwise 正负边际,做候选生成(隐式反馈);LambdaRank listwise 用 NDCG 加权 pairwise 梯度,做最终重排;LambdaMART 把 λ 梯度放 GBDT,做大规模搜索排序。粒度和载体决定各自战场。
why_en: CE is pointwise for CTR, BPR pairwise for candidate generation, LambdaRank listwise for re-ranking, and LambdaMART lambda-gradients-in-GBDT for search ranking.
options: 四者用途完全可互换,选哪个都一样
CE→CTR;BPR→候选生成;LambdaRank→最终重排;LambdaMART→大规模搜索排序
CE 做重排、LambdaRank 做 CTR,和实际相反
四者都是 pointwise,只是名字不同
options_en: Their uses are fully interchangeable; pick any.
CE for CTR; BPR for candidate generation; LambdaRank for final re-ranking; LambdaMART for large-scale search ranking.
CE for re-ranking and LambdaRank for CTR — reversed from reality.
All four are pointwise, just different names.
optionExplanations: 它们粒度和目标不同,用途不可互换,混用会牺牲各自优势。
对;每个损失对应一个阶段/场景,粒度和载体决定它擅长哪一步。
角色说反了:CE 做 CTR/pointwise,LambdaRank 做 listwise 重排。
只有 CE 是 pointwise;BPR pairwise,Lambda 系是 listwise。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in granularity and goal, so uses aren't interchangeable and mixing sacrifices each one's strength.
Correct — each loss maps to a stage/scenario, with granularity and carrier setting what it's good at.
Roles reversed: CE is for CTR/pointwise and LambdaRank for listwise re-ranking.
Only CE is pointwise; BPR is pairwise and the Lambda family is listwise.

scenario: 面试官问"模型校准得好"到底是什么意思。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what 'the model is well-calibrated' actually means.
q: 校准良好的定义是什么?
q_en: What is the definition of well-calibrated?
why: 校准良好=在所有模型输出 P=0.3 的曝光里,约 30% 真的发生了点击;即预测概率与实际频率一致。它和排序能力(AUC)是两回事:模型可以排序很好但概率系统性偏高/偏低。
why_en: Well-calibrated means among all impressions where the model says P=0.3, about 30% actually click — predicted probabilities match observed frequencies.
options: 模型的 AUC 越高就越校准,两者是一回事
在所有预测 P=0.3 的样本里约 30% 真的发生,即预测概率与实际频率一致
校准指模型准确率超过 90%
校准指模型对每个样本都输出 0 或 1 的确定预测
options_en: The higher the AUC the more calibrated; they're the same thing.
Among all samples predicted P=0.3, about 30% actually occur — predicted probabilities match observed frequencies.
Calibration means accuracy above 90%.
Calibration means the model outputs a definite 0 or 1 for every sample.
optionExplanations: AUC 只看排序,不看概率绝对值,高 AUC 也可能概率系统偏差、不校准。
对;校准是"预测概率=实际频率",与排序能力独立,竞价/阈值依赖它。
校准不是准确率,一个高准确率模型概率也可能不校准。
输出确定 0/1 反而丢了概率信息,与校准无关。
optionExplanations_en: AUC only measures ranking, not absolute probability; high AUC can still be systematically biased and miscalibrated.
Correct — calibration is 'predicted probability equals observed frequency', independent of ranking, relied on by bidding/thresholds.
Calibration isn't accuracy; a high-accuracy model can still be miscalibrated.
Outputting hard 0/1 discards probability information and is unrelated to calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率与真实频率一致的程度,说 0.3 就约 30% 会发生。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is how well predicted probabilities match true frequencies, so 0.3 means about 30% occur.

scenario: 广告竞价按 bid=P(click)×出价价值报价,模型的 P(click) 系统性偏高。
scenario_en: Ad bidding sets bid=P(click)×bid_value, and the model's P(click) is systematically inflated.
q: P(click) 校准偏差在二价拍卖里造成什么后果?
q_en: What does miscalibrated P(click) cause in a second-price auction?
why: 因为出价直接乘以 P(click):高估 P(click)→出价偏高→超支/多花钱;低估→出价偏低→丢掉本该赢的曝光、流失营收。所以竞价系统对校准的敏感度极高,光有高 AUC 不够。
why_en: Since bid multiplies by P(click), overestimation overbids and overspends while underestimation underbids and loses winnable impressions and revenue.
options: 没有后果,拍卖只看排序不看概率绝对值
高估 P(click)→超支多花钱,低估→丢曝光流失营收,竞价对校准极敏感
只会影响训练速度,不影响出价
会让模型 AUC 下降,但出价不受影响
options_en: No consequence; auctions only care about ranking, not absolute probability.
Overestimating P(click) overspends, underestimating loses impressions and revenue; bidding is highly calibration-sensitive.
It only affects training speed, not bids.
It lowers AUC but doesn't affect bids.
optionExplanations: 出价直接乘 P(click),概率绝对值错就出价错,不只是排序问题。
对;高估超支、低估丢量,是校准差在竞价里的直接金钱后果。
校准偏差影响的是出价金额,不是训练速度。
校准与 AUC 独立,偏差主要害的是出价而非 AUC。
optionExplanations_en: The bid multiplies by P(click), so wrong absolute probability means wrong bids, not just ranking.
Correct — overestimation overspends and underestimation loses volume, the direct monetary cost of poor calibration in bidding.
Calibration error affects bid amounts, not training speed.
Calibration is independent of AUC; the error mainly harms bids, not AUC.

scenario: 欺诈/医疗分诊用固定阈值(如 0.5)决定是否告警,模型对真实概率 0.4 的样本却输出 0.8。
scenario_en: Fraud/medical triage uses a fixed threshold (e.g. 0.5) to alert, but the model outputs 0.8 for a case whose true probability is 0.4.
q: 校准偏差在阈值决策里造成什么问题?
q_en: What problem does miscalibration cause in threshold-based decisions?
why: 阈值决策直接把概率和临界值比:真实 0.4 却报 0.8,会越过 0.5 阈值触发大量本不该有的告警(过多误报),挤占人工复核、侵蚀对系统的信任。这类系统必须概率校准,阈值才有意义。
why_en: Threshold decisions compare probability to a cutoff, so reporting 0.8 when true is 0.4 crosses the threshold and triggers excessive false alarms that erode trust.
options: 没影响,阈值决策不依赖概率数值
真实 0.4 报 0.8 会越过阈值,产生过多误报、挤占人工复核、侵蚀信任
只会让模型更保守,减少告警
会提升召回且没有任何副作用
options_en: No effect; threshold decisions don't depend on probability values.
Reporting 0.8 when true is 0.4 crosses the threshold, producing excessive false alarms that burden review and erode trust.
It only makes the model more conservative, reducing alerts.
It boosts recall with no downside.
optionExplanations: 阈值决策正是拿概率数值和临界值比,数值错决策就错。
对;高估越过阈值→误报暴增→人工复核过载、信任下降,这是阈值系统的校准代价。
高估是更激进而非保守,会增加而不是减少告警。
误报暴增有明显副作用(信任和人力),不是无副作用的召回提升。
optionExplanations_en: Threshold decisions compare the probability value to a cutoff, so a wrong value means a wrong decision.
Correct — overestimation crosses the threshold, spiking false alarms, overloading review and eroding trust, the calibration cost in threshold systems.
Overestimation is more aggressive, not conservative, increasing rather than reducing alerts.
A spike in false alarms has clear downsides (trust and labor), not a free recall boost.

scenario: 线上模型概率明显不校准,要排查常见成因。
scenario_en: A production model is clearly miscalibrated, and you must diagnose common causes.
q: 以下哪些是常见的概率不校准成因?(多选)
q_en: Which are common causes of miscalibration? (multiple)
why: 常见成因:重正则(把概率往中间压)、focal loss(重塑损失景观、牺牲校准换聚焦难例)、不均衡数据。CE 在均衡数据上开箱校准较好,但生产数据很少均衡。识别成因才能决定是否上后处理校准。
why_en: Common causes are heavy regularization, focal loss (reshapes the loss landscape), and imbalanced data.
options: 过重的正则化
focal loss(重塑损失景观,牺牲校准换聚焦难例)
类别不均衡的数据
使用了 GPU 而非 CPU 训练
options_en: Heavy regularization.
Focal loss (reshapes the loss landscape, trading calibration for hard-example focus).
Class-imbalanced data.
Training on GPU instead of CPU.
optionExplanations: 对;强正则把概率往中间压,削弱与真实频率的对应,导致不校准。
对;focal 为聚焦难例重塑损失,常以牺牲概率校准为代价。
对;不均衡数据让 CE 的开箱校准假设失效,概率系统性偏移。
错;GPU/CPU 只是硬件,不改变模型输出概率的校准性。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — heavy regularization squeezes probabilities toward the middle, weakening the match to true frequency.
Correct — focal reshapes the loss to focus on hard examples, often at the cost of calibration.
Correct — imbalanced data breaks CE's out-of-the-box calibration assumption, biasing probabilities.
Wrong — GPU vs CPU is just hardware and doesn't change output calibration.

scenario: 要量化模型校准程度,常见两个指标是 ECE 和 Brier score。
scenario_en: To quantify calibration, two common metrics are ECE and Brier score.
q: ECE 和 Brier score 各衡量什么?
q_en: What does each of ECE and Brier score measure?
