optionExplanations: 排序质量是下游排序器的目标，检索阶段先别丢东西才是首要。
对；Recall@500 直接衡量覆盖率，漏掉的相关项排序器救不回来，是测验答案。
MRR 关注单个第一名，检索要的是整体覆盖不是排名。
Precision@5 是窄窗口的精度，检索阶段的关键是宽召回不是前 5 精度。
optionExplanations_en: Ordering quality is the downstream ranker's goal; retrieval must first not drop items.
Correct — Recall@500 directly measures coverage; dropped relevants can't be recovered — the quiz answer.
MRR focuses on a single first result; retrieval needs overall coverage, not rank.
Precision@5 is narrow-window precision; retrieval's key is wide recall, not top-5 precision.

termDefinitions.meaning: top-K 候选里覆盖到的相关物品占全部相关物品的比例，衡量检索是否漏掉好东西。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K is the fraction of all relevant items captured within the top-K, measuring whether retrieval drops good items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段推荐的第一阶段，从海量物品中快速召回几百个候选交给排序器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the first stage of two-stage recs, quickly recalling a few hundred candidates from millions for the ranker.

scenario: 两阶段推荐器：检索先从百万物品捞几百个候选，排序器再把候选排成最终列表。
scenario_en: A two-stage recommender: retrieval pulls hundreds of candidates from millions, then a ranker orders them into the final list.
q: 两阶段推荐里，检索和排序各自该优化哪类指标？为什么这样分工？
q_en: In two-stage recs, which metric family does retrieval vs ranking optimize, and why this split?
why: 检索优化 Recall@K（别漏掉好候选，覆盖优先，不管次序）；排序优化 NDCG/Precision@K（把候选排好，次序与位置优先）。分工原因：检索漏掉的东西排序救不回来，而排序质量只在候选集内才有意义。说清这个分工体现架构意识。
why_en: Retrieval optimizes Recall@K (don't lose good candidates, coverage first) and ranking optimizes NDCG/Precision@K (order them well), because dropped candidates can't be recovered and ordering only matters within the candidate set.
tradeoff: 检索：覆盖率(Recall@K) vs 排序：次序质量(NDCG/Precision@K)
diagram:
flowchart LR
  I["百万物品"] --> R["检索\n优化 Recall@K"]
  R -->|几百候选| K["排序\n优化 NDCG/Precision@K"]
  K --> L["最终 top-N 列表"]
options: 检索优化 NDCG、排序优化 Recall@K，先排好次序再保证覆盖
检索优化 Recall@K（保覆盖）、排序优化 NDCG/Precision@K（保次序）
两阶段都优化 accuracy，指标统一便于比较
检索优化 log loss、排序优化 Brier score，都盯概率校准
options_en: Retrieval optimizes NDCG and ranking optimizes Recall@K — order first, then coverage.
Retrieval optimizes Recall@K (coverage), ranking optimizes NDCG/Precision@K (ordering).
Both stages optimize accuracy for a unified, comparable metric.
Retrieval optimizes log loss and ranking optimizes Brier score, both targeting calibration.
optionExplanations: 分工反了：覆盖是检索的职责、次序是排序的职责，颠倒会让漏召回无法补救。
对；这个 Recall@K / NDCG 分工正是两阶段推荐的经典架构，点出它体现架构意识。
统一用 accuracy 抹掉了两阶段各自的优化目标，两头都测不准。
log loss/Brier 是校准类指标，不对应检索覆盖与排序次序的分工。
optionExplanations_en: The split is inverted: coverage is retrieval's job and ordering is ranking's; reversing it makes lost recall unrecoverable.
Correct — the Recall@K / NDCG split is the classic two-stage architecture; naming it signals architectural awareness.
Unifying on accuracy erases each stage's objective, mismeasuring both.
Log loss/Brier are calibration metrics, not matching the coverage-vs-ordering split.

termDefinitions.meaning: top-K 结果里相关物品的比例，适合固定 UI 槽位（如 top-5 应用推荐）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@K is the fraction of top-K results that are relevant, fit for fixed UI slots (e.g. top-5 app recs).

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检索召回候选、再排序精排的架构，两阶段目标不同、指标不同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage recommender retrieves candidates then ranks them, with different goals and metrics per stage.

scenario: 会话级的粗粒度评估：只想知道推荐列表 top-K 里到底有没有至少一个用户会喜欢的。
scenario_en: A coarse session-level check: just whether the top-K recommendation list has at least one item the user likes.
q: Hit rate 衡量什么？它为什么被称为「粗」指标？
q_en: What does hit rate measure, and why is it called a 'coarse' metric?
why: Hit rate 是二元的：top-K 里是否≥1 个相关物品，命中记 1、否则 0。它粗，因为不管相关项排第几、有几个、相关程度多高，只答「有没有」。适合快速会话级体检，不适合细分排序质量。
why_en: Hit rate is binary — whether at least one relevant item is in the top-K — and it's coarse because it ignores position, count, and grade, answering only presence.
options: top-K 里相关物品的加权分级得分，越靠前分越高
二元：top-K 里是否≥1 个相关物品；粗在只答有无、不管位置与数量
第一个相关结果排名的倒数，专测唯一答案位置
预测概率与观测频率的一致程度，衡量校准
options_en: A weighted graded score of relevant items in the top-K, higher for earlier positions.
Binary: whether at least one relevant item is in the top-K; coarse because it ignores position and count.
The reciprocal rank of the first relevant result, for single-answer position.
How well predicted probabilities match observed frequencies — calibration.
optionExplanations: 带位置折扣的分级得分是 NDCG，不是 hit rate。
对；hit rate 只问「有没有命中」，是最粗的会话级信号。
倒数排名是 MRR，衡量的是位置而非有无。
概率与频率一致性是校准，不是 hit rate。
optionExplanations_en: Position-discounted graded scoring is NDCG, not hit rate.
Correct — hit rate only asks whether there's a hit, the coarsest session-level signal.
Reciprocal rank is MRR, measuring position not presence.
Probability-frequency agreement is calibration, not hit rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二元会话级指标：top-K 是否包含至少一个相关物品，粗但直观。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is a binary session-level metric: whether the top-K contains at least one relevant item — coarse but intuitive.

scenario: 在一个静态基准上把 NDCG@10 提了 5%，上线 A/B 却发现 CTR 没涨。
scenario_en: You raised NDCG@10 by 5% on a static benchmark, but the live A/B shows no CTR lift.
q: 为什么静态基准上的 NDCG 提升可能不转化成在线 CTR？
q_en: Why might a NDCG gain on a static benchmark fail to translate into online CTR?
why: 静态基准常缺 position bias 和会话上下文——真实用户部分是「因为排在前面才点」，基准里没有这个信号。于是你在基准上优化的排序改善，到线上被位置偏置和上下文吃掉，NDCG 涨而 CTR 不涨。这是离线-在线解耦的典型。
why_en: Static benchmarks often lack position bias and session context — users click partly by position — so a benchmark NDCG gain gets absorbed live and doesn't lift CTR.
options: 因为 NDCG 计算错误，正确算法下一定会转化
静态基准缺 position bias 与会话上下文，基准上的排序增益到线上被吃掉
因为 CTR 永远和 NDCG 无关，两者根本不该一起看
因为 A/B 样本太少，加大到 10 倍流量 CTR 就会涨
options_en: Because NDCG was computed wrong; with the right algorithm it will always translate.
Static benchmarks lack position bias and session context, so the benchmark's ordering gain is absorbed live.
Because CTR is never related to NDCG and they shouldn't be viewed together.
Because the A/B sample is too small; 10x traffic would lift CTR.
optionExplanations: 不是算错，是基准本身缺了线上才有的信号。
对；缺 position bias/会话上下文让离线增益不转化，正是两相评估里的解耦案例。
NDCG 本就是 CTR 的离线 proxy，说无关错误。
样本量不解决基准缺失线上信号这个结构问题。
optionExplanations_en: It's not miscalculation; the benchmark lacks signals that only exist live.
Correct — missing position bias/session context makes offline gains not translate — a decorrelation case from two-phase evaluation.
NDCG is precisely an offline proxy for CTR; saying they're unrelated is wrong.
Sample size doesn't fix the structural gap of a benchmark missing live signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户部分因结果排位靠前而点击，而非因更相关；静态基准常缺此信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is users clicking partly because a result ranks high, not because it's more relevant — often absent from static benchmarks.

scenario: Uber ETA 预测：想要一个与目标同单位、可直接向业务解释的误差（例如「平均差 2 分钟」）。
scenario_en: Uber ETA prediction: you want an error in the target's own units, directly explainable to the business (e.g. 'off by 2 minutes on average').
q: 要一个可解释、与目标同单位的回归误差，选哪个指标？
q_en: For an interpretable, same-unit regression error, which metric?
why: 用 MAE：平均绝对误差与目标同单位（分钟），「平均差 2 分钟」业务一听就懂。它对每个误差等权、不像 RMSE 那样放大离群点。若偶发大误差代价特别高（如需求预测缺货），才转向 RMSE。
why_en: Use MAE — mean absolute error is in the target's units (minutes), so 'off by 2 minutes' is directly interpretable, and it weights every error equally rather than amplifying outliers like RMSE.
tradeoff: MAE（同单位、可解释、等权误差） vs RMSE（放大离群点、离群代价高时更合适）
whenOtherWins: 若大误差的代价远高于小误差（需求预测大幅低估→缺货、库存崩），要放大离群惩罚，RMSE 比 MAE 更合适。
options: RMSE：平方误差最能压制离群点，最适合 ETA
MAPE：百分比误差跨产品可比，ETA 首选
MAE：与目标同单位、可解释、对误差等权
R²：解释方差比例，最能向业务讲清 ETA 质量
options_en: RMSE: squared error best suppresses outliers, ideal for ETA.
MAPE: percentage error is cross-product comparable, first choice for ETA.
MAE: same units as the target, interpretable, weights errors equally.
R-squared: explained variance best conveys ETA quality to the business.
optionExplanations: RMSE 是放大而非压制离群点，且单位是平方后开根、不如 MAE 直观。
MAPE 是百分比、在真值接近 0 时爆炸，不是同单位可解释的选择。
对；MAE 同单位（分钟）、直接可解释，是 ETA 的自然选择。
R² 是无量纲方差解释比，不能说「平均差几分钟」，解释性差。
optionExplanations_en: RMSE amplifies not suppresses outliers, and its unit is a rooted-square — less intuitive than MAE.
MAPE is a percentage that blows up near zero true values — not the same-unit interpretable choice.
Correct — MAE is in minutes and directly interpretable, the natural ETA choice.
R-squared is a unitless variance ratio and can't say 'off by X minutes' — poor interpretability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均绝对误差：预测与真值差绝对值的平均，与目标同单位、对误差等权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAE (Mean Absolute Error) averages the absolute prediction errors, in the target's units and weighting errors equally.

scenario: 需求预测里偶尔出现的大幅低估会导致缺货，代价远高于日常小误差。
scenario_en: In demand forecasting, occasional large under-predictions cause stockouts, far costlier than everyday small errors.
q: MAE 与 RMSE 在「对离群误差的敏感度」上有何不同？这决定了什么时候选谁？
q_en: How do MAE and RMSE differ in outlier sensitivity, and how does that decide which to pick?
why: RMSE 先平方再开根，大误差被平方放大 → 对离群点敏感；MAE 线性等权 → 对离群点稳健。所以离群代价高（缺货、大额漏检）用 RMSE 逼模型别犯大错；只要平均水平、离群不特殊贵，用 MAE 更可解释。
why_en: RMSE squares errors so large ones dominate (outlier-sensitive), while MAE is linear and robust; pick RMSE when big errors are especially costly and MAE when you want an interpretable average.
tradeoff: RMSE（放大大误差、离群代价高时选） vs MAE（等权、可解释、离群不特殊贵时选）
options: MAE 对离群更敏感、RMSE 更稳健，所以缺货场景用 MAE
RMSE 平方放大大误差(离群敏感)，缺货这类大误差昂贵的场景用它；MAE 等权、更可解释
两者对离群点敏感度完全相同，只是单位不同
RMSE 只能用于分类、MAE 只能用于回归，不可混用
options_en: MAE is more outlier-sensitive and RMSE more robust, so use MAE for stockouts.
RMSE squares large errors (outlier-sensitive), fit for costly-big-error cases like stockouts; MAE is equal-weight and more interpretable.
Both have identical outlier sensitivity, differing only in units.
RMSE is only for classification and MAE only for regression; never mix.
optionExplanations: 敏感度说反了：平方的 RMSE 才对离群敏感，缺货应选 RMSE。
对；平方放大让 RMSE 惩罚大误差，正契合缺货代价高；要可解释均值则 MAE。
平方 vs 线性决定了敏感度不同，并非仅单位差异。
两者都是回归指标，不存在分类专用之说。
optionExplanations_en: Sensitivity is reversed: squared RMSE is the outlier-sensitive one, so stockouts want RMSE.
Correct — squaring makes RMSE punish big errors, fitting costly stockouts; use MAE for an interpretable mean.
Squared vs linear gives different sensitivity, not merely a unit difference.
Both are regression metrics; neither is classification-only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 均方根误差：误差平方求平均再开根，大误差被放大，对离群点敏感。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) is the root of mean squared errors; large errors dominate, making it outlier-sensitive.

scenario: 你想跨不同量级的产品比较预测误差——有的日销 5 件、有的日销 5000 件，绝对误差不可比。
scenario_en: You want to compare forecast errors across products of very different magnitudes — some sell 5/day, some 5000/day — where absolute error isn't comparable.
q: MAPE 解决了什么、又在什么情况下崩掉？
q_en: What does MAPE solve, and when does it break down?
why: MAPE（平均绝对百分比误差）是尺度无关的，能跨不同量级产品比较——用相对百分比而非绝对量。但真值接近 0 时，除以极小分母会让百分比爆炸/无意义，这是它的崩溃点。
why_en: MAPE is scale-independent so you can compare across product magnitudes via relative percentages, but it breaks down when true values approach zero because dividing by a tiny denominator explodes.
options: 解决离群点敏感问题，但在数据量太大时崩掉
尺度无关、可跨量级比较，但真值接近 0 时百分比爆炸而崩掉
解决类别不平衡，但在回归任务上无法使用
让误差与目标同单位，但在跨产品比较时失效
options_en: Solves outlier sensitivity but breaks down with very large data.
Scale-independent for cross-magnitude comparison, but breaks when true values approach zero and the percentage explodes.
Solves class imbalance but can't be used on regression.
Makes error same-unit as target but fails for cross-product comparison.
optionExplanations: MAPE 不是为离群设计，也不因数据量大而崩，崩点是真值近 0。
对；尺度无关是它的价值，真值近 0 的除法爆炸是它的软肋。
类别不平衡是分类问题，MAPE 是回归指标，张冠李戴。
同单位是 MAE 的性质；MAPE 恰恰是无量纲百分比、正为跨产品比较而生。
optionExplanations_en: MAPE isn't for outliers and doesn't break on large data; its break point is near-zero truth.
Correct — scale-independence is its value, and division blow-up near zero is its weakness.
Class imbalance is a classification issue; MAPE is a regression metric — a mix-up.
Same-unit is MAE's property; MAPE is a unitless percentage built precisely for cross-product comparison.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均绝对百分比误差：误差占真值的百分比的平均，尺度无关但真值近 0 时失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) averages the error as a percentage of the true value — scale-independent but breaks near zero.

scenario: 文本摘要任务：要离线评估生成的摘要是否覆盖了参考摘要里的关键信息。
scenario_en: Text summarization: offline-evaluate whether a generated summary covers the key info in the reference summary.
q: 摘要任务的主流自动指标是哪个？它的侧重点是什么？
q_en: Which automated metric dominates summarization, and what does it emphasize?
why: 用 ROUGE：它是召回导向的 n-gram 重叠，衡量「参考摘要里的关键词/短语被生成摘要覆盖了多少」，正契合摘要「别漏掉要点」的诉求，是摘要领域的主流。机器翻译更常用偏精确的 BLEU。
why_en: Use ROUGE — recall-oriented n-gram overlap measuring how much of the reference's key content the summary covers, fitting summarization's 'don't miss the point', and it dominates the field.
tradeoff: ROUGE（召回导向、适合摘要覆盖） vs BLEU（精确导向、适合机器翻译）
whenOtherWins: 若任务是机器翻译、更在意「生成的词有多少确实该出现」（精确度），BLEU 比 ROUGE 更常用。
options: BLEU：精确导向 n-gram 重叠，摘要首选
ROUGE：召回导向 n-gram 重叠，衡量关键信息覆盖，摘要主流
BERTScore：唯一能用于摘要的指标，其余都不行
log loss：摘要作为分类任务用交叉熵评
options_en: BLEU: precision-oriented n-gram overlap, first choice for summarization.
ROUGE: recall-oriented n-gram overlap measuring key-info coverage — dominant in summarization.
BERTScore: the only metric usable for summarization; none other works.
Log loss: treat summarization as classification and use cross-entropy.
optionExplanations: BLEU 偏精确、主用于机器翻译；摘要更看覆盖，用 ROUGE。
对；召回导向让 ROUGE 契合摘要「覆盖要点」的目标，是该领域主流。
BERTScore 也可用，但说它是唯一可用是错的；摘要主流仍是 ROUGE。
摘要是生成任务不是分类，log loss 不适用。
optionExplanations_en: BLEU is precision-oriented and mainly for MT; summarization values coverage, so ROUGE.
Correct — recall-orientation makes ROUGE fit summarization's coverage goal and dominate the field.
BERTScore is also usable, but calling it the only option is wrong; ROUGE still dominates summaries.
Summarization is generation not classification, so log loss doesn't apply.

termDefinitions.meaning: 召回导向的 n-gram 重叠指标，衡量生成文本覆盖了参考里多少内容，摘要主流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ROUGE is recall-oriented n-gram overlap measuring how much of the reference the output covers — dominant in summarization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成文本与参考文本共享的连续 n 个词片段比例，是 BLEU/ROUGE 的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: N-gram overlap is the share of contiguous n-word chunks common to output and reference — the basis of BLEU/ROUGE.

scenario: 生成的句子和参考句意思一致但用了同义改写（'quick brown fox' vs 'fast brown fox'），你要评它质量。
scenario_en: A generated sentence matches the reference in meaning but paraphrases it ('quick brown fox' vs 'fast brown fox'); you must score its quality.
q: BLEU/ROUGE 与 BERTScore 在处理同义改写上有何本质差异？
q_en: What's the essential difference between BLEU/ROUGE and BERTScore on paraphrases?
why: BLEU/ROUGE 靠字面 n-gram 重叠，同义改写（quick↔fast）没有字面重叠就被判低分，抓不到语义。BERTScore 用上下文嵌入算语义相似度，能识别 quick 与 fast 意思相近，捕捉 BLEU/ROUGE 漏掉的改写，越来越用于 LLM 输出评估。
why_en: BLEU/ROUGE rely on surface n-gram overlap and penalize paraphrases with no literal match, while BERTScore uses contextual embeddings to measure semantic similarity and catches paraphrases they miss.
tradeoff: BLEU/ROUGE（字面重叠、快但漏语义） vs BERTScore（语义相似、抓改写但更重）
options: 三者都靠字面重叠，BERTScore 只是算得更快
BLEU/ROUGE 字面重叠、漏同义改写；BERTScore 用嵌入算语义、能抓改写
BERTScore 靠字面重叠、BLEU 靠语义，恰好相反
三者都能完美评估语义，差别只在计算成本
options_en: All rely on surface overlap; BERTScore is just faster.
BLEU/ROUGE use surface overlap and miss paraphrases; BERTScore uses embeddings for semantics and catches paraphrases.
BERTScore uses surface overlap and BLEU uses semantics — the opposite.
All perfectly capture semantics, differing only in compute cost.
optionExplanations: BERTScore 不是字面重叠，它用嵌入算语义，机制本质不同。
对；字面 vs 语义是关键差异，BERTScore 因此能捕捉 BLEU/ROUGE 漏掉的改写。
说反了：BLEU 是字面 n-gram、BERTScore 才是语义嵌入。
BLEU/ROUGE 恰恰抓不到语义改写，不是「都完美」。
optionExplanations_en: BERTScore isn't surface overlap; it uses embeddings for semantics — a fundamentally different mechanism.
Correct — surface vs semantic is the key difference, letting BERTScore catch paraphrases BLEU/ROUGE miss.
Backwards: BLEU is surface n-gram, BERTScore is semantic embedding.
BLEU/ROUGE precisely fail on semantic paraphrase, so not 'all perfect'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精确导向的 n-gram 重叠指标，机器翻译标准，被批评忽略语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is precision-oriented n-gram overlap, standard for MT, criticized for ignoring meaning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上下文嵌入计算生成与参考的语义相似度，能识别同义改写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BERTScore uses contextual embeddings to measure semantic similarity between output and reference, catching paraphrases.

scenario: 开放式聊天机器人/创意写作，自动指标（BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore）与人类判断相关性都很差。
scenario_en: Open-ended chatbots/creative writing where automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore) correlate poorly with human judgment.
q: 这种开放式生成任务，评估的黄金标准是什么？自动指标的定位是什么？
q_en: For open-ended generation, what's the gold-standard evaluation, and how should automated metrics be framed?
why: 黄金标准是人类评估：开放式生成没有单一参考答案，自动指标与人类判断脱节。面试里应承认自动指标只是 proxy，把人类评估作为校准机制——用人评定期校准自动指标是否还可信。
why_en: The gold standard is human evaluation — open-ended generation has no single reference and automated metrics decorrelate — so frame automated metrics as proxies and use human eval to calibrate them.
tradeoff: 人类评估（黄金标准、贵而慢） vs 自动指标（快但对开放式生成是弱 proxy）
whenOtherWins: 若任务有明确单一参考、答案空间窄（如受限模板生成、机器翻译），自动指标够用，不必每次都上人评。
options: BLEU：开放式生成也能用 n-gram 重叠精确评估
人类评估是黄金标准；自动指标只是 proxy，用人评校准
log loss：把生成当分类问题逐 token 评即可
MAPE：用百分比误差衡量生成质量最稳妥
options_en: BLEU: open-ended generation can be precisely scored by n-gram overlap too.
Human evaluation is the gold standard; automated metrics are proxies to be calibrated by human eval.
Log loss: treat generation as classification and score per-token.
MAPE: percentage error most reliably measures generation quality.
optionExplanations: 开放式生成没有单一参考，BLEU 的字面重叠与人类判断脱节。
对；人评是黄金标准，自动指标当 proxy 并靠人评校准，是面试该说的定位。
逐 token log loss 测的是语言模型拟合，不等于开放式生成质量。
MAPE 是回归百分比误差，与文本生成质量无关。
optionExplanations_en: Open-ended generation has no single reference, so BLEU's surface overlap decorrelates from human judgment.
Correct — human eval is the gold standard, with automated metrics as proxies calibrated by it — the framing to state.
Per-token log loss measures language-model fit, not open-ended generation quality.
MAPE is regression percentage error, unrelated to text-generation quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由人对开放式生成质量打分/比较，是自动指标失效场景的黄金标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Human evaluation is people scoring/comparing open-ended generation quality — the gold standard where automated metrics fail.

scenario: 一个模型对一批样本预测「0.7 概率是欺诈」，下游要把这 0.7 当真实概率去算期望损失。
scenario_en: A model predicts '0.7 probability of fraud' for a batch, and downstream treats 0.7 as the true probability to compute expected loss.
q: 「模型校准良好」具体指什么？什么时候校准才重要？
q_en: What exactly does 'well-calibrated' mean, and when does calibration matter?
why: 校准良好 = 预测概率与观测频率一致：所有被预测为 0.7 的样本里，实际约 70% 真的是正例。只要下游把概率当真值字面消费（出价、期望损失、拦截阈值），校准就重要；若只用排序、不看概率数值，则不重要。
why_en: Well-calibrated means predicted probabilities match observed frequencies — among items predicted 0.7, about 70% are truly positive — and it matters whenever probabilities are consumed literally.
options: 指模型排序能力强，AUC 高就等于校准好
指预测概率与观测频率一致（预测 0.7→约 70% 真为正）；概率被字面消费时才重要
指模型对所有样本都输出同一个概率，方差为 0
指训练 loss 收敛到 0，训练充分即校准好
options_en: It means strong ranking ability; high AUC equals well-calibrated.
It means predicted probabilities match observed frequencies (0.7 → ~70% truly positive); matters when probabilities are consumed literally.
It means the model outputs the same probability for all samples, with zero variance.
It means training loss converged to 0; enough training equals calibrated.
optionExplanations: AUC 只管排序，校准好坏与 AUC 高低可以完全脱钩。
对；校准是概率与频率对齐，只有下游消费概率数值时才关键。
同一概率不是校准，是退化的常数预测。
训练 loss 收敛不保证概率刻度准，校准是另一回事。
optionExplanations_en: AUC only concerns ranking and can fully decouple from calibration.
Correct — calibration aligns probability with frequency, crucial only when downstream consumes probability values.
One constant probability isn't calibration; it's a degenerate constant prediction.
Converged training loss doesn't guarantee an accurate probability scale — calibration is separate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率 p 的样本里，真实正例比例约等于 p，概率可被当真值使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Well-calibrated means among items predicted probability p, about p of them are truly positive, so the probability is usable as truth.

scenario: 广告排序用预测 CTR × 出价算期望营收来竞价；若预测 CTR 系统性偏高，就会过度出价、亏钱。
scenario_en: Ad ranking bids using predicted CTR × bid to compute expected revenue; if predicted CTR is systematically too high, you overbid and lose money.
q: 对广告出价系统，除了 AUC 这类排序指标，为什么必须检查校准？
q_en: For an ad-bidding system, why must you check calibration beyond ranking metrics like AUC?
why: 出价把预测 CTR 当真实概率乘进期望营收，概率数值直接决定钱。AUC 只保证「谁比谁点击率高」的排序，保证不了「0.7 就真是 70%」；若系统性高估，AUC 再好也会过度出价亏钱。所以必须在主指标之外查校准（Brier/可靠性图）。
why_en: Bidding multiplies predicted CTR into expected revenue, so the probability value directly sets the money; AUC only guarantees ranking, not that 0.7 means 70%, so overconfidence overbids and loses money.
tradeoff: 只看 AUC（保排序、不保概率刻度） vs 加查校准（保 0.7≈70%，出价才不亏）
whenOtherWins: 若系统只按预测分数排序展示、从不把概率乘进金额或阈值决策，那么排序指标就够，校准不是必需。
options: 不必查校准，AUC 高就代表出价正确
出价把 CTR 当真值乘进营收，AUC 只保排序不保概率刻度；系统性高估会过度出价亏钱
只需查 recall，保证召回足够广告候选即可避免亏钱
校准只对图像任务有意义，广告 CTR 无关
options_en: No need to check calibration; high AUC means correct bids.
Bidding multiplies CTR into revenue; AUC only guarantees ranking not the probability scale, so systematic overestimation overbids and loses money.
Just check recall — enough ad candidates recalled avoids losing money.
Calibration only matters for image tasks, irrelevant to ad CTR.
optionExplanations: AUC 高但概率系统性偏高照样过度出价，排序对≠概率准。
对；钱由概率数值决定，必须在 AUC 之外查校准才不会系统性亏钱。
recall 是覆盖指标，与「概率数值准不准导致的出价对错」无关。
校准对任何消费概率的系统都重要，广告 CTR 正是典型。
optionExplanations_en: High AUC with systematically inflated probabilities still overbids; correct ranking isn't accurate probability.
Correct — money is set by the probability value, so you must check calibration beyond AUC to avoid systematic losses.
Recall is a coverage metric, unrelated to bid correctness driven by probability accuracy.
Calibration matters for any probability-consuming system; ad CTR is the textbook case.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测点击率乘以出价（及价值），概率偏差会直接放大成金钱损益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expected revenue is predicted CTR times bid/value; probability bias scales directly into monetary gain or loss.

scenario: 模型在漂移后的数据上重训，AUC 依旧稳定，但预测概率系统性偏离真实频率。
scenario_en: A model retrained on shifted data keeps a stable AUC, but its predicted probabilities systematically drift from true frequencies.
q: 为什么 AUC 稳定不代表校准没问题？该怎么做？
q_en: Why does a stable AUC not mean calibration is fine, and what should you do?
why: AUC 只看相对排序——把所有概率同比例拉高，排序不变、AUC 不变，但每个概率都错了。数据漂移后重训的模型常「排得对但概率偏」。所以要在主指标旁边同时查校准（Brier score、可靠性图），不能只盯 AUC。
why_en: AUC only measures relative ranking, so uniformly inflating probabilities leaves ranking (and AUC) unchanged while every probability is wrong; check calibration (Brier, reliability diagram) alongside the primary metric.
options: AUC 稳定就一定校准好，无需额外检查
AUC 只看排序，概率同比例偏移排序不变；须在 AUC 旁并行查校准（Brier/可靠性图）
校准问题只能靠提高 AUC 解决，两者是同一件事
只要重训就自动校准，漂移不影响概率刻度
options_en: A stable AUC guarantees good calibration; no extra checks needed.
AUC only measures ranking; a uniform probability shift leaves ranking unchanged, so check calibration (Brier/reliability) alongside AUC.
Calibration issues are fixed only by raising AUC; they're the same thing.
Retraining auto-calibrates; drift doesn't affect the probability scale.
optionExplanations: 排序不变而概率偏移正是 AUC 看不出的盲区，稳定 AUC 不保校准。
对；AUC 与校准可脱钩，必须并行监控校准才抓得到概率漂移。
校准与 AUC 是两个独立维度，不能靠提 AUC 解决。
漂移恰恰会破坏概率刻度，重训不自动修复校准。
optionExplanations_en: Unchanged ranking with shifted probabilities is exactly AUC's blind spot; stable AUC doesn't ensure calibration.
Correct — AUC and calibration decouple, so monitor calibration in parallel to catch probability drift.
Calibration and AUC are independent dimensions; raising AUC won't fix calibration.
Drift precisely corrupts the probability scale; retraining doesn't auto-fix calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预测概率与二元结果差的平方的均值，越低越好，衡量校准与准确度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Brier score is the mean squared difference between predicted probabilities and binary outcomes; lower is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把预测概率分桶、画各桶预测值 vs 实际频率；校准好的曲线贴对角线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reliability diagram bins predicted probabilities and plots predicted vs observed frequency; a well-calibrated curve hugs the diagonal.

scenario: 你要量化一个概率分类器的校准好坏，并直观看出它在哪些概率区间偏乐观/偏悲观。
scenario_en: You need to quantify a probabilistic classifier's calibration and see visually where it's over/under-confident.
q: Brier score 和可靠性图分别提供什么？
q_en: What do the Brier score and the reliability diagram each provide?
why: Brier score 给一个标量：预测概率与二元结果差的平方均值，越低越好，便于比较。可靠性图给一张图：把预测概率分桶，画每桶「预测均值 vs 实际频率」，贴对角线=校准良好，偏离处能看出在哪个区间过/欠自信。一个量化、一个诊断。
why_en: The Brier score gives a scalar (mean squared difference between probabilities and outcomes, lower better) for comparison, while the reliability diagram plots binned predicted-vs-observed frequency to diagnose where the model is over/under-confident.
options: 两者都只给标量分数，无法定位偏差区间
Brier 给标量（越低越好）便于比较；可靠性图分桶画预测 vs 实际，定位过/欠自信区间
Brier 是一张图、可靠性图是一个数，恰好相反
两者都衡量排序能力，与概率刻度无关
options_en: Both give only scalar scores and can't localize the bias region.
Brier gives a scalar (lower better) for comparison; the reliability diagram bins predicted-vs-observed to localize over/under-confidence.
Brier is a plot and the reliability diagram is a number — the opposite.
Both measure ranking ability, unrelated to the probability scale.
optionExplanations: 可靠性图恰恰能定位区间，不是只有标量。
对；Brier 量化、可靠性图诊断，一个便于比较、一个便于看哪里偏。
说反了：Brier 是数、可靠性图是图。
两者衡量校准/概率质量，不是排序能力。
optionExplanations_en: The reliability diagram does localize regions; it's not only a scalar.
Correct — Brier quantifies and the reliability diagram diagnoses: one for comparison, one for seeing where it drifts.
Backwards: Brier is a number, the reliability diagram is a plot.
Both measure calibration/probability quality, not ranking ability.

termDefinitions.meaning: Brier score（标量）与可靠性图（分桶曲线）配合，量化并定位概率偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration diagnostics pair the Brier score (scalar) with the reliability diagram (binned curve) to quantify and localize probability bias.

scenario: 把四类任务的默认离线指标记成一张速查表。
scenario_en: Memorize the default offline metric per task family as a cheat sheet.
q: 补全「任务类型 → 默认离线指标」的速查映射：
q_en: Complete the task-type to default-metric cheat sheet:
text: 分类不平衡→{{AUC-PR}}；搜索排序→{{NDCG}}；检索/候选生成→{{Recall@K}}；ETA/回归可解释→{{MAE}}；摘要→{{ROUGE}}；开放式生成→{{人类评估}}。
text_en: Imbalanced classification → {{AUC-PR}}; search ranking → {{NDCG}}; retrieval/candidate-gen → {{Recall@K}}; interpretable regression/ETA → {{MAE}}; summarization → {{ROUGE}}; open-ended generation → {{human evaluation}}.
why: 记住任务→指标的默认映射，面试里能秒选起点，再按数据分布/业务目标微调（如概率被消费加 log loss/校准、离群贵改 RMSE）。这是本课的核心速查。
why_en: Memorize the task-to-metric defaults so you can pick a starting point instantly, then adjust by distribution/objective (log loss/calibration when probabilities are consumed, RMSE when outliers are costly).

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类、排序/检索、回归、生成四大类，外加横切的校准，各有默认指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The task families are classification, ranking/retrieval, regression, and generation, plus cross-cutting calibration, each with default metrics.

q: 把「为一个新模型选离线指标」的推理步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the reasoning steps for choosing an offline metric for a new model:
steps: 识别任务类型（分类/排序/回归/生成）
看数据分布（是否严重不平衡）和下游是否消费概率
据此定主指标（如不平衡分类→AUC-PR、消费概率→加 log loss）
若下游把概率当真值，额外并行检查校准（Brier/可靠性图）
why: 先定任务类型缩小指标族，再看数据分布与是否消费概率，据此选主指标，最后在概率被消费时并行查校准。顺序错了（如没看分布就选 AUC）就会踩不平衡虚高的坑。
why_en: Identify the task family, then check distribution and whether probabilities are consumed, pick the primary metric accordingly, and add a calibration check when probabilities are consumed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 驱动离线选型决策的核心指标，按任务类型与数据分布确定，可配校准等辅助检查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary metric drives the offline selection decision, chosen by task type and distribution, with auxiliary checks like calibration.

scenario: 内容审核分类，正负类大致均衡，你想要一个阈值无关、便于跨模型比较判别力的指标。
scenario_en: Content-moderation classification with roughly balanced classes; you want a threshold-agnostic metric to compare discrimination across models.
q: 类别均衡、要阈值无关地比判别力，选哪个分类指标？
q_en: For balanced classes and threshold-agnostic discrimination comparison, which classification metric?
why: 用 AUC-ROC：类别均衡时它不被 TN 稀释的问题不突出，且阈值无关、能跨模型比较整体判别力，正契合内容审核这类均衡场景。若类别严重不平衡（欺诈/垃圾），才换 AUC-PR。
why_en: Use AUC-ROC — with balanced classes its TN-dilution issue is minor, and being threshold-agnostic it compares overall discrimination across models, fitting content moderation.
tradeoff: AUC-ROC（阈值无关、均衡场景比判别力） vs AUC-PR（严重不平衡时聚焦稀有正例）
whenOtherWins: 若正例极稀有（欺诈<1%、垃圾邮件），AUC-ROC 会被海量 TN 抬高虚假乐观，此时 AUC-PR 更合适。
options: F1：绑定单一阈值就能比较判别力
AUC-ROC：阈值无关、均衡类别下跨模型比整体判别力
MAE：用绝对误差衡量分类质量
Recall@K：看 top-K 覆盖率评判别力
options_en: F1: bind one threshold to compare discrimination.
AUC-ROC: threshold-agnostic, comparing overall discrimination across models under balanced classes.
MAE: use absolute error to measure classification quality.
Recall@K: judge discrimination via top-K coverage.
optionExplanations: F1 绑定阈值，换阈值就变，不是阈值无关的跨模型判别力比较。
对；均衡+阈值无关正是 AUC-ROC 的主场，内容审核常用它。
MAE 是回归误差，不评分类判别力。
Recall@K 是检索覆盖指标，不衡量分类判别力。
optionExplanations_en: F1 is threshold-bound and shifts with threshold — not threshold-agnostic cross-model comparison.
Correct — balanced plus threshold-agnostic is AUC-ROC's home turf, common in content moderation.
MAE is regression error, not classification discrimination.
Recall@K is a retrieval coverage metric, not classification discrimination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标不依赖某个决策阈值，衡量所有阈值上的整体表现，便于跨模型比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Threshold-agnostic means the metric doesn't depend on one decision threshold, measuring performance across all thresholds for cross-model comparison.

scenario: 为生成类任务挑自动指标时，要清楚每个指标的取向与盲区。
scenario_en: When choosing automated metrics for generation, know each metric's orientation and blind spots.
q: 关于生成类评估指标，以下哪些说法正确？(多选)
q_en: Which statements about generation-evaluation metrics are correct? (multiple)
why: BLEU 精确导向、机器翻译标准、被批忽略语义；ROUGE 召回导向、摘要主流；BERTScore 用上下文嵌入算语义、能抓同义改写。三者都是自动 proxy；开放式生成的黄金标准仍是人类评估。BERTScore 并非「无需参考文本」——它仍要和参考比。
why_en: BLEU is precision-oriented MT-standard criticized for ignoring meaning, ROUGE is recall-oriented for summaries, BERTScore uses embeddings to catch paraphrases; all are proxies and human eval remains the gold standard for open-ended.
options: BLEU 精确导向、机器翻译标准，被批评忽略语义
ROUGE 召回导向，摘要任务主流
BERTScore 用上下文嵌入算语义相似度，能抓 BLEU/ROUGE 漏掉的同义改写
BERTScore 无需任何参考文本即可评分，因此优于所有需要参考的指标
options_en: BLEU is precision-oriented and the MT standard, criticized for ignoring meaning.
ROUGE is recall-oriented and dominant in summarization.
BERTScore uses contextual embeddings for semantic similarity, catching paraphrases BLEU/ROUGE miss.
BERTScore needs no reference text to score, making it superior to all reference-based metrics.
optionExplanations: 对；BLEU 偏精确、MT 标准、忽略语义是其著名短板。
对；召回导向让 ROUGE 契合摘要覆盖，是该领域主流。
对；语义嵌入让 BERTScore 捕捉字面漏掉的改写。
错；BERTScore 仍需与参考比较，并非无参考评分，此说法是杜撰。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — BLEU is precision-oriented, MT-standard, and famously ignores meaning.
Correct — recall-orientation makes ROUGE fit summarization coverage and dominate the field.
Correct — semantic embeddings let BERTScore catch paraphrases surface metrics miss.
Wrong — BERTScore still compares against a reference; 'reference-free' is fabricated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器翻译，把一种语言自动译成另一种，BLEU 是其标准评估指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MT (Machine Translation) automatically translates between languages; BLEU is its standard evaluation metric.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工写的标准答案，BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore 都拿生成结果与它比较。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference text is a human-written gold answer that BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore compare the output against.

scenario: 应用商店首页固定只有 5 个推荐槽位，UI 就展示这 5 个，你要评这固定窗口内的推荐质量。
scenario_en: An app-store home page has exactly 5 recommendation slots showing those 5; you evaluate quality within that fixed window.
q: 固定 UI 槽位（top-5 展示）该用哪个指标？和 Recall@K 有何区别？
q_en: For fixed UI slots (top-5 shown), which metric, and how does it differ from Recall@K?
why: 用 Precision@5：固定只展示 5 个，关键是这 5 个里有多少相关（精度），而不是「有没有把所有相关都捞进来」（那是 Recall@K，检索阶段的目标）。UI 槽位固定 → 分母固定 → Precision@K 最贴。
why_en: Use Precision@5 — with only 5 fixed slots, what matters is how many of those 5 are relevant (precision), not whether all relevants were captured (Recall@K, the retrieval goal).
tradeoff: Precision@K（固定窗口内的精度、展示阶段） vs Recall@K（整体覆盖率、检索阶段）
whenOtherWins: 若你在检索/候选生成阶段、关心「有没有漏掉相关物品」而非前几名精度，就该用 Recall@K 而非 Precision@K。
options: Recall@5：看是否把所有相关物品都捞进这 5 个
Precision@5：看固定展示的 5 个里相关比例，契合固定 UI 槽位
MRR：只看第一个相关结果位置
log loss：评这 5 个的概率校准
options_en: Recall@5: whether all relevant items were captured into these 5.
Precision@5: the relevant fraction among the fixed 5 shown, fitting fixed UI slots.
MRR: only the first relevant result's position.
Log loss: assess the probability calibration of these 5.
optionExplanations: 把所有相关都塞进 5 个既不现实也非目标，覆盖率是检索阶段的事。
对；固定槽位下 Precision@K 直接问「展示的这几个有多少相关」，最贴合。
MRR 只关心第一个，浪费了固定 5 槽的其余信息。
log loss 评概率质量，不衡量固定窗口内的推荐精度。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming all relevants into 5 is neither realistic nor the goal; coverage is retrieval's job.
Correct — with fixed slots, Precision@K directly asks how many shown items are relevant — the best fit.
MRR only cares about the first, wasting the other fixed slots' information.
Log loss assesses probability quality, not recommendation precision in a fixed window.

termDefinitions.meaning: Precision@K = top-K 中相关的比例（展示精度）；Recall@K = 全部相关中被 top-K 覆盖的比例（检索覆盖）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@K is the relevant fraction within top-K (display precision); Recall@K is the fraction of all relevants captured in top-K (retrieval coverage).

scenario: 一个新排序模型离线 NDCG 涨了 2%，团队想据此直接上线。
scenario_en: A new ranker's offline NDCG rose 2%, and the team wants to ship on that alone.
q: 为什么离线指标过关后还必须做 A/B 测试才能上线？
q_en: Why must an A/B test still gate a launch after offline metrics pass?
why: 离线指标是 proxy：2% 的 NDCG 提升可能根本不改变用户行为，甚至反而变差（位置偏置、上下文缺失）。A/B 是上线前的最后一道门，用真实流量验证「离线增益是否真变成业务 KPI 提升」。Google/Meta/Netflix/Uber 都以它为终审。
why_en: Offline metrics are proxies — a 2% NDCG gain may not move behavior or may even degrade it — so an A/B test is the final gate that verifies the offline gain becomes a real business-KPI lift on live traffic.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  O["离线指标(proxy)\nNDCG/AUC/log loss"] --> A["A/B 测试\n真实流量最终门"]
  A -->|KPI 真提升| S["上线"]
  A -->|无提升/退化| R["拒绝"]
options: 不必：离线 NDCG 涨了就代表业务一定提升，可跳过 A/B
离线是 proxy，2% 增益可能不改变行为甚至变差；A/B 用真实流量验证 KPI 是否真提升
A/B 只是走流程，实际决策仍看离线指标
因为 A/B 能替代离线评估，有它就不用再算离线指标
options_en: No need: an offline NDCG rise means business will surely improve, so skip A/B.
Offline is a proxy — a 2% gain may not change behavior or may worsen it — so A/B verifies real KPI lift on live traffic.
A/B is just a formality; the real decision still relies on offline metrics.
Because A/B replaces offline evaluation, so you no longer need offline metrics.
optionExplanations: 把离线 proxy 当业务保证正是本课要破的误区，2% NDCG 未必转化。
对；A/B 是最终门，验证离线增益是否变成真实 KPI 提升，避免上线翻车。
A/B 不是走过场，它给的是离线给不了的 ground truth。
两相互补而非替代：离线负责海选、A/B 负责终审。
optionExplanations_en: Treating an offline proxy as a business guarantee is the fallacy to break; 2% NDCG may not translate.
Correct — A/B is the final gate verifying the offline gain becomes a real KPI lift, preventing bad launches.
A/B isn't a formality; it provides ground truth offline can't.
They're complementary, not substitutes: offline screens, A/B does final judgment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户随机分成对照/实验组、比较业务指标的在线受控实验，是上线前最终门。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test randomly splits users into control/treatment groups to compare business metrics — the final pre-launch gate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关键绩效指标，衡量业务成功的核心数字（CTR、营收/会话、预订率）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is the core business-success number (CTR, revenue/session, booking rate).

scenario: 开始一个 A/B 前，要先写下一个可证伪的假设，而不是「看看新模型好不好」。
scenario_en: Before an A/B, write a falsifiable hypothesis, not 'let's see if the new model is good'.
q: 一个合格的 A/B 假设由哪三部分组成？
q_en: What three parts make a proper A/B hypothesis?
why: 可证伪的假设 = 具体改动 + 预期指标 + 阈值，例如「把 YouTube 推荐的 pointwise 排序器换成 listwise 排序器，会让每次会话平均观看时长提升 ≥1%」。三要素齐全才能事前判定成败、不是事后找说法。
why_en: A falsifiable hypothesis is a concrete change + an expected metric + a threshold, e.g. 'replacing the pointwise ranker with a listwise ranker will raise avg watch time/session by ≥1%'.
options: 改动 + 预期指标 + 阈值（如「换 listwise 排序器 → 观看时长 ≥+1%」）
只要一句「新模型应该更好」即可，指标和阈值上线后再补
预算 + 团队人数 + 截止日期
模型架构 + 超参数 + 训练数据量
options_en: A change + an expected metric + a threshold (e.g. 'switch to listwise ranker → watch time ≥ +1%').
Just 'the new model should be better'; add metric and threshold after launch.
Budget + team size + deadline.
Model architecture + hyperparameters + training-data size.
optionExplanations: 对；改动+指标+阈值让假设可证伪、可事前判定成败。
没有指标和阈值就无法证伪，等于事后随便解释，不合格。
预算/人数/日期是项目管理要素，不是实验假设。
架构/超参是实现细节，不构成可证伪的业务假设。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — change + metric + threshold makes the hypothesis falsifiable and decidable in advance.
Without a metric and threshold it can't be falsified — just post-hoc rationalization, unacceptable.
Budget/headcount/dates are project management, not an experiment hypothesis.
Architecture/hyperparameters are implementation details, not a falsifiable business hypothesis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事前写死「改动→预期指标→阈值」，使实验结果能明确判成败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A falsifiable hypothesis fixes change → expected metric → threshold in advance so the result can be clearly judged.

scenario: Airbnb 测一个提升预订的排序改动：主指标是预订率，同时要盯页面加载时间和房东取消率。
scenario_en: Airbnb tests a ranking change to lift bookings: primary metric is booking rate, while watching page-load time and host cancellation rate.
q: primary metric 与 guardrail metric 有什么区别？各起什么作用？
q_en: What's the difference between a primary metric and a guardrail metric, and what does each do?
why: primary metric 是你想推动的直接目标（预订率/CTR/营收per会话）；guardrail metric 是不能被牺牲的安全约束——即使主指标涨了，只要护栏（延迟、崩溃率、房东取消率）恶化就否决。一个管「有没有变好」，一个管「有没有偷偷变坏」。
why_en: The primary metric is the direct target you want to move (booking rate/CTR/revenue), while guardrails are safety constraints that must not degrade — even a primary win is rejected if a guardrail worsens.
tradeoff: primary（推动的目标） vs guardrail（不可牺牲的安全底线）
options: 两者是同一回事，只是名字不同
primary 是想推动的直接目标；guardrail 是不能恶化的安全约束，恶化即否决
primary 只能有一个数值、guardrail 必须是文本描述
guardrail 是主指标，primary 只是参考背景
options_en: They're the same thing with different names.
The primary is the direct target to move; guardrails are safety constraints that must not degrade — degradation vetoes the launch.
The primary must be a single number and guardrails must be text descriptions.
The guardrail is the main metric; the primary is just background reference.
optionExplanations: 两者角色不同：一个是目标、一个是底线，不能混为一谈。
对；护栏的意义在于「即使主指标赢了，破坏了底线也不上」。
两者都是可量化指标，与「数值 vs 文本」无关。
说反了：primary 才是目标，guardrail 是约束。
optionExplanations_en: They play different roles: one is the goal, one is the floor — not interchangeable.
Correct — a guardrail means 'even if the primary wins, don't ship if the floor is broken'.
Both are quantifiable metrics; this isn't about number vs text.
Backwards: the primary is the goal, the guardrail is the constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实验想直接推动的业务目标（预订率、CTR、营收/会话）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The primary metric is the business target the experiment aims to move (booking rate, CTR, revenue/session).

termDefinitions.meaning: 不能被牺牲的安全约束（延迟、崩溃率、取消率），恶化即否决上线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a safety constraint (latency, crash rate, cancellation) that must not degrade — degradation vetoes launch.

scenario: 一个新推荐模型把点击率提升了 3%，但把 p99 服务延迟从 200ms 拉到 420ms（翻倍）。
scenario_en: A new rec model lifts CTR by 3% but doubles p99 serving latency from 200ms to 420ms.
q: 主指标（CTR）赢了，这个模型该上线吗？体现了什么设计原则？
q_en: The primary metric (CTR) won — should this model ship, and what principle does it show?
why: 不该上：延迟护栏被破坏（翻倍的 p99 会拖慢体验、可能违反 SLA）。这体现「护栏优先」——即使主指标涨了，只要系统健康或 UX 护栏恶化就否决。护栏就是为了挡住这种「赢了指标输了体验」的改动。
why_en: Don't ship — the latency guardrail is broken (doubled p99 hurts UX and may breach SLA); even a primary win is vetoed when a system-health/UX guardrail degrades.
tradeoff: 上线（+3% CTR） vs 否决（p99 延迟翻倍破坏系统健康护栏）
whenOtherWins: 若这类模型部署在离线批处理、延迟根本不进用户关键路径（如隔夜生成推荐），延迟护栏不再是硬约束，就可能放行。
options: 该上线：主指标 CTR 涨了 3%，延迟不重要
不该上：延迟护栏被破坏，护栏优先——主指标赢也否决
该上线，但把延迟阈值临时改高以让它通过
无法判断，A/B 只看主指标，护栏不参与上线决策
options_en: Ship it: the primary CTR rose 3%, latency doesn't matter.
Don't ship: the latency guardrail is broken; guardrails take priority, so a primary win is vetoed.
Ship it, but temporarily raise the latency threshold to let it pass.
Can't tell — A/B only looks at the primary; guardrails don't affect the launch decision.
optionExplanations: 延迟翻倍会伤体验、可能破 SLA，「延迟不重要」是危险误判。
对；护栏就是为挡这种赢指标输体验的改动，破护栏即否决。
为通过而临时放宽护栏是自欺欺人，等于取消了安全约束。
护栏恰恰是上线决策的一部分，忽略它会放行有害改动。
optionExplanations_en: Doubled latency hurts UX and may breach SLA; 'latency doesn't matter' is a dangerous misjudgment.
Correct — guardrails exist to block metric-wins-UX-loses changes; a broken guardrail vetoes.
Loosening the guardrail to pass is self-deception, effectively removing the safety constraint.
Guardrails are precisely part of the launch decision; ignoring them ships harmful changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求快于此值，衡量尾部延迟；翻倍意味着最慢那批用户体验显著变差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value 99% of requests beat — a tail-latency measure; doubling it markedly worsens the slowest users' experience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议，对延迟/可用性等的承诺阈值，护栏常对齐它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed threshold for latency/availability that guardrails often align to.

scenario: 你要为一个推荐模型 A/B 设计一套护栏指标，体现生产成熟度。
scenario_en: You're designing a guardrail set for a rec-model A/B to signal production maturity.
q: 一套成熟的护栏指标应包含哪些？(多选)
q_en: What should a mature guardrail set include? (multiple)
why: 建议至少 2 个护栏：一个 UX（崩溃率、取消率），一个系统健康（p99 服务延迟），可选再加一个业务护栏（广告营收/会话、司机收入）。多维度护栏才能挡住「主指标赢但从别处偷成本」的改动。护栏数量不是越少越好。
why_en: Define at least two guardrails — one UX (crash/cancellation rate), one system health (p99 latency) — plus optionally a business guardrail (ad revenue/session, driver earnings), to block changes that win the primary by stealing cost elsewhere.
options: 至少一个 UX 护栏，如崩溃率或取消率
至少一个系统健康护栏，如 p99 服务延迟
可选一个业务护栏，如广告营收/会话或司机收入
只保留主指标一个，护栏越少实验越干净
options_en: At least one UX guardrail, e.g. crash rate or cancellation rate.
At least one system-health guardrail, e.g. p99 serving latency.
Optionally one business guardrail, e.g. ad revenue/session or driver earnings.
Keep only the primary metric; fewer guardrails make a cleaner experiment.
optionExplanations: 对；UX 护栏挡住「指标涨但用户体验崩」的改动。
对；系统健康护栏挡住「指标涨但延迟/稳定性恶化」的改动。
对；业务护栏挡住「一个业务线赢但另一个业务线亏」的改动。
错；去掉护栏不是更干净，而是失去对副作用的防护，容易上线有害改动。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a UX guardrail blocks 'metric up but experience collapses' changes.
Correct — a system-health guardrail blocks 'metric up but latency/stability worsens' changes.
Correct — a business guardrail blocks 'one line wins while another loses' changes.
Wrong — dropping guardrails isn't cleaner; it removes side-effect protection and ships harmful changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: UX 护栏盯用户体验（崩溃/取消），系统健康护栏盯基础设施（延迟/错误率）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UX guardrail watches user experience (crash/cancellation); a system-health guardrail watches infrastructure (latency/error rate).

scenario: 实验设计里把统计功效(statistical power)设为 0.80。
scenario_en: The experiment design sets statistical power to 0.80.
q: 统计功效 0.80 是什么意思？它对应哪类错误？
q_en: What does statistical power 0.80 mean, and which error does it govern?
why: power=0.80 表示：若真有效应存在，有 80% 概率检测到它、20% 概率漏掉（Type II 错误/假阴性）。power 是给定的容错目标（不是公式算出来的），越高越不容易漏真效应，但需要更大样本。它约束的是「漏检真效应」的风险。
why_en: Power 0.80 means that if a real effect exists you have an 80% chance to detect it and a 20% chance to miss it (Type II error / false negative); higher power misses fewer real effects but needs more samples.
options: 80% 的实验结果一定正确，与错误类型无关
若真效应存在，有 80% 概率检出、20% 概率漏掉（Type II 错误）
有 80% 概率不犯假阳性（Type I 错误）
样本量正好是总流量的 80%
options_en: 80% of experiment results are certainly correct, regardless of error type.
If a real effect exists, an 80% chance to detect it and 20% to miss it (Type II error).
An 80% chance of avoiding a false positive (Type I error).
The sample size is exactly 80% of total traffic.
optionExplanations: power 不是「结果一定正确」，它专指检出真效应的能力。
对；power 管假阴性/Type II，0.80 即 20% 漏检风险。
假阳性由显著性 α 管，不是 power；两者是不同错误。
power 是概率目标，不是样本占流量的比例。
optionExplanations_en: Power isn't 'results are certainly correct'; it specifically measures ability to detect a real effect.
Correct — power governs false negatives/Type II; 0.80 means a 20% miss risk.
False positives are governed by significance alpha, not power; different errors.
Power is a probability target, not a fraction of traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 真效应存在时检测到它的概率，1−β；越高越不漏真效应，但要更大样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Statistical power is the probability of detecting a real effect when it exists (1−beta); higher misses fewer effects but needs more samples.

termDefinitions.term: Type II error / 第二类错误
termDefinitions.meaning: 真有效应却没检测出来（假阴性），概率为 β=1−power。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Type II error is failing to detect a real effect (false negative), with probability beta = 1 − power.

scenario: 实验里有两种可能出错：把没效应的改动误判成有效，或把真有效应的改动误判成无效。
scenario_en: Two ways an experiment errs: calling a no-effect change effective, or calling a real effect ineffective.
q: 显著性 α 和统计功效各控制哪一类错误？
q_en: Which error does significance alpha control versus statistical power?
why: 显著性 α 控制 Type I 错误（假阳性）——把没效应误判成有效的概率（如 α=0.05 即 5%）。power=1−β 控制 Type II 错误（假阴性）——把真效应漏掉的概率。降 α 更严防误报，但会提高漏检；两者此消彼长，靠加样本一起改善。
why_en: Significance alpha controls Type I error (false positive — calling a no-effect change effective, e.g. 5% at alpha=0.05); power controls Type II error (false negative — missing a real effect).
tradeoff: α↓（少假阳性但多假阴性） vs power↑（少假阴性但需更大样本）
options: α 控制假阴性、power 控制假阳性
α 控制 Type I 假阳性、power 控制 Type II 假阴性
两者都控制假阳性，只是数值不同
α 和 power 都与错误无关，只决定样本量
options_en: Alpha controls false negatives and power controls false positives.
Alpha controls Type I false positives; power controls Type II false negatives.
Both control false positives, differing only in value.
Alpha and power are unrelated to errors, only determining sample size.
optionExplanations: 对调了：α 管假阳性、power 管假阴性。
对；α→Type I 假阳性、power→Type II 假阴性，是实验设计的两根轴。
两者管不同错误，不是都管假阳性。
它们直接对应两类错误的容忍度，进而决定样本量。
optionExplanations_en: Swapped: alpha governs false positives, power governs false negatives.
Correct — alpha→Type I false positive, power→Type II false negative, the two axes of experiment design.
They govern different errors, not both false positives.
They map directly to the two error tolerances, which then set sample size.

termDefinitions.term: Type I error / 第一类错误
termDefinitions.meaning: 无真效应却判为有效（假阳性），概率为显著性水平 α。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Type I error is declaring an effect when there is none (false positive), with probability equal to significance level alpha.

termDefinitions.term: significance level α / 显著性水平
termDefinitions.meaning: 允许的假阳性概率上限（常 0.05），越小越难判显著。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The significance level alpha is the allowed false-positive probability (often 0.05); smaller makes significance harder to reach.

scenario: 团队争论 MDE 设多少：有人说按统计公式算，有人说 0.1% 的 CTR 提升根本不值得部署。
scenario_en: The team debates the MDE: some say derive it statistically, others say a 0.1% CTR lift isn't worth deploying.
q: 最小可检测效应(MDE)本质上是统计决策还是业务决策？
q_en: Is the minimum detectable effect (MDE) fundamentally a statistical or a business decision?
why: MDE 是业务决策：它是「小到什么程度就不值得部署」的门槛，由改动的收益与部署/维护成本决定，而非统计公式。例如设 MDE=0.5%，因为 0.1% 的 CTR 提升不值得上线的复杂度。定了 MDE 才反过来算样本量。
why_en: MDE is a business decision — the smallest improvement worth deploying, set by benefit-versus-cost, not a statistical formula — e.g. MDE=0.5% because a 0.1% CTR lift isn't worth the deployment complexity.
tradeoff: MDE 小（能测出微小效应但样本量暴涨） vs MDE 大（省样本但漏掉小而真的提升）
options: 统计决策：由显著性公式唯一确定，与业务无关
业务决策：小到不值得部署的门槛，由收益 vs 成本定，再据此算样本量
由日活用户数直接决定，用户越多 MDE 越小
等于观测到的效应量，实验跑完才知道
options_en: A statistical decision: uniquely fixed by the significance formula, unrelated to business.
A business decision: the threshold below which it's not worth deploying, set by benefit-vs-cost, then used to compute sample size.
Directly set by daily active users; more users means smaller MDE.
Equal to the observed effect size, known only after the experiment finishes.
optionExplanations: MDE 不由统计公式给出，它是你先定的业务门槛、再喂进公式。
对；MDE 是「值不值得部署」的业务判断，决定后才反算样本量。
日活影响样本量与运行时长，不决定 MDE 这个业务门槛。
MDE 是事前设定的目标，不是事后观测到的效应。
optionExplanations_en: MDE isn't given by a statistical formula; it's a business threshold you set first, then feed into the formula.
Correct — MDE is the 'worth deploying?' business call, set first, then sample size is derived.
DAU affects sample size and runtime, not the MDE business threshold.
MDE is a pre-set target, not the post-hoc observed effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最小可检测效应：值得部署的最小改进幅度，是业务门槛而非统计结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MDE (Minimum Detectable Effect) is the smallest improvement worth deploying — a business threshold, not a statistical output.

scenario: 用功效分析算 A/B 样本量：n ≈ (Z_α/2 + Z_β)² · 2σ² / MDE²。
scenario_en: Compute A/B sample size via power analysis: n ≈ (Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta)² · 2σ² / MDE².
q: 样本量随哪些量怎样变化？公式各项分别代表什么？
q_en: How does sample size scale, and what does each term mean?
why: 样本量在 MDE 缩小时暴涨（分母 MDE² → 想测更小效应，样本按平方增长）、在方差 σ² 升高时增大（数据越吵越要样本）、在期望功效升高时增大（Z_β 变大）。Z_α/2、Z_β 是由 α、power 决定的临界值。这决定了「要多久、多少流量」。
why_en: Sample size grows as MDE shrinks (n ∝ 1/MDE², so detecting smaller effects explodes samples), as variance σ² rises, and as desired power rises; Z terms come from alpha and power.
options: 样本量随 MDE 增大而增大、随方差减小而增大，方向都相反
样本量随 MDE 缩小（∝1/MDE²）、方差 σ² 升高、期望功效升高而增大
样本量只由日活决定，与 MDE 和方差无关
样本量随 MDE 缩小而线性下降，越精细越省样本
options_en: Sample size grows as MDE grows and as variance shrinks — both directions reversed.
Sample size grows as MDE shrinks (∝ 1/MDE²), as variance σ² rises, and as desired power rises.
Sample size is set only by DAU, unrelated to MDE and variance.
Sample size falls linearly as MDE shrinks; finer detection saves samples.
optionExplanations: 方向全错：MDE 越小样本越多、方差越大样本越多。
对；1/MDE² 的平方关系是关键——想测半个效应要四倍样本。
MDE 与方差恰恰是样本量的核心驱动，不能忽略。
反了：MDE 缩小让样本按平方暴涨，不是线性下降。
optionExplanations_en: All directions wrong: smaller MDE needs more samples, larger variance needs more.
Correct — the 1/MDE² square law is key: halving the detectable effect needs 4x samples.
MDE and variance are the core drivers of sample size, not ignorable.
Reversed: shrinking MDE explodes samples quadratically, not a linear drop.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 α、power、方差、MDE 反算所需样本量的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Power analysis derives the required sample size from alpha, power, variance, and MDE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指标的波动程度，数据越吵需要越大样本才能压过噪声看清效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Variance σ² is the metric's noisiness; noisier data needs larger samples to see the effect over noise.

scenario: 样本量算得每臂 25 万、共 50 万；日活 10 万，原始需要 5 天。
scenario_en: Sample size is 250K/arm (500K total); with 100K users/day the raw need is 5 days.
q: A/B 运行时长怎么算？为什么要向上取整到整周？
q_en: How do you compute A/B runtime, and why round up to full weeks?
why: 运行时长 = 样本量 / 日流量（这里 50 万 / 10 万 = 5 天），再向上取整到整周（跑 7 或 14 天）。取整到整周是因为工作日和周末用户行为不同，跑满整周才能覆盖完整的周内周期、避免只采到工作日样本带来的偏差。
why_en: Runtime = sample size / daily traffic (500K/100K = 5 days), rounded up to full weeks (7 or 14 days) because weekday and weekend behavior differ, so a full week avoids weekday-only sampling bias.
options: 运行时长 = 样本量 × 日流量，取整到整月即可
运行时长 = 样本量 / 日流量，向上取整到整周以覆盖工作日/周末差异
固定跑 24 小时，流量足够就够了，无需考虑周期
运行到 p 值第一次 <0.05 就停，越快越好
options_en: Runtime = sample size × daily traffic, rounded to full months.
Runtime = sample size / daily traffic, rounded up to full weeks to cover weekday/weekend differences.
Fixed at 24 hours; enough traffic suffices, no need for cycles.
Stop the moment p first drops below 0.05 — faster is better.
optionExplanations: 是除以日流量不是乘，取整到整周而非整月。
对；除法得原始天数，整周取整消除工作日/周末的周期偏差。
固定 24 小时会漏掉周内行为周期，采样有偏。
见 p<0.05 就停是 peeking，会抬高假阳性，正是要避免的。
optionExplanations_en: It's divided by daily traffic not multiplied, and rounded to weeks not months.
Correct — division gives raw days, and full-week rounding removes weekday/weekend cyclic bias.
A fixed 24 hours misses the weekly behavior cycle and biases sampling.
Stopping at p<0.05 is peeking, inflating false positives — exactly what to avoid.

termDefinitions.meaning: A/B 需跑多久 = 所需样本量 ÷ 日流量，取整到整周以覆盖周内周期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Runtime is how long the A/B runs = required sample size ÷ daily traffic, rounded to full weeks for the weekly cycle.

scenario: Instagram Reels 上线首周互动 +5%，到第三周衰减到 +1%。
scenario_en: Instagram Reels shows +5% engagement in week 1, decaying to +1% by week 3.
q: 这是什么效应？会怎样误导 A/B 结论？该怎么缓解？
q_en: What effect is this, how does it mislead A/B conclusions, and how to mitigate?
why: 这是新奇效应：用户只因内容「新」而短暂多互动，早期指标虚高，若此时下结论会高估真实长期效应。缓解：把实验跑 2-4 周，分析时间窗口趋势而非单一聚合值，等新奇消退看稳态水平。
why_en: This is the novelty effect — users engage more just because it's new, inflating early metrics — so decide too early and you overstate the long-term effect; mitigate by running 2-4 weeks and analyzing time-windowed trends.
options: 网络干扰：处理组泄漏到对照组，缓解靠聚类随机化
新奇效应：用户因内容新而短暂多互动，早期虚高；跑 2-4 周看时间窗口趋势
peeking：提前偷看结果，缓解靠预先锁定样本量
分布漂移：训练集代表不了线上，缓解靠重训模型
options_en: Network interference: treatment leaks into control; mitigate with cluster randomization.
Novelty effect: users engage more just because it's new, inflating early metrics; run 2-4 weeks and read time-windowed trends.
Peeking: sneaking early looks; mitigate by pre-committing the sample size.
Distribution shift: training set misrepresents live; mitigate by retraining.
optionExplanations: 泄漏是网络干扰，本例是「新鲜感消退」的时间性衰减，不是干扰。
对；新奇效应让早期虚高，跑够 2-4 周、看窗口趋势才见稳态。
peeking 是提前停实验的问题，本例是效应随时间自然衰减。
分布漂移是离线-在线问题，与「新鲜感消退」无关。
optionExplanations_en: Leakage is network interference; this is temporal decay of novelty, not interference.
Correct — novelty inflates early metrics; run 2-4 weeks and read windowed trends to see steady state.
Peeking is stopping early; here the effect naturally decays over time.
Distribution shift is an offline-online issue, unrelated to novelty fading.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户仅因内容新而短暂多互动，使早期在线指标虚高，随时间衰减。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users engaging more just because something is new, inflating early online metrics that then decay.

scenario: Uber 测新的动态定价：处理组触发涨价 → 司机往涨价区聚集 → 对照组骑手的可用车也变了。
scenario_en: Uber tests new surge pricing: treatment triggers surge → drivers reposition to surge areas → available cars for control riders also change.
q: 这里对照组和处理组为什么不独立？属于什么问题？怎么缓解？
q_en: Why aren't control and treatment independent here, what problem is it, and how to mitigate?
why: 这是网络干扰：用户/资源会互相影响，处理效应「泄漏」进对照组（涨价改变司机分布，波及对照骑手），使对照不再是干净基线、偏差方向不可预测。缓解：聚类随机化——按地理/社交簇整块分配，让同一簇内不跨臂互相影响。
why_en: This is network interference — users/resources interact, so the treatment leaks into control (surge reshuffles drivers, affecting control riders), biasing in unpredictable directions; mitigate with cluster-based randomization.
tradeoff: 用户级随机化（简单但共享资源时会泄漏） vs 聚类随机化（整簇同臂、防泄漏但独立单元更少）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  T["处理组涨价"] --> D["司机往涨价区聚集"]
  D --> C["对照组可用车变化"]
  C --> B["对照被污染\n偏差方向不可预测"]
options: 因为样本量不够，缓解靠加大流量
网络干扰：处理效应泄漏进对照组，对照不再干净；缓解靠聚类随机化
新奇效应：涨价太新导致虚高，缓解靠跑久点
peeking：提前看结果，缓解靠预先锁定分析计划
options_en: Because the sample is too small; mitigate by raising traffic.
Network interference: the treatment leaks into control so control isn't clean; mitigate with cluster randomization.
Novelty effect: surge is too new and inflates metrics; mitigate by running longer.
Peeking: looking early; mitigate by pre-committing the analysis plan.
optionExplanations: 加样本救不了「对照被处理污染」的结构问题。
对；共享司机池让处理泄漏进对照，聚类随机化把互相影响关进同一簇。
这不是新鲜感衰减，是组间通过共享资源相互影响。
peeking 是时间维度偷看，本例是空间/资源上的相互干扰。
optionExplanations_en: More samples can't fix the structural issue of control being contaminated by treatment.
Correct — a shared driver pool leaks treatment into control; cluster randomization confines interactions within a cluster.
This isn't novelty decay; groups interact through a shared resource.
Peeking is a temporal early look; this is spatial/resource interference between groups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户或资源相互影响，使处理效应泄漏进对照组，违反组间独立假设。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Network interference is users/resources interacting so treatment leaks into control, violating between-group independence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理/社交簇整块分配同一实验臂，把相互影响关在簇内以防泄漏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cluster-based randomization assigns whole geographic/social clusters to one arm, containing interactions to prevent leakage.

scenario: 计划跑 21 天，第 4 天看到欺诈下降 3% 且 p<0.05，团队想立刻停实验上线。
scenario_en: Planned for 21 days, on day 4 you see a 3% fraud drop with p<0.05 and want to stop and ship now.
q: 在到达计划样本量前反复偷看、见显著就停，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What's the main risk of peeking before the planned sample and stopping when significant?
why: 这是 peeking：每偷看一次 p 值就等于多做一次假设检验，反复看会把整体假阳性率抬到 5% 以上，见显著就停会「捡」到随机波动造成的假阳性。所以第 4 天的 3% 可能是虚的。这正是课后测验的答案。
why_en: This is peeking — each early look is another hypothesis test, so repeated peeking inflates the overall false-positive rate above 5%, and stopping at significance catches random-noise false positives.
tradeoff: 预锁样本量+分析时点（假阳性受控） vs 见 p<0.05 就停（假阳性被抬高）
whenOtherWins: 若确实需要中途早停，应改用序贯检验(sequential testing)并对显著性边界做校正，而不是拿固定 α 反复偷看。
options: 样本量不足会漏检真效应，属于 Type II 风险
peeking：反复偷看抬高假阳性率，见显著就停会捡到虚假显著
网络干扰让欺诈者互相影响，导致效应虚高
没有风险，p<0.05 就一定是真效应，越早上线越好
options_en: Insufficient samples miss a real effect — a Type II risk.
Peeking: repeated early looks inflate the false-positive rate, and stopping at significance catches spurious significance.
Network interference makes fraudsters interact, inflating the effect.
No risk — p<0.05 is always a real effect, so ship as early as possible.
optionExplanations: 问题不是漏检而是「多次偷看」抬高了假阳性（Type I）。
对；每次偷看=多一次检验，固定 α 下反复看会把假阳性率推过 5%，是测验答案。
这不是干扰问题，是提前停止导致的统计假阳性。
p<0.05 在偷看语境下并不可信，早停恰恰放大假阳性。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't missing an effect but repeated looks inflating false positives (Type I).
Correct — each peek is another test; under fixed alpha, repeated looks push the false-positive rate past 5% — the quiz answer.
This isn't interference; it's statistical false positives from early stopping.
p<0.05 isn't trustworthy under peeking; early stopping amplifies false positives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在达到计划样本量前反复查看结果并在显著时提前停，抬高整体假阳性率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Peeking is repeatedly checking results before the planned sample and stopping at significance, inflating the overall false-positive rate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许中途多次查看但对显著性边界做校正，控制累积假阳性的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential testing permits multiple interim looks while adjusting significance boundaries to control cumulative false positives.

scenario: 业务方确实希望在实验中途能提前叫停明显有效/有害的变体，但又不想抬高假阳性率。
scenario_en: The business genuinely wants the option to stop clearly-good/bad variants mid-experiment without inflating the false-positive rate.
q: 既要允许早停、又要控制假阳性，正确做法是什么？
q_en: To allow early stopping while controlling false positives, what's the right approach?
why: 用序贯检验：它预先设计好中途多次查看时的显著性边界（比固定 0.05 更严），使累积假阳性率仍受控。这样可以合法早停。反面是拿固定 α=0.05 反复偷看，那会把假阳性抬高。默认仍应预锁样本量与分析时点。
why_en: Use sequential testing — it pre-designs stricter significance boundaries for repeated interim looks so cumulative false positives stay controlled, enabling legitimate early stopping.
tradeoff: 序贯检验（合法早停、边界更严、稍损功效） vs 固定样本预锁（最简单但不能中途停）
whenOtherWins: 若不需要早停，最简单稳妥的仍是预先锁定样本量和分析时点、到点再看，无需序贯检验的复杂度。
options: 继续用固定 α=0.05，每天看一次，见显著就停
用序贯检验：预设更严的显著性边界，控制累积假阳性下合法早停
把 α 调到 0.5 让实验更容易显著，就能放心早停
取消所有护栏指标，这样早停不会有副作用
options_en: Keep fixed alpha=0.05, look daily, and stop at significance.
Use sequential testing: pre-set stricter significance boundaries to allow legitimate early stopping with controlled cumulative false positives.
Set alpha to 0.5 so the experiment reaches significance easily, then stop early confidently.
Drop all guardrails so early stopping has no side effects.
optionExplanations: 固定 α 反复看正是 peeking，会抬高假阳性，不是解法。
对；序贯检验用校正后的边界让早停合法、假阳性可控。
把 α 调大只会让假阳性更多，方向完全错误。
护栏与早停的假阳性问题无关，去掉护栏只会更危险。
optionExplanations_en: Fixed alpha with repeated looks is peeking, inflating false positives — not a fix.
Correct — sequential testing's corrected boundaries make early stopping legitimate with controlled false positives.
Raising alpha just makes more false positives — completely wrong direction.
Guardrails are unrelated to early-stopping false positives; removing them is more dangerous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为中途多次查看设计校正过的显著性边界，使累积假阳性受控、可合法早停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential testing designs corrected significance boundaries for interim looks so cumulative false positives stay controlled, allowing valid early stopping.

q: 把 A/B 测试设计的 7 步框架排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the 7-step A/B testing design framework:
steps: 陈述假设（改动 → 指标 → 阈值）
定义主指标 + ≥2 个护栏（UX + 系统健康）
从业务影响确定 MDE
用功效分析算样本量（α=0.05, power=0.80）
估算运行时长 = 样本量 / 日流量，取整到整周
预先锁定分析计划（不 peeking）、用时间窗口趋势应对新奇效应
检查网络干扰，若用户相互影响则改聚类随机化
why: 先立可证伪假设，再定主指标+护栏，从业务定 MDE，据 MDE 算样本量，除以日流量得时长，预锁分析计划防 peeking 与新奇，最后检查网络干扰决定是否聚类随机化。顺序体现「先目标后统计再执行」的全生命周期思路。
why_en: Hypothesis → primary+guardrails → MDE from business → sample size via power → runtime → pre-commit against peeking/novelty → check network interference; the order goes goal, statistics, then execution.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  H["1.假设"] --> M["2.主指标+护栏"]
  M --> D["3.MDE(业务)"]
  D --> N["4.样本量(功效分析)"]
  N --> R["5.运行时长"]
  R --> P["6.预锁分析计划"]
  P --> I["7.查网络干扰"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 实验开始前就固定样本量与分析时点，防止事后偷看与随意早停带来的假阳性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-committing fixes the sample size and analysis time before the experiment to prevent peeking and false positives.

scenario: 三个 A/B 常见陷阱：新奇效应、网络干扰、peeking，症状和缓解各不同。
scenario_en: Three common A/B pitfalls — novelty effect, network interference, peeking — with different symptoms and fixes.
q: 这三个 A/B 陷阱各自的机制与缓解手段是什么？
q_en: What is each of these three A/B pitfalls' mechanism and mitigation?
why: 新奇效应=用户因新而短暂多互动、早期虚高，缓解跑 2-4 周看时间窗口；网络干扰=组间通过共享资源/社交相互影响、处理泄漏进对照，缓解聚类随机化；peeking=提前偷看见显著就停、抬高假阳性，缓解预锁样本量或序贯检验。三者分别是时间性、结构性、统计性的坑。
why_en: Novelty is temporal inflation (mitigate: 2-4 weeks, windowed trends); network interference is structural leakage between groups (mitigate: cluster randomization); peeking is statistical false-positive inflation (mitigate: pre-commit or sequential testing).

rows: 因新而虚高、随时间衰减
组间共享资源相互影响

options: 三者本质相同，都靠加大样本量解决
新奇=时间性虚高(跑久)、网络干扰=结构性泄漏(聚类随机化)、peeking=统计性假阳性(预锁/序贯)
新奇靠聚类随机化、网络干扰靠跑久、peeking 靠加样本，各自对应
三者都是 Type II 错误的不同表现
options_en: All three are essentially the same, solved by more samples.
Novelty = temporal inflation (run longer), interference = structural leakage (cluster randomization), peeking = statistical false positives (pre-commit/sequential).
Novelty via cluster randomization, interference via running longer, peeking via more samples — respectively.
All three are different manifestations of Type II error.
optionExplanations: 加样本救不了泄漏和偷看，三者机制不同、缓解也不同。
对；时间性/结构性/统计性三类坑，缓解手段一一对应。
缓解全部错配：新奇不是聚类能救、peeking 不是加样本能救。
peeking 是抬高假阳性(Type I)，新奇/干扰也不是 Type II，归类错误。
optionExplanations_en: More samples can't fix leakage or peeking; the three differ in mechanism and fix.
Correct — temporal/structural/statistical pitfalls with matching mitigations.
All mitigations mismatched: novelty isn't fixed by clustering, peeking isn't fixed by more samples.
Peeking inflates false positives (Type I), and novelty/interference aren't Type II either — miscategorized.

termDefinitions.term: time-windowed analysis / 时间窗口分析
termDefinitions.meaning: 按周/时段拆看指标趋势而非单一聚合值，用于识别新奇效应的衰减。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time-windowed analysis reads metric trends by week/segment instead of one aggregate, revealing novelty decay.

scenario: 在社交网络/双边市场/共享出行里做 A/B，用户之间会互相影响（分享、抢单、抢司机）。
scenario_en: Running A/B in a social network / two-sided marketplace / ride-share where users interact (sharing, competing for jobs/drivers).
q: 这类用户会相互影响的产品，该最优先防哪个陷阱？用什么随机化？
q_en: For products where users interact, which pitfall to guard first, and what randomization?
why: 最优先防网络干扰：用户级随机化会让处理组的效应通过互动泄漏进对照组，破坏独立性、偏差方向不可预测。改用聚类随机化——按地理/社交簇整块分同一臂，让相互影响都发生在簇内、不跨臂，恢复组间可比性。
why_en: Guard network interference first — user-level randomization lets treatment leak into control via interactions, so switch to cluster-based randomization (assign whole geo/social clusters to one arm) to contain interactions.
tradeoff: 用户级随机化（多独立单元、但共享资源时泄漏） vs 聚类随机化（防泄漏、但独立单元变少、功效下降）
whenOtherWins: 若用户彼此独立、不共享资源也不互动（如互不相关的单机功能），用户级随机化更简单、独立单元更多、功效更高。
options: 先防新奇效应，用用户级随机化即可
先防网络干扰，改用聚类随机化把相互影响关在簇内
先防 peeking，用户之间的影响与随机化无关
先防分布漂移，重训模型即可解决相互影响
options_en: Guard novelty first; user-level randomization suffices.
Guard network interference first; switch to cluster randomization to contain interactions within clusters.
Guard peeking first; user interactions are unrelated to randomization.
Guard distribution shift first; retraining fixes the interactions.
optionExplanations: 用户互相影响时，用户级随机化正是泄漏的来源，防新奇解决不了。
对；聚类随机化把互相影响限制在簇内，恢复处理/对照的可比性。
用户互动恰恰通过随机化单元影响独立性，与 peeking 无关。
分布漂移是离线-在线问题，重训救不了组间干扰。
optionExplanations_en: When users interact, user-level randomization is the leakage source; guarding novelty won't help.
Correct — cluster randomization confines interactions within clusters, restoring treatment/control comparability.
User interaction affects independence via the randomization unit, unrelated to peeking.
Distribution shift is an offline-online issue; retraining can't fix between-group interference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 供需两方在同一平台匹配（骑手-司机、买家-卖家），一方的实验会波及另一方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-sided marketplace matches supply and demand (riders-drivers, buyers-sellers), where an experiment on one side affects the other.

scenario: 实验平台（如 Amazon SageMaker）支持在实验进行中动态调整对照/实验的流量比例，无需重启。
scenario_en: Platforms like Amazon SageMaker support adjusting control/treatment traffic split mid-experiment without restarting.
q: 「动态流量分配」提供了什么能力？和 peeking 早停是一回事吗？
q_en: What does dynamic traffic allocation provide, and is it the same as peeking/early stopping?
why: 动态流量分配让你在实验中途调整每臂的流量占比（如逐步给更优臂加量）而无需重启实验。它是流量运营能力，不等于 peeking——peeking 是拿固定 α 反复偷看并据此下显著性结论；动态分配若要保推断有效，仍需配套的序贯/bandit 统计框架。
why_en: Dynamic traffic allocation lets you adjust each arm's traffic share mid-experiment without restarting; it's a traffic-ops capability, not peeking, and valid inference still needs a sequential/bandit statistical framework.
options: 它等价于 peeking，允许见显著就停并直接下结论
它让中途调整每臂流量比例而无需重启；本身是流量运营，不替代统计框架
它自动消除网络干扰，无需聚类随机化
它把样本量需求降为零，任何效应都能瞬间检出
options_en: It equals peeking, letting you stop at significance and conclude directly.
It adjusts each arm's traffic share mid-experiment without restart; a traffic-ops capability, not a replacement for the statistical framework.
It automatically removes network interference, so no cluster randomization is needed.
It drops the sample-size requirement to zero, detecting any effect instantly.
optionExplanations: 动态分配不是 peeking，也不豁免「反复看会抬高假阳性」的统计问题。
对；它只管流量调度，要保推断有效仍需序贯/bandit 框架配合。
流量调度不解决组间相互影响，网络干扰仍要聚类随机化。
样本量由功效分析决定，动态分配不会把它降为零。
optionExplanations_en: Dynamic allocation isn't peeking and doesn't exempt the false-positive inflation of repeated looks.
Correct — it only schedules traffic; valid inference still needs a sequential/bandit framework.
Traffic scheduling doesn't fix between-group interaction; interference still needs cluster randomization.
Sample size comes from power analysis; dynamic allocation doesn't zero it out.

termDefinitions.term: dynamic traffic allocation / 动态流量分配
termDefinitions.meaning: 实验进行中调整各臂流量比例而不重启的能力，如 SageMaker 支持。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic traffic allocation adjusts each arm's traffic share mid-experiment without restarting, as SageMaker supports.

scenario: 把 A/B 假设写成可证伪的一句话模板，方便面试里直接套用。
scenario_en: Write the A/B hypothesis as a falsifiable one-line template to reuse in interviews.
q: 补全可证伪 A/B 假设的三要素模板：
q_en: Complete the three-part falsifiable A/B hypothesis template:
text: 假设 = 一个具体{{改动}} + 一个预期的{{指标}}移动 + 一个{{阈值}}，例如「换成 listwise 排序器会让观看时长/会话提升 ≥1%」。
text_en: Hypothesis = a concrete {{change}} + an expected {{metric}} move + a {{threshold}}, e.g. 'switching to a listwise ranker raises watch time/session by ≥1%'.
why: 三要素齐全才让实验事前可判成败：改动指明测什么、指标指明看哪个数、阈值（结合 MDE）指明多大才算赢。缺任何一个都退化成「看看好不好」的不可证伪表述。
why_en: All three make the experiment decidable in advance: the change says what to test, the metric which number, the threshold how big counts as a win.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判定实验成功的最小指标移动量，通常与 MDE 一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The threshold is the minimum metric move that counts as success, usually aligned with the MDE.

scenario: 为省时间，工程师想只跑周二到周四三天（流量最大）就得出 A/B 结论。
scenario_en: To save time, an engineer wants to conclude the A/B from just Tue-Thu (highest traffic).
q: 只采工作日高峰三天的样本，会带来什么偏差？为什么要跑满整周？
q_en: What bias comes from sampling only three weekday-peak days, and why run full weeks?
why: 工作日和周末用户行为不同（购物、娱乐、通勤模式都变）。只采工作日会系统性偏向某一类行为，结论无法泛化到全周。跑满整周（7/14 天）覆盖完整周内周期，样本才代表真实流量结构。
why_en: Weekday and weekend behavior differ, so sampling only weekdays systematically biases toward one behavior pattern; run full weeks (7/14 days) to cover the complete weekly cycle.
options: 没有偏差，只要样本量够就行，哪几天都一样
工作日/周末行为不同，只采工作日会系统性偏差；跑满整周覆盖周内周期
偏差来自流量太大，应改采周末低峰几天
只影响运行时长计算，不影响结论的代表性
options_en: No bias — as long as the sample is large, any days are equivalent.
Weekday/weekend behavior differs, so weekday-only sampling is systematically biased; run full weeks to cover the weekly cycle.
The bias is from too much traffic; sample low-peak weekend days instead.
It only affects runtime computation, not the representativeness of the conclusion.
optionExplanations: 样本量大但结构偏，仍无法代表全周行为，天数不是无所谓。
对；周内周期性让整周采样成为必需，否则结论有系统性偏差。
问题不是流量大小，是行为随星期几变化的周期性。
它直接影响样本代表性，不只是时长的算术。
optionExplanations_en: A large but structurally biased sample still can't represent the whole week; the days do matter.
Correct — the weekly cycle makes full-week sampling necessary or the conclusion is systematically biased.
The issue isn't traffic volume but day-of-week behavioral periodicity.
It directly affects sample representativeness, not just runtime arithmetic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户行为随星期几系统变化，要求实验覆盖完整整周以避免采样偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weekly seasonality is user behavior varying systematically by day of week, requiring full-week coverage to avoid sampling bias.

scenario: Airbnb 测一个提升预订的搜索排序改动，要选主指标和护栏。
scenario_en: Airbnb tests a search-ranking change to lift bookings and must pick primary and guardrail metrics.
q: 这个 Airbnb 实验，主指标和护栏分别该选什么？为什么这样搭配？
q_en: For this Airbnb experiment, what primary and guardrails, and why this pairing?
why: 主指标选预订率（直接目标）；护栏选页面加载时间（系统健康——排序变复杂别拖慢页面）和房东取消率（UX/供给健康——别为冲预订推不靠谱房源导致取消飙升）。主指标推目标，两个护栏各守一条不能牺牲的底线。
why_en: Primary = booking rate (direct target); guardrails = page-load time (system health — don't slow the page) and host cancellation rate (UX/supply health — don't chase bookings by pushing unreliable listings).
tradeoff: 只盯预订率（可能偷偷拖慢页面/推高取消） vs 加护栏（守住加载时间与取消率底线）
whenOtherWins: 若这次改动完全不碰服务延迟、也不改变房源质量分布（如纯前端文案改动），相应护栏可以放宽或替换成更相关的。
options: 主指标=页面加载时间，护栏=预订率
主指标=预订率，护栏=页面加载时间 + 房东取消率
主指标=预订率，不需要任何护栏，越简单越好
主指标和护栏都设成预订率，重复以提高可信度
options_en: Primary = page-load time, guardrail = booking rate.
Primary = booking rate, guardrails = page-load time + host cancellation rate.
Primary = booking rate, with no guardrails — simpler is better.
Set both primary and guardrail to booking rate for redundancy.
optionExplanations: 搭反了：预订率是目标（主指标），加载时间是要守的底线（护栏）。
对；预订率推目标，加载时间守系统健康、取消率守供给/UX，正是成熟搭配。
没有护栏就挡不住「冲预订却拖慢页面或推高取消」的副作用。
主指标与护栏设成同一个没有意义，护栏要覆盖不同风险维度。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: booking rate is the target (primary), load time is the floor to protect (guardrail).
Correct — booking rate drives the goal, load time guards system health, cancellation guards supply/UX — a mature pairing.
Without guardrails you can't block the side effect of chasing bookings while slowing the page or raising cancellations.
Setting primary and guardrail identical is pointless; guardrails must cover different risk dimensions.

termDefinitions.term: host cancellation rate / 房东取消率
termDefinitions.meaning: 房东取消已确认预订的比例，Airbnb 的 UX/供给护栏之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Host cancellation rate is the share of confirmed bookings hosts cancel — an Airbnb UX/supply guardrail.

scenario: 团队把 MDE 定成 0.5%，理由是 0.1% 的 CTR 提升不值得部署与维护的复杂度。
scenario_en: The team sets MDE=0.5% because a 0.1% CTR lift isn't worth the deployment and maintenance complexity.
q: 把 MDE 从 0.1% 提高到 0.5% 对实验成本有什么影响？为什么这么设？
q_en: What does raising MDE from 0.1% to 0.5% do to experiment cost, and why set it there?
why: 样本量 ∝ 1/MDE²，把 MDE 从 0.1% 提到 0.5%（放大 5 倍）能把所需样本量缩小约 25 倍，运行时长大幅缩短。这么设是业务判断：0.1% 的 CTR 提升带来的收益盖不住部署/维护成本，不值得为它耗巨量样本去检测。
why_en: Since sample size ∝ 1/MDE², raising MDE 5x (0.1%→0.5%) cuts required samples ~25x and shortens runtime; you set it there because a 0.1% CTR gain isn't worth the deployment cost to detect.
options: 样本量按比例只缩小 5 倍，因为样本量与 MDE 成反比
样本量约缩小 25 倍（∝1/MDE²）、时长大减；这么设因 0.1% 提升不值得部署成本
对样本量没影响，MDE 只改结论解读不改样本
样本量反而增大，因为要更精确地检测 0.5%
options_en: Sample size shrinks only 5x, since it's inversely proportional to MDE.
Sample size shrinks ~25x (∝ 1/MDE²) and runtime drops sharply; set there because a 0.1% lift isn't worth the deployment cost.
No effect on sample size; MDE only changes interpretation.
Sample size grows, because detecting 0.5% needs more precision.
optionExplanations: 是平方反比不是线性反比，5 倍 MDE 对应约 25 倍样本缩减。
对；1/MDE² 让放宽 MDE 大幅省样本，而门槛高低是业务价值判断。
MDE 是样本量公式的分母平方项，影响巨大，不是不改样本。
放宽 MDE（测更大效应）省样本，不是增大。
optionExplanations_en: It's an inverse-square not inverse-linear law; 5x MDE means ~25x fewer samples.
Correct — 1/MDE² makes a looser MDE save many samples, and the threshold is a business-value call.
MDE is the squared denominator in the sample-size formula — a huge effect, not zero.
Loosening MDE (detecting a bigger effect) saves samples, not increases them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 样本量与 MDE 平方成反比，想检测越小的效应，代价按平方暴涨。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sample size is inversely proportional to MDE squared, so detecting smaller effects costs quadratically more.

scenario: 一个新 UI 改版首周各项互动指标暴涨，产品经理想立刻宣布成功、全量上线。
scenario_en: A new UI redesign spikes all engagement metrics in week 1, and the PM wants to declare success and full-roll now.
q: 面对首周暴涨，该怎么判断这是真实提升还是新奇效应？
q_en: Facing a week-1 spike, how do you tell a real lift from a novelty effect?
why: 别看单一聚合值就下结论：把实验跑够 2-4 周，按时间窗口看趋势——若增益从首周高位持续衰减到接近 0，就是新奇效应；若衰减后稳定在一个正的平台期，才是真实长期提升。等新鲜感退潮再判。
why_en: Don't conclude from one aggregate — run 2-4 weeks and read time-windowed trends: if the gain decays toward zero it was novelty, if it stabilizes at a positive plateau it's a real lift.
tradeoff: 首周就下结论（可能被新奇虚高误导） vs 跑 2-4 周看衰减后平台（识别真实长期效应）
whenOtherWins: 若改动本质上就是短命内容（限时活动、突发新闻），本来只需要短期效果，那么首周表现反而是相关的评估对象。
options: 首周暴涨就代表成功，立刻全量上线最稳妥
跑 2-4 周看时间窗口趋势：衰减到近 0 是新奇，稳定在正平台才是真提升
把实验缩短到 3 天，趁热度最高时锁定结论
只要 p<0.05 就上线，趋势无关紧要
options_en: A week-1 spike means success; full-roll immediately is safest.
Run 2-4 weeks and read time-windowed trends: decaying toward zero is novelty, a stable positive plateau is a real lift.
Shorten to 3 days to lock the conclusion at peak hype.
Ship as long as p<0.05; the trend is irrelevant.
optionExplanations: 首周暴涨正是新奇效应的典型症状，据此全量最危险。
对；看衰减后的稳态平台才能区分真提升与新鲜感，是新奇效应的标准应对。
缩短实验会把新奇虚高固化成结论，恰恰放大误判。
在新奇效应下 p<0.05 也可能是短暂虚高，必须看时间趋势。
optionExplanations_en: A week-1 spike is the textbook novelty symptom; full-rolling on it is most dangerous.
Correct — reading the post-decay plateau distinguishes real lift from hype — the standard novelty response.
Shortening freezes novelty inflation into the conclusion, amplifying the misjudgment.
Under novelty, p<0.05 can be transient inflation; you must inspect the time trend.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新奇消退后指标稳定下来的水平，代表真实长期效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The plateau is the level the metric settles at after novelty fades, representing the real long-term effect.

scenario: 在共享司机池的市场里做用户级 A/B，处理效应通过司机重定位泄漏进对照，偏差方向事先无法预测。
scenario_en: A user-level A/B in a shared-driver marketplace where treatment leaks into control via driver repositioning, biasing in an unpredictable direction.
q: 网络干扰的偏差为什么「方向不可预测」？这比一个已知方向的偏差更麻烦在哪？
q_en: Why is network-interference bias 'unpredictable in direction', and why is that worse than a known-direction bias?
why: 泄漏可能高估也可能低估处理效应，取决于资源怎么在组间流动（司机被吸走使对照变差 → 高估处理；或处理组拥堵反噬 → 低估），事前无法确定符号。已知方向的偏差还能事后校正一个方向，方向不可预测则连往哪边修都不知道，只能从设计上（聚类随机化）消除。
why_en: Leakage can over- or under-state the effect depending on how resources flow between groups, so the sign is unknown in advance; a known-direction bias could be corrected one way, but an unknown direction can only be removed by design (cluster randomization).
options: 方向其实可预测，总是高估处理效应，直接减去固定值即可
泄漏可能高估或低估、符号事前未知；不像已知方向能事后校正，只能靠聚类随机化从设计消除
方向不可预测但幅度总是很小，可忽略不计
这不是偏差问题，只是方差变大，加样本即可
options_en: The direction is actually predictable — it always overstates the effect — so subtract a fixed offset.
Leakage can over- or under-state with unknown sign; unlike a known-direction bias you can't post-correct, only remove it by design via cluster randomization.
The direction is unpredictable but the magnitude is always tiny and negligible.
It's not bias but larger variance, fixable by adding samples.
optionExplanations: 泄漏并不总是高估，符号取决于资源流向，减固定值会修错方向。
对；符号未知让事后校正失效，必须用聚类随机化在设计层面切断泄漏。
幅度未必小，且方向不定本身就使结论不可信，不能忽略。
它是系统性偏差不是纯方差，加样本消不掉偏差。
optionExplanations_en: Leakage doesn't always overstate; the sign depends on resource flow, so a fixed offset corrects the wrong way.
Correct — unknown sign defeats post-correction, so cluster randomization must cut leakage by design.
The magnitude isn't necessarily small, and unknown direction alone makes conclusions untrustworthy.
It's systematic bias not mere variance; more samples can't remove bias.

termDefinitions.term: unpredictable bias direction / 偏差方向不可预测
termDefinitions.meaning: 干扰可能高估或低估效应、符号事前未知，无法靠事后减一个固定量校正。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unpredictable bias direction means interference may over- or under-state the effect with unknown sign, uncorrectable by a fixed post-hoc offset.

scenario: 面试官问：既然有标准 A/B 测试，为什么还要 interleaving、bandit、switchback、准实验这些方法？
scenario_en: Interviewer: if we have standard A/B testing, why do we still need interleaving, bandits, switchback, and quasi-experiments?
q: 为什么需要「超越标准 A/B」的实验方法？
q_en: Why do we need experimentation methods beyond standard A/B?
why: 标准 A/B 在四类生产场景会失效：微小排序差异要几百万用户、动态优化时 50/50 会白烧钱、双边市场共享司机导致干扰、平台级发布无法按用户随机。每一类都有专门方法接手，答对方法体现你懂完整部署生命周期。
why_en: Standard A/B breaks in four production settings — tiny ranking effects, dynamic optimization, marketplace interference, and platform-wide launches — and each has a specialized method.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  F1["微小排序差异"] --> M1["Interleaving"]
  F2["动态优化/短命内容"] --> M2["Multi-armed bandit"]
  F3["双边市场干扰"] --> M3["Switchback"]
  F4["平台级/国家级发布"] --> M4["准实验 DiD/合成控制"]
options: 标准 A/B 慢又贵，这些新方法只是更快版本的 A/B，本质机制完全相同
标准 A/B 在四类场景失效（微小排序差、动态优化、市场干扰、平台级发布），每类有专门方法接手
这些方法已完全取代 A/B，任何实验都该改用它们，A/B 已经过时不该再用
它们只是显著性检验的不同叫法，换个名字，实验设计上并无区别
options_en: Standard A/B is slow and costly, and these new methods are just faster versions of A/B with identical mechanics.
Standard A/B fails in four settings (tiny ranking gaps, dynamic optimization, market interference, platform-wide launches), each with a specialized method.
These methods fully replace A/B; every experiment should switch to them because A/B is now obsolete.
They are just different names for significance testing, differing only in label, not in experimental design.
optionExplanations: 不是更快的 A/B：interleaving 是被试内设计、bandit 是自适应分配、switchback 是按时间聚类随机，机制根本不同。
