category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 法务语料里，用户常查精确条款号(如「Section 14.2(b)」)；目前融合总把语义相关但错误的条款排在正确的精确匹配前面。
scenario_en: In a legal corpus, users often query exact clause numbers ('Section 14.2(b)'), but fusion keeps ranking semantically related wrong clauses above the exact match.
q: 该怎么修，让精确条款匹配排上去？
q_en: How do you fix this so exact clause matches rank higher?
why: 在领域标注的查询-文档相关性对上训学习型融合权重：法务这种精确匹配为主的语料要把 BM25 权重调高、稠密调低，让精确词法命中主导排序。RRF 无参数，做不到这种领域自适应。
why_en: Train learned fusion weights on domain-labeled query-document relevance pairs: for exact-match-heavy legal corpora, weight BM25 higher and dense lower so exact lexical hits dominate ranking — parameter-free RRF can't adapt like this.
tradeoff: 学习权重偏 BM25(精确匹配优先但要标注) vs 均等 RRF(无参数但不偏向精确)
whenOtherWins: 若是对话式知识库、查询多为改述，应把稠密权重调高；精确匹配没那么重要时，不必偏向 BM25。
options: 换个更大的 LLM，让它在生成时自己纠正排序
在领域查询-文档相关性对上训学习型融合权重，把 BM25 权重调高，让精确匹配主导
关掉 BM25，只留稠密检索
把 RRF 的 k 调到很大就行
options_en: Switch to a bigger LLM and let it self-correct ranking at generation.
Train learned fusion weights on domain query-document pairs, weighting BM25 higher so exact matches dominate.
Turn off BM25 and keep only dense retrieval.
Just set RRF's k very large.
optionExplanations: LLM 只能用检索给它的候选，排序错了、精确条款没进前列，生成阶段补不回来。
对；学习型融合能按领域把 BM25 权重抬高，让精确条款号命中主导，这正是 L5→Staff+ 的差别。
关掉 BM25 会连精确匹配的能力一起丢掉，与目标背道而驰。
调 k 只是整体压平名次差距，不能让精确匹配相对稠密获得更高权重。
optionExplanations_en: The LLM can only use retrieved candidates; if ranking is wrong and the exact clause isn't near the top, generation can't recover it.
Correct — learned fusion raises BM25's weight for the domain so exact clause hits dominate, the L5-to-Staff+ difference.
Turning off BM25 discards the exact-match ability entirely, opposite to the goal.
Tuning k only flattens rank gaps overall; it can't give exact matches higher weight relative to dense.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用小模型在标注相关性对上学最优的稠密/稀疏权重，按领域自适应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned fusion trains a small model on labeled relevance pairs to learn optimal dense/sparse weights, adapting per domain.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 面试官问检索和重排各优化什么，想看你能否分清 recall 和 precision 的分工。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what retrieval vs reranking each optimize, checking whether you separate recall from precision.
q: 检索(retrieval)和重排(reranking)分别优化什么？
q_en: What do retrieval and reranking each optimize?
why: 检索优化召回：宽撒网，把可能相关的都捞进候选集(宁多勿漏)；重排优化精度：在候选集里把真正最相关的排到前面(宁精勿滥)。融合后的候选集交给重排(下一课)，两阶段各司其职。
why_en: Retrieval optimizes recall: cast a wide net to pull all possibly-relevant chunks into the candidate set; reranking optimizes precision: within that set, push the truly most relevant to the top — the fused candidate set feeds reranking, each stage with its own job.
tradeoff: 检索(最大化召回、宽撒网) vs 重排(最大化精度、精排前列)
options: 两者都优化召回，重排只是跑得更快
检索优化精度、重排优化召回，正好相反
检索优化召回(宽撒网宁多勿漏)，重排优化精度(候选里把最相关的排前)
两者是同一步，不用分开
options_en: Both optimize recall; reranking is just faster.
Retrieval optimizes precision and reranking recall — the reverse.
Retrieval optimizes recall (wide net, don't miss), reranking optimizes precision (top-rank the most relevant in the set).
They're the same step, no need to separate.
optionExplanations: 重排优化的是精度不是召回，两阶段目标不同，不是快慢的差别。
说反了：检索管召回、重排管精度。
对；先宽召回再精排是两阶段设计的核心分工，一个保不漏、一个保排得准。
召回和精度目标不同、放一步会互相牵制，所以拆成检索+重排两阶段。
optionExplanations_en: Reranking optimizes precision, not recall; the two stages have different goals, not a speed difference.
Backwards: retrieval handles recall and reranking handles precision.
Correct — wide recall then precise reranking is the core two-stage split, one ensuring nothing is missed, the other ensuring correct ordering.
Recall and precision are different goals that fight in one step, which is why retrieval and reranking are split.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相关文档中被检索到的比例，检索阶段要最大化它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the fraction of relevant documents that get retrieved; the retrieval stage maximizes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回结果中真正相关的比例，重排阶段要最大化它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of returned results that are truly relevant; the reranking stage maximizes it.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 索引因嵌入升级或分块变更要重建，但服务不能下线(5 万员工随时在用)。
scenario_en: The index must be rebuilt for an embedding upgrade or chunking change, but the service can't go down (50k employees always using it).
q: 怎么做到零停机重建索引？
q_en: How do you rebuild the index with zero downtime?
why: 蓝绿部署：两个索引槽，线上槽继续服务查询，离线槽在后台重建；新索引在 golden query set 上验证(recall@k、MRR)达标后，流量原子切换过去，旧槽留作回滚。全程不下线。
why_en: Blue-green deployment: two index slots, the live one keeps serving while the offline one rebuilds in the background; once the new index passes validation on a golden query set (recall@k, MRR), traffic swaps atomically and the old slot stays for rollback — no downtime.
tradeoff: 蓝绿(零停机可回滚但要双份索引资源) vs 原地重建(省资源但要停机)
whenOtherWins: 若只是日常加几篇新文档、模型没变，增量更新更快更省，不必整套蓝绿重建。
diagram:
flowchart LR L["蓝槽(线上)"] -->|服务查询| U["用户"] G["绿槽(离线重建)"] --> V{"golden set 验证
recall@k/MRR"} V -->|达标| SW["原子切流量"] L -.留作回滚.-> RB["旧索引"]
options: 直接在线上索引上原地改，边改边服务
停机几小时重建，贴公告让员工等
每次查询实时重新嵌入，不用预建索引
蓝绿：线上槽服务、离线槽重建，golden set 验证达标后原子切流量，旧槽留回滚
options_en: Edit the live index in place, serving while editing.
Take hours of downtime to rebuild and post a notice for employees to wait.
Re-embed live on every query, no prebuilt index.
Blue-green: live slot serves, offline slot rebuilds, atomic swap after golden-set validation, old slot kept for rollback.
optionExplanations: 原地改会在重建中途产生不一致状态，查询可能读到半新半旧的索引，质量抖动。
停机违背零停机硬要求，5 万员工随时依赖它，不可接受。
每次查询实时嵌入延迟爆炸，且失去索引意义，扛不住规模。
对；两槽切换让重建全程离线进行，验证达标才切、旧槽可回滚，是零停机重建的标准做法。
optionExplanations_en: In-place edits create inconsistent mid-rebuild states, so queries may read a half-new/half-old index with jittery quality.
Downtime violates the hard zero-downtime need with 50k employees depending on it — unacceptable.
Re-embedding per query explodes latency and defeats the index, unable to handle scale.
Correct — two slots let the rebuild happen fully offline, swapping only after validation with the old slot for rollback, the standard zero-downtime rebuild.

termDefinitions.term: golden query set / 黄金查询集
termDefinitions.meaning: 一组人工标好相关文档的代表性查询，用来验证新索引质量再切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A golden query set is a set of representative queries with hand-labeled relevant docs, used to validate a new index before swapping.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均倒数排名：第一条正确结果名次倒数的平均，衡量排序质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank) averages the reciprocal rank of the first correct result, measuring ranking quality.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 索引更新有两种：每天加几篇新文档，或换嵌入模型后整体重嵌。
scenario_en: Index updates come in two kinds: adding a few new docs daily, or re-embedding everything after an embedding-model change.
q: 增量更新和全量重建各适合什么，代价是什么？
q_en: What do incremental updates and full rebuilds each fit, and at what cost?
why: 增量更新只把新文档加进现有索引，快、适合每日新增；但若中途换了嵌入模型，新向量来自不同模型，会累积 drift、向量空间不一致。全量重建重嵌整个语料保证所有向量一致，但很贵。
why_en: Incremental updates just add new docs to the existing index — fast, for daily additions — but if the embedding model changed, new vectors come from a different model and accumulate drift with an inconsistent space; a full rebuild re-embeds the whole corpus for consistency but is expensive.
tradeoff: 增量(快、省但换模型会 drift) vs 全量(一致但重嵌整库、贵)
options: 两者一样，随便用哪种都行
增量快、适合每日新增，但换模型会累积 drift；全量重嵌整库保一致但贵
增量最贵、全量最快，正好相反
增量会重嵌整库，全量只加新文档
options_en: They're the same; use either.
Incremental is fast for daily additions but accumulates drift if the model changes; full re-embeds the whole corpus for consistency but is costly.
Incremental is costliest and full fastest — the reverse.
Incremental re-embeds the whole corpus while full only adds new docs.
optionExplanations: 两者速度、适用和风险都不同，混用会在换模型时埋下 drift 隐患。
对；增量便宜但要求模型不变，全量贵但保证一致，选择取决于是否换了嵌入模型。
说反了：增量快而便宜、全量慢而贵。
颠倒了：增量只加新文档、全量才重嵌整库。
optionExplanations_en: They differ in speed, fit, and risk; mixing them plants drift when the model changes.
Correct — incremental is cheap but requires an unchanged model, full is costly but consistent, and the choice hinges on whether the embedding model changed.
Backwards: incremental is fast and cheap, full slow and expensive.
Reversed: incremental only adds new docs while full re-embeds the whole corpus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只把新文档加进现有索引，快但要求嵌入模型不变。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An incremental update only adds new docs to the existing index — fast but requires an unchanged embedding model.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 团队一直用增量更新加新文档，期间悄悄把嵌入模型从 v1 换成了 v2，没有做整体重建。
scenario_en: A team keeps using incremental updates to add docs while quietly switching the embedding model v1→v2 without a full rebuild.
q: 这样长期下去会出什么问题？
q_en: What problem builds up over time here?
why: 增量加进来的是 v2 向量、老索引里是 v1 向量→同一索引里向量空间不一致→跨模型相似度失真→检索排序逐渐 drift、质量悄悄退化且难定位。修法是换模型时做全量重嵌，或走平行索引蓝绿切换。
why_en: Incrementally-added v2 vectors mix with old v1 vectors → an inconsistent space in one index → distorted cross-model similarity → retrieval ranking drifts and quality silently degrades, hard to trace — fix by full re-embedding on a model change or a parallel-index blue-green swap.
options: 新增 v2 向量与老 v1 向量混在一起→向量空间不一致→相似度失真→检索 drift、质量悄悄退化；换模型要全量重嵌
没问题，增量更新天然会对齐新旧模型
只会让索引体积变大，检索照常准确
会自动触发一次全量重建，无需担心
options_en: New v2 vectors mix with old v1 → inconsistent space → distorted similarity → retrieval drifts and quality silently degrades; a model change needs a full re-embed.
No problem; incremental updates naturally align old and new models.
It just enlarges the index; retrieval stays accurate.
It auto-triggers a full rebuild, so no worries.
optionExplanations: 对；这正是 drift 的成因，混着 v1/v2 让排序渐坏且隐蔽，换模型必须全量重嵌或平行切换。
增量更新不做任何跨模型对齐，混用只会累积不一致。
问题不在体积而在相似度失真，检索会实质变差。
系统不会自动重建，drift 会一直累积直到有人发现质量下滑。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — this is exactly how drift forms; mixing v1/v2 degrades ranking subtly, so a model change demands a full re-embed or parallel swap.
Incremental updates do no cross-model alignment; mixing only accumulates inconsistency.
The issue isn't size but distorted similarity, so retrieval materially worsens.
The system won't auto-rebuild; drift keeps accumulating until someone notices the decline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引里向量因模型不一致逐渐偏离，导致检索质量悄悄退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Drift is the gradual divergence of index vectors from model inconsistency, silently degrading retrieval quality.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 要对 1000 万个块做全量重嵌，GPU 消耗很大，得控制成本。
scenario_en: You must fully re-embed 10M chunks with heavy GPU usage, and cost must be controlled.
q: 大规模全量重建怎么控成本？
q_en: How do you control the cost of a large full rebuild?
why: 放到业务低峰期、用 spot(抢占式)GPU 实例批量跑：全量重嵌是可容忍中断、非实时的离线批作业，spot 实例比按需便宜很多，低峰期跑不抢占在线资源。代价是 spot 可能被回收，作业要能断点续跑。
why_en: Run it as an off-peak batch on spot (preemptible) GPU instances: full re-embedding is a non-real-time, interruption-tolerant batch job, and spot is far cheaper than on-demand and off-peak avoids competing with online traffic, at the cost that spot can be reclaimed so the job must checkpoint and resume.
tradeoff: spot + 低峰(便宜但可能被回收) vs 按需实例(贵但不中断)
whenOtherWins: 若重建有硬性时限、不能被打断(如合规截止)，就得用按需实例保证不被回收，牺牲成本换确定性。
options: 用最贵的按需 GPU 实时跑，越快越好
在业务高峰期跑，反正集群有余力
低峰期用 spot 抢占式 GPU 批量跑：离线批作业可容忍中断，spot 便宜，作业要能断点续跑
干脆不重建，一直增量下去
options_en: Use the priciest on-demand GPUs in real time, faster is better.
Run it at peak hours; the cluster has spare capacity.
Off-peak batch on spot preemptible GPUs: a batch job tolerates interruption, spot is cheap, and the job must checkpoint and resume.
Just don't rebuild; keep going incrementally forever.
optionExplanations: 按需实例最贵，重嵌又不需要实时，用它是白花钱。
高峰期跑会和在线检索抢 GPU，抬高线上延迟，得不偿失。
对；离线批作业容忍中断，正好吃 spot 的低价+低峰的闲置，代价是要能断点续跑。
一直增量会在换模型时累积 drift，最终质量退化，不重建不是省钱是埋雷。
optionExplanations_en: On-demand is priciest and re-embedding isn't real-time, so using it wastes money.
Peak-hour runs steal GPUs from online retrieval, raising live latency — not worth it.
Correct — a batch job tolerates interruption, exactly fitting spot's low price and off-peak idle capacity, at the cost of checkpoint/resume.
Forever-incremental accumulates drift on model changes and ultimately degrades quality; not rebuilding buries a landmine rather than saving money.

termDefinitions.meaning: 云厂商的闲置算力，价格低但可能被随时回收，适合可中断的批作业。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spot instance is a cloud provider's idle capacity at low price that may be reclaimed anytime, fit for interruptible batch jobs.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 新重建的索引要切上线前，得先过一道质量关，而不是切了再看。
scenario_en: Before a freshly rebuilt index goes live, it must pass a quality gate rather than being swapped in blind.
q: 索引切换前靠什么判断新索引够好、可以切？
q_en: What decides that a new index is good enough to swap in?
why: 用 golden query set(一组人工标好相关文档的代表性查询)在新索引上跑，量 recall@k 和 MRR 达标才切；这是不停机切换的质量闸门，达不到就不切、留在旧索引。
why_en: Run a golden query set (representative queries with hand-labeled relevant docs) against the new index and swap only if recall@k and MRR pass; it's the quality gate for zero-downtime cutover — if it fails, don't swap, stay on the old index.
options: 靠肉眼看几个查询，感觉还行就切
用 golden query set 跑新索引，量 recall@k 和 MRR 达标才原子切换，是切换的质量闸门
直接切，出问题再回滚就行
靠索引大小判断，越大越好
options_en: Eyeball a few queries and swap if it feels okay.
Run a golden query set against the new index and swap only if recall@k and MRR pass — the cutover quality gate.
Just swap; roll back if something breaks.
Judge by index size; bigger is better.
optionExplanations: 肉眼看几个查询没有量化判据，样本偏差大，挡不住质量回退。
对；用标好的黄金查询集量 recall@k/MRR，是可复现、可自动化的达标判据，达不到就不切。
先切再回滚会让用户短暂吃到坏索引，不如切前用黄金集拦住。
索引大小和检索质量无关，大的索引可能召回更差。
optionExplanations_en: Eyeballing a few queries has no quantitative criterion and heavy sampling bias, failing to catch regressions.
Correct — measuring recall@k/MRR on a labeled golden set is a reproducible, automatable pass criterion; if it fails, don't swap.
Swapping first and rolling back exposes users to a bad index briefly; better to gate before the swap with the golden set.
Index size is unrelated to retrieval quality; a bigger index can recall worse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 前 k 个结果里覆盖了多少真正相关的文档，衡量检索召回完整性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: recall@k is how many truly relevant documents appear in the top-k results, measuring retrieval completeness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均倒数排名：第一条正确结果名次倒数的平均，越接近 1 越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MRR (Mean Reciprocal Rank) averages the reciprocal rank of the first correct result; closer to 1 is better.

category: Enterprise Rag Data Strategy Retrieval Pipeline

scenario: 画企业 RAG 的模型架构，面试官想听你把「检索→重排→生成」三阶段各自的优化目标讲清。
scenario_en: Sketching an enterprise RAG model architecture, the interviewer wants each of the retrieval → reranking → generation stages' objectives made clear.
q: 企业 RAG 三阶段流水线各自优化什么目标？
q_en: What objective does each stage of the enterprise RAG pipeline optimize?
why: 三阶段各优化一个不同目标：检索最大化召回(宽撒网别漏)、重排最大化精度(把最相关的排前)、生成最大化忠实度(只根据给定上下文作答别幻觉)。每阶段独立可调、有各自延迟预算，才能分别优化。
why_en: Each stage optimizes a distinct objective: retrieval maximizes recall (wide net, don't miss), reranking maximizes precision (top-rank the most relevant), and generation maximizes faithfulness (answer only from the given context, no hallucination), each independently tunable with its own latency budget.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["查询"] --> R["检索
最大化召回 ~20ms"] --> RR["重排
最大化精度 ~50ms"] --> G["生成
最大化忠实度 ~500ms"] --> A["带引用的答案"]
options: 三阶段都优化召回，只是模型不同、跑得快慢不同
检索最大化召回、重排最大化精度、生成最大化忠实度，各阶段独立可调、有各自延迟预算
检索最大化精度、重排最大化忠实度、生成最大化召回
三阶段其实是一个大模型端到端做，不用分开优化
options_en: All three optimize recall, just with different models and speeds.
Retrieval maximizes recall, reranking maximizes precision, generation maximizes faithfulness — each independently tunable with its own latency budget.
Retrieval maximizes precision, reranking maximizes faithfulness, generation maximizes recall.
The three are really one big end-to-end model, no separate optimization.
optionExplanations: 三阶段目标不同：召回、精度、忠实度各管一段，不是同一目标的三种速度。
对；分三段正是为了让召回、精度、忠实度各自独立调优，一段的旋钮不干扰另一段。
映射错了：检索管召回、重排管精度、生成管忠实度，别对调。
端到端一个模型无法分别为召回/精度/忠实度调优，也没法给每段单独的延迟预算。
optionExplanations_en: The three have different goals — recall, precision, faithfulness — not one goal at three speeds.
Correct — splitting into three lets recall, precision, and faithfulness be tuned independently without one stage's knobs disturbing another.
Mismapped: retrieval handles recall, reranking precision, generation faithfulness — don't swap them.
One end-to-end model can't tune recall/precision/faithfulness separately or give each stage its own latency budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成的答案严格基于给定上下文、不编造，是生成阶段的优化目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithfulness means the generated answer is grounded strictly in the given context without fabrication, the generation stage's objective.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：先检索文档块，再让 LLM 基于块生成有依据的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves chunks first, then has the LLM generate a grounded answer from them.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 面试官问三阶段各用什么模型、各占多少延迟预算，想看你对流水线的量级感。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks which model and latency budget each stage uses, checking your sense of the pipeline's magnitudes.
q: 检索/重排/生成三阶段的模型类型和延迟预算大致怎么分？
q_en: Roughly how do model type and latency budget split across retrieval/reranking/generation?
why: 检索用 bi-encoder+BM25、约 20ms；重排用 cross-encoder、约 50ms；生成用 LLM、约 500ms。延迟从检索到生成逐级放大，生成占大头，所以前两段要尽量便宜、把候选收窄后才交给昂贵的 LLM。
why_en: Retrieval uses a bi-encoder + BM25 (~20ms), reranking a cross-encoder (~50ms), generation an LLM (~500ms); latency grows down the pipeline with generation dominating, so the first two stages stay cheap and narrow candidates before the costly LLM.
tradeoff: 前段便宜快(检索/重排收窄候选) vs 生成昂贵慢(LLM 占大头延迟)
options: 三阶段延迟差不多，都在 500ms 量级
生成最快(~20ms)、检索最慢(~500ms)，正好相反
检索 bi-encoder+BM25 ~20ms、重排 cross-encoder ~50ms、生成 LLM ~500ms，延迟逐级放大、生成占大头
三阶段都用同一个 LLM，延迟一样
options_en: All three have similar latency, around 500ms.
Generation is fastest (~20ms) and retrieval slowest (~500ms) — the reverse.
Retrieval bi-encoder+BM25 ~20ms, reranking cross-encoder ~50ms, generation LLM ~500ms — latency grows down the pipeline, generation dominates.
All three use the same LLM with equal latency.
optionExplanations: 三阶段延迟量级差一个数量级，生成 ~500ms 远大于检索 ~20ms，不是差不多。
说反了：检索最快、生成最慢，正因如此才在生成前收窄候选。
对；便宜的检索/重排先收窄，昂贵的 LLM 只处理少量精排后的块，延迟分配才合理。
三阶段用不同模型：编码器做检索/重排、LLM 做生成，延迟量级不同。
optionExplanations_en: The stages differ by an order of magnitude — generation ~500ms far exceeds retrieval ~20ms, not similar.
Backwards: retrieval is fastest and generation slowest, which is why candidates are narrowed before generation.
Correct — cheap retrieval/reranking narrow first so the costly LLM handles only a few reranked chunks, a sensible latency split.
The stages use different models — encoders for retrieval/reranking, an LLM for generation — with different latency magnitudes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分别把查询和文档编码成向量再比距离，快但不建模两者交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bi-encoder encodes query and document into vectors separately then compares distance — fast but models no interaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档拼在一起送入 transformer 联合打分，精但慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder feeds the query and document jointly through a transformer for a joint score — precise but slow.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 检索为了召回把网撒得很宽，一次拉回 20-50 个候选块，但 LLM 上下文实际只放得下 5-10 个。
scenario_en: Retrieval casts a wide net for recall, pulling 20-50 candidate chunks, but the LLM context only holds 5-10.
q: 为什么在检索和生成之间还要插一个重排阶段？
q_en: Why insert a reranking stage between retrieval and generation?
why: 检索为召回撒宽网(20-50 块)，但上下文只放得下 5-10 块，必须有人把这一大堆里真正最相关的挑到前面。重排就是这个精度过滤器：把宽候选集变成精排短名单，让塞进上下文的都是最相关的。
why_en: Retrieval casts a wide net for recall (20-50 chunks) but the context fits only 5-10, so something must pick the truly most relevant to the top — reranking is that precision filter, turning the broad set into a precise shortlist so only the most relevant enter the context.
options: 重排是精度过滤器：把 20-50 的宽候选集精排成 5-10 的短名单，保证塞进上下文的都最相关
重排只是把检索结果随机打乱，增加多样性
重排负责把候选块翻译成另一种语言
重排是可选的，直接把 20-50 块全塞进上下文最省事
options_en: Reranking is a precision filter: it condenses the 20-50 broad set into a 5-10 shortlist so only the most relevant enter the context.
Reranking just randomly shuffles retrieval results for diversity.
Reranking translates candidate chunks into another language.
Reranking is optional; just stuff all 20-50 chunks into the context.
optionExplanations: 对；召回宽但上下文窄，重排负责在两者之间把最相关的精排到前列，是让上下文装配可行的关键。
打乱只会破坏相关性排序，与重排要提升精度的目标相反。
翻译不是重排的职责，重排是按相关性给候选打分排序。
20-50 块塞不进只放 5-10 的上下文，且会引入大量噪声块，必须重排收窄。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — recall is wide but context narrow, so reranking picks the most relevant to the top between them, making context assembly feasible.
Shuffling destroys the relevance order, opposite to reranking's precision goal.
Translation isn't reranking's job; reranking scores and orders candidates by relevance.
20-50 chunks won't fit a 5-10 context and add noise chunks, so reranking must narrow them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在检索召回的候选集里按相关性精排，选出最相关的少数进上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reranking re-orders the retrieved candidate set by relevance to pick the few most relevant for the context.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 重排要在少量候选块上追求最高相关性精度，愿意为此付更高的单次计算成本。
scenario_en: Reranking wants top relevance precision on a few candidate chunks and will pay a higher per-item compute cost for it.
q: 重排阶段该用 cross-encoder 还是 bi-encoder，为什么？
q_en: Should reranking use a cross-encoder or a bi-encoder, and why?
why: 用 cross-encoder：把查询和每个块拼在一起送进 transformer 联合打分，能捕捉 bi-encoder 漏掉的查询-文档交互(bi-encoder 各自独立编码再比向量，看不到细粒度交互)，精度高。代价是 O(n) 慢，所以只在少量候选上跑。
why_en: Use a cross-encoder: it feeds the query and each chunk jointly through a transformer to capture query-document interactions a bi-encoder misses (bi-encoders encode each independently then compare vectors), giving higher precision, at O(n) cost so it only runs on few candidates.
tradeoff: cross-encoder(联合打分精度高但 O(n) 慢) vs bi-encoder(独立编码快但漏交互)
whenOtherWins: 第一阶段海量检索(在整个索引上打分)必须用 bi-encoder，因为可预计算文档向量、毫秒级 ANN，cross-encoder 在那个规模上跑不动。
options: 用 bi-encoder，独立编码查询和块再比向量，最快所以最适合重排
用 cross-encoder：查询和块拼一起联合打分，捕捉 bi-encoder 漏掉的交互，精度高，只在少量候选上跑
重排不需要模型，按检索分数直接用就行
用一个大 LLM 给每个块写摘要当重排分数
options_en: Use a bi-encoder, encoding query and chunk independently then comparing vectors — fastest, so best for reranking.
Use a cross-encoder: score query and chunk jointly to capture interactions a bi-encoder misses, high precision, run only on few candidates.
Reranking needs no model; just reuse the retrieval scores.
Use a big LLM to summarize each chunk as the rerank score.
optionExplanations: bi-encoder 快是因为独立编码、不建模交互，正因如此精度不如 cross-encoder，做不好重排的精排。
对；联合打分让模型看到查询和块的细粒度交互，精度高；候选已被收窄到 20-50，O(n) 成本可承受。
直接复用检索分数就等于没重排，检索的召回分不足以做精度排序。
让 LLM 逐块摘要又慢又贵，还不如 cross-encoder 直接给相关性分。
optionExplanations_en: A bi-encoder is fast because it encodes independently without modeling interaction, so it's less precise and poor at fine reranking.
Correct — joint scoring lets the model see fine query-chunk interactions for high precision, and with candidates narrowed to 20-50 the O(n) cost is affordable.
Reusing retrieval scores is no reranking; recall-oriented scores don't give precise ordering.
Summarizing each chunk with an LLM is slow and costly, worse than a cross-encoder's direct relevance score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档拼接送入 transformer 联合打分，捕捉两者交互，精但 O(n)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder concatenates query and document into a transformer for a joint score, capturing interaction — precise but O(n).

termDefinitions.fullName: BERT = Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的 cross-encoder 重排器基于微调的 BERT(如 bge-reranker)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common cross-encoder rerankers are fine-tuned BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) models such as bge-reranker.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 面试官要你讲清 cross-encoder 和 bi-encoder 的机制差别，以及为什么两阶段各用一个。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants the mechanism difference between cross- and bi-encoders and why each stage uses one.
q: cross-encoder 和 bi-encoder 在编码方式、速度、精度上如何对比？
q_en: How do cross- and bi-encoders contrast on encoding, speed, and precision?
why: bi-encoder 各自独立编码查询和文档、可预计算文档向量，检索时毫秒级比向量、快但漏细交互；cross-encoder 把查询和文档拼一起联合过 transformer，看得到交互、精度高但每对都要现算、O(n) 慢。所以检索用 bi-encoder、重排用 cross-encoder。
why_en: A bi-encoder encodes query and document separately with precomputable doc vectors, so retrieval compares vectors in milliseconds — fast but missing fine interaction; a cross-encoder feeds them jointly through a transformer, seeing interactions for high precision but computing each pair live at O(n), so retrieval uses bi-encoders and reranking cross-encoders.
tradeoff: bi-encoder(独立编码、可预算、快但漏交互) vs cross-encoder(联合打分、精但每对现算、慢)
options: 两者机制一样，只是名字不同
cross-encoder 独立编码更快、bi-encoder 联合打分更慢，正好相反
bi-encoder 独立编码可预计算、快但漏交互；cross-encoder 联合打分精度高但每对现算、O(n) 慢
两者都必须实时联合打分，无法预计算
options_en: The two mechanisms are the same, just different names.
Cross-encoders encode independently and are faster; bi-encoders score jointly and are slower — the reverse.
Bi-encoder encodes independently (precomputable, fast) but misses interaction; cross-encoder scores jointly (high precision) but computes each pair live at O(n).
Both must score jointly in real time and can't precompute.
optionExplanations: 两者编码方式根本不同，导致速度和精度分野，不是同一机制。
说反了：bi-encoder 独立编码更快、cross-encoder 联合打分更慢。
对；这条差别正解释了为什么海量检索用可预计算的 bi-encoder、少量重排用高精度的 cross-encoder。
bi-encoder 恰恰能预计算文档向量，说都不能预计算是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Their encoding differs fundamentally, driving the speed/precision split — not one mechanism.
Backwards: bi-encoders encode independently and are faster, cross-encoders score jointly and are slower.
Correct — this difference is why massive retrieval uses precomputable bi-encoders and small reranking uses high-precision cross-encoders.
Bi-encoders can precompute doc vectors, so saying neither can precompute is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 计算量随候选数 n 线性增长；cross-encoder 每个候选都要单独过一次模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(n) means cost grows linearly with the candidate count n; a cross-encoder runs the model once per candidate.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: cross-encoder 重排的计算量随候选数 O(n) 线性增长，而重排阶段的延迟预算约 50ms。
scenario_en: Cross-encoder reranking cost grows O(n) with candidate count, and the reranking budget is ~50ms.
q: 「cross-encoder 是 O(n)、预算 ~50ms」这组约束在设计里怎么用？
q_en: How do you use the 'cross-encoder O(n), ~50ms budget' constraints in design?
why: 因为 O(n)：候选越多重排越慢，要把送进重排的候选数封顶在 20-50 才能压进 ~50ms 预算。这不是背数字，而是「复杂度×预算」定出候选上限——检索召回可以宽，但交给重排前必须先截到这个量级。
why_en: Because it's O(n), more candidates mean slower reranking, so cap the candidates entering reranking at 20-50 to fit the ~50ms budget — not a number to memorize but complexity × budget setting the cap: retrieval can recall wide, but must be trimmed to this magnitude before reranking.
options: 把候选数封顶在 20-50：O(n) 下候选越多越慢，这个上限才压得进 ~50ms 预算
候选越多越好，直接把检索的几千个全送进重排
50ms 是要背的硬数字，考点就是记住 50
O(n) 说明重排和候选数无关，塞多少都一样快
options_en: Cap candidates at 20-50: under O(n) more candidates are slower, and this cap fits the ~50ms budget.
More candidates are better; send all thousands from retrieval into reranking.
50ms is a hard number to memorize; the point is recalling 50.
O(n) means reranking is independent of candidate count, so any number is equally fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: 送进重排的候选块数量上限，由 cross-encoder 的 O(n) 成本和延迟预算共同决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The candidate cap is the max chunks entering reranking, set jointly by the cross-encoder's O(n) cost and the latency budget.

optionMeanings: 选项主张：把候选数封顶在 20-50：O(n) 下候选越多越慢，这个上限才压得进 ~50ms 预算。
选项主张：候选越多越好，直接把检索的几千个全送进重排。
选项主张：50ms 是要背的硬数字，考点就是记住 50。
选项主张：O(n) 说明重排和候选数无关，塞多少都一样快。

会让系统依赖「候选越多越好，直接把检索的几千个全送进重排」这个前提。

会让系统依赖「O(n) 说明重排和候选数无关，塞多少都一样快」这个前提。

More candidates are better; send all thousands from retrieval into reranking.
50ms is a hard number to memorize; the point is recalling 50.
O(n) means reranking is independent of candidate count, so any number is equally fast.
optionDirectness_en: Use when it's O(n), more candidates mean slower reranking, so cap the candidates entering reranking at 20-50 to fit the ~50ms budget — not a number to memorize but complexity × budget setting the cap: retrieval can recall wide, but must be trimmed to this magnitude before reranking.
Only fits when this statement is true: more candidates are better; send all thousands from retrieval into reranking.
Only fits when this statement is true: 50ms is a hard number to memorize; the point is recalling 50.
Only fits when this statement is true: o(n) means reranking is independent of candidate count, so any number is equally fast.

It commits the design to this assumption: More candidates are better; send all thousands from retrieval into reranking.

scenario: 通用重排器在法务/医疗语料上分不清「相关」和「看着相关但其实不对」的块，精度不够。
scenario_en: A generic reranker can't tell relevant from look-relevant-but-wrong chunks on legal/medical corpora, so precision is low.
q: 重排精度在专业领域不够，最有效的提升手段是什么？
q_en: What most effectively improves reranking precision in a specialized domain?
why: 在领域相关性判断(query-chunk 是否真相关的人工标注)上微调重排器：让它学会本领域「什么才算真相关」，精度提升很大。通用重排器没见过领域判据，分不清近似相关和真正相关。
why_en: Fine-tune the reranker on domain relevance judgments (human labels of whether a query-chunk pair is truly relevant): it learns what counts as relevant in this domain for a big precision gain, whereas a generic reranker hasn't seen domain criteria and confuses near-relevant with truly relevant.
tradeoff: 领域微调重排器(精度大涨但要标注判断) vs 通用重排器(零成本但领域精度不足)
whenOtherWins: 若语料是通用日常文本、没有专业相关性判据，现成通用重排器已够，微调是多余成本。
options: 把候选数从 20 提到 200，让重排看更多块
换更大的生成 LLM，让它在生成时纠正相关性
在领域相关性判断上微调重排器，让它学会本领域什么算真相关，精度大涨
关掉重排，直接用检索分数排序
options_en: Raise candidates from 20 to 200 so the reranker sees more chunks.
Switch to a bigger generation LLM to fix relevance at generation.
Fine-tune the reranker on domain relevance judgments so it learns what counts as truly relevant, for a big precision gain.
Turn off reranking and order by retrieval score.
optionExplanations: 加候选数只会撑爆 O(n) 延迟预算，不解决「分不清真相关」这个精度问题。
生成 LLM 只能用重排后给它的块，重排排错了 LLM 补不回来。
对；用领域标注微调让重排器习得本领域的相关性判据，是提升领域精度最直接的手段。
用检索分数排序等于放弃精度过滤，专业领域的近似相关块会大量混入。
optionExplanations_en: More candidates only blow the O(n) budget and don't fix the precision problem of confusing true relevance.
The generation LLM can only use the chunks reranking gave it; if reranking mis-ordered, it can't recover.
Correct — domain-labeled fine-tuning teaches the reranker this domain's relevance criteria, the most direct precision fix.
Ordering by retrieval score abandons the precision filter, letting many near-relevant chunks in on specialized domains.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工标注某查询-文档块对是否真正相关，用来微调重排器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relevance judgment is a human label of whether a query-chunk pair is truly relevant, used to fine-tune a reranker.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 一个 8K 上下文窗口，并不是有 8K token 全给检索到的文档块用。
scenario_en: An 8K context window is not 8K tokens all available for the retrieved chunks.
q: 检索块真正可用的「token 预算」怎么算？
q_en: How is the actual 'token budget' for retrieved chunks computed?
why: token 预算 = 窗口大小 − 系统提示 − few-shot 示例 − 为输出预留的 token。8K 窗口扣掉这些后剩下的才是能塞文档块的额度，所以规划上下文不能按窗口全长算。
why_en: Token budget = window size − system prompt − few-shot examples − output reservation; only what remains after subtracting these from the 8K window can hold chunks, so you can't plan context by the full window length.
options: token 预算 = 窗口全长，8K 就是 8K 全给文档块
token 预算 = 窗口大小 − 系统提示 − few-shot 示例 − 输出预留，剩下的才给文档块
token 预算 = 窗口 × 2，因为输入输出各算一遍
token 预算只由文档块数量决定，与系统提示无关
options_en: Token budget = full window; 8K is all 8K for chunks.
Token budget = window − system prompt − few-shot examples − output reservation; only the remainder holds chunks.
Token budget = window × 2, since input and output each count.
Token budget depends only on chunk count, unrelated to the system prompt.
optionExplanations: 系统提示、few-shot、输出都占窗口，按全长算会溢出，真正给块的没那么多。
对；先扣掉固定开销和输出预留，剩下的才是块的额度，这是上下文装配的第一步。
窗口是输入输出共享的总额度，不能翻倍，输出还要预留占用。
系统提示等固定开销直接吃掉窗口，预算当然和它有关。
optionExplanations_en: System prompt, few-shot, and output all occupy the window, so counting the full length overflows; chunks get much less.
Correct — subtract fixed overhead and output reservation first; the remainder is the chunk budget, the first step of context assembly.
The window is a shared input+output total, not doubled, and output must be reserved.
Fixed overhead like the system prompt eats the window, so the budget does depend on it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文窗口扣掉系统提示、few-shot、输出预留后，剩给文档块的 token 额度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The token budget is the window minus the system prompt, few-shot, and output reservation — the tokens left for chunks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 放进提示里的几条示范样例，引导 LLM 的输出格式或行为，占用窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Few-shot examples are demonstration samples placed in the prompt to steer the LLM's format or behavior, occupying the window.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 重排后的候选块加起来超过了 token 预算，你要决定放哪些、溢出的那块怎么处理。
scenario_en: The reranked chunks together exceed the token budget, and you must decide which to include and how to handle the overflow.
q: 上下文装配的基础做法是什么？
q_en: What is the baseline approach to context assembly?
why: 贪心选择+截断：按重排分从高到低依次加块，直到预算用尽；对刚好溢出的那一块，在句子边界处截断(而不是切在 token 中间)，保住语义连贯。这是简单可靠的基线。
why_en: Greedy selection + truncation: add chunks in descending rerank-score order until the budget is exhausted, then truncate the overflowing chunk at a sentence boundary (not mid-token) to keep coherence — a simple, reliable baseline.
tradeoff: 贪心+句界截断(简单可靠但可能砍掉低分块细节) vs 相关性加权分配(更细但更复杂)
whenOtherWins: 若各块相关性差异很大、想让高分块拿更多篇幅、低分块被摘要而非硬截，就升级到相关性加权分配。
options: 把所有块都硬塞进去，超预算也不管
按重排分从高到低加块直到预算用尽，溢出的那块在句子边界处截断保连贯
随机挑几块放进去，反正 LLM 能理解
只放分最低的块，给高分块省空间
options_en: Cram in all chunks, ignoring the budget overflow.
Add chunks in descending rerank score until the budget is used, then truncate the overflowing chunk at a sentence boundary for coherence.
Pick a few chunks at random; the LLM will understand.
Include only the lowest-scored chunks to save room for high-scored ones.
optionExplanations: 硬塞超预算会被模型截断或报错，且截在哪不可控，容易砍掉关键内容。
对；按分贪心装配 + 句界截断，既优先放最相关的、又避免把一句话切碎，是可靠基线。
随机挑放弃了相关性排序，把重排的成果浪费掉。
只放低分块本末倒置，最相关的高分块反而进不去。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming over budget gets truncated or errors, with an uncontrolled cut point that may drop key content.
Correct — greedy assembly by score plus sentence-boundary truncation prioritizes the most relevant while avoiding cutting a sentence apart, a reliable baseline.
Random picks abandon the relevance order, wasting the reranking work.
Including only low-scored chunks is backwards; the most relevant high-scored chunks would be excluded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把溢出的块在句号等句子边界处切断，而非切在 token 中间，保语义连贯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentence-boundary truncation cuts an overflowing chunk at a sentence end rather than mid-token, preserving coherence.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 候选块相关性差异很大：头部两块高度相关、后面几块只是勉强相关，token 预算又有限。
scenario_en: Candidate chunks vary widely in relevance: the top two are highly relevant, the rest only marginally, and the token budget is tight.
q: 比贪心截断更精细的上下文分配怎么做？
q_en: What is a more refined context allocation than greedy truncation?
why: 用相关性加权分配：分越高的块分到越多 token 预算(完整保留)，分低的块被摘要压缩或直接丢弃，而不是一刀切均分。这样把有限预算集中在最相关内容上，比贪心+硬截更省 token、信息密度更高。
why_en: Use relevance-weighted allocation: higher-scored chunks get more of the token budget (kept in full) while lower ones are summarized or dropped, rather than a flat split, concentrating the limited budget on the most relevant content for higher information density than greedy hard truncation.
tradeoff: 相关性加权分配(高分块给更多篇幅、低分摘要/丢弃但更复杂) vs 贪心均等(简单但浪费在低分块上)
whenOtherWins: 若各块相关性接近、预算也够，贪心+句界截断更简单，没必要上摘要和加权的复杂度。
options: 给每块分同样多的 token，公平均分
相关性加权分配：高分块给更多预算完整保留，低分块摘要压缩或丢弃
把所有块都摘要成一句话再放进去
只按块的长度分配，长的给更多预算
options_en: Give every chunk equal tokens, a fair split.
Relevance-weighted allocation: high-scored chunks get more budget in full, low-scored ones summarized or dropped.
Summarize every chunk to one sentence before including it.
Allocate purely by chunk length; longer chunks get more budget.
optionExplanations: 均分把预算浪费在勉强相关的块上，挤掉了高分块本该完整保留的内容。
对；按相关性把预算倾斜给高分块、压缩或丢弃低分块，让有限上下文信息密度最高。
把高分块也摘要成一句会丢关键细节，忠实度反而下降。
按长度分配与相关性无关，可能给一个又长又不相关的块最多篇幅。
optionExplanations_en: An equal split wastes budget on marginally relevant chunks and squeezes out content the high-scored chunks should keep in full.
Correct — skewing budget toward high-scored chunks and compressing/dropping low ones maximizes information density in limited context.
Summarizing even high-scored chunks to one sentence loses key detail, lowering faithfulness.
Allocating by length ignores relevance and may give a long, irrelevant chunk the most room.

termDefinitions.term: relevance-weighted allocation / 相关性加权分配
termDefinitions.meaning: 按重排分把 token 预算倾斜给高分块，低分块摘要或丢弃。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relevance-weighted allocation skews the token budget toward high-scored chunks and summarizes or drops low ones.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 你把最相关的块随手放在了一长串上下文的正中间，前后堆着不太相关的块。
scenario_en: You place the most relevant chunk right in the middle of a long context, padded before and after with less relevant chunks.
q: 「lost-in-the-middle」效应会导致什么，根因是什么？
q_en: What does the lost-in-the-middle effect cause, and why?
why: LLM 更充分利用上下文开头和结尾的信息，中间的相对被忽略。把最相关的块埋在中间→模型对它关注不足→即使检索/重排都对，答案仍可能漏掉这条关键证据。所以要按位置感知排序，把最相关的放首尾。
why_en: LLMs use information at the beginning and end of the context more than the middle, so burying the most relevant chunk in the middle gets it under-attended and the answer may miss that key evidence even though retrieval and reranking were correct — hence position-aware ordering puts the most relevant first and last.
diagram:
flowchart LR B["开头
高关注"] --> M["中间
低关注"] --> E["结尾
高关注"]
options: 没有影响，LLM 对上下文各位置一视同仁
LLM 更关注首尾、忽略中间→最相关块埋中间被关注不足→答案漏关键证据；要位置感知排序
只会让生成变慢，是性能问题
会让 LLM 更关注中间，所以最相关的就该放中间
options_en: No effect; the LLM treats all context positions equally.
The LLM favors the start and end and neglects the middle → a middle-buried top chunk is under-attended → the answer misses key evidence; use position-aware ordering.
It only slows generation — a performance issue.
It makes the LLM focus on the middle, so the most relevant chunk belongs in the middle.
optionExplanations: 实证上 LLM 对首尾利用明显强于中间，位置并非一视同仁。
对；这正是 lost-in-the-middle：把最相关的埋中间会被忽略，修法是把它放首尾。
这是关注度问题不是速度问题，影响的是答案质量而非延迟。
说反了：中间是被忽略的区域，最相关的恰恰不该放中间。
optionExplanations_en: Empirically the LLM uses the start and end far more than the middle, so positions aren't equal.
Correct — this is lost-in-the-middle: burying the top chunk in the middle gets it ignored, fixed by placing it at the ends.
It's an attention issue not speed, affecting answer quality not latency.
Backwards: the middle is the neglected region, so the most relevant chunk should not go there.

termDefinitions.meaning: LLM 对上下文首尾信息利用强、对中间信息利用弱的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lost-in-the-middle is the phenomenon that LLMs use context at the start and end more than in the middle.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 已知 LLM 对上下文首尾利用更强、中间更弱，你要安排 5 个重排后块的摆放顺序。
scenario_en: Knowing LLMs use the start and end more than the middle, you must order 5 reranked chunks in the context.
q: 怎么摆放块的顺序来对抗 lost-in-the-middle？
q_en: How do you order chunks to counter lost-in-the-middle?
why: 用位置感知排序：把最相关的块放在开头和结尾这两个高关注位置，把相对次要的放中间。这样即便存在中间迷失，最关键的证据仍落在模型最能利用的位置上。
why_en: Use position-aware ordering: put the most relevant chunks at the start and end (the high-attention positions) and less relevant ones in the middle, so even with lost-in-the-middle the key evidence sits where the model uses it best.
tradeoff: 位置感知排序(把最相关放首尾、对抗中间迷失) vs 纯按分顺序堆(简单但最相关可能落中间)
whenOtherWins: 若上下文很短(只有 2-3 块)、根本没有「中间」可言，纯按分顺序放就够，位置技巧收益不大。
options: 按重排分从高到低顺序堆，最相关的自然排第一，后面递减
把最相关的块放开头和结尾这两个高关注位，次要的放中间
把最相关的放正中间，因为那里最显眼
随机打乱顺序，避免模型形成位置偏好
options_en: Stack in descending rerank score; the most relevant is first, then decreasing.
Put the most relevant chunks at the start and end (high-attention positions), less relevant in the middle.
Put the most relevant in the dead center since it's most prominent.
Shuffle randomly to keep the model from forming a position bias.
optionExplanations: 纯降序会把第二、第三相关的块推到中间的被忽略区，浪费它们的价值。
对；把最相关的放首尾正好落在模型最能利用的位置，是对抗中间迷失的直接做法。
正中间恰恰是被忽略的区域，把最相关放那里适得其反。
随机打乱既不利用首尾优势，也可能把最关键证据丢进中间。
optionExplanations_en: Pure descending order pushes the 2nd/3rd most relevant into the neglected middle, wasting their value.
Correct — placing the most relevant at the ends lands them where the model uses them best, the direct counter to lost-in-the-middle.
The dead center is the neglected region, so putting the most relevant there backfires.
Random shuffling neither exploits the ends nor prevents key evidence landing in the middle.

termDefinitions.term: position-aware ordering / 位置感知排序
termDefinitions.meaning: 按 LLM 对首尾关注更强的特点，把最相关块放到开头和结尾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position-aware ordering places the most relevant chunks at the start and end, exploiting the LLM's stronger attention there.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 有人提议：把上下文窗口从 8K 换成 128K，把更多块一股脑塞进去，答案就会更好。
scenario_en: Someone proposes swapping the 8K window for 128K and dumping in far more chunks to get better answers.
q: 「窗口越大、塞越多块，答案一定越好」这个想法对吗？
q_en: Is 'a bigger window with more chunks always gives better answers' correct?
why: 不对。更大窗口≠更好答案：块越多噪声越多、关键证据更容易落进被忽略的中间(lost-in-the-middle)，还更慢更贵。正解仍是重排收窄+位置感知排序，把少而精的块放对位置，而非无脑塞满。
why_en: No — a bigger window doesn't mean better answers: more chunks add noise, key evidence is more likely buried in the neglected middle (lost-in-the-middle), and it's slower and costlier; the fix is still reranking to narrow plus position-aware ordering, not stuffing.
options: 对，窗口越大能塞越多，信息越全答案越好
不对：块越多噪声越多、关键证据更易落进被忽略的中间，还更慢更贵；仍要重排收窄+位置排序
对，只要塞满窗口就不用重排了
不对，因为大窗口会让模型崩溃无法生成
options_en: Yes; a bigger window holds more, so more complete info gives better answers.
No: more chunks add noise, key evidence is more likely lost in the neglected middle, and it's slower and costlier; still narrow via reranking plus position ordering.
Yes; just fill the window and you can skip reranking.
No, because a big window crashes the model so it can't generate.
optionExplanations: 更全不等于更好：无关块会稀释注意力，关键证据被埋，答案质量反而下降。
对；大窗口引入噪声和中间迷失、又慢又贵，正解是收窄+摆对位置而非塞满。
塞满不做重排会把大量噪声块喂给模型，正是要避免的做法。
大窗口不会让模型崩溃，问题是注意力稀释和中间迷失，不是无法生成。
optionExplanations_en: More complete isn't better: irrelevant chunks dilute attention and bury key evidence, lowering quality.
Correct — a big window adds noise and lost-in-the-middle and is slow and costly, so narrow and position well rather than stuff.
Stuffing without reranking feeds many noise chunks to the model, exactly what to avoid.
A big window doesn't crash the model; the issue is attention dilution and lost-in-the-middle, not inability to generate.

termDefinitions.meaning: LLM 单次能读入的最大 token 数；更大不自动带来更好答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context window is the max tokens an LLM reads at once; larger doesn't automatically yield better answers.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 上下文窗口 4096 token，其中 800 留给系统提示+few-shot+输出；重排后候选块按分从高到低是 900/800/700/600/500 token。
scenario_en: A 4096-token window with 800 reserved for prompt+output; reranked chunks by score are 900/800/700/600/500 tokens.
q: 这个窗口能放下几个块，第 5 个怎么处理？
q_en: How many chunks fit, and what happens to the 5th?
why: token 预算 = 4096 − 800 = 3296。按分贪心塞：900+800+700+600 = 3000(剩 296)，第 5 个 500 塞不下→在剩余 296 内于句子边界处截断。这演示了「预算=窗口−开销」再贪心装配的完整算法。
why_en: Token budget = 4096 − 800 = 3296; greedily add by score: 900+800+700+600 = 3000 (296 left), the 5th (500) doesn't fit → truncate it at a sentence boundary within the remaining 296, demonstrating budget = window − overhead then greedy assembly.
options: 5 个块全放得下，4096 足够大
只放得下 2 个块，其余全部丢弃
预算 4096：5 个全放，最后一个不用截断
options_en: All 5 fit; 4096 is big enough.
Only 2 fit; discard the rest.
Budget 3296: the first 4 (900+800+700+600=3000) fit, the 5th (500) overflows and is truncated at a sentence boundary within the remaining 296.
Budget 4096: all 5 fit; the last needs no truncation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按分从高到低依次加块直到预算用尽的装配策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Greedy selection adds chunks in descending score until the budget is exhausted.

optionMeanings: 选项主张：5 个块全放得下，4096 足够大。
选项主张：只放得下 2 个块，其余全部丢弃。
选项主张：预算 3296。
选项主张：预算 4096：5 个全放，最后一个不用截断。
optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
适合本题给出的约束。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让系统依赖「5 个块全放得下，4096 足够大」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只放得下 2 个块，其余全部丢弃」这个前提。
会让方案围绕「预算 3296」展开。
会让系统依赖「预算 4096：5 个全放，最后一个不用截断」这个前提。
optionMeanings_en: All 5 fit; 4096 is big enough.
Only 2 fit; discard the rest.
Budget 3296.
Budget 4096: all 5 fit; the last needs no truncation.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: all 5 fit; 4096 is big enough.
Only fits when this statement is true: only 2 fit; discard the rest.
Use when token budget = 4096 − 800 = 3296.
Only fits when this statement is true: budget 4096: all 5 fit; the last needs no truncation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It commits the design to this assumption: All 5 fit; 4096 is big enough.
It commits the design to this assumption: Only 2 fit; discard the rest.
It commits the design to this path: Budget 3296.
It commits the design to this assumption: Budget 4096: all 5 fit; the last needs no truncation.
category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 企业合规要求 RAG 不泄露 PII、不越权、不幻觉、不输出有害内容，单一防护措施不够。
scenario_en: Enterprise compliance requires the RAG to not leak PII, not exceed permissions, not hallucinate, and not output harmful content — one guardrail isn't enough.
q: 企业 RAG 的护栏为什么要分三层，怎么对应流水线位置？
q_en: Why are enterprise RAG guardrails in three layers, and how do they map to pipeline position?
why: 护栏按流水线位置分三层做纵深防御：生成前(块进 prompt 前做 PII 脱敏、权限过滤)、prompt 级(下 grounding 指令、强制引用)、生成后(核验引用、内容安全、幻觉检测)。任一层都不足以单独兜住合规，分层各挡一类风险。
why_en: Guardrails split into three layers by pipeline position for defense-in-depth: pre-generation (PII redaction and permission filtering before chunks enter the prompt), prompt-level (grounding instructions, citation enforcement), and post-generation (citation verification, content safety, hallucination detection) — no single layer suffices, so each blocks a class of risk.
diagram:
flowchart LR Pre["生成前
PII脱敏/权限过滤"] --> Prm["prompt级
grounding/强制引用"] --> Post["生成后
引用核验/安全/幻觉检测"]
options: 护栏只需一层放在生成后就够，前面不用管
护栏按流水线位置分三层(生成前/prompt级/生成后)做纵深防御，各挡一类风险，单层不足以兜住合规
三层护栏都放在生成后，重复三遍更保险
护栏和流水线位置无关，随便放哪层都一样
options_en: One guardrail after generation is enough; the earlier stages need none.
Guardrails split into three layers by pipeline position (pre/prompt/post) for defense-in-depth, each blocking a class of risk, since one layer can't cover compliance.
All three layers go after generation, repeated thrice for safety.
Guardrails are unrelated to pipeline position; put them anywhere.
optionExplanations: 只在生成后拦，PII 早已进了 prompt、越权块早已被读，泄露已发生，拦不住。
对；每层挡不同风险——生成前防泄露、prompt 级促忠实、生成后查幻觉，分层才覆盖全。
三层都堆生成后无法阻止生成前的泄露和越权，位置错了重复也没用。
位置决定能挡住哪类风险，PII 必须生成前挡、幻觉必须生成后查，不能随意。
optionExplanations_en: Blocking only after generation is too late — PII already entered the prompt and unauthorized chunks were already read, so the leak already happened.
Correct — each layer blocks a different risk: pre-gen prevents leakage, prompt-level drives faithfulness, post-gen catches hallucination, so layering covers all.
Stacking all three after generation can't stop pre-generation leakage or over-permission; repetition in the wrong place doesn't help.
Position decides which risk you can block — PII must be caught pre-gen and hallucination post-gen — so it can't be arbitrary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 RAG 流水线不同位置加的安全/合规检查，纵深防御防泄露、越权、幻觉、有害输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guardrails are safety/compliance checks at different pipeline points, a defense-in-depth against leakage, over-permission, hallucination, and harmful output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 个人可识别信息(如身份证号、邮箱、电话)，合规要求在进 prompt 前脱敏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PII (Personally Identifiable Information) like SSNs, emails, and phones must be redacted before entering the prompt for compliance.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 生成前这一层要在文档块进入 prompt 之前，先挡住会造成泄露或越权的风险。
scenario_en: The pre-generation layer must block leakage and over-permission risks before chunks enter the prompt.
q: 生成前(pre-generation)护栏包含哪些措施？(多选)
q_en: Which measures make up pre-generation guardrails? (multiple)
why: 生成前三招都在块进 prompt 之前动手：PII 检测与脱敏(用 NER 或正则抓身份证/邮箱/电话，满足 GDPR/HIPAA)、基于 ACL 的权限过滤(把用户无权看的块直接剔掉)、块相关性阈值(低于阈值的弱相关块不进 prompt)。生成后核验是另一层的事。
why_en: All three act before chunks enter the prompt: PII detection and redaction (NER or regex for SSN/email/phone, for GDPR/HIPAA), ACL-based permission filtering (drop chunks the user may not see), and a chunk relevance threshold (weak chunks below it don't enter). Citation verification belongs to a later layer.
options: PII 检测与脱敏(NER/正则抓身份证/邮箱/电话)，防个人信息进 prompt
基于 ACL 的权限过滤，剔掉用户无权访问的块
块相关性阈值，低于阈值的弱相关块不进 prompt
生成后核验每条引用是否真被块支持
options_en: PII detection and redaction (NER/regex for SSN/email/phone) to keep PII out of the prompt.
ACL-based permission filtering to drop chunks the user can't access.
A chunk relevance threshold so weakly relevant chunks don't enter the prompt.
Post-generation verification that each citation is actually supported by the chunk.
optionExplanations: 对；PII 脱敏挡住个人信息在进 prompt 前就外泄，满足 GDPR/HIPAA 合规。
对；权限过滤挡住越权泄露——用户无权看的块根本不进上下文。
对；相关性阈值挡住噪声块，减少无关内容稀释注意力和引发幻觉的压力。
错；引用核验发生在生成之后，属于生成后层，不是生成前措施。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — PII redaction blocks personal info from leaking before it enters the prompt, meeting GDPR/HIPAA.
Correct — permission filtering blocks over-permission leakage: chunks the user can't see never enter context.
Correct — a relevance threshold blocks noise chunks, reducing attention dilution and hallucination pressure.
Incorrect — citation verification happens after generation, in the post-gen layer, not a pre-gen measure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 命名实体识别，用来在文本中定位姓名/身份证/邮箱等 PII 以便脱敏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NER (Named Entity Recognition) locates entities like names, SSNs, and emails in text so PII can be redacted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 访问控制列表，规定谁能看哪些块，生成前据此过滤越权内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ACL (Access Control List) specifies who may see which chunks, used pre-generation to filter unauthorized content.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 要让 RAG 只根据检索到的块作答、每条结论都能追溯到来源，减少编造。
scenario_en: You want the RAG to answer only from retrieved chunks and make each claim traceable to a source, reducing fabrication.
q: prompt 级护栏靠什么约束模型的生成行为？
q_en: What does the prompt-level guardrail use to constrain generation?
why: 用 grounding 指令：在 prompt 里明确要求「只根据提供的上下文作答、每条结论标注引用的 chunk ID」，并放几个「上下文不足就拒答」的 few-shot 示例。这把忠实度和可追溯性写进指令，减少幻觉。
why_en: Use grounding instructions: the prompt explicitly says 'answer only from the provided context and cite the chunk ID for each claim,' plus a few few-shot refusal examples ('refuse when context is insufficient'), baking faithfulness and traceability into the instructions to cut hallucination.
tradeoff: grounding 指令(强忠实/可追溯但可能过度拒答) vs 自由生成(流畅但易幻觉、不可追溯)
whenOtherWins: 若任务是开放式头脑风暴、本就期望模型发挥而非严格引用，过强的 grounding 指令反而限制有用输出。
options: 不给任何指令，让模型自由发挥最自然
grounding 指令：要求只根据上下文作答、每条结论标 chunk ID、上下文不足就拒答
在指令里要求模型尽量补充上下文之外的背景知识
让模型对每个块都逐字复述，不许改写
options_en: Give no instructions; free generation is most natural.
Grounding instructions: answer only from context, cite a chunk ID per claim, refuse when context is insufficient.
Instruct the model to add background knowledge beyond the context.
Make the model recite each chunk verbatim with no paraphrase.
optionExplanations: 自由发挥没有约束，模型会编造上下文里没有的内容，忠实度和可追溯性全丢。
对；明确的 grounding + 引用要求 + 拒答示例把忠实度写进 prompt，是 prompt 级护栏的核心。
鼓励补充上下文外知识正好相反，会放大幻觉风险，违背 grounding 目标。
逐字复述不是作答，无法综合多块回答问题，也不解决忠实度约束。
optionExplanations_en: Free generation is unconstrained, so the model fabricates content not in the context, losing faithfulness and traceability.
Correct — explicit grounding plus citation requirements and refusal examples bake faithfulness into the prompt, the core prompt-level guardrail.
Encouraging outside knowledge is the opposite, amplifying hallucination and violating grounding.
Verbatim recitation isn't answering, can't synthesize across chunks, and doesn't address the faithfulness constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求模型只依据给定上下文作答、并标注来源，减少编造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounding requires the model to answer only from the given context and cite sources, reducing fabrication.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 模型给了一个带引用的答案，但你担心它「挂着引用却其实没被那个块支持」的幻觉。
scenario_en: The model returns a cited answer, but you worry about hallucinations that cite a chunk that doesn't actually support the claim.
q: 生成后这一层最关键的核验做什么？
q_en: What is the key check in the post-generation layer?
why: 做引用核验：逐条检查每个被引用的块是否真的支持对应结论；若不支持，就用更严格的 prompt 重新生成，或直接返回「无法回答」。这把「假装有依据」的幻觉挡在输出之前，是生成后层的核心。
why_en: Citation verification: check whether each cited chunk actually supports its claim, and if not, regenerate with a stricter prompt or return 'cannot answer,' blocking fake-grounded hallucinations before output — the core of the post-generation layer.
tradeoff: 引用核验(挡住假引用幻觉但增加一轮开销/可能拒答) vs 直接输出(快但放过挂假引用的幻觉)
whenOtherWins: 若是低风险、非合规场景且延迟极敏感，可放宽核验、只抽查，换更低延迟。
options: 统计答案长度，太长就截断
引用核验：逐条查被引块是否真支持结论，不支持就更严格重生成或返回「无法回答」
把答案再翻译一遍检查语法
只要模型标了引用就默认可信，直接输出
options_en: Count answer length and truncate if too long.
Citation verification: check each cited chunk truly supports the claim, else regenerate stricter or return 'cannot answer'.
Re-translate the answer to check grammar.
Trust any answer that cites something and output it directly.
optionExplanations: 长度和是否幻觉无关，截断改不了「引用挂假」的问题。
对；核验每条引用是否被块真正支持，是挡住假接地幻觉、守住忠实度的关键一步。
翻译查语法与引用真假无关，答不到忠实度核验。
标了引用不等于引用为真，正是幻觉常见形态，不能默认可信。
optionExplanations_en: Length is unrelated to hallucination; truncation doesn't fix a fake citation.
Correct — verifying each citation is truly supported by its chunk is the key step blocking fake-grounded hallucination and preserving faithfulness.
Grammar-checking via translation is unrelated to citation truthfulness and misses the verification.
A present citation isn't a true one — that's exactly a common hallucination — so it can't be trusted by default.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐条检查被引用的块是否真的支持对应结论，不支持则重生成或拒答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Citation verification checks whether each cited chunk truly supports its claim, regenerating or refusing if not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断一段文本是否在逻辑上支持另一句话，用来自动化检测幻觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entailment model judges whether one text logically supports a statement, used to automate hallucination detection.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 生成后这一层要在答案返回用户之前，最后把一遍质量与安全关。
scenario_en: The post-generation layer is the final quality and safety gate before the answer reaches the user.
q: 生成后(post-generation)护栏包含哪些检查？(多选)
q_en: Which checks make up post-generation guardrails? (multiple)
why: 生成后三招都在输出前做：引用核验(每条引用是否被块支持，不支持就重生成或拒答)、内容安全/毒性扫描(挡有害输出)、用蕴含模型做幻觉检测(答案是否被上下文蕴含)。PII 脱敏是生成前的事，不在这一层。
why_en: All three run before output: citation verification (is each citation supported, else regenerate or refuse), a content-safety/toxicity scan (block harmful output), and hallucination detection via an entailment model (is the answer entailed by the context). PII redaction is a pre-generation concern, not this layer.
options: 引用核验：每条引用是否被块真正支持，不支持就重生成或返回无法回答
内容安全/毒性分类器扫描，挡住有害输出
用蕴含模型做幻觉检测，判断答案是否被上下文支持
PII 检测与脱敏，防个人信息进入 prompt
options_en: Citation verification: is each citation truly supported, else regenerate or return cannot-answer.
A content-safety/toxicity classifier scan to block harmful output.
Hallucination detection via an entailment model checking if the answer is supported by the context.
PII detection and redaction to keep personal info out of the prompt.
optionExplanations: 对；引用核验挡住「挂假引用」的幻觉，把不被支持的结论拦在输出前。
对；毒性扫描挡住有害/不当内容外发，是面向用户前的安全闸门。
对；蕴含模型自动判断答案是否被上下文支持，规模化地兜住幻觉。
错；PII 脱敏是块进 prompt 之前的生成前措施，不属于生成后层。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — citation verification blocks fake-citation hallucination, stopping unsupported claims before output.
Correct — a toxicity scan blocks harmful/inappropriate content from going out, the safety gate before the user.
Correct — an entailment model auto-judges whether the answer is context-supported, catching hallucination at scale.
Incorrect — PII redaction is a pre-generation measure before chunks enter the prompt, not the post-gen layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用分类器检查输出是否含有害/不当内容，输出前拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A toxicity scan uses a classifier to check output for harmful/inappropriate content and block it before release.

scenario: 护栏阈值设太严，很多合法问题被拒答；设太松，又可能放过有害或越权的输出。
scenario_en: Set guardrail thresholds too strict and many legitimate queries get refused; too permissive and harmful or over-permission output slips through.
q: 护栏阈值该怎么定，两端各有什么代价？
q_en: How should guardrail thresholds be set, and what's the cost at each extreme?
why: 两端都有代价：太严→合法请求被大量拒答、可用性差；太松→有害/越权输出漏出、合规风险。没有普适的点，要用领域专属评估数据校准阈值，在拒答率和风险之间找本领域可接受的平衡。
why_en: Both extremes cost: too strict → many legitimate requests refused, poor usability; too permissive → harmful/over-permission output leaks, compliance risk; there's no universal point, so calibrate thresholds with domain-specific eval data to balance refusal rate against risk for this domain.
tradeoff: 阈值严(少漏有害但多误拒合法) vs 阈值松(少误拒但多漏有害)
options: 阈值越严越好，宁可全拒也不能出错
太严→大量误拒合法请求；太松→漏出有害/越权输出；用领域评估数据校准阈值找平衡
阈值越松越好，尽量别打扰用户
有个全行业通用的最佳阈值，直接照抄即可
options_en: Stricter is always better; refuse everything rather than err.
Too strict → many legitimate requests wrongly refused; too permissive → harmful/over-permission leaks; calibrate with domain eval data to balance.
More permissive is always better; avoid bothering users.
There's a universal industry-best threshold; just copy it.
optionExplanations: 全拒虽不出有害内容，但可用性归零，产品没法用，不是可接受的一端。
对；严松各有代价，只能靠领域评估数据校准，在误拒和漏危险之间找本领域的平衡点。
一味放松会漏出有害/越权输出，合规风险不可接受。
不同领域(法务/医疗/客服)的风险容忍度不同，没有可照抄的通用阈值。
optionExplanations_en: Refusing all avoids harmful content but zeroes usability, making the product unusable — not an acceptable extreme.
Correct — strict and permissive each cost, so only domain eval data can calibrate the balance between wrong refusals and leaked risk.
Blind permissiveness leaks harmful/over-permission output, an unacceptable compliance risk.
Different domains (legal/medical/support) have different risk tolerance, so there's no copyable universal threshold.

termDefinitions.term: domain eval data / 领域评估数据
termDefinitions.meaning: 本领域标注好的测试样例，用来校准护栏阈值在拒答率和风险间的平衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Domain eval data is labeled test cases for the domain, used to calibrate guardrail thresholds between refusal rate and risk.

category: Enterprise Rag Model Architecture Prompt Design

scenario: 问题是「把 Q3 董事会备忘录里的政策变化，应用到 CRM 导出的客户名单上，估算收入影响」——答案要跨多个来源逐步拼出来。
scenario_en: The query is 'estimate the revenue impact of the Q3 board-memo policy change applied to the CRM-exported client list' — the answer must be chained across multiple sources.
q: 这种需要跨源多跳推理的问题，单趟 RAG 为什么不够，该怎么办？
q_en: Why does single-pass RAG fail on this multi-hop cross-source query, and what do you do?
why: 单趟 RAG(检索一次、生成一次)拿不到分散在多来源、且互相依赖的证据。改用 agentic RAG：让 orchestrator 迭代式检索——先拆子问题、各自跑完整检索+重排、评估凑齐没有、不够再精化重查，最后汇总生成。
why_en: Single-pass RAG (retrieve once, generate once) can't gather interdependent evidence spread across sources, so use agentic RAG: an orchestrator retrieves iteratively — decompose into sub-questions, run the full pipeline per sub-question, assess sufficiency, refine and re-retrieve if short, then assemble and generate.
tradeoff: agentic 多跳(跨源拼答质量高但多轮更慢更贵) vs 单趟(快省但答不了多跳依赖问题)
whenOtherWins: 若问题是单跳、一次检索就能覆盖(如「这条条款怎么写的」)，单趟 RAG 更快更省，agentic 是过度设计。
options: 把上下文窗口调到最大，一次性塞进所有来源就够了
用 agentic RAG：orchestrator 迭代检索——拆子问题→各自检索重排→评估充分性→不足再精化重查→汇总生成
换一个更大的 LLM，让它一次生成就把多跳都想明白
多跑几次单趟 RAG 取多数投票
options_en: Max out the context window and stuff all sources in at once.
Use agentic RAG: an orchestrator retrieves iteratively — decompose sub-questions → retrieve+rerank each → assess sufficiency → refine and re-retrieve if short → assemble and generate.
Switch to a bigger LLM to reason out all hops in one generation.
Run single-pass RAG several times and majority-vote.
optionExplanations: 塞满窗口既触发中间迷失，也解决不了「先查到 A 才知道该查 B」的依赖关系，多跳仍断。
对；orchestrator 把大问题拆成子问题逐步检索、评估、精化，正是跨源多跳的正解。
更大的 LLM 补不了缺失的证据——多跳缺的是检索到的事实，不是推理能力。
重复单趟仍是各自独立检索，投票也拼不出需要跨源串联的答案。
optionExplanations_en: Stuffing the window triggers lost-in-the-middle and doesn't resolve the 'find A before knowing to query B' dependency, so multi-hop still breaks.
Correct — the orchestrator decomposes into sub-questions and iterates retrieve/assess/refine, the right answer for cross-source multi-hop.
A bigger LLM can't supply missing evidence — multi-hop lacks retrieved facts, not reasoning power.
Repeated single-pass still retrieves independently, and voting can't assemble an answer needing cross-source chaining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由 orchestrator 编排多轮检索-评估-精化的 RAG，用于跨源多跳问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Agentic RAG has an orchestrator coordinate multiple rounds of retrieve-assess-refine, for multi-hop cross-source queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案需要串联多个来源、一步的结果决定下一步查什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-hop means the answer chains across sources, where one step's result decides what to retrieve next.

scenario: agentic RAG 的 orchestrator 要把一个复杂多跳问题处理成最终答案。
scenario_en: The agentic RAG orchestrator turns a complex multi-hop query into a final answer.
q: 把 agentic RAG orchestrator 的处理步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the agentic RAG orchestrator's steps correctly:
steps: 评估充分性：合起来的上下文够不够回答原问题
把原问题拆成若干独立子问题
每个子问题各自跑完整的检索+重排
不够则生成精化子查询、再检索一轮
带上全部护栏做最终汇总与生成
why: 先拆子问题→各自跑完整检索+重排→评估凑齐的上下文够不够→不够就精化子查询再检索一轮→够了带全部护栏汇总生成。评估-精化构成一个回路，直到充分或触达迭代上限。
why_en: Decompose into sub-questions → run full retrieval+reranking per sub-question → assess whether the combined context suffices → if not, refine sub-queries and retrieve again → once sufficient, assemble and generate with all guardrails; assess-refine forms a loop until sufficient or the iteration cap is hit.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  D["拆子问题"] --> R["各自检索+重排"] --> A{"充分?"}
  A -->|不够| Rf["精化子查询"] --> R
  A -->|够| G["带护栏汇总生成"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个复杂多跳问题拆成若干可独立检索的子问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query decomposition breaks a complex multi-hop question into independently retrievable sub-questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断已检索到的上下文是否足以回答原问题，不足则再检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sufficiency assessment judges whether the retrieved context can answer the original question, retrieving again if not.

scenario: agentic RAG 每多一轮循环，大约就多一次检索延迟 + 一次 LLM 调用，成本和延迟随轮数线性增长。
scenario_en: Each agentic RAG loop adds roughly one retrieval latency plus one LLM call, so cost and latency grow linearly with rounds.
q: 「每轮≈一次检索+一次 LLM 调用」这个量级对设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does 'each loop ≈ one retrieval + one LLM call' imply for design?
why: 循环成本随轮数线性叠加，最坏情况可能无限循环。所以要给最大迭代次数封顶：用轮数上限把最坏延迟/成本框住，达上限还不充分就返回当前最好答案或「无法回答」，而不是无限查下去。
why_en: Loop cost stacks linearly with rounds and could loop unboundedly, so cap the max iterations: an iteration limit bounds worst-case latency/cost, and on hitting it you return the best answer so far or 'cannot answer' rather than looping forever.
options: 给最大迭代次数封顶：每轮≈一次检索+一次 LLM 调用线性叠加，用上限框住最坏延迟/成本
轮数越多越好，一直循环到答案完美为止
每轮成本固定不变，与轮数无关，不用封顶
这只是要背的数字，没有设计含义
options_en: Cap max iterations: each loop ≈ one retrieval + one LLM call stacking linearly, so a limit bounds worst-case latency/cost.
More rounds are better; loop until the answer is perfect.
Per-loop cost is fixed regardless of rounds, so no cap needed.
Just a number to memorize with no design meaning.

scenario: 面试官问什么时候用单趟 RAG、什么时候上 agentic RAG，想看你能否按问题复杂度选。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks when to use single-pass vs agentic RAG, checking whether you choose by query complexity.
q: 单趟 RAG 和 agentic RAG 在适用问题和成本上如何对比？
q_en: How do single-pass and agentic RAG contrast on fit and cost?
why: 单趟 RAG 一次检索一次生成，快而省，适合单跳问题；agentic RAG 多轮检索-评估-精化，慢而贵，但能答需要跨源串联的多跳复杂问题。取舍轴是「问题复杂度 vs 延迟/成本」，按问题选而非一刀切。
why_en: Single-pass RAG retrieves and generates once — fast and cheap, for single-hop queries; agentic RAG does multiple retrieve-assess-refine rounds — slower and costlier but answers multi-hop cross-source queries; the axis is query complexity vs latency/cost, chosen per query not one-size-fits-all.
tradeoff: 单趟(快省但只能单跳) vs agentic(能多跳但多轮更慢更贵)
options: 两者一样，任何问题都该用 agentic 更保险
单趟快省适合单跳；agentic 多轮慢贵但能答跨源多跳，按问题复杂度选
单趟适合多跳、agentic 适合单跳，正好相反
agentic 更快更省，应该全面替代单趟
options_en: They're the same; use agentic for everything to be safe.
Single-pass is fast/cheap for single-hop; agentic is slow/costly but handles cross-source multi-hop — choose by complexity.
Single-pass fits multi-hop and agentic single-hop — the reverse.
Agentic is faster and cheaper and should fully replace single-pass.
optionExplanations: 简单单跳问题用 agentic 是白白多花多轮延迟和 LLM 调用，过度设计。
对；按问题复杂度选——单跳走单趟省成本、多跳才上 agentic，取舍在复杂度与延迟/成本之间。
说反了：单趟只能单跳、agentic 才能多跳。
agentic 因多轮而更慢更贵，不可能全面替代更省的单趟。
optionExplanations_en: Using agentic on a simple single-hop query wastes extra rounds of latency and LLM calls — over-engineering.
Correct — choose by complexity: single-hop uses single-pass to save cost, multi-hop needs agentic, trading complexity against latency/cost.
Backwards: single-pass handles only single-hop and agentic handles multi-hop.
Agentic is slower and costlier due to multiple rounds, so it can't fully replace cheaper single-pass.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索一次、生成一次的基础 RAG，适合单跳问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single-pass RAG retrieves once and generates once, fitting single-hop queries.

scenario: 面试官问「你怎么知道这个企业 RAG 问答系统能用」。有工程师想直接套 BLEU/ROUGE 分数。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'how do you know this enterprise RAG QA system works?' An engineer wants to just report BLEU/ROUGE scores.
q: 为什么 BLEU/ROUGE 不适合评估 RAG 系统？
q_en: Why are BLEU/ROUGE inadequate for evaluating a RAG system?
why: BLEU/ROUGE 是机器翻译的 n-gram 重叠指标，测的是「和参考答案字面像不像」，测不出幻觉、检索错误或伪造引用。而 RAG 的主要失败其实在检索不到位（检索错上下文→答案没有依据），字面重叠完全看不见这条链路。
why_en: BLEU/ROUGE only measure n-gram overlap with a reference and miss hallucination, wrong retrieval, and fabricated citations, whereas RAG's primary failure mode is inadequate retrieval.
tradeoff: 字面重叠指标（易算但盲于幻觉/检索）vs 面向 RAG 的忠实/相关/可溯源评估
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本身就是「输出要逐字贴近唯一标准答案」（如术语翻译、模板填充），n-gram 重叠反而是合适的直接指标。
options: 因为 BLEU/ROUGE 计算太慢，跑一遍要几小时，无法跟上线上流量
因为它们只测 n-gram 字面重叠、盲于幻觉与检索错误，而 RAG 主要失败在检索不到位
因为它们只支持英文，企业多语言合同场景下无法使用
因为它们需要 GPU 推理，成本比直接用 LLM 打分还高
options_en: Because BLEU/ROUGE are too slow to compute, taking hours per run, and cannot keep up with live traffic.
Because they only measure n-gram overlap and are blind to hallucination and retrieval errors, while RAG mostly fails at inadequate retrieval.
Because they only support English and cannot be used for enterprise multilingual contract scenarios.
Because they require GPU inference and cost more than just using an LLM to score.
optionExplanations: 速度不是问题所在：BLEU/ROUGE 其实算得很快，问题是它们测的东西（字面重叠）跟 RAG 的失败模式对不上。
对；RAG 答错通常是检索错了上下文导致答案没根据，n-gram 重叠既看不出幻觉也看不出检索是否切题。
多语言不是核心缺陷，n-gram 指标各语言都能算；真正的缺陷是它衡量的维度错了。
BLEU/ROUGE 是纯字符串统计、根本不用 GPU；成本论点站不住，问题在于指标维度错位。
optionExplanations_en: Speed is not the issue: BLEU/ROUGE are actually fast; the problem is what they measure (surface overlap) does not match RAG's failure modes.
Correct — RAG errors usually come from retrieving the wrong context so the answer lacks grounding, and n-gram overlap sees neither hallucination nor retrieval relevance.
Multilingual is not the core flaw; n-gram metrics work in any language, the real flaw is they measure the wrong dimension.
BLEU/ROUGE are pure string statistics needing no GPU, so the cost argument fails; the issue is the metric measures the wrong thing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：先检索相关文档片段，再让 LLM 基于这些片段作答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves relevant document chunks first, then has an LLM answer grounded in those chunks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器翻译评测指标，衡量生成文本与参考答案的 n-gram 重叠。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is a machine-translation metric scoring n-gram overlap between output and a reference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 摘要评测指标，偏召回地衡量与参考文本的 n-gram 重叠。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) is a summarization metric measuring recall-oriented n-gram overlap with a reference.

scenario: 评估企业 RAG 时要拆成互不重叠的几个维度，避免把不同的失败糊成一个分数。
scenario_en: Evaluating enterprise RAG means splitting into non-overlapping dimensions so different failures don't collapse into one score.
q: RAG Triad（RAG 三元评估）是哪三个维度？
q_en: What are the three dimensions of the RAG Triad?
why: 三个非冗余维度：Faithfulness（答案是否忠于检索到的上下文，抓幻觉）、Relevance（检索到的上下文是否切题，抓上游检索失败）、Groundedness（每条主张是否有引用支撑，抓无依据断言）。三者各抓一类失败，缺一漏一。
why_en: The three non-redundant dimensions are Faithfulness (does the answer reflect retrieved context, catching hallucination), Relevance (does retrieved context answer the query, catching retrieval failure), and Groundedness (is every claim backed by a cited passage).
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["用户 query"] --> R["检索 chunks"] R --> A["生成答案"] R -.Relevance.-> Q A -.Faithfulness.-> R A -.Groundedness
逐条引用.-> R
options: Accuracy、Precision、Recall——沿用分类模型的三个标准指标
Faithfulness（忠实于上下文）、Relevance（上下文切题）、Groundedness（逐条可溯源）
Latency（延迟）、Throughput（吞吐）、Cost（成本）——服务侧三件套
Fluency（流畅度）、Coherence（连贯性）、Diversity（多样性）——生成文本三指标
options_en: Accuracy, Precision, Recall — the three standard classification metrics.
Faithfulness (answer reflects context), Relevance (context answers the query), Groundedness (each claim is attributable).
Latency, Throughput, Cost — the serving-side trio.
Fluency, Coherence, Diversity — three generic text-generation metrics.
optionExplanations: 分类指标假设有单一正确标签，RAG 的开放式答案没有这种标签，也测不出检索链路的问题。
对；这三维分别盯住幻觉、检索是否切题、以及每条主张能否溯源，互不重叠地覆盖 RAG 的失败模式。
延迟/吞吐/成本是服务性能，不评估答案质量；一个又快又便宜的系统照样可能满口幻觉。
流畅/连贯/多样只看文字表面好不好读，答案再通顺也可能完全脱离检索到的事实。
optionExplanations_en: Classification metrics assume a single correct label; RAG's open-ended answers have none and reveal nothing about the retrieval path.
Correct — these three watch hallucination, retrieval relevance, and per-claim attribution, covering RAG failures without overlap.
Latency/throughput/cost are serving performance, not answer quality; a fast cheap system can still hallucinate constantly.
Fluency/coherence/diversity only judge how readable the text is; a fluent answer can still be fully detached from retrieved facts.

termDefinitions.term: RAG Triad / RAG 三元评估
termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Faithfulness、Relevance、Groundedness 三个非冗余维度评估 RAG 的框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The RAG Triad evaluates RAG on three non-redundant dimensions: Faithfulness, Relevance, and Groundedness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案是否只陈述检索上下文支持的内容，用来抓幻觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithfulness measures whether the answer only states what the retrieved context supports, catching hallucination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索回来的上下文是否真的能回答用户 query，用来抓上游检索失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relevance measures whether the retrieved context can actually answer the query, catching upstream retrieval failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案里每一条主张是否都能对应到某个被引用的段落。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Groundedness measures whether every claim in the answer maps to a specific cited passage.

scenario: 有人问：既然 Faithfulness 和 Relevance 都在评估 RAG，是不是测一个就够了？
scenario_en: Someone asks: since Faithfulness and Relevance both evaluate RAG, isn't measuring one enough?
q: Faithfulness 和 Relevance 为什么是「非冗余」的两个维度？
q_en: Why are Faithfulness and Relevance non-redundant dimensions?
why: 两者盯的关系不同：Faithfulness 看「答案 vs 上下文」，Relevance 看「上下文 vs query」。系统可以忠实地复述一段无关上下文（高 Faithfulness、低 Relevance），也可以检索到切题上下文却不用它（高 Relevance、低 Faithfulness），所以必须分开测。
why_en: They watch different relationships — Faithfulness is answer-versus-context and Relevance is context-versus-query — so you can be faithful to irrelevant context or ignore relevant context, and must measure both.
tradeoff: Faithfulness（答案↔上下文）vs Relevance（上下文↔query）——两条不同关系轴

rows: 忠实复述了无关上下文
检索切题却被答案忽略

options: 它们其实等价，Relevance 高必然 Faithfulness 高，测一个即可
Faithfulness 只在生成阶段有意义，Relevance 只在离线阶段有意义，时间上错开
Faithfulness 看答案是否忠于上下文，Relevance 看上下文是否切题；可以忠实于无关上下文，故两者独立
Relevance 是主观指标、Faithfulness 是客观指标，一个靠人一个靠机器，无法比较
options_en: They are actually equivalent — high Relevance implies high Faithfulness, so measure just one.
Faithfulness matters only at generation time and Relevance only offline, so they are separated in time.
Faithfulness checks if the answer is faithful to the context, Relevance checks if the context is on-topic; you can be faithful to irrelevant context, so they are independent.
Relevance is subjective and Faithfulness is objective, one needs humans and one needs machines, so they cannot be compared.
optionExplanations: 反例直接推翻：可以检索到完全无关但被忠实复述的上下文，Relevance 低而 Faithfulness 高。
两者都在评估同一次问答的不同关系，没有时间先后之分，这个划分是编造的。
对；一个比「答案↔上下文」、一个比「上下文↔query」，两条关系轴正交，一个高不推出另一个高。
主观/客观不是它们的区别；两者都可以用 LLM 判、也都可以人工标，区别在比较的对象不同。
optionExplanations_en: A counterexample kills it: context can be totally irrelevant yet faithfully echoed — low Relevance, high Faithfulness.
Both evaluate different relationships within the same QA turn; there is no temporal ordering, this split is invented.
Correct — one compares answer-to-context, the other context-to-query; the two axes are orthogonal, so high in one need not mean high in the other.
Subjective/objective is not the distinction; both can be judged by an LLM or by humans, the difference is what they compare.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个指标测的是不同关系，一个的高低推不出另一个，所以都要测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-redundant means the two metrics measure different relationships, so one's value cannot be inferred from the other.

scenario: 合同问答系统要出审计报告，需要逐条主张都能指到具体段落，光「答案没跑偏」还不够。
scenario_en: A contract QA system must produce audit reports where every claim points to a specific passage; 'the answer didn't drift' is not enough.
q: Groundedness 比 Faithfulness 严在哪里？
q_en: How is Groundedness stricter than Faithfulness?
why: Faithfulness 只要求答案整体不与上下文矛盾；Groundedness 更严，要求「每一条主张」都能映射到某个具体段落 ID，做逐条溯源。审计场景需要 attribution（可归因），所以要用更严的 Groundedness。
why_en: Faithfulness only requires the answer not to contradict the context, while Groundedness is stricter, demanding each individual claim map to a specific passage ID for a per-claim audit trail.
tradeoff: Faithfulness（整体不矛盾即可）vs Groundedness（逐条 attribution，更严）
options: Groundedness 要求每条主张都映射到具体段落 ID（逐条 attribution），Faithfulness 只要整体不与上下文矛盾
Groundedness 只看引用格式对不对，Faithfulness 才看内容对不对，前者其实更松
Groundedness 用机器判、Faithfulness 用人判，严不严只是标注成本高低的说法
两者完全相同，Groundedness 只是 Faithfulness 在多轮对话里的别名
options_en: Groundedness requires each claim to map to a specific passage ID (per-claim attribution), while Faithfulness only needs the whole answer not to contradict the context.
Groundedness only checks citation formatting and Faithfulness checks content, so Groundedness is actually looser.
Groundedness is machine-judged and Faithfulness human-judged; strictness is just about labeling cost.
They are identical; Groundedness is just Faithfulness's alias in multi-turn dialogue.
optionExplanations: 对；粒度是关键——Groundedness 逐条把主张钉到段落上，能出审计追踪，比只看整体一致的 Faithfulness 严。
说反了；Groundedness 恰恰是内容级的逐条溯源，不是格式检查，也不比 Faithfulness 松。
严不严跟谁来判无关，两者都能机判或人判；区别在 Groundedness 的判定粒度更细（逐条）。
两者不同：一个是整体忠实，一个是逐条可归因，不是别名关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — granularity is the key: Groundedness pins each claim to a passage for an audit trail, stricter than Faithfulness's whole-answer consistency.
Backwards; Groundedness is content-level per-claim attribution, not a format check, and is not looser than Faithfulness.
Strictness is independent of who judges; both can be machine or human judged, the difference is Groundedness's finer per-claim granularity.
They differ: one is whole-answer faithfulness, the other per-claim attributability — not aliases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把答案里的每条主张对应到支撑它的具体段落，用于审计追踪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Attribution maps each claim in the answer to the specific passage supporting it, enabling an audit trail.

scenario: 法律 RAG 答案里冒出一条「合同第 7 条约定」的内容，但翻遍所有检索到的 chunk 都没有这一条。
scenario_en: A legal RAG answer states a 'clause 7 of the contract' that appears in none of the retrieved chunks.
q: 「答案发明了上下文里没有的合同条款」这类失败，RAG Triad 的哪个维度最直接抓？
q_en: Which RAG Triad dimension most directly catches 'the answer invented a clause not in any chunk'?
why: 答案陈述了检索上下文里根本不存在的内容，就是典型幻觉，直接由 Faithfulness（答案是否忠于上下文）抓住。Relevance 看的是检索是否切题，这里检索可能没问题，问题出在生成脱离了上下文。
why_en: The answer asserts content absent from the retrieved context, which is textbook hallucination caught directly by Faithfulness, since the failure is generation drifting off the context.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题是「检索回来的段落根本不属于这份合同」，那检索本身就跑偏了，该由 Relevance 先抓。
options: Relevance——因为检索到的段落一定和 query 无关
Faithfulness——答案陈述了上下文里不存在的内容，是脱离上下文的幻觉
Latency——因为发明条款通常是模型算得太快导致的
Diversity——因为答案缺乏多样化的引用来源
options_en: Relevance — because the retrieved passages must be unrelated to the query.
Faithfulness — the answer states content absent from the context, a hallucination detached from the context.
Latency — because inventing a clause usually comes from computing too fast.
Diversity — because the answer lacks diverse citation sources.
optionExplanations: 不一定；检索可能完全切题，问题出在生成端脱离了上下文，这不是 Relevance 的失败。
对；发明上下文里没有的内容 = 幻觉，正是 Faithfulness 盯的「答案是否只说上下文支持的话」。
延迟是服务性能，跟答案是否忠于上下文无关，跑得慢也可能编条款。
多样性衡量文字表面，不判断内容是否有上下文支撑，抓不到幻觉。
optionExplanations_en: Not necessarily; retrieval may be perfectly on-topic, with the failure at generation drifting off context — not a Relevance failure.
Correct — inventing content absent from context is hallucination, exactly what Faithfulness watches: does the answer say only what the context supports.
Latency is serving performance, unrelated to faithfulness; a slow system can invent clauses too.
Diversity judges surface text, not whether content is context-supported, so it cannot catch hallucination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型生成了检索上下文并不支持的内容，看起来可信但没有依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hallucination is when the model generates content the retrieved context does not support — plausible but unbacked.

scenario: 用户问 A 产品线的退货政策，检索器返回的却全是 B 产品线的段落，答案基于这些段落作答。
scenario_en: A user asks about product line A's return policy, but the retriever returns only product line B passages, and the answer is built on them.
q: 「检索回来的 chunk 讨论的是另一条产品线」这类上游失败，该由哪个维度抓？
q_en: Which dimension catches the upstream failure 'retrieved chunks discuss a different product line'?
why: 问题出在检索阶段：拿回来的上下文根本不能回答这个 query，这是 Relevance（上下文↔query 是否切题）抓的上游检索失败。此时答案哪怕忠实复述这些无关段落，Faithfulness 都可能很高，掩盖了真正的问题。
why_en: The failure is at retrieval — the context cannot answer the query — which is caught by Relevance, and Faithfulness can even look high while faithfully echoing the wrong passages.
whenOtherWins: 如果检索段落确实是 A 产品线、切题，但答案却编了段落里没有的政策，那问题在生成端，改由 Faithfulness 抓。
options: Groundedness——因为每条主张都缺引用
Fluency——因为答案读起来不通顺
Faithfulness——因为答案一定与上下文矛盾
Relevance——检索上下文与 query 不切题，是上游检索失败
options_en: Groundedness — because every claim lacks a citation.
Fluency — because the answer reads awkwardly.
Faithfulness — because the answer must contradict the context.
Relevance — the retrieved context is off-topic for the query, an upstream retrieval failure.
optionExplanations: 主张可能都规规矩矩引用了 B 产品线段落，Groundedness 甚至过关，但检索本身错了。
读得通顺与否不解决检索错产品线的问题，答案可能又通顺又错。
答案可能忠实复述了这些无关段落、并不矛盾，Faithfulness 反而高，掩盖了检索失败。
