steps: 数据中心 primary 接收多个 secondary 的汇总
secondary 在本地集群 pull 原始指标
global monitoring 汇总跨数据中心视图
必要时 operator 下钻到本地原始数据
why: 先本地收集，后向上聚合，最后提供全局视图和下钻。这样控制全局入口压力，同时保留排障路径。
why_en: Collect locally, aggregate upward, then provide global views with drill-down to keep ingestion scalable and debuggable.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Raw node metrics"] --> B["Local pull"] --> C["DC aggregate"] --> D["Global view"] --> E["Drill down"]

scenario: 指标走 TSDB，但排障时工程师还要按错误文本、服务名和时间窗口搜索大量日志。
scenario_en: Metrics go to a TSDB, but engineers also need to search large logs by error text, service name, and time window.
q: 日志搜索层适合补什么？
q_en: What should be added for log search?
options: Elasticsearch 这类搜索索引
只用 TSDB 存全文日志
只把日志发到 Slack
把日志存在 DNS 记录里
options_en: A search index such as Elasticsearch.
Use only the TSDB for full-text logs.
Send logs only to Slack.
Store logs in DNS records.
why: TSDB 适合数值时间序列，全文日志需要倒排索引和字段过滤。代价是日志索引成本高，要控制采样、保留期和字段。
why_en: A TSDB fits numeric series, while log search needs indexing for text and fields.
whenOtherWins: 如果只查少量结构化指标，TSDB 查询就够，不需要日志搜索集群。
tradeoff: 全文排障能力 vs 索引成本

每台机器一个完整折线图
只发一封总数邮件
随机排列的文本列表

A full line chart for every machine.
Only send one email with totals.
A randomly ordered text list.

whenOtherWins: 如果只排查一台机器的 CPU 抖动，单机时间序列图更合适。
tradeoff: 大规模概览 vs 单节点细节

scenario_en: Reachability needs only 1 bit: 1 means healthy and 0 means unreachable; the view covers 1,000,000 servers.
q: 这个估算支持哪种可视化判断？
q_en: What visualization decision does this estimate support?

必须给每台机器画完整曲线
只能按机器名分页查看文本

Operators can only page through text by machine name.
Raw logs must be kept forever in memory.

why_en: One million bits divided by eight is about 125 KB, which makes a large health heat map compact.

scenario: 每台机器每秒上报 request_count，dashboard 只需要按服务和机房展示每分钟总量。
scenario_en: Each machine reports request_count every second, while the dashboard needs per-minute totals by service and data center.
q: 聚合流应怎么做？
q_en: How should the aggregation flow work?
options: 按时间窗口和标签聚合，再写入可查询存储
把每个点直接画到用户浏览器
先删除所有标签
只保存最后一台机器的值
options_en: Aggregate by time window and labels, then write queryable storage.
Draw every point directly in the user's browser.
Remove all labels first.
Store only the last machine's value.
why: 服务级 dashboard 需要按窗口和标签汇总，而不是展示所有原始点。代价是标签基数过高会让聚合和存储膨胀。
why_en: Service-level dashboards need windowed label aggregation, but high-cardinality labels can make storage and aggregation explode.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Raw samples"] --> B["Window by 1m"] --> C["Group by service, dc"] --> D["Aggregate sum/p95"] --> E["TSDB/dashboard"]

scenario: CPU 偶尔尖峰到 91% 一秒就恢复；团队只想在持续资源压力时叫醒值班。
scenario_en: CPU briefly spikes to 91% for one second and recovers; the team only wants pages for sustained resource pressure.
q: 告警条件应如何避免噪声？
q_en: How should the alert condition avoid noise?
options: 阈值配持续时间或多次窗口判断
任何单点超过阈值立刻 P0
删除 CPU 指标
只在用户投诉后报警
options_en: Combine the threshold with duration or repeated windows.
Make any single point over threshold a P0.
Delete the CPU metric.
Alert only after user complaints.
why: 持续时间能区分短抖动和真正饱和，减少误报。代价是检测会慢一点，所以关键路径要按风险调窗口。
why_en: Adding duration separates brief spikes from sustained saturation and reduces noisy pages.
whenOtherWins: 如果是数据丢失或安全事件，单次触发也可能必须立刻报警。
tradeoff: 误报率 vs 检测速度

why_en: When a request never reaches the backend, server telemetry is silent, so client-side or external monitoring is needed.

q_en: What is wrong with relying only on total traffic dips?

它能精确指出 BGP 泄漏路径
它一定没有误报

It precisely identifies the BGP leak path.

scenario: 缓存节点会自动扩缩容和故障替换。你不希望每次节点变化都靠人工改配置并重启所有服务。
scenario_en: Cache nodes are added, removed, and replaced automatically; you do not want manual config edits and service restarts for every change.

配置服务监控节点并通知客户端

why_en: A configuration service keeps client routing current as cache nodes join, leave, or fail.
whenOtherWins: 如果集群很小且节点几乎不变，本地或集中配置文件可以先撑住。
tradeoff: 自动发现与健康传播 vs 配置服务复杂度

q: 缓存节点故障时，配置服务到客户端的正确状态链是什么？

steps: 客户端按旧列表继续把部分 key 路由到这台坏节点。
配置服务或监控探测到节点不可用。
客户端收到新列表后重算路由；受影响 key 可能 miss 并回源。
缓存节点宕机或网络隔离。

why: 这条链要讲清楚中间的不一致窗口：故障先发生，客户端视图随后才收敛。代价是窗口内会有 miss、超时或回源压力。
why_en: Membership changes are not instant, so clients may route to a failed node until the configuration view converges.
diagram:
flowchart LR

scenario: 一个缓存分片的主节点宕机时，团队希望还能读到该分片的大部分热门数据，并把热分片读流量分散出去。
scenario_en: When a cache shard's primary fails, the team wants most hot data still readable and hot-shard reads spread out.
q: 分片内部应加入什么结构？

options: 一个 primary 加多个 replica

每次读都全量扫描所有分片
把所有分片合并到数据库进程
options_en: One primary with multiple replicas
Keep only one node with no backup
Scan all shards for every read
Merge all shards into the database process
why: primary-replica 能在主节点故障时保留副本，也能让读流量分摊到多个节点。代价是复制延迟和副本一致性要处理。
why_en: Primary-replica shards improve availability and read scaling, but introduce replication lag and consistency work.
whenOtherWins: 如果缓存完全可丢且回源数据库很轻，单副本缓存能省成本。
tradeoff: 可用性与读扩展 vs 复制成本与一致性

  P --> R1[(Replica A)]
  P --> R2[(Replica B)]

  Client -.read.-> R2

q: 热 key 最直接的缓解是什么？

whenOtherWins: 如果热点来自一个 key 范围而不是单 key，增加虚拟节点或重新分片更合适。

why: 删除不同于普通驱逐：源数据已经不存在，旧缓存继续命中会把已删除对象读回来。失败时要有重试或短 TTL 收口旧值窗口。
why_en: Deletes need explicit invalidation because a stale cache hit can resurrect data that no longer exists in the database.

q: EAT 如何把命中率转成平均访问延迟？
q_en: How does EAT turn hit rate into average access latency?
text: EAT = {{hit ratio × hit time + miss ratio × miss time}}；如果 hit=5ms、miss=30ms，miss 从 10% 降到 5% 会把平均延迟从 7.5ms 降到 6.25ms。
text_en: EAT = {{hit ratio × hit time + miss ratio × miss time}}; with hit=5ms and miss=30ms, reducing misses from 10% to 5% lowers average latency from 7.5ms to 6.25ms.
why: EAT = Effective Access Time，用命中和未命中的加权平均估算读延迟。这个数用于比较驱逐策略是否真的降低用户读延迟，而不是只看算法名字。
why_en: Effective Access Time is the weighted average latency of hits and misses, so hit-rate gains translate directly into user-visible latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: EAT 是命中和未命中路径按比例加权后的平均访问时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Effective Access Time is the weighted average access latency across hits and misses.

scenario: 压测里 hit=5ms、miss=30ms。策略 A 的 miss ratio 是 10%，策略 B 是 5%，其他开销接近。
scenario_en: In a benchmark, hits take 5 ms and misses take 30 ms; policy A has 10% misses and policy B has 5%, with similar overhead.
q: 应该优先采用哪种策略？
q_en: Which policy should you prefer?
options: 策略 A，因为 miss 更多说明更公平
策略 B，因为 EAT 更低
两者完全一样，因为 hit time 相同
删除缓存，因为 miss time 比 hit time 大
options_en: Policy A because more misses are fairer
Policy B because its EAT is lower
They are identical because hit time is the same
Remove the cache because misses are slower than hits
why: 策略 A 的 EAT 是 0.9×5+0.1×30=7.5ms，策略 B 是 0.95×5+0.05×30=6.25ms。这个差距会直接进入平均读延迟。
why_en: Policy B wins because its lower miss ratio reduces the weighted average access time.
whenOtherWins: 如果策略 B 的维护 CPU 或锁竞争远高于 A，就要把算法开销也放进压测。
tradeoff: 命中率收益 vs 驱逐维护成本

scenario: 客户端要连续发 100 个 Redis GET。每次等响应再发下一个时，RTT 和 socket 调用占了大量时间。
scenario_en: A client needs to send 100 Redis GETs; waiting for each response before sending the next wastes RTTs and socket calls.
q: Redis pipelining 优化的是什么？
q_en: What does Redis pipelining optimize?
options: 把多个请求先发出去，减少等待往返和系统调用开销
让 Redis 服务器并行执行同一个 key 的所有写
自动把所有命令持久化为 SQL
删除客户端批处理逻辑
options_en: Send multiple requests before waiting, reducing round trips and syscall overhead
Make the Redis server execute all writes to one key in parallel
Automatically persist every command as SQL
Remove batching logic from the client
why: pipelining 省的是客户端等待 RTT、socket I/O 和系统调用，不是把单个 Redis 实例变成并行执行引擎。批量越多、距离越远，收益越明显。
why_en: Pipelining improves throughput by batching network round trips, not by making one Redis server execute commands in parallel.
tradeoff: 吞吐与 RTT amortization vs 客户端批量管理
codeSample:
redis-cli --pipe <<'EOF'
GET user:1
GET user:2
GET user:3
EOF
# 客户端连续发送命令，再批量读取响应。

保证每个对象都强一致复制

tradeoff: 碎片控制 vs 尺寸类别浪费

q: 一个 cache-aside 分布式缓存读请求的完整状态链是什么？
q_en: What is the full state chain for a cache-aside read in a distributed cache?
steps: 缓存 miss 时，服务回源数据库读取权威值。
缓存客户端用 consistent hashing 选择目标缓存节点。
服务把值写回缓存，并设置合适 TTL。
客户端请求到达服务，服务内的缓存客户端接管读路径。
命中则直接从缓存返回；未命中才进入回源链路。
why: 这条链把客户端路由、命中返回、miss 回源和回填都串起来。代价是 miss 会放大到数据库，所以要监控命中率和回源延迟。
why_en: The read path routes to a cache node first, then falls back to the database only on a miss.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Req[Request] --> Client[Cache client]
  Client --> Hash[Consistent hash]
  Hash --> Node[Cache node]
  Node -- hit --> Resp[Return]
  Node -- miss --> DB[(DB)]
  DB --> Fill[Set cache TTL]
  Fill --> Resp

q: 硬件选择应遵循什么原则？

q: DNS 未命中缓存时，典型解析顺序是什么？
q_en: When DNS caches miss, what is the usual resolution order?
steps: 权威服务器返回目标主机的记录，例如 A 记录里的 IP。
递归解析器先问根服务器该去哪个 TLD。
浏览器拿到 IP 后再连接目标服务。
TLD 服务器告诉解析器该域的权威服务器在哪里。
why: DNS 树按从右到左的域名层级走：根先定位 TLD，TLD 再定位权威服务器，权威服务器给最终记录。缓存命中会跳过其中部分步骤。
why_en: A cache miss walks the hierarchy from root to TLD to authoritative DNS, then the browser uses the returned address.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant R as Recursive Resolver
  participant Root as Root DNS
  participant TLD as TLD DNS
  participant Auth as Authoritative DNS
  B->>R: resolve www.example.com
  R->>Root: ask root
  Root-->>R: ask .com TLD
  R->>TLD: ask .com
  TLD-->>R: ask authoritative DNS
  R->>Auth: ask authoritative
  Auth-->>R: A record
  R-->>B: IP address

q: DNS 域名层级如何被解析？
q_en: How is a DNS name processed through the hierarchy?
text: DNS 名字通常按{{从右到左}}的层级解析：先定位{{TLD}}，再定位组织域和子域。
text_en: DNS names are usually processed {{right to left}}: first the {{TLD}}, then the organization domain and subdomains.
why: 域名右侧更接近根层级，所以 `api.shop.example.com` 会先落到 `.com`，再逐步缩小到 `example` 和子域。这个模型解释了为什么根服务器只需要指路，不保存每台主机。
why_en: DNS works from the root side of the name toward the specific host, so each layer only has to delegate the next step.

q: 解析模式默认更偏向哪一种？
q_en: Which resolution mode is the better default?
options: 递归：每一层服务器继续替上一层往下查
迭代：本地解析器逐层查询并接收下一跳提示

q: 这种 DNS 分流的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of DNS-only load distribution?
options: 缓存会放大不均衡，故障 IP 也可能在 TTL 内继续被返回
DNS 会自动探测每台后端 CPU 并实时避开高负载
客户端一定能拿到最近的数据中心
DNS 可以无限返回所有服务器 IP，不受响应大小影响
options_en: Caching can amplify imbalance, and a failed IP may keep being returned until TTL expires.
DNS automatically probes every backend CPU and avoids high load in real time.
Clients always receive the nearest data center.
DNS can return every server IP without response-size concerns.
why: DNS round robin 是粗粒度分流，缓存层可能把一批用户固定到同一个 IP；服务器坏了也要等缓存过期才收敛。短 TTL 能缓解，但会增加解析流量。
why_en: DNS-only balancing is coarse because resolver caches can skew traffic and keep failed addresses alive until TTL expiry.
tradeoff: 简单全局分流 vs 缓存导致的慢收敛和不均衡

Stateful is always cheaper; stateless is always strongly consistent.

tradeoff: 会话映射控制更强 vs LB 层更易扩展

scenario: 入口层既要支持高吞吐 TCP 转发，也可能要按 HTTP 路径、header 或 cookie 路由。
scenario_en: The entry layer may need high-throughput TCP forwarding, but it may also need routing by HTTP path, header, or cookie.
q: L4 和 L7 LB 的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the tradeoff between L4 and L7 load balancing?
options: L4 看传输层连接，开销低；L7 看应用内容，路由更灵活但更重
L4 只能处理数据库表；L7 只能处理磁盘文件
L4 一定终止 TLS；L7 一定不能看 HTTP
L4 是浏览器缓存；L7 是 DNS 根服务器
options_en: L4 uses transport-layer connection data with lower overhead; L7 inspects application content for more flexible routing at higher cost.
L4 only handles database tables; L7 only handles disk files.
L4 always terminates TLS; L7 can never inspect HTTP.
L4 is browser caching; L7 is a DNS root server.
why: L4 主要按 TCP/UDP 连接信息转发，路径短；L7 能看 HTTP 语义，所以可按 URL、header、cookie 做路由。代价是 L7 要解析更多内容，吞吐和延迟成本更高。
why_en: L4 is faster and more connection-oriented, while L7 is heavier but can route using application-level HTTP information.
tradeoff: 低开销连接转发 vs 应用语义路由能力

termDefinitions.meaning: Layer 7（L7）：OSI 应用层，可理解 HTTP 路径、header、cookie 等语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Layer 7 is the application layer, where routing can use HTTP paths, headers, cookies, and similar semantics.

q: 多层 LB 部署中，请求通常怎样逐层被处理？
q_en: How is a request usually handled in a tiered load-balancer deployment?
steps: Tier-3 L7 LB 终止 TLS、检查 HTTP 路径，并转到后端服务池。
Tier-1 ECMP 路由器把入口流量摊到多个下一层路径。
Tier-2 L4 LB 用连接哈希保持同一连接落到稳定的 L7 LB。
后端服务处理业务逻辑并返回响应。
why: Tier-1 先分散入口流量，Tier-2 保持连接路径稳定，Tier-3 才做 HTTP 级路由和 TLS 卸载。这样把横向扩展、连接一致性和应用语义处理分开。
why_en: The tiers split responsibilities: ECMP spreads traffic, L4 keeps connection routing stable, and L7 performs application-aware forwarding.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["Client"] --> T1["Tier-1 ECMP"] --> T2["Tier-2 L4"] --> T3["Tier-3 L7"] --> B["Backend pool"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Equal-Cost Multi-Path（ECMP）：在多条等价网络路径之间分摊流量的路由方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ECMP is a routing technique that spreads traffic across multiple equal-cost network paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tier-3：这里指最靠近应用后端的 L7 负载均衡层。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tier-3 here means the Layer 7 load-balancing tier closest to application backends.

scenario: 一个聊天应用要保存联系人和消息历史；多用户并发读写、权限、搜索和数据增长都开始让平面文件吃不消。
scenario_en: A chat app stores contacts and message history; concurrent access, permissions, search, and growth are making flat files painful.
q: 为什么应引入数据库？
q_en: Why should you introduce a database?
options: 数据库提供结构化存取、并发控制、权限和索引能力
数据库能保证所有网络请求零延迟
数据库会自动消除所有业务 bug
数据库只用于保存图片二进制，不能保存消息
options_en: A database provides structured access, concurrency control, permissions, and indexing.
A database guarantees zero latency for every network request.
A database automatically removes all business bugs.

q: ACID 四个属性分别保护什么？
q_en: What do the four ACID properties protect?
text: ACID = {{Atomicity}} 保证事务全成或全不成，{{Consistency}} 保证状态合法，{{Isolation}} 隔离并发事务，{{Durability}} 保证提交后可恢复。
text_en: ACID = {{Atomicity}} all-or-nothing, {{Consistency}} valid state, {{Isolation}} concurrent transactions do not interfere, and {{Durability}} committed data survives failure.
why: ACID 是关系型事务的核心口径，用来挡脏读、丢失更新、幻读等并发异常。代价是强约束通常会限制极端写扩展或提高协调成本。
why_en: ACID describes transaction guarantees that protect data integrity, usually at the cost of more coordination.

q_en: Why is consistent hashing better for node additions and removals?
options: 它把 key 和节点放在环上，节点变化时只迁移相邻范围内的数据
它保证所有 key 永远不重新路由，节点变化也零迁移
它把每个查询都广播到所有节点，用全量查询避免迁移
它删除分区键并改用全表扫描，让路由层不用维护状态
options_en: It places keys and nodes on a ring, so node changes move only nearby ranges.
It guarantees keys are never rerouted and node changes move no data.
It broadcasts every query to every node and avoids migration by querying all data.
It removes the partition key and uses full table scans so routing has no state.
why: `hash mod n` 的 n 变了会让大量 key 重新取模；一致性哈希让节点变化只影响环上相邻区间。代价是随机节点分布仍可能不均，常配虚拟节点。
why_en: Consistent hashing limits movement on node changes because only adjacent key ranges on the ring need reassignment.
tradeoff: 扩缩容少迁移 vs 环上分布仍需均衡

scenario: 一个分片商品库需要按 `brand` 查询。写入必须尽量快，但按品牌查询可以接受 scatter-gather。
scenario_en: A sharded product store needs queries by `brand`. Writes must stay fast, while brand queries can tolerate scatter-gather.
q: 二级索引更适合怎么分区？
q_en: How should the secondary index be partitioned?
options: 按 document 本地建索引，每个 shard 只索引自己的数据
按 term 建全局索引，把同一 brand 都路由到少数索引 shard
删除索引，所有查询都让客户端猜 shard
把索引写进 DNS TXT 记录
options_en: Use document-partitioned local indexes, where each shard indexes only its own data.
Use term-partitioned global indexes, routing the same brand to a few index shards.
Delete indexes and let clients guess shards.
Write the index into DNS TXT records.
why: 本地索引的写入只碰当前数据 shard，写路径短；查询 brand 时要 fan out 到所有 shard，再等最慢 shard。这里写入优先，所以接受读侧 scatter-gather。
why_en: Document-partitioned local indexes keep writes local and fast, while accepting scatter-gather reads for secondary-key queries.
whenOtherWins: 如果品牌查询必须低延迟且写入量较小，term-partitioned global index 更合适。
tradeoff: 本地写入快 vs 二级查询 scatter-gather

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scatter-gather sends a query to multiple shards and then collects and merges their results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二级索引：主分区键之外，按其他字段加速查询的索引。

scenario: 数据库已经分片，客户端或路由层必须知道 `userId=42` 当前在哪个 shard；分片迁移时映射会变化。
scenario_en: The database is sharded, and the client or routing tier must know which shard currently owns `userId=42`; mappings change during shard moves.
q: 如何维护分片路由信息？
q_en: How should shard-routing information be maintained?
options: 用协调服务维护 partition 到 node 的映射并通知路由方
把映射硬编码进每个移动 App，永不更新
让所有请求先全表扫描所有 shard
把 shard 映射放进浏览器 CSS 文件
options_en: Use a coordination service to store partition-to-node mappings and notify routers.
Hard-code mappings into every mobile app forever.
Make every request scan all shards first.
Put shard mappings into a browser CSS file.
why: 分片拓扑会变化，路由层需要可更新的权威映射；ZooKeeper 这类协调服务可以保存映射并通知客户端或路由器。代价是协调服务本身要高可用。
why_en: A coordination service keeps shard maps current and notifies routers or clients when topology changes.
whenOtherWins: 如果分片很少且拓扑长期不变，静态配置能先用；如果客户端很厚，也可以缓存映射但要有刷新机制。
tradeoff: 路由信息实时更新 vs 协调服务运维成本

q: 集中式和分布式数据库的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between centralized and distributed databases?
options: 集中式简单且强一致更容易；分布式扩展和就近访问更强但协调更复杂
集中式只能保存 DNS；分布式只能做浏览器动画
集中式天然无单点；分布式天然没有同步成本
集中式一定更快；分布式一定不能查询
options_en: Centralized databases are simpler and easier to keep strongly consistent; distributed databases scale and serve nearby users better but need more coordination.
Centralized databases only store DNS; distributed databases only animate browsers.
Centralized systems naturally have no single point; distributed systems have no synchronization cost.
Centralized is always faster; distributed cannot query.
why: 集中式适合数据能装进单节点且一致性优先的阶段；分布式用更多节点换容量、可用性和地理低延迟。代价是跨节点 join、同步和一致性处理更难。
why_en: Centralized databases are simpler for small strongly consistent workloads, while distributed databases buy scale and locality with coordination cost.
tradeoff: 简单强一致 vs 扩展性和地理可用性

scenario: 分布式查询要在站点 A 和 B join 三张表。`Product` 在 B 有 100,000 行，每行 200 bit；网络 50 Mbps，访问延迟 0.1s。若先在 B 用 `Brand='Wolf'` 过滤到 10 行再发到 A，传输量会大幅下降。
scenario_en: A distributed query joins tables across sites A and B. `Product` at B has 100,000 rows, each 200 bits; the link is 50 Mbps with 0.1s access delay. Filtering `Brand='Wolf'` at B leaves 10 rows before sending to A.
q: 这个例子训练的设计结论是什么？
q_en: What design lesson does this example teach?
options: 尽量在数据源头过滤，少跨站点搬无关行
总是把最大表完整搬到另一个站点
跨站点 join 时网络传输量可以忽略
过滤必须等所有表都搬到同一台机器后再做
options_en: Filter at the data source whenever possible to avoid moving irrelevant rows across sites.
Always move the largest table completely to the other site.
Network transfer volume is negligible for cross-site joins.
Filtering must wait until all tables are moved to one machine.
why: 公式是 T = a + v/b；100,000 行要传约 20,000,000 bit，50 Mbps 下约 0.5s，而过滤到 10 行后传输接近 0.1s 的访问延迟。这个数字告诉我们：分布式查询先做选择和投影，少搬数据。
why_en: The formula T = a + v/b shows that filtering at the source cuts transferred bits, so distributed queries should push selection down.

q: 为什么用 building blocks 组织设计？

options: 能把每个成熟组件当作有接口和代价的模块讨论

options_en: They let you discuss each mature component as a module with interfaces and costs.

why_en: Building blocks save time by reusing known modules, but you still need to explain their interfaces, pressure points, and trade-offs.
whenOtherWins: 如果组件行为本身就是题目重点，例如设计队列或缓存，就要展开内部机制。

q_en: Why is a "NoSQL box" not a complete design?
text: 存储设计要说明 {{访问模式}}, {{主键/排序键}}, {{分页}}, {{版本或幂等键}}；只写一个数据库名字无法判断读写路径。

why: 数据库类型只是起点，真正决定可扩展性的是查询怎么进来、数据怎么分布、重复请求怎么处理。
why_en: The database category is only a starting point; scalability depends on access patterns, keys, and duplicate-handling semantics.

why: 事务让业务代码用 commit/abort 表达原子变化，数据库负责隔离并发和保持约束。但它不自动解决跨服务网络失败或缓存一致性。
why_en: A transaction lets business code express an atomic commit or abort while the database handles concurrency and constraints.
whenOtherWins: 跨多个服务的长流程更适合 saga、消息或补偿动作，而不是把所有步骤塞进单库事务。
tradeoff: 本地一致状态 vs 跨服务可用性

q: 同步 RPC 的调用链正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order of a synchronous RPC call?
steps: 服务端 stub 解包参数并调用目标函数
客户端 stub 把参数序列化成网络消息
客户端 runtime 把消息发到服务端并等待响应
服务端函数执行后把结果交回服务端 stub
客户端 stub 解包响应，调用线程继续执行
why: RPC 的关键链条是 stub 做打包/解包，runtime 做传输，服务端执行真实函数。同步调用期间客户端线程会阻塞到响应或超时。
why_en: In synchronous RPC, stubs marshal and unmarshal data while runtimes transmit messages, and the caller blocks until a response or timeout.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant CS as Client stub
    participant R as RPC runtime
    participant SS as Server stub
    participant S as Server
    C->>CS: call method(args)
    CS->>R: marshal request
    R->>SS: transmit message
    SS->>S: invoke function
    S-->>SS: result
    SS-->>R: marshal response
    R-->>CS: response
    CS-->>C: return value

termDefinitions.meaning: stub 是本地代理代码，负责把函数参数和返回值转换成可传输消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stub is local proxy code that turns function arguments and return values into transportable messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: marshaling 是把内存中的参数编码成标准消息格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Marshaling encodes in-memory arguments into a standard message format.

scenario: 订单服务通过 RPC 调支付服务；客户端超时了，但网络中断前支付服务可能已经扣款。
scenario_en: An order service calls a payment service over RPC; the client times out, but the payment service may already have charged the card before the network failed.
q: 为什么超时不能被 RPC 完全隐藏？
q_en: Why can't RPC fully hide timeouts?
options: 因为调用方无法仅凭超时判断远端是否执行成功
因为 RPC 一定不会序列化参数
因为所有远程调用都必须改成 UDP
因为本地函数也会产生网络分区
options_en: Because the caller cannot know from a timeout alone whether the remote side completed.
Because RPC never serializes arguments.
Because every remote call must use UDP.
Because local functions also create network partitions.
why: 超时只说明调用方没及时拿到响应，不说明远端没做副作用。我会加幂等键、查询状态或补偿流程，避免重试造成重复扣款。
why_en: A timeout only means the caller lacks a response, so idempotency keys or status checks are needed before retrying side effects.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作是纯读且无副作用，简单重试的风险低很多。
tradeoff: 调用抽象简洁 vs 副作用可判定性

顺序一致性

tradeoff: 安全正确性 vs 低延迟高可用

两者都表示数据永不丢失

ACID is only for caches, and CAP is only for single-node databases.
Both only mean low latency.

scenario: 一个服务承诺 99.999% 年可用性；一年按 365 天估算，总时间约 525,600 分钟。
scenario_en: A service promises 99.999% annual availability; using 365 days, the year has about 525,600 minutes.
q: five nines 会迫使哪条设计路径？
q_en: What design path does five nines force?
options: 自动故障检测、快速 failover 和谨慎发布
只靠人工值班，事故后再慢慢恢复
把计划维护都放进业务高峰期
不需要监控，因为停机预算足够宽
options_en: Automated detection, fast failover, and careful releases.
Rely only on humans and recover slowly after incidents.
Schedule planned maintenance during peak business hours.
Skip monitoring because the downtime budget is generous.
why: 公式是 downtime = 525,600 分钟 × (1 - 0.99999) ≈ 5.26 分钟。这个数字会约束故障检测、自动 failover、发布和维护窗口。
why_en: Five nines allows about 5.26 minutes of yearly downtime, which forces fast detection, failover, and careful releases.

scenario_en: A provider claims 99.99% availability, but the contract excludes planned maintenance, partial regional outages, and some attack-related downtime.

q_en: What should you watch when evaluating this SLA?
options: 只看 nines 数字即可
确认停机口径、统计起点和排除项
把 SLA 当作性能延迟承诺
默认所有用户受影响才算停机
options_en: Only look at the number of nines.
Check downtime definitions, measurement start, and exclusions.
Treat the SLA as a latency guarantee.
Assume downtime only counts if every user is affected.

whenOtherWins: 如果只是内部容量草算，先用 nines 做粗估可以，但合同评审不能停在那里。
tradeoff: 宣传指标 vs 可执行故障预算

scenario: 服务一个月只故障一次，但修复花了 12 小时；另一个服务每周都有小故障，但 1 分钟自动恢复。
scenario_en: One service fails only once a month but takes 12 hours to repair; another has weekly small failures but recovers automatically in one minute.
q: 这说明可靠性和可用性怎么区分？
q_en: What does this show about reliability versus availability?
options: 可靠性看故障频率和持续正确运行，可用性还强烈受修复时间影响
可靠性和可用性完全相同，都只看服务名字
只要 MTBF 高，可用性一定高，不受恢复时间影响
MTTR 只影响代码可读性，不影响用户可访问时间
options_en: Reliability is about failure frequency and continued correct operation, while availability is strongly affected by repair time.
Reliability and availability are identical and only depend on the service name.
High MTBF always means high availability, regardless of recovery time.
MTTR affects only code readability, not user-visible access time.
why: 罕见但长时间故障会拖低可用性；频繁但秒级恢复也可能保持较高可用性。设计上要同时提高 MTBF、降低 MTTR。
why_en: Rare long outages can hurt availability more than frequent short ones, so design for both high MTBF and low MTTR.
tradeoff: 少故障 vs 快恢复

scenario: 内部工具流量稳定，单台数据库 CPU 持续 70%，内存不足；目标是快速缓解压力，不想马上改分片和复制拓扑。

tradeoff: 低延迟双向推送 vs 长连接运维成本

options: 所有粉丝都写入时立刻预计算
活跃 feed cache，非活跃读时生成
所有用户每次都全表扫描关注关系

options_en: Precompute for every follower immediately on write.
Use feed cache for active users and generate inactive feeds on read.
Full-scan follow relationships for every user on every read.
Ban celebrities from posting.

whenOtherWins: 如果粉丝量小且读远多于写，全量写时 fan-out 会更简单。
tradeoff: 写放大 vs 首页读取延迟

scenario: 打车系统每 4 秒收到一次司机位置更新；附近司机查询要快，但空间索引更新也会占 CPU 和锁资源。
scenario_en: A ride-hailing system receives driver location updates every 4 seconds; nearby-driver queries must be fast, but spatial-index updates consume CPU and locking resources.
q: 为什么不能只说“用 Quadtree”就结束？
q_en: Why can't you just say "use a Quadtree" and stop?
options: 因为频繁移动会让索引维护成本成为瓶颈
因为 Quadtree 不能表达二维空间
因为附近查询不需要任何索引
因为所有司机位置必须放在 CDN
options_en: Because frequent movement can make index maintenance the bottleneck.
Because a Quadtree cannot represent two-dimensional space.

scenario_en: Estimate a 64-core server handling simple CPU requests: assume 3.5 million instructions per request, CPI=1, and a 3.5 GHz clock.
q: 64K RPS 粗估在设计里怎么用？
q_en: How should the 64K RPS estimate be used in design?
options: 作为服务器数量估算的分母，再用真实压测修正
当作所有请求类型永远成立的 SLA
替代峰值流量、缓存命中率和数据库瓶颈分析
证明单机一定能承接所有生产流量
options_en: Use it as the denominator for server-count estimates, then correct it with load tests.
Treat it as an SLA that holds for every request type forever.
Use it instead of analyzing peaks, cache hit rate, and database bottlenecks.
Use it to prove one machine can handle all production traffic.
why: CPU time = 3.5M × 1 / 3.5GHz = 0.001 秒，所以每核约 1,000 RPS，64 核约 64,000 RPS。这个数是后续估服务器数量的分母。
why_en: At 1 ms per request, one core handles about 1,000 RPS, so 64 cores give roughly 64,000 RPS for capacity estimates.

scenario: 你在做容量草算，需要把机器角色和主要资源压力对应起来，而不是把所有服务器都当同一种盒子。
scenario_en: You are doing a capacity estimate and need to map server roles to their dominant resource pressure instead of treating every server as the same box.
q: 哪些角色映射合理？
q_en: Which role mappings are reasonable?
options: Web server：接负载均衡后的 API 入口，CPU 和网络更关键
Application server：跑业务逻辑和动态内容，CPU/内存压力更大
Storage server：优先提供大容量持久存储
Storage server：一定比所有缓存服务器低延迟
options_en: Web server: API entry point after load balancing, with CPU and network pressure.
Application server: runs business logic and dynamic content, often heavier on CPU and memory.
Storage server: prioritizes large persistent capacity.
Storage server: always lower latency than every cache server.
why: 不同角色的瓶颈不同：入口看连接和 CPU，业务层看逻辑计算，存储层看容量、I/O 和耐久性。混成一种机器会让估算失真。
why_en: Server roles have different bottlenecks, so capacity estimates should separate entry, business logic, and storage pressure.
optionMeanings: 选项主张：Web server：接负载均衡后的 API 入口，CPU 和网络更关键。

scenario: 你要把一个大文件上传平台拆成常见 building blocks：用户上传大视频，后台转码，客户端下载热门视频，服务要限流和监控。

q: 哪组 building blocks 最贴合主路径？
q_en: Which set of building blocks best fits the main path?
options: 大对象存储、异步任务、边缘缓存、限流监控

options_en: Large-object storage, async tasks, edge caching, rate limiting, and monitoring.
Only one in-memory array and cron, with all videos in memory.
Only DNS, with no persistent storage or background jobs.
Only relational transactions, with no transcoding or download cache.
why: 视频是大对象，先落 blob store；转码是异步重任务，交给任务调度；热门下载走 CDN，入口用限流保护，监控看错误和延迟。
why_en: Large videos need blob storage, async transcoding needs task scheduling, popular downloads need a CDN, and rate limiting plus monitoring protect operations.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是小文本 CRUD，关系型数据库和简单后台任务可能足够。
tradeoff: 专用 building blocks vs 单体简化

flowchart LR

scenario_en: A service mostly reads sessions, carts, and preferences by userId, with no joins, complex filters, or cross-row transactions.
q: 为什么 KV store 比 RDBMS 更贴合？
q_en: Why is a key-value store a better fit than an RDBMS here?
options: 它把查询约束成主键访问，换来简单的路由和水平扩展
它自动提供任意字段过滤和多表 join
它要求所有写入走单个 leader 保证串行顺序
它通过固定 schema 降低 value 的版本管理成本
options_en: It narrows access to primary-key lookups, which makes routing and horizontal scaling simpler.
It automatically supports arbitrary field filters and multi-table joins.
It requires all writes to go through one leader for serial order.
It uses a fixed schema to reduce value-version management costs.
why: 我会选 KV store，因为题目只需要按 key 取小对象，数据分片可以直接跟 hash 走。代价是放弃 RDBMS 那套丰富查询和强事务模型。
why_en: A KV store fits because the workload is primary-key access, while the cost is giving up rich relational queries and transactions.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品要大量 join、二级索引过滤和跨实体事务，RDBMS 会更自然。
tradeoff: 主键扩展性 vs 查询表达力

q: Dynamo 风格 KV store 的一致性配置何时确定？
q_en: When is consistency configuration chosen in a Dynamo-style key-value store?
text: 在这个设计里，一致性、可用性、成本和性能的取舍参数应在实例创建时配置，运行中{{不动态修改}}。
text_en: In this design, consistency, availability, cost, and performance knobs are set when the instance is created and are {{not changed dynamically}} at runtime.
why: 这样做能让路由、复制和 quorum 语义稳定。运行时随意改参数会让客户端难以判断一次读写到底承诺了什么。
why_en: Static instance-level settings keep routing, replication, and quorum semantics predictable for clients.

scenario: KV store 遇到网络分区时，业务要求购物车、会话等写入仍被接收，短时间读到旧版本可以接受。
scenario_en: During a network partition, the service must still accept cart and session writes, and short-lived stale reads are acceptable.
q: CAP 取舍应偏向哪一边？
q_en: Which side of the CAP tradeoff should this design favor?
options: CP：拒绝分区侧写入，先保证所有副本一致
AP：继续接收读写，之后用版本合并修复分歧
CA：忽略网络分区，只优化单机一致性
单 leader 串行：所有请求跨分区转到 leader
options_en: CP: reject writes on the partitioned side and preserve replica consistency first.
AP: keep accepting reads and writes, then repair divergence with version reconciliation.
CA: ignore partitions and optimize only single-site consistency.
Single leader: forward every request across the partition to the leader.
optionMeanings: CP 在分区时牺牲可用性。
AP 在分区时保住可用性。
CA 不处理分布式分区现实。
leader 串行把写入口集中起来。
optionDirectness: 适合银行账本这类宁停不乱的场景。
适合用户体验更怕写失败的场景。
只适合单机或同机房小系统讨论。
适合强顺序但网络稳定的部署。
optionScenarioImpacts: 购物车写入会在分区期间失败。
可能出现冲突版本，需要后续合并。
题目的故障模型没有被解决。
分区侧请求会超时或不可达。
why: 我会选 AP，因为题目把“能写进去”放在一致读之前。代价是系统要保存并暴露冲突版本，靠 vector clock 和客户端合并收口。
why_en: I would favor AP because accepting writes matters more than immediate consistency, but the system must later reconcile conflicting versions.
whenOtherWins: 如果写错一次就不可接受，例如资金扣款或库存扣减，CP 或强 leader 方案会更合适。
tradeoff: 写可用性 vs 立即一致性

q: 节点角色应如何设计？

options: 所有节点 peer-to-peer，对外都能协调读写
固定少数 master 节点负责所有写入
让最高配置机器永久保存全部热点 key

Use a small fixed set of master nodes for all writes.
Keep all hot keys forever on the highest-capacity machines.
Stop the cluster and redistribute all data on every scale-out.

why_en: Peer-to-peer nodes plus capacity-weighted virtual nodes let heterogeneous machines join without creating master bottlenecks.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统规模小且强一致写顺序最重要，单 leader 或少量 master 会更容易实现。
tradeoff: 去中心化扩展 vs 集中式顺序控制

q: Dynamo 风格 KV store 如何把 key 映射到 ring？
q_en: How does a Dynamo-style KV store map keys onto the ring?
text: 系统对 key 做 hash 得到固定长度标识符；Dynamo 的经典设计使用 {{MD5}} 产生 {{128-bit}} ID，再用它定位负责节点。
text_en: The system hashes the key into a fixed-length identifier; the classic Dynamo design uses {{MD5}} to produce a {{128-bit}} ID for placement.
why: hash 后的 ID 让任意字符串 key 落到统一的地址空间里。后续 consistent hashing、replica placement 和 preference list 都围绕这个空间工作。
why_en: Hashing keys into one ID space lets consistent hashing and replica placement use the same ring abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: MD5 是一种产生 128-bit 摘要的 hash 算法；这里用于定位，不用于安全签名。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MD5 is a hash algorithm that produces a 128-bit digest; here it is used for placement, not security.

scenario: KV 集群用 `hash(key) % m` 分片。现在从 4 个节点变成 3 个节点，节点本地缓存了自己负责的数据。
scenario_en: A KV cluster shards with hash(key) % m. It shrinks from 4 nodes to 3, and each node locally caches its owned data.
q: 为什么取模分片扩缩容代价高？
q_en: Why is modulo sharding expensive during scale changes?
options: m 变了会让大量 key 换节点，引发数据搬迁和缓存失效
取模会让所有 key 永远落到同一个节点
取模无法用 hash 函数生成数字
取模只影响读路径，不影响数据放置
options_en: Changing m moves many keys to different nodes, causing data movement and cache misses.
Modulo always maps every key to the same node.
Modulo cannot use a hash function to produce numbers.
Modulo only affects reads and not data placement.
why: 问题不在取模算不出来，而是分母一变，大部分 key 的余数都会变。节点要搬大量数据，读请求也会打到没有缓存的新 owner。
why_en: Modulo sharding is painful because changing the divisor remaps many keys, forcing data movement and cache misses.
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 扩缩容扰动

scenario: 你要让 KV store 支持频繁加机器和退机器，同时尽量少移动已有 key。
scenario_en: You need a KV store to add and remove machines often while moving as few existing keys as possible.
q: 为什么选择 consistent hashing？
q_en: Why choose consistent hashing?
options: 它把 hash 空间做成 ring，只让相邻区间在节点变化时移动
它要求所有节点保存完整数据副本
它让每次扩容都重新计算全量 SQL 索引
它用物理时间决定每个 key 的 owner
options_en: It models the hash space as a ring, so only neighboring ranges move when nodes change.
It requires every node to store a full copy of all data.
It rebuilds all SQL indexes on every scale-out.
It uses physical time to decide the owner for each key.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  K["hash(key)"] --> P["position on ring"]
  P --> N["first node clockwise"]
  J["new node joins"]
  J --> S["takes slice from successor"]
  S --> O["other ranges unchanged"]
why: consistent hashing 的核心收益是节点变更只影响 ring 上一段相邻 key。它不是让数据不动，而是把搬迁从近似全量降到局部区间。
why_en: Consistent hashing limits movement to neighboring ranges on the ring instead of remapping most keys.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点数固定且永不扩缩容，简单取模分片的实现成本更低。
tradeoff: 局部搬迁 vs 路由复杂度

q: consistent hashing 中新节点加入时谁受影响？
q_en: Who is affected when a new node joins a consistent-hashing ring?
text: 新节点加入 ring 时，它通常只从顺时针方向的{{后继节点}}接管一段 key；其他节点的 key 区间保持不变。
text_en: When a node joins the ring, it usually takes a key slice from its clockwise {{successor}}, while other nodes keep their ranges.
why: 这就是一致哈希降低扩缩容扰动的地方。新节点和 successor 做数据交接，不需要全体节点一起重排。
why_en: A joining node only exchanges data with its successor, which avoids a cluster-wide reshuffle.

scenario: consistent hashing ring 上有些节点拥有很长的 hash 弧段，导致请求和数据集中到少数机器。
scenario_en: Some nodes on a consistent-hashing ring own long arcs, so requests and data concentrate on a few machines.
q: 如何缓解 ring 上的热点？
q_en: How can you reduce hotspots on the ring?
options: 给每台物理机放多个 virtual nodes，让区间交错分布
把所有热点 key 固定迁到第一台机器
取消 hash，改成客户端随机选节点
每次热点出现就全量重建 ring
options_en: Place multiple virtual nodes per physical machine so ranges interleave.
Move every hot key permanently to the first machine.
Remove hashing and let clients pick random nodes.
Rebuild the entire ring whenever a hotspot appears.
why: virtual nodes 把一台物理机拆成多个 ring 位置，长弧段风险会被摊薄。某台机器故障时，它的负载也会散到多个邻居，而不是压给一个 successor。
why_en: Virtual nodes interleave each physical machine across the ring, smoothing load and spreading failover pressure.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有几台机器和很小数据量，单位置 ring 可能够用，省掉 vnode 管理成本。
tradeoff: 负载均衡 vs 元数据数量

scenario: KV 集群里既有老机器也有新机器，新机器 CPU、磁盘和网络容量更高。
scenario_en: The KV cluster has both old and new machines, and the new machines have more CPU, disk, and network capacity.
q: virtual nodes 如何表达机器容量差异？
q_en: How can virtual nodes represent capacity differences?
options: 给高容量机器分配更多 vnode，让它拥有更多 key range
让所有机器 vnode 数严格相同，避免任何倾斜
只让低容量机器接收写入，高容量机器空闲
把容量信息写进 value，由客户端自行选择节点
options_en: Assign more vnodes to higher-capacity machines so they own more key ranges.
Give every machine exactly the same vnode count to avoid any skew.
Send writes only to low-capacity machines and leave high-capacity machines idle.
Put capacity metadata in values and make clients choose nodes themselves.
why: vnode 数量可以当作权重，高配机器拿更多区间，也就承担更多读写和存储。这样不用要求所有节点硬件同质。
why_en: The vnode count acts as a weight, so larger machines can own more ranges without requiring homogeneous hardware.
whenOtherWins: 如果运维上强制所有机器规格一致，等量 vnode 更简单。
tradeoff: 容量利用率 vs ring 元数据管理

q: 复制模型应选 primary-secondary 还是 peer-to-peer？
q_en: Should replication be primary-secondary or peer-to-peer?
options: primary-secondary：一个 primary 负责写，副本异步跟随
peer-to-peer：任意节点可协调读写，再复制到 preference list
全量复制：每次写同步到集群所有节点
无复制：每个 key 只保存在一个节点上
options_en: Primary-secondary: one primary handles writes and replicas follow asynchronously.
Peer-to-peer: any node can coordinate reads and writes, then replicate to the preference list.
Full replication: synchronously write every update to every node in the cluster.
No replication: keep each key on exactly one node.
optionMeanings: 写入口集中在 primary。
节点角色对等，按 key 选 coordinator。
所有节点都保存每个 key。
没有副本冗余。
optionDirectness: 适合强主写顺序和较小规模。
适合 AP 和无特殊节点要求。

写放大和存储成本过高。
节点丢失就可能丢数据。
why: 我会选 peer-to-peer，因为题目要求故障时继续写，不能让 primary 成为写入单点。代价是系统要接受副本短暂分歧，并用版本与 quorum 收敛。

q: preference list 如何避免副本落到同一物理机？
q_en: How does a preference list avoid placing replicas on the same physical machine?
text: 复制因子为 n 时，coordinator 选择 ring 上后续节点作为副本；构造 preference list 时要跳过已经出现过的{{同一物理节点}}的 vnode。
text_en: With replication factor n, the coordinator picks successors on the ring; the preference list skips vnodes that belong to an already selected {{physical node}}.
why: vnode 是逻辑位置，不跳过同一物理机就会把多个副本放在同一故障域。复制的目标是抗机器故障，不只是凑够 ring 位置。
why_en: Skipping vnodes on the same physical node keeps replicas in separate failure domains.

termDefinitions.meaning: preference list 是某个 key 按 ring 顺序选出的副本节点列表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A preference list is the ordered set of replica nodes selected for a key on the ring.

分区期间所有节点立即删除该 key

q: 版本元数据应选什么？

q: 为什么 `put` 要带上 `get` 返回的 context？
q_en: Why should put include the context returned by get?
text: `get(key)` 返回 value 和版本 context；后续 `put(key, {{context}}, value)` 带回它，系统才能把新写入接到正确的版本历史上。
text_en: `get(key)` returns the value and version context; a later `put(key, {{context}}, value)` supplies it so the system can attach the write to the right version history.
why: context 相当于客户端看到的父版本。没有它，系统只知道来了一个新 value，却不知道它是在覆盖旧版本还是在合并冲突。
why_en: The context identifies the parent version the client observed, so the system can distinguish overwrite from conflict merge.
codeSample:
get(cart:42) -> { value, context: "vc:A=2,B=1" }
put(cart:42, context="vc:A=2,B=1", value=mergedCart)

scenario: 在 Dynamo 风格 KV store 中，vector clock 是每个版本携带的节点 counter 列表，用来比较版本历史。
scenario_en: In a Dynamo-style KV store, a vector clock is the node-counter list attached to each version to compare version history.
q: 比较两个 vector clocks 时能判断哪些关系？
q_en: What relationships can vector-clock comparison reveal?
options: 一个版本包含另一个版本的因果历史
两个版本互不包含，属于并发冲突
两个版本完全相同
哪个机房的物理时钟更准
options_en: One version causally includes the other version's history.
Neither version includes the other, so they are concurrent conflicts.
The two versions are identical.
Which data center has the more accurate physical clock.
why: vector clock 比的是每个节点 counter 的包含关系。它能判断祖先、相同和并发，但不测量墙钟准确度。
why_en: Vector-clock comparison checks counter inclusion, so it can detect ancestry, equality, and concurrency, not clock accuracy.

scenario: 同一个 key 在网络分区期间分叉；vector clock 用节点 counter 记录每个版本来自哪条历史。
scenario_en: The same key diverges during a network partition; vector clocks use node counters to record each version's history.
q: vector clock 冲突到合并的顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order from vector-clock conflict to merge?
steps: 客户端读取到两个 leaf versions，并看到它们互不包含
分区两侧分别写出 [A:2,B:1] 和 [A:2,C:1]
客户端按业务规则合并 value
A 节点先写出父版本 [A:2]
协调节点写入合并结果，并把自己的 counter 加一
why: 完整链条是先有共同父版本，再在分区里分叉，读时暴露 leaf versions，最后由业务合并并写回新版本。代价是客户端要懂对象语义。
why_en: The chain is parent, divergent writes, exposed leaf versions, application merge, and a new version written back by the coordinator.

q: 截断 vector clock 的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the risk of truncating a vector clock?

会让 value 的二进制内容自动损坏

It automatically corrupts the binary value.
It immediately makes all replicas strongly consistent.
It prevents any node from writing that key again.

tradeoff: 元数据上限 vs 因果判断精度

scenario: 一个 key 有 n=3 个副本。你希望一次读和最近一次成功写至少在一个副本上相交。
scenario_en: A key has n=3 replicas. You want every read quorum to overlap with the latest successful write quorum on at least one replica.
q: r 和 w 应满足什么条件？
q_en: What condition should r and w satisfy?
options: r + w > n
r + w = n
r = 1 且 w = 1
r 和 w 都必须等于 0
options_en: r + w > n.
r + w = n.
r = 1 and w = 1.
Both r and w must be zero.
why: r+w>n 逼迫读集合和写集合至少重叠一个副本，读才有机会看到最新写。n=3 时 r=2,w=2 可行，r=2,w=1 不够。
why_en: The rule r + w > n forces read and write quorums to overlap on at least one replica.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确接受更弱读一致性，可以放宽重叠要求来换更高可用性和更低延迟。
tradeoff: 读到新值概率 vs quorum 延迟和可用性

q: 一次 `put` 的 quorum 写入顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order of a quorum write for put?
steps: coordinator 在本地生成新 vector clock 并写本地副本
客户端把 key、context 和 value 发给 coordinator
coordinator 把写入转发给 preference list 里的其他副本
至少 w 个副本确认后，coordinator 向客户端返回成功
未及时确认的副本后续通过修复流程补齐
why: coordinator 自己算一个确认，所以还要等 w-1 个其他副本。代价是未同步副本会短暂落后，后续要靠 read repair、handoff 或 anti-entropy 修复。
why_en: A put succeeds after the coordinator and enough replicas acknowledge it, while lagging replicas are repaired later.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant Q as Coordinator
  participant R1 as Replica1
  participant R2 as Replica2
  C->>Q: put(key, context, value)
  Q->>Q: write local + new vector clock
  Q->>R1: replicate
  Q->>R2: replicate
  R1-->>Q: ack
  Q-->>C: success when w acks

q: 一次 `get` 发现冲突版本后如何收口？
q_en: How does a get converge after finding conflicting versions?
steps: 客户端按业务规则把多个 value 合成一个新 value
coordinator 查询 top n 个可达副本
系统比较 vector clocks，发现互不包含的版本
coordinator 等到 r 个响应后返回 leaf versions 和 context
客户端带合并后的 value 和 context 再次 put
why: 读路径先凑够 r 个响应，再用版本元数据判断是否有分叉。系统不懂购物车或偏好设置的业务语义时，会把合并责任交给客户端。
why_en: The read path gathers r responses, detects divergent leaf versions, and lets the client merge when application semantics are needed.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[client get] --> Q[coordinator]
  Q --> R[query n replicas]
  R --> W[wait for r]
  W --> V{versions related?}
  V -- yes --> One[return latest]
  V -- no --> Many[return versions + context]
  Many --> Merge[client merges]
  Merge --> Put[put merged value]

scenario: 某个 key 的首选副本里有节点临时宕机。业务仍要求写入成功，等节点恢复后再补数据。
scenario_en: One preferred replica for a key is temporarily down. The business still wants writes to succeed and repair when the node returns.
q: 应该用 strict quorum 还是 sloppy quorum？
q_en: Should the system use strict quorum or sloppy quorum?
options: strict quorum：只允许首选 n 个 owner 响应
sloppy quorum：健康后继节点临时代收
停止写入：等所有首选副本恢复
删除该 key：避免不一致
options_en: Strict quorum: only the preferred n owners may respond.
Sloppy quorum: use healthy successor nodes as temporary holders.
Stop writes until all preferred replicas recover.
Delete the key to avoid inconsistency.
why: 我会用 sloppy quorum，因为题目把临时故障下的写可用性放在第一位。代价是临时代收节点要保存 hint，恢复后把数据交还原 owner。
why_en: Sloppy quorum keeps writes available by using healthy fallback nodes, but it needs hinted handoff to return data later.
whenOtherWins: 如果合规要求副本必须只落在指定 owner 上，strict quorum 更可控但可用性更低。
tradeoff: 临时可用性 vs 副本归属纯度

q: hinted handoff 的恢复链路是什么？
q_en: What is the recovery chain for hinted handoff?
steps: A 恢复后，D 把暂存数据转发给 A
写入到来时，原 owner A 临时不可达
D 删除自己的临时副本
coordinator 选择后续健康节点 D 临时代收
D 保存 value，并记录 hint：这份数据属于 A
why: 完整链条是 owner 不可达、健康节点代收、hint 记录归属、owner 恢复后交还、临时副本清理。代价是恢复前读到哪个副本会影响新旧程度。
why_en: Hinted handoff writes to a temporary healthy node, records the real owner, hands data back on recovery, and then deletes the temporary copy.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Q as Coordinator
  participant A as Owner A down
  participant D as Healthy D
  Q->>A: write
  A--xQ: unavailable
  Q->>D: store with hint owner=A
  A-->>D: recovers
  D->>A: hand off data
  D->>D: delete temporary copy

q: 为什么临时故障处理不足以覆盖机房灾难？
q_en: Why is temporary-failure handling not enough for data-center disasters?
text: hinted handoff 能处理短暂节点故障；如果整座机房断电或灾难失效，需要把副本跨{{独立数据中心}}放置。
text_en: Hinted handoff handles short node outages; if a whole data center fails, replicas must be placed across {{independent data centers}}.
why: 节点级临时代收解决的是局部不可达。机房级故障会同时打掉同一故障域里的多个副本，所以副本放置要跨故障域。
why_en: Node-level handoff handles local outages, while data-center failure requires replicas in separate failure domains.

scenario: 一个副本长时间离线后回归，系统要找出它和健康副本之间哪些 key range 不一致，但不能全量扫描和传输全部数据。
scenario_en: A replica returns after a long outage, and the system must find inconsistent key ranges without scanning and transferring the full dataset.
q: 应该用什么反熵机制？
q_en: What anti-entropy mechanism should be used?
options: Merkle tree：先比 root hash，再递归定位差异范围
随机抽样：只查几个 key，没发现就认为一致
全量复制：每次恢复都传完整数据集
物理 timestamp：只保留时间戳最大的副本
options_en: Merkle tree: compare root hashes, then recurse to locate differing ranges.
Random sampling: check a few keys and assume consistency if none differ.
Full copy: transfer the entire dataset on every recovery.
Physical timestamp: keep only the replica with the largest clock.
why: Merkle tree 让两个副本先比摘要，只有摘要不同的子树才继续下钻。代价是 key range 变化时树要重算，尤其节点加入或离开后。
why_en: Merkle trees narrow repair to differing ranges by comparing hashes, but range changes require rebuilding tree state.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据集很小，全量复制可能比维护 hash tree 更省工程成本。
tradeoff: 修复带宽 vs 树维护成本

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Merkle tree is a hash tree whose leaves hash data and whose parents hash child hashes.

termDefinitions.meaning: anti-entropy 是副本之间后台比较并修复不一致数据的过程。

q: Merkle tree 如何定位副本差异？
q_en: How does a Merkle tree locate replica differences?
steps: 如果 root 不同，只递归比较不同分支的 child hash
两个副本先交换某个 key range 的 root hash
定位到不同叶子或小范围后，只同步这些 key
如果 root 相同，认为该范围一致
节点范围变化时，相关 tree 需要重新计算
why: 正常路径是先用 root hash 快速排除一致范围，异常时沿不同分支下钻，最后只传不一致 key。成本收尾是 ring 变化会让 range 和 tree 失效。
why_en: Merkle repair compares roots first, drills only into differing branches, transfers only bad keys, and pays rebuild cost when ranges change.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[exchange root hash] --> B{same?}
  B -- yes --> C[range identical]
  B -- no --> D[compare child hashes]
  D --> E[find differing leaves]
  E --> F[sync only those keys]
  G[node joins/leaves] --> H[recompute affected trees]

scenario: KV 集群里节点会短暂抖动或网络超时。你不希望每次短故障都触发 ring 重平衡和大规模数据迁移。
scenario_en: Nodes in the KV cluster can briefly flap or time out, and you do not want every short outage to trigger ring rebalancing and large data movement.
q: 故障检测应如何处理短暂离线？
q_en: How should failure detection treat short outages?
options: 先标疑似故障，持续失败才改 membership
第一次心跳失败就永久移出 ring 并搬迁
每次失败都立即复制全量数据到所有节点
完全不记录节点状态，靠客户端猜测
options_en: Mark it as suspect first, and change membership only after sustained failure.
Remove it from the ring permanently after the first missed heartbeat and move data.
Copy the full dataset to every node after every failure.
Do not record node state, and make clients guess.
why: 我会把短故障和 membership 变更分开。短抖动用 sloppy quorum、handoff 和重试吸收，持续失败或计划下线才调整 ring。
why_en: Short outages should be absorbed without membership changes, while sustained failures or planned changes update the ring.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点已经确定永久退役，及时改 membership 才能释放责任区间。
tradeoff: 避免抖动迁移 vs 故障收敛速度

scenario: KV store 没有中心 membership 服务。每个节点本地持久化成员变更历史，需要低带宽地传播到全体节点。
scenario_en: The KV store has no central membership service. Each node persists membership history locally and needs to spread it with low bandwidth.
q: 应如何传播 membership？
q_en: How should membership be propagated?
options: gossip：节点随机互相同步 membership history
单中心表：所有节点每毫秒同步读一个主库
客户端广播：每个客户端维护全量节点状态
关闭持久化：重启后重新猜测集群成员
options_en: Gossip: nodes randomly exchange membership history with peers.
Single central table: every node polls one primary database every millisecond.
Client broadcast: every client maintains the full node state.
Disable persistence and guess membership again after restart.
why: gossip 让 membership 视图最终一致，不需要单点协调者。代价是传播有延迟，所以不能把它当作强一致配置总线。
why_en: Gossip spreads membership without a coordinator, but the view is eventually consistent rather than instant.
whenOtherWins: 如果集群很小且已有可靠控制平面，中心 membership 服务更容易审计。
tradeoff: 去中心化传播 vs 收敛延迟

q: gossip 中 token set 表示什么？
q_en: What does a token set represent in gossip membership?
text: 在 consistent hashing 集群里，token set 表示节点在 hash 空间中拥有的{{virtual nodes}}或 token 位置。
text_en: In a consistent-hashing cluster, a token set represents the {{virtual nodes}} or token positions owned by a node in the hash space.
why: membership 不只是知道“有这台机器”，还要知道它负责哪些 ring 位置。gossip 同步这些历史后，节点才能对 key placement 达成最终一致。
why_en: Membership includes both machines and their ring positions, so gossip must converge on token ownership.

scenario: 同一台物理机的多个 vnode 被当成独立成员分别加入 ring，并各自传播 membership 更新。
scenario_en: Multiple vnodes from the same physical machine join the ring as if they were independent members and spread membership updates separately.
q: 这种做法有什么风险？
q_en: What risk does this create?
options: 可能造成逻辑分区，让不同节点学到不一致的更新集合
会让所有 key 自动均匀到每个机房
会消除物理机故障域问题
会让 vector clock 不再需要 counter
options_en: It can create logical partitioning where nodes learn inconsistent update sets.
It automatically balances all keys across every data center.
It removes physical-machine failure-domain risk.
It makes vector clocks no longer need counters.
optionMeanings: 同机 vnode 被当成独立成员传播。
把 membership 问题误当负载均衡问题。
误以为逻辑节点能消除物理故障域。
把 gossip 风险和版本元数据混在一起。
optionDirectness: 适合检查 vnode 与物理节点绑定是否正确。
适合讨论跨机房 placement，不适合本题。
适合反驳单机多 vnode 的误解。
适合 vector clock 卡，不适合 membership 卡。
optionScenarioImpacts: 不同节点可能收敛到不同成员历史。
无法解释更新集合不一致。
同一物理机故障仍会打掉多个 vnode。
counter 是否存在不解决 gossip 分裂。
why: vnode 是逻辑位置，但故障和 membership 语义仍要绑回物理节点。把同机 vnode 当独立成员传播，可能让集群状态分裂。
why_en: Vnodes are logical positions, but membership and failure semantics must still be tied to physical nodes.
tradeoff: vnode 细粒度路由 vs 物理节点成员语义

auto-increment 不能生成任何数字
数据库主键不需要唯一

why_en: Single-node auto-increment works locally, but distributed ID generation must handle uniqueness, throughput, and availability across nodes.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有写入天然只进一个小型数据库，auto-increment 是最简单方案。

scenario_en: Event IDs are used to trace a request across many microservices and to range-scan records by creation time.
q: time-sortable ID 带来什么收益？
q_en: What benefit does a time-sortable ID provide?
options: 仅按 ID 排序就能近似按创建时间排序
它保证所有跨地域事件都有严格因果顺序
它让数据库不再需要任何索引

options_en: Sorting by ID also roughly sorts by creation time.
It guarantees strict causal order for all cross-region events.
It removes the need for every database index.

why: time-sortable ID 把时间信息编码进主键，调试和范围扫描不用再额外查 timestamp 列。它通常只给时间顺序，不等于免费获得严格全局因果。
why_en: A time-sortable ID embeds time into the key, helping scans and tracing without guaranteeing strict global causality.

q: 64-bit numeric ID 的量级够不够？
q_en: Is a 64-bit numeric ID space large enough?
text: 64-bit ID 空间约为 {{2^64 ≈ 1.8×10^19}}；即使一年发 365 billion 个 ID，也能支撑约 {{50 million}} 年量级。
text_en: A 64-bit ID space is about {{2^64 ≈ 1.8×10^19}}; even at 365 billion IDs per year, it lasts on the order of {{50 million}} years.
why: 这里的数字用于判断容量上限不是主要瓶颈；真正难的是分布式唯一性、可用性和顺序语义。64-bit numeric 还让索引和存储比 128-bit 随机字符串更紧凑。
why_en: The 64-bit space is huge enough that the harder problems are distributed uniqueness, availability, and ordering semantics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 64-bit 表示 ID 用 64 个二进制位编码，最多有 2^64 种组合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 64-bit means the ID is encoded with 64 binary bits, giving up to 2^64 combinations.

scenario: 服务需要无需协调地在每台机器本地生成 ID，但下游明确要求 64-bit numeric，并且希望按 ID 插入索引时更紧凑。
scenario_en: A service wants local ID generation without coordination, but downstream requires 64-bit numeric IDs and compact index inserts.
q: UUID v4 为什么不满足这个需求？
q_en: Why does UUID v4 not satisfy this requirement?
options: 它是 128-bit 随机 ID，非 64-bit 且不单调
它必须访问中心数据库才能生成每个 ID
它只能在单机上保证唯一，跨机一定重复
它会让所有事件严格按因果排序并保持 64-bit
options_en: It is a 128-bit random ID, not 64-bit and not monotonic.
It must call a central database for every generated ID.

q: range handler 发号链路是什么？
q_en: What is the ID issuance flow with a range handler?
steps: 应用服务器在本地从 start 递增到 end
range handler 在复制存储中把该 range 标记为 taken
应用服务器耗尽 range 后再请求下一段
应用服务器向 range handler 申请一段 ID
range handler 返回 start/end
why: 中心服务只负责租段和持久化状态，应用服务器负责段内快速发号。如果应用服务器死掉，未发完的段通常丢弃，避免重复回收。
why_en: The handler leases and persists ranges, while app servers issue locally and discard unused IDs on failure to avoid duplicates.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant RH as Range Handler
  participant S as Replicated Store
  App->>RH: request range
  RH->>S: mark range taken
  S-->>RH: committed
  RH-->>App: start/end
  App->>App: increment locally
  App->>RH: request next when exhausted

q: range handler 自身故障时如何恢复？
q_en: How can the range handler recover from its own failure?
text: range handler 要把 range 状态写入{{replicated storage}}；主 handler 故障时，failover server 从 checkpoint 恢复已分配区间。
text_en: The range handler stores range state in {{replicated storage}}; if the primary handler fails, a failover server recovers allocated ranges from a checkpoint.
why: 发号服务不能只把已租 range 放在内存里，否则重启后可能重复分配。复制存储和 checkpoint 让新 handler 接着同一份事实工作。
why_en: Persisted replicated state prevents a restarted handler from leasing ranges that were already handed out.

q: Lamport clock 的更新时间规则是什么？
q_en: What is the update rule for a Lamport clock?
steps: 接收方收到消息后，把本地 clock 设为 max(local, received)+1
进程在本地事件前先把 counter 加一
发送消息时，把当前 counter 附在消息上
若 a happened-before b，则 timestamp(a) 小于 timestamp(b)
相同 timestamp 可用 node id 打破并列，形成任意 total order
why: Lamport clock 维护的是 happened-before 的必要顺序：消息接收一定晚于发送。它能给一致的偏序扩展，但不能单靠两个数字判断谁导致了谁。
why_en: Lamport clocks preserve happened-before ordering through message timestamps, but two values alone do not prove causality.

q: 能否据此判断 7 导致了 9？

不能；Lamport timestamps 完全不支持排序

Yes; the smaller number is always the direct cause of the larger one.
Yes; the smaller node id always means parent event.

q: 为什么 TrueTime 类方案更强？
q_en: Why is a TrueTime-like scheme stronger?
options: 它返回时间区间和不确定性，只有区间不重叠时才断言顺序

why_en: TrueTime models clock uncertainty explicitly with intervals, giving safe ordering when intervals do not overlap.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是需要大致时间排序，Snowflake 成本低得多。
tradeoff: 可证明时间顺序 vs 硬件运维成本

q: TrueTime 类 64-bit ID 可以如何编码不确定性？
q_en: How can a TrueTime-like 64-bit ID encode uncertainty?
text: 一种布局是 41-bit timestamp、{{4-bit uncertainty}}、10-bit worker 和 8-bit sequence；uncertainty 表示时间区间宽度。
text_en: One layout is a 41-bit timestamp, {{4-bit uncertainty}}, 10-bit worker, and 8-bit sequence; uncertainty represents the interval width.
why: timestamp 给排序主轴，uncertainty 让比较方知道这不是精确单点。8-bit sequence 表示每 worker 每个时间粒度 256 个本地序号。
why_en: The timestamp gives the main order, while the uncertainty bits expose the width of the time interval.
codeSample:
41-bit earliest_time | 4-bit epsilon | 10-bit worker | 8-bit sequence

Yes; A's earliest being smaller is enough.

tradeoff: 不丢消息 vs 可能重复处理

q: pub-sub 的基础功能需求有哪些？

text: pub-sub 至少要支持创建 {{topic}}、写入消息、{{subscribe/unsubscribe}}、读取消息、设置 {{retention}} 并在过期后删除。
text_en: Pub-sub should support creating a {{topic}}, writing messages, {{subscribe/unsubscribe}}, reading messages, setting {{retention}}, and deleting expired data.
why: 这些功能覆盖 topic 生命周期、订阅关系和消息生命周期。没有 retention，broker 的磁盘增长就没有清理边界。
why_en: These operations cover topic lifecycle, subscription lifecycle, and message lifecycle.

termDefinitions.meaning: retention 是消息在系统里保留多久，过期后可被清理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Retention is how long messages remain available before they can be deleted.

scenario: pub-sub API 规定单条消息最大 1 MB。团队想把 200 MB 视频文件直接写进消息体。
scenario_en: The pub-sub API caps each message at 1 MB. The team wants to put a 200 MB video directly into the message body.
q: 这个限制带来的设计结论是什么？
q_en: What design conclusion follows from this limit?
options: 把大对象放对象存储，消息只传对象引用和元数据
把 broker 变成视频 CDN
关闭消息大小校验
让消费者猜测文件位置
options_en: Store the large object in object storage and send only a reference plus metadata.
Turn the broker into a video CDN.
Disable message-size validation.
Make consumers guess the file location.
why: 1 MB 是 API 给定上限，不是估算结果；它约束消息只承载小 payload。200 MB 视频应进对象存储，消息里放 URL、id 和校验信息。
why_en: A 1 MB message cap means large blobs belong in object storage, with the message carrying only references and metadata.
whenOtherWins: 如果 payload 本身只有几 KB，直接放消息体能减少一次外部读取。
tradeoff: 小消息快速分发 vs 大对象外部存储

termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the callable interface and set of constraints exposed by a system.

termDefinitions.meaning: MB 是兆字节，常用于描述消息或文件大小。

scenario: 银行交易事件可能几周后还要审计重放；普通分析点击事件处理完就很少再读。
scenario_en: Banking transaction events may need audit replay weeks later, while ordinary analytics clicks are rarely read after processing.
q: retention 应如何设置？
q_en: How should retention be set?
options: 按 topic 或业务类型配置不同保留期
所有 topic 永久保留
所有 topic 处理后立刻删除
让消费者自行删除 broker 磁盘文件
options_en: Configure different retention periods by topic or business type.
Retain every topic forever.
Delete every topic immediately after processing.
Let consumers delete broker disk files directly.
why: 保留期是业务风险和存储成本的取舍，银行审计和临时分析不该用同一个默认值。常见默认值可以是几天，但关键 topic 要单独配置。
why_en: Retention should follow business replay needs and storage cost, so different topics need different policies.
whenOtherWins: 如果法规要求永久留存，才把保留期拉长并接受存储成本。
tradeoff: 可重放窗口 vs 存储成本

scenario: 设计 pub-sub 时，需要保存订阅关系、缓冲待分发消息，并保存消费者的临时读取状态。
scenario_en: In a pub-sub design, you need to store subscriptions, buffer messages to distribute, and keep temporary consumer read state.
q: 哪组基础组件最贴合？
q_en: Which set of building blocks fits best?
options: 数据库存订阅元数据；消息队列/日志缓冲消息；key-value store 存消费状态
只用一个浏览器 localStorage 保存订阅、消息和 offset
只用负载均衡器保存所有消息并执行 fanout
只用 DNS 记录表达订阅关系和消费进度
options_en: A database for subscription metadata, a queue/log for messages, and a key-value store for consumer state.
Use only browser localStorage for subscriptions, messages, and offsets.
Use only a load balancer to store all messages and perform fanout.
Use only DNS records to model subscriptions and consumer progress.
why: 订阅关系是持久元数据，消息需要顺序存储和分发，消费 offset 适合轻量 key-value 读写。把这些职责拆开，扩展和故障处理更清楚。
why_en: Separate subscription metadata, message storage, and consumer state because they scale and fail differently.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单进程教学 demo，可以先用内存结构模拟，但不能代表生产架构。
tradeoff: 职责拆分可扩展 vs 组件数量增加

scenario: 队列式 pub-sub 用一个 topic queue 接收发布者写入，再由 fanout 组件把消息复制到每个订阅者队列。
scenario_en: Queue-based pub-sub uses a topic queue for publisher writes, then a fanout component copies messages into subscriber queues.
q: 基于队列的 pub-sub fanout 路径如何工作？
q_en: How does queue-based pub-sub fanout work?
steps: message director 查询订阅数据库
publisher 把消息写入 topic queue
每个 subscriber 从自己的 consumer queue 读取
message director 把消息复制到每个 consumer queue
subscriber 服务维护订阅关系
why: 这个设计用 topic queue 接收写入，再把消息复制到每个订阅者队列。它概念简单，但订阅者很多时会产生大量队列和消息副本。
why_en: Queue-based pub-sub copies each topic message into subscriber queues, which is simple but expensive at large fanout.

termDefinitions.meaning: pub-sub 是发布者写入 topic、多个订阅者独立接收消息的通信模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Publish-subscribe is a model where publishers write to a topic and multiple subscribers receive messages independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: fanout 是把一条消息分发给多个下游接收者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout means distributing one message to multiple downstream receivers.

termDefinitions.meaning: topic queue 是队列式 pub-sub 中先接收某个 topic 全部写入的队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A topic queue is the queue that first receives all writes for one topic in a queue-based pub-sub design.

只放在 message director 的调用栈

Only in the message director's call stack.

scenario: 一个热门 topic 有 500 万订阅者；队列式设计为每个订阅者维护一个 consumer queue，并把每条消息复制进去。
scenario_en: A hot topic has five million subscribers; the queue-based design maintains one consumer queue per subscriber and copies every message into each queue.
q: 这个设计的主要扩展问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main scaling problem?
options: 队列元数据和消息副本数量随订阅者线性放大
topic 会自动失去所有订阅者
消息会无法被任何人读取
生产者必须等待每个消费者在线
options_en: Queue metadata and message copies grow linearly with subscriber count.
The topic automatically loses all subscribers.
Messages cannot be read by anyone.
The producer must wait for every consumer to be online.
why: 每个订阅者一条队列会把 fanout 成本提前物化成存储和元数据。百万级订阅者下，一条消息可能变成百万份副本，这就是 storage amplification。
why_en: Per-subscriber queues materialize fanout as storage amplification, which explodes for millions of subscribers.
whenOtherWins: 如果订阅者很少且每个都需要独立队列隔离，这个设计可以先用。
tradeoff: 实现直观隔离 vs 存储放大

scenario_en: A pub-sub system must support high-throughput small messages and millions of subscribers without copying each message per subscriber.
q: 应优先采用哪种存储组织？
q_en: Which storage organization should you prefer?
options: 共享 append-only topic log

A full queue copy per subscriber, duplicating every message.

why: append-only log 让消息只存一次，消费者用 offset 表达各自进度。代价是 broker 要管理分区、保留期、消费者 offset 和重平衡。
why_en: An append-only broker log stores each message once and lets consumers track their own offsets.
whenOtherWins: 如果订阅者很少且要强隔离 per-consumer 队列，队列式 fanout 更直观。
tradeoff: 共享日志低放大 vs offset 和分区管理复杂度

q: broker 的 topic log 由哪些概念组成？
q_en: What concepts make up a broker topic log?
text: 一个 topic 可拆成多个 {{partition}}；partition 内消息追加到不可变 {{segment}}；消费者用 {{offset}} 指向读取位置。
text_en: A topic can be split into {{partitions}}; messages append into immutable {{segments}}; consumers read from an {{offset}}.
why: partition 提供并行度，segment 让磁盘文件可滚动和清理，offset 让每个消费者独立恢复。分区内追加顺序通常就是该分区的顺序边界。
why_en: Partitions provide parallelism, segments make storage manageable, and offsets let consumers resume independently.

termDefinitions.meaning: partition 是 topic 的一个有序分片，通常由某个 broker 承载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is an ordered shard of a topic, usually hosted by a broker.

termDefinitions.meaning: segment 是 partition 内的一段日志文件，便于滚动、读取和删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is a chunk of a partition log used for rolling, reading, and deletion.

scenario: 一个 topic 的写入超过单盘 I/O 能力；消息之间没有强 key 顺序要求，只需要把写入摊到多个 broker。
scenario_en: A topic's write rate exceeds one disk's I/O capacity; messages have no strict key-ordering requirement and should be spread across brokers.
q: 生产者应如何分配分区？
q_en: How should producers assign partitions?
options: 用 round robin 或加权 round robin 在分区间分摊
永远写同一个 partition，让单盘继续承受全部写入
让消费者在读取时决定每条消息应该写到哪里
把消息体越大越写到更旧的 segment 来避开新文件
options_en: Use round robin or weighted round robin across partitions.
Always write to one partition and keep all writes on one disk.
Let consumers decide where each message should have been written.
Write larger messages to older segments to avoid newer files.
why: 没有 key 顺序约束时，轮询能把写 I/O 摊到多个分区和 broker。代价是跨分区不再保留生产顺序，消费者要按分区读取。
why_en: Round-robin partitioning spreads write I/O when there is no key-level ordering requirement.
whenOtherWins: 如果同一用户或订单必须有序，应按 key 固定到同一 partition。
tradeoff: 写入负载均衡 vs key 顺序保证

q: partition key 应怎么选？
q_en: How should the partition key be chosen?
options: 用 orderId 分区，让同一订单落到同一 partition
完全随机分区每条订单事件以追求均匀写入
按消息大小分区，让大消息和小消息分离
按消费者机器名分区，把路由绑到实例
options_en: Partition by orderId so one order lands in one partition.
Randomly partition each order event to chase even writes.
Partition by message size to separate large and small records.
Partition by consumer machine name and bind routing to instances.
why: 顺序边界是 orderId，所以同一个 orderId 必须进入同一有序日志。这样不同订单还能并行，代价是热门 orderId 可能形成局部热点。
why_en: Partition by the key whose order you need, so one order's events stay in the same ordered log.
whenOtherWins: 如果完全不需要 key 顺序，随机或轮询分区能更均匀分摊负载。
tradeoff: 单 key 顺序 vs 负载均衡

worker 领取消息并开始处理
处理失败，消息按策略延迟后重新可见或重新入队
运维或修复任务检查 DLQ 并决定重放、修数据或丢弃
重试计数增加并保留失败原因
why: 这条链要讲清楚失败不是直接消失：领取、失败、延迟重试、计数达上限、进 DLQ。代价是重复处理和积压监控，业务要幂等并告警。
why_en: Retries should preserve failure state, stop after a limit, and isolate poison messages in a dead-letter queue.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["Message"] --> W["Worker"]
  W -->|fail| Delay["Backoff delay"] --> Q["Retry queue"] --> W
  W -->|max attempts| D["DLQ"] --> Ops["Inspect / replay / discard"]

scenario: 支付扣款消费者可能重复收到同一扣款消息。产品不能接受重复扣款，也不想丢掉已接受的扣款请求。
scenario_en: A payment-charge consumer may receive the same charge message twice. The product cannot accept duplicate charges and also does not want to lose accepted requests.
q: 应怎样描述投递语义和业务保护？
q_en: How should delivery semantics and business protection be described?
options: 队列用至少一次投递，业务用幂等键保证同一 chargeId 只扣一次
只要队列叫 exactly-once，业务就不需要唯一键
改成最多一次投递，所有失败都静默丢弃
让消费者随机决定是否扣款
options_en: Use at-least-once delivery and an idempotency key so one chargeId is charged once.
If the queue says exactly-once, the business needs no unique key.
Switch to at-most-once delivery and silently drop all failures.
Let the consumer randomly decide whether to charge.
why: 队列层很难单独承诺端到端 exactly-once，尤其跨数据库和外部支付网关。面试里更稳的是至少一次加业务幂等键，用 chargeId 挡重复副作用。
why_en: For payments, combine at-least-once delivery with a business idempotency key rather than trusting the queue alone.
whenOtherWins: 如果消息是可丢的指标采样，最多一次可以用更低成本换简单性。
tradeoff: 可靠投递 vs 重复副作用控制

termDefinitions.meaning: exactly-once 是端到端只生效一次的目标，通常需要队列、存储和业务操作共同配合。

termDefinitions.meaning: 最多一次投递避免重复，但失败时可能丢消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-most-once delivery avoids duplicates but may lose messages on failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: chargeId 是一次扣款业务操作的唯一标识，可用于幂等扣款。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chargeId is the unique identifier for one charge operation and can enforce idempotency.

scenario: 一个热门队列的写入量突然暴涨，导致同 broker 上其他低流量队列的延迟也升高。
scenario_en: A hot queue's write rate spikes, and low-traffic queues on the same broker also see higher latency.
q: 应优先考虑哪种隔离手段？
q_en: Which isolation mechanism should be considered first?
options: 把热门队列拆分或迁移到独立 broker/partition 资源
把所有队列合并到一个更大的锁里并共享瓶颈
关闭低流量队列的监控来隐藏邻居影响
让消费者忽略延迟并继续堆积未处理消息
options_en: Split or move the hot queue onto dedicated broker or partition resources.
Merge all queues behind one larger lock and share the bottleneck.
Disable monitoring for low-traffic queues to hide neighbor impact.
Ask consumers to ignore latency while backlog keeps growing.
why: 热点队列会抢磁盘、CPU 和网络资源，影响同机邻居。把它拆分或独立放置，可以用资源隔离保护其他队列的尾延迟。
why_en: Hot queues should be split or isolated so one workload does not steal broker resources from others.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是消费者太少导致积压，先加消费者可能比迁移 broker 更快。
tradeoff: 性能隔离 vs 迁移和运维成本

scenario: 队列系统上线后，用户抱怨通知延迟。你需要判断是生产变慢、broker 积压，还是消费者追不上。
scenario_en: After the queue system launches, users complain about notification delay. You need to tell whether producers are slow, brokers are backlogged, or consumers are behind.
q: 最应该监控哪组指标？
q_en: Which metrics should you monitor first?
options: 吞吐、depth、lag、retry/DLQ
只监控官网首页颜色和按钮圆角来推断消息延迟
只看消费者机器名长度和实例编号是否好记
只记录每条消息的字体和 UI 展示顺序
options_en: Throughput, depth, lag, retries, and DLQ counts.
Only monitor the marketing homepage color and button radius to infer queue delay.
Only inspect consumer machine-name length and whether instance numbers are memorable.
Only record each message's font and UI display order.
why: 这些指标能把延迟拆成写入速度、队列积压、消费能力和失败重试。没有 lag 和 DLQ，系统只知道慢了，却不知道压力卡在哪一段。
why_en: These metrics separate producer speed, backlog, consumer progress, and failure loops.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题是单个业务结果错误，还需要 trace 和业务日志定位消息内容。
tradeoff: 可观测性成本 vs 故障定位速度

q: 面试中设计 pub-sub 系统时，回答顺序怎样更完整？
q_en: In a pub-sub design interview, what answer order is more complete?
steps: 深入 broker、partition、replication、offset、retention 和失败恢复
先澄清 topic、publisher、subscriber、消息大小、保留期和投递语义
画高层路径：publish 到 topic，broker 存储，subscriber 或 group 读取
最后评估扩展性、可用性、耐久性、顺序和成本取舍
定义核心 API：create、write、subscribe、read、delete
why: 面试回答先定需求和 API，再画主路径，最后下钻关键取舍。这样不会一上来陷进 Kafka 细节，也不会漏掉保留期、顺序和投递语义。
why_en: Start with requirements and APIs, then draw the main path before diving into broker tradeoffs and evaluation.

scenario: 面试官让你总结分布式队列和 pub-sub 的共同评价维度，而不是再列组件名。

只比较哪个产品名更流行，不讨论顺序或投递语义
options_en: Explain tradeoffs by system guarantees.
Say it must be good because it uses many servers, without explaining guarantees or costs.
Only recite all API names without explaining how they satisfy requirements.
Only compare which product name is more popular, ignoring ordering and delivery semantics.
why: 评价题要回到需求是否被满足，以及每个保证花了什么代价。顺序、投递语义、复制和分区是最容易互相牵制的几条轴。
why_en: Evaluate the design by guarantees and tradeoffs, especially where ordering, delivery, replication, and partitioning constrain each other.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确要求选型落地，再把这些维度映射到 Kafka、RabbitMQ、SQS 等具体产品。
tradeoff: 系统保证完整性 vs 组件清单式回答

q: Rate limiter 的核心职责是什么？
q_en: What is the core job of a rate limiter?
text: Rate limiter 在一个时间范围内限制客户端请求数；超过阈值后会 {{throttle 或 reject}} 多余流量。
text_en: A rate limiter caps requests in a time range and {{throttles or rejects}} traffic above the limit.
why: 我会把它放在服务入口附近，先挡住超过配额的请求，再让后端处理正常流量。
why_en: A rate limiter protects backend capacity by blocking or slowing requests after a configured quota is exceeded.

云成本因失控调用持续上涨
把数据库查询自动改写成索引查询
options_en: A retry storm or bad config exhausting backend resources
One tenant consuming the shared quota for a long time
Runaway calls driving cloud cost upward
Automatically rewriting database queries to use indexes
why: 它控制入口流量和公平性，也能限制失控调用的成本；但它不替数据库优化查询计划。
why_en: Rate limiting protects capacity, fairness, and cost, but it does not optimize database queries for you.

q: Leaking bucket 为什么会延迟新请求？
q_en: Why can a leaking bucket delay new requests?
text: Leaking bucket 把请求放进 {{FIFO queue}}，再按固定 outflow rate 处理；突发流量会先填满队列。
text_en: A leaking bucket puts requests in a {{FIFO queue}} and drains at a fixed outflow rate; bursts fill the queue first.
why: 这能保护下游的稳定出流，但新来的请求可能排在旧突发后面。
why_en: It protects downstream steady throughput, but new requests can wait behind an earlier burst.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO means the first queued item is processed first.

q_en: What is the analogy between rate limiting and TCP flow control?

why_en: The analogy is that both mechanisms express receiver capacity before the receiver is overwhelmed.

q: 生命周期管理最应该做什么？

把所有对象永久放在最高性能层
每天随机删除冷对象
禁止对象带任何 metadata

Keep every object forever in the highest-performance tier

Forbid objects from carrying metadata

why_en: Tiering trades read latency for storage cost, and expiration rules remove data that no longer needs retention.

scenario: 估算一个 I/O 密集 blob 服务：峰值按 5M RPS 粗算，每台服务器保守按 500 RPS。
scenario_en: Estimate an I/O-heavy blob service with a rough 5M peak RPS and 500 RPS per server.
q: 服务器数量估算如何得到？
q_en: How do you estimate the server count?
text: 服务器数 = peak RPS / per-server RPS = 5,000,000 / 500 ≈ {{10,000 servers}}。
text_en: Server count = peak RPS / per-server RPS = 5,000,000 / 500 ≈ {{10,000 servers}}.
why: RPS = Requests Per Second，每秒请求数；这个数不是背答案，而是后续负载均衡、机房容量和监控阈值的输入。
why_en: RPS means requests per second, and this estimate feeds load balancing, capacity planning, and monitoring thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: RPS：每秒请求数，用来估算服务吞吐需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPS means requests per second and measures service throughput demand.

scenario: 每天 250,000 个上传，每个视频约 50 MB，缩略图约 20 KB，先按单副本、单清晰度估算。
scenario_en: There are 250,000 uploads per day; each video is about 50 MB with a 20 KB thumbnail, estimated as one copy and one resolution.
q: 每日新增存储量的粗估公式是什么？
q_en: What is the rough daily storage formula?
text: 每日存储 ≈ uploads/day × (video + thumbnail) = 250,000 × (50 MB + 20 KB) ≈ {{12.5 TB/day}}。
text_en: Daily storage ≈ uploads/day × (video + thumbnail) = 250,000 × (50 MB + 20 KB) ≈ {{12.5 TB/day}}.
why: 这个值只是单副本基线；复制、多分辨率和保留策略会把真实容量继续放大。
why_en: This is only the single-copy baseline; replicas, multiple resolutions, and retention increase the real footprint.

scenario: 同一 blob 服务每天新增约 12.5 TB，读路径按 5M DAU、每人 20 次、每次 50 MB 粗算。
scenario_en: The service adds about 12.5 TB per day; reads are estimated from 5M DAU, 20 reads per user, and 50 MB per read.
q: 为什么 outgoing bandwidth 会远高于 incoming bandwidth？
q_en: Why is outgoing bandwidth much higher than incoming bandwidth?
text: 写入带宽约 daily bytes / 86,400；读取带宽约 DAU × reads/user × object size / 86,400，因此读侧可到 {{hundreds of Gb/s}}。
text_en: Ingress is daily bytes / 86,400; egress is DAU × reads per user × object size / 86,400, so reads can reach {{hundreds of Gb/s}}.
why: DAU = Daily Active Users；读多写少会把 CDN、并行下载和缓存放到设计重点。
why_en: DAU means daily active users, and read-heavy bandwidth pushes the design toward CDN, caching, and parallel download.

termDefinitions.meaning: DAU：每日活跃用户数，常用来估算读请求和带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU means daily active users and is often used to estimate read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN：把公开内容缓存到离用户更近的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches public content at edge locations closer to users.

q: Blob store 的高层架构链路是什么？
q_en: What is the high-level architecture flow of a blob store?
steps: Load balancer 把请求分发到 frontend servers
Client 发起上传、下载或删除 API
Frontend 与 manager 协调 metadata 和授权
Data nodes 存储或读取实际 chunks
Monitoring 观察节点和磁盘健康
why: 前端服务器处理 API，manager 负责位置和权限，data node 负责真实字节。
why_en: Frontend servers handle APIs, the manager handles placement and permissions, and data nodes store the bytes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> LB[Load balancer]
  LB --> FE[Frontend]
  FE --> M[Manager]
  M --> MD[(Metadata DB)]
  FE --> DN[Data nodes]
  MON[Monitoring] --> M
  MON --> DN

q: Blob 上传写路径应如何排序？
q_en: What is the correct order of the blob upload path?
steps: Manager 生成 blob ID 并选择 chunk 放置位置
Frontend 接收 uploadBlob 请求
Frontend 把 chunks 写到 data nodes
Manager 记录 blob metadata 和副本信息
客户端拿到 fully qualified blob path
why: 写路径先确定身份和放置，再写真实数据，最后把可寻址路径和元数据发布给客户端。
why_en: The write path chooses placement, writes chunks, records metadata, and then returns the stable blob path.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Frontend
  participant M as Manager
  participant D as DataNodes
  C->>F: uploadBlob
  F->>M: ask placement
  M-->>F: blob id + chunk map
  F->>D: write chunks
  M->>M: record metadata
  F-->>C: blob path

q: Blob 下载读路径应如何排序？
q_en: What is the correct order of the blob download path?
steps: Manager 检查 public/private 权限
Frontend 用 blobPath 请求 metadata
Manager 返回 chunk 到 data node 的映射
Client 或 frontend 从 data nodes 读取 chunks
客户端缓存 chunk metadata 以便后续读
why: 读路径先拿 metadata 和授权，再按 chunk map 读数据；缓存 metadata 能减轻 manager 压力。
why_en: Reads fetch metadata and authorization first, then use the chunk map to read data and cache future lookups.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Frontend
  participant M as Manager
  participant D as DataNodes
  C->>F: downloadBlob(path)
  F->>M: metadata + auth
  M-->>F: chunk map
  C->>D: read chunks
  C->>C: cache metadata

q: List blobs 为什么使用 continuation token？

text: 当 prefix 匹配太多 blob 时，响应返回一页结果和 {{continuation token}}；客户端带 token 请求下一页。

why_en: The token preserves scan position so the service avoids huge responses and fragile offset paging.

q: 90% 场景该用的模式是？
q_en: What cache pattern should you use in most read-heavy systems?
options: write-behind：先写缓存异步再落库
cache-aside + Redis：先查缓存，未命中查库、带 TTL 回填、返回
read-through：缓存层自己负责未命中回源
write-through：写请求同时写缓存和数据库
options_en: Write-behind: write to the cache first and flush to the database asynchronously.
Cache-aside with Redis: check the cache, and on a miss query the database, store with a TTL, and return.
Read-through: the cache layer itself fetches from the database on a miss.
Write-through: writes hit the cache and the database together.
optionMeanings: 写侧优化模式

optionDirectness: write-behind 适合吸收写延迟，但会带来丢失和可见性风险。
cache-aside 适合读多写少，应用 miss 后查库再回填缓存。
read-through 适合缓存层统一封装数据加载，但系统复杂度更高。
write-through 适合写后必须同步更新缓存，但每次写多一跳。
optionDirectness_en: Write-behind absorbs write latency but adds loss and visibility risk.
Cache-aside fits read-heavy systems: the app reads the DB on a miss and fills the cache.
Read-through fits when the cache layer owns loading, but it adds system complexity.
Write-through fits when writes must update cache synchronously, but every write pays an extra hop.
why: cache-aside 实现直白、适配大多数读重系统，是面试默认答案。
why_en: The pattern you will use ninety percent of the time is cache-aside with Redis: check the cache, and on a miss query the database, store with a TTL, and return.
whenOtherWins: 静态资源分发走 CDN、小而少变的配置走进程内缓存——不是所有缓存需求都该进 Redis。

q: 缓存「最难的部分」是什么，有哪些策略？
q_en: What is the hardest part of caching, and what strategies handle it?
options: 内存容量不够；策略是升级更大内存的机器
驱逐策略太复杂；策略是统一用 LRU

序列化开销太大；策略是换二进制格式
options_en: Not enough memory; the fix is a bigger machine.
Eviction policy is too complex; the fix is to standardize on LRU.
Invalidation: invalidate on writes, use short TTLs and accept staleness, or combine both — the choice depends on how fresh the data needs to be.
Serialization overhead is too high; the fix is to switch to a binary format.

q: 防止 cache stampede 的手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which techniques prevent a cache stampede? Select all that apply.
options: 加锁：只让一个请求重建条目，其余等待结果
提前重算：条目过期前主动刷新
错开 TTL：避免大量条目同时过期
把 TTL 全部设为 0
options_en: Locking: let only one request rebuild the entry while the rest wait.
Early recomputation: refresh the entry before it expires.
Staggered TTLs: avoid a mass of entries expiring at once.
Set every TTL to zero.
optionScenarioImpacts: 挡住重建请求同时涌向数据库
让读请求永远撞不上未命中窗口
打散过期时间点，防止大批 key 同时失效
等于关闭缓存，制造问题而非解决问题
why: 锁（single flight）、提前刷新、错峰过期是三板斧；TTL 设 0 等于每次都打库，恰恰制造问题。
why_en: Prevent stampedes with locking so one request regenerates, early recomputation before expiry, and staggered TTLs.

Sharding means you no longer need to think about data consistency.

q: 一致性哈希的工作方式是？

Both servers and keys hash onto a virtual ring, and a key belongs to the next server found clockwise; adding a node only moves the keys between it and its neighbor.

一致性哈希用环把增删节点影响限制在邻近区间。
广播适合发现或同步少量元数据，不适合定位数据归属。

Consistent hashing uses a ring to localize node add/remove impact to nearby ranges.
Broadcast can discover or sync small metadata, not locate data ownership.
why: 环结构把增删节点的影响局部化：移除节点时也只有它的 key 迁给环上的下一台。Memcached/Redis Cluster、Cassandra/DynamoDB、部分 LB 和 CDN 都在用。
why_en: Consistent hashing places servers and keys on a ring where each key belongs to the next server clockwise, so only a small range moves when nodes change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key 都映射到一个虚拟环上，增删节点只影响环上局部一小段 key 的分布算法。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希里承载服务器和 key 哈希值的环形结构。

q: 10 台服务器的集群加 1 台：简单取模 vs 一致性哈希，各要移动多少数据？
q_en: In a 10-server cluster adding one server, how much data moves with modulo hashing versus consistent hashing?

Neither needs to move any data.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps servers and keys onto a virtual ring so adding or removing a node only affects a small local range of keys.

q: PACELC 定理补充了 CAP 的什么盲区？
q_en: What blind spot in CAP does PACELC cover?
options: 分区时选延迟
CAP 适用于单机
网络永远不会分区
平时其实是一致性 vs 延迟的取舍
options_en: During a partition, choose latency.
CAP applies to single machines.
Networks never partition.

CAP only describes behavior during partitions, which are rare; day to day the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency, since strong consistency is slower even on a healthy network because nodes must coordinate before responding.
why: PACELC：分区（P）时选 A 或 C；否则（E）选延迟（L）或一致性（C）。日常运行中强一致的代价是协调延迟。
why_en: PACELC notes that outside rare partitions the real tradeoff is consistency versus latency, since strong consistency requires coordination before responding.

q: 把「订票系统选强一致」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the strong-consistency decision chain for a ticket-booking system in the right order.
steps: 选型：对这些关键路径选择强一致
需求：库存/余额/订座——读到陈旧数据会超卖、放过欺诈或重复订座
缓解：只对关键路径强一致，描述、评论等展示数据用最终一致
代价：分区时部分请求被拒，且日常延迟更高（节点需先协调）
why: 需求（陈旧读有真实代价）→ 选强一致 → 代价（可用性与延迟）→ 缓解（按路径混用一致性模型）。
why_en: Stale reads costing real money lead to strong consistency, whose availability and latency costs are contained by applying it only to critical paths.

scenario: 普通产品型系统设计面试，客户端形态单一，也没有特殊的服务间性能诉求，要快速选定 API 协议。
q: 默认应该选哪种 API 协议？
options: REST
GraphQL
gRPC
SOAP
options_en: REST.
GraphQL.
gRPC.
SOAP.
why: 别过度思考协议选择：没有特殊理由就默认 REST，它简单、通用、考官零解释成本。
why_en: Default to REST, which uses HTTP verbs for CRUD on resources, unless you have a specific reason not to.
whenOtherWins: 客户端多样、数据需求差异大 → GraphQL；内部服务间通信、性能关键 → RPC/gRPC；对接遗留企业系统 → SOAP。
tradeoff: REST『通用、零解释成本』 vs 专用协议『更贴合特定约束，但引入额外复杂度』

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格。
