termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端可以精确声明所需字段的查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language that lets the client specify exactly which fields it needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，常用于服务间通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance remote-procedure-call framework, often used for service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 XML 的老式企业级 Web 服务协议，报文冗长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOAP is an older XML-based enterprise web-service protocol with verbose messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对资源的四种基本操作。

客户端自定义查询形状的协议
面向动作、序列化高效的内部通信协议
基于 XML 信封的老式企业协议
optionScenarioImpacts: 考官几乎不需要额外解释就能读懂你的接口
本场景客户端单一，引入 GraphQL 的复杂度换不来收益
本场景不是服务间调用，用不上它的性能优势
现代产品面试几乎不会以 SOAP 为默认选择
optionDirectness: 适合客户端形态简单、没有特殊协议收益时，REST 的解释成本最低。
适合多端字段差异大时；单一客户端下通常只是增加 schema 层。
适合内部高性能调用；对普通外部产品 API 往往解释成本更高。
适合遗留企业集成；新系统默认选它会带来不必要复杂度。
optionMeanings_en: Resource-oriented HTTP verbs, the industry's default choice.
A protocol where clients shape their own query.

An older XML-envelope enterprise protocol.

scenario: 系统要同时服务移动端、网页端、手表端等多种客户端，各端需要的数据字段差异很大，担心接口返回太多或太少数据。
q: 最匹配的 API 风格是？
options: REST 固定返回全部字段
为每种客户端各复制一套 REST API
GraphQL——客户端精确声明要什么数据
改用 FTP 传输数据
options_en: REST that always returns every field.
Duplicate a separate REST API for each client type.
GraphQL — clients specify exactly what data they want.
Switch to FTP for data transfer.
why: GraphQL 让客户端按需取数，正好解决多样客户端 over-fetch/under-fetch 的痛点。
why_en: GraphQL lets each client specify exactly the data it needs, avoiding over-fetching and under-fetching across diverse clients.
whenOtherWins: 客户端单一、标准 CRUD 场景下 REST 更简单直接，不必引入 GraphQL 的额外复杂度。
tradeoff: GraphQL『按需取数，避免 over/under-fetch』 vs REST『固定形状，简单但可能取多或取少』

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 HTTP 动词对资源做增删改查的 API 风格，返回字段通常固定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style using HTTP verbs on resources, usually with a fixed response shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端可以精确声明所需字段的查询语言，避免多拿或少拿数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a query language letting clients specify exactly which fields they need, avoiding over- or under-fetching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于批量传输文件的协议，不适合按字段取数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is a protocol for bulk file transfer, not suited to field-level data fetching.

用多套接口应对多种客户端的字段差异

把文件传输协议错用在结构化数据接口上

接口数量随客户端数线性增长，维护成本高
同一接口下每种客户端只取自己需要的字段
FTP 没有字段级查询能力，不适配这个需求
optionDirectness: 适合字段形状稳定的单一客户端；多端差异大时容易 over-fetch。
适合少量端且差异固定；端越来越多时接口复制会变成维护债。
适合客户端字段需求差异大、想由客户端声明返回形状的场景。
适合文件传输，不适合表达产品 API 的查询形状。

Uses multiple endpoints to handle differing client field needs.
One endpoint whose field shape is declared by the client.
Misapplies a file-transfer protocol to a structured-data API.

Endpoint count grows linearly with client types, raising maintenance cost.
Each client fetches only the fields it needs from one endpoint.

Duplicated REST endpoints fit a few fixed clients; as clients grow, they become maintenance debt.
GraphQL fits diverse client field needs because the client declares the response shape.

scenario_en: The system serves mobile, web, and watch clients, and each client needs a different field shape from the API.

scenario: 设计内部微服务之间的调用接口：不对外暴露，追求最低开销与最高性能。
q: 最合适的协议是？
options: 对外那套 REST 直接复用
RPC（如 gRPC）——动作导向，序列化高效
GraphQL
轮询 + 邮件通知
options_en: Reuse the same REST API used for external clients.
RPC such as gRPC — action-oriented with efficient serialization.
GraphQL.
Polling plus email notifications.
why: RPC/gRPC 面向动作、序列化高效，在性能关键的内部 service-to-service 通信里快过 REST。
why_en: Use RPC like gRPC for internal service-to-service APIs where performance is critical, since it is faster than REST.
whenOtherWins: 面向外部用户/第三方的公开 API 应默认 REST——生态、可调试性和通用性更好。
tradeoff: gRPC『更快更省，但对外生态和可调试性弱』 vs REST『通用易调试，但内部调用开销更高』

options: POST /v1/tweets，body 只带 { "text": string }
POST /v1/tweet?user_id=123&text=hello
GET /v1/createTweet
POST /v1/tweets，body 带 { "user_id": string, "text": string }
options_en: POST /v1/tweets with a body containing only { "text": string }.
POST /v1/tweet?user_id=123&text=hello.
GET /v1/createTweet.

why: 资源用复数名词（tweets）、创建用 POST、正文只带业务数据；当前用户从 auth token 推导，绝不由客户端在 body 里自报。
why_en: Use a plural resource name with POST and put only the tweet text in the body, deriving the current user from the auth token.
whenOtherWins: 内部高性能调用可用 gRPC 的动作型接口，那时不必套 REST 资源惯例。
tradeoff: 从 token 推导身份『多一次校验，但杜绝伪造』 vs 由客户端传参『少一步，但任何人可冒充他人』

scenario: 发推接口把当前用户写在请求体的 user_id 字段里，服务端直接读取这个字段当作作者。
q: 让客户端在请求体里传 user_id 来标识「当前用户」，隐患是什么？
options: 请求体会变大，浪费带宽
JSON 解析速度变慢
接口无法做 HTTP 缓存
任何人都能伪造别人的身份发帖
options_en: The request body gets larger, wasting bandwidth.
JSON parsing becomes slower.
The endpoint can no longer use HTTP caching.
Anyone can forge another user's identity and post as them.
why: 身份来自认证而非输入：始终从 auth token 推导当前用户，否则请求体里的 user_id 可被随意篡改冒充。
why_en: Never take the current user's identity from the request body; derive it from the authentication token, or anyone can impersonate anyone.
codeSample:
# 不安全：身份来自可篡改的请求体
POST /v1/tweets
body: { "user_id": "123", "text": "hi" }

# 安全：身份来自认证 token
POST /v1/tweets
Authorization: Bearer <token>
body: { "text": "hi" }   # user 从 token 解出

q: REST 资源命名的惯例是？

动词短语（/createTweet）
全大写路径（/TWEETS）

Verb phrases, like /createTweet.
All-uppercase paths, like /TWEETS.
Naming doesn't matter — anything goes.
why: REST 把系统建模成资源集合：路径用复数名词表示事物集合，动作交给 HTTP 动词表达。
why_en: REST resources are plural nouns representing things in your system, with actions expressed by HTTP verbs.
codeSample:
GET  /v1/tweets        # list
GET  /v1/tweets/{id}   # read one
POST /v1/tweets        # create (verb is the HTTP method, not the path)

已经会框架了，重看 intro 补不上深潜缺口。
缺口还没补，hard 题会叠加更多复杂约束。
缺口永远得不到练习机会。
optionDirectness: 适合补深潜和取舍短板；难度刚好上一个台阶。
适合重新了解面试形式；补不上 medium 的深潜缺口。
适合高手压测；当前缺口还没补完会更卡。
适合临时休息；不能解决已经暴露的能力缺口。
optionMeanings_en: Use medium-difficulty problems to practice the deep-dive transition.
Retreat to the most basic introductory material.
Skip the middle tier and jump to the hardest problems.
Treat getting stuck as a reason to quit.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It targets exactly the deep-dive and tradeoff gap described.
You already know the framework; the intro won't fix deep-dive gaps.
The gap is still open, and hard problems stack even more constraints.
The gap never gets a chance to close.
optionDirectness_en: Fits the deep-dive and tradeoff gap with one step up in difficulty.
Fits reviewing interview format, not fixing medium-level deep dives.
Fits expert stress tests; this learner's current gap is still open.
Fits taking a break, but it does not close the exposed gap.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is a detailed exploration of one component or scenario in the design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个方案之间必须取舍的对比关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tradeoff is the balance you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全练习系统设计题的关键规则：
q_en: Fill in the key rule for practicing system design questions:
text: 先{{自己尝试}}，再看{{answer key}}；最后通过{{peer mock}}训练在时间压力下讲出设计。
why: 这条规则把输入学习变成输出训练：先产出，再对照，最后计时讲出来，三步都不能跳。
why_en: The rule turns passive input into active output: attempt first, compare against the answer, then rehearse it under time pressure.
tradeoff: 先产出后对照 vs 先看答案后模仿

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

scenario: 你把某道题的 answer key 从头读到尾，觉得完全看懂了，但没有自己动手画过。
scenario_en: You read a question's answer key end to end and feel you understand it, but you have not drawn the design yourself.
q: 只看题解、不自己画设计，最容易造成什么问题？
q_en: What problem does reading the solution without drawing your own design most often cause?
options: 自动获得口头表达能力
自动知道所有 tradeoff
面试时完全不需要澄清需求
产生“看懂了”等于“会讲会设计”的错觉
options_en: You automatically gain verbal explanation skills.
You automatically know every tradeoff involved.
You no longer need to clarify requirements in the interview.
You get the illusion that understanding equals being able to design and explain it.
why: 阅读答案时结构和取舍已经被作者组织好了；面试现场你必须自己组织，这是两种不同能力。
why_en: Reading a solution can create a false sense of mastery because the author already organized the structure and tradeoffs for you.
optionMeanings: 假设阅读自动训练口头表达。
假设阅读自动覆盖所有取舍场景。
假设阅读能替代需求澄清练习。
把“读懂”错当成“能独立复现”。
optionScenarioImpacts: 表达能力要靠开口讲才能训练，阅读练不到。
换个约束，取舍就会不同，阅读记不住所有变体。
澄清需求是主动提问的技能，读答案不涉及。
面试现场要自己搭结构，读的时候没练过这步。
optionDirectness: 适合已经反复口述的人；单次阅读不会自动给你表达力。
适合固定场景复盘；换约束后仍要重新判断取舍。
适合题面已完全明确；真实面试仍要主动澄清。
适合描述被动阅读风险；它解释了为什么要先自己画。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes reading automatically trains verbal explanation.
Assumes reading automatically covers every tradeoff scenario.
Assumes reading replaces the skill of clarifying requirements.
Mistakes 'I understood it' for 'I can reproduce it myself.'
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Speaking skill only grows by speaking out loud, not by reading.
Change the constraint and the tradeoff changes; reading can't cover every variant.
Clarifying requirements is an active questioning skill reading doesn't touch.
In the real interview you must build the structure yourself, a step reading skips.
optionDirectness_en: Fits someone who already rehearsed aloud; reading once does not build speech.
Fits fixed-scenario review; tradeoffs still change when constraints change.
Fits fully specified prompts; real interviews still require clarification.
Fits the passive-reading risk and explains why drawing first matters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 官方参考题解，用来对照自己的设计差距。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An answer key is the reference solution used to compare against your own design.

scenario: 你练题时经常一会儿讲数据库、一会儿讲缓存、一会儿又回到需求，最后时间不够。
scenario_en: When practicing, you keep jumping from database to cache back to requirements, and you run out of time.
q: 应该如何修正这个跳题问题？
q_en: How should you fix this topic-jumping problem?
options: 继续想到哪讲到哪，不用框架
只画最终架构图，跳过前面阶段
固定用 delivery framework，按阶段控制范围
跳过 requirements，直接讲架构
options_en: Keep improvising, jumping topics without a framework.
Only draw the final architecture diagram, skip earlier stages.
Commit to a delivery framework and control scope stage by stage.
Skip requirements and jump straight into architecture.
why: 框架的价值就是让你线性推进、防止 scope creep；系统设计是逐步收敛问题，不是脑暴组件。
why_en: A delivery framework keeps your answer linear and prevents scope creep during a fast-paced interview.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经能自然组织答案，框架可以隐藏在表达里；但练习阶段仍应显式使用它。
tradeoff: 固定阶段推进 vs 想到哪讲到哪
optionMeanings: 让讨论顺序完全跟着联想走。
把设计压缩成只剩最终结果。
用固定阶段顺序逼自己不跑题。
跳过需求，直接从组件开始想。
optionScenarioImpacts: 正是这种跳跃导致时间不够用完。
没有前面阶段支撑，架构图也讲不清为什么这么画。
每个阶段有时间边界，跳来跳去的问题被结构消除。
没有需求锚点，很容易设计出偏题的系统。
optionDirectness: 适合自由脑暴早期；计时面试里会继续失控。
适合最后汇总结果；缺少前置阶段就讲不清依据。
适合防止跳题；阶段顺序会给每段讨论设边界。
适合需求已明确的复盘；正式回答不能跳过需求。
optionMeanings_en: Let the discussion order follow free association.
Compress the design down to just the final result.
Use a fixed stage order to force yourself to stay on track.
Skip requirements and start thinking from components.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: This jumping is exactly what is eating your time now.
Without earlier stages, you can't justify why the diagram looks that way.
Each stage has a time boundary, so the jumping-around problem is structurally removed.
Without a requirements anchor, it's easy to design the wrong system.
optionDirectness_en: Fits early brainstorming; a timed interview keeps drifting this way.
Fits final summarization, but the diagram needs earlier justification.
Fits the jumping problem because stages set boundaries for each part.
Fits review after requirements are known; a real answer cannot skip them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试时固定推进顺序的答题框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A delivery framework is a fixed sequence of stages for walking through a design answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试开始时明确的功能性和非功能性需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requirements are the functional and non-functional constraints you clarify at the start.

q: 先读 Core Concepts / Key Technologies / Patterns 的收益是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of reading Core Concepts, Key Technologies, and Patterns first? (Select all that apply.)
options: 知道系统设计题常见组件和模式的边界
做题时能复用已有概念，而不是每题从零发明
帮助建立学习范围
保证不用再练任何题
options_en: You learn the boundaries of common components and patterns.
You can reuse existing concepts instead of reinventing them each time.
It helps you scope what you need to study.
It guarantees you never have to practice a question.
why: 基础材料不是替代练题，而是给练题提供词汇和取舍框架；没有基础，题解容易变成死记硬背。
why_en: The foundations give you reusable vocabulary and a tradeoff framework, but they do not replace active practice.
optionMeanings: 了解常见组件/模式各自适用的边界。
把学过的概念当工具直接复用。
明确该学到多深、多广。
假设读完基础就不用再练题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 遇到新题能快速判断该用哪类组件。
省去每题重新发明轮子的时间。
避免漫无目的地乱看资料。
会让你误以为可以跳过输出训练。
optionDirectness: 用来知道组件和模式什么时候适用。
用来把已有概念带进新题，减少从零发明。
用来控制学习范围，避免无目的乱看。
只在不考输出时成立；系统设计仍要练题。
optionMeanings_en: You learn where each common component or pattern applies.
You reuse concepts you've already learned as tools.
It clarifies how deep and how broad to study.
It assumes finishing the foundations means skipping practice.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You can quickly judge which component fits a new problem.
It saves you from reinventing the wheel on every question.
It keeps you from wandering aimlessly through material.
It falsely suggests you can skip output training.
optionDirectness_en: Use this to know when components and patterns apply.
Use this to bring known concepts into new problems.
Use this to scope study instead of wandering through material.
Only works if output is not tested; system design still requires practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里可复用的基础概念。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Core Concepts are the reusable system-design ideas used across designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计常用的具体技术组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key Technologies are the concrete components used in designs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统设计里反复出现的架构套路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Patterns are recurring architecture strategies seen across many designs.

scenario: 你已经练过几道题，准备进入 mock 阶段，想让反馈更贴近目标面试。
scenario_en: You have practiced several questions and are ready for mocks, but you want feedback that matches your target interview.
q: peer mock 对象怎么选更好？
q_en: Who is the better person to choose for a peer mock?
options: 只找完全不了解 system design 的人
优先找目标公司或相近风格的工程师
只对着镜子读答案
只用随机题目生成器，不要反馈
options_en: Find someone with no system design background at all.
Prioritize an engineer from the target company or a similar interview style.
Just read the answer out loud to a mirror.
Use a random question generator with no feedback.
why: 目标公司员工更熟悉该公司的面试节奏和评价偏好；反馈越贴近目标环境，练习价值越高。
why_en: A peer from the target company is more likely to give feedback aligned with that company's interview style.
whenOtherWins: 找不到目标公司的人时，找有系统设计面试经验的工程师，重点是拿到真实追问。
tradeoff: 贴近目标公司的真实反馈 vs 容易约到的泛泛反馈
optionMeanings: 找完全没有相关背景的人陪练。
找了解目标评分标准的人给反馈。
自己对自己复述，没有外部反馈。
只刷题，主动放弃反馈环节。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方提不出有价值的技术追问。
追问方式和评分口味更接近真实面试官。
没有人能指出你漏掉的需求或取舍。
没有反馈就发现不了自己的盲点。
optionDirectness: 适合练普通表达；技术追问和评分反馈会很弱。
适合目标公司冲刺；反馈更接近真实面试口味。
适合自我朗读热身；缺少外部追问和纠偏。
适合扩充题量；不能替代有人反馈的 mock。
optionMeanings_en: Pair with someone who has no relevant background at all.
Find someone who knows the target grading style to give feedback.
Recite your own answer to yourself, with no outside feedback.
Only drill questions and deliberately skip the feedback step.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They can't ask technically meaningful follow-up questions.
Follow-up questions and grading feel closer to the real interviewer.
No one can point out the requirement or tradeoff you missed.
Without feedback, your blind spots stay hidden.
optionDirectness_en: Fits general speaking practice; technical follow-up will be weak.
Fits target-company prep because the feedback matches the real style.
Fits a warm-up read-through, but it lacks outside probing.
Fits adding question volume, not replacing a feedback-based mock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 和另一位工程师模拟真实计时面试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peer mock is a timed practice interview run with another engineer.

q: “读懂题解”和“面试中讲出设计”的最大区别是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest difference between understanding a write-up and explaining a design in an interview?
options: 讲出设计要在时间压力下自己组织结构和取舍
读懂题解更难，因为不需要表达
两者完全一样
讲出设计不需要任何技术判断
options_en: Explaining a design out loud means organizing structure and tradeoffs yourself, under time pressure.
Reading a write-up is harder because it requires no explanation.
The two are exactly the same skill.
Explaining a design requires no technical judgment at all.
why: 面试是实时沟通：要澄清需求、排序问题、画图、解释取舍并响应追问；阅读只是输入的一部分。
why_en: Speaking a design out loud requires actively organizing structure, tradeoffs, and communication under time pressure.
tradeoff: 主动组织表达 vs 被动接收阅读
optionMeanings: 把讲设计当成主动输出加沟通的任务。
颠倒了阅读和表达的难度关系。
否认输入和输出是两种技能。
错误地剥离了技术判断这一核心。
optionScenarioImpacts: 对应面试官真正在评估的能力。
表达通常比阅读更难，不是更容易。
会让人误以为看懂题解就等于会面试。
面试恰恰全程都在考技术判断。
optionDirectness: 适合描述现场面试能力；它强调自己组织和限时表达。
适合只比较阅读负担；没有覆盖面试输出难点。
适合低风险复习；真实面试和阅读不是同一任务。
适合非技术展示；系统设计仍然围绕技术判断。
optionMeanings_en: Treats explaining a design as active output plus communication.
Reverses the actual difficulty relationship between reading and speaking.
Denies that input and output are different skills.
Incorrectly strips out technical judgment as the core.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It matches what the interviewer is actually evaluating.
Speaking is usually harder than reading, not easier.
It wrongly implies understanding a write-up equals being interview-ready.
Technical judgment is exactly what's being tested throughout.
optionDirectness_en: Fits live interview skill because it stresses organizing under time.
Fits comparing reading load, not the hard part of interview output.
Fits low-risk review; real interviews and reading are different tasks.
Fits nontechnical presentation, but system design centers on judgment.

scenario: 主线 common questions 题单大约有 30 道，分布在 easy（约 4 道）、medium（约 13 道）、hard（约 13 道）三档。
scenario_en: The main common questions list has about 30 problems across easy, medium, and hard tiers: roughly 4 easy, 13 medium, and 13 hard.
q: 这个题量和难度分布，最支持哪条备考策略？
q_en: What prep strategy does this problem count and difficulty split support?
options: 跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard
题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上
只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题
在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档
options_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
why: 约 30 道题在三档间分布均衡，说明常见面试难度本身就是均衡分布的；两周内做不完全部，应按难度分层抽样，而不是只啃一档或反复刷同一批题。
why_en: With about thirty problems split evenly across easy, medium, and hard, the right move in a short window is to sample every tier, not just one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文章正文列出的主线练习题单，带书面 write-up。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common questions are the main practice list in the article, each with a written guide.

optionMeanings: 选项主张：跳过 medium，直接从 easy 冲到 hard。
选项主张：题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上。
选项主张：只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题。
选项主张：在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档。

只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
适合本题给出的约束。

会让系统依赖「题量太少，应该把每道题都刷三遍以上」这个前提。
会让系统依赖「只刷 hard，因为面试通常只考最难的题」这个前提。
会让方案围绕「在三档难度里都抽样练习，而不是只刷一档」展开。
optionMeanings_en: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
Sample practice across all three difficulty tiers instead of only one.
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
Only fits when this statement is true: the list is so small you should redo every problem three times.
Only fits when this statement is true: only drill hard problems, since interviews are usually the hardest.
This is the core issue in this scenario.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It commits the design to this assumption: Skip medium and jump straight from easy to hard.
It commits the design to this assumption: The list is so small you should redo every problem three times.

scenario: 你独立完成一题后，对比 answer key 发现自己的高层架构不同。
scenario_en: After completing a problem independently, you compare with the answer key and find that your high-level architecture is different.
q: 最有价值的复盘方式是什么？
q_en: What is the most useful way to review the difference?
options: 直接把自己写的完整答案删除重做一遍
只核对两边用的组件名称是否一致
跳过复盘环节，直接进入下一道练习题
比较背后的 requirements 和 tradeoffs
options_en: Delete your own complete answer and redo it from scratch.
Only check whether the component names on both sides match.
Skip the review step and go straight to the next practice question.
Compare the requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference.
why: 系统设计通常没有唯一图；复盘要找出作者为什么选了某个组件、你漏了哪个约束、哪些取舍没讲清。
why_en: The useful review compares requirements and tradeoffs behind the difference, not the memorization of one architecture diagram.
whenOtherWins: 如果你的方案违反了硬性需求或指标，那不是风格差异，是需要修正的设计错误。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Mine["My design"] --> Gap["Find gaps"]
    Key["Answer key"] --> Gap
    Gap --> Req["Requirements"]
    Gap --> Trade["Tradeoffs"]
    Gap --> Deep["Deep dives"]
tradeoff: 复盘约束和取舍 vs 复盘表面架构图
optionMeanings: 把不同结果当成完全失败处理。
只核对名词，不核对决策依据。
放弃从这道题里学习的机会。
把差异当成理解取舍的线索去追问。
optionScenarioImpacts: 丢掉了本可以对比学习的素材。
组件名一样，决策逻辑可能完全没学到。
同样的缺口会在下一题重复出现。
能定位自己漏掉的约束或没考虑的取舍。
optionDirectness: 适合方案明显错误时重做；这里先要理解差异来源。
适合快速核对表面组件；不能解释为什么选它们。
适合赶进度；会错过这道题给你的反馈。
适合复盘设计判断；差异会指向漏掉的约束。
optionMeanings_en: Treat a different result as total failure.
Only check naming, not the reasoning behind decisions.
Give up the chance to learn from this question.
Treat the difference as a clue to chase down the reasoning.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You throw away material you could have learned from.
Matching names doesn't mean you learned the decision logic.
The same gap will resurface on the next question.
You can pinpoint the missed constraint or unconsidered tradeoff.
optionDirectness_en: Fits clearly broken designs; here you first need the source of the gap.
Fits surface-level component checks, not why those components were chosen.
Fits moving fast, but it throws away the feedback from this question.
Fits reviewing design judgment because differences point to missed constraints.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tradeoffs are the balances you strike when a choice benefits one thing at the cost of another.

q: 补全准备路线的三个基础动作：

text: 理解{{system design interview}}是什么，选择{{Delivery Framework}}，再学习{{Core Concepts}}、{{Key Technologies}}和{{Common Patterns}}。

用 Guided Practice 或白板自己讲一遍
只写代码，跳过架构图

q: 系统设计面试本质上在考察什么能力？
q_en: What ability does a system design interview mainly test?
options: 把模糊的高层问题拆解成解决它所需的基础设施组件
背诵标准架构模板
在白板上手写可运行代码
记住尽可能多的数据库产品名
options_en: Breaking an ambiguous, high-level problem down into the infrastructure pieces needed to solve it.
Reciting a memorized standard architecture template.
Handwriting runnable code on the whiteboard.
Memorizing as many database product names as possible.
why: 题目故意留白、规格不全，考的是你能否拆出服务、数据库、负载均衡等构件并推进出解；比算法题更贴近真实工程判断。
why_en: A system design interview mainly tests whether you can turn an ambiguous problem into the infrastructure pieces needed to solve it.

    Parts --> System["Working system"]

死记硬背通用架构套路
现场手写能跑的代码
背下数据库产品清单
optionScenarioImpacts: 展现工程判断力，考官最想看到的
显得在套模板，经不起追问
偏离设计重点，浪费白板时间
与设计能力无关，答不到点子上

q: 关于「标准答案」，系统设计面试的正确认知是？
q_en: What is the right mindset about standard answers in system design interviews?
options: 每道题都有唯一标准答案，必须精确命中
回答内容不重要，只要讲话时间够长
很多题有多个可行答案，考官看重权衡与表达
只要猜中面试官心中的方案就能过关
options_en: Every question has one exact standard answer you must hit.
Content doesn't matter as long as you talk for a long time.
Many questions have multiple workable answers; interviewers value trade-offs and clarity.
You just need to guess the architecture the interviewer has in mind.
why: 设计面试没有唯一正解；考官评估你在复杂问题里怎么权衡取舍、怎么把思路讲清楚。
why_en: Design interviews are not about one right answer — interviewers assess how you weigh trade-offs and communicate your thinking.
optionMeanings: 假设存在唯一标准答案
假设内容不重要只拼时长
承认多解、看重权衡表达
假设能猜中考官心思
optionScenarioImpacts: 一遇变体或追问就无从下手
显得没有思考，只是在拖时间
让你专注在推理和讲清楚上

optionDirectness: 只有硬性规范题才可能有唯一答案
长时间表达只有在推理清楚时才加分

猜方案不可控，只有澄清约束后才有意义
optionMeanings_en: Assumes there is exactly one standard answer.
Assumes content doesn't matter, only talk time.
Acknowledges multiple answers and values reasoning.
Assumes you can guess the interviewer's mindset.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Leaves you stuck the moment the question varies.
Reads as stalling rather than thinking.
Keeps you focused on reasoning and clear delivery.
Turns prep into an unreliable guessing game.
optionDirectness_en: Only hard-spec questions tend to have one exact answer.
Long answers help only when the reasoning is clear.
For multi-solution prompts, trade-offs and clarity prove the choice.
Guessing is unreliable unless it is grounded in clarified constraints.

q: 与 LeetCode 式算法面试相比，系统设计面试的定位差异是？
q_en: How is a system design interview positioned differently from a LeetCode-style algorithm interview?
options: 更学术、更理论
更看重语法细节
更实践、更接近日常真实工作
在评估中的权重更低
options_en: More academic and theoretical.
More focused on exact syntax details.
More practical and closer to everyday engineering work.
Weighted less heavily in the overall evaluation.
why: 系统设计是实践型面试，多数工程师觉得它比刷题更贴近真实工作，考的是工程判断而非算法技巧。
why_en: System design interviews are practical and feel closer to real engineering work than LeetCode-style algorithm interviews.
tradeoff: 贴近真实工程判断 vs 贴近算法解题技巧
whenOtherWins: 若面试明确是刷题轮（考算法复杂度和边界条件），考察重点确实换成解题技巧而非架构判断。

q: 无论什么级别，候选人在系统设计面试中共同的底线要求是？
q_en: What baseline expectation applies to every level in a system design interview?
options: 至少说出三种消息队列
写出核心模块伪代码
把所有组件讲到源码级深度
完成一个满足需求的完整设计
options_en: Name at least three message queue products.
Write pseudocode for the core modules.
Explain every component down to source-code depth.
Deliver a complete design that satisfies the requirements.
why: 所有级别都要交付一个满足需求、能工作的完整设计；级别差异体现在深度，不是「能不能做完」。
why_en: Every level is expected to deliver a complete, working design that satisfies the requirements, with depth as the only differentiator.
optionMeanings: 考察消息队列产品知识
考察伪代码书写
考察源码级讲解深度
考察能否交付完整设计
optionScenarioImpacts: 与是否达标无关
只在少数题目里用得上
时间根本不够撑到这个深度
是所有级别共同的通过线
optionDirectness: 不是共同要求
不是共同要求
不是共同要求，深度按级别变化
任何级别都要先交付能工作的完整设计
optionMeanings_en: Tests knowledge of message queue products.
Tests writing pseudocode.
Tests source-code-level explanation depth.
Tests whether you can deliver a complete design.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Unrelated to whether you pass the bar.
Only useful for a handful of questions.
There's rarely enough time for this much depth.
This is the shared bar across every level.
optionDirectness_en: Not a universal requirement.
Not a universal requirement.
Not universal; depth expectations vary by level.
Every level must first deliver a complete working design.

q: 同一道题，中级与高级工程师的达标表现差异主要在？
q_en: For the same prompt, what mainly separates a mid-level answer from a senior-level answer?
options: 中级不必收集需求，高级才需要
高级必须堆更多组件数量
中级基础覆盖广，高级快过基础换深挖时间
高级可以跳过高层设计直接细化
options_en: Mid-level doesn't need to gather requirements, only senior does.
Senior engineers must stack in more components.
Mid-level covers the basics broadly; senior moves fast through basics to buy deep-dive time.
Senior engineers can skip high-level design and go straight to detail.
why: 中级把基础做扎实即可；高级要迅速过完基础，把省下的时间投入 deep dive 来展示深度。
why_en: A mid-level engineer nails the fundamentals broadly, while a senior engineer moves through them quickly to leave time for deep dives.
tradeoff: 基础覆盖的广度 vs 深挖展示的深度

termDefinitions.meaning: 深挖：面试中针对某个组件展开的深度追问环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the part of the interview where you go into depth on one specific component.

optionMeanings: 假设中级可以跳过需求收集
假设组件数量代表水平
时间分配策略随级别调整
假设高级可以跳过高层设计
optionScenarioImpacts: 与实际备考建议矛盾
会让设计变得臃肿而非精准
解释了同题不同分的机制
会丢掉展示导航能力的机会
optionDirectness: 需求收集是所有级别的起点
组件数量只有在解决约束时才有意义
级别差异常体现在基础与深挖的时间分配
高层设计仍是进入细节前的共同骨架
optionMeanings_en: Assumes mid-level can skip requirements gathering.
Assumes component count signals seniority.
Time allocation shifts by level.
Assumes senior can skip high-level design.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Contradicts standard interview advice.
Makes the design bloated instead of precise.
Explains why the same question scores differently.
Loses the chance to show navigation ability.
optionDirectness_en: Requirements gathering is the starting point at every level.
Component count matters only when it solves constraints.
Level differences often show up in how time shifts from basics to deep dives.
High-level design is still the shared skeleton before details.

q: 关于 staff+ 级别的系统设计面试，正确的是？
q_en: What is true about staff-plus system design interviews?
options: staff 级打法不同，需按级别调整
与低级别完全一样
staff 级不考系统设计
staff 级只考编码

why_en: Staff-level system design interviews differ substantially from lower levels, so you need to adjust your approach accordingly.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff-plus refers to staff-level and above engineers, who are expected to influence technical direction across teams.

假设 staff 不考设计
假设 staff 只考代码
optionScenarioImpacts: 引导去看 staff 专门指导
会照搬中级/高级的套路失分
会完全不准备这轮，直接翻车
会忽略架构判断力的考察
optionDirectness: staff+ 面试要展示跨团队和更高杠杆的判断
低级别打法只适合较小范围的设计题
staff+ 岗位通常更需要系统设计信号
编码只覆盖实现能力，不能替代架构判断
optionMeanings_en: Acknowledges staff level has its own playbook.
Assumes every level plays the same.
Assumes staff skips system design.
Assumes staff only tests coding.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Points you to staff-specific guidance.
Leads you to reuse mid/senior tactics and lose points.
Leaves you completely unprepared for this round.
Ignores the architectural judgment being tested.
optionDirectness_en: Staff-plus interviews expect broader leverage and cross-team judgment.
Lower-level tactics fit smaller-scope design prompts.
Staff-plus roles usually need an even stronger design signal.
Coding covers implementation skill, not architectural judgment.

q: 补全所有公司评分标准共有的四大主题：
q_en: Fill in the four themes shared by company system design rubrics:
text: 四大评估主题：{{Problem Navigation}} 问题导航、{{Solution Design}} 方案设计、{{Technical Excellence}} 技术卓越、{{Communication}} 沟通与协作。
why: 各公司 rubric 措辞不同，但都绕不开这四件事；准备时可对照这四项逐一自查。
why_en: Every company's rubric touches the same four themes: problem navigation, solution design, technical excellence, and communication and collaboration.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Rubric["Rubric"] --> Nav["Navigation"]
    Rubric --> Sol["Solution"]
    Rubric --> Tech["Technical"]
    Rubric --> Comm["Communication"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 问题导航：把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive it toward a solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方案设计：用核心概念解决拆出的子问题，并拼成协调的整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Solution Design means solving each subproblem with core concepts and assembling them into a coherent whole.

termDefinitions.meaning: 技术卓越：了解现行技术与公认模式，并能应用到问题上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Technical Excellence is knowing current technologies and recognized patterns and applying them to the problem at hand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沟通与协作：能讲清概念、接住反馈、并与面试官协作解题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Communication and Collaboration means explaining ideas clearly, receiving feedback, and working with the interviewer to solve the problem.

q: 「问题导航（Problem Navigation）」考察的核心是？
q_en: What is the core skill tested by Problem Navigation?
options: 尽快先画出最终架构图
拆小问题、排优先级、推进到解
多问问题来拖延时间
证明题目出得有问题
options_en: Rush to draw the final architecture diagram.
Decompose the problem, prioritize, and drive toward a solution.
Ask lots of questions just to stall for time.
Argue that the question itself is flawed.
why: 面试官想看你能否拆解、排序、推进一个规格不全的问题；这常是整场最重要、最拉开差距的一环。
why_en: Problem navigation means decomposing an under-specified problem, prioritizing it, and driving it toward a solution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 问题导航：把模糊问题拆解、排优先级并推进到解的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Problem Navigation is the ability to decompose an ambiguous problem, prioritize it, and drive toward a solution.

optionMeanings: 跳过思考直接出图
拆解、排序、推进三步走
只提问不推进
质疑题目而不作答

正是考官想看的导航能力
显得缺乏决策力
浪费宝贵的面试时间

提问只有服务于决策时才算导航
题目有瑕疵时也要澄清约束并继续推进
optionMeanings_en: Skips thinking and jumps to the diagram.
Decompose, prioritize, then drive forward.
Only asks questions without progressing.
Disputes the question instead of answering.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Reads as though you skipped the thinking step.
Exactly what the interviewer wants to see.
Reads as indecisive.
Wastes valuable interview time.
optionDirectness_en: The diagram belongs after requirements and priorities are clear.
For ambiguous prompts, decompose, prioritize, then move the design forward.
Questions count as navigation only when they drive decisions.
Even with imperfect prompts, clarify constraints and keep progressing.

q: 问题导航维度的常见失败方式有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which are common failure modes in the Problem Navigation dimension?
options: 对问题探索不足、需求收集不充分
把时间花在琐碎无趣的部分而不是最重要的部分
卡死在某一块上无法向前推进
使用了过时的技术选型
options_en: Under-exploring the problem and gathering requirements.
Spending time on trivial parts instead of the important ones.
Getting stuck on one piece and unable to move forward.
Choosing outdated technology.
why: 第四种被点名的失败是没能交付一个能工作的系统；用过时技术属于技术卓越维度，不算导航失败。
why_en: Common navigation failures are under-exploring requirements, focusing on trivial parts, and getting stuck; outdated tech choices belong to a different competency.
optionMeanings: 前期探索不够，理解不完整
时间投在无关紧要处
卡在一处交不出完整系统
技术选型陈旧
optionScenarioImpacts: 后续设计建在不完整理解上
挤占了关键部分的时间

optionDirectness: 需求不完整时，后续设计会建在错误前提上

技术过时属于技术卓越问题，不属于导航本身
optionMeanings_en: Not exploring the problem deeply enough upfront.
Spending time on parts that don't matter.
Getting stuck in one place and stalling the whole design.
Choosing outdated technology.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Later design rests on an incomplete understanding.
Crowds out time for the parts that matter.
Without a fallback, the whole interview stalls.

optionDirectness_en: Incomplete requirements make later design rest on bad assumptions.
Bad prioritization lets trivia crowd out the critical path.
Without a fallback path, one stuck area can stall the whole interview.
Outdated technology belongs to technical excellence, not navigation itself.

q: 许多候选人在面试中无法推进，最常见的根因是？

No structured method — no track to run on.
The interviewer is deliberately being harsh.

用核心概念逐块求解并拼成整体

q: 补全问题导航的正确姿势：
q_en: Fill in the correct Problem Navigation posture:
text: 把复杂问题{{拆解}}成更小、可管理的部分，按{{重要性}}排出优先级，并最终交付一个{{能工作}}的系统。

q_en: Fill in the key points about relational database indexes:
text: 索引通常用 {{B-Tree}} 或{{哈希表}}实现；关系库的优势是支持任意多个索引，还支持{{多列}}索引与专用索引（地理空间、全文）。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash table maps keys to storage locations for near constant-time equality lookups.

q: 补全 NoSQL 的扩展机制：
q_en: Fill in the NoSQL scaling mechanisms:
text: NoSQL 数据库靠{{一致性哈希}}和/或{{分片}}把数据分布到多台服务器上，实现水平扩展。
why: 水平扩展是 NoSQL 的核心卖点之一：一致性哈希让节点增减时数据迁移量最小，分片把数据切分到多台机器。
why_en: NoSQL databases scale horizontally by distributing data across servers with consistent hashing and sharding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种哈希方案，节点增减时只需迁移少量数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing is a hashing scheme that minimizes data movement when nodes are added or removed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多台服务器，靠分片键决定归属。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple servers based on a shard key.

scenario: 你在设计一个写入量很大的事件/日志型系统：数据主要追加写入，偶尔按 key 或时间范围读取，不需要复杂 join，也可以接受按业务选择一致性等级。
scenario_en: You are designing a write-heavy event or log system: data is mostly appended, reads are occasional by key or time range, complex joins are unnecessary, and consistency can be chosen by business need.
q: 在这个写多读少的 NoSQL 场景里，为什么 Cassandra 比 MongoDB、Redis、Neo4j 更直接？

why: Cassandra 的强项是把大量写入水平分散到多节点，用追加写/LSM 风格存储承接高吞吐。MongoDB 偏文档灵活，Redis 偏低延迟内存态，Neo4j 偏图遍历，都不是这个写密集场景的第一反应。
why_en: Cassandra is the most direct fit because the workload is write-heavy, append-oriented, and partitionable, while MongoDB, Redis, and Neo4j optimize for different primary access patterns.
whenOtherWins: 灵活文档选 MongoDB；低延迟内存态选 Redis；图遍历选 Neo4j。

Neo4j：图数据库，围绕节点、边和路径查询优化。

q: 大文件本体和可查询元数据应该怎样拆分存储？
q_en: How should you split large file bodies from searchable metadata?
options: 视频和元数据都放 Postgres
视频和元数据都放 S3
视频放 Blob 存储，元数据放数据库存指针
视频放 Redis，元数据放 S3
why: 要学的不是"S3 这个名字"，而是职责拆分：对象存储负责便宜可靠地保存大二进制；数据库负责索引、过滤、权限和低延迟点查，库里只存指针。
why_en: The design principle is to split responsibilities: blob storage holds large binary objects cheaply and durably, while the database stores searchable metadata and pointers.
whenOtherWins: 数据是小而结构化的记录时直接进数据库即可，没必要引入 Blob 存储这一层。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    File["Large file"] --> Blob["S3 / Blob store"]
    Meta["Metadata"] --> DB["Database"]
    DB --> Ptr["URL pointer"]
    Ptr --> Blob
optionMeanings: 单库方案：把结构化元数据和大二进制文件混在关系库里。
对象存储全包：让 S3 同时承担文件存储和业务查询主库。
职责拆分：Blob/object storage 存文件，数据库存可查询元数据和 object key。
角色反了：把 Redis 当大文件库，把 S3 当元数据库。
optionScenarioImpacts: 查询库会被大文件拖慢，备份和复制成本也会变得很高。
文件保存没问题，但按作者、权限、状态、时间查视频会变得很难。
播放/下载走对象存储或 CDN，列表页/详情页先查数据库拿元数据和文件指针。
热缓存和持久文件存储的边界混乱，系统会又贵又难查。
optionMeanings_en: A single database design mixes structured metadata and large binary objects in Postgres.
An object-store-only design asks S3 to be both file store and business database.
A responsibility split stores blobs in object storage and metadata plus object keys in a database.
This reverses roles by treating Redis as large-file storage and S3 as a metadata database.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The query database becomes bloated and backups and replication get expensive.
File storage works, but querying by author, permission, status, or time becomes awkward.
Playback can use object storage or CDN while metadata queries stay fast in the database.
The system confuses caching, durable storage, and query responsibilities.

q: 为什么 S3 这类 Blob 存储不适合作为业务主数据库？
q_en: Why is S3-style blob storage a poor fit as the primary business database?
options: S3 的存储成本太高
Blob 存储不擅长低延迟查询和索引
S3 不支持超过 1GB 的文件
Blob 存储没有持久性保证
why: S3 的优势是持久、便宜、适合大对象，不是低延迟复杂查询。业务主库要维护索引、权限、状态、分页和一致的元数据更新；对象存储通常只保存大文件本体，数据库保存 object key 和可查询字段。
why_en: Blob storage is excellent for durable large objects, but the business database still needs to handle indexes, permissions, state, pagination, and metadata updates.
scenario: 你已经把图片/视频文件放进 S3，但产品还需要“按用户列出文件、按状态筛选、按时间排序、校验权限、分页返回”。有人提议直接把 S3 当主数据库用。

把对象存储和业务数据库的职责分开。
误以为 S3 存不了大文件。
误以为 S3 不可靠、没有持久性保证。

讨论持久性适合数据丢失风险题；这里 S3 的耐久性不是短板。

q: 把「客户端经预签名 URL 上传大文件」的流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the presigned-URL large-file upload flow in the correct order:
steps: 客户端把文件直接上传到预签名 URL
客户端向服务器请求一个上传用的预签名 URL
Blob 存储回调通知服务器上传完成，服务器把状态更新为已完成
服务器返回预签名 URL 给客户端，并在数据库记下这条记录
why: 标准四步：请求预签名 URL → 服务器发 URL 并落库 → 客户端绕过服务器直传 Blob 存储 → 存储回调通知、更新状态。文件本体不过应用服务器，省带宽。
why_en: The client requests a presigned URL, the server returns it and records it, the client uploads directly to blob storage, and a completion notification updates the status.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant S as 服务器
    participant B as Blob存储(S3)
    C->>S: 1. 请求预签名 URL
    S->>S: 2. 落库并返回 URL
    C->>B: 3. 直接上传文件
    B->>S: 4. 上传完成通知
    S->>S: 5. 更新状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器签发的临时授权链接，客户端可直接用它上传/下载大文件，不经过应用服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a temporary signed link that lets a client upload or download directly without routing through the app server.

q: 预签名 URL 架构下，客户端下载大文件的标准路径是？
q_en: With a presigned-URL architecture, what is the standard path for downloading a large file?
options: 向服务器要预签名 URL，经 CDN 下载
服务器把文件读进内存再转发给客户端
客户端直连数据库读取文件二进制
必须先把文件复制回应用服务器磁盘
why: 下载时客户端向服务器请求文件，拿到预签名 URL，然后经 CDN 下载；CDN 未命中时代理请求到底层 Blob 存储。文件流量同样不经过应用服务器。
why_en: The client asks the server for a presigned URL and downloads through the CDN, which proxies to the underlying blob storage.
options_en: Ask the server for a presigned URL, then download via the CDN
The server reads the file into memory and forwards it to the client
The client connects directly to the database to read the file bytes
The file must first be copied back onto the application server disk

q: Blob 存储靠什么做到极高的持久性？

靠复制和纠删码防数据丢失
把数据全部放内存
只写一份但用更贵的磁盘

q: 为什么 `LIKE "%term%"` 不是可扩展的全文搜索方案？
q_en: Why is `LIKE "%term%"` not a scalable full-text search approach?

q: 补全搜索优化数据库的三项关键技术：
q_en: Fill in the three key techniques behind search-optimized databases:
text: {{分词}}（tokenization）把文本切成一个个单词；{{词干化}}（stemming）把 running/runs 归一成 run；模糊搜索靠{{编辑距离}}容忍拼写错误和变体。
why: 分词让词能映射进倒排索引；词干化让同一词的不同形态互相匹配；模糊搜索用编辑距离（增删改多少字母）容忍拼错，多数搜索库开箱支持。
why_en: Tokenization splits text into words, stemming reduces words to their root form, and fuzzy search tolerates misspellings using edit distance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个词变成另一个词所需的最少增删改次数，用于模糊搜索容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance counts the minimum insertions, deletions, or substitutions to turn one word into another, used for fuzzy matching.

q: 队列如何扩展以承接更大消息量？相关消息如何保序？
q_en: How do queues scale for higher message volume, and how do related messages keep order?
options: 分区到多台服务器，用分区键保证同类消息同分区
只能垂直升级单机
把消息随机复制到多个队列
靠消费者轮询所有分区来保序
why: 和数据库一样，队列靠分区扩展：每个分区独立消费。指定分区键能让相关消息（如同一用户的消息）进同一分区，保持相对顺序。
why_en: Queues scale by partitioning across servers, and a partition key keeps related messages in the same partition.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Key["Partition key"] --> P1["Partition A"]
    Key --> P2["Partition B"]
    P1 --> W1["Worker group A"]
    P2 --> W2["Worker group B"]
options_en: Partition across servers; a partition key groups related messages
You can only scale vertically on one machine
Randomly replicate messages across multiple queues
Consumers poll every partition to keep order

q: 系统处理能力 200/s，持续进来 300/s——队列越积越多。正确的应对是？
q_en: The system handles 200/s but receives a steady 300/s, so the queue keeps growing. What is the right response?
options: 把队列容量调大十倍
再加一个队列串联
背压：队列满时放慢或拒绝新消息
把消息静默丢弃
why: 队列最大的坑：它掩盖了「容量不够」的事实，永远处理不完。答案是背压——队列过载时放慢生产速度或拒绝新消息，把压力传导回上游。
why_en: When demand permanently exceeds capacity, apply backpressure by slowing or rejecting new messages instead of letting the queue grow forever.
options_en: Scale the queue's capacity up tenfold
Chain on another queue
Backpressure: slow or reject new messages when the queue is full
Silently drop messages

q: 把「引入消息队列」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the “introduce a message queue” decision chain in the correct order:
steps: 缓解：加背压——队列过载时放慢或拒绝新消息
需求：流量突发，瞬时请求量远超工作者处理能力，但请求不能丢
代价：链路变异步、延迟上升；容量不足会被队列掩盖、消息越积越多
选型：加消息队列做缓冲，工作者按自己的节奏消费
why: 完整决策链：突发流量不能丢（需求）→ 队列缓冲（选型）→ 异步延迟与容量掩盖（代价）→ 背压兜底（缓解）。面试要能一口气讲完这四步。
why_en: Bursty traffic that must not be dropped leads to a buffering queue, which costs latency and can hide missing capacity, mitigated by backpressure.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Burst["Bursty input"] --> Queue["Queue"]
    Queue --> Cost["More latency"]
    Cost --> Back["Need backpressure"]
tradeoff: 加队列换来不丢请求 vs 付出异步延迟和「掩盖容量不足」的代价

队列比流更快
流不支持分区

tradeoff: 流：保留数据、可重放 vs 队列：消费即消失

Queues are simply faster than streams
Streams don't support partitioning
Queues can replay history, streams cannot

q: 补全事件溯源的定义与卖点：
q_en: Fill in the definition and value of event sourcing:
text: 事件溯源：把应用状态的变化存成一串{{事件}}；把它们{{重放}}即可重建任意时刻的状态，天然适合需要{{审计}}留痕或撤销/重演交易的系统。
why: 事件溯源不存「当前值」而存「每次变化」：重放事件序列可还原任意时点状态，审计、回滚、重演都由此而来。流（配合保留期）是它的天然载体。
why_en: Event sourcing stores state changes as a sequence of events that can be replayed to reconstruct state at any point, ideal for audit trails.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Change["State change"] --> Event["Event"]
    Event --> Log["Append-only event log"]
    Log --> Replay["Replay events"]
    Replay --> State["Reconstructed state at time T"]

scenario: 用 Redis 给 ticket-123 上分布式锁：只有锁不存在时才能拿到（原子），且 10 分钟后自动过期，防止进程崩溃后锁卡死。

q: 哪条命令正确？

options: SET ticket-123 locked
SET ticket-123 locked NX EX 600
GET ticket-123
DEL ticket-123
why: NX 表示「不存在才设置」，利用 Redis 的原子性保证同一时刻只有一个进程拿到锁；EX 600 让锁 600 秒后自动过期，进程崩了锁也不会永久卡死。
why_en: SET with NX acquires the lock atomically only if it is free, and EX six hundred makes it expire so a crashed process cannot hold it forever.
codeSample:
# 原子地「不存在才设置」+ 600 秒自动过期
SET ticket-123 locked NX EX 600
# 完成后释放锁
DEL ticket-123
whenOtherWins: 需要跨多个 Redis 实例的更强安全保证时用 Redlock；重协调场景也可选 ZooKeeper。
tradeoff: 带 NX EX 的原子抢锁+自动过期 vs 普通 SET（无原子性、无过期保险丝）

q: 分布式锁若不设过期时间，进程持锁期间崩溃会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if a distributed lock has no expiration and the holder crashes?
options: 锁永远占用、资源卡死，所以要设锁过期

why: 锁过期是分布式锁的保险丝：持锁进程崩溃或被杀后，锁到期自动释放，别的进程还能拿到。不设过期就可能永久卡死。
why_en: Lock expiry ensures a crashed process cannot leave the lock stuck forever, since it auto-releases after a set time.
options_en: The lock stays held forever, which is why you set an expiry
The lock automatically transfers to the next process
Redis restarts the crashed process
No impact — the lock releases immediately when the connection drops

q: 进程 1 拿到锁 A 后想拿锁 B，进程 2 拿到锁 B 后想拿锁 A——发生了什么？如何预防？
q_en: Process 1 holds lock A and waits for B, while process 2 holds B and waits for A. What happened, and how do you prevent it?
options: 活锁；加随机延迟即可
锁过期；调大 TTL 即可
死锁：双方互等对方释放，锁逻辑要集中管理
脑裂；增加节点解决
why: 两个进程各持一把锁并等待对方，就是死锁。常见错误是把锁散布在四处的代码和基础设施中，导致依赖关系难以看清——集中管理锁逻辑才好预防。
why_en: Two processes each holding one lock while waiting for the other is a deadlock, and scattering lock acquisition across far-flung code makes it hard to prevent.
options_en: A livelock; adding random delay is enough
Lock expiry; just increase the TTL
A deadlock: both sides wait on each other; keep lock logic centralized to prevent it
Split-brain; add more nodes to fix it

q: 补全三种缓存写策略：
q_en: Fill in the three cache write strategies:
text: {{Write-Through}}：同时写缓存和底层存储，一致但写更慢；{{Write-Around}}：绕过缓存直接写存储，减少缓存污染但后续读可能变慢；{{Write-Back}}：先写缓存、异步落库，写快但缓存故障可能丢数据。
why: 三种写策略是「一致性、读性能、写性能」间的取舍：Write-Through 求一致、Write-Around 防污染、Write-Back 求写速但担丢失风险。
why_en: Write-through favors consistency, write-around avoids cache pollution, and write-back is fastest for writes but risks data loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入直接落底层存储、绕过缓存，减少缓存污染。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-around writes directly to the store and bypasses the cache to avoid cache pollution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存、异步落底层存储，写入快但缓存故障可能丢数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-back writes to the cache first and flushes to the store asynchronously, which is fast but risks data loss if the cache fails.

scenario: 用户提交视频转码、报表生成、批量操作等耗时远超几秒的任务，不能让请求同步等待。
q: "管理长任务"模式的核心做法是？
options: 把 HTTP 超时调成 10 分钟
立即确认+后台处理：入队后秒级返回 job ID
让客户端保持连接直到任务完成
把任务全部放进数据库触发器里跑
options_en: Just extend the HTTP timeout to ten minutes.
Split it into immediate acknowledgment plus background processing: enqueue after validation and return a job ID in milliseconds while workers execute it.
Keep the client connection open until the task finishes.
Run the entire task inside a database trigger.
why: 长任务模式 = 即时确认 + 后台处理：Web 服务器校验请求、把作业推进队列，毫秒级返回 job ID；独立的 worker 池从队列拉活执行。
why_en: Split long operations into immediate acknowledgment and background processing: enqueue a job, return a job ID in milliseconds, and let workers execute it.
whenOtherWins: 作业本来就短时别急着塞队列：同步返回结果架构更简单、背压更清晰、用户体验更好。
tradeoff: 响应快、可独立扩缩 vs 多一层队列和状态跟踪的运维复杂度
codeSample:
LPUSH jobs:transcode '{"jobId":"abc123","videoUrl":"s3://in/1.mp4"}'
# Web 服务器校验完立刻入队，毫秒级把 jobId 返回给用户

BRPOP jobs:transcode 0
# worker 阻塞式拉取到作业后异步执行真正的转码
optionMeanings: 用更长超时硬扛同步等待
拆成入队确认与后台执行两段
让请求线程一直占用到完成
把业务逻辑塞进数据库触发器

响应快、worker 和 Web 层能独立扩缩
并发一高连接池就被占满
触发器难调试、无法独立扩容
optionDirectness: 短暂超时问题可临时调大，但不能承载分钟级任务
适合耗时远超请求周期、需要后台执行的作业
长连接只适合等待时间短且并发低的场景
触发器适合短小数据约束，不适合耗时业务作业
optionMeanings_en: Brute-forces synchronous waiting with a longer timeout.
Splits the flow into enqueue-and-acknowledge plus background execution.

Fast responses, with web tier and workers scaling independently.

Keeping the connection open fits only short waits with low concurrency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 作业提交后系统返回的唯一标识，用于后续查询任务状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A job ID is the unique identifier returned after submission, used to check the task's status later.

q_en: What is the core move in the long-running-task pattern?
scenario_en: Users submit work such as video transcoding, report generation, or bulk operations. Each job takes far longer than a few seconds, so the request must not wait synchronously.

q: 把长任务处理的流程排成正确顺序：
steps: worker 持续从队列拉取作业并执行真正的工作
用户提交一个耗时任务
毫秒级返回 job ID 给用户
Web 服务器立即校验请求，把作业推入队列（Redis / Kafka）
why: 提交 → 校验并入队 → 立刻返回 job ID → worker 异步执行。好处：用户响应快、Web 与 worker 独立扩缩、故障隔离。
why_en: The user submits a task, the server validates and enqueues it, returns a job ID instantly, and workers pull and execute it in the background.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["用户提交任务"] --> W["Web服务器：校验"]
    W --> Q["队列 (Redis/Kafka)"]
    W --> R["毫秒级返回 job ID"]
    Q --> K["worker池拉取执行"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，这里可当轻量消息队列用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store, used here as a lightweight message queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/流处理平台，适合高吞吐的作业分发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming and message-queue platform suited to high-throughput job distribution.

q_en: Put the long-running-task flow in the correct order.

零延迟、零成本、零运维
不再需要重试机制
所有任务都能强一致
options_en: Fast user responses, independent scaling of web servers and workers, and fault isolation.
Zero latency, zero cost, and zero operations.
You no longer need a retry mechanism.
Every task becomes strongly consistent.
why: 把重活挪到队列后面：请求毫秒级返回；Web 层和 worker 池按各自负载扩缩；worker 挂了不影响接请求，三者互相隔离。
why_en: Queue-plus-workers gives fast user responses, independent scaling of web servers and workers, and fault isolation.
optionMeanings: 三项具体架构收益
夸大成没有任何代价
误以为异步就不用重试
误以为队列自带强一致
optionScenarioImpacts: 准确描述了这套架构真实带来的收益
误导设计者忽视队列本身的运维成本
会漏掉处理消息重复/丢失的机制
分布式场景下这个假设通常不成立
optionDirectness: 适合真正长任务：把响应、执行、故障边界拆开
零成本说法不适用于任何真实队列系统
异步作业更需要重试和幂等来兜底
强一致需要事务/协调机制，队列本身不提供
optionMeanings_en: Three concrete architectural benefits.
Overstates it as having zero cost at all.
Wrongly assumes async removes the need for retries.
Wrongly assumes a queue grants strong consistency.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Accurately describes what this architecture actually delivers.
Misleads designers into ignoring real operational cost.
Misses the need to handle duplicate or lost messages.
This assumption usually fails in distributed settings.
optionDirectness_en: Fits true long-running work by separating response, execution, and failure boundaries.
Zero-cost claims do not apply to real queue systems.

Strong consistency requires transactions or coordination, not just a queue.
q_en: What three benefits does a queue-plus-worker architecture provide for long-running tasks?

options: 队列的软件许可成本太高

队列天生不支持重试
worker 进程无法水平扩展
options_en: Message queue software licensing is too expensive.
If the job is already short, returning the result synchronously keeps the architecture simpler with clearer backpressure and better user experience.
Queues inherently do not support retries.
Worker processes cannot scale horizontally.
why: 异步化不是免费的：短作业同步返回状态，架构大幅简化、背压天然清晰、用户立刻拿到结果。只有真正的长任务才值得队列+worker的复杂度。
why_en: For short-running jobs, returning the result synchronously keeps the architecture dramatically simpler with clearer backpressure and better user experience.

重试通常是队列系统的基础能力

Attributes the problem to the cost of premature complexity.

Wrongly claims workers cannot scale.

optionDirectness_en: Licensing cost only dominates for specific commercial products.
Fits short jobs because synchronous responses keep backpressure clearer.
Retries are usually a basic queue capability.
Worker pools are designed to scale background execution horizontally.

scenario: 多个用户同时抢最后一张演唱会门票，或同时对同一拍卖品出价——同一资源被并发访问。
q: 这类问题的本质与该套用的模式是？
options: 读扩展问题，加只读副本
竞争问题：需要防竞态、保一致的协调机制
大文件问题，用预签名 URL
实时更新问题，加 WebSocket
options_en: A read-scaling problem, so add read replicas.
A contention problem that needs coordination mechanisms like locks or transactions to prevent race conditions.
A large-blob problem, so use a presigned URL.
A realtime-update problem, so add WebSocket.

why_en: Multiple users grabbing the same ticket is a contention problem that needs coordination mechanisms to prevent race conditions.
whenOtherWins: 如果并发访问的是不同资源、没有共享写目标，就没有竞争问题，普通的扩展手段即可。
tradeoff: 强一致的协调开销 vs 允许竞态导致超卖
optionMeanings: 把问题归为读容量不足
把问题归为并发写同一资源
把问题归为大文件传输
把问题归为服务端推送

锁/事务能保证同一票只卖出一次

适合多个请求同时修改同一资源的场景

optionMeanings_en: Frames it as insufficient read capacity.
Frames it as concurrent writes to the same resource.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个操作并发访问同一份数据、结果取决于执行顺序而产生的不一致 bug。

scenario_en: Multiple users are grabbing the last concert ticket or bidding on the same auction item at the same time, so one shared resource is being accessed concurrently.

q: 处理竞争（contention）的手段谱系包括哪些？（多选）
options: 数据库层：悲观锁、乐观并发控制（OCC）
分布式协调：分布式锁、两阶段提交（2PC）
基于队列的串行化
给客户端加载入动画掩盖延迟
options_en: Database-level: pessimistic locking and optimistic concurrency control.
Distributed coordination: distributed locks and two-phase commit.
Queue-based serialization.
Adding a loading animation on the client to mask latency.
why: 方案从数据库级（悲观锁、OCC）到分布式协调（分布式锁、2PC、队列串行化）。关键是分清什么时候用事务/原子性、什么时候用显式锁。
why_en: Contention solutions range from pessimistic locking and optimistic concurrency control to distributed locks, two-phase commit, and queue-based serialization.
optionMeanings: 单库内的两种并发控制手段
跨库/跨服务的协调手段
把并发请求排成单队列处理
纯前端体验优化，不解决数据问题
optionScenarioImpacts: 覆盖单数据库范围内的竞争
覆盖需要跨系统协调一致性的场景
牺牲部分并发度换取顺序保证
底层数据仍可能被并发破坏
optionDirectness: 适合单库内竞争，优先用数据库原生机制
适合跨库/跨服务且必须原子提交的竞争
适合能牺牲并发度、换取严格顺序的资源
加载动画只适合感知延迟优化，不保护数据
optionMeanings_en: Two concurrency-control tools inside one database.
Cross-database/cross-service coordination tools.
Serializes concurrent requests through a single queue.
Pure frontend polish that does not touch the data problem.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Covers contention scoped to one database.
Covers scenarios needing cross-system consistency.
Trades some concurrency for ordering guarantees.
Underlying data can still be corrupted by concurrent writes.
optionDirectness_en: Fits contention scoped to one database; start with database-native tools.
Fits cross-database or cross-service work that must commit atomically.
Fits resources where you can trade concurrency for strict ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 乐观并发控制：先假设不会冲突、写时校验版本号，冲突了再重试，而不是提前加锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare, checks a version number at write time, and retries on conflict instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交：协调者先让所有参与者"准备好"，都同意了再统一"提交"，用于跨库/跨服务的原子性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit has a coordinator ask every participant to prepare, then commits only once all agree, giving atomicity across databases or services.

q: 解决竞争问题时，推荐的演进顺序是？
options: 一开始就上分布式锁和 2PC 显得更专业

scenario: 订单履约流程横跨多个服务、耗时长，必须扛得住失败、重试和外部依赖抖动，还要保证不重复执行。
q: 现代的推荐方案是？

用工作流引擎（如 Temporal）自动管理状态和重试

把整个流程塞进一个数据库事务
options_en: Each service stores its own state and hand-writes error handling.
Use a workflow engine like Temporal or AWS Step Functions to automatically manage state, failure recovery, and retries.
Use a cron job that checks every order once a minute.
Squeeze the entire flow into a single database transaction.
why: 从状态散落各处、手工错误处理，转向声明式工作流：系统持久化状态、自动恢复和重试，并保留完整审计轨迹。外部 activity 仍可能重试，端到端效果要靠幂等或补偿才能接近 exactly-once。
why_en: Workflow engines like Temporal manage durable state, recovery, and retries automatically, though activities still need idempotency for exactly-once-like effects.
whenOtherWins: 流程简单、只在单服务内时，简单的单机编排就够了；事件溯源则是让每步发事件触发下一步的分布式替代方案。
tradeoff: 自动状态管理和审计 vs 引入工作流引擎的学习和运维成本

q: 事件溯源如何实现多步流程的分布式协调？

scenario: 设计 Uber 或 Gopuff：要按地理位置搜索附近的司机/仓库，实体数量在几十万到上百万。

why: 没有官方推送时只能定期轮询抓快照；要支持历史价格和降价提醒，就必须按时间序列存储并做阈值比较。
why_en: Without an official push feed, the service must poll for price snapshots on a schedule and store them as a time series to support history and threshold alerts.
options_en: Subscribe to an official real-time price push feed and never poll.
Only keep the latest price and discard history.
Write every price as a strongly consistent transaction synced instantly across replicas.
Poll for price snapshots on a schedule, store them as a time series, and fire alerts when a threshold is crossed.

q: Contention 在系统设计里指什么？
options: 多个进程同时争抢同一份资源，比如最后一张票或同一个拍卖品
系统里只有读请求，完全没有写请求发生

The system only receives read requests and never any writes.
The database table only stores static configuration that almost never changes.
Different microservices share no state or data with each other at all.
why: Contention 是多个并发操作争抢同一资源。不协调就会出现 race condition、重复预订、重复扣款或状态不一致。
why_en: Contention happens when multiple processes compete for the same resource at the same time.

q: Lost update 的本质是什么？
options: 两个请求读到同一个旧值，各自写回导致后写覆盖了先写的结果
数据库所在磁盘出现物理损坏，导致这批数据永久丢失
缓存条目 TTL 设置太短，读请求频繁 miss 后要回源
用户在提交表单前离开了页面，请求根本没有发出
options_en: Two requests read the same old value, both write back, and the later write silently overwrites the earlier one's result.
The database's underlying disk suffers physical damage and this batch of data is permanently lost.
The cache entry's TTL is set too short, so reads miss frequently and have to fall back to the source.
The user left the page before submitting the form, so the request was never sent.
why: Lost update 是 read-modify-write 周期里的经典竞态：读和写不是一个原子动作，中间状态可能被别人改变。
why_en: A lost update occurs when concurrent read-modify-write cycles act on the same stale value and one write silently overwrites another.

q: 按正确顺序排列“最后一张票被卖两次”的竞态流程：
steps: Bob 在 Alice 写回前也读到还有 1 张票
Alice 和 Bob 都决定可以购买并继续扣款
Alice 读到 available_seats = 1
两次更新都提交，库存可能到 -1，且两人都收到确认
why: 问题出在读库存和写库存之间有一个时间窗口，两个请求都基于同一个旧事实行动。同步机制的目标就是关闭这个窗口。
why_en: The race happens because both buyers act on the same stale seat count before either write closes the gap between it and the read.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Buyer A
  participant DB as Inventory
  participant B as Buyer B
  A->>DB: read one left
  B->>DB: read one left
  A->>DB: write sold
  B->>DB: write sold again

termDefinitions.meaning: 并发操作的执行顺序影响最终结果是否正确的情形。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is when the outcome depends on the unpredictable timing of concurrent operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个进程/请求同时争抢同一份资源或同一行数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contention means multiple processes compete for the same resource at the same time.

q_en: Put the race that sells the last ticket twice in the correct order.

scenario: 你只需要“有库存时才把库存减 1”，这个规则能直接写成当前行上的 WHERE 条件，不需要先查再判断。
q: 在数据库里落地这条规则最简单且并发安全的做法是什么？
options: 先 SELECT 查询库存，在应用代码里判断是否大于零，确认后再无条件执行一次 UPDATE 写回新库存值
用一条 conditional UPDATE，把 WHERE available_seats > 0 写进同一语句
给整个数据库加一把全局互斥锁，让所有并发到达的购买请求都排队串行执行
把所有并发到达的购买请求直接丢弃，统一提示用户稍后重新下单再试一次
options_en: SELECT the count first, check it's positive in application code, then run a separate unconditional UPDATE to write the new value back.
Use one conditional UPDATE that puts WHERE available_seats > 0 in the same statement.
Put a single global mutex lock on the entire database so every concurrent purchase request queues up and runs serially.
Just drop every purchase request that arrives concurrently and uniformly ask users to reorder a bit later.
why: 当检查条件就是写入行上的谓词时，数据库能在同一条 UPDATE 里完成检查和修改。失败者会匹配 0 行，而不是读到过期值再写坏它。
why_en: A conditional update makes the check and the write one atomic database operation, so the loser matches zero rows instead of overwriting a stale read.
tradeoff: 单条 WHERE 谓词的原子性 vs 应用代码里 read-then-write 的灵活性
whenOtherWins: 如果决策需要应用代码读多行、找连续座位或调用外部服务，单条 WHERE 谓词就不够，需要锁、OCC 或 reservation。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  R[Request buy]
  U[UPDATE where seats gt zero]
  C{Rows changed}
  S[Success]
  F[Sold out]
  R --> U --> C
  C -->|one| S
  C -->|zero| F

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write bundles the check and the write into one atomic statement that only applies if the condition still holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有当前值仍等于预期值时才写入的原子操作。

scenario: 你要用 SQL 原子地把库存减 1，只允许库存大于 0 时才能成功。
q: 哪一项最准确描述这段 SQL 的并发行为？
options: 它先无条件读一次库存，再无条件写一次新值，两次操作之间的间隙仍然会导致超卖
它把检查条件和 decrement 合成一次原子写，只有 available_seats > 0 时才会匹配
它会一直锁住整张 concerts 表，直到应用服务重启才会释放这把锁
只要这条语句被执行，它一定会抛出异常，而不会返回 affected rows 为 0
options_en: It reads the count once unconditionally and writes the new value once unconditionally, so overselling can still happen in the gap between the two steps.
It merges the check and the decrement into one atomic write that only matches when available_seats is greater than 0.
It keeps the entire concerts table locked until the application server eventually restarts.
As long as the statement executes, it is guaranteed to throw an exception instead of ever returning zero affected rows.
codeSample:
UPDATE concerts
SET available_seats = available_seats - 1
WHERE concert_id = 'weeknd_tour'
  AND available_seats > 0;
why: 这是 SQL 里的 compare-and-set：条件仍成立才修改。并发失败时通常表现为 affected rows = 0，而不是业务自动回滚。
why_en: The SQL encodes compare-and-set by updating only when the current row still satisfies the predicate, so a losing write matches zero rows instead of raising an error.
tradeoff: 单条原子 UPDATE 的简单性 vs 先 SELECT 再判断的可读性
whenOtherWins: 如果还要创建 ticket 记录，必须把后续 INSERT 绑定到这条 UPDATE 是否真的改动了行，通常放在同一事务里。

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有当前值仍等于预期值时才写入的原子操作。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条 SQL 语句实际修改的行数；UPDATE 匹配 0 行本身不算报错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The affected row count is how many rows a statement actually changed, and zero rows is not an error by itself.

SET available_seats = available_seats - 1,

q: 这段 SQL 的关键语义是什么？

codeSample:
UPDATE seats
SET reserved_by = 'user123',
    reserved_until = NOW() + INTERVAL '10 minutes'
WHERE seat_id = 'A15'
  AND (reserved_until IS NULL OR reserved_until < NOW());

q: 下面这些跨存储的技术映射，哪些是正确的？（多选）

options_en: Conditional write shows up as SQL WHERE, DynamoDB's ConditionExpression, and Redis's SET NX.

Most NoSQL stores fully support serializable isolation by default.

why: 拍卖很适合 OCC：高价单调上升，业务值本身可以当 guard，输的一方重读当前最高价后再重新出价。
why_en: Auctions fit optimistic concurrency because the monotonically rising high bid is itself a natural version guard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把检查条件和写入合并成一条原子语句，只有条件仍成立才生效。

termDefinitions.meaning: 带过期时间的临时占用记录，用来在不持有数据库事务锁的情况下短期保留资源。

q: Handling Large Blobs 模式解决的核心问题是什么？

why: 服务器角色从数据传输变成访问控制：验证请求、生成临时 scoped credential，然后退出数据路径。

whenOtherWins: 如果文件很小或必须同步检查每个字节再接受，普通 API 上传或代理路径可能更合适。
