scenario: 读写比极端（天天刷、偶尔发），feed 必须 <500ms，读时聚合已被数字证明不可行。
scenario_en: The workload is extremely read-heavy, feed reads must stay under 500ms, and the math has ruled out read-time aggregation.
q: 更根本的解法是？
q_en: What is the more fundamental fix for slow feed reads?
options: 换更大规格、更贵的数据库机型硬扛全部流量
让客户端在本地拉取数据并自行拼装完整的 feed
每次请求都并行发出 1000 个独立的数据库查询
fan-out on write：写时预计算进粉丝 feed
options_en: Switch to a bigger, more expensive database instance type to brute-force all the traffic.
Let the client fetch data locally and assemble the entire feed itself on-device.
Issue one thousand independent parallel database queries on every single request.
Fan-out on write: precompute into follower feeds at write time.
why: 把工作从读时挪到写时：发帖那一刻更新所有粉丝的预计算 feed，读就变成一次极快的 Redis 查询。读多写少的系统里，这笔交换很划算。
why_en: Fan-out on write precomputes each follower's feed at posting time, turning a feed read into a single fast Redis lookup.
whenOtherWins: 百万粉名人的写放大不可承受，所以名人帖仍走读时合并——最终落点是混合方案，而非纯 fan-out on write。

scenario: 发帖后 fan-out 服务要立刻找到「谁在关注发帖人」；但 Follows 主表按 followerId 分区，方向反了。
scenario_en: After a post is created, the fan-out service must quickly find the author's followers, but the main Follows table is partitioned by followerId.
q: 需要补什么索引？
q_en: Which index is needed to fan out a new post to followers?
options: 什么索引都不用加，主表原样就能查
对 caption 字段建一个本地二级索引
GSI：followedId 作分区键、followerId 作排序键
直接对 Follows 表做一次全表扫描

A GSI with followedId as the partition key and followerId as the sort key.

why: fan-out 要按「被关注者」反查粉丝列表，所以建 GSI 把方向倒过来：followedId 分区、followerId 排序，一次 Query 拿到全部粉丝。
why_en: A global secondary index with followed id as the partition key and follower id as the sort key lets the fan-out service quickly find all followers of the poster.

scenario: 在按粉丝数分流的混合方案里，需要定一个具体阈值来区分「名人」和普通用户，这个阈值决定了多少作者走预计算、多少作者走实时合并。
scenario_en: In the hybrid fan-out design, the team needs a concrete threshold to classify celebrity accounts and decide who gets precomputed.
q: 用来区分「名人」与普通用户的示例阈值是？
q_en: What example follower threshold separates celebrities from regular users?
options_en: One thousand followers.
Ten thousand followers.
One hundred thousand followers.
One million followers.
why: 示例阈值 10 万粉：低于它走预计算，高于它走读时合并。记住这是个要调的旋钮，不是魔法常数。
why_en: The example threshold is one hundred thousand followers, below which feeds are precomputed and above which posts are merged at read time.

q: 混合方案下，用户请求 feed 的读路径是？
q_en: In the hybrid design, what does the feed read path do?
options: 只读取 Redis 里已经预计算好的那部分非名人 feed
完全不用 Redis，每次都只实时查询 Posts 表
先返回名人帖，再单独发起一次请求补普通帖，分两次响应
取 Redis 预计算 feed（非名人部分）+ 实时查所关注名人的近期帖子，两者按时间合并后返回
options_en: Only read the already-precomputed non-celebrity portion of the feed in Redis.
Skip Redis entirely and only query the Posts table in real time, every time.
Return celebrity posts first, then issue a separate request for ordinary posts as a second response.
Fetch the precomputed non-celebrity feed from Redis and merge it chronologically with a live query for followed celebrities' recent posts.
why: 读路径变成「预计算 + 实时合并」：Redis 拿大头，名人帖现查现补，最后按时间序 merge。这是牺牲一点读延迟换写侧可控。
why_en: At read time the precomputed Redis feed is merged chronologically with freshly queried recent posts from any followed celebrities.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["feed 请求"] --> R["Redis:预计算 feed
(粉丝数少于 10 万的作者)"] U --> C["Posts 表:所关注名人的近期帖"] R --> M["按时间序合并"] C --> M M --> O["返回用户"]
optionMeanings: 假设所有作者都被预计算了，忽略了名人分支。
假设完全没有预计算，忽略了普通用户的 Redis feed。
把一次请求拆成两次响应，客户端处理复杂且体验变差。
两条数据来源按时间戳合并成一份完整、有序的 feed。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会漏掉用户关注的名人的最新帖子。

scenario: 混合 feed 方案：普通用户发帖时预先写入粉丝 feed；粉丝特别多的账号不做全量写入，而是在读 feed 时再合并他们的新帖。阈值暂定为 10 万粉丝。
scenario_en: In the hybrid feed design, ordinary authors precompute fan-out, while high-follower authors are merged at read time. The initial threshold is 100K followers.
q: 为什么这个「名人阈值」必须仔细调？
q_en: Why must the celebrity threshold be tuned carefully?
options: 太低→更多账号读时合并，读变慢；太高→高粉账号仍写时 fan-out，写放大未解决
这个阈值随便设一个数字就行，对系统几乎没有任何实质影响
阈值设得越高，系统整体表现就会越好，没有代价
阈值设得越低，系统整体表现就会越好，没有代价
options_en: Too low pushes more authors into read-time merging and slows reads; too high leaves write fan-out unsolved.
Just pick any number for this threshold; it has virtually no real effect on the system.
The higher the threshold, the better the system performs overall, with no downside.
The lower the threshold, the better the system performs overall, with no downside.
why: 阈值太低，会把很多中等粉丝账号也当名人，导致更多 feed 请求要实时合并；阈值太高，高粉账号仍会写放大，问题没被控制住。
why_en: The celebrity threshold trades read latency against write amplification: too low creates too much read-time merging, while too high leaves high-follower write fan-out unsolved.
optionMeanings: 准确指出了阈值在两个方向上各自的失败模式。

q: 混合方案给用户体验和运维带来什么副作用？
q_en: What side effects does the hybrid fan-out design create?
options: 混合方案对所有用户来说都不会带来任何体验差异
关注名人多的用户 feed 更慢、体验不一致，还要多维护一套缓存和监控
受影响、体验变差的其实是名人自己刷 feed 的速度
混合方案会让整条写路径彻底不可用，发帖失败
options_en: The hybrid approach causes absolutely no experience difference for any user.
Users following many celebrities get slower, inconsistent feeds, and the team must maintain an extra caching and monitoring system.
It's actually the celebrities' own feed-loading speed that gets affected and slower.
The hybrid approach makes the entire write path unusable, causing posts to fail.
why: 谁关注的名人多，谁的实时合并就重——体验分层了。应对：分用户段设 SLA、给名人帖加缓存；预计算+实时两套系统并存，运维复杂度上升。
why_en: Users following many celebrities get slower feeds, so you need per-segment SLAs, extra caching for celebrity posts, and careful monitoring of two coexisting systems.
optionMeanings: 忽视了实时合并会给部分用户带来的额外延迟。

scenario: 面试官追问：这套按粉丝数分流的混合 fan-out 方案，是不是只是理论上说得通，实际公司会不会真的这么做？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether this follower-count-based hybrid fan-out design is only theoretical or used in real systems.
q: 回答这个追问时，最有力的论据是什么？
q_en: What is the strongest evidence that the hybrid fan-out design is practical?
options: 声称 Instagram 全量预计算所有人的 feed，从不做特殊处理

scenario: 发帖接口必须毫秒级返回，但一条帖子的 fan-out 可能要更新数百万粉丝的 feed，耗时很长。
scenario_en: The post API must return in milliseconds, but fan-out for one post may update millions of follower feeds.
q: 怎么处理这段长耗时工作？
q_en: How should the system handle long-running fan-out work?
options: 在发帖这一次请求里同步做完全部 fan-out 写入
postId 入队，由 Feed Fan-out 服务异步消费——典型的「管理长时任务」模式
放弃 fan-out 优化，全部退回读时聚合方案
让客户端不断轮询后端直到 fan-out 处理完成
options_en: Synchronously complete all fan-out writes within that single post request.
Queue the postId and let a Feed Fan-out service consume it asynchronously, the classic long-running-task pattern.
Abandon the fan-out optimization and revert entirely to read-time aggregation.
Have the client keep polling the backend until fan-out finishes processing.
why: 长耗时工作放队列异步做：发帖立即返回，fan-out 后台慢慢跑。队列还附赠削峰、重试与故障隔离。
why_en: Feed fan-out is a long-running task, so the post id goes onto a queue and a worker service updates follower feeds asynchronously.
whenOtherWins: 粉丝数极小、fan-out 毫秒级完成的场景同步写也无妨，但队列的削峰与重试能力通常仍然值得。
tradeoff: 异步队列削峰 vs 同步简单直接
optionMeanings: 让发帖请求等待数百万次写入全部完成才返回。

增加不必要的网络往返和客户端复杂度。

这是处理长耗时任务的标准模式。
等于放弃了已经做出的架构改进。

q: 把 feed 放 Redis，面试里应主动交代哪些持久性/可用性手段？（多选）
q_en: Which Redis durability and availability measures should you mention?
options: Redis Sentinel：高可用与自动故障转移
Redis Cluster：把数据分片到多个节点
AOF 或 RDB 持久化，故障后可恢复数据
把 Redis 当作永不宕机的黑盒
options_en: Redis Sentinel: high availability and automatic failover.
Redis Cluster: sharding data across multiple nodes.
AOF or RDB persistence so data can be recovered after a failure.
Treat Redis as a black box that never goes down.
why: 主动说出「AOF 持久化 + Sentinel 故障转移 + Cluster 分片」表明你考虑过 Redis 挂掉的后果，而不是把它当魔法黑盒。
why_en: Proactively mention Redis Sentinel for failover, Redis Cluster for sharding, and AOF or RDB persistence so a node failure does not wipe the feeds.
optionMeanings: 监控主从节点，主节点故障时自动切换。
把数据按哈希槽分片到多个节点，突破单机容量上限。
AOF 记录写命令日志、RDB 定期做快照，两者都能在故障后恢复数据。

q: 把 feed 架构的完整决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the full feed-architecture decision chain.
steps: 选型：fan-out on write——发帖时把 postId 预计算进每个粉丝的 Redis feed
缓解：混合方案——粉丝数超过 10 万的名人不预计算，读时实时合并
需求：feed 端到端 <500ms，读写比极端（每天刷多次、偶尔发帖）
代价：名人发帖触发数百万次 feed 写入（写放大）
判断：读时聚合要上千次查询、延迟不可控，必须把计算搬到写时
why: 完整链条：需求（快读+极端读写比）→ 判断（读时算不可行）→ 选型（写时预计算）→ 代价（名人写放大）→ 缓解（阈值分流的混合方案）。
why_en: The decision chain runs from the latency requirement, to rejecting read-time aggregation, to precomputing on write, to the celebrity write-amplification cost, to the hybrid threshold mitigation.
diagram:
graph TD
    ReadSlow[Fanout on read is slow] --> Precompute[Precompute feed]
    Precompute --> WriteFanout[Fanout on write]
    WriteFanout --> CelebProblem[Celebrity write explosion]
    CelebProblem --> Hybrid[Hybrid fanout]
tradeoff: 写时预计算换快读 vs 读时聚合换简单写

q: 补全混合 fan-out 的分流规则：
q_en: Complete the hybrid fan-out routing rule.
text: 粉丝数低于 {{100,000}} 的作者发帖走 {{fan-out on write}}（预计算进每个粉丝的 feed）；超过阈值的名人帖走 {{fan-out on read}}（读 feed 时实时查询并合并）。
why: 一句话记住混合方案：小号写时展开、大号读时合并，阈值 10 万粉。它同时守住了普通用户的读延迟和名人发帖的写放大。
why_en: Authors under one hundred thousand followers get fan-out on write while celebrity posts above the threshold are fetched and merged at read time.

why: 图片是不可变内容，可以放心在边缘缓 24 小时，大幅降低回源与延迟。缓存时长可按内容类型和热度分级配置。
why_en: Since images rarely change after upload, edge locations can cache them for about twenty-four hours.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，过期后需要重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

q: 只加 CDN（不做媒体优化）还遗留什么问题？
q_en: What problem remains if we only add a CDN without media optimization?
options: 加了 CDN 之后媒体读取速度反而会明显变慢下降
CDN 这种边缘缓存架构完全没有能力缓存视频文件
加了 CDN 之后媒体上传本身的速度会跟着变慢
所有设备仍拿同一份高清文件；对缓存策略控制有限，热门媒体可能被边缘淘汰、引发不必要的回源
options_en: Adding a CDN actually makes media read speed noticeably slower and worse.
This edge-caching CDN architecture has no ability whatsoever to cache video files.
Adding a CDN slows down the speed of the media upload process itself.
Every device still gets the same high-resolution file; cache-policy control is limited, and popular media can get evicted and refetched from origin.
why: CDN 解决了「远」，没解决「不分设备」：弱网手机和光纤桌面拿同一份大文件。另外边缘容量有限，热门内容也可能被挤出去。
why_en: A plain CDN still serves the same file to every device and offers limited cache control, so popular media can get evicted and refetched from origin.
optionMeanings: 把 CDN 该带来的加速效果说反了。
CDN 本身完全能缓存视频等各类媒体格式。
CDN 只作用于下载路径，不介入上传流程。
点出了 CDN 单独存在时仍未解决的两个真实局限。
optionScenarioImpacts: 选它误判了 CDN 带来的性能方向。
选它会让团队误以为需要额外方案才能缓存视频。
选它会让团队去错误的地方排查上传延迟问题。
推动团队继续引入设备自适应和智能缓存策略。
optionDirectness: CDN 明显是在加速读取，不是拖慢。
CDN 天然支持缓存各种媒体格式。
上传路径不经过 CDN。
准确指出了纯 CDN 方案仍存在的两个缺口。
optionMeanings_en: Reverses the actual acceleration effect of a CDN.
A CDN fully supports caching video and other media formats.
A CDN only affects the download path, not uploads.
Names the two real gaps a CDN alone leaves unsolved.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Choosing this misjudges the CDN's performance direction.
Choosing this wrongly implies video caching needs a separate solution.
Choosing this sends the team debugging upload latency in the wrong place.
Motivates adding device-aware variants and smarter cache policy.
optionDirectness_en: a CDN clearly speeds up reads, not slows them.
CDNs natively cache all media formats.
the upload path never touches the CDN.

scenario: 弱网手机用户和光纤桌面用户拿到的是同一份高分辨率原图，浪费带宽、加载又慢。
scenario_en: Weak mobile users and fast desktop users receive the same high-resolution original, wasting bandwidth and slowing loads.
q: 最有效的方案是？
q_en: What is the most effective media delivery design?
options: 把所有媒体统一降为最低画质来强行节省带宽
经媒体处理服务生成多分辨率/多格式变体，CDN 按设备与网络下发合适版本
让用户在上传或播放时自己手动挑选清晰度档位
移动端设备一律禁止播放任何形式的视频内容
options_en: Force every media file down to the lowest quality to save bandwidth.
A media processing service generates multi-resolution, multi-format variants, and the CDN serves the right one per device and network.
Let users manually pick a resolution tier themselves when uploading or playing.
Ban every mobile device from playing any form of video content whatsoever.
why: CDN 分发 + 动态媒体优化是终态：手机自动拿小图，桌面拿高清，视频走多码率自适应流。这是大型媒体平台的通用做法。
why_en: A media processing service generates variants per resolution and format, and the CDN serves the right one based on each device and network.
whenOtherWins: 小规模应用不值得维护变体管线——一份原图 + CDN 自带压缩已够，等带宽成本真成问题再上。
tradeoff: 多变体自适应下发 vs 单一质量一刀切
diagram:
graph LR
    Original[Original media] --> Processor[Media optimizer]
    Processor --> Thumb[Thumbnail]
    Processor --> Web[Web variant]
    Processor --> Mobile[Mobile variant]
    Thumb --> CDN
    Web --> CDN
    Mobile --> CDN
optionMeanings: 牺牲所有用户的画质来换取一个统一的低带宽方案。
为不同设备和网络条件生成对应的媒体变体，自动匹配下发。
把选择清晰度的负担转嫁给用户。
用产品限制去规避带宽优化这个技术问题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 光纤桌面用户也被迫看低清内容，体验下降。
弱网手机自动拿小图，桌面用户自动拿高清，两边都满意。
增加了操作步骤，多数用户根本不会主动调整。
移动端用户完全无法看视频，产品功能被阉割。
optionDirectness: 牺牲了本不必牺牲的桌面用户体验。
这是大型媒体平台的行业标准做法。
把工程问题转嫁给了用户。
这是对核心功能的削弱，不是优化。
optionMeanings_en: Sacrifices everyone's quality for one uniform low-bandwidth option.
Generates variants matched to device and network, served automatically.
Shifts the burden of choosing resolution onto the user.
Uses a product restriction to dodge a bandwidth-optimization problem.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Fiber desktop users are forced into low quality too, a worse experience.
Weak-network phones auto-get small images, desktops auto-get high-res.
Adds friction most users will never bother to use.
Mobile users lose video entirely, a crippled core feature.
optionDirectness_en: sacrifices desktop experience unnecessarily.
the industry-standard approach for large media platforms.
shifts an engineering problem onto users.
this cripples a core feature rather than optimizing it.

q: CDN 怎么知道该发哪个媒体变体？
q_en: How does the CDN know which media variant to serve?
options: 客户端在请求里带上设备信息与网络状况，CDN 据此挑选最合适的变体
CDN 在多个候选变体之间随机挑一个下发
由运营人员为每一个用户手动配置变体
由 DNS 域名解析的结果来决定发哪个变体
options_en: The client includes device and network info in the request, and the CDN picks a matching variant.
The CDN randomly picks one variant among the candidates to serve.
Operations staff manually configure a variant for every individual user.
The DNS resolution result determines which variant gets served.
why: 选择变体的信号来自客户端：请求携带设备类型和网络条件，CDN 按这些信息路由到对应版本。
why_en: The client includes its device and network conditions in the request so the CDN can serve the most appropriate variant.
optionMeanings: 变体选择依据客户端请求里携带的真实信号。
假设选择过程不依据任何信号，纯随机。
假设需要人工逐个用户配置，完全不可扩展。
把域名解析这个不相关的机制当成了变体选择依据。
optionScenarioImpacts: 手机弱网自动拿小图，桌面光纤自动拿高清。
同一用户不同请求可能拿到不一致甚至不合适的版本。
5 亿用户级别下，人工配置完全不可能落地。
DNS 只负责把域名解析成 IP，不携带设备或网络信息。
optionDirectness: 这是变体选择的标准依据。
随机选择无法保证匹配设备能力。
在这个规模下完全不可扩展。
DNS 解析和变体选择是两个不相关的机制。
optionMeanings_en: Variant choice is based on real signals carried in the client request.
Assumes the choice process uses no signal at all, purely random.
Assumes manual per-user configuration, completely unscalable.
Mistakes an unrelated mechanism, DNS resolution, for variant selection.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Weak-network phones auto-get small images, fiber desktops auto-get high-res.
The same user's different requests could get inconsistent, ill-fitting versions.
Manual configuration is simply impossible at 500M users.
DNS only resolves domain names to IPs; it carries no device or network info.
optionDirectness_en: the standard basis for variant selection.
random choice can't match device capability.
completely unscalable at this size.
DNS resolution and variant selection are unrelated mechanisms.

scenario: 一条内容眼看要爆红，预计某些地区即将出现巨大访问量，不想让第一波用户全部打回源站。
scenario_en: A piece of content is likely to go viral in certain regions, and the team wants to avoid the first wave of users all hitting origin.
q: 缓存策略上该怎么做？
q_en: What cache strategy should handle a predictable viral spike?
options: 顺其自然，等边缘节点自己按需慢慢回源填充
把边缘缓存的 TTL 整体统一调短一些
提前预热高访问地区的边缘缓存，热门内容缓存更激进
把这条即将爆红的内容暂时从平台下架
options_en: Do nothing special; let edge nodes slowly fill from origin on their own as demand naturally arrives.
Uniformly shorten the edge cache TTL across the board a bit.
Proactively warm edge caches in high-traffic regions, caching popular content more aggressively.
Temporarily take the about-to-go-viral content down from the platform.
why: 对可预测的爆点主动预热边缘，把回源风暴消灭在发生前；同时按热度分级缓存强度。这就是「智能缓存策略」。
why_en: For predictably viral content you proactively warm edge caches in high-viewership regions and cache popular media more aggressively.
whenOtherWins: 流量平稳、没有爆点时，被动按需缓存足矣，预热反而浪费源站带宽。
tradeoff: 主动预热避免回源风暴 vs 被动按需缓存更省资源
optionMeanings: 完全依赖被动缓存机制应对可预测的流量高峰。
缩短过期时间反而会增加回源频率。
提前把内容主动推送到预计高流量地区的边缘节点。
用产品下架去规避一个本可以用缓存策略解决的问题。
optionScenarioImpacts: 第一波用户大量打到源站，可能引发回源风暴。
边缘节点更频繁地过期并重新回源，加重源站压力。
第一波用户就能命中边缘缓存，源站压力被显著削平。
损害了内容可见性，且没有解决底层的缓存能力问题。
optionDirectness: 没有利用「可预测」这个已知信息。
方向反了，会让问题更严重。
主动利用可预测性提前布防。
是产品层面的妥协，不是工程解法。
optionMeanings_en: Relies entirely on passive caching for a predictable traffic spike.
Shortening expiry actually increases origin refetch frequency.
Proactively pushes content to edge nodes in expected high-traffic regions.
Takes content down to dodge a problem caching could solve.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The first wave of users hits the origin hard, risking a stampede.
Edge nodes expire and refetch more often, adding origin pressure.
The first wave already hits the warmed edge cache, sparing the origin.
Hurts content visibility without fixing the underlying caching gap.
optionDirectness_en: wastes the known fact that this spike is predictable.
the wrong direction, making things worse.
proactively exploits predictability ahead of time.
a product compromise, not an engineering fix.

q: 动态媒体优化（多变体）要付出什么代价？
q_en: What cost does dynamic media optimization add?
options: 动态媒体优化管线几乎不会带来任何额外的工程代价
每个媒体要管理多个版本，存储成本与复杂度上升；处理管线还给上传增加延迟，需要细致监控
动态媒体优化会导致用户读取内容的延迟明显上升
动态媒体优化会让已有的 CDN 缓存全部失效作废
options_en: The dynamic media optimization pipeline brings essentially no extra engineering cost at all.
Each media item now has multiple versions to manage, raising storage cost and complexity; the processing pipeline also adds upload latency requiring careful monitoring.
Dynamic media optimization causes users' content read latency to rise noticeably.
Dynamic media optimization invalidates every bit of the existing CDN cache.
why: 变体越多，存储和管理越贵；转码管线又拉长了上传路径。但对大规模媒体平台，这是性能与可管理性之间最划算的折中。
why_en: Multiple variants per file raise storage cost and complexity, and the processing pipeline adds upload latency that needs monitoring.
optionMeanings: 假设多变体管线是免费的，忽略了真实工程代价。
准确点出了存储、复杂度、上传延迟三方面的真实代价。
把读取和上传两个阶段的延迟方向搞混了。
夸大了对 CDN 缓存机制本身的影响。
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让团队低估上线多变体管线所需的工程投入。
帮助团队为存储成本和监控体系做好预算和准备。
会让团队误以为读取变慢了，实际是上传路径变长。
会让团队误判需要重新设计缓存架构。
optionDirectness: 任何新增管线都有真实成本。
完整覆盖了动态媒体优化的代价来源。
读取因为有了合适变体反而更快。
CDN 缓存机制本身没有受到破坏。
optionMeanings_en: Assumes the variant pipeline is free, ignoring real engineering cost.
Accurately names storage, complexity, and upload latency as the real costs.
Confuses which stage, read or upload, actually gets slower.
Overstates the impact on the CDN caching mechanism itself.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Leads the team to underbudget the engineering effort for the pipeline.
Helps the team plan storage cost and monitoring properly.
Wrongly implies reads slow down; it's the upload path that lengthens.
Wrongly implies the caching architecture needs a redesign.
optionDirectness_en: any added pipeline has real cost.
fully covers where the cost actually comes from.
reads actually get faster with a matched variant.
the CDN caching mechanism itself is unaffected.

scenario: 平均每个媒体约 2MB，平台每天产出 1 亿帖，团队要据此估算每日新增的对象存储用量。
scenario_en: Each media object averages about 2MB and the platform creates 100M posts per day, so the team estimates daily object-storage growth.
q: 按日均产出的媒体总量，这个规模应该归入哪个存储区间？
q_en: What storage bucket does daily media output fall into?
options: 约 200TB
约 2TB
约 20PB
约 200GB
options_en: About two hundred terabytes.
About two terabytes.
About twenty petabytes.
About two hundred gigabytes.
why: 100M × 2MB = 200TB/天。这个量级说明媒体存储是成本大头，为「冷数据下沉 Glacier」埋下伏笔。
why_en: One hundred million posts at about two megabytes each add up to roughly two hundred terabytes of new media per day.

scenario: 按每天新增约 200TB 媒体累计，团队要估算十年后总存储规模，判断 S3 长期是否扛得住、是否需要分层。
scenario_en: Starting from about 200TB of new media per day, the team estimates ten-year storage size to judge long-term S3 cost and tiering.
q: 十年周期累计的媒体存储总量应归入哪个数量区间？
q_en: What order of magnitude is ten years of accumulated media storage?
options: 约 750TB
约 75PB
约 750PB
约 7.5EB
options_en: About seven hundred fifty terabytes.
About seventy-five petabytes.
About seven hundred fifty petabytes.
About seven and a half exabytes.
why: 约 750PB / 10 年。S3 装得下但很贵——所以要按访问频率分层，把长期没人看的媒体移去更冷的存储。
why_en: Over ten years the media adds up to roughly seven hundred fifty petabytes, which S3 can hold but not cheaply.

scenario: 每帖元数据约 1KB，平台每天新增 1 亿帖，团队要据此估算元数据数据库每日新增的写入量。
scenario_en: Each post has about 1KB of metadata and the platform creates 100M posts per day, so the team estimates daily metadata writes.
q: 按日均新增帖子折算，元数据数据库每日新增量应归入哪个区间？
q_en: What bucket does daily metadata growth fall into?
options: 约 100TB
约 100GB
约 1GB
约 10PB
options_en: About one hundred terabytes.
About one hundred gigabytes.
About one gigabyte.
About ten petabytes.
why: 100M × 1KB = 100GB/天，比媒体小三个数量级。若 DynamoDB 成本吃紧，不常访问的元数据同样可以下移到 S3。
why_en: One hundred million posts at one kilobyte of metadata each is about one hundred gigabytes of new metadata per day.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 10 年 750PB 的 S3 账单太贵，而其中大量老媒体几乎无人访问。
scenario_en: Ten years of 750PB in S3 is expensive, and much of the old media is rarely accessed.
q: 省钱的正确姿势是？
q_en: What is the right cost-saving storage strategy?
options: 把长期没人访问的老媒体定期直接永久删除
把所有的媒体数据不加区分地统一搬进 Redis 缓存
把老媒体打成 zip 压缩包但仍留在原来的存储层
把长期未访问的媒体下移到更冷存储层（如 Glacier），冷元数据同理下移
options_en: Periodically and permanently delete old media that nobody has accessed in a long time.
Move all media data indiscriminately into the Redis cache.
Zip up the old media into an archive but leave it in the original storage tier.
Move long-untouched media down to a colder tier like Glacier, and shift cold metadata down the same way.
why: 冷热分层是通用省钱模式：访问越少的数据放越冷（越便宜）的层。媒体去 Glacier、冷元数据去 S3，热数据留在原地。
why_en: Move media that has not been accessed in a long time to colder cheaper storage like Glacier, and likewise shift cold metadata out of DynamoDB.
whenOtherWins: 如果老内容仍被频繁回看（周年回顾、经典帖回流），Glacier 的取回延迟和费用反而伤体验，应留在标准层。
tradeoff: 冷热分层省成本 vs 统一标准层保低延迟
optionMeanings: 永久移除数据，用户以后再也无法访问这些历史内容。
把持久化对象存储的数据搬进易失性的内存缓存。
压缩后仍留在原来昂贵的存储层，没有降低成本。
按访问频率把冷数据下沉到更便宜的存储层，热数据留在原地。
optionScenarioImpacts: 用户会永久失去访问自己历史帖子的能力，产品体验受损。
Redis 内存成本远高于对象存储，且重启可能丢数据。
存储账单几乎不变，压缩带来的节省有限。
长期不访问的数据成本大幅下降，访问频繁的数据延迟不受影响。
optionDirectness: 删除数据违背了保留用户内容的产品预期。
用错了存储介质，成本方向反了。
没有解决核心的存储层级问题。
这是解决海量冷数据成本问题的标准做法。
optionMeanings_en: Permanently removes data; users can never access that history again.
Moves data from durable object storage into a volatile memory cache.
Stays compressed in the same expensive tier, barely saving anything.
Tiers cold data down to cheaper storage by access frequency, keeping hot data in place.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Users permanently lose access to their historical posts, hurting the product.
Redis memory costs far exceed object storage, and restarts can lose data.
The storage bill barely changes; compression savings are marginal.
Cold data cost drops sharply while frequently accessed data stays fast.
optionDirectness_en: deleting data violates the expectation of preserving user content.
wrong storage medium, reverses the cost direction.
doesn't address the core storage-tier problem.
the standard fix for massive cold-data cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: S3 的低成本冷存储层，读取延迟高但存储费用低，适合极少访问的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Glacier is S3's low-cost cold storage tier with slower retrieval but much cheaper storage for rarely accessed data.

q: 补全存储温度层级（由热到冷）：
q_en: Complete the storage temperature hierarchy from hot to cold.
text: 存储由热到冷、由贵到省：{{CDN}} → 缓存/内存 → {{SSD}} → {{HDD}} → {{磁带}}；不常被访问的数据往下移一层就能省钱。
why: 「越热越贵」是存储的普适规律。任何成本讨论都可以落到这条链上：找出访问频率低的数据，把它往下挪。
why_en: Storage runs hot to cold from CDN to memory to SSD to HDD to tape, and rarely accessed data can always move down a level to save money.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["CDN(最热最贵)"] --> B["缓存/内存"]
    B --> C["SSD"]
    C --> D["HDD"]
    D --> E["磁带(最冷最省)"]

q: 微服务层面的吞吐扩展怎么做？
q_en: How should stateless microservices scale throughput?
options: 靠人工全天候盯着监控面板去手动添加机器
只做垂直扩展，一路不断买更大规格的单台机器
按 CPU/内存阈值自动水平扩缩容，每组服务前隐含负载均衡器分发流量
部署一台超大规格的单体 Redis 扛下全部业务流量
options_en: Have someone watch the dashboard around the clock to manually add machines.
Only scale vertically, continuously buying an ever-bigger single machine.
Auto-scale horizontally on CPU or memory thresholds, with a load balancer implicitly distributing traffic to each group.
Deploy one oversized monolithic Redis instance to absorb all business traffic.
why: 无状态微服务的标准打法：基于 CPU/内存指标自动水平扩缩，流量由每组服务前的负载均衡器分发。
why_en: Microservices scale horizontally and automatically based on CPU or memory thresholds, with an implicit load balancer in front of each scaled group.
diagram:
graph LR
    LB[Load balancer] --> Post[Post Service pool]
    LB --> Feed[Feed Service pool]
    LB --> Follow[Follow Service pool]
    Post --> DB1[(Post DB shards)]
    Feed --> Redis[(Feed cache shards)]

给 Executions 表按时间建索引
对新建 Job 的写请求做限流

options_en: Poll the database every few minutes for due jobs.
Buffer due jobs in a message queue.
Add a time index on the Executions table.

q: 把 Job 从创建到完成的基本数据流排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the basic data flow of a job from creation to completion:
steps: Worker 在调度时间取走 Job 并执行（失败则指数退避重试）
用户提交 Job：任务、调度时间、参数
更新 Job 在系统中的状态
把 Job 持久化到系统里
why: 基础数据流：用户提交 → 持久化 → Worker 到点取走执行（失败退避重试）→ 更新状态。先建这条简单主线，再逐步增强。
why_en: The basic data flow is submit, persist, execute at scheduled time with backoff on failure, then update status.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["Create Job"] --> B[(Jobs table)]
    B --> C[(Executions table)]
    C --> D["Scheduler scan window"]
    D --> E["Delay queue"]
    E --> F["Worker executes"]
    F --> G["Update status"]

options: 这种单表设计根本无法把 parameters 参数存成 JSON 格式来使用
要找出「接下来几分钟该跑的 Job」，得扫描并求值每一条 CRON 表达式，无法扩展

why_en: Storing CRON in one table forces evaluating every expression to find upcoming jobs, which does not scale.
options_en: This single-table design cannot store the parameters field as JSON at all.

In this design, the user_id field has no way to be recorded at all.
One-time jobs, which use a specific DateTime instead of CRON, cannot be stored in this design either.

q: 把「两层调度架构」的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the full flow of the two-layer scheduler architecture:
steps: Worker 持续轮询 SQS，消息到点变可见即被处理执行
用户创建 Job，写入数据库
Cron 把这批 Job 带上合适的 delay 发到 SQS
Cron 每 5 分钟查数据库，取出接下来约 5 分钟要执行的 Job
why: 两层架构：写库 → cron 每 5 分钟捞出未来 5 分钟的 Job → 带 delay 推入 SQS → Worker 持续拉取、到点执行。数据库低频查、队列保精度。
why_en: The two-layer scheduler writes to the database, a five-minute cron pulls upcoming jobs into SQS with delays, and workers poll SQS to execute on time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["用户创建 Job"] --> DB[("数据库")]
    DB --> C["Cron 每 5 分钟查询"]
    C --> Q["SQS 延迟队列"]
    Q --> W["Worker 拉取执行"]

scenario: 要同时兼顾「数据库不被高频查询压垮」和「Job 能按秒级精度执行」。
scenario_en: The design must keep the database from being overwhelmed by high-frequency queries while still executing jobs with second-level precision.
q: 两层调度架构如何同时满足这两点？
q_en: How does the two-layer scheduler architecture satisfy both at once?
options: 让 Worker 直接每秒查数据库
查库低频（5 分钟一次），队列缓冲保证高吞吐执行
把所有 Job 缓存在应用内存里轮询
取消数据库，全部用 Redis
why: 两层解耦「查库」与「执行」：数据库每 5 分钟才查一次（低负载），消息队列高吞吐让 Worker 一到点就能拉取执行（保精度），去掉了执行频率的上界。
why_en: Splitting database querying from execution lets the database run infrequent queries while the queue delivers jobs at high throughput for precise execution.
whenOtherWins: 如果精度要求很松（比如分钟级即可）且规模很小，单层定期轮询更简单，无需引入队列。
tradeoff: 数据库低频查询 vs 队列保精度、高吞吐
options_en: Have workers query the database every second directly.
Query the database infrequently while a queue buffers jobs for high-throughput execution.
Cache every job in application memory and poll it.
Remove the database entirely and use only Redis.

对；查库低频、队列保证 Worker 能高吞吐及时拉取。
错；全放内存既不持久也无法跨实例共享。
错；去掉数据库会丢失持久记录和崩溃恢复能力。

q: 为什么不能简单地把「未来才执行的 Job」直接放进 Kafka 这类日志型队列？
q_en: Why can't jobs meant to run in the future simply be dropped into a log-based queue like Kafka?
options: Kafka 不支持持久化
Kafka 分区内严格有序，晚入队的排后面
Kafka 无法存 200 字节的小消息
Kafka 不支持多消费者
why: Kafka 分区内严格 FIFO，晚入队但该早执行的 Job 只能排在末尾等前面的跑完，无法按 execution_time 优先，破坏 2 秒精度。需要支持延迟投递的队列。
why_en: A log-based queue like Kafka delivers in order, so a job scheduled sooner still waits behind earlier-enqueued jobs.
options_en: Kafka does not support persistence.
Kafka delivers strictly in order per partition, so late arrivals queue behind it.
Kafka cannot store a 200-byte message.
Kafka does not support multiple consumers.

对；分区内严格顺序消费，晚入队的早到 Job 只能排在后面。
错；200 字节的小消息 Kafka 完全能存。
错；Kafka 天生支持多个消费者组。

scenario_en: The team wants to implement a delayed priority queue with Redis at moderate scale.
q: 该用 Redis 的什么结构，代价是什么？
q_en: Which Redis structure should be used, and what's the cost?
options: 用 Redis List 做 FIFO，无需额外代码
Sorted Set（ZSET）按 execution_time 排序
用 Redis String 存所有 Job
用 Redis Pub/Sub 广播所有 Job
why: Redis ZSET 以执行时间戳为 score 做优先队列，Worker 取 score < 当前时间的项。性能极佳（亚毫秒、原子操作），但要自己写重试、故障处理、管理副本避免单点。
why_en: Redis sorted sets score jobs by execution time for a priority queue, but you must build retries, failure handling, and replication yourself.
whenOtherWins: 在允许托管服务、追求零运维的场景，SQS 原生延迟投递更省心；Redis 适合禁用托管服务或已有 Redis 专长的团队。
tradeoff: 自建 Redis 优先队列（高性能，高运维） vs 托管队列（省运维）
options_en: Use a Redis List as a FIFO, no extra code needed.
A sorted set (ZSET) ordered by execution_time.
Store every job as a Redis String.
Broadcast every job over Redis Pub/Sub.

对；ZSET 用 execution_time 当 score 排序，但要自建重试和高可用。
错；String 存不出可排序、可范围查询的队列结构。
错；Pub/Sub 是广播语义，接收方错过就丢，不是队列。

scenario: 考虑用 RabbitMQ 实现延迟投递。
scenario_en: The team is considering RabbitMQ for delayed message delivery.
q: RabbitMQ 实现延迟投递的典型方式及其难点是？
q_en: What's RabbitMQ's typical way of achieving delayed delivery, and what's the difficulty?
options: 原生 delay 字段，零配置
TTL + 死信交换机（DLX）模拟延迟投递
用 Kafka 分区偏移量实现
RabbitMQ 不支持任何延迟
why: RabbitMQ 靠 TTL + 死信交换机模拟延迟投递；高可用需要额外配置 quorum queues，否则集群只复制拓扑不复制队列内容。
why_en: RabbitMQ can delay via per-message TTL plus a dead-letter exchange, but high availability requires quorum queues.
whenOtherWins: 如果团队已重度使用 RabbitMQ 并接受其运维复杂度，它也能胜任；否则 SQS 的原生延迟更简单。
tradeoff: 自建 RabbitMQ 延迟（可控但复杂） vs 托管队列原生延迟（简单省心）
options_en: A native delay field with zero configuration.
Per-message TTL plus a dead-letter exchange (DLX) simulates delayed delivery.
Kafka-style partition offsets.
RabbitMQ supports no delay at all.
optionDirectness: 错；RabbitMQ 没有原生延迟字段，需要自己搭 TTL+DLX。
对；TTL+死信交换机能模拟延迟，但高可用要配 quorum queues。
错；这是 Kafka 的机制，RabbitMQ 不用分区偏移量。

scenario: Jobs 表按 job_id 分区，Executions 表按 time_bucket 分区；DynamoDB 单个分区的写容量存在上限（约 1,000 WCU）。
scenario_en: The Jobs table partitions by job_id and Executions by time_bucket; a single DynamoDB partition has a write-capacity cap of roughly 1,000 WCU.
q: 这个分区级写容量上限，对分区键设计提出了什么要求？
q_en: What does this per-partition write-capacity cap demand from the partition key design?
options: 分区键必须让写入天然分散到多个分区，否则会撞上限
只要提高读容量就能绕开这个限制
换成 SSD 存储就没有这个限制
分区键随便选，DynamoDB 会自动无限扩容单分区
why: 单分区写容量有限，所以分区键要能让写入自然打散——job_id 唯一天然分散，time_bucket 则可能集中，需要写分片来补。
why_en: Because a single partition's write capacity is capped, the partition key must spread writes naturally across many partitions.
options_en: The partition key must let writes spread naturally, or it will hit the limit.
Just raising read capacity works around it.
Switching to SSD storage removes the limit.
The partition key does not matter; DynamoDB auto-scales a single partition without limit.
optionDirectness: 对；唯一性强的键天然分散，容易集中的键则要靠分片补救。
错；读容量和写容量是两个独立维度，不能互相替代。
错；存储介质不是分区写容量上限的成因。
错；单分区写容量是硬上限，不会自动无限扩容。

scenario: Executions 表按 time_bucket 分区，当前小时的所有写入都砸向同一个分区，形成热分区。
scenario_en: The Executions table partitions by time_bucket, so every write in the current hour lands on the same partition, forming a hot partition.
q: 怎么缓解这个热分区？
q_en: How do you relieve this hot partition?
options: 改用 job_id 作 Executions 分区键
写分片：分区键加随机后缀，写入分散到多分区
把整表搬到内存
降低写入速率
why: 写分片：在 time_bucket 后加随机后缀（time_bucket#shard_3）把同一小时的写分散到多个分区；读取时 Worker 并行查该时间桶的所有分片再合并。
why_en: Write sharding appends a random suffix to the time_bucket so writes spread across partitions, with workers querying all shards in parallel.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入量本就均匀、单分区没到 1,000 WCU，就无需分片——分片会增加读放大（要查多个分片）。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    B["time_bucket"] --> H["hot partition"]
    H --> S1["bucket#0"]
    H --> S2["bucket#1"]
    H --> S3["bucket#N"]
    S1 --> P1[("partition")]
    S2 --> P2[("partition")]
    S3 --> P3[("partition")]
tradeoff: 写分片分散热点 vs 读取要并行查多个分片

Write sharding: append a random suffix to the partition key so writes spread out.
Move the entire table into memory.
Reduce the write rate.

options: Job 一旦执行完毕就立刻把它的记录从数据库里删除
近期保留在主表；过了合理期限（如 1 年）迁到更便宜的存储如 S3
不论新旧，把所有 Job 记录永久留在 DynamoDB 主表里

why_en: Keep recent executed jobs queryable, then archive older ones (after about a year) to cheaper storage like S3.
whenOtherWins: 若合规要求随时快速查询历史全量，或数据量小到成本可忽略，就没必要下沉冷存储。

Keep recent jobs queryable in the main table; archive older ones (say, after a year) to cheaper storage like S3.

Only keep records for jobs that failed, and discard the records of successful ones.

whenOtherWins: 在 Worker 数量少、且需要主动、细粒度健康信号的场景，中心健康检查才相对可行。

scenario_en: Consider detecting worker crashes with job leasing: a worker writes its ID and a lease-expiration time to the database when it takes a job, then periodically renews the lease while processing.
q: 租约方案的主要难点是？
q_en: What's the main difficulty with the leasing approach?
options: 无法记录 Worker ID
续租写入压力大，可能重复执行
根本无法检测宕机
租约必须用内存实现
why: 租约靠数据库分布式锁：Worker 崩溃后无法续租，租约过期别人接管。难点是续租写入量巨大（10k/s、5 秒租约约 5 万次/秒更新）、Worker 间时钟不同步或网络分区会导致同一 Job 被重复执行。
why_en: Job leasing needs heavy lease-renewal writes and suffers clock-skew and partition risks that can cause duplicate execution.
whenOtherWins: 在不用消息队列、必须靠数据库自建协调的环境，租约是可行的宕机检测手段。
tradeoff: 数据库租约（可控但写压力大） vs 托管队列可见性超时（省运维）

Heavy lease-renewal write load, with a risk of duplicate execution.
It cannot detect a crash at all.
Leases must live only in memory.

scenario_en: The goal is to detect and recover a crashed worker's job (an invisible failure) without adding infrastructure or complex coordination.

数据库租约

why: SQS 可见性超时天然处理不可见失败：Worker 取消息后它暂不可见，处理成功就删除；若 Worker 崩溃没在超时内删除，消息自动重现给别的 Worker。无需额外基建和协调。
why_en: SQS visibility timeouts hide a consumed message and re-surface it if the worker crashes before deleting it, needing no extra infrastructure.
whenOtherWins: 如果不能用 SQS（禁托管服务），才回退到租约或健康检查等自建方案。
tradeoff: SQS 内建可见性超时（零基建） vs 自建健康检查/租约（更多控制，更多运维）

scenario: 有个 Job 要跑 5 分钟，但 SQS 可见性超时只设了 30 秒，以便快速检测宕机。
scenario_en: A job takes five minutes to run, but the SQS visibility timeout is set to only 30 seconds so crashes are detected quickly.
q: 怎样既保留快速故障恢复，又不让长任务被误判为失败？
q_en: How do you keep fast failure recovery without misclassifying a long-running job as failed?
options: 把可见性超时直接设成 10 分钟
短超时快速探测，靠心跳定期续期
取消可见性超时
把长任务拆成 30 秒小任务
why: 设短可见性超时（30 秒）以便崩溃后 30 秒内被别人接管；长任务靠周期心跳——每 15 秒调 ChangeMessageVisibility 续期——避免运行中被误重投。兼顾快速探测和长任务。
why_en: Use a short visibility timeout plus periodic ChangeMessageVisibility heartbeats so long jobs stay owned while crashes are detected fast.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有任务都很短、时长可预测，直接设一个略大于最长任务的固定超时就够，无需心跳。
tradeoff: 短超时快速探测 vs 心跳续期保护长任务
options_en: Set the visibility timeout directly to ten minutes.
A short timeout for fast detection, kept alive with periodic heartbeats.
Remove the visibility timeout entirely.
Split every long job into 30-second chunks.
optionDirectness: 错；10 分钟超时会让宕机检测慢很多，拖累恢复速度。
对；短超时快速探测崩溃，心跳续期保护正在跑的长任务。
错；取消超时会让宕机 Job 永远没人接管。
错；拆分任务改变了任务本身的语义，不是通用解法。

q: 「至少一次执行」带来的直接后果是什么，因此必须处理？
q_en: What's the direct consequence of 'at-least-once execution' that must be handled?
options: 会导致 Job 在极端情况下永远都不会被执行
同一 Job 可能被执行多次，因此任务代码必须幂等（idempotent）
会导致 Job 原本的执行顺序被彻底打乱
会导致底层数据库被长时间锁死、无法写入
why: 至少一次意味着可能重复执行，所以任务代码必须幂等——多次执行的结果要和执行一次相同，否则会重复发邮件、重复转账。
why_en: At-least-once execution can run a job multiple times, so task code must be idempotent.
options_en: It would cause a job to never execute at all under extreme conditions.
The same job may run more than once, so task code must be idempotent.
It would cause a job's original execution order to be completely scrambled.
It would cause the underlying database to be locked up and unable to write for a long time.
optionDirectness: 错；至少一次恰恰保证 Job 会被执行，不会永远不跑。
对；可能被执行多次，所以任务代码必须幂等。
错；顺序问题和至少一次语义不是一回事。
错；至少一次不涉及锁死数据库。

q: 「收到就无脑执行、不做任何去重」这种最简做法的风险是？
q_en: What's the risk of the simplest approach -- just executing every delivery with no deduplication?
options: 只会让单次任务的执行速度变得更慢一些
重复执行引发数据不一致：转账可能转多次、计数器可能加多次

Duplicate delivery causes inconsistency, like double transfers or over-counted increments.
It would cause this job to never finish executing at all.
It would leave the system completely unable to record any execution status.

错；无脑执行的 Job 反而会被立刻处理完。
错；状态照常能记录，只是可能被记录了多次。

scenario_en: Idempotency is implemented with a dedup table: before executing, check whether this job_id plus execution timestamp has already been processed, and skip it if so.
q: 这种去重表方案的代价是？
q_en: What's the cost of this dedup-table approach?
options: 这种去重表方案其实完全不需要付出任何额外代价
每次执行都多一次数据库读写、要额外维护并定期清理该表，且检查与写入之间存在小的竞态窗口

why: 去重表用 job_id + 执行时间戳唯一标识：给每次执行增加数据库操作、需维护并定期清理防止无限膨胀，且「检查—写入」之间有小竞态窗口。
why_en: A dedup table adds database ops per execution, needs cleanup to bound growth, and has a small check-then-write race window.
whenOtherWins: 当下游服务无法改造成天然幂等、只能在调度层拦重复时，去重表是可行的兜底。
tradeoff: 去重表兜底（调度层解决） vs 天然幂等（任务层解决）

q: 把「可见失败后的重试流程」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the retry flow after a visible failure:
steps: 带指数退避的 delay 重新入队 SQS（用 attempt 算 DelaySeconds）
try/catch 捕获异常并记录错误
attempt 已达上限（如 3 次）→ 状态置 FAILED，不再重试
状态更新为 RETRYING 并记录 attempt 次数
why: 重试流程：捕获异常 → 置 RETRYING 记 attempt → 带退避 delay 重入队 → 若达上限则置 FAILED 停止。是「至少一次 + 有限重试」的落地。
why_en: On a visible failure: catch the error, mark RETRYING with the attempt count, re-enqueue with backoff, and mark FAILED once the limit is hit.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    F["Job fails visibly"] --> U["mark failed attempt"]
    U --> B["compute backoff"]
    B --> R{"retry left?"}
    R -->|yes| Q["requeue with delay"]
    R -->|no| D["DLQ or terminal failed"]

text: 代码执行可能持续数秒，典型长任务模式是 API 先返回 {{job/submission id}}，后台 worker 执行，客户端用 {{polling}} 查询状态。

scenario: 赛制设定为 90 分钟、10 道题、最多 10 万用户参赛，按解出的不同题目数排名，平局按最早全部完成的时间排序。
scenario_en: The contest lasts ninety minutes, has ten problems, allows up to one hundred thousand users, ranks by distinct solved problems, and breaks ties by earliest completion time.
q: 这些赛制参数对系统设计有哪些实际意味？（多选）
q_en: What design implications do these contest parameters have? (Select all that apply)
options: leaderboard 要按 distinct 解题数排序，并单独跟踪完成时间用于 tie-break
10 万用户量级下，若每次都对全表做实时聚合，数据库压力会很明显
90 分钟时限意味着系统不需要处理任何并发写入
10 道题的规模意味着可以把全部排名放进浏览器本地计算
why: 赛制细节直接决定了 leaderboard 的排序字段和查询压力量级，不只是背景设定。
why_en: The contest rules directly determine the leaderboard's ranking fields and query load, not just background detail.
options_en: The leaderboard must rank by distinct solved-problem count and separately track completion time for tie-breaking.
At a hundred-thousand-user scale, aggregating the full table on every request creates real database pressure.
A ninety-minute window means the system never has to handle concurrent writes.
Ten problems means every ranking can be computed in the browser's local memory.

scenario: 首版想从提交表计算某场竞赛排行榜，按通过的不同题数降序，平局按更早完成排序。
scenario_en: The first version computes one contest leaderboard from the submissions table, ranking by distinct solved count descending and earlier finish time for ties.
q: 哪类 SQL 查询表达了这个逻辑？
q_en: Which kind of SQL query expresses this leaderboard logic?
options: 按赛事过滤后分组，再按解题数和完成时间排序
只扫描 Problem 表，按题目标题排序
只读取每个用户最近的一条提交记录
按提交代码字符串的长度从长到短排序
codeSample:
SELECT userId, COUNT(DISTINCT problemId) AS solved, MIN(submittedAt) AS lastSolveTime
FROM submissions
WHERE competitionId = :competitionId AND passed = true
GROUP BY userId
ORDER BY solved DESC, lastSolveTime ASC;
why: 排行榜核心是每个用户通过的不同题数，平局时按完成时间排序。
why_en: The leaderboard's core metric is each user's distinct solved-problem count, with ties broken by completion time.
whenOtherWins: 高并发实时榜不该每次请求都跑这个聚合，Redis sorted set 更合适。
tradeoff: 按用户聚合统计 distinct 解题数 vs 逐条提交排序

Scan only the Problem table and sort by title.

q: 最合适的核心数据结构是什么？

tradeoff: 增量维护的有序结构 vs 每次读时现场排序

scenario_en: After a submission passes, the system must update one contest leaderboard and let clients read the top 100.
q: 哪组 Redis 命令最贴合？
q_en: Which Redis commands fit this leaderboard path?
options: FLUSHALL 后重新导入全部数据
LPUSH 把用户随机插入一个列表
ZADD 更新分数，ZRANGE 读取排名
GET 每个用户的值，交给客户端自己排序
codeSample:
ZADD competition:leaderboard:abc 95000 user:42
ZRANGE competition:leaderboard:abc 0 99 REV WITHSCORES
why: Sorted set 按 score 维护顺序，top N 查询不需要额外的数据库聚合。

text: 四个核心实体：{{Auction}}（拍卖：起拍价、结束时间）、{{Item}}（商品：名称、描述、图片）、{{Bid}}（出价：金额、出价人、所属拍卖）、{{User}}（发起拍卖或出价的用户）。
why: 先把实体列出来、细节从简，能帮后面 API 设计搭好骨架。Auction 与 Item 分开建模，Bid 通过 auctionId 关联拍卖。
why_en: The four core entities are Auction, Item, Bid, and User, kept light up front to structure the API design that follows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拍卖实体，含起拍价、结束时间、所拍商品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Auction holds the starting price, end date, and the item being sold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 商品实体，含名称、描述、图片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Item holds the name, description, and images of a product.

termDefinitions.meaning: 出价实体，含金额、出价人、所属拍卖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bid holds the amount, the bidder, and which auction it belongs to.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发起拍卖或出价的用户实体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User is the account that starts an auction or places a bid.

scenario: 建模时纠结：把 Item 的字段直接内嵌进 Auction，还是拆成独立实体？卖家常会把流拍的商品重新上架。
scenario_en: During modeling, you are choosing between embedding Item fields inside Auction or making Item a separate entity; sellers often relist unsold items.
q: 把 Item 规范化成独立实体的主要好处是？
q_en: What is the main benefit of normalizing Item into a separate entity?
options: 查询拍卖详情时不用做表 join，读取路径更简单更快
商品可跨多个拍卖复用、可独立更新、更容易加类目/搜索等商品级功能
把商品字段拆开能显著节省数据库总存储空间
把 Item 独立出来能避免出价时的并发竞态条件
why: 拆开的三个好处：商品可在多个拍卖间复用（重新上架）、商品详情可独立于拍卖更新、便于扩展类目/搜索等商品级功能。内嵌反而免了 join。
why_en: Normalizing Item into its own entity lets items be reused across auctions, updated independently, and extended with item-level features.
whenOtherWins: 内嵌进 Auction 也可接受——更简单、读时无需 join；面试里两种都行，关键是把理由讲清楚。
options_en: Queries won't need a table join, so reads are simpler and faster.
Items can be reused across auctions, updated independently, and extended with item-level features like categories or search.
Splitting item fields out saves significant database storage.
Separating Item avoids race conditions when bids are placed.
optionDirectness: 读路径特别紧、商品不会复用时，内嵌字段更省一次 join。
商品会重新上架或独立演进时，拆成 Item 能避免重复维护。
存储成本主导且字段大量重复时才看空间；本题差异不大。
出价竞态发生在并发写最高价时，实体拆分挡不住这个风险。
optionDirectness_en: Embedding wins when reads are extremely hot and items are never reused.
A separate Item helps when products can be relisted or evolve independently.
Storage only matters if duplicated fields dominate; here the space difference is small.
Bid races happen on concurrent highest-price writes, not on the Item boundary.
tradeoff: 跨拍卖复用与独立演进 vs 内嵌免 join 的读取简单性

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalizing means splitting fields into a separate entity or table so they can be reused and updated independently.

q: 创建拍卖的 API 请求体里应包含哪些字段？
q_en: Which fields should the create-auction API request body include?
options: item、startDate、endDate、startingPrice
auctionId、maxBid、userId
item、category、sortOrder
startingPrice、buyNowPrice、shippingFee
why: POST /auctions 带上商品信息、起止时间和起拍价，返回创建好的 Auction & Item。这直接对应功能需求一。
why_en: Creating an auction is a POST to /auctions with the item, start and end dates, and starting price.
codeSample:
POST /auctions -> Auction & Item
{
    item: Item,
    startDate: Date,
    endDate: Date,
    startingPrice: number
}

auctionId, maxBid, userId
item, category, sortOrder
startingPrice, buyNowPrice, shippingFee

做搜索列表页时才需要 category/sortOrder；创建请求不用带排序。
支持一口价或运费时才需要这些字段；本题没有定义它们。

auctionId is used after creation; maxBid belongs to the bidding result.
category and sortOrder matter for search pages, not for the create call.

q: 出价（placing a bid）的 API 应该怎么设计？
q_en: How should the API for placing a bid be modeled?
options: PUT /auctions/:auctionId 更新 maxBid 字段
POST /bids，请求体里带 auctionId
GET /auctions/:auctionId/bid?amount=100
POST /auctions/:auctionId/bids，请求体带 Bid 详情，返回创建的 Bid
why: 出价是在某个拍卖下创建一条 Bid 资源，所以用嵌套路径 POST /auctions/:auctionId/bids，返回创建的 Bid（含接受/拒绝状态）。
why_en: Placing a bid is a POST to /auctions/:auctionId/bids with the bid details, returning the created bid.
options_en: PUT /auctions/:auctionId and update the maxBid field.
POST /bids with auctionId in the request body.
GET /auctions/:auctionId/bid?amount=100.
POST /auctions/:auctionId/bids with the bid details, returning the created bid.
optionDirectness: 只维护当前价时才会覆盖字段；这里还要保留每条 Bid 历史。
扁平 /bids 也能工作，但要在请求体里额外表达 auctionId 归属。
查询状态才用 GET；出价会写入服务器状态，不能放查询参数里提交。
在某个拍卖下创建 Bid 时，嵌套路径和 POST 把语义说清楚。
optionDirectness_en: Overwriting fits a current-price-only model, but this design must keep bid history.
A flat /bids path can work, but the auction relationship is less explicit.
GET is for reading state; bidding writes state and should not be submitted in a query string.
POST under /auctions/:auctionId clearly models creating a Bid for one auction.

q: 查看拍卖页时，GET /auctions/:auctionId 返回什么？

options: 只有 Auction

q: 在高层设计里，API Gateway 承担哪些职责？
q_en: In the high-level design, what does the API Gateway own?
options: 只负责存储拍卖数据、执行出价合法性校验
鉴权、限流、以及最重要的——把请求路由到对应服务
维护每个用户的 SSE 长连接，向客户端广播新出价
计算并写入拍卖当前的最高出价
why: API Gateway 是客户端进后端的统一入口：做鉴权、限流，最重要的是把请求路由到 Auction Service 或 Bidding Service。
why_en: The API gateway handles authentication and rate limiting, and most importantly routes each request to the right service.
options_en: Only store auction data and validate bid legality.
Authentication, rate limiting, and most importantly, routing requests to the right service.
Maintain each user's SSE connection and broadcast new bids to clients.
Compute and write the auction's current highest bid.
optionDirectness: 存储和校验属于后端业务服务；网关不承载拍卖状态。
网关在入口层处理横切逻辑，再把请求送到正确服务。
需要实时推送时才讨论 SSE 连接；它不是普通请求网关的核心职责。
最高价计算属于 Bidding Service 的写路径逻辑。
optionDirectness_en: Storage and validation belong to backend services; the gateway should not own auction state.
The gateway handles cross-cutting entry logic, then routes to the right service.
SSE connections matter for real-time push, not for the basic request gateway.
Computing the highest bid is write-path logic owned by the bidding service.

q: 把「创建一个新拍卖」的数据流排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the create-auction data flow in the correct order.
steps: Auction Service 校验请求，写入拍卖和商品数据
客户端向 /auctions 发送 POST 请求
数据库把数据存入 auctions 和 items 表
API Gateway 把请求路由到 Auction Service
why: 创建拍卖就是基本 CRUD：客户端 POST → 网关路由 → Auction Service 校验并写入 → 数据库落表。此时 Auction Service 只是数据库的薄封装。
why_en: Creating an auction flows from the client's POST through the gateway to the auction service, which validates and writes the data to the database.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|POST /auctions| G[API Gateway]
    G --> A[Auction Service]
    A -->|校验+写入| D[(Database)]

scenario: 出价流量预计是创建拍卖流量的约 100 倍，且出价有复杂的校验、竞态、实时更新逻辑。
scenario_en: Bid traffic is expected to be about 100x auction-creation traffic, and bidding has validation, race-condition, and real-time update logic.
q: 为什么要把 Bidding Service 从 Auction Service 里拆出来？
q_en: Why split Bidding Service out from Auction Service?
options: 拆开能独立扩容、隔离复杂业务逻辑、并分别按写密集/读密集优化
微服务架构在任何规模下都天然优于单体应用
关系型数据库设计规范要求每张表对应一个独立服务
拆分单纯是为了让 API Gateway 的路由规则更简单
why: 三个理由：出价量约是创建量的 100 倍需要独立扩容；出价的校验/竞态/实时更新逻辑复杂，值得隔离；Bidding 可按高吞吐写优化、Auction 按读密集优化。
why_en: A separate bidding service allows independent scaling, isolates complex bidding logic, and lets each service be optimized for its own workload.

q: 只在 Auction 上存一个 maxBidPrice 字段、每次覆盖更新，而不维护 bids 表，会带来什么后果？
q_en: What happens if Auction only stores maxBidPrice and overwrites it instead of keeping a bids table?

It destroys historical data — you can't audit bidding or investigate disputes, and can't disprove a user who claims their bid was never recorded.

q: 如果拍卖页从不刷新最高价，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the auction page never refreshes the current highest bid?
options: 数据库读请求负载会明显升高
用户按过时价格出价，被拒后困惑沮丧，热门拍卖尤其明显
同一个用户的出价会被系统重复提交两次

why: 价格陈旧 → 用户按旧价出价 → 系统拒绝 → 用户困惑。初版解法是每隔几秒轮询一次最新最高价，不完美但能显著减少这种情况。
why_en: Without refreshing, users bid against a stale price and get confusing rejections, so the fix is polling the latest max bid every few seconds.
options_en: Database read load rises noticeably.
Users bid against a stale price and get confused and frustrated when rejected — especially bad on hot auctions.
The same user's bid gets submitted twice by the system.
The auction can never close even after its end time passes.
optionDirectness: 增加读负载是轮询带来的代价；完全不刷新反而少发请求。
用户看到旧价就会按旧价出手，拒绝结果看起来像系统出错。
重复提交要靠幂等键处理；刷新最高价解决不了这个问题。
关闭拍卖由结束时间和后台流程决定，不依赖页面是否刷新。

q: 多个用户同时对同一拍卖出价、只能有一个赢——这对应哪个系统设计模式？
q_en: When multiple users bid on the same auction and only one can win, which design pattern is this?
options: 实时更新（Real-time Updates）模式——服务器主动推送最新状态给客户端
扇出（Fan-out）模式——一条写入需要分发给大量下游读者
处理竞争（Dealing with Contention）模式——多方争抢同一资源时的协调
CQRS 模式——把读路径和写路径拆成两套独立模型
why: 在线拍卖是「处理竞争」模式的经典案例：多方争夺同一资源产生竞态，需要乐观并发控制、行锁或缓存策略来协调。
why_en: Simultaneous bids on the same auction are a textbook dealing-with-contention pattern, coordinated with tools like optimistic concurrency control or row locking.
options_en: Real-time Updates pattern — the server proactively pushes the latest state to clients.
Fan-out pattern — one write must be distributed to a large number of downstream readers.
Dealing with Contention pattern — coordinating multiple parties competing for the same resource.
CQRS pattern — splitting the read path and write path into two separate models.
optionDirectness: 当问题是通知旁观者最新状态时，实时更新才是主角。
当一条写要分发给很多订阅者时，扇出才是主角。
多个写者争同一个最高价位置时，重点是协调竞争。
读写模型需要独立扩展时才考虑 CQRS；它不解决谁赢。
optionDirectness_en: Real-time updates matter when the problem is notifying viewers of new state.
Fan-out matters when one write must be delivered to many subscribers.
When many writers race for one highest-bid slot, the focus is contention.
CQRS helps scale read and write models separately; it does not decide who wins.

q: 当前最高价 $10，A 出 $100、B 紧接着出 $20。没有并发控制时最坏会怎样？
q_en: If the current highest bid is $10, A bids $100, then B bids $20, what is the worst case without concurrency control?
options: B 的 20 美元出价会被正确拒绝，因为读到了最新的 100 美元
A 的 100 美元出价会因为并发冲突而丢失
两个事务互相等待对方释放锁，系统发生死锁
B 读到陈旧的 10 美元，20 大于 10 通过校验——两人都被接受、都以为自己在赢
why: B 基于过时读数（$10）通过了校验，于是 $100 和 $20 都被接受，拍卖出现两个「最高出价者」。B 本应和更新后的 $100 比较而被拒绝。
why_en: User B validates a twenty-dollar bid against a stale ten-dollar read, so both bids get accepted and two users each think they're winning.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as User A

q: 有人认为「竞价其实不需要强一致，最终一致就够」，这个论点的实质与局限是？

论点只在两人出价金额恰好完全相同的情况下才成立
why: 两个 bid 都接受不影响最终结果，事后修正客户端即可——论点成立，但它绕开了核心难点，面试官通常仍要求强一致方案。
why_en: The eventual-consistency argument is valid since the winner is unchanged, but it dodges the hard part, so interviewers still expect strong consistency.
options_en: Invalid — accepting both bids would corrupt who is judged the final winner.
Valid — the final winner is unchanged, so you can just notify B afterward; but it dodges the core difficulty, and most interviewers still expect a strong-consistency solution.
Valid, and every system design interviewer accepts this eventual-consistency approach outright.
It only holds when both bids happen to be for the exact same amount.

q: 第一种保证竞价一致性的思路——行级锁方案——的流程是？
q_en: What is the flow for the row-locking approach to keeping bids consistent?
options: 开事务后 SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 锁住 bid 行，查最大值、比较、插入
不开事务，直接锁住整张 bids 表再插入新出价
先用 Redis 拿一把分布式锁，再对数据库执行插入
完全不加锁，直接插入新出价，靠唯一索引兜底去重
why: 思路是用事务 + SELECT ... FOR UPDATE 把该拍卖的现有 bid 行全锁住，串行化「查最大 → 比较 → 插入」。但它有严重缺陷，不适合生产。
why_en: The row-locking approach wraps a transaction that locks the auction's existing bid rows, checks the max, and inserts the new bid before committing.
options_en: Begin a transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE to lock the auction's bid rows, read the max, compare, then insert.
Skip the transaction and just lock the entire bids table before inserting.
Grab a Redis distributed lock first, then run the database insert.
Insert the new bid with no locking at all, relying on a unique index to deduplicate.
optionDirectness: 行级锁方案靠事务串行化同一拍卖的查最大、比较、插入。
全表锁只适合极小系统；热门拍卖会把无关拍卖也堵住。
跨进程分布式锁是另一类方案；这里讨论数据库行锁。
唯一索引适合防重复请求；它挡不住两个金额都通过旧最大值校验。
optionDirectness_en: Row locking serializes max-read, compare, and insert for one auction inside a transaction.
A table lock only fits tiny systems; hot auctions would block unrelated auctions too.
A distributed Redis lock is a different approach; this card is about database row locks.
A unique index prevents duplicate requests, not two bids validating against the old max.

错。训练、复盘、锦标赛都明确排在范围外，别把设计精力花在这里。

Correct — server-side move validation is the trust foundation of the whole design.
Correct — the leaderboard is the third core requirement, updated after each game ends.

Real-time moves validated by the server.

Million-scale connections and state must be spread across dozens to hundreds of game servers.

scenario: 实时对局服务器短暂不可达，系统必须在「让玩家继续操作」和「暂停对局等待恢复」之间取舍。
scenario_en: The live game server is briefly unavailable, and the system must choose between letting players keep moving and pausing the game until recovery.
q: 在线棋局状态的默认取舍应该是什么？
q_en: What should the default tradeoff be for live chess game state?
options: 优先可用性，客户端各自继续走
优先一致性，暂停棋局直到服务端恢复
让白方客户端成为临时主节点
直接判掉线方负
why: 棋盘和时钟一旦分叉就很难修复，暂停几秒仍可恢复；因此对局状态应选择一致性高于可用性。
why_en: A paused game is recoverable, but divergent boards are corrupt, so game state should prefer consistency over availability.
whenOtherWins: 若是旁观直播或新闻流这类只读体验，短暂旧数据通常比不可用更可接受，可用性会更重要。
optionExplanations: 错误。各自继续会让两边棋盘分叉，之后没法合并。
对。暂停几秒可恢复，分叉的棋盘没法恢复，所以选一致性。
错误。客户端不可信，不能替代服务端做权威判定。
错误。短暂不可达不等于对局作废，判负太重。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — letting both sides keep moving lets their boards diverge with no way to merge back.
Correct — a brief pause is recoverable, a diverged board is not, so consistency wins here.
Wrong — a client cannot be trusted as the authoritative source of truth.
Wrong — a short outage is not the same as a forfeit-worthy failure.
options_en: Prefer availability and let each client keep moving independently.
Prefer consistency and pause the game until the server recovers.
Promote the white player's client to a temporary primary.
Immediately forfeit the disconnected side.
tradeoff: 一致性（暂停恢复）vs 可用性（各自继续可能分叉）

Correct — Game carries all the live state of a chess match.

why: 客户端可以伪造 userId 或 rating 来挑软柿子，身份和评级必须由服务端可信数据决定。

scenario: 两名玩家在同一盘棋里持续互相发送走子，并且服务端要即时推送确认、对手走子和结束事件。
scenario_en: Two players continuously send moves in the same game, and the server must immediately push acknowledgements, opponent moves, and game-end events.
q: 这条实时对局通道最适合用什么？
q_en: What is the best channel for this live game path?
options: 短轮询 REST
Server-Sent Events
WebSocket
每日批处理同步
why: 棋局是双向、低延迟、持续连接的交互，WebSocket 比单向 SSE 或轮询更贴合。
why_en: A chess game needs continuous low-latency bidirectional messages, so WebSocket is the right protocol.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是服务端向浏览器推送只读价格或评论，SSE 可能更简单；如果实时性不强，轮询也足够。
optionDiagrams:
flowchart TD
  C[Client]
  C -->|poll| S[Server]
  S --> C

flowchart TD
  S[Server]
  S -->|one way| C[Client]

flowchart TD

  GS[Game Server]
  B[Player B]

optionExplanations: 错误。轮询间隔会拖慢走子确认，还浪费大量空轮询请求。
错误。SSE 只能服务端推客户端，棋局需要双向发走子。
对。棋局双向、低延迟、长连接，WebSocket 天然匹配。
错误。批处理完全不满足实时对局的时效要求。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — polling intervals delay move confirmation and waste requests when nothing changed.
Wrong — SSE is server-to-client only, but a chess move has to flow both ways.
Correct — a game is bidirectional, low-latency, and long-lived, which is exactly WebSocket's shape.
Wrong — daily batch sync cannot meet a real-time gameplay requirement at all.
options_en: Short-polling REST.
Server-Sent Events.
WebSocket.
Daily batch synchronization.
tradeoff: 双向低延迟长连接（WebSocket） vs 服务端单向推送（SSE）

q: 一个单局 WebSocket 协议中，服务端通常需要推送哪些消息？（多选）
q_en: Which messages should the server usually push in a single-game WebSocket protocol? (Select all that apply)
options: moveAck，带接受/拒绝和权威时钟
opponentMove，带对手走子和权威时钟
gameEnd，带最终结果
clientRatingOverride，接受客户端声明的新等级分
why: 服务端需要回传走子是否被接受、对手合法走子和结束结果；评级不能由客户端声明。
why_en: The server pushes acknowledgements, opponent moves, and game-end results, while ratings must never be client-declared.
optionExplanations: 对。走子是否被接受，必须由服务端回传确认。
对。对手走子和权威时钟都要推给另一方。
对。对局结束时服务端要广播最终结果。
错。评级绝不能由客户端声明，必须来自 Player 记录。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — whether a move was accepted must be confirmed by the server.
Correct — the opponent's move and the authoritative clock both need pushing to the other side.
Correct — the server broadcasts the final result when a game ends.
Wrong — a rating must never be client-declared; it comes from the Player record.
options_en: moveAck, carrying accept/reject and the authoritative clock.
opponentMove, carrying the opponent's move and the authoritative clock.
gameEnd, carrying the final result.
clientRatingOverride, accepting a new rating the client declares.

scenario: 每盘棋的棋盘、轮到谁和两个时钟只有几百字节，走子路径要求端到端低于 200ms。
scenario_en: Each game board, turn marker, and two clocks take only a few hundred bytes, and the move path targets under 200ms end to end.
q: 实时棋局状态应该主要放在哪里？
q_en: Where should live chess game state primarily live?
options: 每步都从共享数据库读写 live state
对象存储中的棋盘快照
运行该盘棋的 Game Server 内存
客户端本地作为真相源
why: 棋局状态很小且短生命周期，放在服务端内存能把校验变成本地操作；持久化 move log 用于恢复而不是服务下一步走子。
why_en: Live chess state is tiny and short-lived, so keeping it in the owning game server's memory gives local validation while the move log handles recovery.
whenOtherWins: 如果单个会话状态很大、持续很久，或必须任意服务器无粘性接管，共享存储会更有吸引力。
optionExplanations: 错误。这会把本可几微秒完成的校验变成网络往返，侵蚀 200ms 预算。
错误。对象存储面向大对象批量读写，不适合几百字节的毫秒级更新。
对。状态小且短命，放内存能把校验变成本地操作。
错误。客户端可被篡改，不能作为对局的权威真相。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — this turns a microsecond-cheap check into a network round trip that eats the 200ms budget.
Wrong — object storage is built for bulk data, not a few hundred bytes needing millisecond updates.
Correct — the state is tiny and short-lived, so memory turns validation into a local operation.
Wrong — a client can be tampered with and cannot be the authoritative source of truth.
options_en: Read and write live state from a shared database on every move.
Store board snapshots in object storage.
Keep it in the memory of the Game Server that owns this game.
Treat the client's local state as the source of truth.
tradeoff: 内存持有换低延迟校验 vs 共享存储换无状态可替换

q: 把每一步 live state 都放 Redis/数据库共享读写，最大的热路径代价是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest hot-path cost of putting every live-state update in Redis or a database?
options: 必须使用 GPU 校验走子
每步多一次网络读写，压缩 200ms 延迟预算
无法保存走子历史
排行榜无法按 rating 排序
why: 每次走子都要读当前棋盘并写回新状态，把本来可本地完成的几微秒校验变成网络往返。
why_en: A shared live-state store adds network reads and writes to every move, turning a local validation into hot-path latency.
optionExplanations: 错误。走子校验是简单规则判断，和 GPU 毫无关系。
对。每步都要读当前棋盘再写回新状态，多一次网络往返。
错误。走子历史照样能写进共享存储，问题不在能不能存。
错误。排行榜排序和 live state 放哪无关，是另一套设计。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — move validation is simple rule-checking, unrelated to GPU work.
Correct — every move now reads the current board and writes the new one back over the network.
Wrong — move history can still be written to shared storage; storage capability is not the issue.
Wrong — leaderboard sorting has nothing to do with where live game state lives.
options_en: You would need GPU validation for moves.
Every move now pays an extra network round trip, squeezing the 200ms budget.
Move history could no longer be stored.
The leaderboard could no longer sort by rating.

q: 将实时棋局放在内存中的决策链，正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct decision chain for keeping live chess state in memory?
steps: 选择 stateful Game Server 持有棋盘和时钟
用 durable move log 作为崩溃后的恢复来源
确认每盘状态只有几百字节且生命周期短
要求走子传播低于 200ms
why: 先由低延迟要求和小状态推出内存持有，再用 move log 补上崩溃恢复。
why_en: The low-latency requirement plus tiny game state justifies an in-memory owner, and the move log supplies recovery.
whenOtherWins: 如果每盘状态很大、生命周期很长，或必须任意节点无粘性接管，共享持久状态会更值得考虑。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  L[Low latency moves]
  T[Tiny live state]
  G[Stateful game server]
  M[Durable move log]
  L --> T --> G --> M

q: 服务端收到合法走子后，热路径中应完成哪些动作？（多选）
q_en: After the server receives a legal move, which actions belong on the hot path? (Select all that apply)
options: 校验走子合法且轮到该玩家
更新内存棋盘并切换时钟
先把走子追加到 durable move log
信任客户端发来的剩余时间作为权威值
why: 服务端必须校验、更新权威状态，并在广播前持久化走子；客户端时钟只能用于显示，不能作为真相。
why_en: The server validates the move, updates authoritative state, and persists the move before broadcasting, while client time is only display data.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant G as Game Server
  participant L as Move Log
  participant O as Opponent
  C->>G: move
  G->>G: validate turn

  G->>L: append move

optionExplanations: 对。合法性和轮次是接受走子前的第一道关卡。
对。合法走子要立刻反映到权威棋盘和时钟。
对。广播前先落 durable log，崩溃后才不丢已看到的走子。
错。剩余时间是可作弊值，必须由服务端自己维护。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — legality and turn order are the first gate before accepting a move.
Correct — a legal move must immediately update the authoritative board and clock.
Correct — persisting before broadcast means a crash never loses a move both players already saw.
Wrong — remaining time is a cheat-sensitive value the server must own itself.
options_en: Validate the move is legal and it is this player's turn.
Update the in-memory board and switch the clock.
Append the move to the durable move log first.
Trust the remaining time the client reports as authoritative.

q: 为什么合法走子要先写 move log，再 ack/push 给双方？
q_en: Why should a legal move be written to the move log before acking and pushing it?
options: 这样可以减少 Redis 内存
否则崩溃恢复后可能缺少玩家已经看见的走子
这样能避免所有网络延迟
这样排行榜能实时更新
why: 如果先广播再崩溃，恢复出的棋盘会缺少双方已经看到的移动，造成不可接受的状态回退。
why_en: Broadcasting before persistence can make recovery lose a move that both players already saw, corrupting the game state.
optionExplanations: 错误。写入顺序和 Redis 内存占用没有关系。
对。先广播再崩溃，恢复出的棋盘会比玩家实际看到的落后一步。
错误。持久化本身也要花时间，不可能消除全部延迟。
错误。排行榜更新在赛后才发生，与走子持久化顺序无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — write ordering has nothing to do with Redis memory usage.
Correct — broadcasting first would let a crash recover a board one move behind what players already saw.
Wrong — persistence itself takes time, so it cannot remove all latency.
Wrong — leaderboard updates happen after the game ends, unrelated to move-persist ordering.
options_en: It reduces Redis memory usage.
Otherwise crash recovery could be missing a move players already saw.
It avoids all network delay entirely.
It makes the leaderboard update in real time.

q: 补全 live state 与持久化的职责分工：
q_en: Fill in the split between live state and durable storage:
text: 实时棋盘的真相源是 Game Server 的{{内存}}；数据库里的追加式 {{Move log}} 主要用于崩溃后 replay 恢复，而不是服务下一步走子。
why: 这能同时得到低延迟和可恢复性，避免把每步校验绑定到远程存储。
why_en: This split gives low-latency local validation while retaining recoverability through replay.

q: 用共享数据库表按 rating 范围查询 pending requests 时，最危险的竞态是什么？
q_en: When using a shared database table for pending requests by rating range, what is the dangerous race?
options: 玩家 rating 会自动下降
两个 matcher 同时把同一个等待玩家配进两盘棋
数据库无法保存 timeControl
排行榜会被重算两次
why: 范围搜索后还要 claim 候选人；若 claim 不是原子的，同一个 pending request 可能被多个 worker 读到并匹配。
why_en: Range search plus non-atomic claiming can let multiple workers book the same waiting player into different games.
optionExplanations: 错误。竞态和 rating 数值升降没有任何关系。
对。范围查询后 claim 不是原子的，两个 worker 都能抢到同一个人。
错误。timeControl 只是普通字段，存储能力不是问题。
错误。排行榜重算发生在赛后，和匹配竞态无关。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — the race has nothing to do with a rating value going up or down.
Correct — a non-atomic claim after a range search lets two workers grab the same waiting player.
Wrong — timeControl is an ordinary field; storage capability is not the issue.
Wrong — leaderboard recomputation happens after games end, unrelated to matchmaking races.
options_en: A player's rating automatically drops.
Two matchers simultaneously pair the same waiting player into two different games.
The database cannot store timeControl.
The leaderboard gets recalculated twice.

scenario: 需要按 rating 做范围搜索、按 time control 隔离池子，并让多台 matcher 共享同一个 pending pool。
scenario_en: The system needs rating-range search, separate pools by time control, and one shared pending pool visible to many matcher workers.
q: pending 匹配池最适合用哪种结构？
q_en: What structure best fits the pending matchmaking pool?
options: Elasticsearch 对请求做全文检索索引
S3 里按 time control 存一份对象列表
单个 matcher 进程内维护一个有序数组
Redis sorted set，按 time control 分 key
why: sorted set 以 rating 为 score，天然支持按分数范围查找、插入和删除；共享 Redis 让 matcher fleet 有同一份视图。
why_en: A Redis sorted set scored by rating supports range lookups, inserts, and removals while giving all matchmakers a shared pool.
whenOtherWins: 如果规模很小且只跑单进程，进程内有序数组更简单；如果需要复杂文本搜索而不是数值范围，搜索索引才有意义。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  P[Player queues]
  Z[Redis sorted set by rating]
  M[Matcher workers]
  G[Create game]
  P --> Z
  M -->|range lookup| Z
  M -->|atomic remove| Z
  M --> G
optionExplanations: 错误。这里要的是数值范围查询，不是文本相关性检索。
错误。S3 面向大对象批量读写，不支持低延迟按分数范围查找。
错误。只在单进程有效，加第二个 matcher 就会有两份不同步的视图。
对。score=rating 天然支持范围查找，且多台 matcher 能共享同一份池子。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — this problem needs numeric range queries, not full-text relevance search.
Wrong — S3 is built for bulk object reads and writes, not low-latency score-range lookups.
Wrong — this only works for one process; a second matcher gets an out-of-sync view.
Correct — scoring by rating gives native range lookups, and a shared Redis pool works across every matcher.
options_en: A full-text search index in Elasticsearch.
A list of objects in S3, one per time control.
An in-process sorted array inside a single matcher.
A Redis sorted set, one key per time control.
tradeoff: 共享可查询的池子（Redis） vs 单进程本地速度（进程内数组）

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 里按分数自动排序的集合结构，支持范围查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis structure that keeps members ordered by score and supports range queries.

scenario: 一个 blitz 玩家 rating=1512 入队，requestId=req_8a3f，还需要保存 playerId、状态和入队时间。
scenario_en: A blitz player with rating 1512 queues as requestId=req_8a3f, and the system also needs to store playerId, status, and enqueue time.
q: 哪组 Redis 操作能同时满足按 rating 排序候选人、又保存这些字段？
q_en: Which Redis operations both sort candidates by rating and store these fields?
options: ZADD mm:blitz 1512 req_8a3f + HSET mmreq:req_8a3f ...
LPUSH mm:blitz req_8a3f + GET req_8a3f
SET mm:blitz 1512 + PUBLISH all
SADD mm:blitz 1512 req_8a3f
why: sorted set 用 rating 排序等待请求，hash 保存 request 的其他字段，两者共同组成可查询、可 claim 的池子。
why_en: The sorted set indexes requests by rating and the hash stores request metadata, forming a searchable and claimable pool.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要 FIFO 队列且不按 rating 搜索，list/stream 可能更合适。
codeSample:
ZADD mm:blitz 1512 req_8a3f
HSET mmreq:req_8a3f playerId 42 rating 1512 status pending enqueuedAt 1718900000
optionExplanations: 对。sorted set 按 rating 排序等待队列，hash 存其余字段，两者配合可查询可 claim。
错误。list 不能按 rating 做范围查找，GET 也读不到一个 list。
错误。SET 只能存一个值，覆盖了其他玩家的 rating，且 PUBLISH all 太粗。
错误。普通 set 不带 score，无法按 rating 范围搜索。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the sorted set orders waiters by rating while the hash holds the rest of the fields, together giving a searchable, claimable pool.
Wrong — a list cannot do rating range lookups, and GET cannot read a list value.
Wrong — SET only holds one value, overwriting other players' ratings, and PUBLISH all is too broad.
Wrong — a plain set has no score, so it cannot support rating-range search.
options_en: ZADD into the sorted set plus HSET for the request's other fields.
LPUSH onto a list plus GET the request.
SET a single value plus PUBLISH to everyone.
SADD into a plain set.
tradeoff: sorted set + hash 可范围查找可 claim vs 简单结构快但查不了范围

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 命令，把多个字段写进一个 hash 结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HSET is a Redis command that writes multiple fields into a hash.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 命令，把成员按分数加入 sorted set。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZADD is a Redis command that adds a member to a sorted set with a score.

scenario: 多个 matcher 同时看到同一个 pending opponent，必须保证只有一个 worker 真正拿到这个玩家。
scenario_en: Several matcher workers can see the same pending opponent, so exactly one worker must actually claim that player.
q: 哪条 Redis 命令最适合做原子 claim？
q_en: Which Redis command is the best fit for an atomic claim?
options: ZRANGEBYSCORE mm:blitz 1462 1562
PUBLISH mm:req_2c91 matchFound
HGETALL mmreq:req_2c91
ZREM mm:blitz req_2c91
why: ZREM 返回实际删除数量，返回 1 的 worker 赢得 claim，返回 0 的 worker 知道候选人已被拿走。
why_en: ZREM is an atomic claim because exactly one worker removes the member and gets a return value of one.
whenOtherWins: 查找候选人时需要 ZRANGEBYSCORE；通知持有长轮询连接的节点时才用 pub/sub。
codeSample:
# 1 means this worker claimed the player; 0 means someone else did
ZREM mm:blitz req_2c91
optionExplanations: 错误。这只是查找候选人，多个 worker 查到同一个人不代表谁拿到了。
错误。发布通知要等 claim 成功之后，不能替代原子删除。
错误。读字段不会移除候选人，无法防止重复配对。
对。ZREM 返回真正删除的数量，返回 1 的那个 worker 才算赢得 claim。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — this only searches for candidates; multiple workers seeing the same person does not decide who wins.
Wrong — publishing the notification only happens after a claim succeeds; it cannot replace the atomic removal.
Wrong — reading fields does not remove the candidate, so it cannot prevent a double pairing.
Correct — ZREM returns how many members it actually removed, so a return of one is the winning claim.
options_en: ZRANGEBYSCORE to search a rating window.
PUBLISH a matchFound event.
HGETALL to read the request's fields.
ZREM to remove the candidate from the sorted set.
tradeoff: 原子 claim（ZREM） vs 只读查找（ZRANGEBYSCORE）

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 命令，从 sorted set 里删除成员并返回实际删除数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZREM is a Redis command that removes a member from a sorted set and returns how many were actually removed.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 命令，按分数范围取出 sorted set 里的成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZRANGEBYSCORE is a Redis command that fetches sorted-set members within a score range.

q: 补全极端 rating 玩家等待过久时的匹配策略：
q_en: Fill in the matchmaking strategy for extreme-rating players who wait too long:
text: 匹配窗口应随等待时间逐步{{变宽}}，例如从 ±50 开始，根据 {{enqueuedAt}} 计算可接受范围，而不是一开始就给所有人无限宽窗口。
why: 这能让普通玩家快速得到公平对局，也让高低分极端玩家最终不至于永远等不到人。
why_en: A widening window balances fairness for common cases with eventual matching for rating extremes.

q: 等待玩家的长轮询连接已经断开后才被 claim，worker 应该怎么处理这次配对？
q_en: If the waiting player's long-poll connection is gone before claim, what should the worker do with this pairing?
options: 照常创建游戏，等玩家之后发现
作废配对，把仍等待的一方放回池子
让断开玩家自动判负
把请求永久删除
why: 若等待方已经收不到 gameId，这盘棋会变成孤儿对局；应撤销这次配对并把可用玩家重新入队。
why_en: If the waiting client cannot receive the match, the pairing would be orphaned, so the available player should be returned to the pool.
optionExplanations: 错误。对方永远收不到 gameId，会变成没人知道的孤儿对局。
对。撤销这次无效配对，把可用玩家重新放回等待池继续匹配。
错误。这不是玩家的错，判负对可用一方不公平。
错误。永久删除会让本该继续排队的玩家彻底出局。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — that side never receives the gameId, leaving an orphaned game nobody knows about.
Correct — void the dead pairing and put the still-available player back in the pool to match again.
Wrong — this is not the player's fault, so forfeiting is unfair to the side that is still available.
Wrong — permanently deleting the request removes a player who should still be queued.
options_en: Create the game anyway and let the player find out later.
Void the pairing and return the still-waiting player to the pool.
Automatically forfeit the disconnected player.
Permanently delete the request.

q: 这类容量论证最关键的方法是什么？
q_en: What is the key method in this kind of capacity argument?
options: 只要用 Redis 就默认已经具备水平扩展能力
只要 QPS 到五位数，不管资源类型就要分片
只看平均吞吐，忽略最热的那个 key
换算成瓶颈资源的操作数，对比单节点吞吐上限
why: 把请求数换算成 ops/s 再对比 Redis 单节点数十万 ops/s 的量级，才能定量证明不需要分片；记住这套「换算+对比上限」的方法，比记住某次算出的具体数字更重要。
why_en: The real skill is converting peak requests into the bottleneck resource's operation count and comparing it to that resource's known single-node ceiling, not memorizing one computed number.
scenario: 面试官问「为什么不马上给匹配池分片」，你需要把峰值请求量换算成 Redis 操作量，再和 Redis 单节点已知的吞吐能力做比较。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you would not shard the matchmaking pool immediately; you need to convert peak requests into Redis operations and compare that with a known single-node Redis ceiling.
options_en: Using Redis at all already implies horizontal scale, so there is nothing to verify.
Any five-digit QPS number means you must shard, regardless of the resource.
Only look at average throughput and ignore the hottest key.
Convert peak requests into the bottleneck resource's operation count and compare it against that resource's known ceiling.

会让方案围绕「换算成瓶颈资源的操作数，对比单节点吞吐上限」展开。

Only fits when this statement is true: any five-digit QPS number means you must shard, regardless of the resource.
